documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe**, writing from **Hven** (*Insula nostra Huaena*), where he had withdrawn after the 1576 royal grant of the island and was then in the midst of building Uraniborg. This is his reply to **Hieronymus Wolf** (1516–1580), the Augsburg humanist and Greek scholar; the surviving Wolf-side letters in this exchange include the 13 November 1571 consolatory letter (identifier brahe-t_15711113001) and a further letter "around the end of March of this [1579] year," to which the present letter responds.
- **Place / dateline.** *Datae in Insula nostra Huaena 1579* = "Given on our Island of Hven, 1579" (O.S.; Denmark kept Old Style until 1700). **The source supplies the year only** — no month or day. The edition label gives the place ("Hven") but no finer date; the header therefore carries the bare year as written. The internal reference to "around the end of March of this year" (*circa finem Martij huius anni*) for the received letter dates the reply to **after late March 1579**, but does not fix its own day; this is left unresolved by this chapter's convention (no silent date construction).
- ***de Cometa … MAeSTLINI*** — the **comet of 1577**. *MAeSTLINUS* = **Michael Maestlin** (1550–1631), then producing his cometary tract (*Observatio et demonstratio cometae … 1577*), later Kepler's teacher. Tycho praises his observation as "coming nearest to the truth" and its supporting *Mathematica demonstratio* ("mathematical demonstration"). External corroboration: a manuscript copy of Maestlin's treatise (with the Kassel observations) was forwarded to Tycho in 1579 by Paul Hainzel (Mosley, *Bearing the Heavens*, p. ~ on the 1579 forwarding).
- ***WILLERUS*** = **Georg Willer**, the Augsburg bookseller/publisher of the Frankfurt–Augsburg fair catalogues — the channel through which Wolf would normally have obtained newly-printed comet tracts quickly.
- ***Dominus PAULUS HAINZELIUS*** = **Paul Hainzel** (Hainzelius), Augsburg patrician and patron of astronomy (with whom Tycho built a large quadrant at Göppingen in 1569); here Tycho's source for the German comet literature and the addressee of a fuller technical letter (*ut latius ad Dominum HAINZELIUM perscripsi*).
- **Astronomy (technical).** *Apogei … anticipatione* → "anticipation of the apogee" (*apogaeum* → **apogee**,); *Excentricitatis Solis augmento* → "augmentation of the Sun's **eccentricity**"; *octavae Sphaerae … promotione* → "advancement of the **eighth sphere**" (the sphere of the fixed stars; its motion — precession/trepidation — here said to be swifter than Copernicus reckons); *motibus coelestium corporum* → "the motions of the heavenly bodies"; *restituendis et corrigendis motibus* → "restoring and correcting the motions," Tycho's *instauratio*/restoration programme. *COPERNICUS* = **Nicolaus Copernicus**.
- ***limitibus ad instrumenta metallica … conficienda instructus*** — *limites* here in the sense of "means / resources / wherewithal" for making large precision metal instruments; rendered "the means [limits]" with the literal kept in brackets, since the word is slightly strained. The whole clause anticipates Tycho's own instrument programme (*instrumenta … magnitudine et habilitate et diligenti elaboratione*, "in magnitude, handiness, and careful workmanship") — the *Mechanica* lexicon: *instrumenta* → **instruments**.
- ***Ephemerides*** — "ephemerides" (astronomical tables); kept as the technical term.
- **Building / Uraniborg.** *aedificatio*, *aedificationum molestias* → "the building" and "the troubles of the building-works" (the construction of Uraniborg, begun 1576); *oeconomiae novae instituendae molestias* → "the troubles of setting up a new household/economy" (the island establishment). *Aedificationis … structuram ita adornavi, ut his utendis sideribusque … observandis … competat* → the building purpose-built for observation — an early statement of Uraniborg's design rationale.
- ***Μ. ANDREAS SEVERINI*** = **Anders Sørensen Vedel** (Andreas Severini Vellejus, 1542–1616), the Danish historian and Tycho's close friend; *Μ.* = Greek-letter abbreviation for *Magister* ("Master," academic). His planned German tour to "survey certain Libraries" (*lustrandi quasdam in Germania Bibliothecas*) — including a visit to Wolf at **Augsburg** (*Augustam … ad vos*) — is the occasion of the letter: a letter of introduction. The closing pun *te non solum TYCHONIS, sed eius insuper amici amicum esse* ("the friend not only of Tycho, but of Tycho's friend") is kept.
- **Greek letter.** *Μ.* (capital Greek Mu) stands for the Latin *Magister*; transcribed as printed in the source block, expanded as "Master" in the translation.
- **Salutation / subscription.** Opening *S.* = *salutem (dicit)* → "Greeting". Close: *Bene vale* → "Fare you well"; *Iterum … vale* → "Again … farewell"; *quam felicissime et diutissime* rendered "as happily and as long-livedly as may be," preserving the doubled superlative flourish. Subscription *T. / Tycho Brahe* kept.
- **Textual crux (minor).** Near the close the source reads *quin intellifas* — an evident misprint/scribal slip for *quin intelligas* ("but that you may understand"); translated as *intelligas*, the printed form retained in the source block by this chapter's convention(2). Likewise *publicârunt* (circumflex) = *publicaverunt*; *MAeSTLINI*, *DIVINAe*, *REDDITAe* preserve the printed *Ae* ligature-capital.
- **Correction.** Latin corrected from 'limitibus' to 'sumtibus' per Dreyer, TBOO VII p.52; English's bracketed hedge '[limits]', tied to the corrupted reading, removed accordingly ('the means' alone already conveys 'sumtibus').

translation.warrant:
Collated against **Dreyer, *Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia*** (the edition of record), reading the printed page images. the edition gives a page reference so this letter was collated, not defaulted to B. Dreyer TBOO VII pp.52-53 read as page images: the closing 'Datae in Insula nostra Huaena 1579' correctly carries no day-number, matching Dreyer's own undated close (no fabricated day found, consistent with the letter's genuinely partial dating). One text error found ('limitibus' for Dreyer's 'sumtibus'), which forces grade Possible notwithstanding the translator's honest bracketed hedge. This supersedes the translator's own the published grade of B, which was apparently assigned without collation.

**1 defect found:**
- **text error** (low). The transcribed original prints 'limitibus' (limits) where Dreyer prints 'sumtibus' (sumptibus, 'at [his own] expense') — the only reading that makes grammatical sense. The published English hedges honestly with 'the means [limits]', reflecting the corrupted source rather than inventing anything. Dreyer prints: *si sumtibus ad instrumenta metallica magna et exquisita conficienda instructus esset (TBOO VII p.52)*.

**Repaired.** Collated the single defect against the Dreyer page image (TBOO VII p.52), which clearly reads 'si fumtibus ad instrumenta metallica magna et exquifita conficienda instructus effet'. Both the Latin and the English hedge that had reflected the corruption were updated in step. No uncertainty remains in this letter.

documents.incipit: NIHIL sane opus erat, amantissime mi TYCHO, tam accurata apud me de intermissione …
documents.editorial_note: **Text recovered.** The postscript or enclosure, missing from the first transcription, has been restored from the text of record and translated. The Source and English columns below are now complete.

text.original:
PAULUS HAINTZELIUS AD TYCHONEM BRAHE.

NIHIL sane opus erat, amantissime mi TYCHO, tam accurata apud me de intermissione literarum excusatione uti, cum tu me eiusdem negligentiae accusare possis. Verum cum nec ipse tu, quanta ex Latini sermonis paupertate laborem, ignores, et egomet mihi plane sim conscius, quanta difficultate, praesertim ad homines doctos, tuique similes scribam, ne mirere, si vel rariores, vel breviores, quam expectas a me, tibi reddantur. Nisi enim habeam, quod vel te scire tua vel utriusque nostrum intersit, nihil est, quod a me expectes. Illud saltem cave, ne propterea quicquam de meo erga te amore detractum suspicere. De me, mearumque rerum statu scias, me, Dei omnipotentis beneficio, cum tota familia recte valere, filioque (ab hinc anno secundo, nimirum 1577, mense Septembri die 14, hora forte 7 3/4 post meridiem) auctum esse; reliqua veteri adhuc loco sita sunt, nisi quod praeterito anno filiam meam ELIZABETHAM, maiorem natu, cum iuvene huius urbis (cui nomen est MELCHIORI IENISCH) despondi, quorum nuptiae die 13. mensis Octobris, quod felix faustumque sit, celebratae sunt, cum tuae mihi plenae humanitatis literae iam ante mensem essent redditae, quibus ego quod in hunc usque diem non respondi, non mea, sed eius, qui tuas mihi reddidit, culpa factum est. Is namque me inscio hinc discessit, et sine meis literis, secus quam promiserat, ad vos redijt, cuius rei optimus mihi testis esse potest LAURENTIUS, hospes tuus.

Observationes Cometae, quas a me petis, ego sane nullas feci, cum nulla idonea ad observandum instrumenta nunc habeam. Aliorum vero observationes et scripta, quae passim in Germania et alibi de hoc Cometa publicata sunt et ad nos pervenerunt, tibique transmitti expetis (quorum certe magnus est numerus) eorum ego tibi aliquot unâ mitto. Sed mehercule non magnopere lectione, et quae tanto itineris spatio perferantur, digna sunt, exceptis observationibus M. MICHÆLIS MÆSTLINI, CORNELIJ GEMMAe Louaniensis, et ELISÆI RŒSLINI, qui eundem Cometam (quemadmodum etiam tu existimas) non in Elementari, sed in Aetherea mundi regione situm atque generatum esse, certis demonstrationibus testantur, eiusque verum locum, motum, magnitudinem, apparitionem et exstinctionem commonstrare videntur. Sed THADÆI HAGECIJ eiusdem Cometae descriptio, et Landgravij diligens observatio, modo rite in calculum adhibita sit, longe diversum ab illorum et tua opinione et sententia statuunt atque sentiunt. MICHÆLIS MÆSTLINI Epistolas ad Dn. HIERONYMUM WOLFIUM scriptas, et ex his excerpta, item Landgravij observationem, si modo genuina est, hîc unâ mitto. His doctissime, humanissimeque mi TYCHO, valeas, et me, sive loquentem tecum per literas, sive etiam tacentem, manere tamen semper in eodem amore et benevolentia erga te tibi plane persuasum habeas. IOHANNES BAPTISTA, frater meus, salutem tibi plurimam hîc referri voluit.

Iterum etiam atque etiam vale.
Dabantur Augustae 25. Martii An. 79.
T.
Paulus Haintzel.

Has saltem optimæ recordationis viri Pauli Haintzelij, Consulis Augustani,
Astronomicarum rerum amantissimi, in cuius etiam horto Quadrantem illum maximum,
cuius alias in meis scriptis fit mentio, extruximus, ternas saltem apponere
licuit literas, licet plures ad me dederit, quæ perierunt, uti etiam nullum
responsum inter chartas meas reperio eorum, quæ ad ipsum scripsi.
text.english:
**Paul Hainzel to Tycho Brahe.**

There was surely no need, my most loving Tycho, to make so careful an excuse to me for the interruption of letters, since you could charge me with the same negligence. But since neither are you yourself unaware how greatly I labour under a poverty of the Latin tongue, and I am for my part fully conscious with what difficulty I write — especially to learned men, and to your like — do not wonder if [my letters] are delivered to you either rarer or briefer than you expect from me. For unless I have something that it concerns either you to know in your interest or both of us, there is nothing for you to expect from me. Only beware of this: do not on that account suspect that anything has been subtracted from my love toward you. As for myself and the state of my affairs, know that I, by the favour of Almighty God, am well together with my whole household, and have been increased by a son (two years ago from now, namely 1577, in the month of September, on the 14th day, at about 7¾ o'clock in the afternoon); the rest still stand in their old place, save that last year I betrothed my elder daughter Elizabeth to a young man of this city (whose name is Melchior Jenisch), whose wedding — may it be happy and auspicious — was celebrated on the 13th day of the month of October, at a time when your letter full of kindness had already a month before been delivered to me; and that I have not until this very day answered it has come about through no fault of mine, but of him who delivered yours to me. For he departed hence without my knowledge, and returned to you without my letters, otherwise than he had promised — of which matter Lorenz, your host, can be my best witness.

The observations of the comet which you ask of me, I have indeed made none, since I now have no instruments suitable for observing. But of others' observations and writings, which have been published here and there in Germany and elsewhere about this comet and have reached us, and which you desire to be sent on to you (of which the number is certainly great), I send you some along [with this]. But, by Hercules, they are not greatly worth reading, nor worth being conveyed over so great a stretch of road, save for the observations of Master Michael Maestlin, of Cornelius Gemma of Louvain, and of Elisaeus Roeslin, who attest by sure demonstrations that this same comet (as you too judge) was situated and generated not in the elementary but in the aethereal region of the world, and who seem to show forth its true place, motion, magnitude, appearance, and extinction. But Thaddaeus Hagecius's description of the same comet, and the Landgrave's careful observation, provided it has been duly brought into the reckoning, establish and hold something far different from both their opinion and judgement and your own. The letters of Michael Maestlin written to Master Hieronymus Wolf, and excerpts from them, likewise the Landgrave's observation, if only it is genuine, I send here along [with this]. With these, my most learned and most kind Tycho, may you fare well, and hold yourself fully persuaded that I — whether speaking with you by letter, or even keeping silent — nonetheless remain always in the same love and goodwill toward you. Johann Baptist, my brother, wished his heartiest greeting to be conveyed to you here.

Again, and again and again, farewell.
Given at Augsburg, 25 March, the year [15]79.
Yours,
Paul Hainzel.

These letters, at least, of Paul Hainzel — a man of most blessed memory, Consul of Augsburg, most devoted to astronomical matters, in whose garden, too, we erected that greatest Quadrant, of which mention is made elsewhere in my writings — these three letters at least it has been possible to append, although he gave more to me, which have perished; just as, likewise, I find no reply among my papers to those things which I wrote to him.

documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent.** *Paulus Haintzelius* = **Paul Hainzel** (1527–1581), patrician of Augsburg, sometime *Stadtpfleger* (city magistrate), patron of astronomy. With him Tycho had built the great 19-foot quadrant at Göppingen in 1569 (see the Wolf letter of 13 Nov. 1571, where the two Hainzel brothers are named). The closing salutation from *Iohannes Baptista, frater meus* identifies **Johann Baptist Hainzel**, his brother.
- ***Latini sermonis paupertate*** — "a poverty of the Latin tongue": Hainzel's self-deprecation about his Latinity; kept literal. (The Latin is in fact competent but heavily Ciceronian-periodic.)
- **The son's birth.** *filioque … nimirum 1577, mense Septembri die 14, hora forte 7 3/4 post meridiem* — a horoscopic-precision timestamp ("on 14 September 1577, at about 7¾ o'clock in the afternoon"), given to a quarter-hour for the casting of a nativity. *forte* ("about / perhaps") is the author's own hedge on the hour and is preserved, not sharpened. *post meridiem* = "in the afternoon / p.m." (O.S.).
- **The daughter's betrothal.** *filiam meam Elizabetham … cum iuvene huius urbis (cui nomen est Melchiori Ienisch)* — **Elizabeth Hainzel**, betrothed to **Melchior Jenisch** of Augsburg; the wedding *die 13. mensis Octobris* (13 October [1578], the "last year" of *praeterito anno*). *quod felix faustumque sit* — "may it be happy and auspicious," the formulaic Roman nuptial blessing, kept as a parenthetical wish.
- ***Laurentius, hospes tuus*** — "Lorenz, your host": a person (otherwise unidentified here) who had lodged Tycho or acted as his host/agent at Augsburg, blamed for failing to carry Hainzel's reply. *hospes* = "host" (one who gives lodging), not "guest" in this context.
- **The comet.** *hoc Cometa* = the **Great Comet of 1577**, the central observational event of these years and the subject of Tycho's *De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis* (1588). The whole second paragraph concerns the dossier of printed comet-tracts Hainzel is forwarding to Hven.
- ***instrumenta*** → **instruments**; Hainzel pleads he has none fit for observing.
- **The cosmological crux of the comet.** *non in Elementari, sed in Aetherea mundi regione situm atque generatum* — "situated and generated not in the elementary but in the aethereal region of the world": the decisive claim that the comet lay **above the Moon**, in the aether, not in the sublunary (elementary) sphere — the supralunary thesis Tycho himself championed (*quemadmodum etiam tu existimas*, "as you too judge"). *verum locum, motum, magnitudinem, apparitionem et exstinctionem* rendered "true place, motion, magnitude, appearance, and extinction" (the comet's first appearance and its fading-out).
- **The observers named.**
 - *M. Michaelis Maestlini* = **Michael Maestlin** (1550–1631), then at Tübingen, later Kepler's teacher; his *Observatio et demonstratio cometae* (1578) placed the comet supralunary. *M.* = *Magister* (academic "Master").
 - *Cornelij Gemmae Louaniensis* = **Cornelius Gemma** (1535–1578) of **Louvain** (son of Gemma Frisius), who likewise treated the 1577 comet in his *De prodigiosa specie naturaque cometae* (1578).
 - *Elisaei Roeslini* = **Helisaeus Röslin** (1545–1616), physician and astronomer of Alsace, author of a 1578 *Theoria nova coelestium* on the comet.
 - *Thadaei Hagecij* = **Tadeáš Hájek z Hájku** (Thaddaeus Hagecius, 1525–1600), imperial physician at Prague, whose *Descriptio cometae* (1578) Tycho prized; here said to reach a conclusion *longe diversum* ("far different") from the supralunary trio and from Tycho.
 - *Landgravij … observatio* = the observation of the **Landgrave** — Wilhelm IV of Hesse-Kassel — whose value Hainzel guards twice with explicit hedges: *modo rite in calculum adhibita sit* ("provided it has been duly brought into the reckoning") and *si modo genuina est* ("if only it is genuine"). Both qualifiers are preserved.
- ***mehercule*** — "by Hercules," a mild classical oath of asseveration; kept.
- ***Dn.*** = *Dominus*, "Master / Lord", of **Hieronymus Wolf** (Hieronymus Wolfius), the Augsburg humanist (1516–1580) and Tycho's correspondent — recipient of Maestlin's letters that Hainzel forwards.
- **Closing formulae.** *Iterum etiam atque etiam vale* — "Again, and again and again, farewell" (an emphatic reduplication of the *Vale* formula); *salutem tibi plurimam … referri voluit* rendered "wished his heartiest greeting to be conveyed to you".
- **Dateline.** *Dabantur Augustae 25. Martii An. 79* = "Given at **Augsburg** (Augusta Vindelicorum), 25 March, the year [15]79" (O.S.). The dateline agrees with the catalogue label (*1579. 25. marts. Augsburg*); no date discrepancy. *Dabantur* (lit. "they were being given," the epistolary plural for the act of dispatch) rendered idiomatically "Given."
- **What this is — a genre shift, not a continuation.** This recovered segment is *not* part of Hainzel's 1579 letter itself (whose actual close the published tail already gives, signed "Paulus Haintzel"). It is Tycho's own **editorial headnote**, written in the first person about Hainzel in the third person and in the past tense ("optimae recordationis" — "of blessed/cherished memory", the formula for the deceased), evidently composed when Tycho later assembled this group of letters for his letter-book. A reader could otherwise mistake it for Hainzel continuing to speak of himself, which the content rules out.
- **What it documents.** Tycho states plainly that only three of Hainzel's letters to him survived to be included, although Hainzel had sent more, now lost — and that he could find no drafts or copies of his own replies among his papers. This is a rare piece of direct evidence for the *compilation history* of Tycho's own letter-collection: an admission of gaps, not a claim of completeness.
- **Paul Hainzel identified.** Paul Hainzel, patrician and Consul (alderman) of Augsburg, a keen amateur astronomer; in his garden outside the city Tycho built the celebrated "great Quadrant of Augsburg" (1570, radius roughly 543 cm/about 19 feet, the largest instrument Tycho ever built), which Hainzel had commissioned and later undertook to see completed; Hainzel also gave Tycho a newly built sextant. The instrument stood until wrecked by a storm around 1575 and was never repaired [Dreyer, *Tycho Brahe* (Edinburgh, 1890); Christianson, *Tycho Brahe and the Measure of the Heavens* (2020); corroborated by Wennberg, *Tänk, om det är så!*, on the quadrant's dimensions and site]. "Consulis Augustani" in the source matches the title given him in the *Progymnasmata*'s account of the 1572 nova observations.
- **Dating implication.** Because the headnote refers to Hainzel as already deceased, it must postdate his death — meaning the note is a later addition to this 1579 letter, not contemporary with it; the works consulted here do not give an exact death year for Hainzel, so this remains a lead rather than a settled fact.
- **Correction.** Restored the valediction abbreviation 'T.' (Tuus, 'Yours') on its own line above the signature, dropped from our transcribed original and consequently from the translation, per Dreyer, Opera Omnia VII p.50.

text.original:
HIERONYMUS WOLFIUS AD TYCHONEM BRAHE.

EADEM Tabellarij fortuna, TYCHO nobilissime, amice colende, hîc sumus usi, qua tua præstantia. Nam Aurifaber ille, qui tuas reddiderat, hinc abijt. Quis literulas sit perlaturus, nescio, sed sub vesperam demum mihi nuntiatum est, ut rescriberem. Itaque cogor esse brevior et ob temporis brevitatem et propter diem festum. Absentibus WILLERI ministris non possum parare libellos nostrorum, qui de atrocissimo illo Cometa, quem unquam vidi, scripserunt. Et sane puto nec Tabellarium grandiusculos libellos perlaturum et quæ tu elaborâris, propediem nos accepturos. Quæ autem de amplitudine vestræ regionis et fortitudine gentis scribis, satis nota nobis sunt, et Cimbros, Ambrones et Teutones a Martha C. MARIJ maga potius, quam a Romanis esse victos arbitramur. Linguam vero vestram ijs ornavit et antiquitatis et proprietatis et copiæ laudibus IO. GOROPIUS, ut eam vel Hebrææ anteponat, nedum Latinæ et Græcæ. Itaque si hîc esses, Cimbrice a te disceremus. Sed fortasse nobis ætas obstaret, quo minus essemus dociles. Nam mortuo adhibere medicinam, et docere senem idem esse Græco proverbio dicitur. Me quidem senectus et pigrum et obliviosum facit, et multipliciter tam corpus quam animum affligit. Quomodo autem me contra eam, tanquam morbum incurabilem muniam, non video, præsertim deficiente hîc vino bono et incorrupto, quo solo tanquam antidoto moderate sumto uti soleo contra tam invictum hostem, uti scis meum morem. Quare sive me hîc enneaticus climacter, ὁ ἀνδροδάμας, sustulerit, sive 66to tollendum reliquerit: susque deque fero, modo CHRISTUS Servator in Palatio sui patris parvulam aliquam cellulam assignet, in qua beate et æternum requiescam, quod ita fore clementia divina fretus confido.

Respublica nostra in eo statu adhuc est, quem hinc discedens reliquisti. HAINZELIUS filius nuper a me uxoris suæ Genesin confici voluit, cum ego respondi, D. TYCHONEM id in melius præstare posse, si vellet. Sed sane dubito, an velles, cum hîc in talibus difficilimus fueris. Isti homines affectibus suis indulgentes, succensent Astrologis et vera et falsa dicentibus. Itaque Tiresias soli Apollini vaticinandum esse dixit apud SOPHOCLEM, qui hominis indignationem, quippe Deus negligat. Eclipsin Solis in ♓ hîc vidimus pene integram, in qua et CYPRIANUS, sed minus tamen quam COPERNICUS aberravit. Cuius Ephemeridas MICHÆL MÆSTLINUS instrumentis cœlo uti opinor adhibitis ab anno 1577 usque ad annum 1588 correctiores se esse editurum mihi pollicetur, nisi Typographus in mora sibi sit. Sed iam manum de tabula. Nam advesperascit et rhabarbarum scriptionem meam interpellat, quo uti sæpius contra Ischiadem et Chiragram cogor. Tuam vero Excellentiam et valere et florere omni bonorum genere ex animo et spero et opto.

Vale.
25. Martij Anno 1579.
text.english:
**Hieronymus Wolf to Tycho Brahe.**

The same fortune with the courier, most noble Tycho, friend to be honoured, have we had here as did your eminence [in writing to me]. For that goldsmith who had delivered your [letters] has gone away from here. Who is to carry these few lines I do not know, but it was only towards evening that word was brought to me that I should write back. And so I am forced to be rather brief, both because of the shortness of time and on account of the feast-day. The servants of Willer being absent, I cannot procure the little books of our people who have written about that most dreadful comet, the [worst] I ever saw. And indeed I think both that the courier will not carry the bulkier little books, and that we shall shortly receive what you have worked out. As for what you write about the extent of your country and the valour of its people, these are well enough known to us; and we hold that the Cimbri, Ambrones, and Teutones were vanquished rather by the sorceress Martha of C[aius] Marius than by the Romans. Your tongue, indeed, Jo. Goropius has adorned with such praises of antiquity, of distinctive character, and of richness, that he sets it even before Hebrew, let alone before Latin and Greek. And so, if you were here, we should learn Cimbric from you. But perhaps our age would stand in the way, so that we should be the less teachable. For to apply medicine to a dead man, and to teach an old man, are said by a Greek proverb to be one and the same thing. Old age, for my part, makes me both sluggish and forgetful, and afflicts in many ways my body as much as my mind. But how I am to fortify myself against it, as against an incurable disease, I do not see — especially when there is lacking here good and unspoiled wine, which alone, as a kind of antidote taken in moderation, I am wont to use against so unconquered an enemy, as you know my custom to be. Wherefore, whether the ninefold climacteric, ὁ ἀνδροδάμας [the man-tamer], shall here have carried me off, or shall have left me to be carried off in my sixty-sixth [year]: I make light of it, provided that Christ the Saviour assign me some little cell in his Father's palace, in which I may rest blessedly and for ever — which, relying on the divine clemency, I am confident will be so.

Our commonwealth is still in the state in which you left it on departing hence. Hainzel the son lately wished his wife's geniture to be drawn up by me, whereupon I replied that Master Tycho could do it better, if he were willing. But I much doubt whether you would be willing, since you were here most difficult in such matters. Those men, indulging their own passions, are angry at astrologers whether they speak the truth or falsehoods. And so Tiresias in Sophocles said that Apollo alone ought to prophesy — he who [being a god] disregards a man's indignation, since he is a god. We saw here the eclipse of the Sun in ♓ Pisces almost total, in which both Cyprian [Leovitius] went astray, yet less so than Copernicus. Michael Maestlin promises me that he will publish ephemerides of the latter, corrected — by using instruments applied to the sky, I suppose — from the year 1577 to the year 1588, unless the printer prove a hindrance to him. But now [I take] my hand from the tablet. For evening draws on, and the rhubarb interrupts my writing, which I am rather often compelled to use against sciatica and gout of the hand. But that Your Excellency may both fare well and flourish in every kind of good things, I both hope and wish from my heart.

Farewell.
25 March, the year 1579.

documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent.** *Hieronymus Wolfius* = **Hieronymus Wolf** (1516–1580), the Augsburg humanist and Greek scholar ("father of Byzantine studies"), librarian of the Fugger collection and rector of the Augsburg gymnasium; a mentor-friend of Tycho's from his Augsburg years. This letter, written within a year of Wolf's death, continues the correspondence whose 1571 instalment (brahe-t_15711113001) shares the same Vienna manuscript volume. The valediction (*Vale*) and the brevity reflect the haste he describes.
- **Heading / register.** *HIERONYMUS WOLFIUS AD TYCHONEM BRAHE* is the editor's letter-rubric, not a salutation formula; rendered literally. *amice colende* = "friend to be honoured," the courtesy register kept. *Excellentia Tua* = "Your Excellency."
- ***Tabellarius*** — "courier/letter-carrier"; the practical difficulty of finding a bearer frames the whole letter. *Aurifaber ille* — "that goldsmith," the previous (unnamed) carrier of Tycho's letters.
- ***WILLERI ministris*** — "the servants of Willer": **Georg Willer**, the prominent Augsburg bookseller-publisher (issuer of the Frankfurt/Augsburg fair catalogues); Wolf cannot obtain the printed pamphlets on the comet because Willer's staff are away.
- ***atrocissimo illo Cometa*** — "that most dreadful comet": the **great comet of 1577**, the object of Tycho's parallax work and of the contemporary German pamphlet literature Wolf wishes to send. *quem unquam vidi* is elliptical ("[the worst] I ever saw"); the implied superlative is supplied in [brackets].
- **The Cimbri allusion.** Wolf answers Tycho's evident pride in his homeland (*amplitudine vestrae regionis et fortitudine gentis*, "the extent of your country and the valour of its people"). *Cimbros, Ambrones et Teutones* — the northern tribes annihilated by **Gaius Marius** (*C. Marii*) at Aquae Sextiae and Vercellae (102–101 BC). *a Martha … maga* — "by the sorceress Martha," the Syrian prophetess Marius reputedly kept in his camp (Plutarch, *Marius* 17); Wolf wittily credits her divination rather than Roman arms. The Cimbri were popularly identified with the Danish Cimbric peninsula (Jutland), hence the local-patriotic point.
- ***IO. GOROPIUS*** — **Johannes Goropius Becanus** (Jan van Gorp, 1519–1573), the Antwerp physician-etymologist whose *Origines Antwerpianae* (1569) argued that the Cimbric / "Brabantic" tongue was the oldest language of mankind, older even than Hebrew — the doctrine Wolf alludes to (*vel Hebraeae anteponat*) with evident irony. *Cimbrice … disceremus* — "we should learn Cimbric [from you]," i.e. Danish.
- **The Greek proverb.** *mortuo adhibere medicinam, et docere senem* — "to physic a dead man and to teach an old man [are one and the same]," rendering a Greek commonplace (cf. the proverb γέροντα μὴ παίδευε, "do not instruct an old man"); Wolf paraphrases it in Latin and ascribes it to "a Greek proverb."
- **Wine as remedy.** *vino bono … tanquam antidoto … contra tam invictum hostem* — wine as his "antidote" against the "unconquered enemy" of old age; the self-deprecating tone (drinking *moderate*, "in moderation") is preserved, not sharpened.
- **The climacteric / Greek.** *enneaticus climacter* = "the ninefold (ennead) climacteric," the astrologically critical year reckoned by nines (here Wolf, aged about 62–63, faces his 63rd — the *grand* climacteric, 7 × 9); *ὁ ἀνδροδάμας* = "the man-tamer / man-subduer," a stock epithet of the dangerous climacteric year (lit. *andro-* "man" + *damáō* "to tame, subdue"). The Greek is transcribed verbatim and glossed in [brackets]; *climacter* kept by this chapter's convention (*annus climactericus* → **climacteric year**). *sive 66to tollendum reliquerit* — "or shall have left [me] to be carried off in my sixty-sixth [year]"; *66to* = *sexagesimo sexto* (ordinal abbreviation), expanded in the sense.
- ***in Palatio sui patris parvulam aliquam cellulam*** — "some little cell in his Father's palace," echoing John 14:2 (*in domo Patris mei mansiones multae sunt*); the consolatory religious turn is kept.
- ***HAINZELIUS filius*** — "Hainzel the son": one of the **Hainzel brothers** of Augsburg (Johann Baptist and Paul Hainzel, the patrician patrons of astronomy with whom Tycho built his 1569 quadrant); here a younger Hainzel asks for his wife's nativity. *Genesin … in melius praestare* = "to draw up the geniture better" (*Genesis* → **geniture**,). *difficilimus* (for *difficillimus*) — "most difficult/reluctant," Wolf recalling Tycho's reluctance over such commissions.
- **The Sophocles allusion.** *Tiresias … apud SOPHOCLEM* — Wolf cites **Sophocles** (the seer Tiresias, *Oedipus Tyrannus* / *Antigone*) for the maxim that prophecy belongs to Apollo alone, "who, being a god, disregards a man's indignation." The syntax is compressed: *qui hominis indignationem, quippe Deus negligat* is read "[Apollo,] who being a god disregards a man's indignation"; the somewhat elliptical clause is rendered with that supplement and flagged here rather than smoothed.
- **Astronomy.** *Eclipsin Solis in ♓ … pene integram* = "the solar eclipse in Pisces almost total" — the partial solar eclipse observed at Augsburg; the glyph ♓ is kept in the source and named **Pisces** in the translation. *eclipsis (Solis)* → **eclipse (solar)**. *in qua et CYPRIANUS, sed minus tamen quam COPERNICUS aberravit* — "in [predicting] which both **Cyprian [Leovitius]** (Cyprianus Leovitius, 1524–1574, the astrologer whose tables Wolf used) erred, yet less than **Copernicus**" — i.e. the eclipse showed the received computations astray.
- ***MICHAeL MAeSTLINUS*** — **Michael Maestlin** (1550–1631), the Tübingen astronomer (later Kepler's teacher), whose published *Ephemerides* affirmed the superiority of the Copernican hypotheses, citing the 1577 comet as evidence (so Gingerich, *Annotated Census*). *Ephemeridas … ab anno 1577 usque ad annum 1588 correctiores* = "corrected ephemerides from 1577 to 1588." *instrumentis coelo … adhibitis* — "by instruments applied to the sky," i.e. derived from observation; *opinor* ("I suppose") is Wolf's own hedge and is preserved. *Typographus* = the printer.
- ***manum de tabula*** — "[I take] my hand from the tablet/board," a proverbial "I'll stop here" (cf. Pliny / Cicero); the elliptical idiom kept, *[I take]* bracketed as supplied.
- **Medicine.** *rhabarbarum* = **rhubarb** (the purgative root); *Ischias / Ischiadem* = **sciatica**; *Chiragra* = **gout of the hand (chiragra)** — the same complaint as in the 1571 letter; both period terms glossed.
- **Dateline / calendar.** *25. Martij Anno 1579* = "25 March 1579." No place is named in the dateline; the witness and content place it at **Augsburg** (*Augusta Vindelicorum*), and the catalogue label confirms it. The label *"1579. 25. marts. (Augsburg)"* agrees with the dateline. **Style:** O.S. (Julian); the Gregorian reform was still three years off, and Lutheran Augsburg in any case retained the Julian calendar until 1700. No in-letter date discrepancy. *propter diem festum* — "on account of the feast-day": 25 March is the Feast of the Annunciation (Lady Day), the festival to which Wolf's apology for brevity refers.

text.original:
A. WELLEIO CONCIONATORI REGIS. SALUTEM IN SALVATORE.

ACCEPI literas tuas, dilecte M. ANDREA, et de equo minus bene vidente D. I. FRANCISCI (cæcum ne appellem, multis deierationibus absterremur) intellexi: qui [quoniam] est vir benevolus et nobis Amicus, eum non denegat sed sponte offert sive venalem, sive commutabilem; ego ubi artificium molæ nostræ, in quo eo uti vellem, paratum fuerit, cum eo de hoc agam, si proprijs equis uti non licuerit, eo quod eo dono destituantur, quo suum etiam carere mallet. Agas itaque ipsi interea meo nomine gratias. De istius vafri hominis perfidia, qui sponte oblatam reconciliationem callide aversatur, ut impune sibi per Legati adventum famam meam læsisse consultum sit, nihil dicam, donec vir ille opt. et æquus adveneri, cuius etiam arbitrio primum stabo, an æquum sit me ista immerito ab eo pati et per civitatem ab ijs, quibus nihil mali volui, sed ab his passus sum, defamari. Quid Hessus iste dicat et quam gratiam referat, nihil curo, cum non alia ab eo exspectârim unquam, neque ob id medicinam conficiam, quod vel gratiam vel lucrum inde sperem ullum, miror saltem eousque Christianismi institutionem pervenisse, ut Magistratus ipse gloriari audeat, a membris Satanæ opem, quam ferre nequeunt, allatam sibi esse, posthabitis Dei auxilio et ab ipso ordinatis medijs. O Doctores, o Discipuli. De Curia ista quæ ad nos pertinet in Angulo Civitatis Matri, ut consuluisti, scripsi, ab ea brevi responsum expecto, quod ubi nactus fuero, modo ex votis nostris contigerit, cum CHRISTIERNO URUP præsens, ubi Haffniam advenero, agam; effice interea apud ipsum, ne curiam suam prius alteri divendat. Controversiam, quæ inter Fratrem meum et BLESSIUM istum incidit, nondum a quoquam intellexi, felicior enim sum in hac Insula, quam quod plurimas mundanæ fabulæ nugas, hominumque Eccentricitates sæpius cum molestia exauditas doleam. Velim tamen ut me de isto negotio certiorem reddas, siquidem Fratris mei magnopere interesse ex te intelligo. Vale et significa quando Iohannes Patri redierit. Iterum vale et saluta Mag. LAURENTIUM Amicum communem meo nomine plurimum.

Datæ Huennæ 21. Maij Anno 79.
T.
TYCHO BRAHE.

Mitto tibi Catalogum librorum Francofurtensium et peto ut BALTHAZARO significari curare velis, ut eos libros quos
lineola in margine notavi, quamprimum licuerit, mihi procurare velit. Sunt
autem novem Latini, tres Germanici et unus Gallicus. Remitto tibi 8
Ioachimicos per hunc CHRISTIERNUM piscium mercatorem, pro quibus ago gratias.
Iterum vale.
text.english:
**To [Anders] Vedel, the King's preacher. Greeting in the Saviour.**

I have received your letter, beloved Master Anders, and have learned about the not-well-seeing horse of Master J. Franciscus (we are deterred from calling it blind by his many oaths): since he is a kindly man and a friend to us, he does not refuse it but freely offers it, whether to be sold or to be exchanged. When the mechanism of our mill, in which I should wish to use it, is ready, I shall treat with him about this — if it shall not prove possible to use my own horses, on the ground that they are without that endowment which he too would prefer his own [horse] to lack. So in the meanwhile give him thanks in my name. Of the treachery of that crafty man, who cunningly turns away from a reconciliation freely offered him, so that he might have contrived to injure my good name with impunity through the coming of the Legate, I shall say nothing, until that excellent and fair-minded man shall arrive — to whose judgment, moreover, I shall first submit [the question] whether it be fair that I should undeservedly suffer these things from him, and be defamed throughout the city by those toward whom I willed no harm, yet at whose hands I have suffered it. What that Hessian says, and what thanks he returns, I care nothing — since I have never expected anything else from him; nor do I prepare medicine on the ground that I hope for any favour or gain from it. I marvel only that the practice of Christianity has come to such a pass that the Magistrate himself dares to boast that help, which they [the members of Satan] cannot give, has been brought to him by the members of Satan, while God's aid and the means ordained by Him are set aside. O [such] Doctors, O [such] Disciples! About that property which belongs to us in the Corner of the city, I have written to [my] Mother, as you advised; I expect a reply from her shortly, and when I have got it — provided it turn out according to our wishes — I shall deal with Christiern Urup in person, when I have come to Copenhagen. See to it meanwhile with him that he does not sell off his property to another beforehand. The dispute that has arisen between my Brother and that Blessius I have not yet learned of from anyone — for I am more fortunate on this Island than that I should have to grieve over the very many trifles of worldly tattle, and the Eccentricities of men, so often and so vexingly heard out. Yet I should like you to inform me about that matter, since I understand from you that it greatly concerns my Brother. Farewell, and let me know when Johannes shall have returned to [his] Father. Again, farewell, and greet warmly in my name Master Laurentius, our common friend.

Given at Hven, 21 May, the year [15]79.
T.
Tycho Brahe.

I send you the Catalogue of the Frankfurt books, and I ask that you see to it that Balthasar be informed, so that he may be willing to procure for me, as soon as it shall have been possible, those books which I have marked with a little line in the margin. There are nine in Latin, three in German, and one in French. I send back to you 8 Joachimsthalers through this Christiern, a fish-merchant, for which I give thanks. Farewell again.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender / recipient.** *Tycho Brahe*, writing from his island of **Hven** (*Huenna*), where building works were under way. The addressee, *A. Welleio* / *M. Andrea* = **Anders Sørensen Vedel** (1542–1616), the historian and royal chaplain, here styled *Concionator Regis* "the King's preacher" — Vedel was preacher at the royal chapel in Copenhagen Castle. A long-standing friend of Tycho's (cf. the 1571 Vedel letter in the pilot).
- **Salutation.** *SALUTEM IN SALVATORE* — "Greeting in the Saviour," a devotional variant of the standard *salutem*, suited to writing to a clergyman.
- **Persons named.**
 - *D. I. FRANCISCI* — "Master J. Franciscus," owner of the horse offered to Tycho; not further identified here. *D.* = *Dominus*, "Master".
 - *Hessus iste* — "that Hessian": rendered as an ethnic/by-name epithet for an adversary in the medical dispute (a man called or from **Hesse(n)**). Whether *Hessus* is a surname or "the Hessian" is not decidable from the text; kept literal and flagged (crux below).
 - *CHRISTIERNO URUP* — **Christiern (Christen) Urup**, a Danish nobleman, owner of an adjoining or desired property ("his property," *curiam suam*) that Tycho wishes to acquire.
 - *BLESSIUM istum* — "that Blessius," a party to a dispute with Tycho's brother; Latinised surname, not securely identified; kept as *Blessius*.
 - *Fratrem meum* / *Fratris mei* — "my Brother": one of Tycho's brothers (most likely **Steen Brahe**, the eldest surviving brother active in Danish affairs), not named in the letter; left unspecified as in the source.
 - *Matri* — "[my] Mother," **Beate Bille**, Tycho's mother (widow of Otte Brahe), whom Tycho must consult about the family property "in the Corner of the city."
 - *Iohannes … Patri* — "Johannes … to [his] Father": a young man (perhaps a student or servant) whose return is awaited; deliberately under-determined in the source ("Father" not further specified).
 - *Mag. LAURENTIUM* — "Master Laurentius," a common friend; *Mag.* = *Magister* (academic "Master,").
 - *Legati adventum* — "the coming of the Legate / envoy": an official whose arrival the "crafty man" hoped to exploit; not identified.
- **Editorial reading.** *qui [quoniam] est vir benevolus* — the bracketed *[quoniam]* ("since") is an editorial supplement carried in the text of record (the relative *qui* is read as causal); kept in brackets in the Source block by this chapter's convention(2), and rendered "since" in the translation.
- **Technical / realia.** *artificium molae nostrae* — "the mechanism (contrivance) of our mill": Tycho's **mill** on Hven (the water-/paper-mill complex he was constructing; the horse was wanted as draught/turning power for the mill works). *Eccentricitates* here is used figuratively, "[men's] eccentricities/oddities," **not** the astronomical *eccentricitas* of the glossary — the same Latin word in a colloquial sense; flagged so a consistency check does not mis-tag it.
- **Medicine / religious-polemic passage.** Tycho defends his practice of preparing *medicina* (Paracelsian/spagyric remedies) against a churchman's charge that such cures come from "the members of Satan." The clause *a membris Satanae opem, quam ferre nequeunt, allatam sibi esse, posthabitis Dei auxilio et ab ipso ordinatis medijs* is reproduced with its full logic: the relative *quam ferre nequeunt* ("which they cannot give") is Tycho's sarcastic aside that the so-called "members of Satan" are precisely unable to furnish such help; *posthabitis … medijs* ("the … means being set aside," ablative absolute) marks what the Magistrate neglects. *O Doctores, o Discipuli* — an exclamatory lament ("O [what] Doctors, O [what] Disciples!"), kept as exclamation.
- **Negation check.** Five operative negations in the body, all preserved one-for-one: *caecum **ne** appellem* ("lest I call it blind"); *eum **non** denegat* ("does **not** refuse it"); *si proprijs equis uti **non** licuerit* ("if it shall **not** prove possible to use my own horses"); *quo suum etiam carere mallet* — the verb *carere* ("to be without/lack") carries privative force, rendered "to lack / be without"; *quibus **nihil** mali volui* ("toward whom I willed **no** harm"); *quam ferre **nequeunt*** ("which they can**not** give"); *medicinam **neque** … conficiam … quod … sperem* ("**nor** do I prepare medicine … on the ground that I hope …"); *ne curiam suam prius alteri divendat* ("that he does **not** sell off his property to another beforehand," negative purpose). None added or dropped.
- **Calendar / place.** *Datae Huennae 21. Maij Anno 79* = "Given at **Hven**, 21 May, [15]79" (**O.S.** — Denmark kept the Julian calendar). The catalogue label agrees with the dateline (1579-05-21, Hven); no discrepancy. *T. / TYCHO BRAHE* — the subscription *T.* is Tycho's initial above his full name.

### Named cruxes
1. ***quo suum etiam carere mallet*** — the clause explaining why Tycho's own horses may not serve: literally "[the endowment] which he [Franciscus] would prefer his own [horse] too to be without." The referent of *eo dono* ("that endowment/gift") is unstated — most plausibly the quality of *sight* (i.e. Tycho's horses, unlike the half-blind offered horse, still **have** the sight that Franciscus would rather his own horse lacked, so that Franciscus is content to part with the defective animal), but the syntax admits other readings (a draught quality wanted for the mill). The text does not decide it; rendered close to the Latin and flagged rather than smoothed.
2. ***Hessus iste*** — surname vs. "the Hessian" undecided (see above).
3. *donec vir ille opt. et aequus **adveneri*** — the form *adveneri* is anomalous (for *advenerit*, future-perfect "shall have arrived"); read as such and so translated; the irregular spelling is left in the Source block.
- **What this is.** A business paragraph preceding the letter's close, showing Tycho using the twice-yearly Frankfurt book-fair catalogue as a live order form: he has marked, by hand, thirteen titles (nine Latin, three German, one French) he wants procured through an intermediary, and is settling an account of 8 Joachimsthalers (Joachimsthaler silver coins, the ancestor of the word "dollar") via a courier.
- **Two named agents, unidentified in the works consulted.** "Balthazaro" — presumably a bookseller or book-buying agent in Vedel's circle, tasked with placing the actual order at Frankfurt — and "Christiernum," described only as "piscium mercatorem" (a fish-merchant), who is here doubling as an informal courier of coin between Hven and Vedel. Neither is corroborated by name among the works consulted; both would repay a dedicated search in the *Tychonis Brahe Opera Omnia* correspondence apparatus or Danish merchant records.
- **Context.** Recipient Anders Sørensen Vedel was Tycho's long-time friend and the Danish royal historiographer; letters between them regularly mix scholarly, financial, and household business in one breath, as here.
- **Coinage note.** "Ioachimicos" = Joachimsthaler, the large silver coin minted from the Joachimsthal mines in Bohemia from 1520, whose name was later clipped to "thaler" and ultimately gave English "dollar" — retained untranslated as a proper coin-name.

documents.abstract: Invites Vedel and the Lord Legate to visit Hven, urging that Laurentius, Doctor Franciscus, Master Ezoccus, and the Royal Treasurer also accompany them.
documents.incipit: DILECTE Magister ANDREA, peto ut iam unâ cum Domino Legato meos lares Huenenses velis …

text.original:
DOCTISSIMO VIRO MAGISTRO ANDREAe SEVERINI WELLEIO, CONCIONATORI IN REGIA HAFFNIENSI, SUO AMICO.
S. P.

DILECTE Magister ANDREA, peto ut iam unâ cum Domino Legato meos lares Huenenses velis invisere prout pollicitus es, et roga meo nomine Dn. Magistrum LAURENTIUM, Amicum nostrum, ut unâ venire velit. Quod si Doctor IOHANNES FRANCISCUS et D. EZOCCUS velint Domino Legato comites esse et ab urbanis molestijs per aliquot dies animum recreare et cum tenui boni consulere, fecerint mihi rem gratam. De Domino Quaestore Regio scripsi Domino Legato. Quod si is me in hac Insula invisere prae negotiis publicis, quibus assidue occupatur, non detrectaverit, fecerit mihi rem gratissimam; non enim diffido ipsum, quamvis pro dignitate et meritis hoc in loco minus sollenniter excipi possit, tamen pro conditione temporis et loci boni consulturum. Vale et significa per puerum meum quid sit futurum.

Iterum vale.
Datae Huenae die 5. Iulij Anno 1579.
T.
Tycho Brahe.
text.english:
**To the most learned man, Master Anders Sørensen Vedel, preacher at the royal residence in Copenhagen, his friend.**
Heartiest greeting.

Beloved Master Anders, I ask that you now, together with the Lord Legate, be willing to visit my home on Hven, just as you promised; and ask in my name our friend Master Laurentius to be willing to come along too. And if Doctor Johannes Franciscus and Master Ezoccus should wish to be the Lord Legate's companions, and for some few days to refresh their minds from the troubles of the city and to take a slender fare in good part, they will have done me a welcome thing. Concerning the Lord Royal Treasurer I have written to the Lord Legate. And if he, despite the public business with which he is constantly occupied, will not decline to visit me on this island, he will have done me a most welcome thing; for I do not doubt that, even though here he can be received less ceremoniously than befits his rank and merits, he will nevertheless take it in good part, according to the circumstance of the time and the place. Farewell, and signify by my boy [the messenger] what is to be.

Again, farewell.
Given at Hven, on the 5th day of July, the year 1579.
Yours,
Tycho Brahe.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe**, writing from his newly-established seat on the island of Hven (Uraniborg, the building of which had begun in 1576). The signature *T. / Tycho Brahe* and the dateline place this firmly in his first years on the island.
- **Recipient.** *Andreas Severini Welleius* = **Anders Sørensen Vedel** (1542–1616), Danish historian, theologian, and ballad-collector, Tycho's close friend (and kinsman by upbringing). The address-line styles him *concionator in regia Hafniensi* — "preacher at the royal residence in Copenhagen," i.e. court chaplain at Copenhagen Castle, the office Vedel then held.
- ***S. P.*** — *salutem plurimam* (sc. *dicit*), "heartiest greeting". *Vale … Iterum vale* — "Farewell … Again, farewell".
- ***lares Huenenses*** — literally "my Hven household gods," a classicising idiom for "my home / hearth on Hven"; rendered "my home on Hven." *Huenae* in the dateline = **Hven** (kept as is by this chapter's convention).
- ***Dominus Legatus*** — "the Lord Legate / Envoy." The honorand of the invitation, evidently a high-ranking official or ambassador then in Copenhagen whom Tycho hopes Vedel will escort to Hven; not named in the letter and not securely identified here — rendered by office, not by a guessed name.
- ***Magister Laurentius*** — "Master Laurentius (Lauritz/Lars)," called *Amicus noster* ("our friend"); a member of Tycho's and Vedel's shared Copenhagen circle. Not further identified in the letter; left in the Latin form with the modern given name flagged.
- ***Doctor Iohannes Franciscus*** and ***D. Ezoccus*** — "Doctor Johannes Franciscus" and "Master Ezoccus," two further members of the party. Neither is securely identifiable from this letter alone; both are left in their epistolary forms (*D.* expanded as *Dominus* = "Master,"). **Crux flagged:** *Ezoccus* is an unusual Latinised form and may be a copyist's spelling in the surviving *Afskrift* (copy); no normalisation is imposed.
- ***Dominus Quaestor Regius*** — "the Lord Royal Treasurer," the crown financial officer (*rentemester* / royal treasurer). Identified here by office only; Tycho says he has written separately to the Legate about him.
- ***cum tenui boni consulere*** / ***boni consulturum*** — the idiom *boni consulere* = "to take (something) in good part, to be content with"; here a courteous self-deprecation about the modest hospitality (*tenui*, "slender [fare/means]") Hven can offer. Rendered "to take a slender fare in good part" / "he will take it in good part," preserving the polite hedge rather than over-translating *tenui* as a specific noun (bracketed sense added only where English requires a head-noun).
- ***per puerum meum*** — "by my boy," i.e. by Tycho's servant/messenger boy; *significa* "signify, send word." Rendered "by my boy [the messenger]," the gloss bracketed.
- ***urbanis molestijs*** — "the troubles of the city" (Copenhagen), contrasted with the rural retreat of Hven; the *-ij-* spelling (*molestijs*) is the period orthography, kept in the source block.
- **Dateline / calendar.** *Datae Huenae die 5. Iulij Anno 1579* = "Given at Hven, 5 July 1579" (O.S.; Denmark kept the Julian calendar). The dateline agrees with the catalogue label (*1579. 5. juli. Hven*); no discrepancy.
- **Edition / witness.** Edition of record: Dreyer, *Opera Omnia* (the *Epistolae* volumes). The sole cited witness is a **copy** (*Afskrift*) in Tycho Brahe's private archive, Rigsarkivet, Copenhagen — so the readings (e.g. *Ezoccus*) descend through a transcript, not an autograph.
- **Correction.** Closing valediction corrected from an expansion of Tycho's own name ('T[ycho].') to its actual sense, the epistolary abbreviation 'Tuus' (Yours) — the same convention used elsewhere in TBOO for this abbreviation.

**1 defect found:**
- **mistranslation** (low). The valediction abbreviation 'T.' immediately above the printed signature 'TYCHO BRAHE' is the standard Latin epistolary abbreviation 'Tuus' (Yours), not an abbreviation of Tycho's own name — the same convention appears elsewhere in TBOO (e.g. Bordingus's letter closes 'T. studiosissimus IACOBUS BORDINGUS' = 'Thy most devoted, Jacob Bording', correctly rendered there). Expanding it as '[Tycho]' produces an odd redundant reading ('T[ycho]. Tycho Brahe.') where the source has a normal 'Yours, Tycho Brahe' closing formula. At: “T[ycho].
Tycho Brahe.”.

documents.abstract: Reminds Dançay of his promise to visit Hven, explains delays caused by travel between Zealand and Scania, and renews the invitation to come with friends.
documents.incipit: MAGNIFICE Domine DANZÆE, Amice semper colende, pollicitus es cum ultimo Haffniae simul …

text.original:
MAGNIFICO ET GENEROSO VIRO DOMINO CAROLO DANZÆO, REGIS GALLIARUM LEGATO ET CONSILIARIO PRUDENTISSIMO, AMICO SUO PERPETUO PLURIMUM OBSERVANDO.

MAGNIFICE Domine DANZÆE, Amice semper colende, pollicitus es cum ultimo Haffniae simul essemus, te Huenenses Lares invisurum, quam primum intelligeres me huc reversum esse, quia vero interea temporis nunc e Selandia in Scaniam, nunc ex hac rursus in illam, partim Regis partim Amicorum negotijs et ex parte etiam proprijs impellentibus iactatus sum tanquam pila missus ab illis, ut noster de aulica senectute dixit PALINGENIUS, adeo ut ante hoc tempus non licuerit nisi aliquantulam requiem hîc figere. Peto itaque ut nunc promissis stare et cum Amicis quoscunque elegeris meas Penates utquamvis pro conditione temporis et loci tenues, tamen ab urbium solenni fastu animum quietis anhelantem nonnihil revocantes invisere non dedigneris. Si Dominus Quaestor Regius comitem se adiungere prae negotijs publicis, quibus occupatur, non detrectaverit, fecerit et is mihi rem gratam. Scripsi M. ANDREAe, quem puto una venturum, secumque M. LAURENTIUM nostrum adducturum. Tuum vero erit quoscunque voles unâ adducere.

Vale.
Datae Huenae 5. Iulii Anno 1579.
T.
Tycho Brahe.
text.english:
**To the magnificent and noble gentleman Master Charles de Dançay, ambassador and most prudent counsellor of the King of France, his perpetual friend, most worthy to be honoured.**

Magnificent Master Dançay, ever to be esteemed friend, you promised, when we were last together at Copenhagen, that you would visit the household of Hven as soon as you should learn that I had returned here; but because in the meantime I have been tossed about — now from Zealand into Scania, now back again from the latter into the former — driven partly by the King's affairs, partly by my friends', and in part by my own, "like a ball flung" by them, as our Palingenius said about old age at court, so much so that until now I have not been able to fix more than a very little rest here. I ask, therefore, that you now stand by your promise, and that you not disdain to visit, together with whatever friends you may choose, my household gods — slender though they are, as befits the condition of the time and place, yet recalling somewhat a mind that pants for quiet from the solemn pomp of the cities. If the Lord Royal Treasurer should not decline to join you as a companion, despite the public affairs with which he is occupied, he will do me too a welcome service. I have written to Master Andreas, who I think will come along, and will bring with him our Master Laurentius. But it will be yours to bring along whomever you wish.

Farewell.
Given at Hven, 5 July, the year 1579.
T[ycho].
Tycho Brahe.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** *Carolus Danzaeus* = **Charles de Dançay** (d. 1589), the long-serving resident ambassador of the King of France (then **Henri III**) at the Danish court — *regis Galliarum legato et consiliario* — and an early friend and supporter of Tycho. The honorific style *magnifico et generoso viro … amico suo perpetuo plurimum observando* is rendered in full by this chapter's convention
- **Author/place.** Written by Tycho from **Hven** (*Huena*; the island granted him by Frederik II in 1576, seat of Uraniborg), inviting Dançay to come over and visit. *Huenenses Lares* / *meas Penates* — literally "the Lares of Hven" / "my Penates" (household gods); rendered "the household of Hven" / "my household gods," the domestic-deity idiom kept for the warmth it carries.
- **Places.** *Haffnia* = **Copenhagen**; *Selandia* = **Zealand**; *Scania* = **Scania** (Skåne, then Danish) — Tycho's family seat Knudstrup lay in Scania, hence the shuttling "now from Zealand into Scania, now back again."
- ***Palingenius.*** *ut noster … dixit PALINGENIUS* = "as our Palingenius said": **Marcellus Palingenius Stellatus** (Pier Angelo Manzolli, c. 1500–c. 1543), author of the widely-read didactic poem *Zodiacus Vitae*. *de aulica senectute* = "about old age at court" (a theme of the poem's courtly books); the simile *iactatus … tanquam pila missus ab illis* = "tossed about … like a ball flung [to and fro] by them" echoes Palingenius's image of the courtier as a plaything. The quotation-marks in the translation flag *pila missus* as the borrowed phrase; "by them" (*ab illis*) refers back to the King's, friends', and his own affairs.
- ***Dominus Quaestor Regius*** — "the Lord **Royal Treasurer**" (the Danish *rentemester* / royal *quaestor*); a specific officer Tycho hopes will accompany Dançay, here left by his office rather than named.
- ***M. Andreae … M. Laurentium nostrum.*** Two academic *Magistri* ("Master,") Tycho has invited. *M. Andreae* (dative of *Andreas*) is most plausibly **Anders Sørensen Vedel** (Andreas Severini Vellejus), Tycho's close friend and correspondent, though the bare praenomen does not put it beyond doubt; *M. Laurentium nostrum* ("our Master Laurentius") is a **Lauritz/Laurentius** of Tycho's circle, not further specified in the text. **Identification crux:** the letter gives only the forenames, so neither Master can be fixed with certainty from this text alone; flagged rather than asserted.
- **Orthography (humanist Latin).** *negotijs, proprijs, Penates … anhelantem*: the *-ijs* spellings are the printed/scribal *-iis*; *hîc* and *unâ* carry the source's circumflexes. *DANZAeO / DANZAeE*: the *Ae* ligature of *Danzaeus* reproduced as printed.
- **Calendar / dateline.** *Datae Huenae 5. Iulii Anno 1579* = "Given at Hven, 5 July 1579" (**O.S.**; Denmark kept the Julian calendar). The dateline matches the catalogue label (1579-07-05, Hven); no discrepancy. The subscription *T. / Tycho Brahe* is rendered "T[ycho]. / Tycho Brahe," the abbreviated first line bracketed.
- **Correction.** Restored the dropped pronoun 'is' in 'fecerit et is mihi rem gratam', per Dreyer, TBOO VII p.56; no change to the English, which already supplied the implicit 'he'.

documents.incipit: EODEM vesperi quo reversus sum domum, scripsi Μ. MACHABÆO, clarissime Domine Magister …

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD ANDREAM SEVERINI VELLEIUM.
S.

EODEM vesperi quo reversus sum domum, scripsi Μ. MACHABÆO, clarissime Domine Magister ANDREA, de equis, et tuas unâ illi misi literas, et effeci ut eadem nocte literæ transveherentur, ut summo mane sequentis diei Lundam venirent. Ego interea nihil ab eo responsi accepi, si tu aliquid, nescio. Equos si ab ipso non acceperis vide ut Haffniæ habeas, ego stabo promissis. Mitto tibi nunc literas ad Amicos in Germania, Norimbergæ ad CAMERARIUM, cui per te HOMELIJ Gnomonica remitto. Scripsi illi ut earum Bibliothecarum quæ in ipsorum urbe sunt, aliarumque memorabilium rerum tibi copiam faceret. Augustæ ad Consulem PAULUM HAINZELIUM et HIERONIMUM WOLFIUM, cui etiam tuos conatus commendavi, ut eos pro virili iuvarent. Scripsi etiam quasdam literas in ædes hospitis mei LAURENTII DEN et peto, ut si qua ratione fieri poterit, efficias ut Globum meum magnum, quem ipse conservat, ante hyemem habere possim; poteris si quos Augustæ emeris libros, ei includere et bene exterius interiusque compactum meo sumptu huc transferri curare. Norimbergæ etiam effice, ut certo ante hyemem ea quæ ad aquæductum meum requiruntur, a GEORGIO LAUBENWOLF Artifice, cui eo nomine prius per te scripsi, obtineam, et vide quid in Machina quam pro Rege parat, paratum sit, et urge opus tanquam id in mandatis a Rege et me haberes. Augustæ videbis et civitatis et civium instructissimas Bibliothecas, inprimis vero Fuggeranam idque per WOLFIUM consequi poteris. Cum Hospite meo LAURENTIO loquere an quicquam de Fratre meo CANUTO intellexerit, et utrum sciat ipsum Venetias ivisse, et an adhuc ibi commoretur, et si is tibi inciderit, vel de illo quicquam audiveris ubi sit, scribe illi meo nomine, ut sit bono animo: Regem esse placabilem et omnia in melius, quam adversarij putant, cessura. Sed hæc quæ de hoc scribo, in secreto coram omnibus et hîc et alibi habe. Si quos libros invenies in Germania, vel de Cometa præter eos, quos habeo, vel aliquid singulare in Astronomicis, mihi coëmas velim, ego pretium lubens restituam.

Bene vale, charissime Domine M. ANDREA, et Deus te feliciter et incolumem ducat et reducat.
Datæ Huenæ 15. Augusti Anno 1579.
T.
TYCHO BRAHE.
text.english:
**Tycho Brahe to Anders Sørensen Vedel. Greeting.**

On the very evening on which I returned home, I wrote to Master Machabæus, most distinguished Master Anders, about the horses, and sent your letter to him along with mine, and arranged that the letters be carried across that same night, so that they should reach Lund at first light the next day. In the meantime I have had no reply from him; whether you have had any, I do not know. If you do not receive the horses from him, see that you have [some] at Copenhagen — I shall stand by my promises. I now send you letters to friends in Germany: at Nuremberg, to Camerarius, to whom through you I am returning Homelius's *Gnomonica*. I have written to him to put at your disposal the libraries that are in their city, and other things worth seeing. At Augsburg, to Consul Paul Hainzel and to Hieronymus Wolf, to whom I have also commended your endeavours, that they may help them with all their might. I have also written certain letters [to be delivered] to the house of my host Laurentius Den, and I ask that, if by any means it can be done, you bring it about that I may have my great globe — which he is keeping — before winter; and if you buy any books at Augsburg you can enclose them with it, and, well packed without and within, see to it that [it all] be conveyed here at my expense. At Nuremberg, too, bring it about that I certainly obtain, before winter, the things required for my aqueduct, from the craftsman Georg Laubenwolf — to whom on that account I have written earlier through you — and see what has been got ready in the machine he is preparing for the King, and press the work forward as if you had it in charge from the King and from me. At Augsburg you will see the most fully furnished libraries both of the city and of its citizens, but above all the Fugger library; and this you will be able to obtain access to through Wolf. Speak with my host Laurentius [to learn] whether he has understood anything about my brother Knud, and whether he knows that he has gone to Venice, and whether he is still staying there; and if he should fall in with you, or you hear anything of him as to where he is, write to him in my name to be of good cheer: that the King is appeasable, and that everything will turn out for the better than his adversaries suppose. But keep what I write about this matter secret in the presence of everyone, both here and elsewhere. If you find any books in Germany — whether about the comet, besides those I have, or anything notable in astronomy — I should like you to buy them up for me, [and] I shall gladly repay the cost.

Fare you well, dearest Master Anders, and may God lead you forth and bring you back happily and unharmed.
Given at Hven, 15 August, the year 1579.
T[ycho].
TYCHO BRAHE.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender / recipient.** *Tycho Brahe* to *Andreas Severini Vellejus* = **Anders Sørensen Vedel** (1542–1616), the Danish historian, Royal Historiographer and Ribe canon (later the editor of the *Hundredvisebog* ballad collection); Tycho's close friend from their shared student years. Vedel is here evidently about to set out on a journey through Germany, and the letter is a travel-and-errands brief: Tycho hands him letters of introduction and a list of commissions to execute en route.
- ***M. Machabæo*** — "Master Machabæus," addressed at/near **Lund** (then Danish) concerning horses. The Macchabæus (Macalpine) family were prominent Danish humanists of Scottish origin descended from the reformer Johannes Machabæus (d. 1557); the individual here is most plausibly a Lund cleric/canon of that family. *Identification flagged:* the source gives only the surname and the academic title *M[agister]*; the precise individual is not securely fixable from the letter alone.
- ***Camerarius*** (Nuremberg) — **Joachim Camerarius the Younger** (1534–1598), the Nuremberg physician and botanist, a learned correspondent through whom Tycho routed introductions and books.
- ***Homelii Gnomonica*** — the *Gnomonica* (treatise on dialling / construction of sundials) associated with **Johann Hommel** (Homelius, 1518–1562), the Leipzig mathematician. Tycho is **returning** (*remitto*) a copy to Camerarius via Vedel; *Gnomonica* kept as the work-title.
- ***Consul Paulus Hainzelius*** — **Paul Hainzel** of Augsburg (one of the Hainzel brothers of the 1571 Wolf letter); *Consul* here = **Bürgermeister** (city magistrate) of Augsburg, with whom Tycho had built the great Göppingen quadrant in 1569. *Hieronymus Wolfius* = **Hieronymus Wolf** (1516–1580), the Augsburg humanist and librarian (see brahe-t_15711113001).
- ***Laurentius Den*** — **Lorenz (Laurentius) Den**, Tycho's host (*hospes*) during his Augsburg residence (1569–70), now the custodian of Tycho's *Globus magnus* (great globe) awaiting shipment north.
- ***Globus meus magnus*** — "my great globe": Tycho's large celestial globe, ordered/begun in Augsburg in his earlier stay and famously not fully completed and delivered to Hven until years later (it was finished at Uraniborg). The instruction to retrieve it "before winter" fits the period when Tycho was still drawing his Augsburg-made apparatus home.
- ***Georgio Laubenwolf Artifice*** — **Georg Labenwolf** (Laubenwolf), the Nuremberg bronze-founder and waterworks/fountain engineer (the family responsible for the Nuremberg "Gänsemännchen" fountain). He is independently documented as the maker of the *Vandkunsten* (waterworks) at Kronborg for Frederik II — which corroborates both the *aquaeductus* commission for Uraniborg and the reference to "the machine he is preparing for the King." *Artifex* rendered "craftsman."
- ***aquaeductum meum / Machina … pro Rege*** — "my aqueduct" = the water-supply / fountain works for Uraniborg; the "machine he is preparing for the King" = a parallel hydraulic commission for Frederik II (consistent with Labenwolf's documented Kronborg waterworks). Tycho asks Vedel to chase the Uraniborg parts and to inspect progress on the royal machine, *"as if you had it in charge from the King and from me."*
- ***Bibliotheca Fuggerana*** — "the Fugger library," the renowned Augsburg book-collection of the Fugger merchant-banking dynasty; access to be arranged through Wolf (who served the Fuggers as librarian).
- ***Frater meus Canutus*** — **Knud Brahe** (1555–1615), Tycho's younger brother, then reported to have gone to **Venice** (*Venetias*). The passage that follows is the letter's confidential core: Knud was at this time in difficulty with the crown, and Tycho wants reassurance passed to him "in my name" — *that the King is appeasable* (*Regem esse placabilem*) and matters will turn out better than his adversaries expect — with the express instruction to keep the whole affair **secret** before everyone, here and elsewhere.
- ***de Cometa*** — "about the comet": Tycho's standing interest in cometary literature (the great comet of 1577, on which he was then at work). He asks Vedel to buy up any comet-books or notable astronomical works he does not already own, against repayment.
- **Epistolary formulae.** Opening *S.* = *salutem [dicit]*, "greeting"; *Bene vale* = "Fare you well." *Domine M[agister] Andrea* = "Master Anders" (academic *Magister*). Subscription *T. / TYCHO BRAHE* preserved.
- **Calendar / place.** *Datae Huenae 15. Augusti Anno 1579* = "Given at **Hven** (the island of Hven, seat of Uraniborg), 15 August 1579" (Old Style; Denmark kept the Julian calendar). The edition label ("1579. 15. august. Hven") agrees with the dateline; no discrepancy.
- **Witness note.** The single recorded witness (A) is a later copy (*Afskrift*) in Tycho Brahe's private archive at the Rigsarkivet, not an autograph; readings follow Dreyer.
- **Orthography.** Source prints *Μ.* (the Greek capital mu, for Latin *M[agister]*) before *MACHABAeO* — retained as printed in the Source block; it stands for the Latin abbreviation and is rendered "Master." Ligature *ae* (as in *MACHABAeO*, *Vesperi*-clause forms) and *unâ / hîc* circumflexes are kept as printed.

documents.abstract: Reports his health, criticises German astrologers for errors in predicting the recent eclipse, and urges Tycho's accurate observations to settle the disputed true motion of the Sun.
documents.incipit: CUM hi populares tui, nobilissime et humanissime D. TYCHO, suam mihi operam benigne …

text.original:
HIERONYMUS WOLFIUS AD TYCHONEM BRAHE.
S.

CUM hi populares tui, nobilissime et humanissime D. TYCHO, suam mihi operam benigne pollicerentur, nolui eos sine meis literis dimittere. Scias ergo me pro ætate mediocri esse valetudine, neque quicquam habere, quod de fortuna etiam magnopere querar, sorte mea philosophica contentus. Sed quid interim Uranie tua? Illam quidem non dormitare, non cessare persuasum habemus. Sed nihil ad nos propter locorum intervalla hactenus est perlatum. Quod tamen ut fiat, si pro humanitate tua curaveris, rem nobis gratissimam feceris. Nostrates Astrologi, CYPRIANUS, TURNEISSERUS, STADIUS, HEINSCHIUS et alij multum a vero tempore initij proximæ Eclipseos aberrarunt. A MÆSTLINO diu nihil accepimus. Motus Solis verus adhuc valde controversus est; qui utinam accuratis tuis observationibus certo deprehendatur et constituatur. Quod quo facilius præstare possis, Deum tibi propitium precor.

Vale.
Augustæ Vindelicorum 8. Februarij Anno 1580.
text.english:
**Hieronymus Wolf to Tycho Brahe.**
Greeting.

Since these countrymen of yours kindly promised me their service, most noble and most courteous Master Tycho, I was unwilling to let them depart without a letter from me. Know, then, that for my age I am of middling health, and that I have nothing for which I might even greatly complain of fortune, content as I am with my philosopher's lot. But what, meanwhile, of your Urania? That she does not slumber, does not idle, we are persuaded. Yet nothing has thus far been brought to us, on account of the distances between our places. But if, in keeping with your kindness, you will see to it that this comes about, you will do me a most welcome thing. Our [German] astrologers — Cyprian [Leowitz], Thurneisser, Stadius, Heinschius, and many others — strayed far from the true time of the beginning of the recent eclipse. From Maestlin we have for a long while received nothing. The true motion of the Sun is still very much in dispute; would that it be securely ascertained and established by your accurate observations. And that you may the more easily accomplish this, I pray God be favourable to you.

Farewell.
At Augsburg, 8 February, the year 1580.

documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent.** *Hieronymus Wolfius* = **Hieronymus Wolf** (1516–1580), the Augsburg humanist and Greek scholar (the "father of Byzantine studies"), then directing the city's library and school; an old mentor-friend of Tycho's from his Augsburg years (1569–70). This is one of his last letters: he died in October 1580, and the note's remark on his "middling health" stands against that backdrop.
- ***hi populares tui*** — "these countrymen of yours": Danish acquaintances of Tycho passing through Augsburg, who carry the letter and had offered Wolf their service. *Populares* here = "fellow-countrymen / compatriots," not "the common people."
- ***sorte mea philosophica contentus*** — "content with my philosopher's lot": the Stoic-humanist commonplace of contentment; kept literal rather than paraphrased to "philosophical resignation."
- ***Uranie tua*** — "your Urania," the Muse of astronomy, here a personification of Tycho's astronomical work; the conceit (she "does not slumber, does not idle") is preserved. Tycho had by 1580 begun building Uraniborg (named for this Muse) on Hven; Wolf's *Uranie tua* and the place-name resonate, but the letter speaks of the Muse/the work, not the building.
- **Astrology / astronomy.** *Nostrates Astrologi* = "our [native, i.e. German] astrologers." The four named:
 - *CYPRIANUS* = **Cyprian Leowitz** (Cyprianus Leovitius, 1524–1574), the Bohemian-born astrologer-astronomer active in Augsburg, author of widely-used ephemerides and eclipse tables. (The same Leowitz whose casting of Wolf's own geniture Tycho had corrected — see the 1571 Wolf letter.)
 - *TURNEISSERUS* = **Leonhard Thurneisser zum Thurn** (1531–1596), the Basel-born physician, alchemist, and almanac-maker, then at the Brandenburg court in Berlin.
 - *STADIUS* = **Johannes Stadius** (1527–1579), the Brabant mathematician and ephemerist (*Ephemerides novae*, based on the Prutenic Tables).
 - *HEINSCHIUS* — most plausibly **Reinhold Heinsius / Heinisch**, a contemporary German almanac- and prognostication-maker; the identification is not fully secure (flagged below).
 - *MAeSTLINO* = **Michael Maestlin** (1550–1631), the Tübingen astronomer (later Kepler's teacher), with whom Tycho and Wolf's circle corresponded.
- ***proximae Eclipseos*** — "the recent eclipse": an eclipse (almost certainly solar, given the predicted-time controversy and the following remark on the Sun's motion) shortly before this letter; Wolf's point is that the published German tables badly missed its *time of onset*. *Eclipsis* → "eclipse" by this chapter's convention
- ***Motus Solis verus … controversus*** — "the true motion of the Sun is still very much in dispute": *motus* → "motion"; Wolf names the unsettled solar theory as the prize Tycho's *accuratis observationibus* ("accurate observations") might decide — an early external statement of the observational programme that would become Tycho's *instauratio astronomiae*.
- **Epistolary formulae.** Heading *S.* = *Salutem* → "Greeting"; *Vale* → "Farewell"; *D. TYCHO* = *Dominus* → "Master".
- **Dateline.** *Augustae Vindelicorum 8. Februarij Anno 1580* = "at **Augsburg** (Augusta Vindelicorum), 8 February, the year 1580" (O.S. — Augsburg/Lutheran reckoning still kept the Julian calendar in early 1580; the Gregorian reform came in October 1582). The dateline agrees with the catalogue label (8 February 1580, Augsburg); no date discrepancy.
- **Orthography.** *MAeSTLINO* and *DIVINAe*-type *ae*-ligatures are reproduced as printed in the source block. *initij*, *alij*, *intervalla* etc. carry the period *-ij* / consonantal-*i* spelling; rendered without comment in translation.
