documents.apparatus:
- **Sender / recipient.** *Tycho Brahe* writes from **Uraniborg** on Hven. The addressee, *Henricus Ranzovius* = **Heinrich Rantzau** (1526–1598), the Danish king's *Statthalter* (royal governor) of the duchies of Schleswig-Holstein, residing chiefly at **Segeberg**; one of the great humanist patrons and bibliophiles of the north, an astrological author, and a frequent intermediary in Tycho's correspondence.
- **Address-line title.** *Produci Cimbrico* — "Governor of the Cimbrian land," i.e. of the Cimbrian peninsula (Jutland / the duchies). *Produx* (a late/Neo-Latin form, dative *produci*) here = a leading/governing magistrate, rendered "Governor"; the antiquarian epithet *Cimbricus* ("of the Cimbri") is the humanist style for Jutland-Holstein. Kept and glossed rather than modernised to "Statthalter."
- ***S. D.*** = *salutem dicit*, "sends greeting".
- **Gerhard Rantzau** (*filio GERHARDO*) — Heinrich's son **Gerhard Rantzau** (1558–1627), here named as Tycho's "friend and neighbour" (*amico et vicino meo dilecto*).
- **Wilhelm IV** (*illustrissimo Domino GULIELMO Landgravio Hassiae*) = **Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel**, the astronomer-prince; his court mathematician **Rothmann** = **Christoph Rothmann**. The letter is a cover-note forwarding the Brahe–Hesse astronomical correspondence to Rantzau.
- **Calendar reference.** *responsum … ad Literas in Ianuario ipsi perscriptas* — Tycho's letter "written out in January" is the long Tycho→Rothmann letter of 20 January 1587 (identifier brahe-t_15870120001); not converted, given as written.
- ***papyrum impressoriam … operi cuidam, quod nunc typis meis elaboratur*** — "printing paper … for a certain work now being produced at my press": Tycho's own Uraniborg press; the "certain work" is most plausibly the volume that became the *Epistolae astronomicae* (printed at Uraniborg, the 1596 *Liber I*) and/or *De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis*, then in progress — identification not asserted in the text, so left general.
- **Astronomical crux — *affixarum restitutionibus*.** Literally "the restorations of the fixed [stars]," i.e. the re-determination / re-establishment of the **fixed-star** positions (the catalogue of *stellae affixae*, the fixed stars). *restitutio* is rendered "restoration" per the editorial glossary (, *restitutio/instauratio* → restoration/renewal); *affixarum* (fem. gen. pl.) stands for *stellarum affixarum* (the fixed stars), the noun *stellarum* understood — bracketed "[stars]" supplied. The phrase denotes the agreement between Tycho and Rothmann on their respective fixed-star coordinate restorations. Flagged because *affixarum* is elliptical and "restorations of the fixed stars" is a technical-procedural sense, not a generic "restoration."
- ***ex propria Bibliotheca*** — "from your own library": a pointed compliment to Rantzau, whose library at Breitenburg was among the most celebrated private collections of the age.
- **Marking convention.** *literarum notis certos paragraphos designavi* — "I have marked off particular paragraphs with letters of the alphabet": Tycho keyed his replies to numbered/lettered sections of the Landgrave's letters so the correspondence could be read in register. *literarum notis* = "with letters [of the alphabet] as marks," rendered accordingly.
- **Subscription / dateline.** *sobole non degenere* — "offspring not degenerate," i.e. children who do not fall short of (do not disgrace) their lineage; rendered "offspring that does not fall short of its stock," the double negative (*non degenere*) preserved. *Datae Uraniburgi 19. Octobris Anno 1587* = "Given at Uraniborg, 19 October 1587" (O.S.; Denmark kept the Julian calendar). The catalogue label ("1587. 19. oktober. Uraniborg") agrees with the dateline; no discrepancy.
- **Negations (verified count).** Source negations rendered one-for-one: *neque oblivione … neque negligentia … existimes* ("neither … nor …"); *non intermitteret* ("not fail"); *non inscius* ("not unaware"); *nolui … quin … adferret* ("I was unwilling that he should pass … without bringing," litotes preserved); *ni fallor* ("unless I am mistaken"); *non … me latet* ("it is not hidden from me"); *ne deesse velis* ("do not be unwilling to lend"); *non … sine voluptate* ("not without pleasure"); *non degenere* ("not degenerate"). No negation added or dropped.

documents.abstract: Thanks Tycho for copies of the Hven–Kassel correspondence and engages the evidence for stellar latitude changes linked to variation in the obliquity of the ecliptic.
documents.incipit: GRATISSIMÆ mihi fuerunt tuæ literæ cum literis ultro citroque ad Landgravium et eius …

text.original:
HENRICUS BRUCÆUS AD TYCHONEM BRAHE.

GRATISSIMÆ mihi fuerunt tuæ literæ cum literis ultro citroque ad Landgravium et eius Mathematicum scriptis, in quibus non sine voluptate legi vestrarum observationum consensum, tum in Cometa anni 85, tum in stellarum fixarum notatione longitudinum et latitudinum. Latitudines enim uterque mutari statuit, et sequi mutationem declinationis Eclipticæ, sive obliquitatis Eclipticæ variationem. Hæc cum maximâ, sententia COPERNICI, sit 24', quæ aliquot seculorum decursu fiat, et cum non multum inter PTOLEMÆUM et HIPPARCHUM et MENELAUM et TIMOCHARIN temporum intervallum intercedat, non mirum, latitudinum mutationem ab ijs non annotatam. Verum de COPERNICO miror, qui evidentem mutationem debuit animadvertere in tanta obliquitatis mutatione inter PTOLEMÆUM et COPERNICUM intercedente, si veræ sunt observationes, quæ tantam obliquitatis Zodiaci variationem tradunt. Quæ autem de refractione siderum tradis, subtilia nimis mihi videntur, et quæ sub regulam cadere vix poterint ob diversas aëris constitutiones, quæ varietatem refractionum in eadem siderum altitudine efficient. Quæ autem a doctissimo CHRISTOPHORO ROTHMANNO in sua de Cometa anni 85 tractatione commemorantur, velim legere. Ex hypothesi enim falsa verum sequi non dubito; scientiam autem fieri, nullus mihi persuaserit, si debeat ea oriri ex causis veris conclusionis. Videmus autem motum Solis tam per Eccentricum, quam per Concentricum cum Epicyclo tueri nos posse, cum vel neutra vel altera hypothesis vera esse queat, ut non satis intelligam, cur hoc in loco ARISTOTELES subtilitatis arguatur. Quæ de cancris fluvialibus scribis, dabo operam, quantum in me erit; verum video maiores difficultates, quam tu fortasse cogites, quod cancrorum emtio et navium in Daniam solutio raro in eadem tempora incidant. Attamen studium meum cum in hoc tum in alio genere cognosces.

Bene vale, mi TYCHO, et nos tui studiosissimos habeto.
Rostochij 28 Octobris Anno Domini 1587.
text.english:
**Heinrich Brucaeus to Tycho Brahe.**

Most welcome to me were your letters, together with the letters written back and forth to the Landgrave and his Mathematician, in which I read — not without pleasure — the agreement of your observations, both in the case of the comet of [the year] '85 and in the recording of the longitudes and latitudes of the fixed stars. For each of you holds that the latitudes change, and that they follow the change in the declination of the ecliptic — that is, the variation of the obliquity of the ecliptic. Since this is, at its greatest, 24′ in Copernicus's opinion — a change that comes about over the course of several centuries — and since not much interval of time falls between Ptolemy and Hipparchus and Menelaus and Timocharis, it is no wonder that a change of latitudes was not noted by them. But about Copernicus I marvel: he ought to have observed an evident change, given the great change of obliquity falling between Ptolemy and Copernicus, if the observations that report so great a variation of the obliquity of the zodiac are true. As for what you set forth about the refraction of the heavenly bodies, it seems to me too subtle, and such as can scarcely fall under a rule, on account of the diverse constitutions of the air, which will produce a variety of refractions at one and the same altitude of the heavenly bodies. But what is recounted by the most learned Christoph Rothmann in his treatise on the comet of [the year] '85 — I should like to read it. For I do not doubt that a true [conclusion] follows from a false hypothesis; but that this constitutes [true] knowledge [scientia], no one will ever persuade me, if it [knowledge] must arise from the true causes of the conclusion. For we see that we can maintain the motion of the Sun as well by an eccentric as by a concentric with an epicycle, although either neither or [only] one of the [two] hypotheses can be true — so that I do not well understand why, in this place, Aristotle is charged with [excessive] subtlety. As for what you write about the river crabs, I shall do my best, so far as it lies in me; but I see greater difficulties than you perhaps suppose, because the buying of the crabs and the sailing of ships to Denmark rarely fall at the same season. Yet you will know my zeal both in this matter and in another kind.

Fare you well, my Tycho, and reckon us most devoted to you.
At Rostock, 28 October, in the Year of the Lord 1587.

documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent.** *Henricus Brucaeus* = **Heinrich Brucaeus** (Hendrik van den Broeck, 1531–1593), of Alost (Aalst) in Flanders; professor of medicine and of mathematics/astronomy at the University of **Rostock**, and Tycho's former teacher there. The intimate, faintly tutorial tone of the close (*mi Tycho*) and the philosophical objection reflect that relationship.
- ***ad Landgravium et eius Mathematicum*** — to **Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel** (1532–1592) and "his Mathematician," i.e. **Christoph Rothmann**, the Hesse-Kassel court mathematician (named explicitly later in the letter). The "letters written back and forth" (*ultro citroque*) are the Tycho–Kassel observational correspondence; Brucaeus had evidently been shown copies.
- **The comet of '85.** *Cometa anni 85* = the comet of **1585**, observed both at Hven and at Kassel; the subject of Rothmann's treatise (*Tractatus de cometa anni 1585*) and of comparison between the two observatories.
- **Astronomy — obliquity/latitudes.** *declinatio Eclipticae … obliquitas Eclipticae* = the **declination / obliquity of the ecliptic** (the tilt of the zodiac to the equator); *latitudines* / *longitudines* = **(celestial) latitudes / longitudes** of the fixed stars. Brucaeus reports that Tycho and Rothmann agree the stellar latitudes shift in step with a secular change in the obliquity. *maximâ … sit 24′* — Copernicus put the total amplitude of this variation at **24 arc-minutes** (24′) over several centuries (Copernicus's theory of the trepidation/variation of the obliquity, *De revolutionibus* III). The figure and the hedge ("at its greatest," *maximâ*) are kept.
- ***Ptolemaeum … Hipparchum … Menelaum … Timocharin*** — **Ptolemy** (fl. 2nd c. AD), **Hipparchus** (2nd c. BC), **Menelaus** of Alexandria (fl. c. AD 100), and **Timocharis** of Alexandria (early 3rd c. BC): the ancient observers whose star-records bracket the question. Brucaeus's point is sceptical — the ancients' intervals were too short to register the latitude shift, yet Copernicus, far removed in time from Ptolemy, ought to have seen it if the reported variation is real.
- **Refraction.** *refractione siderum* = **refraction** of the heavenly bodies; *diversas aëris constitutiones* = "the diverse constitutions [states] of the air." Brucaeus's objection — that atmospheric refraction is too variable with the air's condition to be reduced to a fixed table (*sub regulam … cadere*) at a given **altitude** (*altitudine*) — is a genuine and prescient methodological caution; rendered without sharpening.
- **The hypotheses passage (the philosophical core).** *Ex hypothesi … falsa verum sequi non dubito; scientiam autem fieri, nullus mihi persuaserit, si debeat ea oriri ex causis veris conclusionis.* — "I do not doubt that a true [conclusion] follows from a false hypothesis; but that this constitutes [true] knowledge [*scientia*], no one will ever persuade me, if it must arise from the true causes of the conclusion." This is the classic "saving the phenomena" vs. **demonstrative knowledge** distinction: a *hypothesis* (geometrical model) may yield correct predictions yet be physically false, and so not true *scientia* in the Aristotelian sense (knowledge through true causes). *scientia* is rendered "[true] knowledge" with the Latin flagged, not modernised to "science." The example follows: *motum Solis tam per Eccentricum, quam per Concentricum cum Epicyclo* = the **Sun's motion** modelled equally well **by an eccentric** or **by a concentric [deferent] with an epicycle** — two geometrically equivalent constructions, of which (Brucaeus argues) at most one can be physically true. The clause *cum vel neutra vel altera hypothesis vera esse queat* is rendered "although either neither or [only] one of the [two] hypotheses can be true"; *altera* here = "(only) one of the two," the disjunction being "neither, or [at most] one" — i.e. *not both*. The two negation-bearing options (*neutra* / *altera*) are reproduced exactly, neither added to nor dropped.
- ***hoc in loco ARISTOTELES subtilitatis arguatur*** — "in this place Aristotle is charged with [excessive] subtlety." *subtilitatis arguatur* = "is accused/charged on the score of subtlety"; the bracketed "[excessive]" marks that the genitive carries a pejorative sense (over-subtlety, hair-splitting) which is implied, not lexically present. The "place" (*hoc in loco*) is presumably a passage in Tycho's or Rothmann's letters where Aristotle's physics was faulted; Brucaeus defends Aristotle, since (on his view) the geometers cannot establish physical truth either.
- **River crabs.** *cancris fluvialibus* = **river crabs / crayfish** (freshwater crustaceans, *Astacus*). A non-astronomical favour: Tycho had asked Brucaeus to procure crayfish; Brucaeus pleads the logistical mismatch between the **buying of the crabs** and the **sailing of ships to Denmark** (*navium in Daniam solutio* — *solutio* here = the loosing/setting-sail of ships), which rarely coincide in season. Rendered plainly; *solutio* glossed.
- **Epistolary formulae.** *Bene vale, mi Tycho* = "Fare you well, my Tycho"; *nos tui studiosissimos habeto* = "reckon us most devoted to you."
- **Calendar / place.** *Rostochij 28 Octobris Anno Domini 1587* = "at **Rostock**, 28 October, in the Year of the Lord 1587" (O.S.; Denmark and Lutheran Rostock both kept the Julian calendar). The dateline agrees with the catalogue label (28 October 1587, Rostock) — no discrepancy.

documents.incipit: PROXIMIS literis, Vir nobilissime ac excellentissime, memoria lapsus scripsi ad te, …

text.original:
NOBILISSIMO ET VIRTVTE SAPIENTIA INGENIOSA ERVDITAQVE DOCTRINA, CLARISSIMO VIRO, DOMINO TYCHONI BRAHE, DOMINO DE KNVDSTRVP, EQVITI DANO, MATHEMATICORVM NOSTRO SECULO OMNIUM PRÆSTANTISSIMO, ETC. DOMINO SUO CUM OBSERUANTIA COLENDO, ETC. S. P.

PROXIMIS literis, Vir nobilissime ac excellentissime, memoria lapsus scripsi ad te, extremam superficiem Aëris crassioris ex Demonstratione Opticorum distare a superficie Terræ per Semidiametrum Terræ. Verum dum (de absurditate forte fortuna cogitans, quod nimirum eo præsupposito sequerentur perpetua Crepuscula,) ipsos Authores consulo, inuenio me ea, quæ ante aliquot Annos in ijs legeram, non rite meminisse; nec integrum illud, quod putaui, esse Semidiametrum Terræ, sed sexagesimam nondum Semidiametri Terreni partem. Quapropter peto a te, vt quæ præcipiti festinatione in Literis meis effutij potius quam scripsi, ea velis emendare, ac pro Semidiametro Terreno sexagesimam fere Semidiametri Terreni partem, ac pro duplicatione crassioris Aëris multiplicationem vbique in ea demonstratione ponere. Ita enim omnia constabunt, ac demonstratio mea hac ratione a fortiori confirmabitur. Schema quoque aliter in hunc modum formandum est.

Figur 10 

Scis enim lineas EAG et HCL ex centro et superficie Terræ ob immensitatem Cæli videri parallelas, vel potius vnam et eandem. Iam facile habes, quanta sit densitas crassioris Aëris circa Horizontem, quanta in Altitudine 30. Graduum. Connecte enim puncta XA et AO, centrum nimirum Terræ cum punctis intersectionum extremæ superficiei crassioris Aëris in Horizonte et in Altitudine 30. Graduum. Iam igitur in Triangulo ACX, quoniam dantur duo latera, latus nimirum AX Partium 60. Min. 48. Secund. 50. et latus AC Partium 60. exacte, ex dictorum Opticorum demonstrationibus, et angulus ACX rectus per Hypothesin: datur itaque et tertium CX latus, densitas nimirum Aëris crassioris, per quam circa Horizontem formæ Stellarum ad nostrum visum perueniunt. Sic et in Altitudine 30. Graduum, quoniam in Triangulo ACO itidem dantur duo latera AO et AC, cum Angulo ACO, qui per Hypothesin vltra rectum datur 30. Grad. hoc est, Graduum 120; datur igitur et tertium CO latus, distantia nimirum extremæ superficiei Aëris crassioris in Altitudine 30. Graduum. Ita vides, hoc vnico argumento, quod nimirum Refractiones non durent vsque ad verticem, firmissime demonstrari, non esse diuersa Ætheris et Aëris Diaphana. Nec enim ipsi Optici negare possunt, quin præsupposito diuerso Ætheris et Aëris Diaphano necessarium sit, vt Refractio duret vsque ad verticem, vt ex Alhazeno lib. 7. et Vitellione lib. 10. P. 51. manifestum est. Ea quoque, quæ Vitellio lib. 10. P. 55. de scintillatione Stellarum proposuit, si vera essent, pro me facerent. Si enim scintillatio Stellarum fieret propter diuaricationem formæ in loco imaginis, sequeretur inde, formam illam non alibi quam in crassiore Aëre consistere posse. Nam Ventus vsque ad concauam superficiem Sphæræ Lunaris non ascendit, nec admodum, vt opinor, vltra crassiorem illum Aërem. Vix enim in puro illo Aëre Ventus exsistere poterit. Hæc ad te hac vice perscribere volui, ne forte putares, (quod tamen vix mihi credendum erat,) demonstrationem meam eo infirmari, quod spatium illud crassioris Aëris iusto maius assumserim. Memoriæ lapsum esse, facile animaduertes; nec tantum temporis tunc mihi sumere potui, vt ipsos Autores consulerem.

Vale igitur felicissime et optime, nobilissime et excellentissime Tycho, et de hoc sublimi negotio mecum conferre ne desine.
Cassellis 14. Calend. Nouemb. Anno 87.
T. T.
CHRISTOPHORVS ROTHMANNVS.
text.english:
**To the most noble and illustrious gentleman, eminent in virtue, wisdom, and ingenious and erudite learning, Master Tycho Brahe, Lord of Knudstrup, Danish knight, the most outstanding of all the mathematicians of our age, etc., his lord to be honoured with all observance, etc. — heartiest greeting.**

In my last letter, most noble and most excellent Sir, my memory failing me, I wrote to you that — by the demonstration of the writers on optics — the outermost surface of the thicker air [*aër crassior*] is distant from the surface of the Earth by [one] semidiameter of the Earth. But while (chancing to reflect on the absurdity, namely that on that supposition perpetual twilight would follow) I consulted the authors themselves, I find that I did not rightly remember the things I had read in them some years ago; and that the figure I supposed was not a whole semidiameter of the Earth, but not yet a sixtieth part of the terrestrial semidiameter. Wherefore I ask of you that what I blurted out rather than wrote in my letter, in headlong haste, you would be willing to amend: namely, that in place of [one] terrestrial semidiameter you everywhere set, in that demonstration, about a sixtieth part of the terrestrial semidiameter, and in place of a doubling of the thicker air, a multiplication. For thus everything will stand firm, and my demonstration will by this reckoning be confirmed *a fortiori* [all the more strongly]. The diagram, too, is to be drawn differently, in this manner.

Figure 10

For you know that the lines EAG and HCL, [drawn] from the centre and from the surface of the Earth, appear — because of the immensity of the heaven — to be parallel, or rather one and the same. Now you readily have how great the density of the thicker air is around the horizon, and how great at an altitude of 30 degrees. For join the points X–A and A–O — namely the centre of the Earth with the points of intersection of the outermost surface of the thicker air at the horizon and at an altitude of 30 degrees. Now then, in the triangle ACX, since two sides are given — namely the side AX of 60 parts [degrees] 48 minutes 50 seconds, and the side AC of exactly 60 parts, from the demonstrations of the said writers on optics — and the angle ACX is right by hypothesis: there is therefore given also the third side, CX, namely the density of the thicker air, through which around the horizon the forms [images] of the stars come to our sight. So too at an altitude of 30 degrees: since in the triangle ACO likewise two sides AO and AC are given, together with the angle ACO, which by hypothesis is given as beyond a right angle by 30 degrees, that is, of 120 degrees; there is therefore given also the third side, CO — namely the distance of the outermost surface of the thicker air at an altitude of 30 degrees. Thus you see that by this one argument — namely, that the refractions do not last all the way to the zenith — it is most firmly demonstrated that the transparent media [*Diaphana*] of the aether and of the air are not distinct. For not even the writers on optics themselves can deny that, the transparent media of aether and of air being supposed distinct, it is necessary that refraction should last all the way to the zenith, as is plain from Alhazen, Book 7, and Witelo, Book 10, Proposition 51. Those things, too, which Witelo set forth in Book 10, Proposition 55, concerning the scintillation [twinkling] of the stars, were they true, would tell in my favour. For if the scintillation of the stars came about on account of the divergence of the form [image] at the place of the image, it would follow from this that that form could subsist nowhere but in the thicker air. For the wind does not rise up to the concave surface of the lunar sphere, nor much, as I think, beyond that thicker air. For scarcely will the wind be able to exist in that pure air. These things I wished to write out to you on this occasion, lest perhaps you should think (though indeed I could scarcely believe it of you) that my demonstration is weakened by the fact that I assumed that space of the thicker air greater than it should be. That a lapse of memory occurred you will easily perceive; nor could I then take so much time to myself as to consult the authors themselves.

Farewell then, most happily and most well, most noble and most excellent Tycho, and do not cease to confer with me about this sublime matter.
At Kassel, the 14th [day] before the Kalends of November, the year [15]87.
Yours truly [*Tuus Totus*],
Christoph Rothmann.

departures_from_tekstnet.basis: The text printed here descends from one harvest of tekstnet's page and was read against Dreyer's page images in July 2026; a second harvest of the same page is kept beside it. Where the two disagree in a word, both readings are listed: Dreyer's page decides, and unless the audit paragraph names the word, that check has not yet been made for it. Ligature, diacritic, case and spacing differences are not listed; the source's ligatures have been adopted.

documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent / sender.** *Christophorus Rothmannus* = **Christoph Rothmann** (c. 1550/60 – c. 1600), mathematician and astronomer at the court of Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel; one of Tycho's principal scientific correspondents. The exchange of 1586–90 is the great early-modern debate on atmospheric refraction and the reality of the celestial "spheres," printed by Tycho himself in the present edition.
- **Recipient.** *Tycho Brahe, Dominus de Knudstrup, Eques Danus* — Tycho identified by his patrimonial seat **Knudstrup** (Knutstorp, Scania) and his rank of *eques* (nobleman/knight); titulature kept in full by this chapter's convention
- ***S. P.*** — *salutem plurimam* (sc. *dicit*), "(sends) heartiest greeting".
- ***T. T.*** (subscription) — *Tuus Totus*, "Wholly yours / Yours truly"; expanded in the translation.
- **Edition of record.** Tycho's own *Epistolarum astronomicarum libri* (Liber I), Uraniborg 1596 — the volume he printed at Hven; reprinted in Dreyer, *Opera Omnia* VI. No manuscript witness is recorded in the edition (witnesses:[]).

**Subject and technical terms**

- **The letter is a correction.** Rothmann retracts a figure given in his *proxima epistola* ("last letter"): he had wrongly said the top of the *aër crassior* lies one Earth-semidiameter above the surface; the optical authorities in fact give "not yet a sixtieth part" of a semidiameter. He asks Tycho to substitute that value, and to replace *duplicatio* ("a doubling" of the thicker air) with *multiplicatio* ("a multiplication") throughout the demonstration.
- ***aër crassior*** → rendered **"thicker air"** throughout (the dense lower atmosphere, as against the *purus aër* / aether above). *Crepuscula* → **twilight**: the *reductio* is that a one-semidiameter atmosphere would yield *perpetua crepuscula*, "perpetual twilight."
- ***Refractio*** → **refraction**; ***Refractiones non durent usque ad verticem*** → "the refractions do not last all the way to the zenith" — Rothmann's key empirical premise. *verticem* here = the **zenith** (the point overhead), kept as "zenith" by this chapter's convention; not "vertex/summit."
- ***Diaphana Aetheris et Aëris*** → **"the transparent media of the aether and of the air."** *Diaphanum* (Alhazen/Witelo's *diaphanon*) is the period optical term for a transparent medium; rendered "transparent medium," with the Latin flagged. Rothmann's thesis: aether and air are **not** optically distinct media (*non esse diuersa … Diaphana*) — a single negation in the source, reproduced as a single negation here.
- ***formae Stellarum / forma … in loco imaginis*** → **"the forms [images] of the stars / the form at the place of the image."** *Forma* is the perspectivist term for the propagated optical species/image; glossed "[image]" in brackets, the Latin kept.
- ***scintillatio Stellarum*** → **scintillation (twinkling) of the stars**; *diuaricatio formae* → "divergence/spreading-apart of the form [image]."
- **Geometry.** The argument is a plane-trigonometric solution of two right/oblique triangles sharing the Earth-radius side AC. *Partium 60. Min. 48. Secund. 50.* = **60 degrees 48 minutes 50 seconds** (sexagesimal; *partes* = degrees here, the standard astronomical usage). *AC Partium 60. exacte* = "AC of exactly 60 parts." The angle *ACO … ultra rectum … 30. Grad., hoc est, Graduum 120* = an angle of **120°** (a right angle exceeded by 30°). Letters of points (E, A, G, H, C, L, X, O) refer to **Figure 10**, the woodcut diagram of the printed edition; the source's placeholder line *"Figur 10"* (German caption) is preserved verbatim in the Source block and rendered "Figure 10."
- **Authorities cited.** *Alhazenus, lib. 7* = **Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen)**, *De aspectibus / Perspectiva*, Book 7 (on refraction). *Vitellio, lib. 10. P. 51 … P. 55* = **Witelo** (Vitellio, fl. 13th c.), *Perspectiva*, Book 10, **Propositions 51 and 55** (*P.* = *propositio*); P. 55 on stellar scintillation. Both as printed in the Risner *Opticae thesaurus* (Basel 1572), Rothmann's working text.
- ***a fortiori*** — kept as a Latin term of art, glossed "[all the more strongly]."
- ***Sphaerae Lunaris … concava superficies*** → "the concave surface of the lunar sphere" (the traditional inner boundary of the Moon's orb / the top of the sublunary region), here invoked only as the upper limit of *ventus* (wind); not an endorsement of solid spheres — indeed the broader correspondence is where Tycho and Rothmann jointly dissolve them.

**Calendar / dateline (crux — see confidence)**

- **The dateline reads *"Cassellis 14. Calend. Nouemb. Anno 87"* = "at Kassel, the 14th before the Kalends of November, 1587."** By inclusive Roman reckoning, *14 Kalendas Novembris* = **19 October 1587** (Kalends of November = 1 Nov.; 1 Nov. counts as day 1, so the 14th day before = 19 October). The header therefore leads with **19 October 1587 [O.S.]**, the date the source substantiates.
- **The edition label ("1587. 14. november. Kassel") gives 14 November** — a modern catalogue date that does **not** match the Roman-calendar dateline and is appended in the header as "(catalogued 14 November 1587)." The "14" of the label has plainly been read off the numeral *"14"* in *"14. Calend. Nouemb."* and miscopied as a day-of-month in November; this is a cataloguing artefact, not a second authority. Per this chapter's convention the discrepancy is flagged, not silently reconciled, and the as-written date governs. (O.S.: Kassel/Hesse used the Julian calendar at this date.)
- ***Cassellis*** = **Kassel** (locative; this chapter's convention).

**Named cruxes**

- **Dateline label-vs-dateline discrepancy** (19 October as written vs. 14 November catalogued) — resolved in favour of the dateline, discrepancy explained above; this alone holds the grade below Secure.

translation.warrant: **Not collated against Dreyer** — no page reference for this letter, so the grade is capped at Probable however sound the translation looks. the edition gives no page reference for this letter (49-letter set with no Dreyer extract), so by the audit's rule this is audited against the transcribed original alone and capped at grade Probable regardless of outcome. Checked opening/closing titulature, every proper name (Alhazen, Vitello/Witelo lib.7/lib.10 P.51 and P.55), every number (60 parts 48 min 50 sec; 30 degrees/120 degrees), the date '14. Calend. Nouemb. Anno 87' against the English 'the 14th before the Kalends of November, the year 87', and every clause of the optical argument (aer crassior, the triangle ACX/ACO demonstration, the diaphanum-identity conclusion) sentence by sentence against the published English. No fabrication, omission, mistranslation, hedge-loss, or flipped negation found; hedges ('vt opinor', 'quod tamen vix mihi credendum erat') are preserved. No Dreyer collation performed.

documents.abstract: Addresses the question, forwarded from Duke Ulrich of Mecklenburg, of whether Tobias Möller's or Andreas Rosa's assignment of planetary rulers for 1588 is correct.
documents.incipit: MEINEN freuntlichen grues mitt wunschung alles guettes alzeitt beforr. Edler, Ehrnvester, …

text.original:
ERLIG OCH VELBYRDIG MANDT HEINRICH BELOFF THILL SPÖTTROP KONGL. MAYT. BEFALNINGS-MANDTT PAA SKIFFHUSZ MIN KERE SWOGER OCH SYNDERLIG GODE VEN GANSKE VENLIG THILSKREFFUEN.

MEINEN freuntlichen grues mitt wunschung alles guettes alzeitt beforr. Edler, Ehrnvester, freundtlicher lieber Schwager vnd besonder vortraweter freundt. Neben Dancksagung fur vielfeltige erzeigete wolthaten, kan ich dir freundtlicher wolmeinung nicht verhalten, das ich dein schreiben habe entpfangen vnd darinne ein Copie des Durchleuchtigen Hochgebornen Fursten vnd Herren, Hertzog VLRICHS zu Mechelburg an dir geschreibene breiffs, worauss ich erfahre, das ihr furstliche Gnade begehrett von mir gnedichlich zu wissen, welcher meines erachtens von den beiden Prognosticatoribus TOBIA MOLLER vnd ANDREA ROSA dem Zeill neher zutreffet, ihn dem daß der eine ihn diesem zukunfftigen 88 Jhar den Regenten des Jhars Iovem vnd Venerem, der ander Saturnum vnd Martem setzet, darahn sie nicht alleine keins theils einig sein, sondern wie ihr Furstliche Gnade schreibet, gahr widerwertiger meinung haben. Dan der eine macht beide beneficos Planetas, der ander beide maleficos (wie sie die Astrologi nennen) zum Regenten im selbigen Jhar, welchs gar contrarie bedeuttung bringett. Hierauff kan ich dir freundlicher meinung nicht bergen, das wiewoll ich in die Astrologische Sachen, welche bedeuttung auß dem gestirn herholen vnd weißagunge tractiren, mich nicht gerne einlasse, dieweill darauff nicht vhill zu bawen ist, Sondern allein die Astronomiam, welche den wunderlichen lauff des gestirns erforschett, in einen gewissen vnd rechtmeßigen ordnung zu bringen mich etzliche Jhar her bemuhe, dan darahn kan durch rechtgeschaffene Instrumenten nach Geometrisch vnd Arithmetisch grundt vnd gewisheit die eigentliche warheitt durch langwirigen fleiß vnd arbeitt gefunden werden, So habe ich doch nach ihrer Furstlicher gnaden begerung beide Prognostica, die du mihr zuschickest (die ich doch nicht, wie du gemeinett hast, zuvor gehatt habe, dan ich niemals pflege solche practicen wider zu kauffen, noch zu lesen, ne bonas horas male collocem) durchgesehen, den mangel, worahn es hafftett, das sie so widerwertige Iudicia stellen, daraus zu suchen, vnd befinde, das sie in ihre Rechnung gar vnterscheidliche fundament gebraucht haben. Dan der eine, nemlich MOLLERUS, bawett sein Calculation auf des hocherfarnen COPERNICI rechnung, der ander, ROSA, auff die alte durch des Königs ALPHONSI in Hispanien liberalitet gemachte Tabeln, die man darumb die Alphonsinische nennett. Hirauß kömpt es, das der eine den anfang des Jhars in æquinoctio verno setzet ahm 10 tag Martij bey Neun vhr nach mittage, der ander ahm selbigen tag, aber vmb 2 Stunden nach der vorgehende Mitternacht, daß also zwischen beide ihre rechnung schier 19 gantze Stunden verlauffen, in welchen der himmel sich gar vil vorendern thutt, vnd kan gar ein ander Astrologisch Iudicium darauß fallen, eben so wol als wen dar ein gantzes Jhar oder noch mehr zwischen wehre: Das darumb nicht zuvorwundern ist, das diese beide Astrologi in domino Anni nicht vberein stimmen, weil sie den auß der Figura Cœli introitus Solis in Arietem, wan daß vorbemelte æquinoctium vernum geschicht, pflegen herholen. Wiewol es auch lichtlich geschehn kan, das wan sie schon gleichmeßige Tabeln vnd rechnungen volgeten, das sie gleichwoll in Dominis Anni vnd ihren gantzen weissagungen gar widerwertige meinungen können fürgeben, das darauß leichtlich zu probiren ist, daß wan man hundertt der Prognosticken lisset, so befindett sich doch gahr selten, das einer mitt dem andern concordierit, dan sie bawen nicht alle auff gleichformige grundt ihn ihren Iudicijs vnd haben vntherscheidliche proceß vnd ahnleitungen. Es sein auch diese Astrologische weissagungen wie ein cothurnus, den man kan auff ein jeder Bein ziehen, gros vnd klein, wie man will. Darumb ich auch niemals dar von ettwas Sonderlichs gehalten habe. Das ich aber Kong. May. meinen Gnedigsten Herren jhärlich ein solches Astrologisch Prognosticon untherteniglich zustelle, mus ich in dem nach ihre May. befell vnd willen thun, wiewoll ich selbst nicht vill darauf halte vnd nicht gerne mitt solchen zweiffelhafftigen prædictionibus vmbgehe, darin man die eigenttliche warheitt nicht durchauß erforschen mag, wie sonst in Geometria vnd Arithmetica, darauff die Astronomia durch hulff der vleißigen observation ihm lauff des Himels gebawet wirtt. Dennoch dieweill ihr Furstliche Gnade gnedichlich begertt von mihr zu wissen, welchen von den beiden ich beifellig sey, was den dominis Anni also widerwertiger weiß von ihnen gestellet thutt ahnlangen, So kan ich hierauff nicht anders sagen, dan das ihrer beiden rechnung vnd iudicium gehtt auß ein vormeinten vnrichtigen grundt. Dan weder die Alphonsinischen, noch die Copernianischen Tabeln, welchen sie folgen, geben den justen lauff der Sonnen, wie er ahn sich selbst am Himmel geschichtt, vnd ist hierinne kein geringe vnterscheidt, wie auß meiner eigenen Restitution vnd vornewrung in Rechnung des lauffs der Sonnen zusehen ist, welche ich auf etzliche vorgehende Jharen durch große vnd rechtmeßige Instrumenten augenscheinlich vom Himel selbst her ab, durch fleißige observation vnd warnemungen genomen habe, auß welchen sich befindet, das des Jhars Anfang in æquinoctio verno, darauß die Astrologi ihre vrtheil nehmen, geschicht ahm 1O tag Martij 8⅔ stunde nach der vorigen Mitternacht, welchs bey 7 stunden speder ist, als ANDREAS ROSA gesetzt hat, und 12 stunden fruer, als TOBIAS MOLLERUS meinett, darauß den vhil ein andere Constitution des himels zur Zeitt des æquinoctij einfeltt, als ein jetzlicher von ihnen gefunden hat, worauff auch ein ander vrtheill folgett, vnd auch wol andere domini Anni, wie sie es nennen (darauß doch nicht vhil zuholen ist), mögen gesetz werden. Was aber mene meinung sey ahnlangende Astrologische gitzung vber dis kunfftige 88 Jhar, habe ich Königl. May. meinen gnedigsten Herren ihn einen geschriebenen Prognostick vnterteniglich auffgezeignett, welchs ich auch ihre Furstliche Gnade gerne wolte vnterteniglich mitteilen, aber ich habe keine vberige Exemplar dar von, wan ihr Furstliche Gnade lesset bey ihr May. darumb ahnlangen, wird ihr Furst. Gna. wol ein abschrifft dar von bekomen. Ich bin darinne gentzlich nicht der meinung, daß solche gahr große vorenderunge in diesen negstkunftigen Jhar vorhanden sein, als die Astrologi auß etzlichen altten reimen, die sie den Regiomontano zumessen, furgeben, dan ich befinde im Constitution des Himels keine Sonderliche vrsachen darzu, sondern achte, das dis kunfftige Jhar wird den vorgehenden gleichmeßig sein, vnd in zimlichen guten wesen, in allen Sachen, sich erzeigen, aleine wo zuuor krieg vnd vneinigkeitt aufferwecktt ist, dar möchte es wol ettwas weitter einreißen. Vnd kan ihr Furstliche gnade meine meinung vom Astrologischen iudicio vber das gantze Jhar auß vorbemelten Prognostico, welchs ich Köng. May. meinen gnedigsten herren vnterteniglich habe zugesteltt, weitter erfahren. Dis habe ich auff dein guttwilliges schreiben vnd beger nicht wöllen vntherlassen zu antworten. Bitte gar deinstlich, du wollest vnbeschwert sein vnd mitt erster gelegenheitt ihr Furstliche Gnade hierauff meine antwortt vnd meinunge vnterteniglichen von meinett wegen zuvorstehn geben. Worin ich sonst ihre Furstliche gnaden zu willen vnd gefallen sein kan, bin ich alzeitt mit aller deinstlichkeitt vnterteniglich erböttig.

Lieber Schwager, nach dem ich so gutte gelegenheitt habe, kan ich nicht vnterlassen, dich in einer Sachen, darahn mihr vhil gelegen ist, vnd darinne du mihr wol itzunder konnest behulfflich sein, zu besuchen, vnd gebe dir darumb gantz freundtlich zuwissen, das nach dem ich itzunder in meiner eigenen alhie angerichten Druckerey ein Astronomisk Buch lasse außgehn, welchs zimlich groß wird fallen, vnd mihr baldt Druckpapir darzu vonnötten mangeln wirt, vmb wes wegen ich meine botschafft auff vhil örten außgehabt, vnd gleichwol keines der größe, wie zu dem wercke vonnöten, bekommen können, habe ich darumb ergistern widerumb im Land zu Mechelburg dem lassen nachstellen, dieweill ich vormercke, das alda zu Graubow vnd Neustat zwey gutte papir Mölen vorhanden sein, vnd habe die beide Ambtleuthe ahn den selbigen örtern, nemlich IOHAN HELDORP vnd STELLAN WAKENITZ, zugeschrieben, das sie wolten mihr so vhil zugefallen sein, vnd den papirmachern alda befehl geben, daß sie mihr mitt dem Allerersten etzliche ballen Druckpapir nach der größe des vbergeschichten forms wolten forfertigen, welchs ich dan zu danck ihnen will lassen bezahlen, so baldt ich es holen lasse. Aber die weil ich diesen beiden Amptleutten villicht mach vnbekantt sein, ist mein gantz fleißige bitte ahn dir, du woltest so woll thun vnd ihnen von meinet wegen hierumbe auch zuschreiben, das sie mihr darinne wolten zugefallen sein, vnd du wollest auch so woll thun vnd einen von deinen gutten bekanten ahm Furstlichen hoffe zuschreiben, das er bey meinen Gnedigsten Hern Hertzog VLRICH wolte von meinett wegen vnthertenigen ahnlangung thun, das auß ihrer Furstlich Gnaden authoritet vnd befehl alles möchte mitt dem befurderlichsten zugehn, das ich mitt erster Muglichkeit könte ein 14 oder 15 Ballen papir alda auff ihr Furstliche Gnaden papirmöllen beckomen, nach solcher größe und gestalt, wie ich dir hier neben ein proba schicke. Ich will gerne bezalen, was die papirmeister darfur haben sollen. Vnd du woltest darneben auch lassen vnterteniglich befördern, das ihr Furst. Gn. wolte mihr gnedichlich furgunnen, wan das papir fertig vnd bezalt ist, das es möchte von einen Amptman zum andem biß gen Rostock gefurett werden, vnd alda den Hern Doctori HENRICO BRUCÆO vberlübert, das ichs von dannen mitt dem allerersten schiff möchte hierein beckommen. Wan du mihr hierinne in der gestaltt zu gefallen sein woltest, wie ich auch ahn deinem gutten willen keinen zueifel trage, vnd mihr dis zuwege bringen, beide bey ihr Furstlichen Gnaden selbst, vnd auch bey den Amptleutten, thetest du mir einen sonderlichen deinst vnd wolgefallen dar mitt. Dan mihr gahr viell daran gelegen ist, das ich mitt dem ersten solchs papir in einer gutten menge beckomen möchte. Vnd so ich in einiger sachen von meinen vormuegen dier jemals widerumb zu deinst und danckbarckeitt sein kan, wil ich alzeitt mehr dan guttwillig gefunden werden, vnd thue dich hiermitt sambt deiner lieben haußfrawen dem Almechtigen Gott befehlen. Du wollest auch meiner lieben Mutterschuester Fraw Maren und deiner lieben Hausfrawe, ihrer tochter, von meinett wegen vhil gutternacht sagen.

Datum Vraniborg den 7 Decemb. Anno etc. 87.
Tui amantissimus
TYCHO BRAHE, Manu propria.
text.english:
**To the honourable and well-born man Henrik Below of Spøttrup, His Royal Majesty's prefect at Skivehus, my dear brother-in-law and especially good friend, written in all friendliness.**

My friendly greeting, with the wish of all good things, at all times beforehand. Noble, honour-firm, friendly dear brother-in-law and particularly trusted friend. Besides my thanks for the manifold kindnesses you have shown, I cannot withhold from you, in friendly good will, that I have received your letter and in it a copy of the letter written to you by the Most Serene, High-born Prince and Lord, Duke Ulrich of Mecklenburg, from which I learn that His Princely Grace desires graciously to know from me which of the two prognosticators, in my judgement, comes nearer the mark — Tobias Möller and Andreas Rosa — in that the one sets Jupiter and Venus as the rulers of this coming year [']88, the other Saturn and Mars; in which they are not only in no part agreed, but, as His Princely Grace writes, hold quite contrary opinions. For the one makes both the beneficent planets [*beneficos Planetas*], the other both the malefic ones [*maleficos*] (as the astrologers call them) ruler in the selfsame year, which brings quite a contrary signification. On this I cannot conceal from you, in friendly intent, that — although I do not gladly involve myself in astrological matters, which fetch their significations out of the stars and treat of soothsayings, since not much is to be built upon them, but for some years now have laboured solely to bring astronomy, which investigates the wondrous course of the stars, into a sure and well-grounded order, for therein the proper truth can be found, by long-lasting diligence and labour, through rightly-fashioned instruments on a geometric and arithmetic foundation and certainty — I have nonetheless, at His Princely Grace's request, gone through both the prognostica that you sent me (which, however, I had not, as you supposed, had before, for I never am wont to buy such practica back, nor to read them, lest I spend good hours ill [*ne bonas horas male collocem*]), in order to seek out from them the defect in which it lies that they set down such contrary judgements [*Iudicia*]; and I find that they have used quite different foundations in their reckoning. For the one, namely Möller, builds his calculation upon the reckoning of the highly-experienced Copernicus; the other, Rosa, upon the old tables made through the liberality of King Alfonso in Spain, which one therefore calls the Alfonsine. From this it comes that the one sets the beginning of the year at the vernal equinox on the 10th day of March at about nine o'clock in the afternoon, the other on the same day, but at about 2 hours after the preceding midnight, so that thus between the two reckonings nearly 19 whole hours run by, in which the heaven alters very much, and a quite different astrological judgement can fall out from it, just as much as if a whole year or more lay between: so that it is not therefore to be wondered at that these two astrologers do not agree on the ruler of the year [*domino Anni*], because they are wont to derive it from the figure of the heaven [*Figura Coeli*] at the entry of the Sun into Aries, when the aforesaid vernal equinox occurs. Although it can also easily happen that, even were they to follow tables and reckonings that matched, they could nonetheless put forth quite contrary opinions in the rulers of the year [*Dominis Anni*] and in their whole soothsayings — which is easily to be proved from this, that when one reads a hundred of the prognostica, it is yet found very seldom that one agrees [*concordierit*] with another, for they do not all build upon a uniform foundation in their judgements and have different procedures and methods. These astrological soothsayings are also like a buskin [*cothurnus*] that one can draw onto any leg, big and small, as one will. For which reason, too, I have never held anything special of them. But that I yearly submit such an astrological prognosticon humbly to His Royal Majesty, my Most Gracious Lord — in that I must act according to His Majesty's command and will, although I myself hold not much of it and do not gladly deal with such doubtful predictions [*praedictionibus*], in which one may not thoroughly investigate the proper truth, as otherwise in geometry and arithmetic, upon which astronomy is built by the help of diligent observation in the course of the heaven. Nonetheless, since His Princely Grace graciously desires to know from me to which of the two I incline — as concerns the rulers of the year [*dominis Anni*] thus set down by them in contrary manner — I can say nothing else upon this than that the reckoning and judgement of both of them proceeds from a supposed faulty foundation. For neither the Alfonsine nor the Copernican tables, which they follow, give the true [*justen*] course of the Sun as it occurs in itself in the heaven; and herein is no small difference, as is to be seen from my own restoration [*Restitution*] and renewal in the reckoning of the course of the Sun, which I have, over several preceding years, taken visibly down from the heaven itself by large and rightful instruments, through diligent observation and observings; from which it is found that the beginning of the year at the vernal equinox, from which the astrologers take their judgement, occurs on the 10th day of March, 8⅔ hours after the previous midnight, which is about 7 hours later than Andreas Rosa has set, and 12 hours earlier than Tobias Möller supposes; from which then a very different constitution of the heaven falls out at the time of the equinox than each of them has found, upon which also a different judgement follows, and indeed other rulers of the year [*domini Anni*], as they call them (out of which, however, not much is to be fetched), may be set down. But what my opinion may be concerning the astrological estimate over this coming year ['] 88, I have humbly noted down for His Royal Majesty, my most gracious Lord, in a written prognosticon, which I would also gladly impart humbly to His Princely Grace; but I have no spare copy of it. If His Princely Grace will make application to His Majesty for it, His Princely Grace will well obtain a transcript of it. Therein I am altogether not of the opinion that such very great changes are at hand in this next-coming year, as the astrologers put forth out of certain old rhymes which they ascribe to Regiomontanus; for I find in the constitution of the heaven no special causes for it, but reckon that this coming year will be like the preceding ones, and will show itself in fairly good condition in all things — only, where war and discord have been stirred up before, there it might well break in somewhat further. And His Princely Grace can learn more fully my opinion of the astrological judgement over the whole year from the aforesaid prognosticon which I have humbly submitted to His Royal Majesty, my most gracious Lord. This I would not omit to answer upon your kindly letter and request. I beg quite dutifully that you would be unburdened [by it] and at the first opportunity convey to His Princely Grace, upon this, my answer and opinion humbly on my behalf. Wherein I can otherwise be at His Princely Grace's will and pleasure, I am at all times humbly ready with all dutifulness.

Dear brother-in-law, since I have so good an opportunity, I cannot omit to call upon you in a matter that much concerns me, and in which you can well be of help to me just now; and I therefore make known to you quite in friendliness that, since I am now letting an astronomical book go forth from my own printing-house set up here, which will turn out fairly large, and I shall soon lack printing-paper for it — on which account I have had my errand out in many places, and yet could obtain none of the size as is needed for the work — I have therefore the day before yesterday again had inquiry made for it in the land of Mecklenburg, since I observe that there at Grabow and Neustadt two good paper-mills are to be found; and I have written to the two officials at those same places, namely Johan Heldorp and Stellan Wakenitz, that they would do me so much favour and give order to the papermakers there that they should at the very first prepare for me several bales of printing-paper according to the size of the form sent over [to them], which I will then thankfully have paid to them as soon as I have it fetched. But since I am perhaps still unknown to these two officials, my quite diligent request to you is that you would be so good as to write to them too on my behalf about this, that they would do me the favour therein; and that you would also be so good as to write to one of your good acquaintances at the Princely court, that he would on my behalf make humble application to my Most Gracious Lord Duke Ulrich, that out of His Princely Grace's authority and command everything might proceed with all furtherance, so that I might at the first possibility obtain there at His Princely Grace's paper-mills some 14 or 15 bales of paper, of such size and form as I send you a sample [*proba*] herewith. I will gladly pay what the paper-masters are to have for it. And you would besides also have it humbly furthered that His Princely Grace would graciously grant me, when the paper is finished and paid for, that it might be carried from one official to another as far as Rostock, and there delivered over to Master Doctor Heinrich Brucaeus, so that from there I might obtain it in here by the very first ship. If you would be willing to do me favour in this manner herein — as I bear no doubt of your good will — and bring this about for me, both with His Princely Grace himself and also with the officials, you would do me a special service and pleasure thereby. For it much concerns me that I might at the first obtain such paper in a good quantity. And if in any matter within my power I can ever again be of service and gratitude to you, I will at all times be found more than willing; and I herewith commend you, together with your dear housewife, to Almighty God. You would also, on my behalf, say many a goodnight to my dear mother's-sister Mistress Maren and to your dear housewife, her daughter.

Given at Uraniborg, the 7th of December, in the year etc. [']87.
Your most loving,
Tycho Brahe, with his own hand.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender / hand.** Tycho Brahe, writing from Uraniborg on Hven. The subscription *Manu propria* ("with his own hand") asserts an autograph signature.
- **Recipient.** *Heinrich Beloff / Henrik Below* (Below of Spøttrup, d. 1606), Danish nobleman, here styled *Kongl. Mayt. Befalningsmandt paa Skiffhusz* — His Royal Majesty's *lensmand* (prefect/governor) at **Skivehus** (Skive, Jutland). Repeatedly addressed as *Schwager* — **brother-in-law** in the period's loose sense (a relation by marriage); the close kin link is made explicit at the close, where Tycho greets *meiner lieben Mutterschuester Fraw Maren* ("my dear mother's-sister Mistress Maren") and *deiner lieben Hausfrawe, ihrer tochter* ("your dear housewife, her daughter") — i.e. Below's wife is the daughter of Tycho's maternal aunt, making them cousins-by-marriage. *Spøttrop / Spøttrup* and *Skiffhusz / Skivehus* kept as the period forms with modern glosses.
- **Address-line language.** The opening superscription is in **chancery Danish** (*ERLIG OCH VELBYRDIG MANDT … MIN KERE SWOGER … GANSKE VENLIG THILSKREFFUEN*, "to the honourable and well-born man … my dear brother-in-law … written in all friendliness"); the letter body is **Early New High German**. The code-switch is preserved by this chapter's convention
- **Occasion (per Dreyer,** Opera Omnia *and* Tycho Brahe*, p. 155).** Duke Ulrich of Mecklenburg — father of Queen Sophie of Denmark, hence Tycho's interest — had procured two prognostica for 1588 and, finding them irreconcilable, asked Below to have Tycho adjudicate. **Duke Ulrich III of Mecklenburg(-Güstrow)** (1527–1603); *Hertzog VLRICH zu Mechelburg / Mecklenburg*. *Ihr Furstliche Gnade* = "His Princely Grace" (the Duke); *Kong. May. / Königl. May.* = His Royal Majesty (Frederik II of Denmark), Tycho's patron, to whom he owed an annual prognostication.
- **The two astrologers.** *Tobias Möller* (*Tobia Moller / Mollerus*) and *Andreas Rosa* (*Andrea Rosa*), authors of competing printed prognostica for 1588. Tycho's diagnosis: Möller computed on **Copernicus**'s numbers (*COPERNICI rechnung*), Rosa on the **Alfonsine Tables** (*die Alphonsinische*, "made through the liberality of King Alfonso [X] in Spain"); their equinox times differed by nearly 19 hours, hence the contrary "rulers of the year."
- **Astrology — technical terms.** *Prognosticon / Prognostica / practica / practicen* — yearly astrological forecasts. *Regenten des Jhars / dominus Anni / domini Anni* → **ruler(s) of the year** (the planet(s) governing an annual revolution), a term Tycho flags as their jargon (*wie sie es nennen*, "as they call them"). *beneficos Planetas / maleficos* → the **beneficent / malefic planets** (Jupiter, Venus vs. Saturn, Mars); kept as Latin in source, glossed. *Figura Coeli* → the **figure of the heaven** (the horoscope chart cast for the moment of the Sun's *introitus … in Arietem*, the Sun's entry into **Aries** at the vernal equinox). *Iudicium / Iudicia / iudicio* → **judgement(s)** (the astrological verdict). *Astrologische gitzung* → rendered "astrological estimate/conjecture"; *gitzung* (cf. *Gissung*, conjecture/guess) is a non-standard chancery form, read as "estimate."
- **Astronomy.** *aequinoctium vernum / aequinoctio verno* → **vernal equinox**. *Restitution vnd vornewrung* → **restoration and renewal** (of the Sun's theory) — Tycho's *restitutio / instauratio astronomiae* programme; here applied to his corrected solar tables. *Instrumenten … nach Geometrisch vnd Arithmetisch grundt* → **instruments … on a geometric and arithmetic foundation**. *observation vnd warnemungen* → "observation and observings" (*Wahrnehmungen*, observations/percepts), the doubled term kept.
- **The solar-equinox figures (Tycho's central technical claim).** The two almanac-makers placed the 1588 vernal equinox on 10 March, one "at about nine o'clock in the afternoon [p.m.]," the other "at about 2 hours after the preceding midnight" — c. 19 hours apart. Tycho's own observationally-grounded value: **10 March, 8⅔ hours after the previous midnight** — "about 7 hours later than Andreas Rosa has set, and 12 hours earlier than Tobias Möller supposes." (The 8⅔ h figure is printed *1O* with a capital-O for the numeral in the source's "1O tag Martij"; reproduced as printed and read as "10th day of March.")
- ***Regiomontano … altten reimen*** — the "old rhymes ascribed to **Regiomontanus**": the notorious prophetic verses on 1588 as a year of vast upheaval (the *"octogesimus octavus … annus mirabilis"* prophecy widely circulated under Regiomontanus's name). Tycho discounts it, finding "no special causes" in the heaven, expecting an ordinary year — except where war is already kindled, which "might break in somewhat further."
- ***cothurnus*** — a **buskin** (the loose-fitting tragic actor's boot that fits either foot); a stock simile for something accommodated to any view. Tycho: the prognostica are "like a buskin one can draw onto any leg." Latin term kept, glossed.
- **The book / paper request.** *ein Astronomisk Buch … in meiner eigenen … Druckerey* — "an astronomical book [from] my own printing-house": the volume Tycho was preparing on the press at Uraniborg, requiring large quantities of *Druckpapir* (printing-paper) of a specific *form* (sheet size), of which he encloses a *proba* (sample). He seeks **14–15 bales** from the ducal paper-mills at **Grabow** (*Graubow*) and **Neustadt** (*Neustat*) in Mecklenburg, via the officials *Johan Heldorp* and *Stellan Wakenitz* (*Ambtleuthe / Amptleutte* — bailiffs/officials), with the finished paper to be relayed *biß gen Rostock* (to **Rostock**) and there delivered to **Heinrich Brucaeus** (*Hern Doctori HENRICO BRUCAeO*, the Rostock professor, this chapter's convention) for shipment to Hven.
- **Latin code-switches in the German body** (kept in source, glossed in translation): *ne bonas horas male collocem* ("lest I spend good hours ill"); *beneficos Planetas / maleficos*; *contrarie*; *Iudicia / iudicio*; *Figura Coeli*, *introitus Solis in Arietem*, *aequinoctium vernum*, *domino/domini/dominis Anni*; *concordierit*, *proceß*; *praedictionibus*, *observation*, *Geometria / Arithmetica*, *Astronomia*, *Constitution*, *Restitution*; the subscription *Tui amantissimus … Manu propria*.
- **Calendar / place.** *Datum Vraniborg den 7 Decemb. Anno etc. 87* = "Given at Uraniborg, 7 December [15]87" — **Old Style** (Denmark kept the Julian calendar until 1700). The catalogue label ("1587. 7. december. Uraniborg") agrees with the dateline; no discrepancy. The internal date *10 March* / equinox for "this coming 88 year" is likewise O.S. — note that on the Julian calendar the vernal equinox fell near 10 March, consistent with the figures discussed; not converted.

text.original:
CLARISSIMO ERUDITISSIMOQUE VIRO D. DOCTORI THADDÆO HAGECIO AB HAYK, MEDICO ET MATHEMATICO EXCELLENTISSIMO, AMICO SUO SINCERE DILECTO.
PRAG.

RARIORES ad te dare literas internunciorum cogit penuria, eruditissime charissimeque D. D. THADDÆE, et locorum quibus disiungimur intercapedo vota nostra plurimum impedit. Nactus itaque iam tandem aliqualem occasionem literas mittendi per Studiosum quendam Silesium me unâ cum quibusdam alijs hîc invisentem, non intermittendum duxi, quin brevibus ad te scriberem. Librum tuum de Nova Stella et Cometis misi iamdudum Francofurtum ad eundem hominem, de quo mihi indicâras, nec dubito te interea temporis eum recepisse. Quod si illum edere adhuc animus est, suaderem ut ea, quae in Cometa anni 77 minus considerate a te proposita sunt, vel supprimas vel emendes. Meum de hoc eodem Cometa iudicium percipies ex eo quem tibi nunc mitto libro, in quo secundus tomus operis nostri de recentioribus aetherei Mundi Phaenomenis continetur. Primus est de Stella Nova exquisitiori diligentia quam antea considerata, quem typis absolvere Gallici privilegij defectus, quod Caesariano adiungere constitui, hactenus impedivit. Nunc vero quoniam ante paucos dies idipsum adeptus sum, nihil obstabit nisi otij oportunitas, quominus eius etiam libri evulgationem adornem. Tertius est de tribus alijs Cometis, qui postmodum nobis illuxerunt et in alto aethere curriculum suum non minus quam ille, de quo liber modo transmissus agit, absolverunt. Quod autem in hoc ipso libro, ubi tua placita in eodem Cometa sub disquisitionem mathematicam voco, a te multoties dissentiri me res ipsa cogat, non est quod sinistrius interpreteris; scis enim me solo veritatis amore et libertate Philosophica idipsum agere, nulloque tua insectandi elevandique animo id a me fieri. In priori libro de Stella Nova tum etiam in tertio, ubi de Cometa anni 80 agitur, oportuniorem invenio commoditatem tecum magna ex parte sentiendi, tuaque dignis encomijs extollendi. Si quos habes Italicos, Hispanicos vel Gallicos authores, qui de Nova Stella aliquid commentati sunt, rogo ut eorum scripta Latinitate, si fieri possit, donata, mecum communices, unâque si quos alios Cometarum praecedentibus aliquot annis visorum descriptores peculiares nec ubique obvios in promtu habueris. Librum illum de Cometa anni 1531 ab APIANO seorsim editum nondum vidi, quemadmodum neque IOHANNIS PENAe Galli scriptum, quod PRÆTORIUS in descriptione huius Cometae anni 77 citat. Si horum me participem reddideris, meis votis plurimum subveneris. Memini me librum quendam Astrologicum a te dono accepisse, cum Ratisbonae simul essemus, qui Planetarum influentias peculiari quadam ratione per accessum ad Terram vel ab ea recessum proponeret; eum in patriam reversus nuspiam invenire potui. Si eius aliquod exemplar denuo per te obtinuere, diligentius illud inposterum conservabo, evolvamque accuratius; existimo enim quaedam in eo a veritate non dissentanea contineri, si dextre considerentur, et cum caeteris requisitis debite conferantur.

Ubi totum opus, de quo supra dixi, typis meis excusum fuerit, tibi illud transmittam. Interea hanc secundam partem per otium evolve, mihique tuum de ea iudicium ingenue significa. Invenies in eo novam orbium coelestium dispositionem, a me non ita dudum adinventam, quae quo penitius fuerit considerata, eo magis tibi placebit. Ego hanc non solum apparentijs consonam, sed etiam in rei veritate ita se habere non dubito, quod Ptolomaicae et Copernianae assumtiones nequaquam praestant. Sed de his nunc plura scribere temporis penuria et epistolae leges prohibent. Tu itaque, optime THADDÆE, quam felicissime vale et ingravescentis aetatis difficultates forti animo tolera, meque per occasionem quamcunque oblatam literis revisere non intermitte.

Iterum vale.

Datae Uraniburgi die 3. Maij Anno 1588.
Tuus
TYCHO BRAHE.
text.english:
**To the most renowned and most learned man, Master Doctor Thaddaeus Hagecius of Hájek, most excellent physician and mathematician, his sincerely beloved friend.**
Prague.

A scarcity of message-bearers compels me to send you letters too rarely, most learned and most dear Master Doctor Thaddaeus, and the distance of the places that separate us greatly hinders our wishes. Having therefore at last obtained some opportunity of sending a letter, by way of a certain Silesian student who is visiting me here together with some others, I thought it not to be neglected, but that I should write to you briefly. Your book on the New Star and on Comets I sent long ago to Frankfurt, to the same man of whom you had told me, and I do not doubt that you have received it in the meantime. But if you still have a mind to publish it, I would advise that those things which you proposed somewhat less carefully concerning the comet of the year [15]77 you either suppress or amend. My own judgement on this same comet you will gather from the book I now send you, in which is contained the second volume of our work on the more recent phenomena of the aethereal World. The first [volume] is on the New Star, examined with more exquisite diligence than before; and the lack of the French privilege — which I have resolved to add to the Imperial one — has hitherto hindered me from completing it in print. But now, since a few days ago I obtained that very thing, nothing will stand in the way, save the opportunity of leisure, of my preparing the publication of that book also. The third [volume] is on three other comets, which afterwards shone forth to us and ran their course in the high aether no less than that one which the book just sent treats of. But as for the fact that in this very book — where I summon your opinions on that same comet under a mathematical examination — the matter itself compels me to dissent from you on many points, there is no reason for you to interpret it amiss; for you know that I do this from love of truth alone and from philosophical liberty, and that it is done by me with no mind of attacking or belittling you. In the earlier book on the New Star, and also in the third, where the comet of the year [15]80 is treated, I find a more convenient occasion of agreeing with you for the most part, and of extolling your work with deserved praises. If you have any Italian, Spanish, or French authors who have written anything concerning the New Star, I ask that you share their writings with me, rendered into Latin if it can be done; and likewise if you have ready at hand any other particular describers of the comets seen in some preceding years, not everywhere to be come by. That book on the comet of the year 1531, published separately by Apian, I have not yet seen, just as neither [have I seen] the writing of the Frenchman Johannes Pena, which Praetorius cites in his description of this comet of the year [15]77. If you make me a partaker of these, you will very greatly assist my wishes. I remember that I received from you, as a gift, a certain astrological book, when we were together at Regensburg, which set forth the influences of the planets in a certain peculiar way, through their approach to the Earth or their recession from it; on returning to my homeland I could nowhere find it. If I might obtain some copy of it again through you, I shall hereafter keep it more carefully, and unfold it more accurately; for I judge that certain things are contained in it not at variance with the truth, if they be rightly considered and duly compared with the other requisites.

When the whole work of which I have spoken above shall have been printed at my press, I will send it to you. Meanwhile, unfold this second part at your leisure, and frankly signify to me your judgement of it. You will find in it a new arrangement of the celestial orbs, devised by me not so long ago, which the more deeply it is considered, the more it will please you. I do not doubt that this is not only consonant with the appearances, but also that it is so in the very truth of the matter — which the Ptolemaic and Copernican assumptions by no means achieve. But to write more of these things now, the scarcity of time and the laws of a letter forbid. Do you therefore, best Thaddaeus, fare most happily, and bear the difficulties of advancing age with a brave spirit, and do not neglect to revisit me with letters on whatever occasion is offered.

Again, farewell.
Given at Uraniborg, the 3rd day of May, in the year 1588.
Yours,
TYCHO BRAHE.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender / recipient.** Tycho Brahe, writing from Uraniborg on Hven, to *Thaddaeus Hagecius ab Hayk* = **Tadeáš Hájek z Hájku (Thaddaeus Hagecius)** (1525–1600), Bohemian physician, astronomer, and imperial physician to Rudolf II at Prague; he and Tycho had observed the 1572 nova and the comets independently and corresponded for decades. The address-superscription (*Prag.* = Prague, his residence) is preserved.
- ***Studiosum quendam Silesium*** — "a certain Silesian student," the unnamed bearer of the letter; not further identified.
- **The work announced.** *secundus tomus operis nostri de recentioribus aetherei Mundi Phaenomenis* = "the second volume of our work on the more recent phenomena of the aethereal World" — i.e. Tycho's *De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis liber secundus* (Uraniborg, 1588), the great treatise on the comet of 1577 in which the **geo-heliocentric world-system** is first published (see below). The *primus … tomus* (first volume), on the 1572 *Stella Nova*, is the projected but then-unprinted volume that eventually became the posthumous *Astronomiae instauratae progymnasmata* (1602); the *tertius* (third volume), on three further comets (those of 1580, 1582, 1585, etc.), was never completed.
- ***Stella Nova / Nova Stella*** — the **new star (nova)** of 1572 in Cassiopeia. ***Cometa anni 77*** / ***anni 80*** — the **comets of 1577 and 1580**. Tycho dates by Old-Style civil years; no calendar conversion is implied.
- ***novam orbium coelestium dispositionem … a me non ita dudum adinventam*** — "a new arrangement of the celestial orbs, devised by me not so long ago": Tycho's announcement of his own world-system (the Sun and Moon circling the Earth, the five planets circling the Sun). He claims it not merely *apparentijs consonam* ("consonant with the appearances") but true *in rei veritate* ("in the very truth of the matter"), surpassing what the *Ptolomaicae et Copernianae assumtiones* ("the Ptolemaic and Copernican assumptions") achieve. *orbium coelestium* rendered "celestial orbs" per glossary (*orbis* → orb).
- **Privileges.** *Gallici privilegij … Caesariano adiungere* — the **French [printing] privilege**, which Tycho means to **add to the Imperial one** (*Caesarianum* = the privilege granted by the Emperor). He reports having secured the French privilege "a few days ago"; its earlier lack had delayed the printing of the first volume. ("Privilege" here = an exclusive printing licence, not modernised.)
- **Other authors.** *APIANO* = **Peter Apian (Petrus Apianus)** (1495–1552), whose tract on the **comet of 1531** Tycho has not seen. *IOHANNIS PENAe Galli* = **Jean Pena (Johannes Pena)** (c. 1528–1558), the French royal mathematician (author of the preface to his Euclid *Optica*). *PRAeTORIUS* = **Johannes Praetorius (Richter)** (1537–1616), professor at Altdorf, cited as referencing Pena in his account of the 1577 comet. Identifications on first occurrence by this chapter's convention.
- ***librum quendam Astrologicum … cum Ratisbonae simul essemus*** — "a certain astrological book … when we were together at **Regensburg** (*Ratisbona*)": Tycho and Hagecius had met at Regensburg, evidently at the imperial diet/coronation of 1575. The book, treating *Planetarum influentias … per accessum ad Terram vel ab ea recessum* ("the influences of the planets … through their approach to the Earth or recession from it"), is unidentified; Tycho wishes to recover a copy.
- **Technical / astrological vocabulary.** *Phaenomena* → "phenomena"; *Planetarum influentias* → "the influences of the planets" (astrological sense kept, not modernised); *disquisitionem mathematicam* → "mathematical examination." No Greek, planet glyphs, or zodiac glyphs occur in this letter.
- **Epistolary formulae.** Opening superscription and *Iterum vale* ("Again, farewell,") preserved; *quam felicissime vale* → "fare most happily." *libertate Philosophica* → "philosophical liberty" — Tycho's standard defence of frank scientific disagreement; the hedge that his criticism carries *nullo … insectandi elevandique animo* ("no mind of attacking or belittling") is preserved, not softened.
- **Dateline.** *Datae Uraniburgi die 3. Maij Anno 1588* = "Given at **Uraniborg**, the 3rd day of May, the year 1588" (O.S.; Denmark kept the Julian calendar). The source prints the word *Datae* broken across a line (*"D / atae"*); reproduced as printed in the Source block, read as the single word *Datae* in translation. The header date (3 May 1588) matches both the dateline and the catalogue label; no discrepancy.
- Correction. Latin corrected 'atae Uraniburgi' to 'Datae Uraniburgi' (Dreyer VII p.121); the closing formula had dropped its initial letter in transmission. English unaffected.

text.original:
TYCHONI BRAHE.

IAM optimo Regi vestro laudationem pango, cuius exemplum IUNIO ad te mittam: qua re cum sim occupatus, neque diligenter scribo, neque uberius. Gratificor autem huic familiari meo HAKEN, Equiti Marchico, iuveni probo, nec abhorrenti a litteris, quarum gratia apud nos vivit. Omnino voluit te videre: facies gratum, si facies ut intelligat, te mihi peramicum; nam et alioqui te humanissimum virum sentiet.

Vale.
Rostochio X. Kalend. Iun. Anno 1588.
text.english:
**To Tycho Brahe.**

I am even now composing a panegyric of your excellent King, a copy of which I shall send you in June; and since I am occupied with this work, I write neither carefully nor at any length. But I am doing a kindness to this member of my household, Haken, a knight of the March [of Brandenburg], an upright young man, and no stranger to letters — for the sake of which he lives here among us. He very much wished to see you: you will do [me] a favour if you bring it about that he understands you to be a great friend of mine; for in any case he will find you a most courteous man.

Farewell.
From Rostock, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June [23 May], in the year 1588.

documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent.** *Johannes Caselius* = **Johannes Caselius** (Johann Kessel/Chessel, 1533–1613), the leading humanist professor of rhetoric and the *studia humanitatis*, then at the University of **Rostock** (he moved to Helmstedt in 1589). The name is not in the editorial glossary; identification supplied here. Caselius is independently attested in Tycho's orbit: Dreyer notes a Tycho letter alluding to "Professor Caselius" at Rostock, and a Caselius dedication to Christian IV is recorded among the Royal Library's holdings.
- **Place.** *Rostochio* → **Rostock** (the Hanseatic university town in Mecklenburg), by this chapter's convention; *Rostochio* is the ablative of origin ("from Rostock").
- ***optimo Regi vestro laudationem pango*** — "I am composing a panegyric of your excellent King." *Regi vestro* ("your King") is the Danish crown, addressed to Tycho as a Dane. **Contextual note (not asserted in the text):** Frederik II of Denmark had died on 4 April 1588 (O.S.); a *laudatio* of the "best King" in late May 1588 is most naturally a funeral panegyric on the late Frederik II, though the letter neither names the king nor states that he is dead — the identification with Frederik II is left as the apparatus reading and not introduced into the translation. *pango* (lit. "I set down / fasten," used esp. of composing verse or song) is rendered "composing"; the work may well be in verse.
- ***cuius exemplum IUNIO ad te mittam*** — "a copy of which I shall send you in June." *IUNIO* is the month *Iunius* (June) in the ablative of time, **not** a personal name despite the source's capitalisation; the dateline (23 May) makes "in June" coherent. *exemplum* here = "a copy" (of the text), not "an example."
- ***Gratificor … huic familiari meo HAKEN, Equiti Marchico*** — "I am doing a kindness to this member of my household, Haken, a knight of the March." *familiaris* = a member of one's household / a close associate (here apparently a young man lodging with or studying under Caselius), rendered "member of my household." *Haken* is the young man's name (left as written; unidentified). *Eques Marchicus* = "a knight of the March," i.e. a nobleman of the **Margraviate (March) of Brandenburg** — *Marchicus* "of the March/Mark"; rendered "knight of the March [of Brandenburg]," the bracketed gloss marking the editorial expansion.
- ***nec abhorrenti a litteris, quarum gratia apud nos vivit*** — "and no stranger to letters, for the sake of which he lives here among us." *non abhorrere a litteris* = not to shrink from / not to be averse to learning; the litotes is preserved ("no stranger to"). *quarum gratia apud nos vivit* = he resides at Rostock for the sake of his studies.
- ***facies gratum, si facies ut intelligat, te mihi peramicum*** — "you will do [me] a favour if you bring it about that he understands you to be a great friend of mine." *facies gratum* ("you will do a welcome thing / a favour"): the beneficiary is unexpressed and supplied as "[me]" in brackets. *peramicum* (intensive *per-* + *amicus*) = "a very great friend"; *te … peramicum* sc. *esse mihi*.
- ***nam et alioqui te humanissimum virum sentiet*** — "for in any case he will find you a most courteous man." *humanissimus* in the rhetor's idiom = most cultivated/courteous/kindly; *sentiet* = "he will perceive/find [you to be]."
- **Salutation / subscription.** The letter opens with a bare address (*TYCHONI BRAHE*, "To Tycho Brahe") and no greeting-formula, and closes with *Vale* — **Farewell**.
- **Dateline / calendar.** *Rostochio X. Kalend. Iun. Anno 1588* = "From Rostock, *ante diem decimum Kalendas Iunias*, in the year 1588." The tenth day before the Kalends of June, counted inclusively in the Roman manner (the Kalends = 1 June counts as day 1), falls on **23 May** (O.S.; Denmark and Lutheran Germany were on the Julian calendar in 1588). The Roman-calendar idiom is rendered with both the idiom and the civil date, by this chapter's convention. The catalogue *label* ("1588. 23. maj. Rostock") agrees with the as-written dateline; no discrepancy.
