documents.apparatus:
**Edition of record & witnesses.** *Tychonis Brahei et ad eum doctorum virorum epistolae ab anno 1588* (= Dreyer, *Opera Omnia* VII). MS witnesses as given in the edition: **A** = Vienna, ÖNB cod. Vindob. lat. 10686.81, described as a draft (*Kladde*) with corrections in Tycho's own hand; **B** = Pulkovo (now St Petersburg?). The superscript ⟨A⟩ markers scattered through the source mark words/readings carrying a variant or correction in witness A; they are reproduced as ⟨A⟩ sigla in the Source block and not rendered in the translation (they are not part of Tycho's text).

**Correspondent.** *Thaddaeus Hagecius ab Hayck* = **Tadeáš Hájek z Hájku** (Thaddaeus Hagecius, 1525–1600), Bohemian court physician, astronomer and astrologer to Maximilian II and Rudolf II at Prague, author of the *Dialexis de novae … stellae … apparitione* (1574). Tycho and Hagecius met at **Regensburg** in 1575 at the coronation/inauguration of Maximilian II as King of the Romans ("about fourteen years ago, when the present Emperor was being inaugurated") and corresponded for the rest of Hagecius's life.

**Persons named.**
- *Dithmarsus ex Urso denominatus* / *Ursus* = **Nicolaus Reimers Baer ("Ursus")**, of Dithmarschen (c. 1551–1600), whose *Fundamentum astronomicum* (1588), dedicated to Landgrave Wilhelm IV, set out a geoheliocentric system. This is the foundational document of the celebrated **Tycho–Ursus plagiarism controversy**; Tycho here gives his own narrative (the 1584 visit in Erik Lange's retinue; the discarded diagram with the solar orb wrongly enclosed *within* the Martian one). Rendered "plagiarism / Plagiarists" per Tycho's *plagium / Plagiarij*.
- *Ericus Langius* = **Erik Lange** (c. 1553–1613), Danish nobleman and alchemist, later betrothed to Tycho's sister Sophie Brahe; Ursus was in his service in 1584.
- *Gulielmus / Guilielmus, Hassiae Landgravius* = **Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel**, dedicatee of Ursus's book.
- *Dominus Curtius* = **Jacob Kurz von Senftenau (Jacobus Curtius)**, Imperial Vice-Chancellor (*Imperij Procancellarius*) and privy councillor to Rudolf II, himself learned in mathematics; he had received Tycho's *De mundi … phaenomenis* (the "second book") via Hagecius.
- *Winchlerus* = **Nicolaus Winckler** (Winkler) of Hall, physician-astronomer, author of a tract on the comet of 1580 which Tycho criticized; the *tractatiuncula* on "page 446" is Tycho's critique within the *De mundi … phaenomenis* (1588). Tycho's metaphors (*forti dolabra dedolatus … acriori pectine depexendus … latus claudere ultimum*) are kept as figures ("hewn down with a strong axe," "combed with a sharper comb," "close the rank in the last place").
- *Maesthlinus* = **Michael Maestlin** (1550–1631), Tübingen astronomer (Kepler's teacher), whose cometary hypothesis (heliocentric, with the 1577 comet circulating about the Sun) Tycho here defends in part against Hagecius's strictures.
- *Praetorius* = **Johannes Praetorius** (1537–1616), professor of mathematics at Altdorf.
- *Raymundus* = the *impudens Raymundus* who attacked Hagecius — most plausibly **Raimarus / Raymarus** (a polemical opponent); the exact identity is not made explicit. *Theologastri* rendered "theologasters" (contemptuous diminutive, kept).
- *Regiomontanus Francus* = **Johannes Regiomontanus** (1436–1476), of Franconia, on cometary parallax. *Digessaeus Anglus* = **Thomas Digges** (c. 1546–1595), English author on the 1572 nova and cometary parallax. *Witichius* = **Paul Wittich** of Wrocław (c. 1546–1586), mathematician, whose library and Copernicus annotations Tycho here tries to acquire from Wittich's sister at **Wrocław** (*Vratislavia*).
- *Munosius Hispanus* = **Jerónimo Muñoz** (Hieronymus Munyos), Valencian author on the 1572 nova. *Cornelius Frangipani* = the Italian writer on the nova cited in Hagecius's *Dialexis*. *Apianus* = **Peter Apian** (1495–1552); his *Astronomicum* (the *Astronomicum Caesareum*, 1540) and a separate tract on the comet of **1532**. *Fracastorius* = **Girolamo Fracastoro**, *Homocentrica* (1538). *Ioannes Vogelinus Viennensis* = **Johann Vögelin** of Vienna, who claimed a parallax of c. 35° for the 1532 comet (Tycho calls it "monstrous"). *Ioannes Poena Gallus* = **Jean Pena** (c. 1528–1558), French mathematician, on the fluidity of the heavens.
- *Wernerus* = **Johann Werner** of Nuremberg, *De motu octavae sphaerae* (and the tract on the *cornicula* — see crux below). *Dominus Fabricius bonae memoriae* = **Paul Fabricius** (1519–1589), Imperial physician-mathematician at Vienna, here reported newly dead; he had obtained Werner's book for Tycho.
- *Andreas Duditius* = **Andreas Dudith** (1533–1589), humanist and former bishop, recently deceased; Tycho mourns him.
- *Trapezuntius* = **George of Trebizond** (1396–1486), whose commentaries (on Ptolemy's *Almagest*) Hagecius had asked about publishing.
- *Archidux Maximilianus* = **Archduke Maximilian III of Austria** (Grand Master of the Teutonic Order, *der Deutschmeister*), the Habsburg claimant in the Polish succession war of 1587–88, defeated and captured at Byczyna (1588) and released in 1589 — Tycho rejoices at his safe return.
- *Henricus Ranzovius* = **Heinrich Rantzau** (1526–1598), royal *Statthalter* (Vicar) in Holstein, scholar and Tycho's patron-correspondent, who urged the publication of Tycho's learned correspondence (realized as the *Epistolarum astronomicarum liber primus*, 1596).
- *Ioannes Craig Scotus* = **John Craig** (d. 1620), Scottish physician at Edinburgh (later to James VI), the Aristotelian critic of Tycho's cometary doctrine against whom Tycho wrote the enclosed *Apologetica responsio*.

**Places.** *Praga* = Prague; *Hafnia* = Copenhagen; *Uraniburgum* = Uraniborg on Hven; *Ratispona* = Regensburg; *Rostochium* = Rostock; *Lubeca* = Lübeck; *Hamburgum* = Hamburg; *Vratislavia* = Wrocław (Breslau); *Megapolensis ducatus* = the Duchy of Mecklenburg ("the neighbouring Duchy"); *Edenburgum* = Edinburgh; *Holsatia* = Holstein.

**Astronomy — technical (glossary–5.2).** *parallaxis* → parallax; *acronychus / in transitu acronycho* → **acronychal** (rising at sunset / opposition to the Sun) — kept as the technical term; *oppositio Solis* → opposition to the Sun; *elongatio* → elongation; *Dodecatemorion* (pl. *Dodecatemoria*) → **dodecatemory** (one zodiacal sign = 30°; "two dodecatemoria" = 60°, a sixth of the circle) — kept and glossed; *retrogradationes et stationes* → retrogradations and stations; *Epicyclus / Aequans / deferens* → epicycle / equant / deferent; *octava sphaera* → the eighth sphere (of the fixed stars); *aux* / *Aequinoctiorum reciprocatio* → the reciprocation (trepidation) of the equinoxes; *prosthaphaereses* → **prosthaphaereses** (kept by this chapter's convention); *Epocha commutationis mediae* → the Epoch of the mean commutation; *Radix motuum* → the root of the motions; *Canones Coperniani / Alphonsini* → the Copernican / Alphonsine Canons (tables); *hypothesis systematis mundani* → the hypothesis of the world-system (Tycho's geoheliocentric model — "this neoteric invention of ours," devised "about six years ago," i.e. c. 1583). *De mundi … phaenomenis* (the 1588 comet book) is referred to throughout as *liber noster secundus aethereorum Phaenomenωn* — note the Greek-spelled genitive *Phaenomenωn* (omega), kept as printed.

**Greek.** *τεκμήρια* (*tekmēria*) — "evident proofs / sure signs"; transcribed and translated. *ἀδύνατον* (*adynaton*) — "impossible"; transcribed and translated ("is not so *impossible*"). Both are kept in the Source block.

**Astrology.** *Centiloquium* — the pseudo-Ptolemaic *Centiloquium*; Tycho quotes its maxim that "love and hatred pervert the judgements of many" (a recognized aphorism, here paraphrased rather than verbatim — flagged). Planet glyphs named in English with the glyph kept in the Source block by this chapter's convention: ♂ Mars, ♄ Saturn, ♀ Venus, ☿ Mercury.

**Alchemy / Hermetic.** *Archeus* (*Archaeo cooperante*) → **Archeus** kept (the Paracelsian inner formative spirit/principle); *terrestria … astra* → "terrestrial stars"; the *Hermes Trismegistus* maxim *quicquid est superius, idem esse inferius* = the "as above, so below" tag of the *Tabula Smaragdina*, here paraphrased — rendered literally and flagged. The whole passage is a genuine Tychonic cosmological-alchemical excursus (Earth as passive recipient of celestial influence, forming subterranean "stars" via its *Archeus*); rendered without modernizing.

**Verse / sententiae (kept as verse / quotation).**
- *Sic vos non vobis mellificatis apes* — the famous Virgilian (*Maro*) tag "Thus do ye bees make honey, but not for yourselves"; left as the half-line + *etc.* as Tycho gives it.
- *Fortis et ad cursum magno cum robore fertur, / Si tamen instiges, acrius ibit equus* — an elegiac couplet (Ovidian in flavour), set as verse.
- *Est aliquid prodiret tenus, si non datur ultra* — Horatian sententia ("It is something to advance just thus far, if it is not granted to go beyond"), kept as quotation.
- *Hoc opus, hic labor est … quos ardens deduxit ad ardua virtus* — a Virgilian allusion (*Aeneid* 6.129, "hoc opus, hic labor est") fused with an *ardua virtus* tag; rendered with the quoted phrasing kept in italics.
- *Difficilia, quae pulchra* — proverbial ("the difficult things are the beautiful"); kept.
- *ut est varium et mutabile semper femina* — Virgilian (*Aen.* 4.569–70, "varium et mutabile semper femina"); kept as quotation. Misogynist register preserved as in the source, not softened.
- *Gratior est pulchro veniens e corpore virtus* — Virgilian (*Aen.* 5.344); kept as quotation.
- *corvi Aesopici … alienis plumis* — the Aesopic crow adorned in others' feathers; kept as the fable allusion.

**Measure / economy.** *quartam Tonnae auri partem* → "a quarter of a tun of gold" (*tønde guld* = a Danish money-of-account, 100,000 *rigsdaler*; thus Tycho claims to have spent well over 25,000 *rigsdaler*); kept literally and glossed. *20 floreni* → 20 florins (the price of the Apian). *duodecim … ulnas in altitudine* → "about twelve ells in height" (the paper-mill water-wheel); *ulna* = ell, kept.

**Self-description (the Hven paper-mill).** The passage on the *molendinum pro papyro conficienda* — the paper-/grist-/fulling-mill Tycho built on Hven in 1589, with its great wheel, dammed water supply and fishponds, "that the whole island … may serve our Urania" — is a documentary set-piece; rendered literally.

**Calendar / dating (by this chapter's convention — no silent conversion).**
- **Header dateline.** The subscription reads *Datae Uraniburgi prim. Cal. Novemb. stylo veteri Anno 1589*. *Cal. Novemb.* = the **Kalends of November = 1 November**; *prim.* is read as *prima(s)/primis* ("on the very Kalends"), giving **1 November 1589 Old Style**, in agreement with the edition label "1589. 1. november." (Note: *pridie Cal. Novemb.* would mean 31 October; the abbreviation here is *prim.*, not *prid.*, and the label confirms 1 November — so the Kalends reading is followed and no discrepancy arises.) Tycho explicitly states he writes *stylo veteri* (O.S.); Denmark used the Julian calendar.
- **In-letter dates are reported, not converted.** Tycho carefully tracks the style of each incoming letter: Hagecius's first written *Cal. Novembris veteri stylo anno 88* (1 Nov. 1588 O.S.), received 27 April [1589]; the second written 10 May [O.S. implied], received 31 August; the **third written *20. Maij novo stylo*** (20 May N.S.) — Hagecius in Imperial/Catholic Prague used **New Style**, and Tycho notes the contrast — received mid-September; the fourth dated 7 September, received 30 October ("the second-to-last [day] of October"). Tycho stresses that his own datings are *secundum veterem anni Iuliani numerationem, qua etiamnum nos utimur* ("according to the old Julian reckoning, which we still use"). The 10-day O.S./N.S. gap is exactly the calendar matter flags; **no date here is silently reconciled** — they are reproduced as Tycho gives them.
- *ante Pasca* → "before Easter"; *Francofurtianae nundinae* → the Frankfurt (book) fair; *vernales / autumnales nundinae* → the spring / autumn fairs.

**Named cruxes.**
1. **The Werner title (*liber Werneri de elementis cornicis*).** The phrase *de elementis cornicis* is obscure; *cornicis* (gen. of *cornix*, "crow," or of *cornicula*) does not yield an obvious sense for a Werner mathematical tract. Werner's known work is *De motu octavae sphaerae* (Nuremberg 1522), which Tycho names in the same breath. *cornicis* may be a corruption/abbreviation in the witness, or a reference to a now-obscure subsidiary tract. Rendered tentatively as "On the Elements of the *Cornicula*" with the Latin kept; **flagged, not smoothed.**
2. **"prim. Cal. Novemb." abbreviation.** Read as *primis/prima Calendis Novembris* = 1 November; secure given the label agreement, but the unexpanded *prim.* is noted for the record (it is not *pridie*).
3. **Identity of *Raymundus*.** The *impudens Raymundus* who attacked Hagecius is named only by this single word; the specific person is not securely fixed here.
- **What the recovered text is.** The bulk of the postscript to Tycho's 1 November 1589 letter to Thaddaeus Hagecius, entirely absent from the prior transcription (only the closing valediction after it survived as the published tail).
- **Recipient.** Thaddaeus Hagecius ab Hayek (Tadeáš Hájek z Hájku, 1525–1600), Emperor Rudolf II's imperial physician at Prague, Tycho's friend and correspondent since they met at Rudolf's 1575 coronation as King of the Romans; Hagecius had earlier given Tycho his treasured manuscript of Copernicus's unpublished *Commentariolus* [Christianson, *On Tycho's Island*; Christianson, *Measure of the Heavens*].
- **Subject.** Tycho's campaign to secure printing privileges (early-modern copyright protections against piracy) from multiple European monarchs for his forthcoming publications. He already held one from the King of France, on parchment with the king's own signature, and was expecting one from the King of Spain; **Daniel Rogers**, styled here "the Queen of England's second Legate" to Denmark, had promised to obtain an English one — this matches Thoren's account that "Tycho entrusted his hopes for an English copyright to Daniel Rogers, who came to Hven in 1588" pursuing exactly this [Thoren, *Lord of Uraniborg*]. Rogers died in 1590, within a year of this letter. Tycho now asks Hagecius to use his friend **"Magnificus Dominus Curtius"** to obtain a grander Imperial privilege from the Prague Chancery, on parchment, under the Emperor's own hand — this is very likely the same Curtius (probably the Bohemian chancellor Jacobus Curtius) in whose Prague house Tycho would later live and die, per Dreyer, *Tycho Brahe* (1890).
- **Religious reticence.** Tycho explicitly asks that the privilege not dwell on "Religionibus et scandalizationibus" — a rare direct statement of his deliberate avoidance of confessional controversy in his printed apparatus, leaving judgment of hypocrites and true worshippers to God alone; he closes the point with an unattributed prophetic saying about running unsent and crying out unheard, which echoes (without being verbatim) the Vulgate topos of the false, unsent prophet, cf. Jeremiah 23:21 ("non mittebam prophetas, et ipsi currebant") — flagged as a crux below.
- **The Epistolae astronomicae.** Tycho asks Hagecius to return transcripts of his own letters "for a volume that is to contain Astronomical Letters" — a direct, seven-years-early reference to the *Epistolae astronomicae*, printed at Uraniborg in 1596 [Nielsen, *Dansk Bibliografi*, no. 430], documenting the collection process for that book.
- **Cost of the document.** Tycho records paying 12 florins to the scribe for the paper copy of the privilege, per a "Taxator" (official assessor)'s valuation, and offers to pay more liberally for a parchment original — a concrete data point on the cost of engrossing an official instrument in Tycho's world.
- **Correction.** Restored Dreyer's reading in three places on TBOO VII pp.213 and 218: 'conicis' for the corrupted 'cornicis' (Werner's treatise on the conic elements, not an invented '*Cornicula*'), 'numero 1500' for an erroneous 'numero 150' in the count of Progymnasmata copies still held back from circulation, and 'Astronomicas' for the ungrammatical 'Astronomicus'. The English translation was corrected to match: the fabricated title '*the Cornicula*' now reads 'Conics', and the reserved-copy figure now reads 1500.

translation.warrant:
Collated against **Dreyer, *Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia*** (the edition of record), reading the printed page images. All 24 Dreyer pages read as page images (TBOO VII pp.196-218) and collated them line-by-line against the full the transcribed original and the published English (some 53 paragraphs). Verified opening salutation and closing signature/postscript verbatim; verified every proper name (Hagecius, Erik Lange, Ursus, Wilhelm of Hesse, Curtius, Winckler, Raymundus, Maestlin, Praetorius, Regiomontanus, Digges, Wittich, Munoz, Frangipani, Apian, Fracastoro, Vogelinus, Pena, Werner, Fabricius, Dudith, Maximilian, Trapezuntius, Craig, Rantzau, Rogers); every date (27 April, 10/20 May, 7 September, anno 82, ante quinquennium/triennium, 24 November, 26 January); every number/sum (14 years, 4:6 ratio, quarter-tun of gold, 20 years, 15/35/33/3.25 degrees, pag.206/86/133/275, sextans, tria exemplaria, 150 copies, 20 florenis, 12 florenos, 12-ell wheel); and every place-name (Prague, Copenhagen, Uraniborg, Regensburg, Rostock, Lubeck, Hamburg, Poland, Wroclaw, Mecklenburg, Edinburgh, Holstein, England, France, Spain, Denmark, Frankfurt, Vienna). Apart from the two source-text corruptions noted (both isolated single-word slips, one of which also corrupted the translation into a fabricated book-title), the translation is exceptionally faithful across the full 24-page letter: negations, hedges, disjunctions (aut...aut), and the dense argumentative passages on Mars parallax, the Tychonic system, and the Ursus plagiarism affair are all rendered with the correct sense, subject, and antecedent. No omissions or fabricated clauses were found.

**3 defects found:**
- **text error** (low). The transcribed original reads 'cornicis' where Dreyer prints 'conicis' - Werner's real treatise is 'De elementis conicis' (on conic elements/conic sections), a known historical work; 'cornicis' is a corrupted transcription. Dreyer prints: *Pro libro WERNERI de elementis conicis et motu octavae sphaerae mihi transmisso... (TBOO VII p.213, line 2)*.
- **mistranslation** (medium). Downstream of the transcribed original corruption, the translation fabricates a nonexistent title 'the Cornicula' instead of rendering Werner's actual, identifiable work as 'the conic elements' / 'Conics'; a scholar relying on this translation would go looking for a non-existent treatise. At: “For Werner's book On the Elements of the Cornicula and the Motion of the Eighth Sphere”.
- **text error** (low). The transcribed original has the ungrammatical 'Astronomicus' where Dreyer prints 'Astronomicas' (agreeing with 'Epistolas'; this is Tycho's own project, the later-published Epistolae Astronomicae). The English translation itself correctly renders 'Astronomical Letters,' so this defect does not propagate into the translation. Dreyer prints: *Ego enim volumini, quod Epistolas Astronomicas continebit, huiusmodi destinavi. (TBOO VII p.218, line 39)*.

**Repaired.** All four fixes were collated directly against the Dreyer page images for TBOO VII pp.212-215 and pp.216-219. The record's three listed defects — the 'cornicis'/'conicis' text error, its downstream 'Cornicula' mistranslation, and the 'Astronomicus'/'Astronomicas' text error — are all directly confirmed by the page images and now fixed. In addition, a suspected '1500/150' error in the reserved-copies figure, not in the audit's list, was checked at p.213 line 19: Dreyer clearly prints 'numero 1500', while both the transcribed original and the English read '150' — a genuine, previously-undetected text error, now fixed in both languages and logged as a fourth correction. No other passage on the collated pages disagreed with Dreyer, and nothing outside these four sites was altered.

text.original:
DOCTISSIMO VIRO MAGISTRO ANDREÆ WELLEIO, CANONICO RIPENSI, AMICO SUO DENTUR.
S.

SI vales bene est, ego cum meis (quod Deo acceptum refero) mediocriter me habeo. Miror, te multo tempore nihil ad me dedisse literarum neque cum HELIA meo quidpiam scripsisse. Sicut prorsus mei immemor factus? Da operam, ut exarationem quandam eorum habeam, quæ in Privilegio Danico commode continebuntur, de quibus aliquoties tecum egi, sed Iutica fides in verbis quidvis etc. Cuperem hac hyeme habere, nam primus Tomus mei operis iam sub prelo est. Moletrina papyro conficiendæ destinata unâ cum annexis iam parata est, et aqua adest in sufficienti copia non saltem hyberno, sed etiam æstivo tempore, omniaque rite se habent, saltem chartopæus defideratur. Nam is, qui ERICO inservierat, quem Lubecam pro veteramentis conquirendis misi, nusquam postea comparuit. Si talem Artificem illic expiscari poteris, mitte illum huc mature, pro suo labore debite remunerandum. Distantias omnium locorum in Cymbria et alibi in Dania, quotquot hactenus adeptus es, mihi describi cura et quamprimum huc mitti. Rectius erit, si unius loci a duobus alijs, qui triangulum ferme effecerint, intercapedinem denotaveris, quoties id fieri queat; tum etiam sylvæ, flumina, portus, littora, anfractus et similia, qua fieri potest diligentia, designanda veniunt. Effice ut cito habeam, nam præterquam quod Daniæ chartam aliquando per ocium emendate conficiendam mediter, in hoc etiam quem nunc imprimi curo libro, in tabella quadam, ubi longitudines et latitudines diversorum Europæ locorum correctiores, quoad eius fieri potest, ob meridianorum differentias discernendas comprehenduntur, Patriæ etiam nostræ insigniora quædam loca secundum longum et latum verificata apponere animus est. Fac itaque, ut nulla sit in te mora, quin propediem quæ desidero obtineam, et per hunc ipsum nuncium vel quemvis alium obvium rescribe. Vale et METTAM tuam unâ cum utroque Parente cæterisque Ripensibus amicis saluta.

Datæ Uraniburgi die 20. Novemb. 89.
Tuus
TYCHO BRAHE
manu propria.
text.english:
**To be delivered to the most learned man Master Anders Vedel, canon of Ribe, his friend.**
Greeting.

If you are well, it is good; I, with my household — for which I give thanks to God — am moderately well. I wonder that for a long while you have sent me no letters, and have written nothing even by way of my [servant] Elias. As though you had become quite forgetful of me? See to it that I may have some draft of those things which can conveniently be contained in the Danish Privilege, about which I have dealt with you several times — but "Jutish good faith in words [is] anything you please," etc. I should like to have it this winter, for the first volume of my work is now under the press. The mill destined for the making of paper, together with its appurtenances, is now ready, and water is at hand in sufficient supply not only in the winter but also in the summer season, and everything is in good order; only a papermaker is wanting. For the man who had served Erik — whom I sent to Lübeck to seek out old rags [for paper] — has nowhere appeared since. If you can fish out such a craftsman thereabouts, send him here in good time, to be duly rewarded for his labour. Take care to have the distances of all places in the Cimbrian peninsula [Jutland] and elsewhere in Denmark, as many as you have so far obtained, written out for me and sent here as soon as possible. It will be more correct if you note the interval of one place from two others which form roughly a triangle, as often as that can be done; then too the woods, rivers, harbours, shores, windings [of the coast] and the like ought to be marked down, with what diligence may be possible. Bring it about that I may have it quickly, for — besides that I am planning at some time, at leisure, to make a corrected map of Denmark — in this very book also, which I am now having printed, on a certain table, where the longitudes and latitudes of various places of Europe are set down more correctly (so far as that can be done) for distinguishing the differences of the meridians, it is my intention to add certain of the more notable places of our homeland too, verified according to longitude and latitude. See to it, therefore, that there be no delay on your part, but that I shortly obtain what I desire; and write back by this same messenger or by any other that comes to hand. Farewell, and greet your Mette together with both her parents and the rest of your friends at Ribe.

Given at Uraniborg, the 20th day of November, [15]89.
Yours,
TYCHO BRAHE,
in his own hand.

departures_from_tekstnet.basis: The text printed here descends from one harvest of tekstnet's page and was read against Dreyer's page images in July 2026; a second harvest of the same page is kept beside it. Where the two disagree in a word, both readings are listed: Dreyer's page decides, and unless the audit paragraph names the word, that check has not yet been made for it. documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent.** *Magister Andreas Wellejus, canonicus Ripensis* = **Anders Sørensen Vedel** (1542–1616), the Danish historian and royal historiographer, canon of Ribe (Lat. *Ripa*); Tycho's old friend from their student years. Tycho's request for distance-measurements supports both Vedel's and his own cartographic and historical projects.
- **Place.** *Uraniburgum* = **Uraniborg**, Tycho's observatory-castle on the island of Hven. *Ripa* = **Ribe**, in Jutland; *Cymbria* = the **Cimbrian peninsula**, i.e. Jutland (the humanist name from the Cimbri). *Lubeca* = **Lübeck**.
- **Persons named.** *Helia meo* — "my Elias," evidently a servant or messenger of Tycho's (the diminutive-affectionate *meus*); not further identified here. *Erico* — "Erik," likewise unidentified; the man Tycho mentions had formerly been in this Erik's service. Both are flagged as unidentified rather than guessed at.
- **Salutation.** *S.* = *salutem* (dicit), "greeting". The address-line *…AMICO SUO DENTUR* ("let it be given to … his friend") is the exterior direction/superscription.
- ***Privilegium Danicum*** — "the Danish Privilege": a printing privilege (royal licence/copyright) for Tycho's works to be issued under Danish authority; Tycho wants Vedel to draft the text of what it should cover. Rendered literally "Danish Privilege" and glossed.
- ***Iutica fides in verbis quidvis*** — "Jutish good faith in words [is] anything you please": a proverbial gibe at the unreliability of Jutlanders' promises (Vedel was a Jutlander, of Ribe), Tycho twitting his friend for his long silence. The clause is elliptical (no main verb); rendered with a bracketed copula and the *etc.* kept, the proverbial force flagged rather than smoothed.
- **Papermaking.** *primus Tomus mei operis iam sub prelo est* — "the first volume of my work is now under the press": the *Astronomiae instauratae progymnasmata* (begun printing at Uraniborg c. 1588–89). *Moletrina papyro conficiendae destinata* — "the mill destined for the making of paper," Tycho's own paper-mill at Hven. *chartopaeus* (= *chartopoeus*, Gr. χαρτοποιός) — "papermaker," the craftsman who makes the sheets; rendered "papermaker." *veteramenta* — "old rags / cast-off cloth," the linen rag-stock from which hand-made paper is beaten; rendered "old rags [for paper]." *Artifex* — "craftsman."
- **Cartography / surveying.** *Distantias … describi … unius loci a duobus alijs, qui triangulum ferme effecerint, intercapedinem* — "the distances … the interval of one place from two others which form roughly a triangle": Tycho is requesting **triangulation** data for a map of Denmark. The phrasing describes the triangulation principle without using a single technical term; rendered descriptively. *anfractus* — "windings, bends [of the coastline]." *Daniae chartam … emendate conficiendam* — "a corrected map of Denmark." *tabella … ubi longitudines et latitudines … ob meridianorum differentias discernendas* — "a table … where the longitudes and latitudes … for distinguishing the differences of the meridians": a geographical coordinate table planned for the book under the press. *secundum longum et latum verificata* — "verified according to longitude and latitude" (*longum/latum* here = the long/lat coordinates).
- ***Mettam tuam*** — "your Mette": **Mette**, Vedel's wife (rendered with the Danish given-name form, since the Latin accusative *Mettam* simply Latinises the Danish name). *utroque Parente* — "both her parents" (taken as Mette's parents, the natural antecedent of *tuam*); the Latin *uterque Parens* could in principle mean Vedel's own two parents, but the possessive attaches to Mette — the reading is noted.
- ***manu propria*** — "in his own hand," the autograph subscription formula.
- **Calendar.** *Datae Uraniburgi die 20. Novemb. 89* = "Given at Uraniborg, 20 November [15]89" (O.S.; Denmark kept the Julian calendar). The dateline date agrees with the catalogue label (*1589. 20. november. Uraniborg*); no discrepancy.
- **Textual note.** *defideratur* (line: *saltem chartopaeus defideratur*) is a printer's/copyist's spelling of *desideratur* ("is wanting/lacking"); kept as printed in the Source block, rendered "is wanting." MS witness A is a later copy (*Afskrift*) in Tycho's private archive, not an autograph original.

documents.incipit: ECQVID id est mi ROTHMANNE, quod tam inuito animo accipias, adeoque sinistre …

text.original:
CLARISSIMO ET ERVDITISSIMO
VIRO, D. CHRISTOPHORO ROTHMANNO,
ILLVSTRISSIMI PRINCIPIS WILHELMI LANDTGRAVII HASSIAe, ETC. MATHEMATICO EXIMIO, AMICO
SUO PLURIMUM DILECTO. S. D.

ECQVID id est mi ROTHMANNE, quod tam inuito animo accipias, adeoque sinistre interpreteris meas vltimo ad te datas literas, nimisque rhapsodice ad eas respondeas, cum amicae inter nos collationis, atque veritatis in abscondito latentis penitius eruendae gratiâ, bona intentione scriptae sint: Neque enim ego te vspiam in illis impietatis accusaui. De pietate vel impietate cuiusuis, nullum mihi arrogo iudicium, Id scrutatori cordium omnium, vti par est, relinquens. Nec etiam te authoritati sacrarum literarum, quasi data opera, aliquid detrahere absolute dixi, saltem quod Mosis verba de Luna, luminari minore, incompetenter ad corporis, ipsis plaerisque Stellis reuera minoris, magnitudinem transtuleris, cum potius de lucis Terras contingente praeeminentia accipienda veniant, te admonui. Rationibus quoque vt existimo non incongruis adiectis. Quod etiam Prophetis nimium deroges, eos non plusquam vulgus imperitum in Astronomicis et Physicis intellexisse asseuerando, vtvt diuinitus, immeditate instructi fuerint, et praeterea antiquiss. Patrum visibilem a DEO conditarum rerum excolentium traditiones non paucas, nostris procul dubio ab Ethnicis acceptis certiores et meliores in promptu habuerint, non approbandum duxi, in qua etiamnum persisto sententia. Neque enim vnquam leuiter de his decernendum censui. Multa quidem et non posthabenda, de ijs quae Physice in sacris literis continentur, nuper etiam secundum vulgarium Philosophorum ratiocinationes, explicuit Franciscus Vallesius, neque absque solerti, quo ad ea principia, labore; Licet et multo plura in his longe aliter secundum veriorem Physicam, forte quoque ex his ipsis non minima de parte potius petendam, enucleanda delitescant. Quin et Lambertus Danaeus, vir sane apprime eruditus, et de instituendis alijs optime meritus, Physicam suam Theologicam, tam ex veteri quam nouo Codice non inutili labore extruxit. Possentque fortasse multa de his aliâs dici, quae peculiare et reuera Metaphysicum, non quale nobis Stagyrita iste Graecus obtrusit, requirerent volumen. Literas tuas quin satis caperem, nec morbus, licet et ille grauis erat, corporis tamen non ingenli, nec occupationum, quamuis et hae non paucae implicationes, adeo vt putas, impedierunt. Nulla enim in illis irresolubilia latebant aenigmata, re omni dudum satis perspecta; Nec quicquam tibi obijcio, quod ex literis illis colligi non possit, imo forte plusquam opus est, parco. Conferantur saltem tuae et meae, dijudicentque alij, affectibus non indulgentes, neque sibijpsis nimium placentes. Quatenus sacris literis contraria induxeris, et antea et iam aliquo modo indicaui, te vbique studiose id facere non dixi. Nec ego licet Theologiam non profitear, neque quispiam eorum qui eam solide et sincere exercent, tuis assertionibus e Dedomenis sacrarum literarum assentiri possumus: Frustra itaque praetendis hoc diuerticulum, Cum duo dicunt vnum, non tibi concedi vt sint vnum, Neque enim alijs concedendum duco, quod hîc reprehendo. Augustinum satis libere de sacris nonnunquam pronuntiasse, interdum non incomposite, interdum vero frigidiuscule pro eâ temporibus Apostolorum viciniore aetate, non equidem Dei gratiâ sum ignarus. Sed quid ista omnia huc conferunt, aut ad rem de qua agitur, faciunt. Quaestio mouebatur, an mobilitas Terreni Globi, eademque triplex a Copernico asserta reuera constare possit, anque illa inuentioni nostrae praeferenda foret, et vtrum sacrae literae illius imaginationi contrariarentur, necne: Si quid igitur habes e sacris Oraculis, aut horum Interpretibus, vtpote Augustino vel alijs Patribus, pro hac Copernicea assertione, tuaque astipulatione faciens, ex eorum scriptis id cita. Modo iustae fuerint rationes, ijs non refragabor. Id satis scio, Augustinum, quem solum nominas, motum Terrae, neque annuum neque diurnum vsquam concessisse, ex quo rotunditati eius tanquam minus Mathematicus, Antipodas denegando, detraxerit. Quod tamen illi condonandum est. Quare cum rotundam esse non perceperit, motum etiam rotunditati competentem longe minus admittere potuit. Theologorum vestratium opinationes, et de his censuras, etsi extra eorum forte Professionem, minusque deliberatas, non equidem contemno. Sed cum videam illos tantum hoc nomine accersitos atque interrogatos, an liquiditas Caeli e sacris literis, sine orbium realitate astrui possit (prout tua clausula innuit) cumque scias me etiam longe antequam de his somniâris idipsum concessisse, atque pronuntiasse, miror, cur haec nihil huc facientia obijcias. Neque enim existimo vestris Theologis de terna Terrae volubilitate propositam esse quaestionem, cum paucissimi ex illis, eam etsi quam maxime vellent, caperent, vtvt Terrenis, quemadmodum et alibi fit, non parum forte addicti. Cum igitur de mobilitale Terrae ex Aristarcho et quibusdam alijs veteribus per Copernicum renouata introductaque controuersia solummodo inter nos mouebatur, qua quaeso cohaerentia impulsus eam cum limpiditate Caeli confudisti, quam ego nunquam denegaui, sed primus forte omnium id ita se habere non saltem asseuerare, sed e certissimis demonstrationibus probare elaboraui. An hoc est Mathematicum, disparia coniungere atque implicare. Quod ne quidem Dialectici, siue Artificiales, siue naturales in diuersis terminis admiserint.

Liquidissimam et vbique peruiam esse Aetherei Mundi substantiam e sacris literis probari posse, vel ipsis silentibus Theologiae Professoribus, iam dudum compertum habeo. Multaque in eius rei testimonium consignaui diuinitus patefacta Oracala. Quin et Clarissimus ille, deque Doctrina publica egregie meritus vir D. CASPARVS PEVCERVS literis ad me hoc praesertim nomine datis, plurima sacrarum literarum dicta, huc facientia collegit, meaeque sententiae circa tenuissimam, limpidissimam et nihilominus superelementarem Caeli materiam erudite atque egregie subscripsit. Idque potissimum, vt Hypothesium mearum inuentionem minime absurdam esse inde quoque comprobaret. Quando ego meas de Caeli materia vbique peruia nullisque orbibus solidis conferta, vt in gratiam veterum hactenus creditum est, et nihilominus Aëre Elementari atque animali velut Ioannes Pena Gallus, tu et quidam alij promulgare audetis, non coinquinatas ratiocinationes plenius, quam adhuc factum est, in publicum edidero, alijsque dijudicandas concessero, vtique sacrarum literarum, quae primas in omni sapientia stabilienda, atque scientia condenda obtinere merentur, autoritatem citare, vel te non monente, nequaquam intermissurus sum. Dei enim solius gloriam in omnibus spectandam semper censui, id quod et tu recte approbas, cum veritas absque ipsius patefactione et dono introspici nequeat; Omne enim donum perfectum a Deo. Meam quintam Essentiam, quam Aetheri, apud Chymicos locutione non ignota, neque veteribus etiam Philosophis, adeoque ne ipsi Aristoteli (licet in his non vbique satis perspicaci) improbata, tribuo, salse mihi exprobare videris; Sal vero dulce, limpidum, omnique terrestreitate defaecatum, exaltatum, nullaque ex parte insipidum, aut graueolens, sed perpetuitati Circulari analogum, nondum degustati; vbi olfeceris, aut saporem eius perceperis, tum primum de his sententiam profer; Interea satius est immaturo supersedere praeiudicio. Rogas, ne de Crepusculis te caecum efficiam, neque temeritatis accusem, quasi illa scribas, quae non expertus sis. At ego nec te occaecare, nec temerarium pronuntiare vnquam praesumsi; Vtinam et me et te atque alios a caligine mentis, qua plusquam credimus offuscati sumus, temeritateque Mundana liberari liceret, aeque atque oculorum externam imbecillitatem, vel Chymicis praesertim medijs emendare non vsque adeo difficile est, sane in eo, quo ad fieri posset, quamplurimum elaborandum censerem. Neque enim opera illa inutiliter collocata foret. Scire te ais Crepusculum desinere, Sole P. 17. sub Horizonte depresso, vulgariter Crepusculum pro luce dubia accipiendo. Existimas itaque me vulgo saltem approbatam et hactenus in Astronomorum libris contentam opinionem venditare, nihilque e proprijs aduersionibus huc contulisse; At quae haec est insimulatio. Tamdiu ne tecum per literas egi, vt adhuc me veritatis esse studiosum, neque aliunde quam vel iusta ratiocinatione atque experientia, vel quod potissimum est, patefactione diuina eam conquirere, neque data opera falsum pro vero astruere, incompertum habeas. Sufficienter colligere potuisti, me ne in maioribus quidem, et ad rem Astronomicam plus facientibus caecutire velle, nedum vt in Crepusculis, facilimo negotio animaduertibilibus, irrita et Antiquorum saltem sententiae vulgari colludendo quippiam citra propriam animaduersionem pronuntiarem. Crepusculum cum nulla Aëris pars vndiquaque circa Horizontem vel minimum albescat, determinandum, satis sciebam, quod etiam tum a me ipso, tum a mihi septenis vel octonis ad minimum in rebus Astronomicis inseruientibus studiosis, quam diligentissime aliquoties factitatum est, ita vt nullum, ne quidem minimum vestigium Aëris a Sole illuminati in vlla citima Horizontis superficie dignosci potuerit, quando tempora Crepusculorum denotata sunt; Adhibitis Stellarum Aequatorijs a Meridiano remotionibus, Solisque exacto loco, et omnibus per trutinam Geometricam diligenter expensis, tibique si oculos aperire velles, eandem ob caussam, ne pro libito aut vulgari opinione constituta, persentisceres, liberaliter communicatis. Si itaque tu duobus oculis, et binis quoque saltem Organis acrius haec discernere potes, quam nos omnes sedecim ad minimum luminibus, totidemque et pluribus sicubi opus fuerit, Instrumentis, equidem hanc lincaeitatem atque mediorum modicam requisitionem tibi non inuideo, miror magis. Imo maius adhuc acumen plenioremque sufficientiam congratularer. Tu itaque de Crepusculis, tuo sensu abundando tibi quicquid libuerit, persuade, Ego ea quae indicaui, et pluribus etiam experimentis satis rata esse, nullique verae refragationi obnoxia, minime haesito. Vide saltem ne aliorum non indubias animaduersiones eleuando, vt tuis assertionibus de Aëris atque Aetheris consimili existentia (quam magna ex parte ob vaporum in diuersis Horizontibus discrepantiam, et in Borealioribus magis quam Australibus incrassatam sublimatamque probare conaris) patrocineris, pluribus vaporibus, obscuritatibus atque nebulis veritatem ipsam, ad quam tendere deberemus, inuoluas, quam omnes circa Horizontem terrestrem, quouis in loco, siue Australi siue Boreo densae et fuscae vaporositates. Proinde, cur Refractionibus non ad amussim subscribam, nescire vis, cum alias per Instrumenta eruere non potueris, ideoque nihil hîc in mei gratiam faciendum et propterea iniqua me postulare hoc postulando, asseueras. At quando ego a te vnquam petij, vt posthabita veritate, quidpiam in mei gratiam proferres, aut adeo iniqua vrsi? id enim reuera iniquum foret, si hoc fecissem. Imo multo potius de veritate ipsa penitius enucleanda semper admonui, cum haec sit virtutum omnium pene pulcherrima praestantissimaque. Refractiones a te assertas, cur omni ex parte approbare nequeam, et mea me docent Instrumenta: Si in vno atque altero, ijsdemque saltem bicubitalibus, vtvt ex mea inuentione profectis, et per Wittichium vobis propalatis, neque etiam tunc satis maturis, haec et alia quam ego plusquam vicenis Organis, plerisque eorum quadricubitalibus et quincubitalibus, pluribus quoque adhibitis Obseruatoribus visus acumine satis valentibus, accuratius collimare solus potes, est quod tibi et hanc praerogatiuam non inuideam; Quin et sic erit, cur mihi gratias agas, quod te per a me excogitata Instrumenta (neque enim id iam ignoras) tam perspicacem reddiderim. Id saltem tibi persuade, quemadmodum in palestrica Arte fieri solet, nullum Athletam Progymnastis suis, ea confestim indicare, quae sibi ipsi in exercitio isto defectu aliquo vnquam obessent; Sic etiam nec Wittichium nec vllos alios omnia mea, quae veritati peruestigandae ad amussim sunt necessaria ita diuulgasse, quin adhuc potiori ex parte apud suum Autorem sarta tecta maneant. Frustra itaque de tuis Instrumentis atque Obseruationibus nimium gloriaris: Forte si hîc esses omniaque ipsemet per longe plura minimeque dubia Organa, vel tuis solius oculis, me praesente intuereris, aliud diceres. Sed et Refractiones tuas nimium modicas esse et Crepuscula nimis lata, non satis inter se conueniunt. Oportet itaque in alterutris vel vtrisque errorem non modicum latere, aut sane Aërem in hoc parum Borealiore loco, quantum ad Crepuscula attinet, aliquanto defaecatiorem, quam illîc esse, quo ad Refractiones vero turbidiorem, id quod vel te ipso iudice simul consistere nequit. Attende igitur his diligentius, vel si minus lubet, aut in procinctu non est, acquiesce saltem aliorum minime dubiae decisioni neque hîc tibi quidpiam immature decernendum praesume. Titulum libri mei alias in dubium vocatum, aut etiam attentatum, nunc approbas, nec amplius reprehensione dignum aestimas; Licet illum quem allegasti, non publice ediderim, aut vlli libro praefixerim, sed saltem in literis quibusdam ad Illustriss. Principem tuum datis illum obiter annotârim. Gratulor itaque et tibi et mihi, quod tam pulchre resipueris, antea enim obiecisti, me corruptionem Caelo introducere, cum generationis illic circa Cometam vocabulo vterer, nimis rigide verba mea vrgendo. At vide potius, ne de industria nunc asserendo, Cometas in Caelo generari, alicubi praeter opinionem pecces, non tam Grammatice quam Physice, modo vocabuli proprietatem retinere deceat. Quod non assertiue sed dubitanter atque interrogatiue ista proposuisti, vt meam sententiam plenius explicarem, id nihil apud me noui est; Nam et Wittichius et plaerique alij sic mecum egerunt, obijciendo ea quae nullum mererentur dubium, vt alia quaedam expiscarentur. Verum postquam ego in eo, tum etiam alijs idipsum mature experirer, cautior factus sum, vtvt non pauca in Germania hincinde meis sumptibus et laboribus comparata, idque Dei solius gratiâ ab alijs pro suis etiamnum venditentur, dictitenturque: Quod parui facio. Neque aegre fero aliquos riuulos ad Exteros deriuari, ipso fonte penes suum Dominum adhuc Dei beneficio scaturiente. Non tamen sunt falsa proponenda, vt cognoscantur vera; Vera enim et falsa sunt dissentanea, nisi quis, vti apud Geometras fit, cum assertiue nihil probari possit, per negationem, rem in absurdum deducat. Sic etiam quae de Cometarum cauda proposuisti, tum in scripto illo tuo de Cometa Anni 85. tum literis ad me datis nunc reuocas, neque te illa tanquam vera vrsisse, sed tantum, vt meo iudicio subijceres, asseris. Licet vero et scriptum illud et literae tuae quiddam aliud prae se ferant, attamen quod et hîc in viam redieris bene me habet. Placet enim, quod ratiocinationes tuas et quae ex Illustrissimi Principis Obseruatione de Cometa Anni 58. comprobationis loco adduxisti, quam parum valida sint (ex quo ista tibi in superioribus literis ob oculos posuerim) iam satis videas, adeo vt te ista non scripsisse, ipsemet, vti apparet, malles. Quae excusandae istius Obseruationis caussa vltra ea quae ego produxi, adfers, apud me facilem merentur locum, qui non tam Obseruationi aliquantulum deuiae, sed potius, quod tu hanc non satis circumspecte nimium vrseris, omniumque aliorum in plurimis Cometis inuenta hinc eludere conatus sis, imputem. Rogas vt ego haec non publicem, vtque tuam de Cometarum generatione sententiam scriptis meis non immisceam. Atqui te hîc celare non possum, me per literas rogatum a Nobilissimo viro D. HENRICO RANZOVIO, Vicario Regio in Holsatia, tum etiam Clarissimo et Eruditissimo D. CASPARO PEVCERO, Philosopho eximio, atque quibusdam alijs non ineruditis viris id expetentibus approbantibusque, peculiari Tomo vno vel altero Epistolas Astronomicas mihi a varijs hincinde perscriptas, vna cum mea ad singulas responsione publicem. Quod et illis non denegandum duxi. Cumque dictus RANZOVIVS principaliter Illustrissimi Principis tui, atque tuas Typis consignari expetisset, et per se mererentur, vt priorem et principaliorem voluminis partem occuparent, iamque liber ille sub Praelo sit, ea quae alijs addixi, rursus in tuam gratiam detractare et facta infecta reddere nequeo. Nec video cur id a me expetendum fuerat, curque id concederem, cum nihil hac in re, tuo Illustrissimo Principi, quod obsit, aut vlla ex parte deroget, sed saltem quae in ipsius Celsitud. praedicationem, vti par est, potius cedant, admittatur. Nec etiam tibi quicquam hinc creatur periculi aut detrimenti, cum honorifice semper de te loquar et sentiam. Quod si tu quaedam in prioribus scriptis et literis proposita, postea mutas, et re rectius deliberata corrigis, tuae existimationi hinc nihil decedit, etiamsi priora publicentur. Imo praestat alios cognoscere, quam difficile sit, etiam ingeniosis et industrijs viris veritatis latebras extricare, et quod non omnia quae prima fronte recte se habere putantur, vndiquaque rite constent. Quodque dies diem doceat, et posteriores cogitationes, vt plurimum, licet non semper, priores antecellant. Reuocârunt alij admodum eximij viri multa a se prius minus considerate pro veris habita, etiam in ijs materijs, vbi non adeo difficilis erat atque hîc veritatis peruestigatio. Quando ex professo circa totius Operis Epilogum, quod de Ascititijs Caeli Phaenomenis prae manibus habeo, Cometarum naturam et procreationem, iuxta omnium quotquot mihi innotuerunt opinationes disquiro, hanc etiam tuam, cum alijs quibusdam communem praetermittere, vt quam incongrua sit, quod et alias tibi scripsi, ne indicem, haud possum. Attamen cum videam te in his teipsum corrigere atque priores conceptiones antiquare, faciam eius quoque illic mentionem, idque conuenienter excusabo. Ego tuum scriptum de Cometa publici iuris non faciam: Nihilominus nonnulla hinc citare atque expendere in laudabilem tui mentionem potius cedet, quam quod reprehensioni erit. Dicis quidem me pugnaturum cum muto, si id agam. At non mutus eras cum haec scriberes, literisque ad me datis consignares; Sunt enim notae scriptae, praesertim tua propria manu exaratae, pro ipsis verbis et loquela, imo et plus merentur ponderis. Sic etiam quantum ad meas literas attinet, quas publici iuris reddere, nisi rogatus ab amicis, vt dixi, nunquam constitueram, cum saltem obiter, prout in buccam venerat, inter plurima negotia exaratae erant, scias me non adeo earum penitere, quin tibi liberum relinquam, siue priuatim, siue publice, quocunque libuerit modo, quae in his contenta sunt, discutere, probare vel improbare. Si quid iustis rationibus, vel tu vel quispiam alius non rite in his alijsue meis constare sufficienter demonstrarit, ego illa corrigere non erubesco. Neque ego cum praeiudicio vllo, quippiam in tuis disquirendis aggrediar. Vide vt eodem candore circa mea quoque vtaris, nec iuuenili quodam feruore sententiam immaturam pronunties. Gratulor tibi, quod ex cogitatione materiae Stellarum et viae lacteae ad aliam opinionem diuerteris circa Cometarum conformationem, quam ea erat, qua antea imbutus parum Physica, longeque minus Mathematica: Es enim hîc in bona via, si eam ingredi callueris, omniaque hospitia noueris. Nec enim satis mirari poteram, qua iudicij nebula tantas absurditates astruere, vt corpus Cometarum, vel teipso fatente, prope Reuolutiones Saturninas a Terris distans (vt de eo qui Anno 85. apparuit, consignasti) ideoque necessario et Terra et Mari omnibusque circumfluis vaporibus multis parasangis maius existens, prout ferunt Geometricae demonstrationes, nihilominus hinc in supremum Aethera ascendisse, nescio quo incognito raptu, et partem esse suo toto multo maiorem, pronuntiare ausus sis; idque prorsus contra rationes Mathematicas. Si Physicis ita sentire lubet, coniungant has naenias caeteris. Bene igitur superinducis, quod ea, quae de Trabibus discurrentibus, quarum forte occasione in tam absona prolapsus es, cum reuera huc nihil conferant, tantumque haec inuicem distent, quantum Caelum et Terra, prorsus falsa esse deprehenderis. Habebam in animo, te vltimis literis et de his admonere, quod quomodo neglexerim, non recordor. Nam in scripto tuo de Cometa Anni 85. vbi talia asseuerare conaris, ad marginem memoriae caussa haec annotâram, quae vel tunc vel alias per opportunitatem commonefacienda duxi. Halitus isti siue Chasmata longe sunt nobis propiora, quam quod hyberno tempore a Sole nimium infra Horizontem depresso, illuminari queant, veluti ratio docet Geometrica et Optica. Quin et Anno 1588. eius rei euidens feci periculum die 6. Decemb. circa octauam vespertinam. Animaduerti enim tunc accurata inspectione Chasmata quamplurima hincinde versus Septentrionem volantia albicantiaque, ita vt lumen quoddam vmbram etiam Terrae illustrans prae se ferrent, longe nobis viciniora esse, quibusdam densioribus nubibus circa Horizontem Boreum segregatim dispersis, adeo vt Chasmata illa inter nos et nubes, discurrere euidenter apparerent, ita vt et alij ex meis, quibus monstrabam, id satis perspicue discernerent. A Sole igitur versus Antipodas submerso, ista vaporum illuminatio fieri nequibat; cum ne nubes quidem longe a Terra remotiores ipsius lumen percellere potuerit, quod facile Geometrice haec mensurando patebit. Nubes autem illae, de quibus loquor, non fuerunt continuae, sed circa Horizontem sparsim dispositae, ad Altitudinem, quo ad visibilem Horizontem, circiter graduum 10. Cum igitur Radij Solares partem vmbrae Terrae nobis adeo propinquam in ista eius sub Horizontem demersione non contingant, frustra asseritur, per illuminationem ab hoc quippiam eiuscemodi contingere. Simile quid saepius consideraui, praesertim hoc ipso Anno die 2. Ianuarij, cum quoque circa octauam vespertinam, quando plurima ad Septentrionem hîc spectabantur Chasmata, quae nubibus longe propiora cernebantur. Quapropter frustra hinc aliquid subsidij petijsti, pro innaturali illa Cometarum generatione stabilienda. Atque si scire cupis, quid ego de his Chasmatis sentiam, Sulphureitatem quandam Terrestrem in propinquo Aëre ardentem, discurrentemque, et nonnunquam vsque ad verticem ascendendo totum Caelum complentem, in modica tamen a visu nostro distantia, esse iudico, ventorum aut siccitatis et frigoris breui subsequentium praenuntia; interdum etiam, si saepius contingant, nimisque diu durent, Aëris ad contagium Epidemicae luis propensi indicia. Habet enim morbus iste cum Sulphurea natura non parum commune, vnde etiam per Sulphur terrestre excellenter depuratum exaltatumque, praesertim si in liquorem gratum reclinetur, expeditius soluitur, tanquam simile suo simili. Neque enim id Galenicorum semper verum est: Contraria contrarijs curari. Haec de his te nunc commonere placuit. Rectissime itaque feceris, si totum illud caput, de materia Cometarum, eorumque illuminatione, vti spondes, mutaueris, et consideratius tractâris. Nec opus est, vt alius adhuc expectetur Cometa. Nam illi qui vel nostro Aeuo proxime praeterierunt, priorem tuam opinionem nequaquam consistere posse affatim conuincunt; id quod te nostrae in his animaduersiones facile edocebunt, modo aliquid fidei mereri poterint. Sin autem nostras decisiones, licet ea, qua fieri potuit diligentia conquisitas, nec vti spero citra rem prolatas, non tales esse, vt ijs tuto nitendum existimes; agedum expecta adhuc alium Cometam si quis interea occurrerit, et eum diligentius, modo id tibi concessum fuerit, demetiendo perscrutare. Si tunc aliquîd diuersi a nostris conclusionibus adinueneris, satis erit temporis, id quicquid erit in medium proferre; interea si iudicium suspenderis, modo nostris acquiescere displiceat, non inconsultum erit. Planetas in subtilissimo purissimoque Aëre pendere (licet id admodum improprie dicatur, cum reuera non pendeant) quod vlterius mecum disceptare nolis, libenter accipio: beneque facis, Caeli materiam non amplius animalem et elementarem vocando. Nihil enim hîc vnquam apud me obtinebis. Si meae rationes, partim prolatae, partim alibi vlterius declarandae, et vel ex inferioribus palpabilibusque rebus, superioribus tamen analogis, allatae, tibi non sufficient, vt quicquid velis sentias, satis per me licet. Tracta hanc quaestionem vbicunque libuerit, et siue me immiscueris siue non, idem erit. Ego meam sententiam satis probabiliter tueri, quando hac de re agendi occasio dabitur, non supersedebo. Iudicium doctissimorum virorum et rem ipsam intelligentium nullatenus subterfugio; Neque enim ego ipsemet mihi tantum arrogo, vt solus litem hanc dirimere praesumam. Philalithiam semper in pretio habui, maiori forte meo incommodo (quod tamen non aegre fero) quam emolumento. Neque praeiudicij fascino, vt imputare videris, vnquam me offuscari, data opera, permisi: Quantum enim mihi diuinitus concessum est, verum a falso discernere, perpetuo annixus sum. Si tertiam aliquam personam appellas (video enim te Iuridice mecum in re Mathematica agere, nam et Frater tuus retulit te ad Iuris prudentiam inclinare, forte quod haec magis lucrosa et Mundo spectabilior sit) et ego conditionem accipio, lubenterque prouoco ad quosuis in Germania vel alibi Philosophos, harum rerum capaces. Vtque denominetur aliquis; ad Clariss. Excellentissimumque virum D. CASPARVM PEVCERVM, si ita lubet, rem omnem desero, cum is et Philosophiae et Mathematicarum disciplinarum in primis sit gnarus, Theologiaeque studio, vnde haec quaestio magna ex parte decidi poterit, non segniter addictus, et simul iudicio aetateque graui praeualeat: Nec, tanquam meis partibus nimis fauorabilis Iudex sit futurus (scis enim, si Iurisperitus esse vis, fauorem Iudicis plus valere, quam decem leges scriptas in Codice) tibi suspicandum venit, nunquam enim mihi notus est: At cum tuo Illustriss. Principe, quem suum optimum benefactorem, in literis ad me datis, nec immerito vocat, et tecum etiam praesens non ingratam contraxit amicitiam. Si qui sunt alij inter vestrates, vel etiam alibi, ad quos appellationem instituere vis, et ego eosdem appello, modo rem de qua agitur, penitius introspexerint, atque tam superiora quam inferiora intelligere, haecque inuicem tanquam vnum ex altero cognoscentes conciliare didicerint. Quicquid enim est supra, id etiam infra, vt inquiebat Hermes ille vere inter Mortales Trismegistus. Trinitatis absconditum latere in omnibus rebus creatis mysterium recte mihi astipularis, quamuis tua de his Philosophia quam adducis, magis sit exterior, quam interna, nimisque sensibus obuia; Cum id quod potissimum est, et in quo rei nucleus versatur, prima fronte non appareat, Non enim satis est dictum, ex Terra, Aqua et Aëre omnia inferiora constare, cum et hae ipsae matres alia quaedam terna habeant principia, Philosophis vulgaribus nondum satis perspecta, de quibus nunc non est disputandi locus. Subiungis deinde te videre, quod iam tandem obtinueris, me Diaphanitatem Aëris puri, nihil differre a Diaphanitate materiae Planetis circumfusae, tibi concessisse, nec ob id dubitas, quin veritas temporis filia me reliquam etiam tuam sententiam suo tempore sit edoctura. At quibus vnquam perspicillis haec ita acute vidisti? Aut quibus modis e scriptis meis id vnquam colligere potuisti; Miratus sum ista legens, cur astruere velis, me mihi ipsi contraria hac in parte proponere; Inspexi itaque denuo Exemplar literarum tibi vltimo inscriptarum, e quibus procul dubio haec colligere volebas. At ego nihil eiuscemodi in illis inuenio, imo potius tuae assertioni plane contrarium. Dedi illic primo Exemplum e rebus inferioribus quae beneficio Artis Spagyricae in tantam subtilitatem exaltari queant, vt Diaphanitatem, quantum sensibus discernatur, consimilem repraesentent, et nihilominus diuersae esse substantiae ostendi, Ideoque non sequi id, quod tu intendebas, etiamsi concederetur, ob Refractiones ad verticem non tendentes Caeli et Aëris purioris quo ad Diaphanitatem inperceptibilem esse discrepantiam, propterea ex vna et eadem constare materia. In hunc modum tecum ratiocinatus sum, neque ob id concessi Aëris et Aetheris Diaphanitatem omnino eandem esse: Imo haec verba aliud indicantia subiunxi. Sic quoque Caeli et Aëris Diaphanitatem, si vel prorsus eaedem forent, quod tamen nondum satis obtentum est, nihilominus diuersam substantiam atque materiam habere nihil impedit; Cur igitur quaeso gloriaris, te a me id obtinuisse quod ego apertis verbis dixi nondum satis obtentum esse? Cur adeo iniuriose mea inuertis? Curque iudicium de his Placitis tam inconsiderate praecipitas? Si veritas Temporis filia me vnquam melius informârit, vtique veritatem acceptare non tergiuersabor; idque quacunque tandem occasione concessum fuerit. Necdum tamen video, cur vllis tuis opinionibus, de quibus inter nos controuersum est, assentiar: Neque euidenter demonstrabis, me quippiam eorum, quae ad te hactenus vel obiter scripsi, aut aliâs emisi, quod vllius sit momenti, retractasse, Quemadmodum tu non pauca vel in his ipsis literis, antea acriter defensa, non saltem in dubium vocas, sed prorsus irrita esse cupis. Vt te non asseruisse Prophetas in Physica nihilo plus calluisse, quam vulgus iners: Et Mosen de duobus magnis luminaribus loquentem contra Geometricas Demonstrationes fecisse, quasi hoc non esset detrahere sacris literis: Quaestionem de motu Terrae Copernicaeo motam, cum materia Caeli implicare, atque hanc ex Augustino atque alijs Neotericis Theologis, confundendo Caelum et Terram niti probare: Te titulum Tomorum meorum de Cometarum caelesti generatione non reprehendere, cum antea obieceris me corruptionem in Caelum introducere, si generationem astruam. Cometarum caudas tot verbis, tum etiam ex Obseruatione aliqua, antea tanquam partes corporis essent, ex eâdem materia constantes asseuerâsse, et iam non amplius ea pro veris habere, imo ipsam Obseruationem perscriptam infectam cupere: Totam de Cometarum generatione sententiam, prius adeo vel propter Graminaeum quendam, mihi obtrusam, nunc ita posthabere, vt integrum caput ea de caussa in scripto tuo mutandum, aliterque tractandum censeas: Trabes discurrentes, antea a Sole illuminatas, nunc lumine eius orbare, et si quae sunt alia Corollaria. Nolo enim omnia nimis scrupulose eruere. Haec tamen non ideo recenseo, quod te deuiationes tuas agnoscere atque emendare exprobrare velim. Id enim laudo, et vtinam saepius sic feceris, teque a veritate Temporis filia, vti recte dixisti, instrui permiseris. Sic centrum Circuli quod est vnicum, collineatius attigeris. Si ostenderis vnquam me aliqua scripsisse quae reuocatione indigeant, gratias habebo; Me quicquam meorum adhuc retractasse nec dum sum conscius; non quod id fieri nequeat, vt sumus homines, sed quia quod tu in nostris scriptis te videre dicas, nondum meis patuerit oculis, neque id adhuc agnoscam. Comparatio illa, quam proposui, tibique aliquatenus explicui, inter liquorem Aquae et Vini, vtroque depurato, respectu materiae Aëris et Caeli, forte maiorem merebatur acceptionem, quam vt ita exciperetur. Reuera enim Caelum ita se habet ad Aërem Elementarem, sicut Spiritus aliquis Vini vel alterius generosi liquoris ad Aquam defaecatam. Et licet Diaphana pene eadem sint, tamen substantia longe diuersa. Neque scio an melior comparatio e rebus terrestribus deduci possit. Hinc est, quod quidam Philosophantium Vini praesertim Spiritum aliquoties modeste exaltatum depuratumque, ac tandem circulatione continua atque diutina ab Elementari intemperantia liberatum, Aether appellare, vel Caelum Philosophicum non dubitârint, quamuis an id ea ratione fieri queat, qua illi proponunt, vt quaedam alia non desiderentur nunc dicere nolim. Id saltem aperte affirmare ausim, in singulis terrestribus substantijs aliquid latere caelesti naturae analogum, in quibusdam plus, aliquibus vero minus, quod nec Aërem, nec Aquam, aut Terram, aut etiam Ignis Elementum (si id in rerum natura foret) proprie sapiat, quamuis et haec Elementaria singulis vna insint grossiori quadam compagine: Neque existimandum venit, a Sole saltem vel reliquis Sideribus, hanc vim superelementarem elementaribus inesse, licet et hoc aliqua ex parte non negârim. Sunt enim quaedam his, quaedam alijs Sideribus magis conformia, Interim tamen et vniuersalem Caeli essentiam in qua hae Astrales virtutes habitant, non aliter quam Sidera ipsa in Caelo suae naturae competenti voluuntur, quaelibet inferiora, quo ad magis vel minus aemulantur. Sed haec de his nunc sit disseruisse satis, cum ad vulgo receptam Philosophiam non pertineant, atque illic forte vix recipiantur. Hypotheses Ptolemaicas vel Copernianas, vtram harum approbaueris, per me tibi liberum erit. Suaderem saltem, vt de Caelo e Caelo ipso, non ex Chartis et ingeniosis Demonstrationibus, ipsi Caelo forte non vbique consonis, iudicium formares. Liceat itaque et mihi, quid me Caelum in his edocuerit, libere pronuntiare. De Surreptore mei Systematis nolo hîc verbum addere, neque enim dignus est. Respondi tibi breuiter in vltimis, ad ea quae huic nostrae Hypothesium innouationi obiecisti; pleniorem resolutionem eiuscemodi et aliorum dubiorum obtinebis, quando ex professo de motu Secundorum Mobilium egero, eundemque quo ad numerationem ipsi Caelo ad amussim conformem reddere elaborâro, et vt (fauente Caelorum opifice) confido, ad optatum finem rem omnem deduxere. Si quae plura interea excogitâris, quae in contrarium adferri posse existimes, libere illa proferendo, rem non ingratam feceris. Nonnunquam enim contradicendo Veritas illustrior redditur. Occasiones quae me ad talem Caelestium Reuolutionum ordinationem impulerunt, tibi etiam breuiter indicaui. Neque enim temere, aut leui de causa huc perductus sum, sed ipsum me Caelum ita de se sentire docuit, nullo alio Praeceptore aut vllis libris, vel Tabularum Farraginibus quippiam huc conferentibus. Contuli etiam cum quibusdam alijs in Germania eruditis Mathematicis de hac nostra Neoterica inuentione, quae licet quibusdam Aristoteleis praesertim Orbium realitatibus nimium addictis, non admodum arrideat, attamen cordatioribus et qui sine praeoccupata sententia rem ponderant, rectiusque introspiciunt, admodum concinna censetur. Quamuis vt dicam id quod res est, aliorum iudicia licet non contemnam, tamen siue pro vel contra faciant, non multum moror, modo ipsa caelitus deducta experientia rem ita se habere euidenter conuincat. Scio quam abstrusa semper fuerint Naturae penetralia, quamque ea quae in Physicis nos rite perspecta habere arbitramur, longissime saepenumero a scope aberrent. Idcirco non tam aliorum Autoritati atque applausui, acquiescendum existimo, quin nos ipsos an res ita se habeat, vel secus, periculum facere, et Obseruationum ac Demonstrationum trutina omnia expendere, atque comprobare deceat. Sed de his nunc non est locus pluribus disserere. At quoniam video Copernicaeam circa Triplicem Terrae motum sententiam tibi admodum arridere; proponam in quolibet horum vnicum saltem, licet multo plura dari queant, non adeo operosum dubium. Primo quantum ad Diurnum circa suum axem motum, quo Terra 24. Horis conuolui fingitur, sicque vniuersalis cursus ab ortu in occasum excusatur, attinet; Dic mihi, quî fieri possit, vt globus plumbeus ex altissima turri iusto modo demissus, punctum Terrae infra se positum perpendiculariter ad amussim contingat; id enim circumducta interea Terra, cum cursus eius sit velocissimus, fieri nequaquam posse, te supputatio docebit Geometrica: Siquidem in vno Scrupulo secundo temporis Terra reuolui debeat etiam in his Borealioribus plagis sesquicentum passus maiores proxime. Hinc caetera ratiocinare. Neque enim casus plumbi Aërem concomitatur, sed violenter illum transit. Circa alterum motum Terrae Annuum, qui octauam Sphaeram tantopere remoueret vt orbis quem haec designaret respectu eius euanescat, Edissere, anne hîc tibi verisimile videatur, spatium quod est a Sole, tunc centro vniuersi, ad Saturnum plusquam 700 vicibus contineri intra hunc et Affixarum Sphaeram, idque totum nullis Sideribus refertum. Atqui id fieri necesse est, si saltem Orbis Annuus Terrae instar vnius minuti apparebit. Imo tunc quoque Stellae Fixae Tertiae magnitudinis, quae vnum minutum in Diametro habent, necessario erunt aequales toti huic Orbi Annuo, id est comprehendent in Diametro 2284. Semidiametros Terrae. Distabunt enim 7850000 ijsdem Semidiametris proxime. Quid dicemus de Stellis primae magnitudinis; quarum aliquae bina, quaedam fere terna minuta in Diametro visibili occupant; Et quid si adhuc altius remoueatur octaua Sphaera, vt motus Terrae annuus illic prorsus euanescat? Deduc si lubet, haec Geometrice, et videbis quanta absurda, vel sic inferendo (vt de alijs non dicam) assumtionem hanc concomitentur. Tertius, sublato Annuo, per se ruit; vel si vna cum illo tibi constare posse videatur, quî quaeso fieri poterit, vt Axis Terrae in contrarium motui centri annuatim adeo correspondenter gyretur, vt quiescere nihilominus appareat? Quomodo etiam Axin et Centrum duplici diuersoque motu agitari datur, in corpore vnico et simplici? Vt de tertio illo circa Axem diurno superueniente, nihil replicem. Taceo quoque librationum intricationes, nec promotioni Fixarum cui destinantur vbique correspondentes, valde absonas esse. Haec et similia tute tecum perpende, atque si dabitur, per ocium resolue. Plura habebis aliâs. Si igitur Copernicea ratiocinatio constare non poterit, vt sane non potest, Ptolemaica, quâm Copernicus (vt alia taceam) satis refutauit, nihil impediet quo minus nostra inuentio locum mereatur. Exponis demum caussas cur Illustriss. Princeps tuus meis non responderit, quas et libenter accipio. Scriberem nunc ipsius Cels. sed nihil occurrit, praeter ea quae vltimis consignaui. Simulque vereor ne ipsius C. Reipublicae administratione alijsque curis occupatam meis ieiunis literis molestem. FRISCHLINVS de quo scribis, huc non venit, neque literas vllas a te misit, alias non inhumaniter a me excipiendus. Audiui enim virum esse variae literaturae et facundum. Facis insuper mentionem Molendini Papyro conficiendae idonei, quod me extructurum indicaui, ne toties et tam diu charta impressoria pro meis lucubrationibus excudendis, e Germania afferenda frustrer, idque Principi tuo placuisse ais, quod facile credo. Nam et in his confluentiam quandam inuicem habemus. Quemadmodum enim ipsius Cels. Architecturâ, Aggeribus, Fossis, Aquaeductibus, Piscinis, Hortis et Molendinis similibusque Mechanicis structuris conficiendis delectatur, sic et ego pro meo modulo, praesertim Aestiuo tempore, quando altioribus vacare non licet, haecque commodius tractantur. Nam et illa Geometricum quid redolent, si modo debita Symmetria conficienda sint. Molendinum illud iam paratum est, aggere altissimo latissimoque sufficientem Aquam tam Aestiuo quam Hyberno tempore cohibente, Rotaque 12. vlnarum in Diametro minima Aqua impulsa, et duplex praeter Papyraceum opus peragente. Piscinis etiam quamplurimis hinc inde ordine dispositis, vt quando necesse fuerit, hae quoque Moletrinae Aquas suppeditare queant. Haecque omnia ante paucos annos sicca erant. Quin et alterum Molendinum pro Rusticis meis et opificibus, in vicinia circumhabitantibus hîc molior, vbi etiam nulla pene Aqua in promptu nunc putatur. Nolo enim, vt alij Chartaceas operas et quae ad propria mea domestica pertinent, perlustrent atque intempestiuius interturbent. Si Victorinus Schonfeldt huc filium suum miserit me inuisendi caussa, per me illi id licet: Quamprimum illi vel mihi ita videbitur, vt ad suos remeet, vtrique satis liberum erit. An promotus fit in Magistrum liberalium Artium nec ne, apud me perinde est, Mallem tamen illum talem esse, quam appellari. Sed hoc non tam leui pretio prostat; sufficeret harum discipulum esse. Sed video mi Rothmanne me in respondendo tuis strictioribus et festinanti calamo, vti apparet, exaratis literis fuisse nimis copiosum, quod eo promptius admisi, ne tuam paucitatem (tanquam retaliationi nimium indulgendo) vel prorsus nulla, vel etiam breuiore rescriptione vlcisci velle viderer. Licet enim ego et pluribus nunc, quam tu istas scribendo vel forte vnquam alias implicer negotijs, tamen haec tuis quin responderem adeoque luculenter nullis alijs impediri volui occupationibus; quod et in vltimo datis praeter morbum quem significabam, reuera ita se habuit, vt tanto interlapso tempore tibi procul dubio et commodius minusque aduersum rescribendi suppetierit otium. Si tamen quid in his liberioris admonitionis scriptum est, in meliorem partem accipe et communium studiorum Amori tribue. Vale et si vacat, iam statim rescribe, vt ad Nundinas proxime instantes Deo volente responsum denuo nanciscaris. Has interea festinanti quoque calamo exaratas boni consule.
Iterum feliciter vale.
Datae Vraniburgi 24. Nouemb. Anno 1589.
TYCHO BRAHE.


*[Postscript — restored from Dreyer, Opera Omnia VI, pp. 199–200; dropped by the working transcription. See Apparatus.]*
POSTSCRIPTA. QVONIAM ex literis vestris, tum etiam aliunde percepi, ILLVSTRISSIMVM PRINCIPEM LANDGRAVIVM, suas aliquot Annorum in affixis Stellis obseruationes publici iuris facere decreuisse, tuaque opera in hoc negotio exsequendo vti: Rogo, per Astronomiae honorem & commodum, vt labores hos, Herculeis forte non minores, maturare non pigeat, ne nimium procrastinando, aut prorsus intercidant, aut vix tandem in commune Artis huius promouendae emolumentum, lucem publicam videant. Hinc enim, tam illi, qui modo sunt superstites, quam posteri, quos tam sublimium cura rerum tangit, facile decernent, quam erroneis inerrantium Stellarum locis, caeloque minus congruis, tot iam sectilis ob Artificum siue penuriam, siue incuriam, hactenus Vsi simus, cum certiora in promptu non fuerint: viaque simul constare queat, Quantae molis erat Stellarum inquirere Hermas: Et, vt collatis vestris animaduersionibus cum meis, quas propediem (fauente Stellarum opifice) publicare constitui, quanta accuratior & laborum constantia res haec vtrinque exantlata sit, dignoscas. Nam quod vestrae restitutiones pene in omnibus Stellis, quasi vnciola Vnius gradus, a nostris abundando, differant, id suam apud eos, qui rei perplexam difficultatem intelligunt, facile excusationem merebitur. Neque etiam aliter fieri poterat, quin Stellarum a vobis praefiniti limites, nonnihil distantiam genuinam ab aequinoctii puncto excederent, cum solummodo per Stellam Veneris vespertinam (nec item Eoam) haud etiam satis crebro, idipsum exsecuti sitis, refractione Venerem tunc in longitudine, paululum iusto vlterius oculis insinuante. Vnde consectarium est, Stellas ab hac per intercapedinem deriuatas, etiam longitudinibus, magis quam opus erat, accrescere: vt nihil dicam de lubrica illa obseruandi via per Asimutha & Altitudines, vna cum temporum ex horologiis minus tuto obtentis denotationibus, quibus omnibus vos, vti non frustra suspicor, nimis secure confiditis. Verum, quia in primo nostro Torno Progymnasmatum Astronomicorum, capite secundo, vbi de Stellarum fixarum exacta verificatione, ex professo ago, quomodo non solum e Venere occidentali a Sole, sed etiam eadem orientali, Stellarum termini in Vnum & eundem locum tandem ad amussim recidentes, & sibijpsis apprime analogi a nobis constituti sint, abunde exponam: simulque, post octingentarum circiter, canonicam in certa loca, quoad longum & latum distributionem, Landgrauianae quoque in his rectificationis, & cur illa propemodum 5. vt indicam, minutis, nostram fere vbique exsuperet, mentionem nonnullam interseram. Nolo nunc pluribus idipsum hic inculcare. Tu saltem da operam, vt vestris hac quoque in parte Atlanticis laboribus, eorum cupidi propediem fruantur. Iamque iterum vale.
text.english:
**To the most renowned and most learned man, Master Christoph Rothmann, distinguished mathematician of the Most Illustrious Prince Wilhelm, Landgrave of Hesse, etc., his most beloved friend — heartiest greeting.**

What is the meaning of this, my dear Rothmann, that you take so unwillingly, and interpret so unfavourably, the letter I last sent you, and reply to it in so disjointed [*rhapsodice*] a fashion — when it was written with good intent, for the sake of friendly comparison between us and of drawing out more deeply the truth that lies hidden? For nowhere in that letter did I accuse you of impiety. Of anyone's piety or impiety I arrogate to myself no judgement, leaving that, as is fitting, to the searcher of all hearts. Nor did I say absolutely that you detract anything from the authority of Holy Scripture as if of set purpose; I only admonished you that you had transferred Moses's words about the Moon, the "lesser light," incompetently to a magnitude of body — though it is in fact smaller than most of the stars — whereas they ought rather to be understood of the pre-eminence of its light as it touches the Earth. I added reasons too, not, I think, unfitting ones. And that you also derogate too much from the Prophets — in asserting that they understood no more in astronomy and physics than the ignorant crowd, however much they were divinely and immediately instructed, and that besides they had ready to hand not a few traditions of the most ancient Fathers, who cultivated the study of the visible things created by God, traditions surer and better than ours, which were doubtless received from the heathen — this I judged not to be approved, and in that opinion I still persist. For I have never thought one ought to decide lightly about these matters. Indeed Franciscus Vallesius has lately expounded many things, and not to be despised, concerning what is contained physically in Holy Scripture — even following the reasonings of the common philosophers — and that, as regards those principles, not without skilful labour; although many more things in these matters lie hidden, to be unfolded far otherwise according to a truer physics, and perhaps too to be sought rather, in no small part, from these very [Scriptures]. Moreover Lambert Daneau, a man truly most highly learned and excellently deserving in the instruction of others, has built up his *Physica Theologica* from both the Old and the New Codex with no useless labour. And many things could perhaps be said about these matters elsewhere, which would require a special and truly *metaphysical* volume — not of the kind that that Greek man of Stagira [Aristotle] has thrust upon us. As for my not sufficiently understanding your letter — neither illness, though it was grave (an illness of the body, however, not of the mind), nor occupations, though these too were no few entanglements, hindered me to the degree you suppose. For no insoluble riddles lurked in it, the whole matter having long been clear enough; nor do I object anything to you that could not be gathered from that letter — indeed I perhaps spare you more than is needful. Let yours and mine at least be compared, and let others judge — others who do not indulge their passions, nor are too well pleased with themselves. To what extent you have introduced things contrary to Holy Scripture, I indicated in some way both before and now; that you do this studiously everywhere I did not say. Nor can I — though I do not profess theology — nor can any of those who practise it solidly and sincerely, assent to your assertions out of the *data* [*Dedomenis*] of Holy Scripture. In vain, therefore, do you put forward this evasion, that, when two say "one," it is not granted to you that they be "one"; for neither do I hold that to be granted to others which here I censure. That Augustine sometimes pronounced rather freely about sacred things — at times not inelegantly, at times indeed somewhat feebly, allowance being made for that age nearer the times of the Apostles — of this, by God's grace, I am not ignorant. But what do all these things contribute here, or what do they do toward the matter under discussion? The question raised was whether the mobility of the terrestrial globe, and that threefold [mobility] asserted by Copernicus, can really hold together; and whether it ought to be preferred to our own discovery; and whether Holy Scripture contradicts that imagining or not. If, therefore, you have anything from the sacred Oracles, or from their interpreters — Augustine, say, or other Fathers — making for this Copernican assertion and for your endorsement of it, cite it from their writings. Provided the reasons be just, I shall not resist them. This much I know well: that Augustine — whom alone you name — nowhere conceded a motion of the Earth, neither annual nor diurnal, since, as a man somewhat less of a mathematician, he detracted from its roundness by denying the Antipodes. Which, however, must be pardoned him. Wherefore, since he did not perceive it to be round, far less could he admit a motion suited to its roundness. The opinions of your theologians, and their verdicts on these matters — though perhaps outside their profession, and less deliberated — I do not, to be sure, despise. But since I see that they were summoned and questioned only on this head, whether the fluidity of the heaven can be established from Holy Scripture without the reality of the orbs (as your clause hints), and since you know that I, long before you dreamed of these things, had myself conceded and pronounced the very same — I wonder why you object these things that contribute nothing here. For I do not suppose that the question of the Earth's threefold whirling was put to your theologians, since very few of them would grasp it, however much they might wish to — being, as happens elsewhere too, perhaps not a little addicted to earthly things. Since, therefore, only the controversy about the mobility of the Earth — renewed and reintroduced by Copernicus out of Aristarchus and certain other ancients — was being moved between us, by what coherence, I ask, were you driven to confound it with the limpidity of the heaven, which I never denied, but rather perhaps first of all men laboured not merely to affirm but to prove, from the most certain demonstrations, that it is so? Is this "mathematical," to join and entangle disparate things — which not even the dialecticians, whether artificial or natural, would have allowed in different terms?

That the substance of the aetherial world is most fluid and everywhere passable can be proved from Holy Scripture, even with the professors of theology silent — this I have long held ascertained. And I have recorded many divinely-revealed Oracles in testimony of that fact.
