documents.abstract: Concedes complete defeat in the astronomical disputation with Tycho, reports distributing copies of Tycho's portrait among friends including Curtius who forwarded one to Bavaria.
documents.incipit: NOBILISS. D. TYCHO et amice observande. Quod tam diu ad tuas binas non responderim, multa …

text.original:
NOBILISS: VIRO, VIRTUTE ET ERUDITIONE PRÆSTANTI D. TYCHONI BRAHE DANO, DOMINO IN KNUDSTORPFF ET URANIEBURGO ETC DOMINO ET AMICO OBSERVANDO. S.

NOBILISS. D. TYCHO et amice observande. Quod tam diu ad tuas binas non responderim, multa fuerunt quae me impediverunt: tum valetudo adversa, quae me per integram propemodum Quadragesimam afflixit, tum etiam curae domesticae ac crebrae profectiones medicinae faciendae gratia. Huc accesserunt alia plurima, quae saepe praeter spem incidere consueverunt. Etiamsi vero aliquod otium habuissem, non tamen aliquid nostrae illi disputationi adijcere potuissem, vel nunc quoque possem; adeo exacte omnia abs te excussa, examinata, meaque argumenta diluta sunt, ut me veritate et evidentia demonstrationum victum esse fateri necesse sit, nisi manifestae veritati repugnare velim. Exempla aliquot tuae effigiei accepi, quae inter amicos distribui. D. CURTIUS noster quoque unam accepit, misitque in Bavariam ad quendam sibi bene notum et celebrem Poëtam, qui arguto aliquo epigrammate eam ornaret. Sed nondum accepit responsum. Hîc Pragae hoc tempore nullum eiusmodi Poëtam, quod sciam, habemus, qui meo desiderio satisfacere, et quomodo pictor faciem et lineamenta corporis, sic ille mentem et vim eius depingere posset. NICOLAUS RAYMARUS, quem tu plagij accusaveras, ante septimanas aliquot huc venit et innotuit D. CURTIO qui illum Caesari ita commendavit, ut pro Mathematico, tenui satis, in his initijs, stipendiolo sit receptus. Hodie hinc Francofurdum pro advehenda sua suppellectili discedit, mox huc rediturus. Aliud quod scribam nunc nec habeo, nec vacat.

B. V.
Datae Pragae die 29 Augusti novo stylo Anno 1591.
T. studiosiss.
THAD.


*[Postscript — restored from Dreyer, Opera Omnia VII, p. 305; dropped by the working transcription. See Apparatus.]*
POST SCRIPTA. HERI venit ad me quidam artifex, eius nomen ignoro, vir aetate grandeva, et narravit se vixisse aliquandiu tecum, saepeque multa de me audivisse: cum igitur venisset in hanc urbem, salutandi et alloquendi gratia me accessisse. Mira quaedam et Geometrica profitetur, potissimum currum quendam admirabilem, cuius rotae emensa milliaria sonitu quodam indicent, et nescio quae alia; nam plenius cum illo colloqui non licuit et aliorum interventu abruptum fuit nostrum colloquium. Electori Saxoniae, Principi Pomeraniae et quibusdam alijs eiusmodi currum se confecisse aiebat. Intellexi Caesari quoque sua servitia offerre velle.
text.english:
**To the most noble man, outstanding in virtue and erudition, Master Tycho Brahe the Dane, Lord of Knudstrup and Uraniborg etc., his lord and friend to be honoured — greeting.**

Most noble Master Tycho and friend to be honoured. That I have been so long in replying to your two letters, there were many things that hindered me: both ill health, which afflicted me through almost the whole of Lent, and also domestic cares and frequent journeys for the sake of practising medicine. To these were added very many other things, such as often tend to befall beyond expectation. But even had I had some leisure, I could not on that account have added anything to that disputation of ours, nor can I even now: so exactly has everything been sifted and examined by you, and my arguments dissolved, that I must needs confess myself vanquished by the truth and the evidence of the demonstrations, unless I were willing to fight against manifest truth. I have received several copies of your portrait, which I have distributed among friends. Our Master Curtius too received one, and sent it into Bavaria to a certain poet well known to him and celebrated, that he might adorn it with some witty epigram. But he has not yet received a reply. Here at Prague at this time we have no poet of that kind, so far as I know, who could satisfy my desire and could depict — as a painter [depicts] the face and the lineaments of the body, so he — his mind and his power. Nicolaus Raymarus, whom you had accused of plagiarism, came here some weeks ago and became known to Master Curtius, who so commended him to the Emperor that he has been taken on as Mathematician, on a little stipend slight enough, in these beginnings. Today he departs hence to Frankfurt to fetch his household goods, intending soon to return hither. Anything else to write I now neither have, nor is there leisure.

Fare you well.
Given at Prague, the 29th day of August, New Style, in the year 1591.
Most devoted to you,
Thad[daeus].


*[Postscript:]* POSTSCRIPT. Yesterday there came to me a certain craftsman — his name I do not know — a man advanced in age, and he related that he had lived with you for some time, and had often heard much about me; and so, when he had come into this city, he had approached me for the sake of greeting and conversing. He professes certain wondrous and Geometrical things, above all a certain marvellous cart, whose wheels indicate by a kind of sound the miles measured out, and I know not what else; for it was not granted to converse with him more fully, and our conversation was broken off by the intervention of others. He said he had made a cart of this kind for the Elector of Saxony, for the Prince of Pomerania, and for certain others of the like. I understood that he wishes to offer his services to the Emperor too.

documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent.** *THAD. / Thaddaeus Hagecius* = **Tadeáš Hájek z Hájku (Thaddaeus Hagecius ab Hayek)** (1525–1600), Bohemian physician, astronomer and personal physician to Emperor Rudolf II at Prague; an early and central observer of the 1572 nova, a long-standing correspondent of Tycho and the principal conduit through which Tycho's later relations with the Imperial court ran. The subscription *THAD.* abbreviates his Christian name.
- **Recipient titulature.** *D. TYCHONI BRAHE DANO, DOMINO IN KNUDSTORPFF ET URANIEBURGO* — "Master Tycho Brahe the Dane, Lord of Knudstrup and Uraniborg": *Knudstorpff* = **Knudstrup** (the Brahe family seat in Scania), *Uranieburgo* = **Uraniborg** on Hven.
- ***tuas binas*** — "your two letters" (*binas* sc. *literas*); rendered "your two letters."
- ***Quadragesimam*** — **Lent** (the forty-day fast); here a time-marker for the duration of Hagecius's illness, kept as the liturgical season.
- ***nostrae illi disputationi … meaque argumenta diluta sunt … victum esse fateri*** — "that disputation of ours … my arguments dissolved … to confess myself vanquished." This refers to the running **cosmological controversy** between the two over Tycho's geo-heliocentric world-system; Hagecius here concedes the point. *diluta* ("watered down, dissolved, refuted") is rendered "dissolved"; the concession is preserved at its full force without sharpening Tycho's claim beyond what Hagecius grants ("vanquished by the truth and the evidence of the demonstrations").
- ***Exempla aliquot tuae effigiei*** — "several copies of your portrait." The reference is to printed/engraved likenesses of Tycho being circulated among the learned; *effigies* = likeness/portrait.
- ***D. CURTIUS noster*** — **Jacobus Curtius (Jakob Kurz von Senftenau)** (d. 1594), Imperial Vice-Chancellor at Rudolf II's court and himself an amateur astronomer in correspondence with Tycho; *noster* ("our [Curtius]") marks the shared acquaintance.
- ***in Bavariam ad quendam … celebrem Poëtam … arguto … epigrammate*** — Curtius sent a portrait into **Bavaria** to a celebrated poet to furnish a "witty epigram" (*argutum epigramma*) — a learned verse-eulogy to accompany the likeness. The poet is not named.
- ***quomodo pictor faciem … sic ille mentem et vim eius depingere posset*** — "as a painter [depicts] the face … so he [could depict] his mind and power": the painter–poet topos (the painter renders the body, the poet the soul). The elliptical Latin (the verb *depingit* is supplied from *depingere*) is rendered with a bracket-free but explicit parallel; no editorial word is added beyond the supplied verb signalled by "[depicts]".
- ***NICOLAUS RAYMARUS, quem tu plagij accusaveras*** — **Nicolaus Reimers Bär**, "Reimarus Ursus" (c. 1551–1600), the Dithmarschen mathematician whom Tycho had **accused of plagiarism** (*plagium*) for publishing in his *Fundamentum astronomicum* (1588) a geo-heliocentric world-system Tycho held to be stolen from Hven — the origin of the bitter Tycho–Ursus priority dispute. Hagecius reports, neutrally, Ursus's arrival at Prague and his appointment. *plagium accusare* = "to accuse of plagiarism"; kept as the period term.
- ***innotuit D. CURTIO qui illum Caesari ita commendavit, ut pro Mathematico … stipendio sit receptus*** — Ursus "became known to Master Curtius, who so commended him to the Emperor [*Caesar* = **Rudolf II**] that he was taken on as Mathematician [i.e. **Imperial Mathematician**], on a stipend slight enough, in these beginnings." *tenui satis … in his initijs* ("slight enough … in these beginnings") is Hagecius's own hedge on the smallness of the initial salary; preserved, not smoothed.
- ***Francofurdum pro advehenda sua suppellectili*** — "to **Frankfurt** to fetch his household goods" (*suppellex* = furniture/household stuff); *advehenda* future-passive (gerundive of purpose), "for the bringing-up of."
- ***B. V.*** — *Bene vale*, "**Fare you well**".
- ***T. studiosiss.*** — *Tui studiosissimus*, "**Most devoted to you**" (subscription formula).
- **Calendar.** The dateline reads *die 29 Augusti **novo stylo** Anno 1591* — **29 August 1591, New Style (Gregorian)**, explicitly so marked by the writer; the catalogue label likewise gives "n.s." Hagecius, in Catholic Imperial Prague, dates New Style; the corresponding Old Style date (which Tycho on Hven kept) would be 19 August 1591, but the letter is **not** silently converted: the header carries the as-written N.S. date by this chapter's convention, and the 10-day gap is noted here only.

- **§1 Dreyer collation.** Closing postscript (a visiting artisan's mileage-measuring odometer-cart), restored from Dreyer VII p.305 (dropped by the working transcription).
- **Correction.** Three small corrections against Dreyer (TBOO VII pp.303-306): the postscript's "aliquando" restored to "aliquandiu" (a stay of some duration, not a single occasion); "stipendio" restored to the diminutive "stipendiolo"; and the closing dateline's inserted "Hîc" removed (Dreyer reads simply "Datæ Pragæ").

translation.warrant:
Collated against **Dreyer, *Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia*** (the edition of record), reading the printed page images. Dreyer TBOO VII pp.303-306 read as page images (the Hagecius letter runs from '[E codice Vindobonensi lat. 10686 58]' on p.304 through the postscript on p.305; pp.303 and 306 belong to the flanking Maginus letters and were read only to confirm the boundaries). Collated the whole body - the Lenten-illness excuse, the portrait-distribution and Curtius/Bavarian-poet passage, the Nicolaus Raymarus/plagiarism paragraph, and the full postscript about the unnamed elderly craftsman and his sounding-wheel cart offered to the Elector of Saxony, the Prince of Pomerania, and the Emperor - against the printed page, word by word. Found three genuine divergences between the transcribed original and Dreyer's print (listed above); the 'aliquando/aliquandiu' one is substantive enough to change a scholar's read of the craftsman's prior relationship to Tycho, so the letter is graded C and verdict *serious* despite the translation itself being a faithful rendering of the (corrupted) source it was given.

**3 defects found:**
- **text error** (medium). Dreyer prints the durative adverb 'aliquandiu' (for some time) but our transcribed original has 'aliquando' (once, at some point) - a dropped syllable that changes a duration of residence into a single occasion, a fact about the unnamed craftsman's relationship to Tycho that a scholar would take away differently. Dreyer prints: *et narravit se vixisse aliquandiu tecum, saepeque multa de me audivisse (TBOO VII p.305, postscript, l.2)*.
- **text error** (low). Dreyer prints the diminutive 'stipendiolo' (a paltry little stipend); the transcribed original drops the diminutive ending to plain 'stipendio'. Minor, since 'tenui satis' already conveys smallness, but a genuine divergence from the printed text. Dreyer prints: *ut pro Mathematico, tenui satis, in his initijs, stipendiolo sit receptus (TBOO VII p.305, l.10)*.
- **text error** (low). the transcribed original inserts 'Hîc' (here) into the closing dateline; Dreyer's closing formula reads simply 'Datae Pragae' without it. Low-impact (the place is already named), but the English 'here at' is an artifact of the corrupted source, not of Dreyer's text. Dreyer prints: *Datae Pragae die 29 Augusti novo stylo Anno 1591 (TBOO VII p.305, l.13-14)*.

**Repaired.** Verified against Dreyer TBOO VII pp.303-306. Page 305 confirms all three text error: line 10 reads "ftipendiolo"; lines 13-14 read "Datæ Pragæ" with no "Hîc"; and the postscript (headed POST SCRIPTA on the same page) reads "vixiße aliquandiu tecum". All three fixed in the Latin, with light corresponding adjustments to the English. No other defects found across the four pages.

documents.abstract: Orders Tycho to repair the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings at Roskilde Cathedral before winter, invoking obligations in his letter of enfeoffment.
documents.incipit: Christian.

text.original:
TYGE BRAHE TILL KNUDSTRUP FICK BREFF FORBERØRTE HELLIGE THRE KONGER CAPELLES BYGNING ANRØRENDIS VT SEQUITUR.

Christian.

WOR gunst thilfornn. Viid, epter att Wij komme wdi forfaringe, huorledis Hellige [thre] konger capelle wed Roschilde domkircke schall møgit werre bygfeldig och forfalden, att thend klart will nederfalde och wdj grunden forderffuis, saa frampt ther till met thet første icke schaffuis raad och kommis till hielp, och epterdi ditt forleeningsbreff paa for:ne capelle eblant andit nochsom thilholder dig at schulle holde for:ne capelle med residentzen och andit guodtz, ther tilliggendis er, wed guoed heffd och macht, tha bede Wij dig och wille, attu met thet forderligste tiltencker at schaffue raad och middell, att samme capelle wißeligen inden winteren paakommer igien kand bliffue forferdiget och forbedrit epter ditt forleeningsbreffs liudelße och indtholdt. Saaframpt for:ne capelle paa sin heffd, grund och bygning for din forsømmelße schyldt lider ydermere nogen bryst, schade och forderff, eller och anden wbeleiglighet ther aff kunde indtfalde, Wij tha thet icke schulle wiide huoß dig, och dertill wdi saa maade tiltencke andre raad och middell, wed huilcke for:ne capell kand holdis wed sin thilbørlig heffd och magt. Ther med scheer Wor aluorlig wilge och befalning. Thj thag her aldelis ingen forsømmelße fore.

Befalendis dig Gud.
Haffniæ 30. augusti a:o 91.
text.english:
**Tyge Brahe of Knudstrup received a letter concerning the building [maintenance] of the aforesaid Chapel of the Three Holy Kings, as follows:**

Christian.

Our favour beforehand. Know that, after we came into knowledge how the Chapel of the Three [Holy] Kings at Roskilde Cathedral is said to be much dilapidated and decayed, so that it will plainly fall down and be ruined to its foundations, if remedy be not provided for it and help brought to it at the very first; and since your letter of enfeoffment upon the aforesaid chapel, among other things, sufficiently enjoins you that you are to keep the aforesaid chapel, together with the residence and other property belonging to it, in good upkeep and condition: therefore we ask you, and will [it], that you with all dispatch take thought to provide ways and means, so that the same chapel may surely, before winter come on, be put in good repair again and amended according to the tenor and content of your letter of enfeoffment. If the aforesaid chapel, in its upkeep, foundation, and fabric, should through fault of your negligence suffer any further defect, harm, and ruin, or else any other inconvenience could fall out therefrom, then we shall not let that rest with you, and shall thereupon, in such case, take thought for other ways and means, whereby the aforesaid chapel may be kept in its due upkeep and condition. Herewith is done our earnest will and command. Therefore undertake herein absolutely no negligence.

Commending you to God.
At Copenhagen, 30 August, year [15]91.

documents.apparatus:
- **Issuer.** **Christian IV of Denmark** (1577–1648; r. from his father Frederik II's death in 1588). In 1591 the fourteen-year-old king was still a minor under the regency council (Frederik II had died 4 April 1588; Christian was not crowned until 1596), so this chancery missive issues in his name but under the regency's administration. The single-word subscription *"Christian."* is the king's chancery superscription, not an autograph.
- **Recipient.** **Tycho Brahe**, here styled *Tyge Brahe till Knudstrup* — "Tyge Brahe of Knudstrup," his patrimonial seat in Scania, the form used for him as a nobleman and crown fief-holder rather than as the astronomer of Hven.
- **Subject — the chapel and the fief.** The **Chapel of the Three Holy Kings** (*Hellige Tre Konger Kapel*, the Chapel of the Magi) is the burial chapel attached to **Roskilde Cathedral**, built under King Christian I (consecrated by 1463) as a royal mausoleum. Its associated prebend/canonry was a crown benefice; Tycho held it (with revenues attached) under a *forleningsbrev* ("letter of enfeoffment / letter of grant"), which carried the upkeep of the chapel and its residence as a charge upon the holder. The letter is a formal admonition that he is failing that obligation.
- **Document type.** A chancery-register entry (Sjællandske Tegnelser). The **Latin rubric** *"…HELLIGE THRE KONGER CAPELLES BYGNING ANRØRENDIS **ut sequitur**"* ("concerning the building [maintenance] of the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings, **as follows**") heads the Danish body — a code-switch preserved by this chapter's convention *bygning* here denotes the upkeep/fabric-maintenance of the building, not new construction; rendered "building [maintenance]."
- **Negations and legal force (counted; none added or dropped).** The source carries exactly three negations, each translated and none introduced:
 1. *…saa frampt ther till met thet første icke schaffuis raad och kommis till hielp* — "if remedy be **not** provided for it and help brought to it at the very first": the conditional protasis describing what causes the ruin. Rendered as a negative conditional, mood preserved (subjunctive/passive *schaffuis, kommis* = "be provided / be brought").
 2. *Wij tha thet icke schulle wiide huoß dig* — "then we shall **not** let that rest with you." The chancery idiom *vide hos (en)* = "to leave / let rest with (someone)"; the negation makes this a threat, not a reassurance: should the chapel decay further through Tycho's negligence, the king will *not* leave the matter in Tycho's hands but will himself "take thought for other ways and means" — i.e. transfer the charge (and by implication the fief). The smoother but wrong reading ("we shall not know it from you") is rejected; the legal sense is removal of trust/responsibility.
 3. *Thj thag her aldelis ingen forsømmelße fore* — "Therefore undertake herein **absolutely no** negligence." *aldelis ingen* = "absolutely no" (intensifier + negative), the closing imperative. *tage … fore* = "to undertake / set about." Kept as a single emphatic negative command.
- **Conditional structure.** The threat-clause *"Saaframpt for:ne capelle … lider ydermere nogen bryst, schade och forderff, eller och anden wbeleiglighet …, Wij tha thet icke schulle wiide huoß dig, och dertill … tiltencke andre raad och middell"* is one conditional period: protasis "if the chapel suffers further defect through your negligence," apodosis "then [we] shall not leave it with you, and shall take thought for other means." *schulle … tiltencke* are modal/future ("shall take thought"); the future-conditional force is preserved without sharpening into a flat present.
- **Orthography (chancery Danish, c. 1591).** *WOR gunst thilfornn* = *Vor gunst tilforn* ("Our favour beforehand," the royal address-formula, this chapter's convention); *Viid* = *Vid* ("Know"); *komme wdi forfaringe* = *kom i forfaring* ("came into knowledge / learned"); *bygfeldig* = "dilapidated, in need of repair" (lit. "fall-prone in fabric"); *forfalden* = "decayed"; *klart will nederfalde* = "will plainly fall down"; *wdj grunden forderffuis* = "be ruined to its foundations"; *forleeningsbreff* = *forleningsbrev* ("letter of enfeoffment / letter of grant"); *for:ne* = *fornævnte* ("aforesaid," the standard chancery abbreviation); *eblant andit* = *iblandt andet* ("among other things"); *nochsom thilholder* = "sufficiently enjoins / obliges"; *residentzen* = "the residence"; *heffd och macht/magt* = "upkeep and condition (legal possession and standing)"; *forderligste* = "most expeditious / with all dispatch"; *tiltencker / tiltencke* = "take thought, devise"; *raad och middell* = "ways and means"; *wißeligen* = "surely, assuredly"; *inden winteren paakommer* = "before winter comes on"; *forferdiget* = "completed/repaired"; *forbedrit* = "amended/bettered"; *liudelße och indtholdt* = "tenor and content"; *bryst* = "defect, lack" (*brøst*); *wbeleiglighet* = *ubelejlighed* ("inconvenience"); *indtfalde* = "fall out, arise"; *thilbørlig* = "due, proper"; *aluorlig wilge och befalning* = "earnest will and command"; *aldelis* = "altogether, absolutely."
- **Calendar / place.** *Haffniae 30. augusti a:o 91* = "At **Copenhagen** (*Hafnia*), 30 August, year [15]91" (O.S.; Denmark kept the Julian calendar until 1700). The dateline date agrees with the edition label (30 August 1591); no in-letter date discrepancy. The dateline place-name is Latin (*Haffniae*) while the body is Danish — a code-switch preserved. *Befalendis dig Gud* ("Commending you to God") is the closing formula in place of *Actum*.

Collated the full letter (entry 89) against Dreyer TBOO XIV p.60, reading the page image; the Danish text matches Dreyer word for word (the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings at Roskilde, the letter of enfeoffment, the deadline before winter, the date Haffniae 30 augusti a:o 91), and the translation renders every clause faithfully. No defects found.

documents.abstract: Requests the elk Tycho promised, wanting it as a companion for his deer-park elk, and offers Zapfenburger wine in return.
documents.incipit: VNSERN gnedigen Gruß zuvor/ Vester lieber Besonder/ Wir mögen euch gnediglich nicht …

text.original:
DEM VESTEN/ VNSERM LIEBEN BESONDERN/ TYCHONI BRAHE, HERRN ZU KNUDSTRUP.
WILHELM VON GOTTES GNADEN/ LANDTGRAUE ZU HESSEN/ GRAUE ZU CATZENELNBOGEN/ ETC.

VNSERN gnedigen Gruß zuvor/ Vester lieber Besonder/ Wir mögen euch gnediglich nicht verhalten/ daß wir in vnserm Thiergarten ein Elendsthier haben/ daß sich dan diesen Winter vnd Sommer vber wol gehalten/ vnd fein zugenommen hat/ jm auch sonst nichts mangelt/ alß daß es keinen Gehülffen hat. Weyl wir dan auß ewerm jüngsten Schreiben sub dato den 2. Aprilis verstanden/ daß jr auch ein Elendthier hettet/ vnd vns dasselbige gerne zustehen lassen woltet/ So nemen wir dasselbige von euch zu gnedigen danck an/ vnd haben demnach nicht vnderlassen wollen/ gegenwertigen Botten zu euch abzufertigen/ vnd jm zu befehlen/ daß er bemelt Elendt bey euch abholen/ vnd vns zufüren soli. Woferne jr vns nu dasselbige/ ewerm Zuschreiben nach/ folgen lassen wollet/ wie wir vns gleichwol zu euch versehen thun/ so geschicht vns daran zu angenemen gefallen/ vnd wollen wir es hiernechst mit einem hübschen Zapffenburger gegen euch erwidern/ vnd sonst in Gnaden eingedenck seyn.

Wir zweiffeln auch nicht/ jr werdet in dem Deutschen Exemplari Gesneri de Animalibus Quadrupedibus gelesen haben/ was er fol. 85. von einem Thier/ so Rix, oder wie etliche wollen/ Orix genandt wird/ schreiben thut/ Möchten gerne wissen/ ob jr davon etwas in Erfarung bracht/ oder auch mit Leuten geredt/ die es gesehen/ oder berichten können/ was es vor ein gelegenheit darumb habe/ vbi inveniatur, et si tansæ proceritatis,quantæ a Gesnero pingitur, siet.

Vnser Mathematicus CHRISTOPHORVS ROTHMANNVS ist bey vns noch nicht widerumb ankommen/ vnd ob wir jn wol zu vns anhero erfordert/ so hat er sich doch seiner Schwacheit halben (darumb wir gleichwol keine eigentliche gelegenheit wissen) entschüldigen lassen.

Die begerte Papiermacher haben wir bißhero vber angewendten fleiß nicht bekommen können/ Wir haben aber vnsern Dienern/ so wir jetzt angehende Franckfurder Meß abgefertigt/ befolen/ daß sie sich daselbst fleissig vmbhören sollen/ ob sie dieselbigen zuwegen bringen mögen/ Was nu dieselbigen außrichten/ davon solt jr hiernechst berichtet werden.

Was wir dißmal von Zeitungen bey handen gehabt/ davon thun wir euch hierneben Abschrifft zufertigen/ vnd werdet jr darauß vernemen/ wie es in Franckreich vnd andern orten jetziger zeit stehet/ vnd daß es miserrimus Status totius Europæ ist. Was jhr dan de Statu Daniæ vnd sonst newes habt/ begeren wir gnediglich/ vns solchs hinwider zu communiciren.

Vnd bleiben euch mit gnedigem guten Willen wolgewogen.
Datum in vnser Stadt vnd Vestung Cassel/ am 31. Augusti, Anno 1591.
WILHELM LANDSGRAFF ZU HESSEN


*[Postscript — restored from Dreyer, Opera Omnia VI, p. 241; dropped by the working transcription. See Apparatus.]*
POSTSCRIPTA. WAN auch ewere Obseruationes Stellarum Fixarum & erraticarum fertig, möchten wir dieselbige wol haben, mit den vnsern zu rectificiren. Mit dem Orix wollet fleissig nachfragen, ob vnd an was orten man es finde, vnd wie es allenthalben qualificiret. Dan Brieffszeiger ewer Vetter Ascanius Bilde, wil dero im Thiergarten zu Coppenhagen vnd zu Croneburg oder Friderichsburg effictae gesehen haben, Aber bey weitem deserviret er es nicht so groß alß Gesnerus, dan 23. Span ist ein grosse höhe von einem Thier, doch ists dem Creatori nicht vnmöglich.
text.english:
**To the honourable, Our trusty and well-beloved, Tycho Brahe, Lord of Knudstrup.**
**Wilhelm, by the grace of God, Landgrave of Hesse, Count of Katzenelnbogen, etc.**

Our gracious greeting beforehand. Our trusty and well-beloved: we would not graciously withhold from you that we have in Our deer-park an elk, which has indeed borne up well through this winter and summer and has put on good condition, and which lacks nothing else save that it has no companion. Since, then, We understood from your most recent letter, dated 2 April, that you too had an elk, and were willing to let Us have it, We accept it from you with gracious thanks; and We have accordingly not wished to refrain from dispatching the present messenger to you, and from charging him to fetch the said elk from you and bring it to Us. If, then, you will now let Us have the same, according to your written undertaking — as indeed We do expect of you — that will be done to Our agreeable pleasure, and We will requite it to you hereafter with a fine [cask of] Zapfenburger, and otherwise remain graciously mindful [of you].


We do not doubt, moreover, that you will have read in the German copy of Gesner *On the Four-Footed Animals* what he writes at folio 85 of an animal that is called *Rix*, or, as some will have it, *Orix*. We should gladly know whether you have learned anything about it, or have spoken with people who have seen it or can give report of it — what the circumstances of it are, where it is found, and whether it is of as great a stature as it is depicted by Gesner.

Our mathematician Christoph Rothmann has not yet come back to Us; and although We did indeed summon him hither to Us, he has nonetheless excused himself on the ground of his ill health (the precise occasion of which We do not, however, rightly know).

The paper-makers you desired We have hitherto, for all the diligence applied, not been able to obtain; but We have charged Our servants, whom We have now dispatched to the coming Frankfurt fair, that they shall diligently make inquiry there whether they may procure the same. What they then accomplish, of that you shall be informed hereafter.

Such tidings as We have had to hand this time, of these We send you a transcript herewith; and from it you will perceive how matters stand in France and in other places at the present time, and that it is a most wretched state of all Europe. What, then, you have concerning the state of Denmark and other news, We graciously desire you to communicate the same to Us in return.

And We remain well-disposed toward you with gracious good will.
Given in Our city and fortress of Kassel, on 31 August, in the year 1591.
Wilhelm, Landgrave of Hesse.


*[Postscript:]* Postscript. When, too, your observations of the fixed and the wandering stars are ready, We should gladly have the same, to rectify them with Our own. About the oryx We would have you diligently inquire — whether, and in what places, it is to be found, and how it is everywhere qualified [of what nature it is]; for the bearer of this letter, your kinsman Ascanius Bilde, will have it that he has seen some of the kind in the deer-park at Copenhagen and at Kronborg or Frederiksborg. But by his account it is by far not so large as Gesner [makes it]; for 23 spans is a great height for an animal — yet to the Creator it is not impossible.

documents.apparatus:
- **Issuer.** *Wilhelm von Gottes Gnaden, Landtgraue zu Hessen* = **Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel** (1532–1592), the "astronomer-prince" of Kassel, Tycho's leading princely correspondent and the patron of the Kassel observatory; *Graue zu Catzenelnbogen* = Count of **Katzenelnbogen** (an inherited Hessian comital title). The princely *Wir / euch* register and full titulature are preserved throughout, by this chapter's convention
- **Recipient address.** *DEM VESTEN / VNSERM LIEBEN BESONDERN / TYCHONI BRAHE, HERRN ZU KNUDSTRUP* — "To the honourable [*vest* = *fest*, the standard chancery honorific for a nobleman], Our trusty and well-beloved [*Vnserm lieben Besondern*, the fixed princely address-formula, this chapter's convention], Tycho Brahe, Lord of **Knudstrup**" (Tycho's ancestral Scanian seat).
- **Opening formula.** *VNSERN gnedigen Gruß zuvor* = "Our gracious greeting beforehand".
- **Subject — the elk exchange.** *Elendsthier / Elendthier / Elendt* = **elk (moose)** (Frühneuhochdeutsch *Elend(t)* "elk"); the Landgrave's elk in his *Thiergarten* ("deer-park, menagerie") lacks a *Gehülffe* ("companion, mate"), and he takes up Tycho's prior offer (in a letter *sub dato den 2. Aprilis*, "dated 2 April") of a second elk from Hven.
- **Latin code-switches.** *sub dato* = "dated"; the German text switches into Latin for set phrases, in the chancery manner: *miserrimus Status totius Europae* = "a most wretched state of all Europe"; *de Statu Daniae* = "concerning the state of Denmark"; *communiciren* = the Latinate verb "to communicate."
- ***Zapffenburger*** — a wine. The term denotes a wine of the *Zapfenberg* type (a sweet/strong wine of the kind dispensed *vom Zapfen*, "from the spigot"); rendered "a fine [cask of] Zapfenburger," with *[cask of]* bracketed as an editorial supplement since the source names only the wine, not its vessel. The Landgrave offers it as a *Gegengeschenk* (return-gift) for the elk.
- **The Gesner zoological query.** *dem Deutschen Exemplari Gesneri de Animalibus Quadrupedibus* = "the German copy of **Gesner**'s *On the Four-Footed Animals*" — Conrad Gesner's *Historia animalium* (Liber I, *De quadrupedibus uiuiparis*, Zurich 1551), in its German translation (the *Thierbuch*). *fol. 85* is cited as written. The animal *Rix … oder … Orix* is the classical **oryx** (the antelope of Pliny and Aelian); the Landgrave asks Tycho for natural-historical intelligence on it.
- **Latin natural-history crux.** *vbi inveniatur, et si tansae proceritatis, quantae a Gesnero pingitur, siet* — "where it is found, and whether it is of as great a stature as it is depicted by Gesner." **Two printed forms flagged, not silently corrected**: *tansae* is read as *tantae* ("so great / as great"), and *siet* as an archaising/poetic form of *sit* ("it be"). Both readings are adopted in the translation while the printed forms are kept in the Source block; neither alters the sense.
- ***Vnser Mathematicus Christophorus Rothmannus*** = **Christoph Rothmann**, the Landgrave's mathematician at Kassel (and himself a long-standing Tycho correspondent). He had left Kassel in 1590 — ostensibly to visit Hven — and never returned to his post; here the Landgrave reports that Rothmann has excused himself *seiner Schwacheit halben* ("on the ground of his ill health"), the cause of which the Landgrave professes not to know.
- ***die begerte Papiermacher*** — "the paper-makers you desired": Tycho had asked the Landgrave's help in recruiting skilled paper-makers (for his paper-mill on Hven); the Landgrave reports he could not get them, but has set his servants to inquire at the **Frankfurt fair** (*Franckfurder Meß*, the great autumn book-and-trade fair).
- ***Zeitungen*** — "tidings, news-reports" (here in the early sense of circulated news-sheets / dispatches, not a printed newspaper); the Landgrave encloses a transcript (*Abschrifft*) reporting the wars in **France** (the French Wars of Religion).
- **Orthography (chancery German, c. 1591).** *v/u* for *u/v* (*vnserm, vber, vns*); *jr / jm / jn* = *ihr / ihm / ihn*; *daß … daß* used for both conjunction and relative *das*; *soli* is a printer's setting of *soll*; *thun / thut* = *tun / tut*; *Weyl* = *weil*; *gnediglich* = *gnädiglich*.
- **Calendar / place.** *Datum in vnser Stadt vnd Vestung Cassel / am 31. Augusti, Anno 1591* = "Given in Our city and fortress of **Kassel**, on 31 August, in the year 1591" (O.S.; Hesse-Kassel, a Protestant state, kept the Julian calendar at this date). The dateline agrees with the edition label.

- **§1 Dreyer collation.** German closing postscript, restored from Dreyer VI, p. 241 (dropped by the working transcription); the bearer "Ascanius Bilde", the "23 spans", and the oryx reading confirmed against the facing Latin (VI, p. 242). This is the source of the "23 spans" datum the next letter (15910926001) refers back to.

documents.abstract: Explains the three-and-a-half-month delay in receiving Wilhelm's May letter, then discusses the first volume of *De Recentioribus coeli Phaenomenis* and its treatment of the stellar restoration.
documents.incipit: DURCHLEUCHTIGSTER/ Hochgeborner Fürst. Ewer F. G. sind meine fleißwillige Dienste nach …

text.original:
DEM DURCHLEUCHTIGSTEN/ HOCHGEBORNEN FÜRSTEN VND HERRN/ HERRN WILHELM, LANDTGRAUEN ZU HESSEN / GRAUEN ZU CATZENELNBOGEN/ DIETZ/ ZIEGENHAIN VND NIDDA: MEINEM GNEDIGEN HERRN.

DURCHLEUCHTIGSTER/ Hochgeborner Fürst. Ewer F. G. sind meine fleißwillige Dienste nach allem vermügen jeder zeit zuvoran bereit. Gnedigster Herr/ Ew. F.G. an mich vnder dato den 22. Maij nechsthin/ auß jhrer Stadt vnd Vestung Cassel außgangenes Schreiben/ ist mir nu erst den 7. huius allhie auff Vraniburg zu handen Commen. Wo es so lange 3½. Monat/ vnder Wegen sey auffgehalten/ kan ich nicht wissen/ sonst hette ichs zeitlicher zu beantworten nicht vnderlassen.

Was erstlich meines fürhabenden Operis primum Tomum de Recentioribus cœli Phænomenis belangt/ in welchem Capite 2. Stellarum fixarum Restitutio fundamentaliter tractirt wirdt/ dessen Ew. F. G. in jhrem Schreiben gedenckt/ Darauff kan Ew. F. G. ich dienstlich nicht verhalten/ daß dasselb Opus noch nicht vollends durch den Druck verfertigt ist/ Denn ich diesen Sommer anderer nothwendiger auffliegender Gescheffte halben nicht weyl gehabt/ solchem auffzuwarten. Wenn aber Gott Gnat vnd gelegenheit verleihen wirdt/ daß es diesen Winter möchte fertig werden/ alßdenn wil ichs Ew. F. G. jhrem begeren nach/ mittheilen.

Daß Ew. F. G. Mathematicus, ROTHMANNVS, noch nicht zu Ew. F. G. wider ankommen gewesen/ solchs thut mich nicht wenig verwundern/ denn er hat sich bey mir nicht anders mercken lassen/ denn daß er von stunden wider zu rück gen Cassel sich begeben wolte/ welches nu eben ein Jahr verlitten ist. Wofern der Morbus (desse nEw. F. G. meldung thut) in causa were/ daß er so lange außbleibt/ so hette er je mitler zeit sich können curiren lassen. Er ließ sich solchs mangels allhie gar nicht vernemen/ sonst were vielleicht hie so gut Paracelsisch Remedium dagegen zu finden/ alß anderßwo/ welches jhme auch ohn zweiffel wolbewust ist. Ich gedencke aber/ so er noch nicht widerumb zu Ew. F. G. ankommen ist/ er werde sich mit dem ersten wider einstellen. Es were gut/ daß er das Opus Stellarum Fixarum mit erster gelegenheit verfertigte/ auff daß die langweylung vnd groß angewandte mühe vnd fleiß nicht hinder bliebe/ sondern andern / vnd Posteritati zu nutz kommen möchte.

So viel das Riensthier betrifft/ da Ew. F. G. von schreibt/ hab ich wol auch in dem Deutschen Gesnero, welchs Buch mir auch bey der handt ist/ sein Iconem vnd Descriptionem gefunden/ der es ein Roßhirsch nennet/ Aber bißhero hab ich noch nicht erfahren können/ daß ein solches allhie soll verhanden seyn. Ich bin selber zu etlichen malen bey Königlicher Maiestat/ Hochlöblicher gedechtnuß/ im Thiergarten gewesen/ hab aber kein solchs allda jemals vernommen. Deßgleichen auch nicht zu Koppenhagen. So ich aber noch einige wissenschafft darumb kriegen kan/ wil Ew. F. G. ich davon Bericht zustellen.

Der Rhenböcke oder Thier/ seyndt wol allhie ein oder zwey auffm Holm zu Koppenhagen gegangen/ wie ich im worigen Schreiben angezogen hab/ Aber sie können allhie den Sommer vber nicht leben/ vnd die Hitze vertragen/ viel weniger im Landt zu Hessen/ oder andern orten/ die mehr gegen Süden liegen/ Denn sie haben jhre stelle in dem gar Septentrionali parte Noruegiæ vnd Sueciæ, vnd können nicht wol an andern orten vberbleiben. Aber die Elendsthier/ wiewol sie auch auß Norwegen vnd Schweden jren vrsprung haben/ so können sie doch allhie in Dennemarck etliche Jar vber/ wenn sie wol vnderhalten werden/ verharren. Versehe mich darumb/ man werde sie auch in Deutschlandt ziehen vnd halten können/ Denn es bißweylen hie im Sommer wol so hitzig ist alß dort. Ich hab letzst mal/ da Ew. F. G. ich zuschrieb/ eines hie gegen vber in Schonen/ auff meinen Gütern gehabt/ vnd wie ichs hab wollen herüber auff diese Insul holen lassen/ ist es an die Stadt/ mit Namen Landskronen/ die hie gegen vber ligt/ ankommen/ vnd allda etliche Tage auffm Schlosse/ bey einem Edelmann/ der meiner Schwester Tochter hat/ von luft wegen auffgehalten/ da es denn/ alß man vber Tisch gesessen/ ein mal die Treppe hinauff gegangen/ vnd sich in der Stuben von starckem Bier so voll getruncken/ daß es im wider herab gehen/ die Stiege hinab gefallen/ vnd das eine Bein zerbrochen/ welchs man mit keinem fleiß wider heylen kunde lassen. Vnd ist also darüber gestorben. So baldt ich aber ein anders oder ein par widerumb bekommen kan/ die zam seyn/ wil Ew. F. G. ich die gutwillig vnd mit allem fleiß zuschicken.

Ferner/ da Ew. F. G. in jrem Schreiben mention thut vom Papiermacher/ daß Ew. F. G. nach einem oder zween zu Franckfurt wolte vmbhören lassen/ kan Ew. F. G. ich nicht bergen/ daß ich selber schon einen bekommen hab/ der deß Handtwercks gnugsam erfaren/ vnd nu mit einem Gesellen im Wercke ist/ vmb Druckpapier zu machen. Thu mich gleichwol gegen Ew. F. G. dienstlichst vnd zum höchsten bedancken/ daß dieselbige gnedigen willens gewesen/ vnd sich nicht beschweret/ solch vngemach meinet halben auff sich zu nemen. Wo Ew. F. G. ich hinwiderumb nach meinem geringen eussersten vermügen zu dienst vnd gefallen seyn kan/ darzu erbiete ich mich gantz willig/ vnd soll Ew. F. G. mir ohn das zu gebieten haben.

Wil Ew. F. G. in Schirm deß Allerhöchsten zu langwiriger glücklicher Gesundtheit vnd Landsregierung hiemit dienstfleissig befolen haben.
Datum Vraniburg, den 8. Septemb. Anno 1591.
Ewer F. G.
Dienstwilliger
TYCHO BRAHE.


*[Postscript — restored from Dreyer, Opera Omnia VI, pp. 236–237; dropped by the working transcription. See Apparatus.]*
POSTSCRIPTA. AVFF daß aber diß mein Schreiben nicht alleine von den Irdischen Thieren, sondern etwas de Caelestibus (quæ nostra est voluptas) inhalte, wolte ich nicht vnderlassen, Ew. F. G. zu significiren, daß Martis Stella, der sonsten mehr alß die andern Planeten den Calculum Astronomicum eludirt, ist im letzsten Acronycho situ, welches geschehen ist im anfange deß 9. Tags Iunij, circa [Perigæum] solare, mit dem Calculo Coperniceo gar nahe vbereingestimmet, also daß kaum ½. Gratis gefehlet hat, so doch den Numeris Alphonsinis nach bey 4½. Grad zu viel gewesen, welchs sonsten in andern Oppositionibus Solis & Martis, deren ich [aliquot] obseruat, nicht geschicht. Vnd hab Martem zuvor, wenn er ist pernox gewesen, circa Arietis & Libræ initia, in medio quasi loco inter Apogæum & Perigæum solare, considerirt, daß er alßdan von deß COPERNICI Calculo bey 2. oder 3. Grad abgewichen ist, vnd das in partes contrarias, prout ferebat Eccentricitatis solaris ratio. Es hat auch die Alphonsina Supputatio allda nicht bestehen können. Auß diesem ist leichtlich [ab ijs qui rem penitius introspicientes] abzumercken, daß da noch ein ander [inæqualitas] fürhanden sey, e solari Eccentricitate proueniens, die sich in den apparentem motum Planetarum insinuirt. Vnd wird in Marte, quoad tres superiores, am meisten gespürt, dieweyl er seinen Circuitum ad Solem nicht so groß hat alß die andern, daß darumb Eccentricitas Solis respectu ambitus, quem is designat, ein sensibilem proportionem hat, die doch in Ioue geringer, vnd in Saturno gar wenig gespürt wirdt. Hierauß ist zu schliessen, daß vnsere Inuention in Hypothesibus caelestibus, welche ich lib. 2. de æthereis Phaenomenis cap. 8. generaliter & lato modo indicirt hab, alleine mit den Apparentes vbereinzustimmen vermag. Vnd daß weder die alte Ptolemeische, noch die newe Coperniceische hierin nicht bestehen, denn sie können diese inæqualitatem nicht gebürlich excusiren. Jch hab auch von diesem in geheim mit Ew. F. G. Mathematico, alß er hic war, geredt, der sich denn nicht wenig darob verwundert hat, vnd bekandt, daß er zuvor darhin nicht hab gedencken können, sonst hette er sein Iudicium de meis Hypothesibus nicht also præcipitirt. Vnd ist viel anders hierneben zu mercken, welches zu weitleufftig wer allhie zu erkleren. Diß hab ich nu allein zum Beschluß, vnd vmb einige Astronomische Collation halben, Ew. F. G. anzeigen wollen. Bittendt, Ew. F. G. wolle diesem, nach jrem hohen in hac scientia Verstande, nachdencken, vnd mir jhre Meynung davon gnedigst zukommen lassen. Datum vt supra.
text.english:
**To the Most Illustrious, High-born Prince and Lord, Lord Wilhelm, Landgrave of Hesse, Count of Katzenelnbogen, Dietz, Ziegenhain and Nidda: my gracious Lord.**

Most Illustrious, High-born Prince. To Your Princely Grace my diligent and willing services are at all times ready beforehand, to the utmost of my power. Most gracious Lord, Your Princely Grace's letter to me, under the date of the 22nd of May last, issued from your city and fortress of Kassel, has only now, on the 7th of this month [*huius*], come to my hands here at Uraniborg. Where it was delayed so long — three and a half months — on the way, I cannot tell; otherwise I should not have failed to answer it more promptly.

As regards, first, the first volume of my projected work *On the more recent phenomena of the heavens* [*Operis … primum Tomum de Recentioribus coeli Phaenomenis*], in the 2nd chapter of which the restoration of the fixed stars [*Stellarum fixarum Restitutio*] is treated from the foundations, which Your Princely Grace mentions in your letter — concerning this I cannot, in duty, conceal from Your Princely Grace that the same work is not yet fully completed through the press; for this summer, on account of other necessary business pressing upon me, I have not had leisure to attend to it. But when God grants grace and opportunity for it to be finished this winter, then I will, according to Your Princely Grace's desire, communicate it [to you].

That Your Princely Grace's mathematician, Rothmann [*ROTHMANNVS*], had not yet returned to Your Princely Grace — this causes me no little astonishment; for he gave me to understand nothing other than that he meant to betake himself back to Kassel forthwith — which is now just a year gone by. If the illness [*Morbus*] (of which Your Princely Grace makes mention) were the cause that he stays away so long, then he could surely in the meantime have had himself cured. He let no want of that sort be perceived here at all; otherwise there would perhaps be as good a Paracelsian remedy [*Paracelsisch Remedium*] to be found here against it as anywhere else — which is also without doubt well known to him. But I think that, if he has not yet returned to Your Princely Grace, he will present himself again at the first [opportunity]. It would be well that he complete the work on the fixed stars [*Opus Stellarum Fixarum*] at the first opportunity, so that the long tedium and the great pains and diligence expended should not be left behind [unfinished], but might come to the benefit of others, and of posterity [*Posteritati*].

As far as concerns the reindeer [*Riensthier*] of which Your Princely Grace writes: I have indeed found its picture [*Iconem*] and description [*Descriptionem*] in the German Gesner [*Gesnero*] too — which book is also at hand for me — who calls it a "horse-stag" [*Roßhirsch*]; but hitherto I have not been able to learn that such a one is to be had here. I have myself been several times in the deer-park [Thiergarten] of His Royal Majesty, of most laudable memory; but I have never heard of any such there. Nor likewise at Copenhagen. But if I can yet get any knowledge of one, I will furnish Your Princely Grace with a report of it.

Of the reindeer-bucks, or [reindeer] beasts [*Rhenböcke oder Thier*], there have indeed gone one or two here on the Holm at Copenhagen, as I noted in my previous letter; but here they cannot live through the summer and bear the heat — far less in the land of Hesse, or other places that lie more toward the south — for they have their place in the wholly northern part of Norway and Sweden [*Septentrionali parte Noruegiae vnd Sueciae*], and cannot well survive in other places. But the elk [*Elendsthier*], although they too have their origin out of Norway and Sweden, can nonetheless endure here in Denmark for several years, if they are well kept. I expect, therefore, that one will be able to rear and keep them in Germany too, for here it is at times in summer indeed as hot as there. The last time, when I wrote to Your Princely Grace, I had one over here across the way in Skåne [Schonen], on my estates; and when I meant to have it fetched over here to this island, it came to the town named Landskrona, which lies here across the way, and there it was kept some days at the castle, for the air's sake, with a nobleman who has my sister's daughter [to wife]; whereupon — as they sat at table — it once went up the staircase, and in the chamber drank itself so full of strong beer that, on going down again, it fell down the stair and broke its one leg, which with no diligence could be got to heal again. And so it died of it. But as soon as I can get another, or a pair, that are tame, I will willingly and with all diligence send them to Your Princely Grace.

Further, since Your Princely Grace in your letter makes mention of the papermaker — that Your Princely Grace would have inquiry made after one or two at Frankfurt — I cannot hide from Your Princely Grace that I have myself already obtained one, well enough experienced in the craft, who is now at work with a journeyman to make printing-paper [*Druckpapier*]. I render, nonetheless, my most dutiful and highest thanks to Your Princely Grace that you were of gracious will, and did not think it a burden, to take such trouble upon yourself for my sake. Wherein I can in turn be of service and pleasure to Your Princely Grace, according to my slight and utmost power, thereto I offer myself wholly willingly; and Your Princely Grace shall in any case have me at your command.

Herewith I would commend Your Princely Grace, in the protection of the Most High, to long-lasting, happy health and government of your land, in dutiful diligence.
Given at Uraniborg, the 8th of September, in the year 1591.
Your Princely Grace's
dutiful and willing servant,
TYCHO BRAHE.


*[Postscript:]* Postscript. But that this my letter may treat not only of the earthly animals but also somewhat of the celestial [bodies] (which is Our delight), I would not refrain from signifying to Your Princely Grace that the star Mars — which more than the other planets otherwise eludes the astronomical computation — in its last acronychal position, which occurred at the beginning of the 9th day of June, near the solar [perigee], agreed very nearly with the Copernican computation, so that it fell short by scarcely ½ a degree, whereas by the Alphonsine Numbers it was in excess by about 4½ degrees; which otherwise does not happen in other oppositions of the Sun and Mars, of which I have observed several. And I had earlier, when Mars was all-night visible, near the beginnings of Aries and Libra, in a place as it were midway between the solar apogee and perigee, considered that it then departed from Copernicus's computation by about 2 or 3 degrees, and that in contrary directions, as the reckoning of the solar eccentricity bore. There too the Alphonsine reckoning could not hold. From this it is easily to be noted, by those who look into the matter deeply, that there is yet another inequality present, arising from the solar eccentricity, which insinuates itself into the apparent motion of the planets. And it is most sensed in Mars, as regards the three superior [planets], inasmuch as its circuit about the Sun is not so great as the others', so that for that reason the eccentricity of the Sun, in respect of the circuit which it describes, bears a sensible proportion — which, however, is smaller in Jupiter, and very little sensed in Saturn. From this it is to be concluded that our discovery in the celestial hypotheses, which I have indicated generally and in a broad manner in Book 2 of the De aethereis Phaenomenis, chapter 8, is alone able to agree with the Appearances; and that neither the old Ptolemaic nor the new Copernican [hypotheses] hold here, for they cannot duly excuse this inequality. I have also spoken of this in confidence with Your Princely Grace's mathematician, when he was here, who thereupon marvelled not a little, and confessed that he had not been able to think of it before, else he would not have so precipitated his judgement of my hypotheses. And there is much else to be noted alongside this, which would be too lengthy to explain here. This I have wished to indicate to Your Princely Grace only by way of conclusion, and for the sake of some astronomical collation; begging that Your Princely Grace will, according to your high understanding in this science, reflect upon it, and graciously let me have your opinion thereof. Given as above.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender / recipient.** Tycho Brahe, writing from **Uraniborg** on Hven, to **Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel** (1532–1592), the astronomer-prince whose Kassel observatory and correspondence (largely conducted through his mathematician Rothmann) were Tycho's chief scholarly counterpart in the 1580s. The full chancery titulature (*Graf zu Katzenelnbogen, Dietz, Ziegenhain und Nidda*) is preserved by this chapter's convention
- **Edition of record.** Printed by Tycho himself in the *Epistolarum astronomicarum libri* (Liber I, Uraniborg 1596), the volume from which the edition's edition field is taken; the text is also in Dreyer, *Opera Omnia* VI. No MS witness is recorded in the source header.
- **Language.** Verified by reading as **Frühneuhochdeutsch chancery German**, not Danish; the heuristic tag *de* is correct. The register is the formal *Ew. F. G.* (*Eu[e]r Fürstlich[e] Gnaden* = "Your Princely Grace") address maintained throughout, with constant code-switching into Latin for technical and bibliographic nouns. Latin embeddings retained and italicised on first use: *Operis primum Tomum de Recentioribus coeli Phaenomenis*, *Capite 2.*, *Stellarum fixarum Restitutio*, *fundamentaliter tractirt*, *Mathematicus*, *Morbus*, *in causa*, *curiren*, *Paracelsisch Remedium*, *Opus Stellarum Fixarum*, *Posteritati*, *Iconem*, *Descriptionem*, *mention*, *Septentrionali parte Noruegiae … Sueciae*.
- **The work in progress.** *primum Tomum de Recentioribus coeli Phaenomenis … Capite 2. Stellarum fixarum Restitutio* = the first volume of the *Astronomiae instauratae progymnasmata* (the "Introduction to the renewed astronomy"), whose long-delayed printing occupied Tycho's Uraniborg press; *Stellarum fixarum Restitutio* = "the restoration of the fixed stars" (the fixed-star catalogue), rendered "restoration" per the editorial glossary (, *restitutio/instauratio*).
- **Rothmann.** *ROTHMANNVS* = **Christoph Rothmann**, the Landgrave's mathematician, who had visited Tycho on Hven in 1590 and — as this letter records — never returned to Kassel. The *Morbus* ("illness") is the reason the Landgrave had offered; Tycho is sceptical, noting Rothmann showed no sign of it on Hven and could have sought a *Paracelsisch Remedium* ("Paracelsian remedy") there. *Paracelsisch Remedium* kept as a period term (cf. *remedium magneticum* — not modernised).
- **Zoological matter.** The bulk of the letter answers the Landgrave's request for northern animals. *Riensthier* = **reindeer** (*Rangifer*); Tycho cross-refers to the **German Gesner** (*Gesnero* = the German-language edition of Conrad Gesner's *Historia animalium* / *Thierbuch*), where the beast is figured under the name *Roßhirsch* ("horse-stag"). *Rhenböcke oder Thier* = "reindeer-bucks, or [reindeer-]beasts"; *auffm Holm zu Koppenhagen* = on the **Holmen** (the naval-yard island) at Copenhagen. *Königliche Maiestat, Hochlöblicher gedechtnuß* = the late **King Frederik II** (d. 1588), "of most laudable memory." *Elendsthier* = **elk / moose** (*Alces*; German *Elen[d]tier*) — the comic centrepiece anecdote. *Septentrionali parte Noruegiae und Sueciae* = "the northern part of Norway and Sweden."
- **The elk anecdote.** *Schonen* = **Skåne** (then Danish), where Tycho held estates across the Øresund; *Landskronen* = **Landskrona**, the town opposite Hven. The nobleman "who has my sister's daughter [to wife]" is not named in the text; left unidentified rather than guessed. The elk drinks itself drunk on strong beer at table, falls down the castle stair, breaks a leg, and dies — reported deadpan. No interpretive softening applied.
- **Papermaker.** *Papiermacher … Druckpapier* — the Landgrave had offered to find a papermaker at Frankfurt for Tycho's press; Tycho reports he has already engaged one, working with a *Geselle* (journeyman) to make printing-paper for Uraniborg.
- **Calendar.** The dateline *den 8. Septemb. Anno 1591* matches the catalogue label exactly (no discrepancy). Denmark and Hesse-Kassel both kept the **Julian calendar**, so the date is **O.S.** *den 7. huius* = "the 7th of this [month]," i.e. 7 September 1591 (O.S.), the day before writing. The incoming letter's date *den 22. Maij* (22 May) is likewise O.S.; Tycho's "three and a half months" in transit is his own reckoning of the 22 May → 7 September interval and is reproduced, not recomputed.
- **Formulae.** Opening *Ewer F. G. sind meine fleißwillige Dienste … zuvoran bereit* and the closing *in Schirm deß Allerhöchsten … befolen haben / … Dienstwilliger* are the standard subordinate-to-prince courtesy frame (servant writing to lord, the inverse of the Landgrave's princely *Wir/euch* register); translated, not dropped.

- **§1 Dreyer collation.** German closing postscript "POSTSCRIPTA … de Caelestibus", restored from Dreyer VI, pp. 236–237 (dropped by the working transcription); the Mars opposition (early 9 June, near solar perigee), the Copernican-vs-Alphonsine error, and the self-citation "lib. 2 de aethereis Phaenomenis cap. 8" confirmed against the facing Latin (VI, p. 239); bracketed words supply garbled tokens per the Latin.

translation.warrant: **Not collated against Dreyer** — no page reference for this letter, so the grade is capped at Probable however sound the translation looks. the edition gives no page reference for this letter, so by the audit's rule this is audited against the transcribed original alone and capped at grade Probable; no Dreyer collation performed. Checked the full German the transcribed original against the published English sentence by sentence: the salutation and address block, the 3.5-month delivery-delay detail, the Operis primum Tomum de Recentioribus coeli Phaenomenis / chapter 2 passage, the Rothmann-illness-and-Paracelsian-remedy paragraph, the reindeer (Riensthier/Roßhirsch, Gesner citation) paragraph, the elk (Elendsthier) and the Landskrona anecdote (nobleman married to the writer's sister's daughter, the animal's death from drinking beer and falling down stairs), the papermaker paragraph, the closing and date '8 September 1591', and the restored Latin/German postscript on the Mars-acronychal-position observation (9 June, agreement with Copernicus to within 1/2 degree vs. Alphonsine excess of about 4.5 degrees; the Aries/Libra 2-3 degree divergence; Book 2 De aethereis Phaenomenis cap.8). Every proper name, number, date, and clause has a counterpart in the source; no fabrication, omission, mistranslation, or hedge-loss found.

documents.incipit: DURCHLEUCHTIGSTER/ Hochgeborner Fürst. Gnedigster Herr/ Ewer F. G. kan ich dienstlich …

text.original:
DEM DURCHLEUCHTIGSTEN/ HOCHGEBORNEN FÜRSTEN VND HERRN/ HERRN WILHELM, LANDTGRAUEN ZU HESSEN/ GRAUEN ZU CATZENELNBOGEN/ DIETZ/ ZIEGENHAIN VND NIDDA: MEINEM GNEDIGEN HERRN.

DURCHLEUCHTIGSTER/ Hochgeborner Fürst. Gnedigster Herr/ Ewer F. G. kan ich dienstlich vnangezeigt nicht lassen/ wie daß ich derselben Schreiben von jrem Denischen Jungen/ dem Bilden meinem Vettern den 23. Septembris wol empfangen hab. In welchem Ew. F. G. abermals von dem Elendsthier (wovon ich ein mal in meinem Schreiben Zusage gethan) meldung thut. Was aber dasselbig Thier (da ichs noch im vorradt hette/ vnd willens war/ Ew. F. G. vberzuschicken) am Beinbruche fürn zusall bekommen hab/ vnd darüber gestorben sey/ solchs ist in meinem vorigen Schreiben gnugsam angezogen/ Welch Schreiben ich dem Edlen vnd Vesten Henrich Rammel/ meinem besondern gutem Freunde/ so baldt er mir Ew. F. G. Brieff (deß Datum vnderm 22. Maij stehet) hat zugeschickt/ widerumb vberliefern lassen. Darauff er mich folgendts allhie besucht/ vnd also solchen Brieff mit einem eigen Botten an Ew. F. G. abzufertigen verheissen. Er hat auch allhie das mal vnder andern mit mir von dero Theologorum (die Anno 1529. zu Marpurg zusammen gewesen) Vergleichung geredt/ vnd darneben ein Deutsches Scriptum (welchs Ew. F. G. jme vberschickt) gezeigt/ worin dieselbige Concordantien Articulweiß verfast/ vnd mit Ew. F. G. Handtschrifft allenthalben zu weiterer Versicherung vndergezeichnet seyndt. Vnd wiewol ich damals dieselbige mit den jenigen/ die in Historia Augustanæ Confessionis, Francofordiæ ad Mænum, per Matthiam Ritterum Ecclesiasten Anno 1578. editâ, et a Chytræo prius contextâ, fol. 643. et seq. commemorirt werden/ ob alles da bona fide, wie es sich gebürt/ Latine referirt vnd reddirt wirdt/ zu conferiren willens gewesen bin/ So ists doch (dieweyl gedachter Ramelius von hinnen nach Pommern notwendiger Gescheffte halben eylete/ vnd auch vmb anderer fürfelle willen) nachblieben. Es kan aber Ew. F. G. leichtlich mit dem jetztgedachten Lateinischen Exemplari ein Collation hierin instituiren lassen/ ob alles gebürlich vnd rechtmessig transferirt worden. Welchs ich auch gern thun wolte/ wan Ew. F. G. mir auch ein Abschrifft davon gnediglich communiciren, oder aber daß mir ermeldter Ramelius ein Copey von dem seinigen mitteile/ gestatten wolte. Dan ich vermercke wol auß der widerparteyischen Theologen zu vnsern zeiten außgangenen Scriptis, daß sie nicht allenthalben candide et conuenienter Aruersariorum sententias citiren vnd außlegen/ sondern daß ein grosse Philautia, ambitio, odium, vnd vincendi vindictæque cupiditas bey jnen mehrern teils vberhandt genommen/ Ita vt sub prætextu promotionis veritatis Euangelicæ, seipsos et sua vt plurimum quærant. Aber man mag sie in jrer Würde bleiben/ vnd jre Sachen selber verantworten lassen.

Anlangendt aber mein vorbemeldts Schreiben (in welchem ich alle gelegenheit vom Elendsthier vermeldet hab) schicke ich Ew. F. G. nu dasselb zu. Dan da obgedachter Ramelius auff dem Wege/ alß er von hinnen nach Deutschlandt reysete/ erfaren/ daß Ew. F. G. Junge allhie verhanden war/ hat er mir den Brieff wider zurück geschickt/ vnd darneben einen andern/ den er selbst an Ew. F. G. dirigirt, auff daß ich Ew. F. G. Jungen dieselbe/ vmb andere Vnkosten zu vermeyden/ mitgeben kündte/ welchs ich auch gethan hab/ dieweyl der Junge widerumb zu Ew. F. G. baldt zurück zeucht. Jch hab auch vnder der zeit/ die er hie im Lande verharret/ allenthalben bey meiner Freundtschafft nachforschen lassen/ ob jrgendts ein Elendsthier/ das zahm sey/ verhanden were/ aber niergendts ein solchs erfragen können/ sonst hette ich jetzunder Ew. F. G. eines mit demselbigen Jungen (der mir gnugsam zu verstehen gab/ was Ew. F. G. fur grosse Lust zu einem solchen Thier habe) vbergeschickt. Auff das aber Ew. F. G. gleichwol hierin mit dem ersten möchte gewilfart werden/ hab ich hinauff in Norwegen an Königlicher Maiestat allda Stadthalter/ den Edlen vnd Wolgebornen Axel Güldenstern/ welcher mein gar nahe Verwandter vnd sehr guter Freundt ist/ fleissig geschrieben vnd angelangt/ daß er mir auffs wenigst ein par derselbigen Thier/ die da jung weren/ mit erster gelegenheit herab schicken wolte/ dan dero in seinem Lehen vnd Gebiete etliche verhanden seyndt. Hab auch gleichfalls einem andern Edelman in Norwegen/ der mir nahe beschwägert ist/ geschrieben/ daß er mir auch ein par auß seinem Lehen (da man auch der Gattung nicht wenig findet) mit dem ersten wolte zustehen lassen. Bin darumb guter hoffnung/ ich werde auffs wenigste von dieser einem/ wo nicht von allen beyden/ dero Thieren etliche bekommen. Welchs/ so es nicht vorm Winter geschehen kan/ hoffe ich doch auffs Vorjar Ew. F. G. hierin nach jrem willen dienstlich zu seyn.

Was antrifft das ander Thier/ welchs Orix genandt wirdt/ hab ich das auch in meinem Deutschen Gesnero nachgesucht/ vnd ein kurtze Beschreibung davon am 68. Blat gefunden/ doch keine Verzeichnuß darbey/ So meldets auch nicht/ wie hoch vnd groß es seyn soll. Worauß ich vermercke/ daß Ew. F. G. Deutscher Gesnerus ein ander Buch vnd Exemplar sey/ dan welchs mir bey der Handt ist. Es muß ein gewaltig groß Thier seyn/ vnd wol bey zweyer Mans höhe erreichen/ wan es 23. Spann hoch ist. Von diesem weiß man in vnsern Landen/ vnd den jenigen/ die noch mehr gegen Norden gelegen seyndt/ bißhero gar nichts zu sagen/ dan es wirdt allda kaum gefunden. Ich bin wol newlich in erfarung kommen/ daß vorbemeldter Axel Güldenstern vor kurtzer zeit/ ein seltzames vnd zuvor nicht viel bekandtes Thier in Norwegen/ von den jenigen Leuten/ die vber die hohe vnd mit Schnee bedeckten Klippen auff besondern langen vnd breiten Höltzern vnder den Füssen fast gemacht/ gar schnell lauffen/ also/ daß sie ein Hirsch ereylen können/ soll auffgespürt haben. Aber was es für ein Thier sey/ vnd wie groß/ hab ich noch nicht gnugsam erfaren können. So baldt ich einige Wiffenschafft davon kriege/ wil ich Ew. F. G. solchs anzeigen.

Von den Obseruationibus Stellarum Fixarum, davon Ew. F. G. allhie auch meldung thut/ hab ich in meinem vorigen Schreiben anzeigung gethan/ daß dasselbig Buch/ darin sie begriffen werden/ noch nicht vollendts in Druck verfertigt sey. So baldt aber das geschicht/ soli Ew. F. G. dasselb zuzuschichen nicht vnderlassen werden.

Daß Ew. F. G. Mathematicus ROTHMANNVS, noch bißhero sich nicht hat eingestelt/ thut mich je lenger je mehr verwundern/ vnd es muß seltzame Vrsache haben/ daß er so lange außbleibt. Ewer F. G. wirdt wol Mittel finden/ daß sie jn widerumb zu sich alliciren könne/ wan sie schon einige Liberalitet, mehr alß sonst/ auff jn wagen solle/ auff daß er das vorgenommene Opus Fixarum Stellarum desto williger vnd bälder verfertige. Es mangelt jme am Ingenio vnd Wiffenschafft darzu nicht/ Aber mir hat wol an jme gedaucht/ daß er (wie Ew. F. G. auch zuvor von jm geschrieben hat) einen eigenwillischen Kopff haben solte/ worauff jme nur gelüstete seinen eigen Hut auffzusetzen. Wie man dan offt findet/ daß excellentia Ingenia auch jre sonderliche Gebrechen vnd Næuos haben/ die man dan/ so sie nicht anders zu corrigiren seyndt/ gedulten mag. Jch versehe mich zu jme/ er werde sich noch besinnen/ vnd sich zu Ew. F. G. wider einstellen/ vnd im fürhabenden Wercke keinen fleiß vnd mühe sparen/ damit es mit dem ersten an Tag möchte kommen.

Von den Papiermachern hab ich Ew. F. G. auch im vorigen Schreiben zuverstehen geben/ daß ich deren jetzunder keinen bedürffe/ dieweil ich selbs schon lengst Leute bekommen hab/ die mir die Arbeit verrichten. Thu mich gleichwol für den erbottenen gnedigen willen/ gegen Ew. F. G. dienstlich vnd zum höchsten bedancken: Gleichsfalls auch für die mitgeteilte newe Zeitung/ die mir gar angenem gewesen seyndt.

Was diese Länder antrifft/ weiß ich Ew. F. G. nichts newes widerumb zuzuschreiben/ dan daß Status Daniæ vnd Noruegiæ, noch (Gott Lob) gar friedig vnd richtig sey. Der Allmechtige Gott wölle weiter Gnade verleihen. Weiß E. F. G. dißmal weiters nicht zuzuschreiben/ Wo aber etwas fürfellt/ solches soll Ew. F. G. mit erster gelegenheit referirt werden.

Vnd wil Ew. F. G. in Gottes Allmechtigen gnadenreichen Schirm/ zu langwiriger Gesundtheit vnd friedlicher Landsregierung/ hiemit befohlen haben.
Datum Vraniburg, den 26. Septembris, Anno 1591.
Ewer F. G.
Dienstwilliger
TYCHO BRAHE.


*[Postscript — restored from Dreyer, Opera Omnia VI, p. 246; dropped by the working transcription. See Apparatus.]*
POSTSCRIPTA. NACH dem ich vermercke auß Ew. F. G. Brieff, daß der [ROTHMANNVS] noch nicht in so lange zeit angekommen ist, gedencke ich wol, daß er auch die Descriptionem meorum Instrumentorum, welche er hic verzeichnet hat, kaum wirdt Ew. F. G. zugeschickt haben. Darumb hab ich nicht wollen vnderlassen, meinem Deutschen Amanuensi zu befehlen, daß er von new ein [Verzeichnuß] davon, so viel jm in der eyl müglich were, zusammen schriebe, welche Ew. F. G. hierbey mit vorgemeldten Knaben bekommen wird. Wan ich selbst ein mal besser weyl habe, bin ich willens alle meine Instrumenta Astronomica deutlicher vnd fleissiger, beyde mit jrer Fabricâ vnd [vsu] zu beschreiben. Ew. F. G. wolle diese geringe Consignation in gnedigen Willen annemen. Datum vt supra.
text.english:
**To the Most Serene, High-Born Prince and Lord, Lord Wilhelm, Landgrave of Hesse, Count of Katzenelnbogen, Dietz, Ziegenhain, and Nidda: my gracious Lord.**

Most Serene, High-Born Prince, most gracious Lord. I cannot dutifully leave Your Princely Grace unadvised that I duly received Your Grace's letter from your Danish page, Bille my kinsman, on 23 September. In it Your Princely Grace once more makes mention of the elk [*Elendsthier*] (of which I once made a promise in my letter). But that this animal — when I still had it in store and was minded to send it over to Your Princely Grace — suffered, by mishap, a broken leg and thereupon died, this was sufficiently set out in my previous letter; which letter I had delivered back to the Noble and Steadfast Henrik Ramel, my especially good friend, as soon as he had sent on to me Your Princely Grace's letter (which bears the date 22 May). Whereupon he afterwards visited me here, and so promised to dispatch that letter to Your Princely Grace by a courier of his own. He also, on that occasion, spoke with me, among other matters, about the reconciliation of those theologians (who came together at Marburg in the year 1529), and showed me besides a German document (which Your Princely Grace had sent over to him) in which those concords are set down article by article, and subscribed throughout, for further assurance, with Your Princely Grace's own hand. And although I was at that time minded to compare these with those [accords] that are recorded in the *History of the Augsburg Confession* — published at Frankfurt-on-Main by Matthias Ritter, churchman, in the year 1578, and previously composed by Chytraeus, fol. 643 and following — [to see] whether everything there is reported and rendered into Latin in good faith [*bona fide*], as is fitting, yet it was left undone (since the said Ramel was hastening hence to Pomerania on necessary business, and also on account of other occurrences). But Your Princely Grace can easily have a collation undertaken in this matter with the Latin copy just mentioned, [to see] whether everything has been translated fittingly and rightly. Which I too would gladly do, if Your Princely Grace would graciously communicate to me a transcript thereof, or else permit the said Ramel to share with me a copy of his own. For I do well perceive, from the writings put forth by the theologians of the opposing party in our times, that they do not everywhere cite and expound their adversaries' opinions candidly and fittingly [*candide et convenienter Adversariorum sententias*], but rather that a great self-love, ambition, hatred, and lust to conquer and to take revenge [*Philautia, ambitio, odium, vincendi vindictaeque cupiditas*] has for the most part got the upper hand among them — so that, under the pretext of promoting the truth of the Gospel, they for the most part seek themselves and their own [*Ita ut sub praetextu promotionis veritatis Evangelicae, seipsos et sua ut plurimum quaerant*]. But one may let them remain in their dignity and answer for their affairs themselves.

As concerns my aforesaid letter (in which I reported every circumstance about the elk), I now send the same to Your Princely Grace. For when the above-mentioned Ramel, on his way as he was travelling hence to Germany, learned that Your Princely Grace's page was present here, he sent the letter back to me, and besides it another which he himself had addressed to Your Princely Grace, so that I might give them to Your Princely Grace's page — to avoid other expenses — which I have indeed done, since the page is shortly returning again to Your Princely Grace. During the time he tarried here in the land, I also had inquiry made everywhere among my kinsfolk whether a tame elk were anywhere to be had, but nowhere could such a one be obtained; otherwise I would now have sent Your Princely Grace one by that same page (who gave me sufficiently to understand what great desire Your Princely Grace has for such an animal). But so that Your Princely Grace might nonetheless be obliged in this at the first [opportunity], I have diligently written to and applied to His Royal Majesty's governor up in Norway, the Noble and Well-Born Axel Gyldenstierne, who is my very near kinsman and very good friend, that he would send down to me at the first opportunity at least a pair of those animals that are young, since there are several to be had in his fief and territory. I have likewise written to another nobleman in Norway, who is closely related to me by marriage, that he too would let me have a pair from his fief (where also one finds not a few of the kind) at the first [opportunity]. I am therefore in good hope that I shall obtain some of those animals, at the least from one of these, if not from both. And should this not be able to happen before winter, I yet hope to be at Your Princely Grace's service in this, according to your wish, by next spring.

As concerns the other animal, which is called the oryx [*Orix*], I have looked it up too in my German Gessner, and found a short description of it on leaf 68, but no illustration alongside it; nor does it state how tall and large it is supposed to be. From which I perceive that Your Princely Grace's German Gessner is another book and copy than the one I have to hand. It must be a mighty large animal, and may well reach two men's height, if it is 23 spans tall. Of this [animal] one knows hitherto nothing at all to say in our lands, nor in those that lie still further to the north, for it is scarcely found there. I have indeed recently come to learn that the above-mentioned Axel Gyldenstierne is said, a short time ago, to have tracked down a strange and previously not much known animal in Norway, [reported] by those people who, over the high and snow-covered crags, run very swiftly upon particular long and broad boards almost fastened under their feet, so that they can overtake a stag. But what kind of animal it is, and how large, I have not yet been able to learn sufficiently. As soon as I get any knowledge of it, I will signify it to Your Princely Grace.

Concerning the *Observations of the Fixed Stars* [*Observationibus Stellarum Fixarum*], of which Your Princely Grace here also makes mention, I gave notice in my previous letter that the book in which they are contained is not yet entirely finished in print. But as soon as that is done, sending the same to Your Princely Grace shall not be neglected.

That Your Princely Grace's mathematician Rothmann has still not so far presented himself astonishes me more and more the longer [it goes on], and there must be some strange cause that he stays away so long. Your Princely Grace will surely find means by which you may entice him back to you again — even should you have to venture some liberality upon him, more than usual — so that he may complete the more willingly and the sooner the undertaken *Work on the Fixed Stars* [*Opus Fixarum Stellarum*]. He does not lack the talent and learning for it [*Ingenio und Wissenschaft*]; but it had indeed seemed to me of him that he (as Your Princely Grace too has previously written of him) was likely to have a self-willed head, set on nothing but putting on his own hat. As one often finds that excellent talents [*excellentia Ingenia*] also have their particular failings and blemishes [*Naevos*], which one may then bear with, if they are not otherwise to be corrected. I trust of him that he will yet bethink himself, and present himself to Your Princely Grace again, and spare no diligence and pains in the work in hand, so that it might come to light at the first.

Concerning the paper-makers, I have likewise given Your Princely Grace to understand in my previous letter that I have need of none of them at present, since I have long since myself obtained people who do the work for me. Nonetheless I dutifully and most highly thank Your Princely Grace for the gracious goodwill offered: likewise also for the new tidings imparted, which were very agreeable to me.

As concerns these lands, I know of nothing new to write back to Your Princely Grace, save that the state of Denmark and of Norway [*Status Daniae und Norvegiae*] is still (praise God) quite peaceful and in good order. May Almighty God grant further grace. I know nothing further to write to Your Princely Grace at this time; but should anything occur, it shall be reported to Your Princely Grace at the first opportunity.

And I herewith commend Your Princely Grace to the gracious protection of God Almighty, to long-lasting health and peaceful governance of your lands.
Given at Uraniborg, the 26th of September, in the year 1591.
Your Princely Grace's
obedient servant,
TYCHO BRAHE.


*[Postscript:]* Postscript. Since I perceive from Your Princely Grace's letter that Rothmann has still, in so long a time, not arrived, I rather think that he, too, will scarcely have sent to Your Princely Grace the description of my instruments which he drew up here. Therefore I would not refrain from charging my German amanuensis to draw up afresh a register thereof, so far as was possible to him in the haste — which Your Princely Grace will receive herewith by the aforesaid boy. When I myself once have better leisure, it is my intention to describe all my astronomical instruments more clearly and carefully, both as to their make and use. May Your Princely Grace receive this slight consignation [inventory-description] with gracious goodwill. Given as above.

departures_from_tekstnet.basis: The text printed here descends from one harvest of tekstnet's page and was read against Dreyer's page images in July 2026; a second harvest of the same page is kept beside it. Where the two disagree in a word, both readings are listed: Dreyer's page decides, and unless the audit paragraph names the word, that check has not yet been made for it.
