documents.abstract: Thanks Craig for his letters, explains a missed meeting with Junius at Helsingør, and briefly addresses the dispute over comets.
documents.incipit: S.GRATISSIMAe mihi fuere literae tuae, vir eruditissime, quas accepi nuper refertissimas …

text.original:
ERUDITISSIMO ET HUMANISSIMO
VIRO D. THOMAe CRAGIO I. V. D. AMICO
SUO PLURIMUM DILECTO. EDENBURGI.

S.GRATISSIMAe mihi fuere literae tuae, vir eruditissime, quas accepi nuper refertissimas singularis in me benevolentiae et amoris notis. Quocirca etiam fusius respondere illis decreveram, modo Magnificus D. P. IUNIUS, uti proposuerat, in insula hac me invisisset. Sed spirante mox Austro, Helsingorae eum paratum iam navem ascendere cursim tantum salutare licuit, ita ut hac ratione omnis mihi rescribendi oportunitas tum sublata fuerit, et ne nunc quidem ob varias occupationes aliaque impedimenta otium ullum relictum sit, ut, quantum velim, literis complectar. Nihilominus breviusculas hasce ad te dare censui, ne ad humanissimam tuam Epistolam plane obmutescere viderer. Quod vero ad negotium de Cometis attinet, mihi perinde est, sive quis in coelo eos credat, sive in aëre versari. Sufficiet quod ex quinque huiusmodi crinitis sideribus, quae annis aliquot proxime elapsis, arduo et indefesso labore observavi, nullum infra Lunam fuisse, quin et eorum quaedam ne tantillam paralaxin, qualem Sol efficit, admisisse, ideoque ipso longe altiora et a terris remotiora extitisse invictis rationibus demonstrârim. Unde apertissime liquet omnes Aristotelicos, qui tot iam seculis contrariam tutati sunt sententiam, hac in parte plurimum aberrasse et Cometas sublunares efficiendo toto (prout dici solet) coelo deviasse. Fratri autem tuo non invideo hunc ob autoritatem ARISTOTELIS errorem, quem cum multis alijs communem habet, miseret potius quod cum Mathematicus sit, caeteris oculatior non existat. Ad literas eius respondissem quidem, si ea quae prae se ferunt, sincere et sine arroganti praeiudicio dicta esse comperissem. Verum existimo eas Capnurania ista scoptica non multo mansuetiores, adeo ut inter alia hospitalitatem etiam meam (ne quid dicam amplius) in dubium vocare non vereatur, dum sic scribit: Cupivit doctiss. vir D. legatus ut secum te inviserem, non patiuntur id amici. Si venissem, gratusne fuissem hospes? Caetera per temetipsum et pro tuâ prudentiâ atque humanitate satis intelligis. De meâ vero benevolentia erga te, cuius singularem candorem et virtutem pari doctrinâ coniuntam, cum ex praestantissimi D. PETRI IUNIJ relatione, utut inter nos breviculâ, tum ex proprijs tuis literis atque carminibus perspectam habeo, non est quod addubites, imo si quid tibi quod gratum sit per me praestari queat, invenies me quam paratissimum. Cum autem eleganti poëticâ venâ te praeditum esse ex versibus eiusmodi gratia conscriptis non obscure perspexerim, Epistolam hanc Elegiacam ad imitationem Ovidianarum nupere animi causa sororis nomine a me lusam adiungere volui, ut videas me non semper sublimia et coelestia, sed etiam terricolis, ut plurimum, usitata nonnunquam (obiter tamen) tractare.

Vale.
Datae Uraniburgi 26. Iulij Anno 1594.
text.english:
**To the most learned and most courteous Master Thomas Craig, Doctor of Both Laws, his most dearly beloved friend. At Edinburgh.**

Greeting. Most welcome to me were your letters, most learned Sir, which I received lately, crammed full with marks of your singular goodwill and affection toward me. For this reason I had even resolved to answer them at greater length, provided that the Worshipful Master P. Junius had, as he had proposed, visited me on this island. But, the south wind soon springing up, I was permitted only to greet him hurriedly at Helsingør as he was already standing ready to board ship — so that in this way every opportunity of writing back was then taken from me; nor even now, on account of various occupations and other hindrances, is any leisure left me to embrace [the matter] in a letter as fully as I should wish. Nevertheless I judged it right to send you these rather brief lines, lest I should seem to fall altogether silent in the face of your most courteous letter. But as for the business concerning the comets, it is all one to me whether one believes them to dwell in the heaven or in the air. It will suffice that, out of five such hairy stars [comets] which over some years now last past I have observed with arduous and unwearied labour, I have demonstrated by unanswerable reasonings that not one was below the Moon — indeed that certain of them admitted not even so much as that tiny parallax which the Sun produces, and were therefore far higher than [the Sun] itself and more remote from the earth. From which it is most plainly evident that all the Aristotelians, who for so many centuries now have maintained the contrary opinion, have in this matter erred most greatly, and, by making comets sublunary, have gone astray (as the saying goes) by the whole heaven. As for your brother, I do not begrudge him this error on the authority of Aristotle, which he holds in common with many others; rather I pity that, being a mathematician, he is no more clear-sighted than the rest. I would indeed have answered his letters, had I found that what they profess was said sincerely and without arrogant prejudice. But I judge them not much milder than that scoffing *Capnurania* of his — so much so that, among other things, he does not even shrink from calling my very hospitality (to say nothing further) into question, when he writes thus: "The most learned Worshipful Master ambassador wished that I should visit you in his company; my friends do not allow it. Had I come, should I have been a welcome guest?" The rest you understand well enough for yourself, and by your own prudence and courtesy. But as to my goodwill toward you — whose singular candour and virtue, joined with equal learning, I have come to know thoroughly, both from the report of the most excellent Master Peter Junius, brief though it was between us, and from your own letters and poems — there is no reason for you to be in any doubt; nay rather, if anything that may be agreeable to you can be furnished through me, you will find me most ready. And since I have perceived not obscurely, from verses composed for the sake of such [a favour], that you are endowed with an elegant poetic vein, I wished to append this Elegiac Epistle, lately composed by me in play, for my heart's relief, in my sister's name, in imitation of Ovid's [*Heroides*], that you may see that I do not always treat of lofty and celestial matters, but sometimes also (in passing, however) of things familiar to the dwellers on earth, as is mostly the case.

Farewell.
Given at Uraniborg, 26 July, in the year 1594.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe**, writing from **Uraniborg** on the island of Hven (Latin *Uraniburgum*; this chapter's convention).
- **Recipient.** *D. Thomae Cragio I. V. D.* = **Master Thomas Craig**, **Doctor of Both Laws** (*Iuris Utriusque Doctor* — of canon and civil law); the eminent Scottish jurist and Latin poet Thomas Craig of Riccarton (c. 1538–1608), at Edinburgh. The salutation singles out his learning and humanity; the body praises his "letters and poems" and his "elegant poetic vein," consistent with Craig the neo-Latin poet rather than with his comet-disputing brother.
- ***Fratri autem tuo*** — "As for your brother": the comet antagonist is **John Craig** (the physician and Aristotelian, d. 1620), Thomas's brother, with whom Tycho had carried on a bitter epistolary dispute over the placement of comets (c. 1589–94). Tycho here replies courteously to the conciliatory *Thomas* while declining to engage *John's* renewed attack. *cum Mathematicus sit* — "being a mathematician": Tycho pointedly pities that John, though trained in mathematics, is no more clear-sighted than the lay Aristotelians.
- ***Magnificus D. P. IUNIUS* / *praestantissimi D. PETRI IUNIJ*** — **Master Peter (Petrus) Junius**, the intermediary who had carried Craig's correspondence and Craig's good report of Thomas to Tycho; named first by initial (*D. P. IUNIUS*) and later in full (*D. PETRI IUNIJ*). The text twice calls his contact with Tycho brief (*cursim … salutare*; *utut inter nos breviculâ*).
- ***Capnurania ista scoptica*** — "that scoffing *Capnurania* of his." ***Capnurania*** is **John Craig's own polemical coinage**, a Greek-derived portmanteau (καπνός *kapnos*, "smoke" + Οὐρανία/*Urania*, the muse of astronomy / the heavens), insinuating that Tycho's celestial comets are mere smoke or vapour. Tycho retained the term and titled his rebuttal the *Capnuraniae restinctio* ("the quenching of the *Capnurania*," ed. in Dreyer, *Opera Omnia* IV). *scoptica* (Greek σκωπτικός, "scoffing, satirical") is kept and glossed; **the neologism is flagged, not Englished**, by the audit's rule.
- **Embedded quotation.** *Cupivit vir D. legatus … gratusne fuissem hospes?* — Tycho quotes John Craig's own words verbatim (the *legatus* = an ambassador in whose company Craig had wished to visit Hven, but was prevented by his friends), as the instance in which Craig had impugned Tycho's hospitality. Rendered as direct speech in quotation marks; *vir D. legatus* literally "the man, Master ambassador."
- **Astronomy / the comet argument.** *crinitis sideribus* = "hairy stars," i.e. **comets** (the literal sense of *cometa* < κομήτης); rendered "hairy stars [comets]." *infra Lunam … sublunares* = below the Moon / **sublunary** — the Aristotelian doctrine that comets are atmospheric (sublunary) exhalations, which Tycho's parallax measurements of five comets refuted. *paralaxin* = **parallax**; *qualem Sol efficit* — Tycho's standard of comparison is the (small) solar parallax. *toto … coelo deviasse* — "gone astray by the whole heaven," a proverbial Latin idiom (*toto caelo errare*, to be utterly wrong); Tycho marks it as proverbial with *prout dici solet* ("as the saying goes"), preserved.
- ***Epistolam hanc Elegiacam … ad imitationem Ovidianarum … sororis nomine*** — "this Elegiac Epistle … in imitation of Ovid's [*Heroides*] … in my sister's name." Tycho appended to this letter a Latin verse epistle in elegiac couplets, written *animi causa* ("for diversion / for the heart's relief") and *in the name of his sister* — almost certainly **Sophie Brahe** — modelled on Ovid's *Heroides* (verse letters in a woman's voice). The enclosed poem is not part of this letter's prose text. *lusam* (from *ludere*) = "composed in play / as a literary diversion"; the modest framing is preserved, not sharpened into a claim of seriousness.
- ***terricolis … usitata*** — "things familiar to the dwellers on earth," opposed to *sublimia et coelestia* ("lofty and celestial matters"): Tycho's self-deprecating contrast between his astronomy and this occasional verse. *obiter tamen* ("in passing, however") is his hedge that such earthly trifling is only incidental — preserved.
- **Orthography (as printed).** *oportunitas* for *opportunitas*; *autoritatem* for *auctoritatem*; *coniuntam* for *coniunctam*; *perspexerim*; the *-ij* digraph (*proprijs, carminibus … IUNIJ, alijs*) is the period spelling for *-ii*; circumflexes (*fusiùs* etc., here *fusius / breviculâ / prudentiâ / venâ*) are the editor's. The edition header carries inline lettered footnote markers (superscript "A") on several words (*eruditissimeᴬ, refertissimasᴬ, fusiùsᴬ, Capnuraniaᴬistaᴬ, perspexerimᴬ, sororisᴬ*); these are apparatus sigla, not part of the text, and are omitted from the Source block.
- **Calendar / place.** *Datae Uraniburgi 26. Iulij Anno 1594* = "Given at **Uraniborg**, 26 July 1594" — **Old Style** (Denmark kept the Julian calendar until 1700; this chapter's convention). The edition *label* ("1594. 26. juli. Uraniborg") agrees with the dateline; no discrepancy. (Edinburgh likewise remained on Old Style in 1594, so no cross-style ambiguity arises with the Scottish recipient.)
- **MS.** The sole witness is the Vienna draft (*Kladde*), cod. Vindob. lat. 9737f.
- **Correction.** Latin: restored the dropped abbreviation 'doctiss.' (doctissimus, 'most learned') before 'vir D. legatus', per Dreyer, Opera Omnia VII, p.366. English: added 'most learned' to the corresponding quoted clause.

documents.abstract: Declares the sale of his half-share of Knudstrup to his brother Steen Brahe, reserving the right to retain the style 'of Knudstrup' for life.
documents.incipit: JEG Tygge Brahe thill Knudstrup kienndiß och giør witterligt for alle med thette mitt …

text.original:
JEG Tygge Brahe thill Knudstrup kienndiß och giør witterligt for alle med thette mitt obnne breff, att effter som jeg nu haffuer soldt och skiødt till min kierre broder, erllig och welbyrdig manndt Steenn Brahe till Knudstrup, min halffpartt aff Knudstrups hoffuittgaardt och grund, och jeg mig dog ther hos forbeholldett att maa och skall ald min liffstiid schriffuis och kalldis aff samme Knudstrup gaardt, liige som jeg giorde, førenndt jeg thennd affhenndt och soldt haffuer, eptherthi thennd hafuer verett min federnne gaardt och mig arffueligenn thillfaldenn som min rette sedegaardt, saa beplichter jeg mig dog med thette breff, att enndog jeg baade selff schriffuer och kaller, och aff anndre, huem som held[s]t thed vere kannd, mig lader schriffue och kalle aff for:ne Knudstrups gaardt, att thed alligeuell icke skall komme for:ne min kierre broder Steenn Brahe eller hanns arffuinge thill hinder eller skade i nogen maade. This till ydermere vidnisbyrtt haffuer jeg trøgtt min signete her neden for thette mit obne breff, och mig med egenn hannd vnnderschreffuit, och wenligen ombedett erllig och welbiurdige menndt, Dethleff Holck thill Høygaardt och Eske Biillde til Ellinnge, thette breff med mig thil widnisbyrtt att besegle.

Giffuit vdi Helsingøer thennd x augustj anno Mdlxxxxiiij
Thyge
Brahe (l.s.)
egen hand

Dettleff
Holck (l.s.)
egen handtt
text.english:
I, Tyge Brahe of Knudstrup, acknowledge and make known to all by this my open letter that, inasmuch as I have now sold and conveyed to my dear brother, the honourable and well-born man Steen Brahe of Knudstrup, my half-share of the principal estate and land of Knudstrup — and have nonetheless reserved to myself therewith that I may and shall, for all my lifetime, be written and styled "of" that same estate of Knudstrup, just as I did before I parted with and sold it, inasmuch as it has been my paternal estate and has fallen to me by inheritance as my rightful ancestral seat — I do nevertheless bind myself by this letter that, although both I myself write and style [myself thus], and have myself written and styled by others, whosoever they may be, "of" the aforesaid estate of Knudstrup, it shall nevertheless not be to the hindrance or harm, in any manner, of my aforesaid dear brother Steen Brahe or his heirs. In further witness whereof I have impressed my seal here below this my open letter, and have signed it with my own hand, and have in friendship requested the honourable and well-born men Detlev Holck of Højgård and Eske Bille of Ellinge to seal this letter, together with me, in witness.

Given at Helsingør, the 10th [day] of August, in the year 1594.
Tyge
Brahe (place of the seal)
[in his] own hand

Detlev
Holck (place of the seal)
[in his] own hand

documents.apparatus:
- **Document type.** Not an ordinary letter but an **open letter / deed of declaration** (*åbent brev*) issued by Tycho in his own name — a self-binding instrument annexed to the **sale of his half-share of Knudstrup to his brother Steen Brahe**, the transaction completed by mid-1594 (J. R. Christianson, *On Tycho's Island* / *Lord of Uraniborg*; cf. Dreyer, *Tycho Brahe*: Knudstrup was inherited jointly by Otte Brahe's two eldest sons, Tycho and Steen). The edition's recipient:empty is therefore correct: an open letter is addressed to all (*for alle*), not to a single recipient.
- **Issuer.** **Tycho Brahe** (1546–1601), here styling himself *Tygge Brahe thill Knudstrup* ("Tyge Brahe of Knudstrup") — the very style whose reservation is the subject of the deed.
- **Steen Brahe of Knudstrup** (1547–1620), Tycho's younger brother, royal councillor; by this conveyance he obtained sole ownership of the family seat without awaiting Tycho's death.
- **Knudstrup** (Knutstorp, Scania) — the Brahe family's *fædrenegård* (paternal estate) and *sædegård* (ancestral noble seat), Tycho's birthplace.
- **Witnesses.** **Detlev Holck of Højgård** (*Dethleff Holck thill Høygaardt*) and **Eske Bille of Ellinge** (*Eske Biillde til Ellinnge*), Danish noblemen requested to co-seal; both named within the body. Only Holck's subscription and seal survive in the closing autograph block as transcribed here.
- **Legal force of the binding clause.** The operative sentence carries a single negation governing the whole reservation: *att thed alligeuell **icke** skall komme … thill hinder eller skade i nogen maade* = "that it shall **nevertheless not** be to the hindrance or harm … in any manner." Tycho reserves the honorific style "of Knudstrup" for life but expressly disclaims any property or legal consequence flowing from it against Steen or his heirs. The single negation is reproduced as one; the concessive *enndog … alligeuell* ("although … nevertheless") pairing is kept intact.
- **Orthography (chancery Danish, c. 1594).** *kienndiß* = *kendes* ("acknowledge"); *giør witterligt* = *gør vitterligt* ("make known"); *obnne / obne breff* = *åbne brev* ("open letter"); *skiødt* = *skødt* ("conveyed," verb of *skøde*, the deed of conveyance); *halffpartt* = *halvpart* ("half-share"); *hoffuittgaardt* = *hovedgård* ("principal/manorial estate"); *forbeholldett* = *forbeholdt* ("reserved"); *liffstiid* = *livstid* ("lifetime"); *schriffuis och kalldis* = *skrives og kaldes* ("be written and styled"); *førenndt* = *førend* ("before"); *affhenndt* = *afhændet* ("alienated, parted with"); *eptherthi* = *eftersom/efterdi* ("inasmuch as"); *federnne gaardt* = *fædrenegård* ("paternal estate"); *arffueligenn thillfaldenn* = *arveligen tilfaldet* ("fallen to [me] by inheritance"); *sedegaardt* = *sædegård* ("ancestral noble seat"); *beplichter* = *forpligter* ("bind/oblige"); *held[s]t* — the source reads *held* with the *s* of *heldst* (= *helst*, "soever") not written; supplied in brackets; *for:ne* = *fornævnte* ("aforesaid," the standard chancery abbreviation); *alligeuell* = *alligevel* ("nevertheless"); *arffuinge* = *arvinger* ("heirs"); *hinder* = *hinder* ("hindrance, impediment"); *i nogen maade* = *i nogen måde* ("in any manner"); *This* = *des / dess* ("thereof," the chancery formula *des til ydermere vidnesbyrd*, "in further witness whereof"); *trøgtt min signete* = *trykt mit signet* ("impressed my seal"); *wenligen ombedett* = *venligen ombedet* ("in friendship requested"); *besegle* = *besegle* ("to seal").
- **Seal notations.** *(l.s.)* expands *loco sigilli*, "in the place of the seal" — the editorial marker for where a seal was impressed; *egen hand / egen handtt* = *egen hånd*, "[in his] own hand," noting the autograph subscription.
- **Calendar / place.** *Giffuit vdi Helsingøer thennd x augustj anno Mdlxxxxiiij* = "Given at **Helsingør** (Elsinore), the 10th [day] of August, in the year 1594" (O.S.). documents.abstract: Rebukes Tycho for failing to repair the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings at Roskilde Cathedral and demands completion before Christmas.
documents.incipit: Christian 4..

text.original:
TILL TYGE BRAHE HELLIG THRE KONGERS CAPELL WDI ROSCHILDE DOMBKIRCKE ANRØRENDIS VT SEQUITUR.

Christian 4..

WOR gunst thilfornn. Wiid, epter att Wij thig thilforn haffue thilschreffuit, attu wden forßømmelße schulle lade forethage thend bygning paa thet capell wdi Roschilde domkircke, som kaldis Hellig thre konger capell, och Wore kierre foreldre, salige och hoglofflige ihukommelße, haffue theris begraffuelße wdi, huilckit dog her thill aldelis icke er scheedt, meden samme capell io meere och meere dag fran dag forderffuis och forargis, och forwndre Wij Oß høyligen, attu samme Wor befaling icke anderledis haffuer achtit och epterkommit och samme bygning forferdigit. Tha bede Wij dig och wille, attu aldelis er fortenckt wdi for:ne bygning paa for:ne capell endeligen och wden ald wndschylding at lade forethage och forferdige inden juell førstkommendis wdi thet allersenniste, wdi huis maade thett kunde haffue wdi behoff att byggis och ferdigis paa. Saa frampt thet icke scheer, att for:ne bygning inden for:ne dag och thiid bliffuer forferdigit, tha wille Wij naadigst befale Wor embidtzmand paa Wor gaard wdi for:ne Roschilde for:ne bygning at schulle lade ferdig giørre, och tha strax att forleene en anden med for:ne capell och theß thilliggendis guoedtz och indkompst, och attu thig med thett allerførste her om emoed Oß ercklerer, huad thu er herwdinden thilßindtz att wille giørre, paa thet Wij kunde wiide, huor epter Wij Oß schulle forholde.

Ther met etc.
Actum Cold[ingæ] 4. septembris a:o 94.
text.english:
**To Tyge Brahe, concerning the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings in Roskilde Cathedral, as follows.**

Christian IV.

Our favour beforehand. Know that, since we have heretofore written to you that you should without neglect have undertaken that building-work on the chapel in Roskilde Cathedral which is called the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings, and in which our dear parents, of blessed and most laudable memory, have their burial — which nonetheless has not at all been done up to now, while that same chapel is decaying and being damaged more and more day by day — we are therefore greatly astonished that you have not otherwise heeded and complied with this our command and completed that same building-work. We therefore ask and will of you that you be wholly mindful, finally and without any excuse, to have that aforesaid building-work on the aforesaid chapel undertaken and completed before Christmas next at the very latest, in whatever manner it may have need to be built and finished. So far forth as it does not come to pass that the aforesaid building-work is completed within the aforesaid day and time, then we will most graciously command our official at our manor in the aforesaid Roskilde to have the aforesaid building-work made ready, and then forthwith to enfeoff another with the aforesaid chapel and its appurtenant property and income; and [we will] that you declare yourself to us concerning this at the very first, [as to] what you are minded herein to do, so that we may know how we are to govern ourselves accordingly.

Therewith, etc.
Done at Kolding, 4 September, year [15]94.

documents.apparatus:
- **Issuer.** **Christian IV of Denmark** (b. 1577, r. 1588–1648), here writing in his own name at age 17 in the third year after his 1593 accession to personal rule (the regency council had governed 1588–93). The chancery hand subscribes him *"Christian 4.."* (so written, with the doubled point).
- **Recipient and benefice.** Tycho Brahe had held the prebend (canonry) of the **Chapel of the Three Holy Kings** (*Hellig Tre Kongers Kapel*) in Roskilde Cathedral since the grant of 1 May 1579 from Frederik II — a sinecure carrying income and the obligation to maintain the chapel fabric and to support two choirboys (*tho smaa sincker*). The chapel is the burial place of Christian I and later Danish kings; the *"kierre foreldre"* ("dear parents") here are **Frederik II** (d. 1588) and Queen **Sophie of Mecklenburg** — though Sophie was living in 1594, the chancery formula *"of blessed and most laudable memory"* with *foreldre* is the dynastic burial-chapel formula and is reproduced as written, not corrected (see crux below).
- **Document type and code-switch.** A chancery-register entry (*Sjællandske Tegnelser* XVIII, 364), not an autograph. The **Latin rubric** *"…ANRØRENDIS **ut sequitur**"* ("concerning… **as follows**") heads the Danish body — a code-switch preserved by this chapter's convention, exactly as in the parallel 1584 Frederik II letter.
- **Legal force — the threat (translated with negation count fixed).** The operative clause is a royal ultimatum with three explicit negations / privatives, reproduced one-for-one: (1) *"huilckit dog her thill **aldelis icke** er scheedt"* = "which nonetheless has **not at all** been done up to now"; (2) *"attu… befaling **icke** anderledis haffuer achtit"* = "that you have **not** otherwise heeded"; (3) *"endeligen och **wden ald** wndschylding"* = "finally and **without any** excuse." The conditional *"**Saa frampt** thet **icke** scheer, att… bliffuer forferdigit, **tha** wille Wij…"* is a negative protasis governing a future apodosis: "**So far forth as** it does **not** come to pass that [the work] is completed…, **then** we will…" — i.e. *if you fail to finish it by Christmas, then* the king will (a) have it finished by his own Roskilde official and (b) **enfeoff another** with the chapel and its revenues — a threat to revoke Tycho's benefice. The fourth negation-like privative *"**wden** forßømmelße"* ("**without** neglect," in the recital of the earlier order) is also kept. Total: four privative/negative markers (*aldelis icke, icke, wden ald, wden*) plus the conditional *icke scheer* — all five preserved; none added.
- **"bede Wij dig och wille."** The doublet *bede… och wille* couples a courteous "ask" with the binding *ville* of the royal will ("ask and will of you"); the closing *"och attu… ercklerer"* depends on this same *wille*, hence the bracketed "[we will] that you declare." The mood is a command softened by petitionary form, not a request — rendered to keep both registers.
- **Orthography (chancery Danish, c. 1594).** *WOR gunst thilfornn* = *Vor gunst tilforn* ("Our favour beforehand," the royal address-formula, this chapter's convention); *Wiid* = *Vid* ("Know," imperative); *attu* = *at du*; *thilschreffuit* = *tilskrevet* ("written to"); *wden forßømmelße* = *uden forsømmelse* ("without neglect"); *forethage* = *foretage* ("undertake"); *scheedt* = *sket* ("done, happened"); *forderffuis* = *fordærves* ("is spoiled/decays"); *forargis* = *forarges* ("is damaged/marred"); *forwndre Wij Oß høyligen* = *forundre vi os højligen* ("we are greatly astonished"); *achtit* = *agtet* ("heeded, regarded"); *epterkommit* = *efterkommet* ("complied with"); *forferdigit / forferdige* = *færdiggjort / færdiggøre* ("completed / complete"); *for:ne* = *fornævnte* ("aforesaid," the standard chancery abbreviation); *fortenckt* = *betænkt* ("mindful, intent"); *juell førstkommendis* = *jul førstkommende* ("Christmas next-coming"); *allersenniste* = *allersidste* ("very latest"); *Saa frampt* = *såfremt* ("so far forth as, provided that, if"); *embidtzmand* = *embedsmand* ("official, officer"); *gaard* = *gård* ("manor, estate"); *forleene* = *forlene* ("enfeoff, grant in fief"); *theß thilliggendis guoedtz och indkompst* = *dets tilliggende gods og indkomst* ("its appurtenant property and income"); *ercklerer* = *erklærer* ("declare"); *thilßindtz* = *tilsinds* ("minded, disposed"); *huor epter… forholde* = *hvorefter… forholde* ("how we are to conduct/govern ourselves").
- **Calendar / place.** *Actum Cold[ingae] 4. septembris a:o 94* = "Done at **Kolding**, 4 September [15]94" (O.S.; Denmark kept the Julian calendar until 1700). *Actum* "Done/Given" kept by this chapter's convention; *Cold.* expanded to the Latin locative *Coldingae* (Kolding, the royal residence Koldinghus in Jutland). The dateline as written (4 September 1594) agrees with the catalogue label.

documents.abstract: Explains his long absence by severe arthritis and nephritic pain, reports a partial recovery, and mentions searching Frankfurt catalogues.
documents.incipit: QVANTOS sustinuerim hactenus cruciatus, vir Nobilissime et Eruditissime, non opus esse …

text.original:
NOBILISSIMO ET SINGVLARI ERVDITIONE, VIRTVTE, ET INTEGRITATE PRÆSTANTISSIMO VIRO, DOMINO TYCHONI BRAHE, DOMINO DE KNUDSTRUP, EQUITI DANO, ETC. DOMINO ET AMICO SUO CUM OBSERVANTIA COLENDO. S. P.

QVANTOS sustinuerim hactenus cruciatus, vir Nobilissime et Eruditissime, non opus esse arbitror ut scribam. Tanti certê fuerunt, ut anima vix corpori inhærere potuerit, recurrente subinde arthritide et immanissimis nephriticis doloribus. Qui etiam in causa fuêre, quo minus ad Illustrissimum Principem ac Dominum meum ante ipsius obitum reuerterer, tibique ea, quæ promiseram, transmitterem. Sed iam ante paucas aliquot Septimanas Diuino fauore aliquo modo cæpi respirare. DEVS æternus Opt. Max. in cuius conspectu ego ambulo, pro sua inexhausta misericordia etiam in posterum auxilio suo mihi adsit, et quod cæpit, clementer ad finem perducat. De nostris autem studijs ut aliquid attingam, diligenter hactenus scrutatus sum Catalogos Francofurtenses, num a TYCHONE BRAHE quid editum in ijs invenire possem: Verum nihil reperi. Miror igitur, quid causæ sit, quod Opus illud tuum de Cometis supprimas, nec in publicum prodire sinas, præsertim cum non tantum illud iamdudum fuerit absolutum, verumetiam toties et tanto tempore tam certo promiseris, te propediem illud emissurum. Equidem libenter, quantum in me esset, VRANIAM nostram ornarem et excolerem. Sed quid mihi sit obstaculo, vides. Quod igitur mihi denegatur, tu eo ardentius suppleas. Nec enim Mathematica Studia parum illustrabis, Posteritatique commendabis, si Opus illud tuum divulgabis. Incusantur enim vulgo, quasi sint sine fructu. Sed cum ex Opere illo tuo animaduertent, nos ea, quæ hactenus ignoratione Matheseos pro veris credita sunt, falsissima esse, certissime demonstrare posse, obturabis ora tam temere iudicantium, illosque suæ temeritatis conuinces, modo apud ipsos veritatis inuentio et tam abditissimarum tamque a nobis procul dissitarum rerum cognitio, fructus censeatur. Incitabis simul etiam heroica et præclara ingenia ad æmulationem, turpeque sibi esse ducent, si hæc ignorent: quemadmodum solet præclaris ingenijs nihil detestabilius videri, quâm præclara quæque ignorare. Præterea quot viros doctos putas editionem tuam singulari cum desiderio expectare? Qui certe plures sunt, quam tu tibi persuadere potes, quique de te non aliter nisi præclare sentiunt. Noli igitur ulterius istorum omnium expectationem suspendere, aut etiam tua ipsis invidere. Sed spero non committes, ut studia Mathematica diutius isto tuo ornatu careant, proptereaque minus colantur. Hæc fuêre, quæ ad te hoc tempore perscribere volui: quæ licet fortasse non sint magni momenti; tamen nactus certum hominem, qui ad vos iret, vacuas ad Amicum Literas quam nullas dare malui. Accipies igitur hæc in meliorem partem, silentiumque meum diuturnum supradictâ de causâ sufficienter excusatum habebis. Hortum sororis tuæ Philosophicæ, Dominæ SOPHIÆ BRAHE Matronæ perquam solertissimæ et Nobilissimæ, Illustrissimo Principi ac Domino meo, felicissimæ recordationis, pro dignitate commendassem, si ipsius Celsit. accessissem. Attamen per Literas omnia Illustriss. ipsius Celsit. significaui.

Vale feliciter et optime mî Nobilissime et Eruditissime Domine BRAHE, Vraniamque, quod facis, splendide ornare pergito.
Bernburgi 28. Septemb. Anno 1594.
T. T.
CHRISTOPHORVS ROTHMANNVS.
text.english:
**To the most noble man, most outstanding in singular erudition, virtue, and integrity, Master Tycho Brahe, Lord of Knudstrup, Danish knight, etc., his lord and friend to be honoured with respect. Heartiest greeting.**

How great the torments are that I have endured up to now, most noble and most learned Sir, I do not think there is any need to write. They were certainly so great that my soul could scarcely cling to my body, with arthritis and most savage nephritic [kidney] pains recurring time and again. These were also the cause why I did not return to the Most Illustrious Prince, my lord, before his death, and why I did not send on to you those things I had promised. But now, some few weeks ago, by divine favour I have in some measure begun to breathe again. May the eternal God, Best and Greatest, in whose sight I walk, of his inexhaustible mercy be present to me with his aid hereafter too, and graciously bring to its end what he has begun. But to touch on something of our studies: I have hitherto diligently searched the Frankfurt catalogues, [to see] whether I might find anything published in them by Tycho Brahe; but I found nothing. I wonder, therefore, what the reason is that you suppress that work of yours on the comets, and do not let it come out into public, especially since it has not only long since been finished, but you have so often and over so long a time so surely promised that you would shortly send it out. For my part I would gladly, as far as lay in me, adorn and cultivate our Urania. But you see what is an obstacle to me. What therefore is denied to me, may you supply the more ardently. For you will not a little illuminate the mathematical studies, and commend them to posterity, if you publish that work of yours. For they are commonly charged [with being], as it were, without fruit. But when from that work of yours they shall perceive that we can most certainly demonstrate those things which hitherto, through ignorance of mathematics, have been believed true to be utterly false, you will stop the mouths of those who judge so rashly, and convict them of their rashness — provided that with them the finding-out of truth, and the knowledge of things so deeply hidden and so far removed from us, be reckoned a fruit. At the same time you will also spur on heroic and illustrious minds to emulation, and they will count it a disgrace to themselves if they should be ignorant of these things — just as to illustrious minds nothing is wont to seem more detestable than to be ignorant of whatever is illustrious. Besides, how many learned men do you think await your edition with singular longing? They are certainly more than you can persuade yourself, and they think of you in no other way than splendidly. Do not therefore any longer keep all these men's expectation in suspense, or even begrudge them what is yours. But I hope you will not let it come about that the mathematical studies should longer lack this adornment of yours, and on that account be the less cultivated. These were the things I wished to write out to you at this time; which, although they may perhaps not be of great moment, yet, having got hold of a trustworthy man who was going to you, I preferred to give empty Letters to a Friend than none at all. You will therefore take these in the better part, and will hold my long silence, for the cause stated above, to be sufficiently excused. I would, as was fitting, have commended the garden of your philosophical sister, the Lady Sophie Brahe, a matron exceedingly skilful and most noble, to the Most Illustrious Prince my lord, of most happy memory, if I had approached His Highness. Nevertheless by Letters I signified everything to His Most Illustrious Highness.

Fare happily and very well, my most noble and most learned Master Brahe, and continue, as you do, splendidly to adorn Urania.
At Bernburg, 28 September, the year 1594.
Yours truly [T. T.],
Christoph Rothmann.

documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent.** *Christophorus Rothmannus* = **Christoph Rothmann** (c. 1550/60 – c. 1600), mathematician–astronomer at the court of Landgrave Wilhelm IV of Hesse-Kassel, Tycho's principal scientific correspondent there and a defender of the Copernican system against Tycho. He left Kassel on 1 September 1590, ostensibly to return there, but went instead to his native Bernburg; after a long silence this is **his last known letter to Tycho** (Dreyer, *Tycho Brahe*, on the 1590 departure and the September 1594 letter). The closing *T. T.* = *Tuus Totus* ("Wholly yours" / "Yours truly").
- **Recipient titulature.** *Domino de Knudstrup, Equiti Dano* = "Lord of **Knudstrup**, Danish knight" — Tycho's ancestral seat in Scania and his noble rank. *S. P.* = *salutem plurimam* ("heartiest greeting," this chapter's convention).
- **Place.** *Bernburgi* = **Bernburg** (Bernburg an der Saale, in Anhalt; Sachsen-Anhalt), Rothmann's birthplace and where he had withdrawn.
- ***Illustrissimum Principem ac Dominum meum … felicissimae recordationis*** — "the Most Illustrious Prince, my lord, … of most happy memory": Rothmann's patron, identified from the literature consulted as **Joachim Ernst, Prince of Anhalt (Anhalt-Bernburg)** (1536–1586), who had supported his studies at Wittenberg. The phrase *ante ipsius obitum* ("before his death") and *felicissimae recordationis* mark the prince as already deceased; he had died in 1586, so the unfulfilled return and the *significaui* ("I signified … by letters") describe relations during the prince's lifetime — **flagged below as a chronological crux.**
- **Medicine.** *arthritide* = "arthritis" (gout/joint disease); *immanissimis nephriticis doloribus* = "most savage nephritic pains," i.e. kidney pains (the stone) — period terms, kept and glossed. Both recur as Rothmann's standing complaint in this correspondence.
- ***Catalogos Francofurtenses*** — the **Frankfurt [book-fair] catalogues** (the *Messkataloge*), the standard early-modern record of newly published books; Rothmann had searched them in vain for anything printed by Tycho.
- ***Opus illud tuum de Cometis*** — "that work of yours on the comets," Tycho's projected/long-promised treatise on comets (the volume that would become *De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis*, 1588, on the comet of 1577, and the planned further volume); Rothmann presses Tycho on its non-appearance in print. *iamdudum … absolutum* ("long since finished") is Rothmann's claim, kept as his assertion.
- ***URANIAM nostram*** / ***Uraniam … splendide ornare*** — "**our Urania**" / "splendidly to adorn Urania": Urania, Muse of astronomy, here a metonym for the science of astronomy itself; *ornare/excolere Uraniam* ("to adorn / cultivate Urania") echoes the Tychonic sign-off register (cf. this chapter's convention, *sacris Uraniae lita*). Kept as figure, named in the translation.
- ***studia Mathematica … isto tuo ornatu*** — "the mathematical studies … this adornment of yours": *Mathematica/Mathesis* in Rothmann's usage = the mathematical sciences (astronomy chief among them); the defence against the charge that they are *sine fructu* ("without fruit") is a topos of the period's apologetics for mathematics.
- ***sororis tuae Philosophicae, Dominae Sophiae Brahe*** — "your philosophical sister, the Lady **Sophie Brahe**" (1559–1643), Tycho's learned younger sister, known for her work in horticulture, chemistry/alchemy, and genealogy; *Philosophicae* marks her as a fellow student of natural philosophy. *Hortum … pro dignitate commendassem* ("I would … have commended [her] garden as was fitting") points to her noted garden/horticultural interest. *Matronae perquam solertissimae* = "a matron exceedingly skilful."
- ***Celsit. / Illustriss. ipsius Celsit.*** — *Celsitudo* = "Highness"; the abbreviations are expanded in translation as "His Highness" / "His Most Illustrious Highness."
- **Greek / symbols.** None in the text.
- **Orthography (humanist Latin print, 1596 edition).** *câepi* for *coepi*, *fuêre* for *fuerunt*, *quâm* for *quam*, *câeperit*-type *ae→ae*-ligature spellings, consonantal *u/v* (*reuerterer, conuinces, diuulgabis, significaui*) and *i/j* (*studijs, ijs, Mathematica Studia*) are the edition's forms, reproduced as printed; not normalised.
- **Calendar / place.** *Bernburgi 28. Septemb. Anno 1594* = "At Bernburg, 28 September 1594." A plain civil dateline that **agrees with the catalogue label** ("1594. 28. september. Bernburg"); no conversion is made. Bernburg in Anhalt kept the **Julian (Old Style)** calendar in 1594 (Protestant Germany did not adopt the Gregorian reform until 1700), so the date is read as O.S. — flagged for completeness rather than asserted from any in-text style marker.

text.original:
NOBILITATE GENERIS, VIRTUTE AC ERUDITIONE ILLUSTRI VIRO, DOMINO TYCHONI BRAHE, DOMINO DE KNUDSTRUP ET URANIBURGO, FAUTORI SUO OMNI OBSERVANTIA COLENDO. S.

NISI quodammodo T. E. Generosissime Domine TYCHO mea erga T. E. debita observantia, et mihi tua in me benivolentia perspecta esset, vererer sane ne meum incusares officium, quod toto iam pene semestri nihil ad te literarum transmiserim. Id quod meae ingratitudini aut incuriae nequaquam ascribas velim. In ea siquidem locorum adyta hîc detrudimur, ad quae commeantibus hinc inde ad vos Tabellarijs haud ita crebro praebetur aditus. Scripsi tamen non ita dudum ad V. E. cum internuncio quodam Marpurgensi, qui Herbornae, assumpto Chartopaeo quodam, me convenerat. Is in Daniam, adhibito eiusdem Opificij comministro, se unâ confestim profecturum et te operam suam in Officina Chartacea aliquamdiu elocaturum spondebat. Verum trifurcifer iste Marpurgium rediens causa nescio qua clam se subduxit, meque ita praeter opinionem thaleris aliquot, quos pro commeatu isti nebuloni praenumeravi, callide emunxit. Sed patior hoc quieto quid est iacturae eo facilius, quod iam demum quid eiusmodi committendum sit agyrtis et vespertilionibus, meo qualicunque damno rectius sapiam. Caeterum CLAVIJ hunc in Sphaeram SACROBOSCI Commentarium ad te ablegavi ob tractatulum quendam de Nova Stella Anni 72 insertum. In quo multa, si recte memini, praesertim de generatione et situ eius Aethereo, idque inter Firmamenti Sidera, magnitudine primaeva apparenti etc. vestris non omnia dissona placitis adfert. Miror hominem Peripateticum a suae sectae Coriphaeo ARISTOTELE tam libere in plerisque his dissentire. Quo nomine CRAIGO illi Scoto iurato ARISTOTELIS mancipio, veritatis perduelli, longe, meo iudicio, anteponi merebitur. Vidi egomet non ita dudum Epistolas illius nonnullas ad te de negotio Cometico perscriptas. Inaudieram etiam a Conterraneis eius circumferri Capnuraniae istius nugamenta et cum doctis quibusdam communicari. Exoptant igitur mecum et expetunt quidam vestrarum laudum et lucubrationum studiosi, ut non tantum Apologiam Scoticis istis de Cometarum ortu, situ ac motu a vobis oppositam somnijs, sed etiam Lichnuraniam quandam, reliquas Capnuraniae illius tenebras ac densos fumos suis radijs discutientem, publici iuris faceretis. Sed quid ego noctuas Athenas? Catalogum vero hunc recentiorum auctorum addidi, si quos forte proximo mercato Francofurtensi ex ijs, qui hîc assignantur, novellis libris vobis per me coëmi expetiveritis. In quem usum, quas ex vestris pecunijs reliquas habeo, tum si quid ulterius sit erogandum, lubens impendam. Reperietis etiam his adiunctam terrae, ut vocant, sigillatae portiunculam quandam, quae tribus hinc circiter milliaribus ubertim effoditur. Quod vero OTTONI auctor et suasor fuerim, ut unâ ad te perscriberet, in meliorem partem interpreteris oro. Dudum siquidem a me petijt, ut sibi permitterem amoris et benevolentiae testificandae gratia, literas suas ad te daret. Id quod me illi tum concessurum spondebam ubi sine crassioribus mendis proprio Marte epistolam conficere valeret. Itaque iam aggressus est me suasore, et quidem felicius quam sperabam. Paucula a me limitata, nonnulla interpolata. Vides igitur non obscura ingenij hac praesertim aetate indicia. Quem in virum bonum ac doctum successu temporis pervasurum mihi persuadeo, si modo quemadmodum inceperit, ita in posterum inoffenso pede ad callem VIRTUTIS ac VERITATIS contenderit.

Vale praecipuum Patriae ornamentum, vita, ut dignus, quam diutissime, si quisquam, incolumi, meque tuo favore dignare.

Iterum quam felicissime vale.
Sigenae Nassoviorum 23. Octob. Anno 1594.
T. amplissimi nominis honoris
desiderij studioss.
CUNRADUS BERGENSIS.

Sciatis globum cœlestem secundum vestras observationes restitutum et affabre
solerterque elaboratum his nundinis prodijsse, magna sane multorum gratulatione.
Sed nimis care æstimabatur nempe unâ cum terrestri æqualis magnitudinis 22
thal.
text.english:
**To the man illustrious in nobility of birth, in virtue, and in learning, Master Tycho Brahe, lord of Knudstrup and of Uraniborg, his patron to be honoured with every mark of respect — greeting.**

Were the respect I owe to Your Excellency, most noble Lord Tycho, and the goodwill of yours toward me which I have clearly perceived, not in some measure [assured], I should indeed fear that you might reproach my dutifulness, in that for almost a whole half-year now I have sent you no letter. This I would by no means have you ascribe to ingratitude or carelessness on my part. For we are thrust away here into such remote recesses of place that, to the couriers travelling to and fro to you, access is not so very often afforded. Yet I wrote to Your Excellency not so long ago by way of a certain Marburg messenger, who had met with me at Herborn, having taken on a certain paper-maker. He gave his word that he would set out together, at once, into Denmark — having engaged a fellow-workman of the same trade — and that he would hire out his labour to you for some while in [your] paper-mill. But that thrice-gallows-rogue, returning to Marburg, made off in secret for some reason I know not, and so, contrary to my expectation, slyly fleeced me of the several thalers which I had paid in advance to that scoundrel for his journey. But I bear this trifle of a loss the more calmly because at last I may know better — at whatever cost to myself — what is to be entrusted to mountebanks and bats [= shifty night-creatures]. For the rest, I have dispatched to you this Commentary of Clavius on the *Sphere* of Sacrobosco, on account of a certain little treatise inserted [in it] concerning the New Star of the year [15]72. In which, if I remember rightly, he brings forward much — especially concerning its generation and its aetherial situation, and that among the stars of the firmament, [and] its original [first-appearing] magnitude, etc. — not all of it discordant with your views. I marvel that a Peripatetic man dissents so freely from Aristotle, the Coryphaeus [chief] of his own sect, in most of these matters. On which score he will deserve, in my judgment, to be set far before that Craig, the Scot, a sworn bondman of Aristotle and a [public] enemy of the truth. I myself saw not long ago several letters of his written out to you about the cometary affair. I had also heard that the trifles of that *Capnurania* [smoke-of-the-sky] of his are being passed about by his countrymen and shared with certain learned men. And so certain men devoted to your praises and your lucubrations long for, and seek, together with me, that you would make public not only the *Apologia* set by you against those Scottish dreams about the rising, situation, and motion of comets, but also a certain *Lichnurania* [lamp-of-the-sky], scattering with its rays the remaining shadows and dense smokes of that *Capnurania* of his. But why [do I carry] owls to Athens? I have, moreover, added this catalogue of more recent authors, in case you should perhaps wish me to buy up for you at the next Frankfurt fair some of the new books out of those that are listed here. To which use I will gladly devote whatever I have left over from your monies, and then anything further that may have to be laid out. You will also find joined to these a little portion of what they call sealed earth [*terra sigillata*], which is dug up abundantly about three miles from here. As for my having been the prompter and persuader to Otto, that he should write to you at the same time, I beg you to interpret it in the better part. For he asked me some while ago to allow him to send his own letter to you, for the sake of attesting his love and goodwill. This I then gave my word I would grant him once he was able to compose a letter by his own effort without the grosser errors. And so he has now set to it at my urging, and indeed more happily than I had hoped. A few things [were] trimmed by me, some interpolated. You see, then, no obscure signs of talent, especially at this age. I am persuaded that with the passage of time he will turn out a good and learned man, if only, just as he has begun, he will so press on hereafter with unstumbling foot toward the path of VIRTUE and TRUTH.

Farewell, foremost ornament of our country; may you, as you deserve, live as long as may be — unharmed, if anyone may be so — and deem me worthy of your favour.

Again, fare you as happily as may be.
At Siegen of the Nassaus, 23 October, the year 1594.
Most devoted to the honour of your most ample name and to [your] regard,
Conrad of Bergen.

You should know that a celestial globe, restored according to your observations and skilfully and ingeniously worked, has come out at this [book] fair, to the no small congratulation indeed of many. But it was valued too dearly — namely, together with a terrestrial [globe] of equal size, at 22 thalers.

documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent.** *Cunradus Bergensis* = **Cort (Conrad) Aslakssøn** (1564–1624), the Bergen-born Norwegian theologian and astronomer, at this date one of Tycho's pupils and assistants; he had left Hven and was acting abroad as Tycho's book-buyer and travelling tutor. He later became professor of theology at Copenhagen. The signature Latinises his given name (Cort/Conrad) and his birthplace (Bergen). This chapter's own letters confirm the role: Tycho's June-1598 letter to Grynaeus names "Otto Brahe, who together with his tutor Cort Aslakssøn had recently been resident at Basel."
- **Recipient titulature.** *Dominus de Knudstrup et Uraniburgo* — "lord of **Knudstrup** [the Brahe family seat in Scania] and of **Uraniborg** [Tycho's observatory-residence on Hven]."
- **Place.** *Sigenae Nassoviorum* = **Siegen**, the seat of the counts of Nassau-Siegen (Nassau-Dillenburg lands); *Herborna* = **Herborn** and *Marpurgum* = **Marburg**, both in/near Hesse — the region's Reformed academies (the Hohe Schule at Herborn; the university at Marburg), consistent with Aslakssøn's Reformed-territory itinerary.
- **John Craig (the controversy).** *Craigo illi Scoto … de negotio Cometico* = **John Craig** (Johannes Craigius, d. 1620), the Scottish physician and Aristotelian with whom Tycho conducted a sustained epistolary controversy over comets (whether they are sublunary or supralunary) in 1589–90, continuing into 1592; Aslakssøn says he had seen several of Craig's letters to Tycho on the matter. The edition's letter-register lists "CRAIGIUS Scotus" / John Craig ↔ Tycho letters (1590–92). Aslakssøn's *iurato Aristotelis mancipio, veritatis perduelli* ("a sworn bondman of Aristotle, an enemy of the truth") is a partisan flourish on Tycho's behalf, kept as written.
- **Clavius / Sacrobosco.** *Clavii … in Sphaeram Sacrobosci Commentarium … de Nova Stella Anni 72* — **Christoph Clavius**'s *In Sphaeram Ioannis de Sacro Bosco commentarius*, which from its expanded editions carries a treatment of the **new star (nova) of 1572** (Tycho's *De nova stella*). Aslakssøn notes — with the hedge *si recte memini* ("if I remember rightly"), preserved — that the Jesuit Clavius, though a *Peripateticus* (Aristotelian), grants the nova an *aetherial situation … among the stars of the firmament* with a *primary magnitude* (so its location in the heavens, not the sublunary realm), positions "not all discordant" with Tycho's. *Coriphaeus* (Gk. κορυφαῖος, "chorus-leader, chief") kept as "Coryphaeus."
- **Greek-derived coinages (named cruxes).** Two mock-learned neologisms, built on Greek and left untranslated in the body with bracketed glosses:
 - *Capnurania* (Gk. καπνός *kapnós* "smoke" + οὐρανία *ouranía* "of the heaven/sky") — literally "smoke-of-the-sky," Aslakssøn's contemptuous coinage for Craig's cometary doctrine (comets as terrestrial exhalations/smoke); rendered "[smoke-of-the-sky]." The precise title/sense Craig himself used (if any) is not recoverable from this letter; the coinage may be Aslakssøn's own jibe rather than a real title — flagged.
 - *Lichnurania* (Gk. λύχνος *lýchnos* "lamp" + οὐρανία) — "lamp-of-the-sky," the antithetical work Aslakssøn wishes Tycho would publish, "scattering with its rays" the *smokes* of the *Capnurania*; rendered "[lamp-of-the-sky]." A nonce-word coined to balance *Capnurania*; not an attested title.
- ***Apologia*.** *Apologiam … Scoticis istis … somnijs … oppositam* — the **defence (Apologia)** Tycho is urged to publish against Craig's positions; per Nielsen's bibliography of Tycho's printed works, no such printed *Apologia* against Craig appeared (Tycho's comet polemic remained in correspondence and in the *De mundi* material). Rendered "*Apologia*."
- **Proverbs / allusions.** *quid ego noctuas Athenas?* — "owls to Athens" (the Greek proverb *γλαῦκ' Ἀθήναζε*, "to carry owls to Athens" = to do something superfluous; the owl was Athena's bird and the city's emblem); the elliptical phrasing is kept. *proprio Marte* — "by his own effort/unaided" (idiom, "by one's own Mars"). *inoffenso pede* — "with unstumbling foot."
- **Material enclosure.** *terra … sigillata* — **terra sigillata** ("sealed earth"), the medicinal clay sold in stamped cakes; Aslakssøn encloses a sample dug "about three miles" off. *milliare* = a (German) mile; left as "miles," the period unit not modernised.
- **Persons mentioned.** *Otto* — the young **Otto (Otte) Brahe** whom Aslakssøn was tutoring (a kinsman in Tycho's orbit; the same Otto Brahe + Aslakssøn pairing recurs in Tycho's 1598 Grynaeus letter), here making his first attempt at a Latin letter to Tycho under Aslakssøn's supervision (*paucula a me limitata, nonnulla interpolata* — "a few things trimmed by me, some interpolated"). *Chartopaeus / Officina Chartacea* — a **paper-maker** and a **paper-mill**: the absconding messenger had promised to bring a paper-maker to work in Tycho's mill on Hven; *trifurcifer* ("thrice-gallows-rogue"), *nebulo* ("scoundrel"), *agyrtae et vespertiliones* ("mountebanks and bats") are Aslakssøn's invective for the cheat, kept in register.
- ***thaleri*** — **thalers** (the silver coin), kept untranslated.
- **Closing formulae.** *T. … desiderij studiosiss. — Cunradus Bergensis* rendered by this chapter's convention; *Vale … Iterum … vale* → "Farewell … Again, fare you …".
- **Calendar.** *23. Octob. Anno 1594* — **23 October 1594**, Old Style (Denmark and the Reformed German territories were still on the Julian calendar in 1594; the writer flags no New-Style equivalent). The dateline date agrees with the catalogue label ("1594. 23. oktober. Siegen"); no discrepancy.
- **What this is.** A newsy paragraph preceding the letter's close — Cort Aslakssøn reporting fresh book-fair intelligence to Tycho: a celestial globe built on Tycho's own corrected star positions has just appeared for sale, admired for its workmanship but criticised as overpriced.
- **Independent confirmation — this is a known, cited episode.** Adam Mosley's *Bearing the Heavens* reports, from Tycho's own correspondence, that "in October of 1594, Aslachus had informed him that the van Langren instruments were available at the book-fairs, to the combined pleasure and dismay of the masses... the dismay by their price: 22 thalers for the celestial globe along with its terrestrial partner" [Mosley, *Bearing the Heavens* (Cambridge, 2007)]. The date (October 1594), the price (22 thalers for the pair), and the informant ("Aslachus" = the Latinized Cort Aslakssøn) all match this letter precisely — this recovered segment is very likely the primary-source basis for Mosley's own footnote. Mosley further suggests this report may have inclined Tycho toward supporting Willem Blaeu's rival globe project instead.
- **The globe-maker identified.** The globes in question are almost certainly the products of the van Langren family workshop (Arnold Florent van Langren and sons), Dutch globe- and instrument-makers who had obtained Tycho's revised star catalogue and were marketing celestial/terrestrial globe pairs at the Frankfurt fair in this period.
- **The correspondent.** Cort Aslakssøn (Latinized Cunradus Aslacus/Aslachus Bergensis, i.e. "of Bergen"; here signing as "Cunradus Bergensis" — see the letter's own signature), a Norwegian-Danish theologian and philosopher who served among Tycho's assistants and later became a professor at Copenhagen [New Dictionary of Scientific Biography — "Tycho's assistant, Cort Aslakssøn"; Zeeberg, *Urania Titani* bibliography].
- **Correction.** Latin corrected from 'apparent' to 'apparenti' per Dreyer, TBOO VII p.367.

translation.warrant:
Collated against **Dreyer, *Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia*** (the edition of record), reading the printed page images. Collated the full letter (Cort Aslaksen/Cunradus Bergensis to Tycho, 23 Oct 1594) against Dreyer TBOO VII pp.366-368 page images, including a second close re-read of p.367. Every proper name (Clavius, Sacrobosco, Craig, Otto/Cunradus Bergensis), number (22 thalers, three miles, year 1594/72), and closing formula matches Dreyer word for word except the single dropped letter noted above. English translation is otherwise accurate and complete throughout, including the postscript.

**1 defect found:**
- **text error** (low). The transcribed original reads the participle/adjective 'apparenti' as the finite verb 'apparent' (dropped final -i); a one-letter corruption relative to Dreyer's printed text. Does not materially mislead the English, which already renders the sense adjectivally. Dreyer prints: *magnitudine primaeva apparenti etc. (TBOO VII p.367, line c. 15)*.

**Repaired.** Collated the single defect against the Dreyer page image (TBOO VII p.367), which clearly reads 'magnitudine primaeva apparenti etc.'. A one-letter correction; the translation was already adjectival and needed no change. No uncertainty remains in this letter.

documents.abstract: Authorizes replacing the Roskilde chapel vaulting with beams and orders the renovation of the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings completed without delay.
documents.incipit: Christian 4..

text.original:
TILL TYGE BRAHE HELLIGE THREE KONGERS CAPELLIS BYGNING WDI ROSCHILDE DOMBKIRCKE AHNRØRENDIS VT SEQUITUR.

Christian 4..

WOR gunst thilfornn. Wiid, eptersom Wij nogen thiid siden forleeden naadigst haffue schreffuit thig thill om Hellige tre kongers capell wdi Roschilde dombkircke, som wor møgit bygfeldig och brøstholden, attu thend med thet allerførste schulle lade igien forferdige och forbygge, och du nu wnderdanigst lader giffue thilkiende, att samme capell beßuerligen kand igien forferdigis och siiden holdis wed heffd och magt enten met thag eller wdi andre maade, med mindre att thend øffuerste huelning motte affthagis och igien leggis med bielcker och loffte. Tha paa thet samme capell med thet første motte igien bliffue forferdigit och siiden theß bedre kunde holdis med thag och anden nottorfft wed heffd och bygning, bede Wij thig och wille, attu lader samme øffuerste huelling affthage och thet igien lader legge met bielcker och loffte paa the beste maade forwarit, och for:ne bygning paa for:ne capell med thet allerførste schee kand lader ferdig giørre.

Ther met etc. Befallendis etc.
Hafniæ 8. 9bris a:o 94.
text.english:
**To Tyge Brahe, concerning the building of the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings in Roskilde Cathedral, as follows.**

Christian IV.

Our favour beforehand. Know that, whereas we did some time ago now graciously write to you concerning the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings in Roskilde Cathedral, which was much in disrepair and decayed, that you should at the very first have it repaired and rebuilt again — and you now most humbly give us to understand that the same chapel can but with difficulty be repaired again and thereafter kept in good repair and condition, whether by roofing or in any other manner, unless the uppermost vaulting were to be taken down and laid again with beams and a ceiling: therefore, so that the same chapel may at the first be repaired again and thereafter be the better kept in repair and building with roofing and other necessaries, we ask of you and will [it], that you have the same uppermost vaulting taken down, and have it laid again with beams and a ceiling secured in the best manner, and have the aforesaid building-work upon the aforesaid chapel made ready at the very first that may be done.

Therewith, etc. Commending [you to God], etc.
At Copenhagen, 8 November, in the year [15]94.

documents.apparatus:
- **Issuer.** **Christian IV of Denmark** (r. 1588–1648), then ruling under the regency council in his minority (he was crowned in his own right in 1596). The letter is a chancery instruction issued in his name.
- **Recipient and capacity.** **Tyge (Tycho) Brahe**, here addressed not as royal astronomer but as a **canon (prebendary) of Roskilde Cathedral**: from 1579 Tycho held the prebend (canonry) of the Chapel of the Three Holy Kings (*Helligtrekongers kapel*), a substantial Roskilde benefice whose income was charged with the upkeep of the chapel fabric. The crown is calling on him to discharge that maintenance obligation.
- **Document type.** A chancery-register entry (Sjællandske Tegnelser XVIII, 368). The **Latin rubric** *"… AHNRØRENDIS **ut sequitur**"* ("concerning … **as follows**") heads the Danish body — a code-switch preserved by this chapter's convention *AHNRØRENDIS* = *anrørendes* ("concerning"); cf. the parallel formula in the 1584 Frederik II compass-letter.
- **Subject.** *Hellige tre kongers capell* = the **Chapel of the Three Holy Kings** (the Magi), a late-Gothic chapel adjoining Roskilde Cathedral, the royal burial church of Denmark. *bygfeldig och brøstholden* — a chancery doublet, "in disrepair and decayed / dilapidated."
- **The structural crux of the order.** The substance turns on a single conditional: *med mindre att thend øffuerste huelning motte affthagis och igien leggis med bielcker och loffte* = "**unless** the uppermost vaulting were to be taken down and laid again with beams and a ceiling." Tycho had reported (the king relays) that the chapel could *not* be durably repaired by re-roofing alone **unless** the top vault were removed and replaced by a flat timber beam-and-board ceiling; the king accordingly **commands** exactly that course. The translation preserves the report → exception → command chain without smoothing it; *huelning/huelling* = "vaulting" (the masonry vault), *bielcker och loffte* = "beams and a [timber] ceiling/loft."
- **Negation / conditional check.** The body contains exactly **one** negating/limiting operator — *med mindre* ("unless"), governing the vaulting clause — and one near-negative adverb, *beßuerligen* ("with difficulty / hardly"); both are reproduced and neither added nor dropped. *enten … eller … wdi andre maade* = "whether [by roofing] … or in any other manner" is a disjunction, not a negation. The directive *bede Wij thig och wille* is a polite-but-binding royal command ("we ask of you and will it"); rendered with its commanding force intact.
- **Orthography (chancery Danish, c. 1594).** *WOR gunst thilfornn* = *Vor gunst tilforn* ("Our favour beforehand," the royal address-formula, this chapter's convention); *Wiid* = *Vid* ("Know"); *eptersom* = *eftersom* ("whereas, inasmuch as"); *attu* = *at du*; *schreffuit* = *skrevet*; *forferdige / forferdigis* = *forfærdige(s)* ("repair, put in order"); *forbygge* = "build up/rebuild"; *wnderdanigst* = *underdanigst* ("most humbly/submissively"); *thilkiende* = *til kende* ("give to understand"); *beßuerligen* = *besværligen* ("with difficulty"); *holdis wed heffd och magt* = *holdes ved hævd og magt* ("kept in repair and condition"); *thag* = *tag* ("roof"); *øffuerste huelning/huelling* = *øverste hvælving* ("uppermost vaulting"); *affthagis / affthage* = *aftages / aftage* ("be taken down / take down"); *bielcker* = *bjælker* ("beams"); *loffte* = *lofte* ("ceiling, loft"); *nottorfft* = *nødtørft* ("necessaries, what is needful"); *for:ne* = *fornævnte* ("aforesaid," the standard chancery abbreviation); *schee kand* = *ske kan* ("may be done").
- **Closing formula.** *Ther met etc. Befallendis etc.* — the abbreviated chancery sign-off; *Befallendis* = *Befalendes* ("Commending [you to God / to God's protection]"), the conventional epistolary commendation, here truncated with *etc.* and so completed in brackets.
- **Calendar / place.** *Hafniae 8. 9bris a:o 94* = "At **Copenhagen** (*Hafniae*), 8 November ( *9bris* = November, the ninth month of the Roman year reckoned from March) [15]94" (O.S.). The Latin place-name and month-abbreviation in an otherwise Danish letter are preserved by this chapter's convention; *9bris* is the standard early-modern shorthand for *Novembris*, not "September." The dateline (8 November 1594) and the catalogue label (8 November 1594, Copenhagen) agree; no discrepancy.

documents.incipit: VORES ganske venlig helßen nu oc allthid forsent med Gud. Gunstige welbiurdige Tyge …

text.original:
COPIE AFF ITT BREFF, SOM BLEFF SCHREFFUEN THILL TYGE BRAHE.

VORES ganske venlig helßen nu oc allthid forsent med Gud. Gunstige welbiurdige Tyge Brahe, nest wores wenlig tacksigelße for all beuiste ære oc gode, giffuer wi eder thillkiende, att oß nu nyligen er forekommen en woris tienere, Lauge vdj Klare mølle, met klagemaall po en aff eders thienere ved naffn Peder, i Hellig 3 kongers mølle, huilched hand schrifftlig vdj dette medfølgendis breff forfatted oc oß offuerantuordet haffuer. So wilde wi, førend wi wores bonde met retten forsuare, lade eder, som wores universitetz gode wen oc fordrer, saadant wide, begierendis ganske gierne her om eders raad oc gode suar, om i selff wille straffe eders thienere, som denne fattige mand i so maade haffuer forwretted, eller wi hannem for saadant skall lade thilltale, huilcked wi dog icke gierne giorde, der som wi wiste, attj derudoffuer skulle lade eder i nogen mode fortørne, men megit heller giør allthid gierne, huer y sit sted, hues eder thill ære, willie oc thieniste kand werre. Dett kiende Gud, huilchen wi will her med haffue eder befaled.

Datum Hafniæ 11. novembris anni 1594.
Rector och mænige professores
academiae Hafniensis.
text.english:
**Copy of a letter that was written to Tyge Brahe.**

Our wholly friendly greeting, now and always, sent in advance with God. Gracious, well-born Tyge Brahe: next after our friendly thanks for all the honour and kindness shown [us], we make known to you that there has lately come before us one of our servants, Lauge at Klare Mill, with a complaint against one of your servants, by name Peder, at the Mill of the Holy Three Kings, which [complaint] he has set down in writing in this accompanying letter and handed over to us. So we wished — before we defend our peasant at law — to let you, as our University's good friend and patron, know of such a matter, asking very gladly herein for your counsel and good answer: whether you yourself will punish your servant, who has in this manner wronged this poor man, or [whether] we shall have him prosecuted for such [conduct] — which, however, we would not gladly do, if we knew that thereby you should in any way be displeased; but [we] much rather do always gladly, each in his own place, whatever may be to your honour, goodwill, and service. That God knows, to whom we will herewith have commended you.

Given at Copenhagen, 11 November in the year 1594.
The Rector and the general body of professors
of the University of Copenhagen.

documents.apparatus:
- **Senders.** The *Rector och maenige professores academiae Hafniensis* = the **Rector and the assembled professors of the University of Copenhagen** (the *Consistorium*, the university's governing senate). *Maenige* (= *menige*) here is the chancery sense "common / general (body)," i.e. the full collegium, not "ordinary." The letter survives as the consistory's own register copy (hence the Danish rubric *COPIE AFF ITT BREFF* heading it).
- **Recipient.** *Tyge Brahe* = **Tycho Brahe**, addressed as the university's *gode wen oc fordrer* ("good friend and patron / promoter"). *Fordrer* (= *forfremmer / befordrer*) carries the sense of one who advances or furthers the institution's interests — rendered "patron."
- **The dispute.** A jurisdictional courtesy over a quarrel between two millers' households: *Lauge vdj Klare mølle* — **Lauge (Laurids) at Klare Mill**, a tenant ("servant"/*bonde*) of the university — has lodged a written complaint against *Peder, i Hellig 3 kongers mølle* — **Peder at the Mill of the Holy Three Kings** (*Hellig 3 kongers mølle*, the mill named for the Magi), one of Tycho's servants. The two mills lay near Copenhagen; the university defers to Tycho on whether he will discipline his own man before it takes the matter to law on its tenant's behalf.
- **Legal sense — handled with care.** The operative offer is a strict either/or framed as a request for Tycho's *raad oc gode suar*: *om i selff wille straffe eders thienere … eller wi hannem … skall lade thilltale* = "**whether** you yourself will punish your servant … **or** [whether] we shall have him prosecuted." The single negation in the courtesy clause is reproduced exactly: *huilcked wi dog **icke** gierne giorde, der som wi wiste, attj derudoffuer skulle lade eder … fortørne* = "which, however, we would **not** gladly do, if we knew that thereby you should be displeased." The clause is a conditional courtesy (the university would rather Tycho act himself than risk offending him by prosecuting his servant); its mood is the past subjunctive/conditional of polite deference (*wilde … giorde … wiste … skulle*), rendered as such without sharpening into an assertion or a threat.
- **Orthography (chancery Danish, c. 1594; German-influenced spelling).** *helßen* = *hilsen* ("greeting"); *forsent* = *forsendt* ("sent ahead/forward"); *welbiurdige* = *velbyrdige* ("well-born," the standard address to nobility); *nest* = *næst* ("next [after]"); *tacksigelße* = *taksigelse* ("thanks"); *beuiste* = *beviste* ("shown, demonstrated"); *thillkiende … giffuer* = *giver til kende* ("make known"); *forekommen* = *forekommet* ("come before [us]"); *klagemaall* = *klagemål* ("complaint, plaint"); *po* = *på* ("against / upon"); *huilched* = *hvilket* ("which"); *medfølgendis* = *medfølgende* ("accompanying, enclosed"); *forfatted* = *forfattet* ("composed, set down"); *offuerantuordet* = *overantvordet* ("handed over, delivered"); *forsuare* = *forsvare* ("defend [at law]"); *fordrer* = *forfremmer / befordrer* ("patron, furtherer"); *begierendis* = *begærende* ("asking, desiring"); *straffe* = "punish"; *forwretted* = *forurettet* ("wronged"); *lade thilltale* = *lade tiltale* ("have prosecuted / proceeded against at law"); *attj* = *at I* ("that you," polite plural); *derudoffuer* = *derudover* ("thereby, on that account"); *i nogen mode* = *i nogen måde* ("in any way"); *fortørne* = *fortørne* ("anger, displease, offend"); *hues* = *hvad/hvis* ("whatever"); *werre* = *være* ("be"); *kiende* = *kende* ("know"); *befaled* = *befalet* ("commended, entrusted").
- **Calendar / place.** *Datum Hafniae 11. novembris anni 1594* — the dateline is in Latin: "**Given at Copenhagen** (*Hafnia*), 11 November in the year 1594" (O.S.; Denmark held to the Julian calendar until 1700). The Latin signature rubric *Rector och maenige professores academiae Hafniensis* code-switches Danish *och maenige* between the Latin *Rector* and *academiae Hafniensis* — the mixed register preserved by this chapter's convention Dateline and catalogue label agree (11 November 1594); no date discrepancy.

documents.incipit: MAGNIFICE d:ne rector och hederlige och høylerde professores vdj Kiøbenhaffns …

text.original:
MAGNIFICO D:NO RECTORJ OC HEDERLIGE OC HØYLERDE PROFESSORIBUS Y KIØBENHAFFNS VNIUERSITET, MINE SYNDERLIGE GODE WENNER, GANDSKE WENLIGENN THILLSCHREFFUIT.

MAGNIFICE d:ne rector och hederlige och høylerde professores vdj Kiøbenhaffns vniversitet, synderlige gode venner. Nest min wenlig tacksigelse for allt beuiist gode, huilchet at forskylle ieg stedße vill findis aff formuenn willig, giffuendis eder der hoes gandske wenligen thilckiende, att eders schriffuelse er mig for nogle dage thillhende kommen, huor vdj y lod mig forstaa om eders thiener vid naffn Lauge møller vdj Klare mølle y Roskiilde, at hand haffuer ført nogenn klagemaall offuer en aff mine thiener vid naffn Peder møller, som ligger til Kongernis cappell sammesteds, huilche hans klagemaall schrifftligen forfattede y mig med samme eders breff tillkickedt haffuer. Derhoes begierendis, att ieg selff samme min thienner wilde straffe, som eders møllere y saa maade haffde foruretted, eller oc lade eder hannom tilltale for retten. Saa kand ieg eder her paa till itt wenligt suar icke forholle, att ieg strax schreff Mogens Bertellßønn, forstander y hospitalidt der j Kiøbenhaffnn, blant andet till, at handt vilde giffue eder paa mine wegne thilckiende, att ieg vilde haffue budt epther min møller och haalde hannom slige klagemaal forre, och høre huad hand der thil haffde at suare, siiden vilde ieg schriffue eder beskeen der paa igien, giffuendis ether selff att betencke, at ieg icke saa strax paa den andens klagemaall och beretning kunde beskylle och straffe min thiener aldelis vhørt oc foruden nøyagtig beuisning offuer hannom, quia (utj scitis) audienda etiam altera pars, et conuincenda antequam puniatur, et procedendum secundum leges receptas, si aliter causa transigi nequeat. Haffuer ieg derforre strax sendt bud epther for:ne min møller, oc ladet lest for hannom eders møllers schrifftlige klagemaall, och giffuid hannem respiit, ocsaa schrifftligen at suare der till, huilcke hans giensuar oc replication ieg sender ether her hoes. Dersom den icke siunis eder at kunde følge skell, och hans gienpart icke will lade sig nøye der met, kand ieg for min personn well liide, att de taler hiinn anden thill med loug och rett, oc at der bliffuer paa deris werne thing legittime citeret oc deciderit vdj sagen, thj y skulle ingelunde giøre mig imod der medt, att y lader forsuare ethers thiener och lader min thiltale, saa wiit y kunde giøre med loug och ret. Jeg will icke heller haffue wiidere der imod att siige eller minn thiener att handtheffue, end som billigt och ret kand verre. Huilchet ieg haffde at giffue ether thill it wenligt suar paa eders schriffuilße vdigien tilckiende. Tackendis ether der hoes gandske gierne, att y wilde lade mig slig leylighedt thillschriffue, før end y secundum strictum jus lod procedere der medt. Och will gierne slig och ald anden beuiist gode och welluillighet hoes eder alle och en huer vdj sehr, saa wiit mig mueligt kand werre, stedße findis gandske goduillig igien att forskylle, y huis maade ieg wedt ether thill aere och gode kandt werre, Och vill her med nu och alltiid haffue ether Gud allermegtigste befahledt.

Datum Vraniborg den 7. dag decembris a:o 94.
Tycho Brahe
manu pp:a.
text.english:
**To the Magnificent Master Rector and the honourable and most learned Professors in the University of Copenhagen, my especial good friends, written quite amicably.**

Magnificent Master Rector and honourable and most learned Professors in the University of Copenhagen, [my] especial good friends. Next [after] my friendly thanks for all kindness shown — which I shall ever be found willing to repay according to my ability — I make known to you herewith, quite amicably, that your letter reached my hands some days ago, in which you gave me to understand concerning your servant by name Lauge Møller [the miller] at Klare Mølle in Roskilde, that he has lodged a certain complaint against one of my servants by name Peder Møller [the miller], who belongs to the Kings' Chapel in that same place, which complaint of his, drawn up in writing, you have sent to me with that same letter of yours. Therewith requesting that I myself would punish that same servant of mine, who had in such manner wronged your miller, or else let you proceed against him at law. So I cannot withhold from you here, by way of a friendly reply, that I straightway wrote, among other matters, to Mogens Bertelsen, the warden at the hospital there in Copenhagen, [asking] that he would on my behalf give you to understand that I would have sent for my miller and put such complaints to him, and hear what he had to answer thereto, [and] thereafter I would write you an account of it in return — giving you yourself to consider that I could not so straightway, on the other [party's] complaint and report, accuse and punish my servant altogether unheard and without sufficient proof against him, *quia (uti scitis) audienda etiam altera pars, et convincenda antequam puniatur, et procedendum secundum leges receptas, si aliter causa transigi nequeat* [because, as you know, the other party too must be heard, and must be convicted before being punished, and one must proceed according to the received laws, if the case cannot be settled otherwise]. I have therefore straightway sent for my aforesaid miller, and had your miller's written complaint read out to him, and given him a respite [in which] to answer it, likewise in writing, which answer and reply of his I send you herewith. If it does not seem to you to be able to satisfy reason, and his counterpart [i.e. the opposing party] will not be content therewith, I can well bear, for my own person, that they address one another at law and in [the] court, and that there be lawful summons issued and the matter decided at their proper venue [thing]; for you shall by no means thereby act against me by your defending your servant and letting [proceedings be brought against] mine, so far as you can do with law and justice. Neither will I have anything further to say against it, nor [seek] to uphold my servant, beyond what may be fair and just. This [is what] I had to give you to understand, by way of a friendly reply to your letter in return. Thanking you withal quite gladly that you were willing to write to me of such occasion, before you proceeded therein *secundum strictum jus* [according to strict law]. And I will gladly be found ever quite well-disposed to repay such, and all other kindness and goodwill, with you all and with each one in particular, so far as may be possible for me, in whatever manner I may be able to [serve] your honour and good. And herewith [I] will now and always have you commended to God Almighty.

Given at Uraniborg, the 7th day of December, in the year [15]94.
Tycho Brahe,
in his own hand.
