documents.abstract: Reports learning from Matthew Roydon that Tycho has moved to Germany, expresses relief at sparing a journey to Denmark, and hopes Tycho may settle in Hesse.
documents.incipit: CUM nuper ex Italia per utramque Germaniam in Angliam venissem, Generose et …

text.original:
MAGNIFICO ET PRÆSTANTISSIMO VIRO DOMINO TYCHONI BRAHE, NOBILI DANO, DOMINO ET FAUTORI SUO OBSERVANDISSIMO. HambURGK.
S. P. D.

CUM nuper ex Italia per utramque Germaniam in Angliam venissem, Generose et præstantissime Domine TYCHO, accepissemque a quodam meo amico Domino MATTHÆO ROYDON, Anglo, Mathematum, ut mihi videbatur, scientissimo, te ex Dania atque Uraniburgo tuo in Germaniam concessisse, atque adeo cum Lare prope Francofurtum ad Mœnum consedisse, gaudebam simul et dolebam. Gaudebam equidem, tum quod meæ, quam alioqui in Daniam ad te suscepturus eram, profectionis compendium facerem; tum etiam quia sperabam te Hassiæ nostræ, cum in proximo eius esses, futurum aliquando inquilinum. Id quod quamvis optare verius, quam sperare potuerim, quippe qui non ignorabam te Daniæ Regnum patriam tuam cum Hassiæ vix commutaturum, nihilominus quo facilius illud crederem, fecit Illustrissimi Principis MAURITIJ Domini mei clementissimini in viros præclaros amor ac munificentia singularis, utpote et quæ tibi cum laudatissimæ memoriæ parente eius diu intercessit familiaritas. Dolebam tamen, quod adversi aliquid in Dania tibi evenisse referrent, tuæque abitionis ex Dania alij alias recensebant causas. Siquidem fuerunt hîc in Anglia, qui tibi cum PETRO SEVERINO Medico litem fuisse nescio quam asseverarent, teque indignitatis adversarij puditum esse, et ideo inde discessisse. Alij Cancellarium Regium feudum aliquod tibi a FRIDERICO II felicis memoriæ concessum, sibi arrogasse, aliaque ad Astronomiæ studium exædificandum adminicula, ab eodem Rege et Regni Proceribus tibi nuncupata, nunc fuisse adempta caussabantur. Hoc verisimilius et mihi et illis visum est, illud de medico plane incredibile. Quotusquisque enim est, qui ignorat, te ex præclarissima prosapia ibidem prognatum, et summæ apud Regem auctoritatis virum tam levi molimine non posse ex patria moveri, ut taceam e patria emoveri. Verum cum in Angliam etiam delatum sit, SEVERINUM illum apud hunc novellum Cancellarium multum valere, adeo ut is ferme totus ab illo dependeat, atque obscurum non sit, Doctorem illum (ut referunt) diutina tui invidia laborasse, fortassis hoc, quod per semetipsum non potuit exequi, per hunc Cancellarium, cui Rex plurimum tribuere dicitur, effectum dedisse.

Hæc, Illustrissime et præstantissime Vir, quamvis ad me nihil spectant, tibi significo, ut etiam externorum de tuo Uraniburgo inopinato discessu iudicium ac sollicitudinem cognoscas. Cæterum paucis abhinc diebus, cum de loco ubi hæreres sollicitus, eos qui ex Germania recens venirent, interrogarem, intelligo te non prope Francofurtum, ut ille existimabat, sed iuxta Hamburgum sedes posuisse. Quare rogatus ab amicis Anglis, qui ad te abituri erant, has ad te depropero, ut cognoscam, an inibi sis mansurus, an vero alio iturus. Qua in re illis rem gratam facturum me non dubito, tibi etiam non iniucundum futurum illud arbitratus sum, si intelligeres etiam in Anglia esse, quos amor tui sollicite tangeret. Quamobrem plane confido, te has meas literas, quamvis ab homine tibi hactenus ignoto et tua familiaritate indigno profectæ sint, æqui bonique consulturum, et ad illas prima data occasione responsurum.

Faxit Deus, ut te aliquando, Vir Præstantissime, in Hassia videamus, exinde enim magnum decus ac nomen accessurum Patriæ meæ existimarem. Sin minus id superis visum sit, efficiam, ut te aliquando, volente Deo, ubicunque Germaniæ etiam sis, invisam, coramque venerer. Vale et meæ impudentiæ ignosce, vir longe præstantissime. Salutem porro accipe a multis in Anglia tibi etiam forte ignotis, nominis tamen tui observantissimis.

LondiniAngliæ, anno 1598, 15. Calend. Februarij.
T. Magnif. addictissimus
HENRICUS ELLENBERGER,
Hassus. M.
text.english:
**To the magnificent and most excellent man, Master Tycho Brahe, noble Dane, his lord and patron most to be esteemed. [At] Hamburg.**
**Sends [him] heartiest greeting.**

When I had lately come out of Italy, through both Germanies [i.e. Upper and Lower Germany], into England, generous and most excellent Master Tycho, and had learned from a certain friend of mine, Master Matthew Roydon, an Englishman most learned (as it seemed to me) in the mathematical sciences, that you had withdrawn from Denmark and from your Uraniborg into Germany, and had even settled with your household near Frankfurt-am-Main, I rejoiced and grieved at once. I rejoiced, to be sure, both because I should thereby spare myself the journey I was otherwise about to undertake into Denmark to you, and also because I hoped that you would one day become a resident of our Hesse, since you would be in its near neighbourhood. And although I could wish for this more truly than I could hope for it — for I was not unaware that you would scarcely exchange the Kingdom of Denmark, your native land, for Hesse — nevertheless what made me believe it the more readily was the singular love and munificence of the Most Illustrious Prince Maurice, my most clement lord, toward distinguished men, and likewise the long-standing familiarity that subsisted between you and his parent of most praised memory. Yet I grieved, because they reported that something adverse had befallen you in Denmark, and different men gave different accounts of your departure from Denmark. For there were here in England those who asserted that you had had some quarrel or other — I know not what — with Peter Severinus the physician, and that you had been ashamed of your adversary's unworthiness, and had therefore departed thence. Others alleged that the Royal Chancellor had arrogated to himself a certain fief granted to you by Frederick II of happy memory, and that the other aids for building up the study of astronomy, assigned to you by that same King and by the Magnates of the Realm, had now been taken away. This seemed the more likely both to me and to them; that other [story] about the physician, plainly incredible. For how few there are who do not know that you, sprung there from a most distinguished lineage and a man of the highest authority with the King, cannot by so slight a contrivance be moved out of your homeland — to say nothing of being driven out of your homeland. But since it has also been brought to England that that Severinus prevails greatly with this new Chancellor, so much so that the latter depends almost wholly upon him, and since it is not obscure that that Doctor (as they report) has long laboured under an envy of you, perhaps he has accomplished, through this Chancellor — to whom the King is said to grant very much — that which he could not carry out by himself.

These things, Most Illustrious and most excellent man, although they in no way concern me, I make known to you, so that you may also learn the judgement and the anxious concern of foreigners regarding your unlooked-for departure from your Uraniborg. For the rest, a few days ago, when, anxious about the place where you might be lodging, I was questioning those who had recently come from Germany, I understand that you have placed your seat not near Frankfurt, as he supposed, but next to Hamburg. Wherefore, being asked by my English friends who were about to set out to you, I hasten this [letter] to you, that I may learn whether you are going to remain there, or rather to go elsewhere. In which matter I doubt not that I shall be doing them a welcome service; and I judged that it would also be not unpleasing to you, were you to understand that there are even in England those whom love of you anxiously touches. For which reason I fully trust that you will take this my letter in good part — although it has proceeded from a man hitherto unknown to you and unworthy of your familiarity — and will answer it at the first opportunity given.

God grant that we may one day see you, Most excellent man, in Hesse; for from that I should reckon that great honour and renown would accrue to my native land. But if it be less than this in the eyes of those above, I shall bring it about that one day, God willing, wherever in Germany you may be, I shall visit you and revere you in person. Farewell, and forgive my boldness, man by far most excellent. Receive, further, a greeting from many in England, perhaps likewise unknown to you, yet most respectful of your name.

At London in England, in the year 1598, on the 15th [day before the] Kalends of February.
Your Magnificence's most devoted,
Henricus Ellenberger,
a Hessian. M[aster].

departures_from_tekstnet.basis: The text printed here descends from one harvest of tekstnet's page and was read against Dreyer's page images in July 2026; a second harvest of the same page is kept beside it. Where the two disagree in a word, both readings are listed: Dreyer's page decides, and unless the audit paragraph names the word, that check has not yet been made for it. documents.apparatus:
- **Correspondent / sender.** The edition header gives the sender as "Heinrich Ellenberger," matching the subscription *Henricus Ellenberger, Hassus. M.* — Henricus (Heinrich) Ellenberger, a **Hessian** (*Hassus*) holding the degree *Magister* (*M.*), writing from London as a young scholar previously unknown to Tycho (he calls himself *homine tibi hactenus ignoto*, "a man hitherto unknown to you"). He presents himself as a subject and well-wisher of the Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel.
- **Recipient / address.** *TYCHONI BRAHE, NOBILI DANO … HambURGK* — Tycho, then in the Hamburg area during the early exile (Wandsbek/Wandsburg, just outside Hamburg, where he had settled in 1597–98 after leaving Hven). The address-line town **Hamburg** corrects the rumour, repeated in the body, that he was near Frankfurt.
- ***S. P. D.*** = *salutem plurimam dicit*, "sends heartiest greeting".
- **Matthew Roydon.** *MATTHAeO ROYDON, Anglo* = **Matthew Roydon** (d. c. 1622), the English poet and member of the Chapman–Raleigh literary-scientific circle, here Ellenberger's informant on Tycho's movements. The Dreyer *Opera Omnia* index (vol. XV) records the name at VIII 21, 462, locating this letter in **Dreyer VIII**.
- **Maurice of Hesse.** *Illustrissimi Principis MAURITIJ Domini mei clementissimi* = **Moritz ("the Learned"), Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel** (r. 1592–1627), Ellenberger's sovereign. *laudatissimae memoriae parente eius* ("his parent of most praised memory") = **Wilhelm IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel** (d. 1592), Tycho's astronomical correspondent — hence the "long-standing familiarity" Ellenberger invokes as grounds for hoping Tycho would settle in Hesse.
- **Peter Severinus.** *PETRO SEVERINO Medico* = **Peder Sørensen / Petrus Severinus** (1542–1602), royal physician (*Medicus*) at the Danish court and a leading Paracelsian. The letter relays — and Ellenberger himself rejects as *plane incredibile* ("plainly incredible") — an English rumour of a *lis* ("quarrel/lawsuit") between Tycho and Severinus; he then floats the alternative that Severinus may have worked against Tycho indirectly, *per hunc Cancellarium*, through the new Chancellor. **No silent sharpening:** the whole Severinus narrative is reported speech, governed by *asseverarent … referrent … ut referunt … fortassis* ("they asserted … they reported … as they report … perhaps"); the hedges are preserved and the rumour is **not** stated as fact.
- **The Chancellor and the fief.** *Cancellarium Regium … feudum … a FRIDERICO II felicis memoriae concessum* — the **Royal Chancellor of Denmark** (*hunc novellum Cancellarium*, "this new Chancellor": **Christian Friis** of Borreby, appointed 1596) is rumoured to have seized a fief granted to Tycho by **Frederick II** ("of happy memory," d. 1588) and to have withdrawn the other supports (*adminicula*) for astronomy assigned by the King and the realm's magnates. This — the loss of Crown patronage under the new regime of Christian IV — Ellenberger and his informants find *verisimilius* ("the more likely") explanation for Tycho's departure.
- ***per utramque Germaniam*** — "through both Germanies," i.e. Upper and Lower Germany (the customary early-modern division), not two distinct countries; rendered literally with the gloss.
- **Persons sending greetings.** *Salutem … a multis in Anglia … nominis tui observantissimis* — anonymous English admirers of Tycho's name; left unnamed in the source.
- **Dateline / calendar.** *LondiniAngliae, anno 1598, 15. Calend. Februarij* = "At London in England, 1598, the 15th day before the Kalends of February." Reckoned inclusively (Kalends of February = 1 February as day 1), *15 Kal. Feb.* = **18 January**. This agrees with the edition's catalogue label "1598. 18. januar." England and Denmark both still kept the **Julian (Old Style)** calendar in 1598; the date is therefore O.S. with no conversion required, and none is applied. *Anno 1598*: by the Julian historical year used here, with no Annunciation-style year-start complication arising in the text.
- ***T. Magnif. addictissimus*** = *Tuae Magnificentiae addictissimus*, "most devoted to Your Magnificence," the subscription formula matched in register to the honorific patterns.
- **Orthography.** Printed *PRAeSTANTISSIMO, MATTHAeO, clementissimini* (a printer's slip for *clementissimi*), *LondiniAngliae* (set without space) are reproduced as printed in the Source block; *clementissimini* is read as *clementissimi* in the translation, the printed form retained above by this chapter's convention

Collated opening/closing lines and every proper name (Matthaeus Roydon, Petrus Severinus, Fridericus II, Mauritius), date (15 Calend. Februarij = 18 Jan), and place (Hamburgk) against the printed text; the transcribed original matches Dreyer word for word and the English renders it accurately throughout. No fabrication, omission, mistranslation, hedge-loss, or text error found.

documents.incipit: OPTIME a te factum, Exoptatissime mi OLIGERE, Cognate et Affinis desideratissime, quod …

text.original:
NOBILISSIMO ET PRÆSTANTISSIMO VIRO, DOMINO OLIGERO ROSÆKRANTZIO DE ROSENHOLM, COGNATO ATQUE AFFINI SUO UNICE DILECTO.

OPTIME a te factum, Exoptatissime mi OLIGERE, Cognate et Affinis desideratissime, quod hisce indicaris et tuæ moræ caussas, ac quod CRAGIUS noster Lubecam confestim transiturus sit, non autem huc, uti sperabamus, venturus. Utrumque vestrum satis excusatum habeo, cum neuter proprij adhuc sit arbitrij. Tu ergastulo et compedibus istis aureis solutus, brevi (quod etiam tibi summopere exopto) tibi ipsi redderis, quo virtuti et studijs, non aulicis indulgeas affanijs. Tumque te promissi fidem liberaturum nullus addubito. Interea quod nonnihil Iutizâris, cum et Iutus sis et in Iutia verseris, nolo Scanico supercilio exactius rimari. Adsis nobis felici sidere, quam primum adfueris, quod etiam, ut mature fiat, et cupio et opto. Iam enim teneris, quia sponte promisisti; nec nippizare licet Iuto in Scanicas transituro Nuptias, gentemque Scanicam constantem et dicti factique memorem æmulaturo: transplantatione quadam, ut fieri solet, quam etiam tibi non ingratam aut infelicem futurum, auguror atque confido.

Si res meæ ullo modo id patientur, dabo operam, ut intra triduum vel quatriduum Lubecæ adsim. Et si communis ille noster, dum per diem unum vel alterum isthic commoror, supervenerit, erit mihi gratissimum, quod ipsius fruar alloquio; utcunque iam antea prævidebam, non licere illi hac transire, vel mea forte de caussa. Quod ex alto rideo. Habeo alias Lubecæ quod agam, satisque necessario. Nam res meæ atque Instrumenta nuper eo appulerunt, quorum quædam huc recepi, quædam isthic in ædibus RANZOVIJ conservantur. Et nemo adest, qui discrete ordinare possit, quæ et quomodo huc vehenda, ita ut nunc discohærentia attulerint aurigæ, non sine meo incommodo et temporis dispendio. Sunt et alia quædam, quæ isthic exequi constitui, quæ etiam volens reieci in tempus tui vel ipsius adventus, ne peregre abessem, aliquo vestrum huc interea superveniente, utque aliquem ex vobis, si non utrunque, eo deducerem, prout res vestræ ferrent, absolutis interea quibusdam ex meis, quæ præ manibus habeo, et indies urgeo. Vellem autem, ut tuum ad nos accessum ita disponeres, quo Lubeca redux hîc domi esse queam, ubi adveneris. Quod etiam ipsas, quas tibi isthic vestri Politici nectunt, moras, sponte effecturas prævideo. Promisit OTTO LINDENOW, se tibi certo traditurum centum illos Ioachimicos, quos mihi pro curru et tribus equis sibi venditis debet, quando me accederes. Rogo itaque, ut ante abitum eos ad te recipias et meo nomine persolutionis des chirographum, tecumque eosdem sumas. Cuperem etiam, mi amantissime Cognate atque Affinis, quod quingentos vel sexcentos Ioachimicos mihi uspiam, sub tuo tamen silenter nomine procurares, quos etiam tecum adferre queas. Restituet eos ad Pascha ESCHILLUS BILLEUS noster, quem satis integræ esse fidei, nosti, ex ijs, quos mihi debet, duobus millibus. Et si opus erit, curia mea Haffniensis interea pignoris loco erit, tam pro summa quam interesse; aut etiam ædes in orientali platea Haffniæ SCHYRMANNI, quas hypothecæ loco habeo pro 1000 Ioachimicis, qui illi ad festum Paschatis resignati sunt iam antea. Pendet vero domus quotannis 80 Ioachimicos, interesse pro millenis paulo maius solito, ut res satis tuta sit. Sin vero commode fieri nequeat, ut hac in parte nostris desiderijs morem geras, nolim te nimium sic occupari, aut ullas adventus tui remoras inde invenire. Caussa, cur id expetam (ut tibi secreto eam communicem, cui his maiora concredo) est, quod post paucas hebdomadas tres ex meis, quos intimos habeo, in diversa Germaniæ loca ablegare decreverim: inter quos etiam filius natu grandior erit, qui nunc apud Administratorem per mensem abest, ipso sic volente. Et quoniam emissarij mei præcipuos Germaniæ Magnates, adeoque ipsum Imperatorem quidam ex ijs meo nomine accessuri sunt, de rebus magni momenti, uti ipsemet facile coniectari possis, isthic acturi, et a me quædam exhibituri, volo ut nihil ijs ad viaticum desit, quo minus omnia decenter et honorifice peragant. Cumque summa hîc sit annonæ caritas, adeo ut triplo ferme pluris veneant, quam Rostochij, ubi 700 thaleros intra anni quadrantem insumpsi, facile æstimare poteris, quantam hîc, cum familia, quæ 24 personas attingit, per dimidium fere annum exposuerim pecuniam. Summa vero illa maior, quam mecum accepi, apud Duces Megapolitanos fœnori exposita est: uti nihil inde repetere liceat ante statutum tempus. Charissime OLIGERE, te in his facturum, quicquid per te præstari queat, omnino mihi persuadeo. Neque quid amplius peto aut desidero. Ego tibi vicissim in quovis officij genere exhibendo quam lubentissime morem geram.

Vale, resalutatus a meis omnibus quam officiosissime.
Dabantur raptim Wandesburgi die 22. Ianuarij, quo ipse Tabellarius tuas attulit, anni 98.
Tuus TYCHO BRAHE,
manu propria.
text.english:
**To the most noble and most excellent gentleman, Master Holger Rosenkrantz of Rosenholm, his kinsman and relative-by-marriage, uniquely beloved.**

You did most kindly, my much-longed-for Holger, dearest of kinsmen and relatives, in informing me by these [lines] both of the reasons for your delay, and that our friend Cragius is to pass on directly to Lübeck and is not, as we had hoped, going to come here. I hold each of you sufficiently excused, since neither of you is as yet his own master. You, once released from that workhouse and those golden fetters, will shortly (which indeed I most earnestly wish for you) be restored to your own self, so that you may give yourself to virtue and to studies, not to courtly vexations. And I have no doubt that you will then redeem the pledge of your promise. Meanwhile, that you play the Jutlander somewhat — since you are both a Jute and dwelling in Jutland — I will not scrutinise too exactly with a Scanian's raised eyebrow. Be present with us under a happy star as soon as you can be present, which I both desire and wish to come about in good time. For you are now bound, since you promised of your own accord; nor is it permitted to a Jute, who is about to cross over into a Scanian marriage and to emulate the Scanian people — steadfast and mindful of word and deed — to *nippizare* [shilly-shally / haggle]: by a certain transplanting, as is wont to happen, which I forecast and trust will prove neither unwelcome nor unhappy for you.

If my affairs will in any way allow it, I shall take pains to be at Lübeck within three or four days. And if that common [friend] of ours should turn up while I tarry there a day or two, it will be most welcome to me, that I may enjoy his conversation; although I already foresaw beforehand that he is not permitted to pass this way, perhaps even on my account. At which I laugh from on high. I have, besides, business to do at Lübeck, and that necessarily enough. For my goods and instruments have lately put in there, some of which I have received here, while some are kept there in Rantzau's house. And there is no one at hand who can judiciously arrange what is to be carried here and in what manner, with the result that the carters have now brought [things] disjointedly, not without inconvenience to me and waste of time. There are also certain other matters which I have resolved to carry out there, which too I have willingly put off to the time of your coming, or his, lest I be away abroad while one of you turned up here in the meantime — and so that I might conduct one of you, if not both, thither, as your affairs should allow, certain of my own [tasks] being finished meanwhile, which I have in hand and press on with daily. But I should wish you to so arrange your coming to us that, on my return from Lübeck, I may be here at home when you arrive. Which I also foresee that the very delays your politicians are weaving for you there will of themselves bring about. Otto Lindenow has promised that he will certainly deliver to you those hundred Joachimsthaler which he owes me for a carriage and three horses sold to him, when you come to me. I ask, therefore, that before [your] departure you take them in [hand] and, in my name, give a written acknowledgment of payment, and bring the same with you. I could also wish, my most loving kinsman and relative, that you would procure for me somewhere five or six hundred Joachimsthaler — under your own name, though, and quietly — which you might likewise bring with you. Our [friend] Eskil Bille will repay them by Easter — a man, as you know, of fully sound credit — out of the two thousand which he owes me. And if there be need, my Copenhagen courtyard-house [*curia*] will meanwhile stand in the place of a pledge, both for the principal and for the interest; or else Schyrmann's house in the eastern street of Copenhagen, which I hold by way of mortgage for 1,000 Joachimsthaler, that were already before this assigned over to him at the feast of Easter. The house in fact pays 80 Joachimsthaler yearly, the interest on the thousand being a little more than the usual, so that the matter is secure enough. But if it cannot conveniently be done that you gratify our wishes in this part, I should not want you to be too much taken up in this way, or to find therein any delays to your coming. The reason why I seek it (that I may share it with you in secret, to whom I entrust greater things than these) is that, after a few weeks, I have resolved to dispatch three of my [men], whom I count my intimates, to different places in Germany — among whom my elder-born son too will be, who is now away for a month at the Administrator's [court], he himself so willing it. And since my emissaries are to approach the chief magnates of Germany, and indeed the Emperor himself — certain of them in my name — there to treat of matters of great moment, as you may yourself easily conjecture, and to present certain things from me, I want nothing of their travelling-money to be lacking, that they may carry everything out fittingly and honourably. And since the dearth of provisions here is so great that they sell for nearly three times more than at Rostock — where I spent 700 thalers within a quarter of a year — you will easily be able to reckon how much money I have laid out here, with a household that reaches 24 persons, over nearly half a year. But that larger sum which I brought with me has been put out at interest with the Dukes of Mecklenburg, so that nothing may be recalled from there before the appointed time. Dearest Holger, I am wholly persuaded that you will do in these matters whatever can be performed by you. Nor do I ask or desire anything further. I, in my turn, will most gladly gratify you in showing every kind of good office.

Farewell, greeted again in return by all my [household] most dutifully.
Given hastily at Wandsbek on the 22nd day of January — the very [day] on which the courier brought your [letter] — of the year [15]98.
Your TYCHO BRAHE,
with his own hand.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe** (1546–1601), writing from his self-imposed exile at **Wandsbek** (*Wandesburgum*), the castle near Hamburg belonging to Heinrich Rantzau, where Tycho settled in 1597 after quitting Denmark. This is the period of the search for a new patron that culminated in the move to the Imperial court of Rudolf II; the *Astronomiae instauratae mechanica* (Wandsbek, 1598) was being readied for the press, its foreword to Rudolf II dated 31 December 1597 (Christianson, *On Tycho's Island*).
- **Recipient.** *Oligerus Rosaekrantzius de Rosenholm* = **Holger Rosenkrantz** (1574–1642), "the Learned," Danish nobleman of Rosenholm, later a councillor of state; here Tycho's young kinsman, addressed throughout as *cognatus atque affinis* (kinsman by blood and by marriage). He was about to marry into a Scanian family (see the Jute/Scanian banter), and would assist Tycho at the Wandsbek lunar-eclipse observation later in 1598.
- ***cognatus atque affinis*** — "kinsman and relative-by-marriage": *cognatus* = a blood relation, *affinis* = a connection by marriage; both kept distinct.
- ***Cragius noster*** — "our Cragius": most probably **Niels Krag** (Nicolaus Cragius, 1550–1602), the Danish humanist historian and diplomat; the identification is not in the letter itself and is flagged as editorial.
- ***communis ille noster*** — "that common [friend] of ours," left unnamed in the source (Tycho is being discreet); rendered with the bracketed gloss, the referent not asserted.
- ***ergastulo et compedibus istis aureis*** — "that workhouse and those golden fetters": a metaphor (cf. the 1571 Wolf letter's *ergastulum*) for Rosenkrantz's court service, the "golden fetters" being the gilded constraint of attendance at court. *ergastulum* = a slaves' workhouse/prison.
- ***aulicis affanijs*** — "courtly vexations / fuss"; *affania(e)* is a late/rare word for trifling annoyances or idle talk.
- **Jute / Scanian banter.** *Iutizâris … Iutus … in Iutia … Scanico supercilio … Iuto … in Scanicas … Nuptias … gentemque Scanicam … nippizare* — a sustained play on regional identity: Rosenkrantz is a **Jute** (from Jutland) about to cross over into a **Scanian** marriage (Scania, then Danish, was Tycho's own home region). Tycho teases that Rosenkrantz "plays the Jutlander" (*Iutizaris*, a coinage = behaves Jute-fashion, i.e. dawdles/temporises), which he, with a "Scanian's raised eyebrow" (*Scanico supercilio*), will overlook.
- **Crux: *nippizare*.** "nor is it permitted to a Jute … to *nippizare*." *nippizare* is a rare/coined verb of uncertain sense — most plausibly "to be stingy / haggle / shilly-shally," continuing the regional jest (a Jute must not haggle or hang back when crossing into a Scanian marriage). The Source block keeps the printed form; the translation keeps *nippizare* italicised with a bracketed gloss [shilly-shally / haggle] rather than committing to one sense. **Flagged, not smoothed.**
- ***in aedibus Ranzovij*** — "in Rantzau's house": **Heinrich Rantzau** (Henrik Rantzau, 1526–1598), the Holstein statesman and humanist, Tycho's host-patron at Wandsbek; his town establishment at Lübeck stored part of Tycho's instruments in transit.
- ***Ioachimici*** — **Joachimsthaler** (the silver *thaler* struck at Joachimsthal/Jáchymov); rendered "Joachimsthaler." Distinguished in the same letter from plain *thaleri* ("thalers," used of the Rostock expenditure).
- ***Otto Lindenow*** — **Otte Lindenow**, a Danish nobleman, Tycho's debtor for "a carriage and three horses."
- ***chirographum*** — a hand-written bond / acknowledgment of payment (a receipt under one's own hand); kept as "written acknowledgment."
- ***Eschillus Billeus noster*** — **Eskil Bille**, a Danish nobleman, Tycho's debtor "for two thousand [Joachimsthaler]," vouched for as a man of sound credit (*integrae fidei*).
- ***curia mea Haffniensis*** — "my Copenhagen courtyard-house": *curia* here = a town manor/courtyard property (*Hafnia* = **Copenhagen**, this chapter's convention), offered as security (*pignoris loco*, "in the place of a pledge").
- ***aedes … Schyrmanni … hypothecae loco … ad festum Paschatis resignati*** — Schyrmann's house in the "eastern street" of Copenhagen, held by Tycho *by way of mortgage* (*hypotheca*) for 1,000 Joachimsthaler, "assigned over" (*resignati*) at Easter. The financial mechanics (annual yield of 80 Joachimsthaler; interest "a little more than usual") are rendered as written; *Schyrmann* unidentified beyond the name.
- ***filius natu grandior … apud Administratorem*** — Tycho's **elder son** (Tyge Brahe the Younger, b. 1581), away "at the Administrator's" — i.e. at the court of an *Administrator* (the holder of a secularised prince-bishopric or regency); the specific office is not named in the letter, so left as "the Administrator's [court]." **Flagged** as under-determined.
- ***emissarij … praecipuos Germaniae Magnates, adeoque ipsum Imperatorem … accessuri … de rebus magni momenti*** — Tycho's confidential disclosure that he is about to send intimates (including his elder son) to the leading **magnates of Germany** and to **the Emperor himself** (Rudolf II) "on matters of great moment": the patronage embassy that preceded Tycho's move to the Imperial court. The phrase *ut tibi secreto eam communicem* ("that I may share it with you in secret") marks the confidence; preserved.
- ***Duces Megapolitanos*** — the **Dukes of Mecklenburg** (*Megapolis* = Mecklenburg, a learned Graecism on *megalē polis* ≈ "great town", folk-etymology of Mecklenburg); with whom Tycho's reserve capital was "put out at interest" (*foenori exposita*).
- ***Rostochium*** — **Rostock**; the comparison point for living costs ("700 thalers within a quarter of a year").
- **Epistolary formulae.** Salutation in the dative-of-address (titulature), by this chapter's convention *Vale* = "Farewell." *resalutatus a meis omnibus* = "greeted again in return by all my [household]." *manu propria* = "with his own hand" (autograph subscription).
- **Dateline / calendar.** *Dabantur raptim Wandesburgi die 22. Ianuarij … anni 98* = "Given hastily at **Wandsbek**, 22 January … of the year [15]98" (**O.S.** — Denmark and the Lutheran north kept the Julian calendar until 1700). The edition *label* ("1598. 22. januar. Wandsburg") agrees with the dateline; no discrepancy. The clause *quo ipse Tabellarius tuas attulit* ("the very day on which the courier brought your [letter]") dates Tycho's reply to the day of receipt; preserved.

documents.incipit: VNSERN gunstigen gruss zu uor. Ehrenuehster besonder lieber. Es hatt der ehrenuehste …

text.original:
AN DEN HOFMEISTER VNDT CANTZLER.

VNSERN gunstigen gruss zu uor. Ehrenuehster besonder lieber. Es hatt der ehrenuehste Vnser lieber besonder Tycho Brahe Vns vmb intercession an die königliche w: zue Dennemarcken, Vnsern freundtlichen hertzvielgeliebten hern vattern vndt sohn, wie auch an Vnsere freundtliche vielgeliebte tochter die könnigin, in seinen sachen vndterthenigst angehaltten. Weil Wir ihm denn füglich solches nicht haben abschlagen können, so haben Wir ihm wie beyliegendt an jhr k: w: allerseits geschrieben, vndt weil Wir wissen, daß jhr viel gutes bey den sachen ttuen könnet, so begehren Wir gantz gnedigst, ihr wollet so viel sich jmmer fugen wil deß beste vorwenden helfen, damitt er vonn jhr k:w: mitt guetter resolution möge versehen werden, wie Wir denn inn gnaden nicht zweiffeltt, jhr werdet Vnsern halben den vertrawen nach an euch nichts erwinden laßen. Deßselbe wollen Wir mitt allen gnedigen vndt gönstigen willen, darmitt Wir euch ohne deß gewogen, hienwiederumb verschulden.

Datum Cölln an der Sprew, den 25. januarij anno 98.
text.english:
**To the Steward and the Chancellor.**

Our gracious greeting beforehand. Honourable [and] particularly dear [one]. The honourable, Our dear and particular Tycho Brahe has most humbly applied to Us for [Our] intercession with the Royal Majesties of Denmark — Our friendly, heartily-beloved lord father and son, and likewise with Our friendly, dearly-beloved daughter the Queen — in his affairs. Since We could not in fairness refuse him this, We have accordingly written, as enclosed, to their Royal Majesties one and all; and since We know that you can do much good in these affairs, We most graciously desire that you, so far as ever may be fitting, help to put forward [his] best [interest], so that he may be furnished by their Royal Majesties with a good resolution — even as We do not, in [Our] grace, doubt that you, for Our sake [and] in keeping with the trust [reposed in you], will let nothing be wanting on your part. The same We will requite again with all the gracious and favourable goodwill wherewith We are in any case well-disposed toward you.

Given at Cölln an der Spree, the 25th of January, in the year [15]98.

documents.apparatus:
- **Issuer.** *Joachim Friedrich* = **Joachim Friedrich, Elector of Brandenburg** (1546–1608; Elector from 1598, in the year of this letter). The royal "We" (*Wir / Vns*) and the gracious-superior register (*gnedigst, in gnaden*) are those of a reigning prince addressing officers of another crown. Title rendered "Elector of Brandenburg" in the header; the text itself names no title, opening directly with the address-line.
- **Addressees.** *Der Hofmeister vndt Cantzler* = the two senior officers of the Danish crown: the **Hofmeister** (Rigshofmester / Lord High Steward), at this date **Christoffer Valkendorf** (1525–1601), and the **Cantzler** (Chancellor), **Christian Friis af Borreby** (1556–1616). The edition names both as recipients; the letter is a single missive addressed jointly to the two offices (the singular *Ehrenuehster besonder lieber*, "particularly dear one," is the chancery address-formula and does not by itself decide whether it was issued in one copy or two — flagged, not resolved). The surviving witness is a later copy in Langebek's *Diplomatarium*.
- **Subject — Tycho.** *Tycho Brahe … vmb intercession … in seinen sachen vndterthenigst angehaltten* — Tycho, by then estranged from the Danish court and on the point of leaving Denmark (he quit Hven in 1597 and was abroad — Rostock, then Wandsbek — in 1597–98), had asked the Elector to intercede with the Danish crown "in his affairs." This is one of the intercession letters Tycho solicited from German princes during his self-imposed exile, seeking a favourable settlement (restoration of favour / his estates / pension) before his eventual move to the Imperial court.
- **The kinship formulae.** *die königliche w: zue Dennemarcken … Vnsern freundtlichen hertzvielgeliebten hern vattern vndt sohn … Vnsere freundtliche vielgeliebte tochter die könnigin* — "the Royal Majesties of Denmark … Our friendly, heartily-beloved lord father and son … Our dearly-beloved daughter the Queen." These are conventional princely courtesy-kinship terms ("father," "son," "daughter") expressing the dynastic web binding the Brandenburg and Danish-Oldenburg houses, **not** literal immediate-family relations; the plural *die königliche w: … allerseits* ("their Royal Majesties … one and all") shows the addressees are collective. The translation keeps the courtesy terms as written and flags their conventional force here rather than asserting a specific genealogy. *königliche w:* = *königliche Würden* (Royal Majesties / Royal Dignities), the abbreviation expanded in sense.
- **Latin / chancery code-switches.** *intercession* (intercession, mediation), *resolution* (a formal resolution / decision — *mitt guetter resolution möge versehen werden*, "be furnished with a good resolution"), and *Datum* (Given) are Latin code-switches embedded in the German, by this chapter's convention; kept and glossed.
- **Negations (counted, per the legal-force rule).** Three negations stand in the source and exactly three in the translation: (1) *nicht … abschlagen können* — "could not refuse"; (2) *nicht zweiffeltt* — "do not doubt"; (3) *nichts erwinden laßen* — "let nothing be wanting." None reverses a command; all are courtesy-register assurances. The clause *jhr werdet … an euch nichts erwinden laßen* is the standard chancery litotes "you will let nothing be lacking on your part" (i.e. you will do your utmost) — rendered as such, not sharpened.
- **Orthography (chancery German, c. 1598).** *zu uor* = *zuvor*; *Ehrenuehster* = *Ehrenfester* ("Honourable," the formal address-epithet); *besonder lieber* = *besonderer lieber*; *vmb* = *um*; *ttuen* = *tun* (with the scribe's doubled initial); *vorwenden* = *vorwenden* ("put forward, employ on [someone's] behalf"); *fugen* = *fügen* ("be fitting"); *hienwiederumb* = *hinwiederum* ("in return"); *verschulden* = *verschulden* (here "requite, deserve [your goodwill] in return," not "incur guilt/debt"); *gewogen* = "well-disposed." *Sprew* / *Spree*; *Cölln an der Spree* is the Berlin sister-town and seat of the Brandenburg residence (today part of Berlin).
- **Calendar / place.** *Datum Cölln an der Sprew, den 25. januarij anno 98* = "Given at **Cölln an der Spree**, 25 January [15]98." Brandenburg, as a Lutheran territory, kept the **Julian calendar (Old Style)** in 1598 (the Protestant estates of the Empire did not adopt the Gregorian reform until 1700); the date is therefore O.S., consistent with the Danish addressees, who likewise used Old Style. No in-letter date discrepancy. The edition *label* gives the same date (25 January 1598, Cölln an der Spree); header and label agree.

text.original:
EXEMPLUM LITERARUM ELECTORIS
BRANDENBURGENSIS AD REGEM
DANIÆ.

DURCHLEUCHTIGER könig, E:K:W: seindt Vnsere freundtwillige dienste vndt waß Wir
der vatterlichen verwandtnuß nach viel mehr ehr, liebs vndt guts vermögen,
allzeit zuuor. Freundtlicher hertzvielgeliebter herr vetter vndt sohn, E:K:W:
geruhen freundtlich, jhr den einschluß vorlesßen zue laßen, wes gestalt Wir von
den ehrenuehsten Vnsern lieben besondern Tycho Brahen vmb intercessionschrifft
an E:K:W: bittlich angelanget vndt ersuchet worden.

Ob Wir nuhn wohl nicht gemeinet E:K:W: mitt etwas, so derselben zue
wieder sein möchte, verdrisßlich zue sein, dahero Wir denn auch fest hierundter
(sintemahln was ausser seinen Tycho Brahens bericht, wie es vmb seine sachen
gewandt, eigenlich nichts bewust, zue dem auch E:K:W: Vns dermasßen bekandt, das
sie auch ohne vnsere vorschrifft einen jeden was billich wiederfahren zue lasßen
geneigt) bedenckens getragen, dannoch aber vndt weil Wir sein suchen, bitten
vndt erbietten gleichwohl nicht vnbillich vermergken, zue dem auch bey E:K:W:
nicht vernommen, das sie ihme mitt vngnaden gewogen sein soltten, so haben Wir
endtlich seinen vndterthenigen suchen statt geben, vndt die gebetene
vorbittschrifft fuglich nicht verweigern mögen. Ersuchen dem nach E:K:W: hier
mitt ganz dienst- vndt freundtlich bittendt, E:K:W: solches nicht allein von Vnß
nicht vbel aufnehmen, sondern auch sein Tycho Brahens wegkziehen auß Dennemargk
im keinen vngnaden vermergken vndt sein gnedigster
könig vndt herr sein vndt bleiben, auch nach dero gelegenheitt die Verordnung
thuen wollen, daß ihme, seinen ferner vndterthenigst suchen vndt bitten nach,
sowoll der hienwegnehmung seiner vff der insul zue Vranenburgk noch habenden
jnstrument vndt waß ihm aldar mehr zueständig sein möchte, vndt dann erstettung
seines angezogenen Verlages, als auch der perpetuirten fundation halben zue
nutzlicher werkstellung deß astronomischen studij, gewelfahrt, vndt er also
hierinn, inn einem vndt dem andern, so viel muglich dieser Vnser, ihm zwar zue
gnaden aber E:K:W: gar nicht zue einigen vorgrifft, gemeinten intercession
seiner geschöpften hofnung nach empfindtlich geniessen möge. Das wirdt
er sich vngezweiffelt nach höchsten seinem vermögen zuuordienen bevleisßigen,
vndt Wir seindt E:K:W: zu allen behaglichen freundtwilligen diensten jederzeitt
geflisßen.

Datum Cölln an der Sprew, den 25. januarij anno 98.

V:G:g: Jochim Friederich
churfurst zue Brandenburgk.

Mutatis mutandis an die königin, dasß jhr k: w: bey derselben herrn gemahl
deß beste inn gueten andtwort verwenden wolle.
text.english:
**Copy of a letter of the Elector of Brandenburg to the King of Denmark.**

Most Serene King, [be assured of] our amicable services beforehand at all times, and of whatever, by reason of our paternal kinship, we are able [to do] far more in honour, love, and good. Most amicable, dearly-beloved lord cousin and son: may it please Your Royal Majesty graciously to have the enclosure read out to her, [as to] in what manner we have been petitioned and entreated by the honourable, our trusty and well-beloved Tycho Brahe for a letter of intercession to Your Royal Majesty.

Now, although we were indeed not minded to be irksome to Your Royal Majesty with anything that might be contrary to her — wherefore we also bore firm hesitation in this matter (inasmuch as, apart from his, Tycho Brahe's, [own] report of how things stand with his affairs, [we] are in truth aware of nothing; and besides, Your Royal Majesty is so [well] known to us that she is inclined, even without our recommendation, to let everyone have done to him what is fair) — yet nonetheless, and because we for our part do not deem his application, request, and offer unfair, and because we have moreover not heard from Your Royal Majesty that she should be disposed toward him with disfavour, we have at length given place to his humble application, and could not in propriety refuse the requested letter of intercession. Accordingly we entreat Your Royal Majesty herewith, requesting in all dutiful and amicable wise, that Your Royal Majesty not only would not take such a thing ill of us, but would also not regard his — Tycho Brahe's — departure out of Denmark with any disfavour, and would be and remain his most gracious king and lord, and would also, as her opportunity allows, make the ordinance that he — according to his further most-humble application and request — may, both as regards the removal of his instruments still remaining on the island at Uraniborg, and whatever else there might further belong to him there, and then [as regards] the reimbursement of his alleged outlay [Verlag], as well as on account of the perpetuated foundation for the profitable carrying-out of the astronomical study, be furthered; and that he thus herein, in the one matter and the other, may, so far as possible, palpably enjoy, according to the hope he has conceived, this our intended intercession — [made] indeed to his favour, but in no way to any prejudice of Your Royal Majesty. This he will undoubtedly strive to deserve to the utmost of his ability; and we are at all times zealous for Your Royal Majesty in every agreeable and amicable service.

Given at Cölln an der Spree, the 25th of January, in the year [15]98.
By the grace of God, Joachim Friedrich,
Elector of Brandenburg. With the necessary changes, [the like was written] to the Queen: that Her Royal Highness would be pleased to employ her best [endeavour] with her lord consort toward a favourable answer.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Joachim Friedrich, Elector (Kurfürst) of Brandenburg** (1546–1608; Elector from January 1598). He addresses the young Danish king as *herr vetter vndt sohn* ("lord cousin and son"), the standard inter-dynastic courtesy register; the *vatterlichen verwandtnuß* ("paternal kinship") reflects the Brandenburg–Denmark marriage ties (Joachim Friedrich's family was allied to the Danish house; Christian IV's sister Anna would later marry into the line).
- **Recipient.** **Christian IV of Denmark** (r. 1588–1648, ruling in his own right from 1596). The accompanying same-day letter from the same Elector to the Danish *Hofmeister* and *Kanzler* (Christoffer Valkendorf and Christian Friis) survives in the same correspondence series; this is the parallel petition to the king himself.
- **Document type & rubric.** The Latin heading *EXEMPLUM LITERARUM ELECTORIS BRANDENBURGENSIS AD REGEM DANIAe* ("Copy of a letter of the Elector of Brandenburg to the King of Denmark") marks the text as a register/file copy (the witness is Langebek's *Diplomatarium*, an 18th-c. transcription, hence "Afskrift"). The code-switch into Latin for the rubric over a German body is preserved by this chapter's convention
- **Historical context.** Tycho left Denmark in the spring of 1597 and by January 1598 was at Wandsbek (in the territory of Heinrich Rantzau), where he was completing the *Astronomiae instauratae mechanica* (1598). This letter is an intercession seeking three concessions from the crown: (1) the **removal of the instruments still on Hven** (*hienwegnehmung seiner vff der insul zue Vranenburgk noch habenden jnstrument*); (2) the **reimbursement of his outlay** (*erstettung seines angezogenen Verlages*); and (3) the honouring of **the perpetuated foundation** for his astronomical work (*perpetuirten fundation … deß astronomischen studij*).
- **Honorific abbreviations.** *E:K:W:* = *Eurer Königlichen Würden* ("Your Royal Majesty / Dignity"), the courtesy title used throughout; rendered "Your Royal Majesty." *V:G:g:* = *Von Gottes gnaden* ("By the grace of God"), the standard subscription style for a sovereign prince. The princely *Wir* and the address forms are kept in the elevated register.
- **Negations (flagged for legal/courtesy force).** The central period turns on a chain of deliberate litotes, all reproduced exactly: *nicht gemeinet … verdrisßlich zue sein* ("not minded to be irksome"); *nicht vnbillich vermergken* ("do not deem unfair"); *nicht vernommen, das sie ihme mitt vngnaden gewogen* ("not heard that she should be disposed toward him with disfavour"); *fuglich nicht verweigern mögen* ("could not in propriety refuse"); and the paired *nicht allein … nicht vbel aufnehmen, sondern auch … im keinen vngnaden vermergken* ("not only would not take it ill … but would also not regard [it] with any disfavour"). Six distinct negating turns in all; none added, none dropped. The closing qualifier *ihm zwar zue gnaden aber E:K:W: gar nicht zue einigen vorgrifft* ("indeed to his favour, but in no way to any prejudice of Your Royal Majesty") is the diplomatic safeguard and is rendered with its full hedge.
- **Lexical notes.**
 - *intercessionschrifft / vorbittschrifft* — "letter of intercession" (a formal letter of recommendation on a third party's behalf); kept consistent with the rubric and body.
 - *angezogenen Verlages* — *Verlag* here = "outlay, expenditure advanced" (the money Tycho laid out, not the modern "publishing house"); *angezogen* = "alleged, cited, brought forward." Rendered "his alleged outlay [Verlag]," with the German kept in brackets, since the elector reports Tycho's claim without himself vouching for the amount (he has just said he knows the affair only *ausser seinen Tycho Brahens bericht* — "apart from Tycho Brahe's [own] report").
 - *perpetuirten fundation* — "the perpetuated foundation": the endowment/foundation (Latinate *fundatio*) for the support of Tycho's astronomical studies, which Tycho sought to have continued ("perpetuated"); rendered literally, the institutional sense flagged rather than narrowed.
 - *werkstellung* (= *Werkstelligung*) — "carrying-out, execution"; here *zue nutzlicher werkstellung deß astronomischen studij* = "for the profitable carrying-out of the astronomical study."
 - *empfindtlich geniessen* — "palpably / perceptibly enjoy [the benefit of]," i.e. that Tycho actually feel the good effect of the intercession; rendered "palpably enjoy."
 - *geruhen* — "may it please / deign"; *einschluß* — "the enclosure" (the appended document Tycho's case rested on).
- **Orthography (chancery German, 1598).** Characteristic *v/u* and *w* spellings and chancery doublings: *vndt* = *und*; *zuuor* = *zuvor*; *vermergken* = *vermerken*; *vnbillich* = *unbillig*; *vff* = *auf*; *jnstrument* = *Instrument(e)*; *wegkziehen* = *wegziehen*; *hienwegnehmung* = *Hinwegnehmung*; *erstettung* = *Erstattung*; *vorgrifff* (*vorgrifft*) = *Vorgriff* ("prejudice, encroachment"); *Sprew* = *Spree*. *Cölln an der Spree* is the twin town of Berlin (the electoral residence), not Cologne on the Rhine.
- **Calendar / place.** *Datum Cölln an der Sprew, den 25. januarij anno 98* = "Given at Cölln an der Spree, 25 January [15]98." Denmark and Brandenburg both kept the **Julian calendar (Old Style)** at this date, so the dateline is O.S.; no conversion is made. The header date matches the dateline as written; the edition *label* ("1598. 25. januar. Cölln an der Spree") agrees, so no discrepancy.
- **A parallel letter to the Queen.** The docket confirms that a second, adapted copy of this same intercession ('mutatis mutandis') was sent to 'the Queen' — Anne Catherine of Brandenburg, the Elector's own daughter, married to King Christian IV at Haderslevhus Castle in November 1597 — asking her to use her influence with 'her lord consort' (Christian IV) toward a favourable reply to Tycho's petition.
- **Corroboration.** John Robert Christianson, *Tycho Brahe and the Measure of the Heavens* (2020), records that after the Brandenburg-Danish wedding at Haderslevhus, Elector Joachim Friedrich and Electress Catherine met Tycho, received him warmly, and 'agreed to write to Queen Anna Catherine and King Christian IV on his behalf' — independently confirming the two-track intercession (King and Queen) this recovered docket describes.

documents.incipit: DURCHLEUCHTIGER könnig, Euer K: W: sey Vnser diensthaffter ehrengruss vndt was Wir der …

text.original:
DEM DURCHLEUCHTIGEN FÜRSTEN, HERN CHRISTIANO DEM VIERDTEN, ZU DENNEMARGKEN, NORDWEGEN, DER WENDEN VNDT GOTHEN KÖNNIGE, HERTZOGEN ZU SCHLESSWIGK, HOLSTEIN, DER STORMAREN VNDT DITMARSCHEN, GRAFFEN ZUE OLDENBURG VNDT DELMENHORST, UNSERM FREUNDTLICHEM VIELGELIEBTEN HERRN SOHN, ZU JHR: K: W: HÄNDEN.

DURCHLEUCHTIGER könnig, Euer K: W: sey Vnser diensthaffter ehrengruss vndt was Wir der mutterlichen vervandtnuss nach viel mehr leibs vnd guts vermugen, zuuohrn. Freundtlicher hochvielgeliebter herr vetter, sohn, vndt bruder, Wir wollen zu dem Allmechtigen vngezweiffelt hoffen, das E:K:W: sambt dero vielgeliebter gemahlin, Vnser hertzlieben tochter, noch bey guetter leibsgesundheitt vndt allem königlichen Wohlstände gnediglich erhalten werden, wie Wir denn derselben königlichen w:, vndt J:L: solches auß mütterlichen hertzen wünschen thuen.

Vnsern freundtlichen hertzvielgeliebten herrn gemahl vnd kinder wollen E:K:W: noch bey zimblicher leibs vermögenheitt vndt zuestande wissen, allein das wass fur Vnsere person etzliche tage hero vonn dem husten vndt anderer zuefelligen schwacheitt dermassen zugesetzt, daß Wir auch Vnsern gnedigen geliebten herrn vattern, hochlöblicher chriftmilder gedechtnus, wie gerne Wir auch gewolt hetten, die letzte ehr bey dero churfurstl: begrebnus nicht haben leisten können; haben aber dennoch dem Allmechtigen nuhn mehr fur zimbliche besßerung zuedancken, dessen barmhertzigkeit vns sambtlich darbey gnediglich lang erhalten wolle. Es werden auch E:K:W: auß Vnsers hertzlieben hern gemahls an E:K:W: gethanes vorbittlich schreiben, sie haben lassen vndterthenigst vortragen, welcher gestelt dero 1: vmb gnedigste vorschrifft an E:K:W: voer dem erenuehsten Vnserm lieben besonderen Tycho Brahen vndterthenigst angelangt; wann er denn dergleichen auch Vns vmb vorbittschrifft ersucht, vndt Wir niemals vermerckt, daß E:K:W: ihme mitt vngnaden gewogen, auch seine bitt nicht vnzimblich erachten, so gelanget hiemit an E:K:W: Vnser freundtliches bitten, E:K:W: ihn dermasßen mitt gnedigster andtwort wollen versehen lasßen, damitt er seiner geschepsten hoffnung nach im wergk spuren möge, daß diesse Vnsere ihm zue gnaden gemeinte Vorschrift ihm sonderlich zue erlangung seines begehren ersprißlich gewesen, wie Wir denn gar nicht zweiffeln, E:K:W: sich hierumb werden, jhrer angebornen guetigkeitt nach, gegen ihme, so weitt sichs immer der billigkeitt vndt gerechtigkeitt nach (in masßen Wir auch weitters nichts begeren) leiden wil, gnedigst erzeigen. Vndt thuen E:K:W: sambt dero vielgeliebten gemahl, Vnser hertzlieben tochter, zue allen könniglichen wohlergehen, glichlicher regierung vndt guetter bestendig gesundheitt dem Allmechtigen ganz mutterlich beuehlen.

Datum Cöln an der Sprew, den 4. februarij anno 98.
Vonn Gottes gnaden Katharina geborne marggraffin
auch churfurstin zue Brandenburgk,
inn Preußen hertzogin.
text.english:
**To the Most Serene Prince, the Lord Christian the Fourth, King of Denmark, Norway, the Wends and the Goths, Duke of Schleswig, Holstein, of the Stormarn and the Dithmarschen, Count of Oldenburg and Delmenhorst, our friendly, much-beloved Lord Son — into His Royal Majesty's [own] hands.**

Most Serene King, [be] to Your Royal Majesty Our dutiful and honourable greeting, and, according to the bond of motherhood, whatever much more We are able [to render] of body and goods, beforehand. Friendly, most heartily beloved Lord cousin, son, and brother: We will hope, undoubting, to the Almighty, that Your Royal Majesty, together with your much-beloved consort, Our heart-dear daughter, are still graciously preserved in good bodily health and in all royal well-being — as We do indeed wish the same to that same Royal Majesty and to Her Beloved Grace out of a motherly heart.

Our friendly, most heartily beloved Lord consort and children Your Royal Majesty may know to be still in tolerable bodily capacity and condition; save only that, as for Our own person, for some days past the cough and other incidental weakness have so afflicted [Us], that We were also unable to render the last honour to Our gracious beloved Lord father — of most laudable, devout-in-Christ memory — at his electoral funeral, however gladly We should have wished [to do so]; yet We have nonetheless now to thank the Almighty for a tolerable improvement, whose mercy may graciously preserve us all therein long. Your Royal Majesty will also [learn] from Our heart-dear Lord consort's letter of intercession addressed to Your Royal Majesty — which they had most humbly submitted — in what manner there had most humbly arrived [a request] for a most gracious letter of recommendation to Your Royal Majesty on behalf of the most honourable, Our trusty and well-beloved Tycho Brahe; since he has then likewise besought Us also for a letter of intercession, and We have never noted that Your Royal Majesty was disposed toward him with disfavour, and do also not deem his request unreasonable — there reaches Your Royal Majesty herewith Our friendly request, that Your Royal Majesty would have him furnished with such a most gracious answer that he, according to the hope he has conceived, may perceive in the deed that this Our recommendation, intended for his benefit, has been especially fruitful to him for the attainment of his desire; as indeed We do not at all doubt that Your Royal Majesty will, according to your inborn kindness, show yourself herein most graciously toward him, so far as it may ever admit according to equity and justice (in which measure We also desire nothing further). And We commend Your Royal Majesty, together with your much-beloved consort, Our heart-dear daughter, to the Almighty for all royal welfare, fortunate governance, and good lasting health, quite as a mother [does].

Given at Cölln an der Spree, the 4th of February, in the year [15]98.
By the grace of God, Katharina, born Margravine,
also Electress of Brandenburg,
Duchess in Prussia.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Katharina of Brandenburg-Küstrin** (1549–1602), Electress of Brandenburg, wife of Elector **Johann Georg of Brandenburg**. She was the maternal grandmother of Christian IV: her daughter **Anna Catharina of Brandenburg** (1575–1612) married Christian IV in 1597. The kinship triple in the salutation (*"herr vetter, sohn, vndt bruder"* — "Lord cousin, son, and brother") is conventional inter-dynastic courtesy address, not literal; she calls the queen *"Vnser hertzlieben tochter"* ("Our heart-dear daughter"), which is literal.
- **Recipient.** **Christian IV of Denmark and Norway** (r. 1588–1648). The titulature in the address-block is the standard Danish royal style: King of Denmark, Norway, the Wends and Goths; Duke of Schleswig, Holstein, Stormarn and Dithmarschen; Count of Oldenburg and Delmenhorst.
- **Subject — the Tycho intercession.** The letter is a *Vorbitte* / *Vorschrift* (a letter of intercession + recommendation) on behalf of **Tycho Brahe**, here styled *"dem erenuehsten Vnserm lieben besonderen Tycho Brahen"* ("the most honourable, Our trusty and well-beloved Tycho Brahe" — *lieben besonderen* is the German chancery formula glossed at this chapter's convention *Vester lieber besonder* → "Our trusty and well-beloved"). It coordinates with a parallel intercession from her husband the Elector (*"Vnsers hertzlieben hern gemahls … vorbittlich schreiben"*). Dating (4 Feb. 1598) and content place it amid the deteriorating relations between Tycho and the Danish court that culminated in his departure from Denmark in 1597; the Brandenburg electoral couple are lobbying the young king on his behalf. Tycho had evidently solicited the intercession himself (*"wann er denn dergleichen auch Vns vmb vorbittschrifft ersucht"*).
- **Negation count.** The body contains exactly **three** negations, all preserved: (1) *"die letzte ehr … nicht haben leisten können"* — "were **unable** to render the last honour" [at her father's funeral]; (2) *"Wir niemals vermerckt, daß E:K:W: ihme mitt vngnaden gewogen"* — "We have **never** noted that Your Royal Majesty was disposed toward him with disfavour"; (3) *"auch seine bitt **nicht** vnzimblich erachten"* — "do **also not** deem his request unreasonable" (a single negation governing the litotes *unzimblich* "unreasonable"; rendered as one "not," not doubled). The parenthetical *"in masßen Wir auch weitters **nichts** begeren"* — "in which measure We also desire **nothing** further" — is a fourth negative element (*nichts*), preserved. None of these reverse a command; the controlling speech-act is a request (*"Vnser freundtliches bitten"*), and the conditional logic is straightforward (since X, and since not-Y, and not-Z → therefore We request), so no Possible-grade ambiguity arises.
- **The qualifying clause** *"so weitt sichs immer der billigkeitt vndt gerechtigkeitt nach … leiden wil"* — "so far as it may ever admit according to equity and justice" — is a deferential limiting clause: the Electress asks the king to favour Tycho only insofar as equity and justice permit, explicitly adding that she desires nothing beyond that. The hedge is preserved, not sharpened into an unconditional plea.
- **Her father's funeral.** *"Vnsern gnedigen geliebten herrn vattern, hochlöblicher chriftmilder gedechtnus … dero churfurstl: begrebnus"* — Katharina's father was **Margrave Johann (Hans) of Brandenburg-Küstrin** (d. 1571); *"chriftmilder"* is a chancery spelling of *christmilder* ("devout/charitable in Christ," a memorial epithet for the deceased), rendered "devout-in-Christ memory." She reports being kept by illness from attending the funeral — apparently a recent re-interment or commemorative obsequy, since the date of her own letter (1598) post-dates the Margrave's death by decades; the text does not specify the occasion, and it is left unresolved rather than supplied.
- **Court-German orthography (Frühneuhochdeutsch / chancery, c. 1598).** Representative forms: *vndt / vnd* = *und*; *vff*-type *v/u* alternation throughout (*vermugen, vermögenheitt*); *könnig / könniglichen* = *König(lichen)*; *zuuohrn* = *zuvorn* ("beforehand," the address-formula,); *gnediglich / gnedigst* = *gnädiglich / gnädigst*; *thuen / thuen … beuehlen* = *tun / befehlen*; *besßerung, ersprißlich, lasßen, masßen* show *ß/ss* alternation; *Sprew* = *Spree*; *marggraffin* = *Markgräfin*; *churfurstin* = *Kurfürstin*. *husten* = "cough."
- **Abbreviations expanded in sense.** *E:K:W:* = *Euer Königliche Würden* ("Your Royal Majesty/Dignity"); *J:L:* = *Ihre Liebden* ("Her Beloved Grace," conventional address for a princess — here the queen); *dero 1:* — an abbreviation in the witness, most plausibly *dero Liebden* ("their Beloved Grace," i.e. the Elector); read as the source of the humble request, but the contracted "1:" is editorially uncertain and is flagged here rather than silently expanded.
- **Calendar.** *"den 4. februarij anno 98"* = 4 February 1598. Brandenburg and Denmark both kept the **Julian calendar (Old Style)** in 1598 (Protestant territories did not adopt the Gregorian reform until 1700), so the dateline is O.S.; no conversion is applied. The catalogue label ("1598. 4. februar. Cölln an der Spree") agrees with the dateline.
- **Place.** *Cöln / Cölln an der Sprew* = **Cölln an der Spree**, the twin town of Berlin on the Spree (seat of the Brandenburg court; later merged into Berlin), not Cologne on the Rhine.
- **MS witness.** The Opera Omnia text rests on the transcript (*Afskrift*) in **Langebek's Diplomatarium**, Rigsarkivet, Copenhagen — i.e. a later copy, not the original sent letter; readings such as *dero 1:* should be weighed with that transmission in mind.

documents.incipit: SERENISSIME et potentissime rex, domine clementissime. Regiæ tuæ Majestati in hoc novo …

text.original:
AD REGEM DANIÆ.

SERENISSIME et potentissime rex, domine clementissime. Regiæ tuæ Majestati in hoc novo conjugio adeoque toto regimine optima quæque et faustissima ex animo precor et voveo ac gratias, quas possum, maximas pro beneficiis a laudatissimæ memoriæ parente Friderico mihi præstitis quamplurimis submisse ago, quodque inde ab eo anno, quo Regia Tua Majestas in lucem hanc prodiit, divina illa scientia astronomica in Dania, patria mea dulcissima, liberaliter sustentata sit. Et sane non minora de Regia Tua Majestate mihi indubie pollicebar et citra frustraneam spem expertus fuissem, ni quorundam insatiabili mei odio laborantium (uti non exiguis indiciis reor) malevolus in me animus obstitisset, quos tamen nullo pacto læsi unquam, imo cuidam, quem horum latentem et inveteratum machinatorem existimo non parum profui. Quamobrem statim a Regiæ Tuæ Ma:tis coronatione mutationum incidere occasiones, uti sunt rerum humanarum subinde quædam vicissitudines. Idque forte fataliter evenit, ipsis jam astris artis suæ excercitium alio dirigentibus et destinantibus, cum et tertius annorum climactericus, per se alterationibus obnoxius, a prima Uraniburgi isthic fundatione ageretur. Præterea Regiæ Tuæ Majestati humiliter et enixe gratias habeo, quod, siquidem ita necessitas postularet, ut me cum iis, quibus tantopere invigilo, exercitiis astronomicis in vicinam Germaniam conferrem, nec iter impedire, nec retinere, nec etiam, cum Rostochii per anni quadrantem in propinquo manerem, aut postea, dum in extremis Holsatiæ finibus moror, revocare voluerit, quo mea studia non retardarentur, et astronomiam universaliter, ut toti orbi noster undiquaque inserviret labor et acceptum sit condendi propositum. Quo sane nomine eo magis Regiæ Tuæ Majestati me obstrictum video. Nam licet hoc maximo meo factum fuisset incommodo, et majore fortassis aliorum, qui nostra undiquaque avide expetunt et nequaquam contemptui habent, ob amorem tamen in Patriam et honorem regi meo serenissimo præstandum nolens volens obtemperare atque particularia universalibus præponere coactus fuissem, cum minori meo et aliorum emolumento. Quapropter etiam, cum Rostochii ea de caussa tam diu non sine periculo ob luem epidemicam isthic grassantem neque sine magnis expensis ob familiæ copiam et annonæ caritatem subsisterem, ad Regiam Tuam Maiestatem submisse literas dedi et abitus mei caussas nonnihil, quantum licuit, attigi, meamque operam Regiæ Tuæ Majestati et patriæ submisso animo sinceraque intentione obtuli, in omnibus, quæ in ipsius et patriæ honorem per me unquam præstari possent, modo tolerabilibus conditionibus id fieret, et indemnitati meæ competenter consuleretur. Quæ literæ, quod non eo, quo a me scriptæ, candido nimirum et in patriam studioso affectu animoque in serenissimum regem meum submisse obsequioso, acceptæ sint aliorum, uti existimo, eas sinistre admodum interpretantium malevolentia admissum est, sive quod aliquo clanculario mei laborarent odio (cujus tamen me iis caussas dedisse non sum conscius) sive quod suo sic abundare sensu vellent. Quod equidem nec iis invideo, nec ægre fero. Regiam vero Ma:tem Tuam, horum neutiquam consciam, lubenter in his excusatam habeo. Verum sit hoc quicquid velit, quod veritas, temporis filia, aliquando prodet meamque integritatem tuebitur, tamen de patria mea (uti par est) honorifice sentire, et Regiæ Majestatis Tuæ honori, quantum in me est, submisse studere ejusque virtutes deprædicare non desinam. Utque id aliqua nunc ex parte declarem atque Majestati Tuæ pro beneficiis clementer præstitis, qua possum, submissione me gratum ostendam, duos eidem libros, in ipsius regno primum natos, hic vero in Germaniæ vicinæ finibus nuper completos offero et exhibeo. Regiam etiam Tuam Majestatem, cum et aliis regibus et principibus viris eadem mittam, præterire minime decuit aut licuit. Submisse itaque et humiliter rogo, Regia Tua Majestas hoc regio et clementi animo acceptare non dedignetur. Plura et his majora de rebus astronomicis, annuente astrorum opifice, subjuncturus sum, quorum maiorem partem itidem in Regiæ Tuæ Majestatis regno, patria mea charissima, pluribus jam annis a me elaboratam, reliquam vero hic per otium hybernum ulterius confectam atque absolutam, in Regiæ tuæ Majestatis et regni honorem, favente eodem numine, propediem publicare decrevi et Regiæ Tuæ Majestati, modo id ei non ingratum intellexero, demisse offerre. Interim et semper, ut Regiæ Tuæ Majestati ego meaque omnia quam commendatissima sint, qua possum et decet submissione precor.

Deus opt: max: Regiam Tuam Ma:tem in regnorum et ditionum gubernandorum utilitatem et commodum cum ser:ma et optima conjuge quam diutissime florentem et incolumem conservet.

Datæ ex arce Ranzoviana Wandesburgk, prope Hamburgum sita, die 7. februarii anni 1598.
text.english:
**TO THE KING OF DENMARK.**

Most serene and most mighty king, most gracious lord. To Your Royal Majesty I pray and vow from my heart all that is best and most auspicious in this new marriage, and indeed in your whole reign; and I humbly render the greatest thanks I can for the very many benefits bestowed on me by your parent Frederick of most laudable memory, and because, ever since the year in which Your Royal Majesty came forth into this light, that divine science of astronomy has been liberally maintained in Denmark, my sweetest homeland. And indeed I was assuredly promising myself no lesser things from Your Royal Majesty, and should have experienced them without disappointment of that hope, had not the malevolent disposition of certain men toward me — men labouring under an insatiable hatred of me (as I judge from no slight indications) — stood in my way; men whom I nevertheless never in any way injured, nay, to a certain one of them, whom I reckon the hidden and inveterate contriver of these things, I did no small service. For which reason, immediately after Your Royal Majesty's coronation, occasions of changes began to arise, as there are from time to time certain vicissitudes in human affairs. And this perhaps befell by fate, the very stars now directing and ordaining the exercise of their art elsewhere, since the third climacteric year — of itself liable to alterations — was being reckoned from the first founding of Uraniborg yonder. Furthermore, I humbly and earnestly give thanks to Your Royal Majesty, that — since necessity so demanded that I betake myself, together with those astronomical pursuits over which I keep so watchful a vigil, into neighbouring Germany — you were unwilling either to impede my journey, or to detain me, or even, when I was staying nearby at Rostock for a quarter of a year, or afterwards while I tarry in the farthest bounds of Holstein, to recall me, so that my studies might not be retarded, and that our labour might everywhere serve astronomy universally [and] the whole world, and the purpose of establishing it might be welcome. On which account, to be sure, I see myself the more bound to Your Royal Majesty. For although this had been done to my very great inconvenience, and perhaps to the greater [inconvenience] of others, who eagerly seek out our works on every side and by no means hold them in contempt, yet out of love toward my Homeland and the honour to be rendered to my most serene king I should have been compelled, willing or unwilling, to comply, and to set particular [interests] before universal ones, to the lesser profit of myself and of others. Wherefore also, since for that cause I was staying at Rostock so long, not without danger from the epidemic plague raging there, nor without great expenses on account of the size of my household and the dearness of provisions, I humbly addressed a letter to Your Royal Majesty and touched somewhat, so far as was permitted, upon the reasons for my departure, and offered my service to Your Royal Majesty and to my homeland, with a humble disposition and sincere intention, in all things that could ever be performed by me toward the honour of [Your Majesty] and of the homeland — provided it were done on tolerable conditions, and provided my own being-kept-harmless were duly looked to. That this letter was not received in the spirit in which it was written by me — namely with that frank affection, zealous toward my homeland, and with a mind humbly deferential toward my most serene king — came about, as I think, through the malevolence of others who interpret it altogether perversely, whether because they laboured under some clandestine hatred of me (for which, however, I am not conscious of having given them cause), or because they wished thus to overflow with their own opinion. Which, for my part, I neither begrudge them nor take amiss. But Your Royal Majesty, in no wise privy to these things, I gladly hold excused in this matter. Yet be this whatever it will — for that the truth, the daughter of time, will one day bring it forth and will protect my integrity — nonetheless I shall not cease to think honourably of my homeland (as is fitting), and, so far as in me lies, humbly to study Your Royal Majesty's honour and to proclaim your virtues. And that I may now in some part declare this, and show myself grateful to Your Majesty, with what humble submission I can, for the benefits graciously bestowed, I offer and present to the same two books, first born in [Your Majesty's] own kingdom, but here lately completed within the bounds of neighbouring Germany. Nor was it at all seemly or permissible to pass over Your Royal Majesty, since I am sending the same [books] to other kings and princely men as well. Humbly therefore and submissively I ask that Your Royal Majesty may not disdain to accept this with a royal and gracious disposition. More things, and greater than these, concerning astronomical matters I shall append, the Maker of the stars granting it; the greater part of which, likewise elaborated by me over many years now within Your Royal Majesty's kingdom, my dearest homeland, and the remainder further wrought and completed here during the winter's leisure, I have resolved — the same divine power favouring — shortly to publish, to the honour of Your Royal Majesty and the kingdom, and humbly to offer to Your Royal Majesty, provided I understand it to be not unwelcome to him. In the meantime, and always, I pray with what submission I can and as is fitting, that I and all that is mine may be most heartily commended to Your Royal Majesty.

May God, Best and Greatest, preserve Your Royal Majesty, to the profit and advantage of the kingdoms and dominions to be governed, flourishing and unharmed together with your most serene and most excellent consort for the very longest time.

Given from the Rantzau castle Wandsburg, situated near Hamburg, on the 7th day of February in the year 1598.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe** (1546–1601), writing from his self-imposed exile after leaving Hven. The letter is a draft (*Kladde*) preserved in the Basel autograph collection.
- **Recipient.** *Regem Daniae* = **Christian IV of Denmark** (1577–1648, r. from 1588, crowned 1596). The opening congratulations on the king's "new marriage" refer to his marriage to **Anne Catherine of Brandenburg** (concluded late 1597). The phrase *inde ab eo anno, quo Regia Tua Majestas in lucem hanc prodiit* ("ever since the year in which Your Royal Majesty came forth into this light," i.e. 1577) links the king's birth-year to the founding period of Uraniborg (Hven granted 1576, building begun 1576/77).
- **Occasion & the "two books."** Tycho writes from Wandsbek, where he was a guest of **Heinrich Rantzau**, after leaving Denmark (he had wintered at Rostock, then moved into Holstein). The *duos libros … in ipsius regno primum natos, hic vero in Germaniae vicinae finibus nuper completos* ("two books, first born in [your] kingdom but lately completed here in the bounds of neighbouring Germany") is the presentation of the ***Astronomiae instauratae mechanica*** (Wandsbek, 1598) together with the companion volume Tycho was issuing at the same time. **Identification flagged:** the text names neither book; the standard pairing of the two Wandsbek presentation volumes is the *Mechanica* and the printed **star-catalogue** (the thousand-star catalogue, circulated as a manuscript/printed companion to the *Progymnasmata*). The translation keeps the neutral "two books"; the specific titles are supplied here as context, not asserted from the letter.
- **Place.** *arce Ranzoviana Wandesburgk, prope Hamburgum* = the **Rantzau castle at Wandsbek** (modern Wandsbek, a district of Hamburg), the seat of Heinrich Rantzau, *Statthalter* of the Danish king in Holstein; rendered "Wandsburg" in the header to match the as-written *Wandesburgk*. *Holsatia* = **Holstein**; *Rostochium* = **Rostock**.
- **Astronomy / programme.** *astronomiam universaliter … condendi propositum* — Tycho's lifelong **programme of establishing/restoring astronomy** (cf. *astronomia instaurata*,, *restitutio / instauratio*); *toti orbi … noster … labor* — "our labour [serving] the whole world." *astrorum opifice* / *eodem numine* — "the Maker of the stars" / "the same divine power," reverent periphrases kept.
- **Astrology.** *tertius annorum climactericus … a prima Uraniburgi … fundatione* = "the **third climacteric year** reckoned from the first founding of Uraniborg" (a climacteric at a multiple of seven; Uraniborg founded 1576 → the 21st year, 1597, falls in this window). *ipsis jam astris artis suae excercitium alio dirigentibus et destinantibus* — "the very stars now directing and ordaining the exercise of their art elsewhere": Tycho frames his departure in astrological-fatalist terms while attributing the proximate cause to court enemies. The hedge *forte fataliter* ("perhaps by fate") is preserved.
- **Polemical hedges (preserved, not sharpened).** Tycho repeatedly veils his accusations: *quorundam insatiabili mei odio laborantium (uti non exiguis indiciis reor)* — "certain men labouring under an insatiable hatred of me (as I judge from no slight indications)"; *cuidam, quem … latentem et inveteratum machinatorem existimo* — "a certain one whom I reckon the hidden and inveterate contriver." The unnamed "contriver" is left unnamed in the translation, as in the source. The qualifier *quantum licuit* ("so far as was permitted") and the conditional *modo tolerabilibus conditionibus … et indemnitati meae competenter consuleretur* ("provided on tolerable conditions … and provided my keeping-harmless were duly looked to") are kept with their hedged force.
- **Negation count.** The clause listing the king's forbearance contains a coordinated triple negation governed by one *voluerit*: *nec iter impedire, nec retinere, nec etiam … revocare voluerit* — "you were unwilling **neither** to impede my journey, **nor** to detain me, **nor** even … to recall me." Rendered as three negated infinitives under "you were unwilling," preserving the king's non-interference (the king did **not** obstruct Tycho's departure). No negation added or dropped.
- ***veritas, temporis filia*** — "the truth, the daughter of time" (*Veritas filia Temporis*), the classical-Renaissance commonplace (Gellius via Erasmus' *Adagia*); kept as the sententious aside it is.
- **Sign-off / titulature.** *Deus opt: max:* = *Deus Optimus Maximus*, "God, Best and Greatest"; *ser:ma et optima conjuge* = "most serene and most excellent consort" (Anne Catherine). The dense honorific register (*Regia Tua Majestas*, *submisse*, *humiliter*, *demisse*, *clementer*) is kept throughout as Tycho's deferential address to his sovereign.
- **Calendar.** *die 7. februarii anni 1598* = 7 February 1598. Denmark was on the **Julian calendar (Old Style)** in 1598; the date is so marked. The dateline agrees with the catalogue label ("1598. 7. februar. Wandsburg"); no discrepancy. Date not converted.
- **Orthography / abbreviations.** *Ma:tis / Ma:tem* = *Majestatis / Majestatem*; *ser:ma* = *serenissima*; *opt: max:* = *Optimus Maximus*; *caussas / caussa* = *causas / causa* (period spelling); *excercitium* = *exercitium*; *charissima* = *carissima*; *hybernum* = *hibernum*. Forms kept as printed in the Source block.
