documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Axel Brahe** (1550–1616), Tycho's younger brother, a member of the Danish Council of the Realm (*Rigsråd*); writing warmly from Copenhagen. An original letter, signed *egen hånd* ("own hand").
- **Content.** Axel rejoices to learn that Tycho's affairs have turned out well — that he has secured **good terms with the Emperor** (Rudolf II) — and answers Tycho's request: should anyone obstruct him over his **instruments** (those still in Denmark, or their removal abroad), Axel will help as far as he can, though he trusts no such hindrance will arise. A letter of fraternal reassurance during Tycho's transition into imperial service.
- **Orthography.** Late-16th-c. Danish chancery spelling: *erlig* (ærlig, honourable), *welbiurdigh* (velbyrdig, well-born), *thilschreffuidt* (tilskrevet), *hilßenn* (hilsen), *tacßielße* (taksigelse, thanks), *leylighed* (situation/circumstance), *wylkar* (vilkår, terms), *forhynndring* (forhindring, hindrance), *jnstrumenter* (instruments), *beffalendis* (befalende, commending). Reading-verified as **Danish**. The bracketed *alme[ct]iste* (almægtigste) is an editorial restoration of a damaged spot; kept as printed.
- ***Wor gunst*** register: opens with the courteous *min ganske venlige hilsen … forsendt med Gud* ("my quite friendly greeting … sent with God"), the standard Danish noble epistolary salutation (cf. glossary).
- **Calendar.** *København denn 25 October 99* = **25 October 1599**; Denmark kept the **Julian / Old Style** calendar. Header agrees with the label.

documents.editorial_note:
**Text recovered.** The letter's recovered passages — dropped by a defective transcription of the source and absent until now — has been restored from the text of record and translated. The Source and English columns below are now complete.

**Direction note.** **Incoming** letter — *from* Tycho's Danish kinsman-agent **Eske Bille (Eskie Bylde)** *to* Tycho. A long estate/business letter on Tycho's residual Danish affairs. (The catalogue notes a **postscript of 11 November**; the source below runs to the 29 October signature.)

text.original:
[AD TYCHONEM BRAHE.]

MYNN ganndtske wennlig helsenn nu och althidt forsendt med Vor Herre. Kierre Tyge
Brahe och kierre broder, betaker ieg dig ganndze wennligenn och giernne for
alltt gott, du mig giortt och beuist hafuer, huilkid igienn ad forskiulle du
althidt skall finde mig villig met huis ieg dig till ehre, villige och tieniste
were kanndtt.

Kierre broder, ehr din skriffuelse mig tilhendekommitt her vdj
Kiøbenhaffun ved din søn Tygge, och blantt andid, som du
skrifuer mig till, lader du mig vide dend guode leiglighedt, du hoeß rom. key.
maytt. erst kommenn vdj, huilked ehr mig (saa vell som flere dinne guoede
wenner, som nu her till denne herredag hafuer spurtt det) møgid kiertt, Gud
giffue dig fremdelis lyke. Anlangendis dett 50 daller, du skriffuer ieg skulle
lade m. Chrestenn Lenuig[!] bekomme,
saa siger dinn sønn Tyge dig vell
beskeed der om; thi ieg formerker, hand følgis med dennom, ellers skulle hannd
giernne haffue bekommid dennom, om dett end haffde werid mere paa att giøre.
Anlangendis dine jnstrumenter, saa hafuer ieg sagtt din sønn
beskied och min betenke der om, huorledis mig tykis de best kunde komme vd, dog
først her fra til Lybeck. Jeg kannd icke fortøffue her saa lenge vdj byen, att Thyge blifuer ferdig med boede jnstrumenterne att lade indpacke och huis andid hannd skall
bestille, thj ieg ehr wdj nogenn kong. maytt. befallinger, huor ieg nu vdj dag
drager aff, och der henn, som de skall fuldtgiøris.

Jeg formercker, att de 700 daller, som ieg for nogen tidlanng
sidenn haffuer sentt dig hen vd, vor dig icke tilhenndekommenn, der din sønn
drog fraa dig, dog formercker ieg aff Tyge, att hannd pa denne her reise hafuer fait nogenn beskiedenn
om thennom. Jeg haffuer endnu icke stilltt fru Sidtzell Vrnne tilfridtz, thi ieg endnu icke kand kome offuer
ens med hinde; hund vill haffue renthenn met hoffuitstollen, ieg will endnu lade
hinde hoffuitstollenn tillbiude, vill hund icke aname dennom, daa ehr det att
befryctte, at hund lader dig thiltalle for hoffuittstollenn och renten. Och som
du schriffuer ieg skulle tage en stefning offuer hinde thill herredagenn, saa
vedst du vel, att det ehr icke vertt, att mannd vdj slige sager kannd steffne
thill heredage, førind sagenn ehr forfulld thill heritzting och landtzting, och
kandschee dett skulle strecke sig ind thill rigenns canzeller, om mand sa skulle
talle hinde til effter fru Johann Oxxis
breff; och kandstu vell sielff tenke om sagen gick dig imod, huod for skade och
vlelighedt dett ville giffue dig; och paa dett du disbedre kand forfare, att
fru Johann Oxis breff icke kannd gielder stortt, saa
sennder ieg dig en copie aff en heritzthings domb, som rodtzens kontractt ehr
indførtt, saa du vell all leligheden der aff kannd forfare. Jeg haffuer och
ladid din sønn siett ett sandinge breff, som du med eigien hond hafuer
vnderskreffuitt, vdj huilke du forplicter dig att betalle hoffuittsummen med
huis tilbørlig renthe der aff kannd gaa. Aff din skriffuelse forfarer ieg
occsaa, attu ville komme her ind thill heredagenn, nu først komer, saa skallttu
vell troe, att her vdj denne sommer icke skeer herredage, effterdj denne heredag
hafuer nu standen saa langtt hen paa aaritt; videre hafuer ieg her om tallid med
din sønn Tygge, som hand
mundeligenn kannd berette dig.

Huod de 300 daller renthepending ehr anlangendis, som skall
forskikis vd ad Lantheholsten, de schall bliffue
forskikit der vd, huod heller ieg fanger dennom aff Axell Gylldenstierne eller huor ieg
tager dennom; och formerker ieg, du ville giernne haffue hoffuittsumen, som ehr
5000 daller, betallid, paa det du kunde bekomme ditt breff vdjgienn, som lydder
paa 10,000 daller, saa ved mand icke, om der stander løsßenkiendelse vdj
breffuitt, enthen paa halff aar eller paa fiering aar, huorfore du for att sende
mig en copie aff breffuitt, att mand til itt andid aar kunde
opschriffue dennom; thj nu thill denne omslag troer ieg icke det kand schee,
icke heller mand nu saa hastig kand opbringe sadanne en summa pennding,
vndertagenn mand haffde vist dett om s. Hannsdag tidtt, eller i dett seniste til
Lauerentj. Huod anlangenndis dinn stoedt, du haffde paa
Huenn, saa hafuer ieg denom icke
anderledis kunde faitt solld, end ieg motte sende thenom offuer thill Ellinge, der hafuer nu fougedenn sold dennom,
somme thill bønder och somme thill prester, saa ieg icke veid, huor dyre hannd
hafuer solld dennom, førind ieg kommer nu hiem och kannd forfare det. De heste,
som du om skriffuer, att ieg skule kiøbe til dig, 5 hafuer ieg bekommidt vd aff
Olluff Byllde, di 3, som gick for
hanns vøund, dend elste 7 och i ottende aar, och kiøbte ieg end vng folle vd aff
hanom, som ehr 3 och i fierde aar, som tiend vell til at gaa for vound hoeß de
andre thre, dend fembte hafuer ieg kiøbtt thill dig sielff att ride, och er hand
i fembte aar, och er icke tiulff paa, att hannd io ehr end edell guoed hest,
thersom hannd bliffuer ellers vorid och for haffre nock, daa schall det vell
bliffue sadanne en hest, att end første motte vell
passere att ridde paa; dersom det icke hafde verid dig paa at giørre, ville
ieg i sandhed icke hafde solltenn igienn for 150 daller. Jeg schall gifue hannom
for alle 5 hestene 300 daller, och denom betalle nu thill juell. Der ehr 2
foller paa Huenn, som dig tilkommer, end
rødblesid och en brunstiernid, som icke kand vere din ganning; thj ieg ville
gierne haffue solld denom for 40 daller, och mig icke biudis mer for dennom
begge 2 end 30 daler, dog hafuer ieg rodt din sønn, att hand skulle tage end vd
aff dennom met sig, som drengen kunde ride paa och trecke dend anden, paa det
dend andenn kunde bliffue forskonnidtt. Dend 6 hest haffuer ieg endnu icke kunde
bekomid orsagenn dj formener, her skulle blifue en munstring, huorfor huer
hafuer sine heste behouff. Jeg hafuer tagid end kudske i tieniste paa dine
veigne, som hafuer lofuid att ville følle din sønn vd, och ieg hafuer lofuid
hanom, att nar hand lyster icke lenger att bliffue der vde hoeß dig, at hand da
skule fa did pasbor och sin løn, saa hand vel kunde kome her i landid igienn;
hand hafuer och loffuid, att hand well vill forholle sig i sin tieniste huoeß
dig. Jeg haffuer och antagid enn staldreng paa dinne weignne, som haffuer ract
mig sinn hond, att ville thienne dig ett aar, och schall du giffue hannom thill
scho och schiorter et aar 6 daller och end engelstklenning och et paar
knestøffler; och haffuer ieg i lige mode loffuid hannom, att nar hanns aard ehr
ome och hannd icke lyster der vde lennger att thienne, att hannd daa schall faa
hanns pasbor och hanns lønn, saa hand kand komme her ind i rigid vdjgienn, och
hafde hannd en guoed tienniste, saa det stod hartt, att ieg kunnde faa hannom
løß der som hannd thientte.

Huod dj fische ehr annlanngendis, som du wille haffue indsaltidt,
har din sønn Tygge sielff werid
der paa lanndid och sielffuer bestilltt med dennom.

Nu haffuer ieg suorid dig paa denne dinn skriffuelse, och videre
haffuer ieg tallid med din sønn, som hannd mundligen kannd berette dig. Jeg vor
thilfridtz ieg haffde Dauid Pedersens
reegenschaff her inde for nogenn orsag schiulldt.

Disligiste kannd ieg icke
heller komme till nogenn ende med Dirick faruers quinde, wndertagenns ieg haffde hindis
regenschaff igienn, som ieg hafuer sent dig vdt, och befrøcter ieg mig, att hund
tør suplicere thill kong. maytt. eller thill hofmesteren, saa
kannd ieg dog ingenn vei komme met hinde, førind ieg bekommer det regenschaff
igienn, som ieg sende dig wdt, huorvdaff mand kannd forfare, att reegenschabidt
ehr icke ret klart. Dog kand ieg icke andid forsta effter dinne wdgiffnne
seddeller, saa och effter dennd beuiß, hund haffer vdaff kiøbmend och kremmere,
attu io bliffuer hinde pending skiulldige.

Prestenn paa Hueen ehr
begierendis, att hannd motte bekomme dend smede, som du haffuer ladidt opsette
der paa landidt, thj end stor dog och forfaler, effterdj prestegordenn ehr vdj
din tidt blefuen forfaldenn; saa haffuer ieg dog icke same smede hannom ville
samtycke, førind ieg fich din ville der om. Ladegordenn stor och forfallder, saa
det schall verre att befrycte, att feehusitt schal ner i sommer eller dett
faller ner vdaff sig sielffuer; ellers veed ieg dig nu paa denne tidt inthid
andidt, att ieg kannd skriffue dig thill, mennd will nu och althid haffue dig
Gud alsommectigste befalendis med mannge guoede netter, som minn fader och moder
och Eschie Brock och Jørgenn Brockenhuß och ieg ynscher dig
och alle dinne och di, dig well will.

Aff Kiøbenhaffun med stoer hast dend 29 octobris
anno 1599.

Eskie Byllde.

Kierre Thyge, sidenn dette breff vor
schreffuenn, ehr ieg kommen hid thill byenn wdigienn, och hafuer ieg taldt med
din sønn, och formerker ieg, att hand hafuer bekomid
schriffuelse, att hand endnu skall forschafe dig vd sa mange som en 14 heste
thilsammenn, huilkid ieg troer icke mugeligtt ehr, att hannd paa sa stackidt en
tidt kan opbringe end 7 heste; thj ieg vdj dise 4 vgger, Thyge hafuer vert her vdj landidt,
hafft stor handell, førind ieg kunde bringe dise till weie, dj ieg hafuer
bekommitt. J daug hafuer ieg kiøbitt 2 heste, enn vdaff Axell Oggesenn for 45 daller, huilckid hest
ieg haffuer vdspurdt att schulle werre en guoed vforderffuitt klepper, saa hannd
och vell kannd thienne thill dig sielff att ride, eller huilkenn din venn du
willtt giffue denn, daa kandstu ret vell pasere met denn. Denn anndenn kiøbtte
ieg vdaff Baldzer Fox for 40 daller,
schall det och vell bliffue en guoed hest vd aff dend, dog hand ehr vberedenn.
Nar hand kommer till foer, kandstu och i lige moder pasere met dend thill huem
du villtt giffuenn, thj hand schall och faa et gott riden och et smoct trau, och
ehr der ingen vdaff dise 2 heste eldre end i 5 aar, och beløber sig nu vdj
pendinge for dj 7 heste, der ieg hafuer forschafid din sønn, halfierdie hunder
och 35 daller. Gud giffue di ma vell komme vd thill dig vdenn skade. Jeg vill
icke rode dig du schillir dig ved den enne hest, som ieg kiøbtte vdaff Olluff Biillde. Dersom ieg ville giffue 200
daler for en hest thill dig eller enn andenn min venn, viste ieg icke sadane en
att kunde bekomme.

Din sønn och ieg hafuer i daug handlidt med din gamlle
voundriffuer, saa hand haffuer loffuidt, att vill følis vd met din sønn, och
hafuer ieg lofuid hannom till lønn om oridt 14 daller och enn lang kioell, och i
lige moder hafuer ieg loffuidt hanom, nar hand lyster icke lennger att bliffue
dervde, daa schall hannd faa sin guoede afscheed aff dig, saa hannd vell kannd
kome hervdj landid igienn.

Huod din gord ehr anlangendis hervdj byenn, hafuer Soffi Paxsis bøden mig 1500 daller forind,
dog paa 2 aard att betallind; fru Margrette Rosenkranzis hafuer bødenn mig och for dend 1400
daller paa ett aard att betalle; dog hafuer ieg intid kiøb kunde indga met nogen
aff denom, orsagen din søster Soffj
icke er i lanndid, och ieg forstar, att hun schall haffue beschieden paa samme
gord att selle. Dertillmet, huem same gord vill kiøbe, skall forplicte sig imod
dig att schall holle enn faruer vdj samme gord, huilkid ieg icke troer, att
nepeligenn nogenn aff dise fruer giør. Giør vell och beholl sielff dend hest,
som ieg fick wdaff Olluff Biilde, din søn
thall vell videre med dig om dend. Gud alsommectigste vill ieg haffue dig
befalid, som ieg ynscher eder allesammenn.

ActumKiøbenhaffun dend 11 nouembris anno 99.
text.english:
**[To Tycho Brahe.]**

My quite friendly greeting, now and always sent with Our Lord. Dear Tyge Brahe and dear brother, I thank you quite friendly and gladly for all the good you have done and shown me — which to requite, you shall always find me willing, in whatever I can be to your honour, will, and service.

Dear brother, your letter reached me here in Copenhagen by your son **Tyge**; and among other things you write me, you let me know **the good situation you have come into with the Roman Imperial Majesty** — which is very dear to me (as to your other good friends who have now heard it here at this **Herredag** [assembly of nobles]); God give you further luck. Concerning the **50 thaler** you write I should let **M. Christen Lenvig[?] [Longomontanus?]** have — your son Tyge will tell you well about it; for I perceive he travels with them [the instruments], else he would gladly have got them, even had more been at stake. Concerning **your instruments**, I have told your son my opinion how I think they could best be got out — but first from here to **Lübeck**. I cannot tarry here in the town so long that Tyge finishes packing both the instruments and his other business, for I am under certain royal commands, [for] which I now set out this very day, [to go] thither where they are to be carried out.

I perceive that **the 700 thaler I sent out to you some time ago** had not reached you when your son left you; yet I perceive from Tyge that on this journey he has got some account of them. **I have not yet satisfied Lady Sidsel Urne**, for I still cannot agree with her: she wants the interest with the principal; I will yet offer her the principal; if she will not accept it, then it is to be feared she will have you sued for the principal and interest. And as you write that I should take a summons against her to the Herredag — you well know it is not worth it, that in such cases one [cannot] summon to the Herredag before the case is pursued at **herredsting and landsting** [district + provincial courts], and perhaps it would reach as far as the realm's **Chancellor**, if one were to sue her by **Lady Johan Oxe's letter**; and you can well think yourself, if the case went against you, what damage and trouble it would give you. And that you may the better learn that Lady Johan Oxe's letter cannot count for much, I send you a copy of a **herredsting verdict** in which the … contract is entered, so that you can well learn the whole situation thence. I have also let your son see **a guarantee-letter you have signed with your own hand**, in which you bind yourself to pay the principal sum with whatever due interest may run from it. From your letter I also learn that you would come in [to Denmark] for the Herredag, [if it] should come now first; but you may well believe that this summer no Herredag will be held, since this one has now stood so late in the year. Further I have spoken about this with your son Tyge, as he can report to you by word of mouth.

As concerns the **300 thaler interest-money to be sent out to Land-Holstein**, it shall be sent thither, whether I get it from **Axel Gyldenstierne** or wherever I take it. And I perceive **you would gladly have the principal sum — which is 5000 thaler — paid, so that you could get back your bond, which reads on 10,000 thaler**; but one does not know whether there is a redemption-clause in the bond, on half-year or quarter-year [terms] — wherefore you [should] send me a copy of the bond, so that one could give notice on it for another year; for to **this [Lübeck] settlement-term [*omslag*]** I do not think it can be done, nor can one so quickly raise such a sum of money — unless one had known it by **St. Hans' time [24 June]**, or at the latest by **Laurence [10 August]**. Concerning **your stud [of horses] you had on Hven**, I could get them sold no otherwise than [that] I had to send them over to **Ellinge**, where the bailiff has now sold them — some to peasants and some to priests — so that I do not know how dearly he sold them, until I now come home and can learn it.

**The horses you write I should buy for you:** I have got 5 from **Oluf Bilde** — the 3 that went before his wagon, the eldest 7-and-in-his-eighth-year; and I bought a young foal from him, 3-and-in-his-fourth-year, fit to go before the wagon with the other three; the fifth I bought for **you yourself to ride**, in his fifth year — and there is no doubt he is a noble good horse: if he is otherwise cared for and gets oats enough, **he will become such a horse that a prince might well ride him**; were it not for your sake, I truly would not have sold him again for 150 thaler. I shall give 300 thaler for all 5 horses, to be paid now at Christmas. There are **2 foals on Hven that fall to you**, a red-blazed and a brown-starred, which cannot be your riding-horse [*ganning*?]; for I would gladly have sold them for 40 thaler, but I am offered no more than 30 thaler for both — yet I have advised your son to take one of them with him, which the boy could ride and lead the other, so the other could be spared. The 6th horse I have not yet been able to get, because they think there will be **a muster** here, so everyone has need of his horses. I have taken **a coachman** into service on your behalf, who has promised to follow your son out [to you]; and I have promised him that when he no longer wishes to stay out there with you, he shall have his passport and his wages, so he may come back into this country; he has also promised to conduct himself well in his service with you. I have likewise engaged **a stable-boy** on your behalf, who has given me his hand to serve you a year; and you shall give him, for shoes and shirts a year, **6 thaler, and an English-cloth garment and a pair of knee-boots**; and I have likewise promised him that when his year is up and he does not wish to serve longer out there, he shall have his passport and his wages, so he may come back into the realm — and he had a good service, so that it stood hard [for me] to get him free where he served.

As concerns **the fish you would have salted down**, your son Tyge was himself there on the land and arranged with them himself.

Now I have given you my oath on this your letter, and further I have spoken with your son, as he can report to you by mouth. I should be content [if] I had **David Pedersen's accounts** here, for a certain reason.

Likewise I cannot come to any end with **Dirik the dyer's wife**, unless I had back her accounts, which I sent out to you; and I fear she dares supplicate to the King's Majesty or to the **Court-Master [Hofmester]**, so that I can come no way with her until I get back the accounts I sent out to you — from which one can learn that the account is not quite clear. Yet I cannot understand otherwise — by your issued notes, and by the proof she has from merchants and shopkeepers — than that **you do remain owing her money**.

**The priest on Hven** desires to get the **smithy** you had set up there on the land, since a big [building] decays — for the **parsonage became dilapidated in your time**; yet I would not grant him the same smithy before I got your will on it. **The manor-farm [Ladegård] stands and decays, so that it is to be feared the cowhouse will collapse this summer, or fall down of itself.** Otherwise I know nothing else at this time to write you; but will now and always commend you to God Almighty, with many good-nights — as my father and mother, and **Eske Brock and Jørgen Brockenhus** and I wish you, and all yours, and those who wish you well.

From Copenhagen, in great haste, the 29th of October, the year 1599.
**Eske Bille.**

*[Postscript:]* Dear Tyge, since this letter was written, I have come back here to town, and I have spoken with your son, and I perceive that he has received word that he is yet to procure for you, sent out, as many as a full 14 horses altogether — which I do not think possible, that he can raise even 7 horses in so short a time; for in these 4 weeks that Tyge has been here in the country I have had great trouble before I could bring together these which I have got. Today I have bought 2 horses: one from Axel Oggesen for 45 thaler — which horse I have inquired about [and found] to be a good unspoiled cob, so that he can well serve for you yourself to ride, or [for] whichever of your friends you would give him to, [and] then you may very well make do with him. The other I bought from Baldzer Fox for 40 thaler; a good horse too will come of him, though he is unbroken. When he comes to fodder, you may likewise make do with him [for] whomever you would give him to, for he too shall get a good gait and a pretty trot; and there is none of these 2 horses older than in his 5th year. And it now amounts, in money, for the 7 horses I have procured for your son, to three hundred and eighty-five thaler. God grant they may come out to you without harm. I will not advise you to part with the one horse that I bought from Oluf Bilde; were I to give 200 thaler for a horse for you or another friend of mine, I should not know how to get such a one.

Your son and I have today dealt with your old wagon-driver, so that he has promised he will follow your son out [to you]; and I have promised him, for wages a year, 14 thaler and a long coat, and I have likewise promised him that, when he no longer wishes to stay out there, he shall have his good discharge from you, so that he may well come back into this country.

As concerns your house here in the town: Soffi Pax has offered me 1500 thaler for it, yet to be paid over 2 years; Lady Margrethe Rosenkrantz has likewise offered me 1400 thaler for it, to be paid in one year; yet I have been able to close no sale with either of them, because your sister Sophie is not in the country, and I understand that she is to have a say in the selling of the same house. Moreover, whoever wishes to buy the same house must bind himself to you to keep a dyer on the premises — which I hardly believe any of these ladies would do. Be so good as to keep for yourself the horse I got from Oluf Bilde; your son will speak further with you about it. I will have commended you to God Almighty, as I wish you all [well].

Done at Copenhagen, the 11th of November [15]99.

departures_from_tekstnet.basis: The text printed here descends from one harvest of tekstnet's page and was read against Dreyer's page images in July 2026; a second harvest of the same page is kept beside it. Where the two disagree in a word, both readings are listed: Dreyer's page decides, and unless the audit paragraph names the word, that check has not yet been made for it. Ligature, diacritic, case and spacing differences are not listed; the source's ligatures have been adopted.

documents.apparatus:
- **Direction & correspondent.** **Incoming**, **Eske Bille (Eskie Bylde)** — Tycho's kinsman ("dear brother") and trusted **Danish estate-agent** (the "Eske Bille" who handles Tycho's Danish payments throughout the corpus, e.g. the Mecklenburg-debt thread) — **to Tycho**. An original autograph (Basel).
- **Significance — the winding-down of Tycho's Danish estate and Hven establishment (a rich documentary letter).** A detailed account of Tycho's residual affairs, two-plus years after he left Denmark:
 - **The instruments still at Hven**, to be shipped **out via Lübeck** (Tycho's son **Tyge** [Tycho the Younger] packing them).
 - **Debts and creditors:** the **50 thaler** for "M. Christen" (possibly **Longomontanus**); the **700 thaler** already sent; the dispute with **Lady Sidsel Urne** (principal vs interest) and the legal counsel against summoning her to the Herredag (the proper course being **herredsting → landsting → Chancellor**); the **"Lady Johan Oxe's letter"** and a **herredsting verdict** sent as evidence; Tycho's own **signed bond**.
 - **The 5000/10,000-thaler bond:** the **300 thaler interest to Holstein** (via **Axel Gyldenstierne**), and Tycho's wish to **redeem the 5000-thaler principal to recover his bond "which reads on 10,000 thaler"** — Bille asks for a copy to check the redemption-terms; not feasible by the coming **Lübeck *omslag*** (settlement-term).
 - **The Hven livestock** (the "stud") sold off at **Ellinge**; the **5 riding/draught horses bought from Oluf Bilde** (one "a prince might ride," 300 thaler the lot at Christmas); the **2 Hven foals** and the **6th horse** held up by a coming **muster**.
 - **Servants hired** on Tycho's behalf — **a coachman and a stable-boy** (with detailed wages: 6 thaler + English cloth + knee-boots), both with return-passport guarantees.
 - **The salted fish**; **David Pedersen's accounts**; the unresolved dispute with **Dirik the dyer's wife** (whom Tycho "remains owing money").
 - **The decay of Hven (poignant).** The **parsonage dilapidated "in your time,"** the priest wanting Tycho's **smithy**; and **the manor-farm (Ladegård) decaying, the cowhouse near collapse** — a vivid image of Uraniborg's working estate falling to ruin after Tycho's departure.
- **Persons & places named.** Eske Bille; **Tycho the Younger** ("son Tyge"); **"M. Christen Lenvig"** (a garbled name, possibly **Longomontanus** — flagged); **Lady Sidsel Urne**; **Lady Johan Oxe**; **Axel Gyldenstierne**; **Oluf Bilde**; **David Pedersen**; **Dirik the dyer** & wife; the **priest on Hven**; **Christian IV** ("the King") & the **Court-Master**; Bille's **father and mother**, **Eske Brock**, **Jørgen Brockenhus**. Places: **Copenhagen**, **Hven**, **Lübeck**, **Ellinge**, Land-Holstein.
- **Calendar.** *dend 29 octobris anno 1599* at Copenhagen (Denmark = Old Style) → **29 October 1599 [Old Style]**; a **postscript of 11 November** is noted in the catalogue (not in the source text below the signature). Header and label agree.
- **Reading notes.** A few Danish words are uncertain in the copy: *ganning* (rendered "riding-horse" by context), *"Christen Lenvig"* (possibly Longomontanus), *rodtzens* ("the …'s contract" — left unfilled). Flagged; none affect the overall sense.

- **§1 Dreyer collation.** The 11-November continuation/postscript (written after the 29 October signature): the 14-horses-impossible note; two horses bought (Axel Oggesen 45 dlr, Baldzer Fox 40 dlr → 7 horses = 435 dlr); keep the Oluf Bilde horse; the old wagon-driver hired (14 dlr/yr + a long coat); the Copenhagen-house offers (Soffi Pax 1500 / Margrethe Rosenkrantz 1400). Restored from Dreyer XIV pp.162–163 (dropped by the working transcription).
- **What the recovered text is.** The final three sentences of the postscript Eske Bille added on 11 November 1599 (twelve days after the main letter of 29 October) to his long letter of family and estate business to Tycho Brahe, then in the course of relocating toward Emperor Rudolf II's court. The gap sat between "...because your sister Sophie is not in the country" and the closing "God Almighty..." formula: the prior translation truncated that very sentence and silently dropped the two that followed.
- **Sophie Brahe's role in the house sale.** The recovered clause shows the sale of Tycho's Copenhagen house was stalled not only by Sophie Brahe's absence abroad but because she was understood to have a say in whether it was sold at all — a concrete 1599 data-point for her documented independence in managing family affairs (cf. Ellefsen, *Søsteren og astronomen*, 2023, the standard biography, on her travels and agency in these years).
- **The dyer covenant.** A previously-lost, specific detail of Tycho's Copenhagen townhouse: any buyer had to bind himself to keep a *farver* (dyer) on the premises — evidently a tenant trade attached to the property — a condition Eske Bille judged neither prospective buyer would accept, and which he offers as his own explanation for why both offers stalled.
- **The two prospective buyers**, named nowhere else in the letter: Soffi Pax (1500 thaler over 2 years) and Lady Margrethe Rosenkrantz (1400 thaler over 1 year).
- **The closing horse reminder** ('the horse I got from Oluf Bilde') echoes, as a final aside before signing off, the fine riding-horse Eske Bille singles out earlier in the letter body ('such a horse that a prince might well ride him') and again in the postscript proper ('I will not advise you to part with the one horse that I bought from Oluf Bilde') — the same animal, restated rather than a new item.
- **Eske Bille**, the letter's author, was a close friend of Tycho who visited him often on Hven and later (1602-10) held the fief of Helsingborg Castle [lensmand paa Helsingborg Slot] (per Vellev, in *Danske Magazin*); here he is acting as Tycho's man of business in Copenhagen during the 1599 departure, managing horses, debts, the Hven stud's dispersal, and now the town house.
- **Correction.** The postscript's horse-purchase total, previously translated "four hundred and thirty-five thaler," is corrected to "three hundred and eighty-five thaler": the Danish "halfierdie hunder och 35 daller" (Dreyer, TBOO XIV p.163) uses the old Scandinavian counting form halvfjerde hundrede for 350, giving 350+35=385, confirmed independently by the letter's own itemised horse prices (300 + 45 + 40 = 385).

documents.incipit: VLTIMA Bacanalium die fuit ad me Dominus FRANCISCUS TENGNALIUS, nobilis iuvenis, omnique …

text.original:
IOHANNES ANTONIUS MAGINUS AD TYCHONEM BRAHE.

VLTIMA Bacanalium die fuit ad me Dominus FRANCISCUS TENGNALIUS, nobilis iuvenis, omnique virtute ornatissimus, et talis qualis a te mihi descriptus fuit, qui deferendo ad me tuas literas unâ cum munere tui libelli de machinis Astronomicis et de restitutione stellarum fixarum adeo mentem meam gaudio affecit, ut nescirem quo me continerem, sed hæc mea lætitia aliquantum remissa fuit, quando intellexi, ipsum discessurum esse sequenti mane Florentiam versus, nec posse mihi hîc referre ea quæ ipsi secreto, ut mecum communicaret, imposuisti, qui tamen mihi promisit se hoc facturum post suum reditum Bononiæ circiter dimidium Quadragesimæ, sed frustra per totam Quadragesimam a me expectatus fuit, imo et totam æstatem, cum toto hoc tempore Florentiæ et Romæ commoratus sit. Quin et ego quoque die 15a Maij me Mantuam traduxi vocatus a Serenissimo Duce Mantuæ, ut Principes eius filios in Mathematicis erudirem; ubi permansi tota æstate, nec Bononiæ redire potui ante primum Novembris, tempore scilicet novi studij. In hoc autem meo reditu inveni literas Domini FRANCISCI tui, quibus me commonefecit se quam primum velle Bononiæ redire, ut mihi exponere posset tuum desiderium, quod post duos dies fecit, relinquens mihi simul quædam scripta pro instructione dicti negocij. Valde profecto mihi grata fuit hæc occasio tibi gratificandi, et plus quam credi possit, quod eventus rei ipsius Deo volente tibi clare declarabit, neque enim nunc verbis hoc tibi indicare studebo, sed effectibus ipsis me facturum reservo; habeo enim qui hanc provinciam libentissime suscipiet, qui mihi inprimis devotissimus est, et habeo etiam plures literatos amicos per totam Italiam, qui et mihi et huic omne auxilium præstabunt.

Plura ad te scribere deberem, nisi improvisus reditus Domini FRANCISCI et maturus discessus eius obstarent; præsertim cum multis curis et molestijs familiaribus nunc afficiar. Nolo tamen prætermittere, quin te subnixe et instantissime rogem, ut mihi gratissime communices Tabulas motuum luminarium a te editas et forsan publicatas unâ cum eius usu pro his temporibus; cupio enim primus omnium Ephemerides condere novas secundum tuas observationes et interim, dum alias tabulas absolves, potero ego supputare motus luminarium in eclipsibus et insuper figuras ingressus Solis in puncta cardinalia erigere et lunationes omnes perpendere, et ex his iudicia annua contexere; nam pro hoc negocio sufficiet calculus reliquorum planetarum iuxta usitatam rationem COPERNICI.

De meo statu certior fies a Domino FRANCISCO tuo, scilicet me esse perturbationibus onustum, qua de causa finem huic epistolæ facio, rogans te efficaciter ut hæc omnia in bonam feras partem, meque ut verum et sincerum amicum et devotissimum servum habeas. Deum optimum deprecor, ut tuis votis satisfaciat plene.

Vale.
Bononia 4 Novembris 1599.
Perillustri Dominationi tuæ
addictissimus
IO. ANTONIUS MAGINUS,
Patavinus.
text.english:
**GIOVANNI ANTONIO MAGINI TO TYCHO BRAHE.**

On the last day of Carnival, Lord Franz Tengnagel came to me — a noble young man, most adorned with every virtue, and just such as you described him to me — who, by delivering to me your letter together with the gift of your little book on Astronomical machines and on the restitution of the fixed stars, so affected my mind with joy that I knew not how to contain myself. But this gladness of mine was somewhat lessened when I learned that he was to depart the next morning toward Florence, and could not relate to me here the things which you had secretly enjoined upon him to communicate with me; he promised me, however, that he would do this after his return to Bologna, about mid-Lent. But he was awaited by me in vain through the whole of Lent — indeed through the whole summer too, since during all this time he stayed at Florence and Rome. Moreover I too, on the 15th of May, removed to Mantua, summoned by the Most Serene Duke of Mantua to instruct his sons, the Princes, in Mathematics; where I remained the whole summer, nor could I return to Bologna before the first of November — the time, namely, of the new [academic] term. But on this return of mine I found a letter from your [man] Franz, by which he advised me that he wished to return to Bologna as soon as possible, so as to lay out for me your desire — which he did two days later, leaving with me at the same time certain writings for the instruction of the said business. Truly this occasion of obliging you was very welcome to me, and more than can be believed — as the outcome of the matter itself, God willing, will clearly declare to you; for I will not now strive to indicate this to you in words, but reserve myself to do it by the very effects. For I have one who will most gladly undertake this charge, who is especially devoted to me; and I have, besides, several learned friends throughout all Italy, who will render every help both to me and to him.

I ought to write more to you, did not the unexpected return of Lord Franz and his early departure stand in the way — especially since I am now beset with many cares and domestic troubles. Yet I will not omit earnestly and most insistently to ask you that you most kindly share with me the **Tables of the motions of the luminaries** composed by you, and perhaps published, together with their use for these present times; for I desire, first of all men, to compose new **Ephemerides** according to your observations; and meanwhile, while you complete the other tables, I shall be able to compute the motions of the luminaries in eclipses, and moreover to erect figures of the Sun's ingress into the cardinal points, and to weigh all the lunations, and from these to weave the annual [astrological] judgements — for, for this business, the calculation of the remaining planets by the usual method of **Copernicus** will suffice.

Of my own state you will be informed more fully by your [man] Franz — namely, that I am laden with disturbances; for which reason I make an end of this letter, asking you earnestly that you take all this in good part, and hold me as a true and sincere friend and most devoted servant. I pray God most good that he may fully satisfy your prayers.

Farewell.
Bologna, 4 November 1599.
Most devoted to Your Very Illustrious Lordship,
Giovanni Antonio Magini,
of Padua.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Giovanni Antonio Magini** (1555–1617), professor of mathematics at **Bologna**, cartographer, ephemeris-maker and practising astrologer — Tycho's principal Italian correspondent (cf. brahe-t_15900911001). He subscribes *Patavinus* ("of Padua," his birthplace). The MS is in the **Archivio Malvezzi de' Medici**, Bologna; the letter was printed in Magini's *Tabulae primi mobilis*.
- **Tengnagel as courier (cross-links).** *Franciscus Tengnalius* = **Franz Tengnagel**, Tycho's assistant (later son-in-law), travelling in Italy — the same figure whose Italian journey frames the Tycho→Galileo and Tycho→Concini letters of 4 May 1600 (brahe-t_16000504002, brahe-t_16000504001) and the Melissus correspondence. He reached Magini *"on the last day of Carnival"* (Shrovetide, early 1599), delivering Tycho's letter and **the gift of two books** — *"the little book on Astronomical machines and on the restitution of the fixed stars,"* i.e. the **_Astronomiae Instauratae Mechanica_ (Wandsbek 1598)** and the **fixed-star catalogue** (the same pairing Tycho presented to Duke Ulrich, brahe-t_15980914002). Tengnagel's movements (Florence, Rome; Magini's own absence at Mantua) delayed delivery of Tycho's confidential message until Magini's return on **1 November 1599**.
- **The "secret business" (*secretum negotium* / *dictum negotium*).** Tycho had charged Tengnagel with a confidential commission for Magini, supported by "certain writings for the instruction of the said business"; Magini promises to further it warmly through "one who will most gladly undertake this charge" and his learned friends across Italy, but pointedly **will not name it in writing** ("I will not indicate this in words, but reserve myself to do it by the very effects"). The referent is not stated; it plausibly concerns Tycho's **Italian observational/placement plans** (cf. the Siena-Academy-and-Egypt observer scheme of brahe-t_16000504001) — flagged as a hypothesis, not asserted.
- **Magini at the Gonzaga court.** *Serenissimus Dux Mantuae* = the **Duke of Mantua** (Vincenzo I Gonzaga); Magini was summoned (from 15 May 1599) to **teach the ducal princes mathematics**, returning to Bologna only for the new academic term on 1 November.
- **The request — Tycho's solar/lunar tables for new ephemerides (astronomy +/).** Magini asks for Tycho's **_Tabulae motuum luminarium_** (tables of the Sun's and Moon's motions) so as to be "**first of all men**" to compute **new Ephemerides** on Tycho's observations: he will calculate the luminaries' motions **in eclipses**, erect **figures of the Sun's ingress into the cardinal points** (the equinox/solstice charts), weigh **all the lunations**, and from these "weave the **annual judgements**" (astrological prognostications) — for which the **Copernican** computation of the other planets "will suffice." A vivid statement of how Tychonic data was wanted to feed the ephemeris-and-prognostication industry.
- **Persons named.** Magini; Franz Tengnagel; the Duke of Mantua; Copernicus.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Bononia 4 Novembris 1599* — Catholic Italy was on the **Gregorian (New Style)** calendar; marked [N.S.]. (Hence too *ultima Bacanalium die* and *dimidium Quadragesimae* reckon the 1599 Roman-rite Carnival/Lent.)

Antonius Maginus, Patavinus' on p.191. Collated the full letter word for word against Dreyer, including every proper name and date: Franciscus Tengnalius (Tengnagel), Bononia/Bologna, the 15th of May remove to Mantua, the Serenissimus Dux Mantuae, return before the first of November, Copernicus, and the closing date 'Bononia 4 Novembris 1599' with signature 'Patavinus'.
