- **Direction & sender.** An **inbound** family letter **to** Tycho. **Erik Brahe Stensen (*Stennonides*, "son of Steen")** — a **nephew of Tycho**, son of Tycho's brother **Steen Brahe** — writing as a young student abroad. Warmly dutiful in tone, it credits Tycho's "authority" with having helped persuade his father to fund the boys' education.
- **Recipient.** **Tycho Brahe**, *Dominus de Knudstrup*, addressed as *patruus* (**paternal uncle**) — the precise kin-term confirming Erik as a brother's son.
- **The student colony at Herborn.** Erik and his companions have been **more than half a year at Herborn** (the Calvinist *Hohe Schule* in Nassau, a noted centre of Reformed learning), intending to stay until **Michaelmas (29 September)**. With him are *frater meus Georgius* = his **brother Jørgen (Georg) Brahe** and *patruelis Falcho* = his **cousin Falk Brahe**, all studying together. They await news from Denmark via *tabellarius Aeschildus* = the **courier Eskild**.
- **Other Danes abroad (the "chatter").**
 - *frater meus Otto … cum Aslachio* = Erik's brother **Otte Brahe**, travelling with **Cort Aslaksen (Aslachius)** (1564–1624), the Danish theologian and natural philosopher — last heard of in **England or Scotland**, now presumed home.
 - *Tago Tot* = **Tage Thott**, a Danish nobleman studying at **Heidelberg**; other noble Danes are said to have gone on to **Geneva**.
- **News from Denmark (datable rumours).**
 - *Aeschildus Sefeldius … subito vita defunctum* = **Eskild Seefeld (Skeel?)**, reported to have **died suddenly just after his daughter's wedding**.
 - *Fridericus Rosenkrantius caussa cecidisse et infamem pronuntiatum* = **Frederik Rosenkrantz** (1571–1602), reported to have **lost his case and been declared infamous** — the legal aftermath of the 1599 court scandal (the affair with Rigborg Brockenhuus) that cost him honour and estates. (The same Frederik Rosenkrantz whose later, "happier breeze" Winshemius reports in brahe-t_16000813001 — the two letters bracket his disgrace and partial rehabilitation.)
- **Place.** *Herborna Nassoviorum* = **Herborn in Nassau**.
- **Epistolary formulae.** The health-formula opening (*Si … vales, … est quod gaudeam; ego … valeo*, the classical *si vales bene est* topos); *T. T.* = *Totus Tuus* ("Wholly yours"); *m. pp.* = *manu propria* ("with his own hand"). *Stennonides* is a patronymic ("son of Steen").
- **Calendar.** Dateline *12 maj anno 1600* at Herborn; no style marker. Reproduced as written, not converted.

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD ANONYMUM.

ILLUSTRIS ET GENEROSE VIR, DOMINE OBSERVANDISSIME.

DE ijs, quæ nuper ad Illustrem Dominationem Vestram per meum, quem isthuc ablegavi, domesticum perscripsi et referri volui, nunc pluribus non agam, ne eadem repetendo ei nimium molestus videar, sperans nihilominus, Illustrem Domem Vestram desiderijs meis lubenti animo annuituram, atque ut res optatum finem sortiatur, effecturam. Verum aliud quid incidit, de quo nunc Dominationem Vestram reverenter et obnixe rogandam duxi. Venit hisce diebus huc e Dania quidam Generosi Stemmatis Iuvenis, e splendidissima et antiquissima ROSENKRANTZIORUM familia isthic oriundus, FRIDERICUS nomine, qui Regis per sexennium Cubicularius fuit. Is militiam aliquandiu sequi et in ea se exercere in animum induxit, et primum Serenissimo Principi, Archiduci Austriæ, Domino MATTHIÆ, Sacræ Cæsareæ Maiestatis, Domini nostri clementissimi, fratri, aliquantisper in aula ipsius Celsitudinis humilime inservire cupit, ut paulatim addiscendo mores et consuetudinem earum regionum in bello Ungarico postea inter equitatus exercitum locum oportunum pro se et sibi inservientibus aliquot equitibus obtinere possit. Quare cum dictus ROSENKRANTZIUS mihi non saltem consanguinitatis iure iunctissimus existat, sed et ab intimis in patria nostra eius de caussa per literas rogatus sim, ut, quantum in me est, conatus ipsius promovere laborem, idcirco ad Illustrem Generositatem Vestram confugio atque ab ea quam officiosissime peto, ut illi literas ad Serenissimum Austriæ Archiducem, Dominum MATTHIAM, intercessorias procurare non degravari velit, quo eo facilius et promptius in eius Celsitudinis aulicum servitium recipi et postea in Ungaria contra Turcas militare et suam fortunam experiri queat, sicque virtutis bellicæ laude, ad quam strenue aspirat (utut aliâs non saltem genere clarus sit, sed et in literis bene versatus, simulque Latinæ, Italicæ, Gallicæ et Hispanicæ linguæ, præter Teutonicam et vernaculam, gnarus) ornatior ad suos aliquando redeat, et Patriæ eo magis in posterum usui esse possit. Sed quia de Illustris Domis Væ erga me singulari benevolentia, quam aliâs satis perspectam habeo, nihil addubitem, eam etiam hac in parte meæ expectationi non defuturam confido. Ideoque illam aliâs occupatissimam ulterius remorari desino. Deus Opt. Max. Illustrem Domem Vestram quam diutissime sospitem conservet.

Dabantur ex arce Cæsarea Benaticka die 15 Maij Anno 1600.
text.english:
**Tycho Brahe to an anonymous [correspondent].**

Illustrious and generous man, most-to-be-revered lord.

Of those matters which I lately wrote out in full to Your Illustrious Lordship through my servant, whom I sent thither, and wished to be reported, I will not now treat at more length, lest by repeating the same I seem too troublesome to you — hoping nonetheless that Your Illustrious Lordship will assent to my desires with willing mind, and will bring it about that the matter reach its wished-for end. But another thing has come up, about which I have now thought to ask Your Lordship, reverently and earnestly. There came hither these days, from Denmark, a certain youth of generous lineage, sprung there from the most splendid and most ancient family of the Rosenkrantzes — Frederik by name — who was for six years Chamberlain to the King. He has resolved to follow soldiering for a time and to train himself in it, and first desires most humbly to serve a while in the court of His Highness the Most Serene Prince, Archduke of Austria, Lord Matthias, brother of His Sacred Imperial Majesty our most clement Lord; so that, gradually learning the manners and usage of those regions, he may afterward, in the Hungarian war, obtain a suitable place among the cavalry, for himself and for several horsemen serving under him. Wherefore, since the said Rosenkrantz is most closely bound to me not only by right of blood-kinship, but I have also been asked by letters, by [my] intimates in our homeland, on his account, to labour — so far as in me lies — to advance his endeavours: I therefore take refuge with Your Illustrious Generosity, and ask of it most dutifully, that you would not find it a burden to procure for him letters of intercession to the Most Serene Archduke of Austria, Lord Matthias, whereby the more easily and readily he may be received into His Highness's court service, and afterward soldier in Hungary against the Turks and try his fortune; and so, with the praise of martial valour to which he strenuously aspires (though otherwise he is not only illustrious by birth, but also well versed in letters, and at the same time skilled in the Latin, Italian, French and Spanish tongues, besides German and his vernacular), he may someday return the more adorned to his own people, and the more be of use to the Fatherland hereafter. But since I doubt nothing of Your Illustrious Lordship's singular benevolence toward me, which I have otherwise sufficiently perceived, I trust that it will not fail my expectation in this part either. And so I cease to detain you, otherwise most busy, any further. May God, best and greatest, preserve Your Illustrious Lordship in safety as long as may be.

Given from the imperial castle of Benátky, the 15th day of May, in the year 1600.

- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe** at **Benátky**.

documents.incipit: MEIN willige dienst mit wunschunge alles gudts beuor. Wollgeborner vnd edler herr, herr …

text.original:
DEM WOLGEBORNEN VNND EDLEN HERRN GOTTFFRYD VON BERBISTORFF, AUFF GRUSCHOW VND STRUCK, RÖMISCH. KEY. MAY. RAADT, MEINEM GUNSTIGEN LIEBEN HERRN, FREUND VND NACHPAREN

MEIN willige dienst mit wunschunge alles gudts beuor. Wollgeborner vnd edler herr, herr Gottfryd von Berbistorff, gunstiger herr vnd freundt. Des herrn schreiben ist mir heute durch dero abgefertigten behendigt, worin ich des herrn freundtlichen guten willen kegen mir erspure, in deme das err mich in diesen nechstkunftigen pfingstagen, nebenst andern seinen freunden zu sich so freundtlich geladen, wor fur ich auch dem herrn, das er mich alss ein frembden vnd vnbekanten dieser örter solche freundtschafft selbstwillig erzeiget, gar dienstlich bedanck, vnd wolte gerne bey dem herrn auf angedeuteten tagk mich einstellen, wen nicht zur selbigen zeit ich anderswo mich hette versprochen. Den wie ich fur 14 tage zu Prage auf des herrn haubtmans von Brandeiss hochzeit gewesen, hab ich dem wolgebornen herren Carll von Wartenberch mussen angeloben, das ich in nebenst dem wollg. herrn Ehrenfridt von Minckwitz kunftigen pfingstage wollte besuchen, vnd ist genanter herr von Wartenbergk seidthero selber alhie bey mir gewesen vnd weiteren beschlus darauf haben wollen, in welchen ich auch consentiert. Es hat auch der obgedachte herr Minkwitz gistern von Prag mir zugeschrieben, das er eigentlich beschlossen, auf zukunftigen donnerstagk oder freitagk aufs lengste alhie (ob Godt will) bey mir zu sein, das wir vns folgendes miteinander konten zu dem herrn von Wartenbergk, wie zugesagt, begeben. Nach dieser gelegenheit, versihe ich, werdt der herr mich entschuldigt haben, das ich auf dissmall, wie ich gerne wolte, nicht kan zu ime kommen. Was aber dissmall, wegen gemelter vhrsachen, nich gescheen kan, gelobe ich dieweill auf einander maell mit Gottes heulffe wiedereinzubringen, vnd will gerne dem herrn, besunders weil wir so nahent nachbar, nach sein wille vnd gelegenheit besuchen; verhoffe, das der herr in demselben widervmb vnbeschwert sich wirt finden lassen. Bitte auch hieneben gantz dienstlich, er wolle alles zum besten ausdeuten vnd aufnemen. Thue hiemit vns beiderseits in gnedigen schutz des Allmechtigen treulich befehlen.

Datirt auf dem keiserlichen hause Bennatick den 15. maj: a:o 1600.
text.english:
**To the well-born and noble Lord Gottfried von Berbisdorf, [lord] of Gruschow and Struck, councillor of the Roman Imperial Majesty, my favourable dear lord, friend and neighbour.**

My willing service, with the wish of all good, beforehand. Well-born and noble lord, Lord Gottfried von Berbisdorf, favourable lord and friend: the gentleman's letter was handed to me today through his dispatched [messenger], wherein I perceive the gentleman's friendly good will toward me, in that he has so kindly invited me, together with his other friends, to him on these coming Whitsun days; for which I also very serviceably thank the gentleman — that he, to me, a stranger and unknown in these parts, has of his own accord shown such friendship — and I would gladly present myself at the gentleman's on the day indicated, were I not at that same time engaged elsewhere. For, as I was a fortnight ago at Prague at the wedding of the lord captain of Brandeis, I had to pledge to the well-born Lord Carl von Wartenberg that I would visit him, together with the well-born Lord Ehrenfried von Minckwitz, next Whitsun; and the said Lord von Wartenberg has since been here with me himself and wished a further arrangement upon it, to which I also consented. The aforesaid Lord Minckwitz, too, wrote to me yesterday from Prague that he has firmly resolved to be here with me (God willing) next Thursday, or Friday at the latest, so that we might thereafter betake ourselves together to the Lord von Wartenberg, as promised. In view of this circumstance, I trust the gentleman will have excused me, that this time, much as I would wish it, I cannot come to him. But what this time, for the reasons stated, cannot take place, I promise meanwhile to make good on another occasion, with God's help; and I will gladly visit the gentleman — especially since we are such near neighbours — according to his will and convenience; and I hope the gentleman will in the same matter again show himself unburdened [i.e. agreeable]. I also ask herewith, quite serviceably, that he be pleased to construe and take everything for the best. Herewith faithfully commending us both to the gracious protection of the Almighty.

Dated at the imperial house of Benátky, the 15th of May, in the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe** at the imperial house of **Benátky nad Jizerou**; a social note **declining a Whitsun invitation** on account of a prior engagement — a glimpse of Tycho's integration into the Bohemian nobility around Benátky.
- **Recipient.** *Gottfried von Berbisdorf, auf Gruschow und Struck, Röm. Kais. Maj. Rat* = **Gottfried von Berbisdorf**, hereditary lord of Gruschow and Struck and a **councillor of the Imperial Majesty (Rudolf II)**, addressed as Tycho's *Herr, Freund und Nachbar* ("lord, friend and neighbour"). Tycho calls himself, with courteous self-deprecation, *ein Fremder und Unbekannter dieser Örter* — "a stranger and unknown in these parts."
- **Persons named.**
 - *der Hauptmann von Brandeis* = the **captain (governor) of Brandýs nad Labem** (Brandeis), at whose Prague wedding (a fortnight earlier) Tycho had made the prior engagement.
 - *Carl von Wartenberg* = **Karl von Wartenberg**, a Bohemian nobleman whom Tycho is bound to visit at Whitsun.
 - *Ehrenfried von Minckwitz* = **Ehrenfried von Minckwitz**, who is to come to Benátky first ("Thursday, or Friday at the latest") so that he and Tycho may go on together to Wartenberg.
- **Place.** *das kaiserliche Haus Bennatick* = the imperial house of **Benátky**; *Prag* = Prague; *Brandeis* = **Brandýs nad Labem**.
- **Register & formulae.** Noble-courteous chancery German, the recipient addressed in the third person as *der Herr* ("the gentleman") throughout. Opening *mein williger Dienst mit Wünschung alles Guten zuvor* → "my willing service, with the wish of all good, beforehand"; *datirt* → "dated." *nechstkünftige Pfingsttage* = the coming days of **Whitsun / Pentecost** (the fixed point around which the social engagements turn).
- **Witness note.** The Basel manuscript is a *Kladde* — a **retained draft / office copy**; the subscription is accordingly not written out.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *den 15. Maij a:o 1600*; the edition marks **n.s. (New Style)**, consistent with Tycho's Imperial-service dating. The movable feast *Pfingsten* (Whitsun) is to be read on the same New-Style reckoning. Reproduced, not converted.

documents.incipit: QUAS circa Martij medietatem ad me dedisti literas, Excellentiss. Domine MONAVI, amice …

text.original:
CLARISSIMO ET EXCELLENTISSIMO VIRO, DOMINO IACOBO MONAVIO, PATRITIO VRATISLAVIENSI, ILLUSTRIS DUCIS SILESIAe CONSILIARIO DIGNISSIMO, AMICO SUO INPRIMIS HONORANDO.

S. P.

QUAS circa Martij medietatem ad me dedisti literas, Excellentiss. Domine MONAVI, amice inprimis honorande, eas nuper accepi, cum autem non suppeteret certus tabellarius, responsionem hucusque distuli, quam etiam nunc accurtare cogor, siquidem plurimis alijs distrahar negotijs, nec tamen per internuntium hunc sponte sese offerentem occasionem datam negligere lubuit. De Typographo itaque vestro sic habe: Videtur is plus iusto poscere, cum Witebergae vel Lipsiae longe minori pretio mea excudi possint, ubi etiam id effici curabo, si propria mea typographia huc satis mature non advenerit.

Domino Doctori FISCHERO brevibus, prout haec otij penuria exigit, rescripsi, ut gratum ipsius in me studium mihi esse cognoscat. Si literas illas SCULTETUS noster ad eum non direxerit, sed ad te pervenerint, ut illi per oportunitatem mittantur, provideas quaeso.

Libros Witichianos me iam facilius obtenturum existimo, quam dum tenax et difficilis eius soror vixit. Non tamen omnes cuperem, sed solummodo eos, quos in apposita scheda ex relatione veteris mei domestici, M. CHRISTIERNI LONGOMONTANI, tibi noti, qui mecum nunc est, denotavi. Si tamen separatim inde nihil relicti pupilli tutores divendere voluerint, me de iusto omnium precio certiorem redde, aut, si fieri possit, solummodo eorum, quos consignavi. Sin vero omnino renuerint inde quippiam distrahere, da saltem operam, ut tua interposita fide eos, quos maxime vellem, per pauculas septimanas mutuo obtineam; restituam ad praefinitum tempus integre et inviolate.

Ad Dominum DANIELEM BUCRETIUM, quem memini me semel atque iterum olim in Insula nostra Uraniburgica invisisse, literas etiam dedi, de observationibus, si quae supersunt, ab haeredibus illius, qui aliquando apud vos fuisse dicitur, Astronomi impetrandis, quas velim illi tradi, et responsum mature urgeri.

Cum ante paucos dies hîc mecum fuisset Generosus Baro CAROLUS de WARTEBERG, catalogum librorum totius Bibliothecae optimae recordationis Domini ANDREAe DUDITHIJ mihi inspiciendum dedit, qui etiamnum penes me est, illi restituendus, cum instantibus diebus festis eum, prout ab eo rogatus promisi, in sua arce 7 miliaribus hinc distante D. V. invisero. Optarem itaque, ut interea ab haeredibus, sive per te ipsum, sive alium aliquem, expiscari velis, an aliquos ex ijs, qui mihi maxime arriserunt, videndi copia concedi possit, et an separatim nonnullos venundare velint; vix enim emptorem pro universa Bibliotheca invenient. Si id, quod desidero, fieri posse, a te intellexero, mittam designationem eorum, quos potissimum expeterem, quod et nunc fecissem, nisi otij penuria omnium plenariam perlustrationem impedivisset.

Caesar necdum Pilsna Pragam reversus est, neque certo constat, quam cito id fiet; speramus tamen statim a Pentecostes festo ipsius Maiestatem adventuram. Aderunt etiam tunc aliquot, uti aiunt, Germaniae Principum Legati. De rebus Ungaricis nihil nobis hîc innotuit, quod non pariter ad vos relatum existimem.

Anglici et Danici Legati nunc Embdae conveniunt, res magni momenti invicem tractaturi, de quibus si inter eos non convenerit, periculum est, ne dissensio illa bellum pariat, quod tamen Deus avertat, cui te tuaque omnia commendo, in quo etiam sanus vale et vive cum omnibus.

Dabantur Benaticae 16 Maij A. 1600.
text.english:
**To the most renowned and most excellent man, Lord Jacob Monau, patrician of Breslau, most worthy Councillor of the Illustrious Duke of Silesia, his friend especially to be honoured.**

Heartiest greeting.

The letter you sent me about the middle of March, most excellent Lord Monau, friend especially to be honoured, I received recently; but since no sure courier was at hand, I have deferred my reply until now — which I am also now compelled to shorten, being distracted by very many other affairs, yet I did not wish to neglect the opportunity given by this messenger offering himself unbidden. Concerning your **Printer**, then, take it thus: he seems to demand more than is fair, since my [works] can be printed at **Wittenberg or Leipzig** at a far lower price — where I will also have it done, if my own printing-press does not arrive here early enough.

To Lord Doctor **Fischer** I have replied briefly, as this scarcity of leisure demands, that he may know his devotion toward me is welcome to me. If our **Scultetus** has not directed those letters to him, but they have come to you, please see that they be sent to him at an opportunity.

The **Wittich books** I think I shall now obtain more easily than while his tenacious and difficult **sister** was alive. Yet I would not want all of them, but only those which I have noted in the appended schedule, from the report of my old servant Master **Christen Longomontanus** — known to you, who is now with me. If, however, the guardians of the orphan left [behind] are unwilling to sell anything from it separately, inform me of the just price of the whole, or, if it can be done, only of those I have listed. But if they altogether refuse to sell anything from it, at least take pains that — your good faith being interposed — I may obtain on loan, for a few weeks, those I most want; I will restore them at the appointed time, whole and unharmed.

To Lord **Daniel Bucretius** — whom I remember to have visited me once and again, formerly, on our island of **Uraniborg** — I have also given a letter, about the **observations**, if any survive, to be obtained from the heirs of that Astronomer who is said once to have been among you; which letter I should wish delivered to him, and a reply pressed in good time.

When, a few days ago, the Generous Baron **Karl von Warttenberg** was here with me, he gave me to inspect the **catalogue of the books of the whole Library of Lord Andreas Dudith of best memory** — which is still with me, to be returned to him when, on the coming feast-days, I shall visit him (as, at his asking, I promised) in his castle, **seven miles** distant from here. I should wish, therefore, that meanwhile you would — through yourself or another — fish out from the **heirs** whether the chance of seeing some of those that most pleased me can be granted, and whether they are willing to sell some separately; for they will scarcely find a buyer for the whole Library. If I learn from you that what I desire can be done, I will send a list of those I should most especially seek — which I would have done even now, had not the scarcity of leisure prevented a full perusal of all.

The Emperor has not yet returned from **Pilsen** to Prague, nor is it certain how soon it will be; yet we hope His Majesty will come immediately after the feast of **Pentecost**. There will then be present too, as they say, some legates of the German Princes. Of **Hungarian** affairs nothing has become known to us here that I do not think has equally been reported to you. The **English and Danish legates** are now meeting at **Emden**, to treat together of matters of great moment; about which, if they do not agree, there is danger lest that dissension breed **war** — which may God avert, to whom I commend you and all yours; in whom also fare well and live, sound, with all [yours].

Given at Benátky, 16 May, the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Jacob Monau (Monavius)** of **Breslau** (cf. brahe-t_16000110001, of which this is the continuation). Tycho's principal Silesian book-agent.
- **Significance — a major book-acquisition / provenance letter.** Three threads:
 1. **The Wittich books (continuation of brahe-t_16000110001).** Tycho expects to obtain them "more easily now that his **tenacious and difficult sister** [the *sister-heir* of the earlier letter] is dead." He wants **not all, but only specific titles** noted in an appended schedule drawn up from the report of **Longomontanus** (who had known Wittich's books at first hand and "is now with me"). The estate has passed to **the guardians of an orphan** (*pupillus*); Tycho offers to buy the whole, or his listed items, or — failing sale — to **borrow** the key books "for a few weeks," on Monau's surety, to be returned "whole and unharmed." A precise window onto the dispersal of **Paul Wittich's library** (incl. the hand-annotated Copernicus copies).
 2. **Daniel Bucretius & the dead Breslau astronomer.** Tycho routes the request for the **observations** of the unnamed deceased Breslau astronomer (cf. brahe-t_16000110001) through **Daniel Bucretius** (Daniel Brouček/Bucretius, the Breslau mathematician who had twice visited Tycho on Hven, and would later help edit Tycho's works; cf. brahe-t_15980627001).
 3. **The library of Andreas Dudith (the notable new item).** **Baron Karl von Warttenberg** had brought Tycho the **catalogue of the whole library of Andreas Dudith** (*Andreas Dudithius*, 1533–1589 — the Hungarian humanist, ex-bishop of Pécs, diplomat and astronomical correspondent, who died at Breslau; a recurring figure in the edition, e.g. brahe-t_15880817001). Tycho, about to visit Warttenberg "in his castle seven miles hence," asks Monau to sound out **Dudith's heirs** whether they will let him see, and **sell separately**, the books that "most pleased" him — "for they will scarcely find a buyer for the whole Library." Tycho will then send a target-list. A first-rate document of Tycho's late library-building and of the **dispersal of Dudith's renowned collection**.
- **Printing.** Monau's Breslau **printer** "demands more than is fair"; Tycho will print at **Wittenberg or Leipzig** instead, unless his **own press** reaches Bohemia in time (cf. the printing plans of brahe-t_16000110001, brahe-t_16010415002).
- **News (spring 1600).** **Rudolf II** still at **Pilsen** (plague-displaced), hoped back after **Pentecost**, with German princes' legates expected; **Hungarian** war-news; and the **Anglo-Danish conference at Emden** (1600 — the disputes over Sound dues / northern trade), which Tycho fears "may breed war."
- **Persons named.** Jacob Monau; **Tobias Fischer** (*Doctor Fischer*, the poet; cf. brahe-t_16000110001); **Bartholomäus Scultetus** (*Scultetus noster*, the Görlitz mathematician); **Paul Wittich** (his sister, the orphan-heir, the guardians); **Christen Longomontanus**; **Daniel Bucretius**; the unnamed dead Breslau astronomer; **Karl von Warttenberg**; **Andreas Dudith** (and his heirs); **Rudolf II**.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Benaticae 16 Maij A. 1600*; **New Style** (imperial). Header agrees with the label.
- **Correction.** Latin corrected from 'septimanae' to 'septimanas' (plural accusative, agreeing with 'pauculas'), per Dreyer, Opera Omnia VIII p.320.

documents.incipit: CLARISSIME et præstantissime vir, accepi quidem literas tuas unâ cum carminibus in mei …

text.original:
CLARISSIMO ET DOCTISSIMO VIRO, DOMINO TOBIÆ FISCHERO, PHILOSOPHIÆ ET MEDICINÆ DOCTORI EXIMIO, AMICO SUO INPRIMIS DILECTO.

CLARISSIME et præstantissime vir, accepi quidem literas tuas unâ cum carminibus in mei gratiam a te eleganter et erudite concinnatis, antecedente anno, cum primum Pragam venissem, a Domino Doctore SWALBIO, communi nostro amico, mihi redditas, tum quoque alteras hoc ipso anno Mense Martio ad me datas. Verum quod hactenus neutris responderim, velim occupationum mearum multitudini, quodque varie interea partim locorum mutationibus, partim alijs impedimentis distractus fuerim, tribuas, meque pro tuo singulari candore excusatum habeas. Fuerunt sane utræque illæ literæ mihi longe acceptissimæ, nam præter insignem humanitatem pari eruditioni coniunctam, quæ inde satis superque elucebat, eximium etiam et sincerum erga me, licet de facie tibi ignotum, amorem et animum candoris integerrimi refertissimum affatim ostendebant, pro qua tua in me sincera, licet antea nihil tale a te promeritum, benevolentia tibi gratias habeo quam maximas, et te vicissim intime diligere, atque in amicorum, quos selectiori albo inscribo, annumerare non desinam, daboque operam, ne te certâsse priorem pœniteat.

Cœterum quod ad carmina illa tua, quæ etiam mihi longe gratissima erant, attinet, velim, ut in meliorem partem accipias, quod paucula quædam in ijs alterârim, prout metri illius genus postulare videbatur secundum eos criticos, qui libertatem illam, qua tu nonnunquam usus es, curiositate quadam non facile admittunt. Quid vero pauculis in locis mutatum sit, carmen illud denuo exaratum et excellentiss. Domino MONAVIO (si recte memini) transmissum patefaciet. Nescio tamen, an ultimus versus isthic ita transformatus sit, prout postea (ni fallor) incidit, qui sic habet:

Gloria vana rudis vulgi, laus una placere
Bonis, malorum negligere calumnias.

Laudo ingenium tuum, laudo venam mellifluam et delicatam, et si plura eiuscemodi aut etiam alio carminis modo per otium luseris mecumque communicaveris, erit id mihi gratum, eaque prioribus adiungam. Coacervo multorum excellentium Poëtarum mea de causa, postquam patria excessi, exarata Poëmata, donec libellum aliquem mediocrem adimpleverim; videbis suo tempore sylvulam.

Opera mea Astronomica tibi impertiri necdum licet, ea enim ad manus non habeo, nam sunt inter res meas, quæ adhuc Magdeburgi reservantur, brevi tamen ex clementissima voluntate Cæsaris huc advehenda, neque etiam omnia, quæ typis prius inchoata habeo, plane ad Colophonem deducta sunt, ob eam, quæ mihi in Patria evenit, studiorum conturbationem. Spero tamen, me, favente divino Numine, cuius provisu Cæsarea Maiestas e tanto naufragio hunc portum, tantisque turbulentijs hoc otium benignissime mihi indulsit, ea, quæ desiderantur, propediem absoluturum, et plura additurum; tunc te voti compotem haud invite reddam, interea morulam intervenientem pro tuo candore in meliorem partem accipe.

Globi MERCATORIS, de quibus scribis, iam ferme antiquati sunt, vixque, quod sciam, reperiuntur exemplaria. Duo talium parandorum artifices Batavi, quorum unus Amsterodami IACOBUS FLORENTIUS, alter Alcmariæ WILHELMUS IANUS nominatus, globos secundum nostram in fixis sideribus restitutionem diligenter elaborârunt. Quorum posterior dimidium annum mecum in Insula nostra Uraniburgica fuit, atque ibidem stellas suo, quod attulit, globoso corpori, me circiter millenas illi concedente, insignivit. Si aliquam ex his nancisci posses reformationem, diceres MERCATORIS vel aliorum globos, ex erroneis stellarum canonibus, non autem cœlitus verificatis locis, conformatos, ijs non æquiparari posse. Nescio, an Francofurtum hi neoterici advehantur, sed si Bohemiam aliquando ingressus me inviseris, exemplum monstrabo, tunc simul alia, quæ penes me elaborata habeo, siquidem te etiam his studijs affici videam, lubens ostendam, tecumque de talibus iucunde conferam.

Vale.
Dabantur ex arce Cæsarea Benatika 16 Maij A. 1600.
text.english:
**To the most renowned and most learned man, Lord Tobias Fischer, distinguished Doctor of Philosophy and Medicine, his friend especially beloved.**

Most renowned and most excellent man, I did indeed receive your letter, with the poems elegantly and learnedly composed by you in my honour — delivered to me last year, when I had first come to Prague, by Lord Doctor **Schwalb**, our common friend — and also others, sent me this very year in the month of March. But that I have hitherto answered neither, I would have you attribute to the multitude of my occupations, and to my being meanwhile variously distracted, partly by changes of place, partly by other impediments; and hold me excused, after your singular candour. Both those letters were indeed far most welcome to me: for besides the remarkable humanity joined to equal erudition, which shone forth from them more than enough, they abundantly showed an exceptional and sincere love toward me — though unknown to you by face — and a mind most full of the most upright candour; for which sincere benevolence of yours toward me (though I had previously deserved nothing such from you) I give you the greatest thanks, and will not cease, in turn, to love you intimately and to count you among the friends I inscribe on the more select roll; and I will take pains that you do not regret having striven first [in friendship].

For the rest, as concerns those poems of yours — also far most pleasing to me — I would have you take in good part that I altered a very few things in them, as the kind of that metre seemed to demand, according to those critics who do not easily admit, with a certain fastidiousness, that liberty which you have sometimes used. What has been changed in a very few places, that poem — written out anew and sent to the most excellent Lord **Monau** (if I rightly remember) — will reveal. Yet I know not whether the last verse there was so transformed as it afterward (unless I am mistaken) occurred [to me], which runs thus:

*"The glory of the rude crowd is vain; the one [true] praise is to please*
*the good, [and] to disregard the calumnies of the wicked."*

I praise your genius, I praise your mellifluous and delicate vein; and if you compose more of this kind — or even in another manner of poem — at leisure, and share them with me, it will be welcome, and I will add them to the earlier ones. I am heaping up the Poems composed by many excellent Poets on my account, since I left my fatherland, until I shall have filled some moderate little book; you will see in time a little **sylva** [collection].

My **Astronomical works** I cannot yet impart to you, for I do not have them at hand: they are among my things still kept at **Magdeburg**, soon however to be brought hither by the Emperor's most clement will; nor are all the things I had earlier begun in print quite brought to the colophon, on account of that disturbance of my studies which befell me in my fatherland. Yet I hope — by the favour of the divine Power, by whose provision the Imperial Majesty most kindly granted me this harbour out of so great a shipwreck, and this leisure out of so great turbulences — soon to complete what is wanting, and to add more; then I will, not unwillingly, make you master of your wish; meanwhile take the intervening little delay in good part, after your candour.

The **globes of Mercator**, about which you write, are now almost antiquated, and scarcely, so far as I know, are copies to be found. **Two Dutch craftsmen for making such [globes]** — one at **Amsterdam, named Jacobus Florentius**, the other at **Alkmaar, named Wilhelm Janus** — have diligently elaborated globes **according to our restitution in the fixed stars**. Of these, the **latter was with me half a year on our island of Uraniborg, and there marked the stars upon the globe-body he had brought — I granting him about a thousand**. If you could obtain one of these renewed [globes], you would say that Mercator's globes, or others' — fashioned from erroneous star-catalogues, not from positions verified from the sky — cannot be matched with them. I know not whether these new ones are brought to Frankfurt; but if, having entered Bohemia at some time, you visit me, I will show you a specimen; then at the same time I will gladly show you other things I have elaborated, if I see you too taken with these studies, and will pleasantly confer with you about such matters.

Farewell.
Given from the imperial castle of Benátky, 16 May, the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient & occasion.** Tycho's **reply to Tobias Fischer** (the Silesian poet-physician of Schweidnitz; cf. his letter brahe-t_16000318001), written the same day as the Monau letter (brahe-t_16000516001). Tycho admits Fischer to his friendship and thanks him for two sets of verses (delivered via **Doctor Schwalb**, *Swalbius*, in 1599 and March 1600).
- **The poems and the *sylvula*.** Tycho explains his **emendation** of Fischer's verses (tightening a metrical "liberty" the strict critics dislike), the corrected copy sent to **Monau**, and quotes the **revised closing distich** — *"Gloria vana rudis vulgi, laus una placere / Bonis, malorum negligere calumnias"* ("the glory of the rude crowd is vain; the one praise is to please the good and ignore the wicked's calumnies"). He is **collecting friends' commendatory poems** "since I left my fatherland" into a planned **little *sylva*** (verse-anthology in his honour).
- **His works still at Magdeburg.** Tycho cannot yet send his **astronomical works** (still stored at **Magdeburg**, awaiting the imperial transport; the *Progymnasmata* not yet "brought to the colophon" because of "the disturbance … in my fatherland"). The "harbour out of so great a shipwreck … this leisure out of so great turbulences" is his standard figure for the imperial refuge.
- **Significance — the Tychonic celestial globes and Willem Jansz (Blaeu) at Uraniborg (cornerstone of cartographic history).** Asked about **Mercator's globes** ("now almost antiquated"), Tycho names **two Dutch globe-makers who built globes on his restored star-positions**:
 - **Jacobus Florentius of Amsterdam** = **Jacob Floris van Langren** (of the Van Langren globe-making house);
 - **Wilhelm Janus of Alkmaar** = **Willem Janszoon (Blaeu)** (1571–1638), the future great Amsterdam cartographer.
 **The latter "was with me half a year on the island of Uraniborg, and there marked the stars on the globe-body he had brought, I granting him about a thousand."** This is Tycho's own testimony to **Blaeu's ~half-year stay at Hven (1595–96) and the c. 1,000 Tychonic star-positions** he set on his celestial globe — the documentary basis for the **Blaeu globes** carrying Tycho's catalogue, far superior to globes "from erroneous star-catalogues, not positions verified from the sky." (This **resolves the "Dutch globe-maker" item** flagged from brahe-t_16000506001, where Tycho's gift-globe to Elector Christian II was made by "a skilled Dutchman at Uraniborg" — i.e. Blaeu.)
- **Persons named.** Tobias Fischer; **Bartholomäus Schwalb** (*Swalbius*); **Jacob Monau**; **Mercator** (Gerardus); **Jacob Floris van Langren** (*Jacobus Florentius*); **Willem Janszoon Blaeu** (*Wilhelm Janus* of Alkmaar); **Rudolf II**.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Benatika 16 Maij A. 1600*; **New Style** (imperial). Header agrees with the label.

documents.abstract: Invokes their old Uraniborg acquaintance and asks Bucretius to help locate a Breslau figure known to have been devoted to astronomy or judicial astrology.
documents.incipit: CLARISSIME et praestantissime vir, vetus illa inter nos, cum me in Insula prioris …

text.original:
CLARISSIMO ET PRÆSTANTISSIMO VIRO, DOMINO DANIELI BUCRETIO, PHILOSOPHIAe ET MEDICINAe DOCTORI EXIMIO VRATISLAVIAe DEGENTI, AMICO SUO INPRIMIS DILECTO.

S. P.

CLARISSIME et praestantissime vir, vetus illa inter nos, cum me in Insula prioris habitationis Uraniburgica, dum in iuventute peregrinareris, semel atque iterum invisisti, contracta notitia, cuius te adhuc memorem esse non dubito, efficit, ut eo liberius hoc tempore ad te scribam, praesertim cum aliquid inciderit, in quo tua opera mihi usui esse possit, quod et te mihi non denegaturum, singularis tua humanitas et erga me, prout a M. CHRISTIERNO LONGOMONTANO, qui ante biennium apud vos fuit, et nunc apud me est, intellexi, benevolum studium, alias etiam mihi perspectum, fidem facit. Est autem eiuscemodi.

Retulit mihi priori anno excellentiss. vir, Dominus D. HIERONIMUS TREUTLERUS, cum simul Pragae essemus, Vratislavij aliquando fuisse Astronomiae vel etiam Astrologiae iudiciariae impense addictum virum, quem observationes quasdam in motu Astrorum obtinuisse aiebat, quas etiamnum filius eius secum reservârit. Quare te per veterem nostram amicitiam rogatum cuperem, ut a filio illo vel alijs haeredibus mihi observationum illarum, quotquot adhuc in promptu sunt, copiam impetrare velis. Etsi enim vix credere queam, eas ad tantam praecisionem deductas esse, quantam ego in talibus requiro, et rei inquirendae subtilitas per se postulat, cum idoneis organis proculdubio destitutus fuerit, tamen qualescunque tandem sunt, eas obtinere averem. Est aliquid prodire tenus, si non datur ultra. Si itaque id, quicquid est observationum, ad mundum accurate descriptum, tua intercessione et diligentia consecutus fuero, officium, quovis alio, quantum per me licet, compensandum, mihi hac ratione praestiteris. Vale. Plura enim ob aliarum occupationum molem nunc non vacat. Salutat te supradictus M. CHRISTIERNUS officiose, et pro pristinis illi, cum apud vos esset, beneficijs, non saltem is, sed et ego, gratias agimus. Scripturus est ipsemet tibi, cum rectius vacârit.

Iterum quam felicissime vale.
Datae ex arce Caesarea Benatika 16 Maij A. 1600.
text.english:
**To the most renowned and excellent man, Lord Daniel Bucretius, distinguished doctor of philosophy and medicine, dwelling at Breslau, his especially beloved friend.**

Heartiest greeting.

Most renowned and excellent Sir: that old acquaintance struck up between us — when, travelling in your youth, you visited me once and again on the island of my former dwelling, Uraniborg — of which I do not doubt you are still mindful, makes me write to you the more freely at this time, especially since something has arisen in which your service may be of use to me; and that you will not deny me this, your singular kindness, and the well-disposed zeal toward me (as I have understood from Master Christen Longomontanus, who was with you two years ago and is now with me), elsewhere too well known to me, give me assurance. The matter is of this kind.

Last year the most excellent man, Lord Doctor Hieronymus Treutler, related to me, when we were together at Prague, that there had once been at Breslau a man earnestly devoted to Astronomy — or even to judicial Astrology — who, he said, had obtained certain observations in the motion of the stars, which his son still keeps by him. Wherefore I should wish to ask you, by our old friendship, that you would obtain for me from that son, or from the other heirs, a copy of those observations, as many as are still at hand. For although I can scarcely believe that they were brought to such precision as I require in such matters, and as the delicacy of the inquiry itself demands — since he was doubtless destitute of suitable instruments — yet, whatever in the end they are, I should be eager to obtain them. It is something to advance so far, if it is not granted [to go] beyond. If therefore I shall, through your intercession and diligence, come into possession of whatever there is of these observations, accurately copied out fair, you will have rendered me by this means a service to be repaid by any other, so far as lies in my power. Farewell — for more there is now no leisure, owing to the mass of other occupations. The aforesaid Master Christen greets you dutifully; and for the former kindnesses [shown] him while he was with you, not only he but I too render thanks. He will write to you himself when he has the better leisure.

Again, most happily, farewell.
Given from the Imperial castle of Benátky, the 16th of May, in the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe** at **Benátky nad Jizerou**, shortly before the move to Prague; the letter belongs to his campaign to gather and absorb earlier observational data into his own restored astronomy.
- **Recipient.** **Daniel Bucretius**, doctor of philosophy and medicine, *Vratislaviae degens* — **resident at Breslau (Wrocław)**. Tycho recalls that Bucretius had, in his youthful travels, visited him *more than once* on Hven; he is used here as a local intermediary at Breslau.
- **Persons named.**
 - *M. Christiernus Longomontanus* = **Christen Sørensen Longomontanus** (1562–1647), Tycho's longest-serving and most senior assistant, who had himself been at Breslau "two years ago" and is now back with Tycho; he both vouches for Bucretius's goodwill and adds his own greeting.
 - *Dominus D. Hieronymus Treutlerus* = **Hieronymus Treutler (Treutler von Krottendorf)** (1565–1607), jurist, the informant (met at Prague the previous year) for the report of the Breslau observer.
 - The **unnamed Breslau astronomer/astrologer**, *Astronomiae vel etiam Astrologiae iudiciariae impense addictus*, deceased, whose **son** (or other heirs) is said to retain his *observationes in motu astrorum*. He is not identified in the source; Tycho's request is precisely to recover whatever survives of his papers.
- **Astronomy.** *observationes … in motu astrorum* = **observations of the motion of the stars**; *praecisio* = **precision**; *idonea organa* = **suitable instruments** (*organa* in Tycho's sense,) — the lack of which makes Tycho doubt the data's accuracy even as he seeks it. The *Astronomia / Astrologia iudiciaria* distinction (mathematical astronomy vs. **judicial astrology**) is kept as written.
- **Allusion.** *Est aliquid prodire tenus, si non datur ultra* adapts **Horace, *Epistles* I.1.32** (*est quādam prodire tenus, si non datur ultra*) — "it is something to advance so far, if to go further is not granted"; the literary tag is preserved and glossed, not paraphrased away.
- **Place.** *arx Caesarea Benatika* = the **Imperial castle of Benátky**; *Vratislavia* = **Breslau / Wrocław**.
- **Epistolary formulae.** *S. P.* = *salutem plurimam* ("heartiest greeting"). *Vale … iterum quam felicissime vale* → "Farewell … again, most happily, farewell." *Datas* (sc. *literas*, epistolary) → "Given."
- **Calendar.** Dateline *16 Maij A. 1600*; edition marks **n.s.** (New Style), consistent with the Benátky/Prague series of this month. Reproduced, not converted.
- **Correction.** Latin: 'invasisti' corrected to 'invisisti', and 'Datas' corrected to 'Datae', per Dreyer, Opera Omnia VIII, pp. 323-324.

translation.warrant:
Collated against **Dreyer, *Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia*** (the edition of record), reading the printed page images. Read the full Dreyer extract (pages 1-4, TBOO VIII pp. 322-325) as page images; the Bucretius letter itself occupies pp. 323-324, which were also each re-read individually to check two disputed words closely. Collated the full letter clause-by-clause: heading/address, opening line, the Longomontanus/Treutler/observations narrative, every proper name (Daniel Bucretius, Christiernus Longomontanus, Hieronimus Treutlerus), place names (Uraniburgica, Vratislavia/Breslau, Praga, Benatika/Benátky), the biennium figure, and the closing date (16 Maij 1600) against the transcribed original and the published English. Found no fabrication, omission, mistranslation, or hedge-loss in the English translation — it is faithful sentence-by-sentence, and in both disputed spots below it actually follows Dreyer's correct reading rather than our own (corrupted) the transcribed original. Found two text error instances where the transcribed original itself departs from Dreyer ('invasisti' for Dreyer's 'invisisti'; 'Datas' for Dreyer's 'Datae'). Per the grading rule, any text error caps the grade at C regardless of translation quality, so grade is C; verdict is *minor* since neither defect changes the sense actually delivered to a reader of the English translation.

**2 defects found:**
- **text error** (medium). The transcribed original reads 'invasisti' (from invado, 'you invaded/attacked'), but Dreyer's print clearly shows 'invisisti' (from inviso, 'you visited') — two different verbs, not a spelling variant. The published English correctly follows Dreyer's 'invisisti' ('you visited'), so the translation itself is unaffected, but our stored Latin the transcribed original is corrupted relative to the edition of record. Dreyer prints: *femel atque iterum invifisti (= invisisti) — p. 323, line 17*.
- **text error** (low). The transcribed original reads 'Datas', Dreyer prints 'Datae' (the standard closing formula, agreeing with implied litterae). The English 'Given' is compatible with either reading, so no translation-level consequence, but it is a real divergence between the transcribed original and Dreyer. Dreyer prints: *Datae ex arce Cæfarea Benatika 16 Maij A. 1600. — p. 324, line 4*.

**Repaired.** Verified both defects by direct visual inspection of the Dreyer TBOO VIII pp.322-325 page images. 'invififti' (p.323) and 'Datae' (p.324) are both unambiguous. Neither correction affects the English translation, which was already faithful to Dreyer's readings. No other divergence from Dreyer was found in this letter.

documents.abstract: Certifies that Kepler spent four months (February–May 1600) at Benátky working diligently on astronomical exercises with Tycho's instruments and observations.
documents.incipit: EGO TYCHO BRAHE de Knudstrup et Uraniburg in Regno Daniæ, nunc vero Sacræ Cæsæ Matis …

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD IOANNEM KEPLERUM.

EGO TYCHO BRAHE de Knudstrup et Uraniburg in Regno Daniæ, nunc vero Sacræ Cæsæ Matis cliens in arce Bohemiæ Bennaticha habitans, notum facio omnibus et singulis hasce litteras inspecturis, cuiuscunque status, dignitatis et conditionis fuerint, earundem exhibitorem, ornatissimum et eruditissimum virum M. KEPLERUM, Ill. Ducatus Styriæ Statuum Mathematicum, hoc labente Anno Epochæ Christianæ 1600 ab initio mensis Februarij usque ad finem Maij, per quatuor nimirum intercedentes menses pro maiori parte hîc in dicta Cæsaris arce Bennaticha mecum fuisse, seque interea in meo convictu honeste gessisse et apprime diligentem operam in exercitijs et studijs Astronomicis præstitisse, intermediantibus meis iustæ magnitudinis et conformationis instrumentis et observationibus multiplicibus atque diutinis, mutuaque inter nos de talibus atque alijs ad Philosophiam facientibus collocutione: ut omnino mihi persuadeam, illum id temporis non minus frugifero hîc collocasse, quam si interea domi desedisset, imo si absque invidia id affirmare liceret, longe utilius. Quo nomine etiam eius præsentia et conversatio mihi imprimis grata extitit, multoque adhuc gratior futura, si eadem in posterum sæpius et diutius concedi poterit.

Quapropter omnibus illustribus, præstantibus et cordatis viris prænominatum M. KEPLERUM de meliore nota quam commendatissimum esse cupio, utque eius laudabile propositum et conatus egregios in hac sublimi et a vulgi captu semota scientia ulterius et plenius excolenda adiuvent et promoveant, quibus possum precibus obnixe et officiose rogo atque obtestor: fecerint sic meo equidem iudicio Reipubl. litterariæ, præcipue vero divinæ illius Astronomiæ totiusque eruditæ Matheseos alumnis rem admodum utilem atque acceptam, quin et non saltem ipsi M. KEPLERO commodam, sed et mihi ob conformia studia longe gratissimam, ac quocunque per me licuerit officio vicissim compensandam et obsequiosa mente perpetuo recolendam. In quorum omnium evidentiorem et pleniorem testificationem sigillum meum apposui et propria manu subscripsi.

Actum in arce Cæsarea Bennaticha inchoante mense Iunio Anno 1600.
TYCHO BRAHE,
manu propria.
text.english:
**Tycho Brahe, [concerning] Johannes Kepler.**

I, Tycho Brahe of Knudstrup and Uraniborg in the Kingdom of Denmark, but now client of His Sacred Imperial Majesty, dwelling in the Bohemian castle of Benátky, make known to each and all who shall inspect this letter, of whatever status, dignity and condition they may be, that the bearer of the same — the most accomplished and most learned man, Master Kepler, Mathematician of the Estates of the Illustrious Duchy of Styria — in this passing Year of the Christian Era 1600, from the beginning of February until the end of May, that is, through the four intervening months, was for the greater part here with me in the said Imperial castle of Benátky; and that he meanwhile conducted himself honourably in my company, and rendered exceptionally diligent work in astronomical exercises and studies — with the mediation of my instruments of fitting size and construction and of my manifold and long-continued observations, and of our mutual conversation about these matters and others conducing to Philosophy — so that I am wholly persuaded that he spent that time here no less fruitfully than if he had meanwhile sat at home, nay (if it might be affirmed without envy) far more usefully. On which account his presence and converse was especially welcome to me, and will be much more welcome still, if the same may in time to come be granted more often and for longer.

Wherefore I desire that the aforenamed Master Kepler be most warmly commended, in the best regard, to all illustrious, excellent and sensible men; and with what prayers I can I earnestly and dutifully ask and beseech them to aid and promote his laudable purpose and his outstanding endeavours toward the further and fuller cultivation of this sublime science, set apart from the grasp of the common crowd. They will thus, in my judgement, do a thing very useful and welcome to the Republic of Letters, but especially to the nurslings of that divine Astronomy and of all learned Mathematics; nay, a thing not only of advantage to Master Kepler himself, but also — on account of our kindred studies — far most pleasing to me, to be repaid in turn by whatever service shall lie in my power, and perpetually cherished with an obliging mind. In clearer and fuller testification of all which, I have affixed my seal and subscribed with my own hand.

Done in the Imperial castle of Benátky, at the beginning of the month of June, in the year 1600.
TYCHO BRAHE,
with his own hand.

documents.apparatus:
- **Genre.** This is not an ordinary letter but an **open testimonial / letter of recommendation** (*litterae testimoniales*) — a public certificate, drawn in the notarial first person (*Ego Tycho Brahe … notum facio omnibus et singulis hasce litteras inspecturis*), sealed and autograph, attesting Kepler's residence and conduct and commending him to "all illustrious men." The heading *ad Ioannem Keplerum* in the source marks the subject; the document was given **to** Kepler to carry (*earundem exhibitorem*, "the bearer of the same").
- **Occasion.** It closes **Kepler's first stay with Tycho** — from the beginning of February to the end of May 1600, the very months of their first collaboration at Benátky (Kepler had arrived 4 February). Tycho here certifies that period and, by commending Kepler to patrons, smooths his position as he returned to Graz amid the Styrian Counter-Reformation expulsions. Within months Kepler would join Tycho's household permanently; on Tycho's death (24 October 1601) he succeeded him as Imperial Mathematician and inherited the observations this document describes.
- **Self-titling.** *Tycho Brahe de Knudstrup et Uraniburg in Regno Daniae, nunc vero Sacrae Caesareae Maiestatis cliens* — Tycho styles himself by his Danish patrimony (**Knudstrup**) and his lost observatory (**Uraniborg** on Hven,), "but now **client** [retainer] of His Sacred Imperial Majesty" (**Rudolf II**), resident at Benátky.
- **Kepler's title.** *M. Keplerus, Ill. Ducatus Styriae Statuum Mathematicus* = **Johannes Kepler**, *Magister* (academic Master,), **mathematician to the Estates of the Duchy of Styria** (his Graz appointment as *Landschaftsmathematiker*).
- **Astronomy.** *mea iustae magnitudinis et conformationis instrumenta et observationes multiplices atque diutinae* = Tycho's **instruments** (*instrumenta/organa*,) "of fitting size and construction" and his "manifold and long-continued **observations**" — the working capital of the Benátky establishment that Kepler had been set to use (notably on the Mars data). *exercitia et studia Astronomica* rendered "astronomical exercises and studies."
- **Formulae.** *Respublica litteraria* → "the Republic of Letters"; *Astronomiae … alumni* → "the nurslings of Astronomy"; *Actum* → "Done"; *manu propria* → "with his own hand" (autograph + seal attestation). The humility/"without envy" topos (*absque invidia*) is preserved.
- **Calendar & dating crux.** The subscription reads *inchoante mense Iunio Anno 1600* — "**at the beginning of June 1600**" — and the body's own span (*ab initio mensis Februarij usque ad finem Maij … per quatuor intercedentes menses*) requires a date *after* the end of May. The header therefore **leads with the as-written date (beginning of June 1600)**; the edition's catalogue label "**1600. april**" disagrees and is recorded as *(catalogued April 1600)* by this chapter's convention, **not** silently adopted. The April label is most likely a catalogue mis-entry, since the text cannot have been written before the residence it certifies had ended. No calendar-style marker (O.S./N.S.) is given; in Imperial service Tycho was by now dating New Style (cf. the surrounding 1600 letters), but the testimonial states no style, so none is asserted here.
- **Witnesses.** Two Vienna manuscripts (ÖNB cod. lat. 10703 and 10686) preserve the text within the Tychonic/Keplerian *Nachlass* — the same Vienna codices that hold much of the observational archive (cf. the KB↔Vienna collation work).

Read the Dreyer page images (TBOO VIII pp. 323-326) visually, not digitised text layer. The letter text on pp. 324-325 (heading 'TYCHO BRAHE AD IOANNEM KEPLERUM' through 'manu propria.') matches the transcribed original word for word, including every proper name (Knudstrup, Uraniburg/Uraniborg, Bennaticha/Benátky, KEPLERUM), number (1600 x3, 'four intervening months' = Feb-May inclusive), and date formula. Specifically checked the flagged day-number concern: the closing reads 'Actum in arce Caesarea Bennaticha inchoante mense Iunio Anno 1600' in both the transcribed original and Dreyer's print — 'inchoante mense Iunio' (beginning of the month of June) with no day-number given, matching the record's date '1600-06-00' and rendered correctly in English as 'at the beginning of the month of June' with no invented day. Compared every clause of the published English against the transcribed original sentence by sentence: no fabricated names/numbers/clauses, no silently dropped sentences, no flipped pronouns/antecedents (all 'he'/'his' correctly track Kepler throughout, all 'my'/'I' correctly track Tycho, including the seal/subscription clause), no hardened hedges. Word order and some connective-phrase rendering (e.g. 'nimirum' as 'that is') differ but do not change meaning, per the audit's instruction to ignore such variance.

documents.incipit: MAGNIFICE Domine TYCHO, Vir praestantissime: Non vulgari laetitia fui affectus, quando …

text.original:
MAGNIFICO NOBILISSIMO ET AMPLISSIMO VIRO D. TYCHONI BRAHE, MATHEMATICORUM SECULI NOSTRI ET PRÆSERTIM APUD SACRATISSIMAM CÆSAREAM MAIESTATEM PRINCIPI, DOMINO ET AMICO SUMME OBSERVANDO. BENNATICAe BOHEMORUM.

MAGNIFICE Domine TYCHO, Vir praestantissime: Non vulgari laetitia fui affectus, quando mihi redditae sunt literae tuae XVI Maij scriptae, e quibus libentissime cognovi, meas, quas mense Martio scripseram, rectâ pervenisse in manus tuas. Eram enim de ijs nonnihil sollicitus, postquam missae fuerant ad illum, quem Pragae non invenerant.

Ad typographum nostrum quod attinet, facile poteram cogitare hoc ipsum, quod contigit: nimirum te pretio magis aequo posse alicubi locorum curare tua inprimenda, quam apud nos, ubi non sunt omnia sic expedita et in promptu. Boni tamen consules meum studium qualecunque gratificandi tuis postulatis et desiderijs: opto ex animo, ut in re alia possim tibi probare meum animum tibi deditissimum.

Ad Doctorem BUCRETIUM quod attinet: is te amanter, diligenter et officiose rogat, et pro missis literis humaniss. magnas agit gratias. Bene te iubeo sperare et de Wittichianis reliquijs et de chartis alterius illius, qui quondam apud nos vixit, Astronomi. Utroque loco hanc rem tanta et fide et diligentia et tam accurate et sedulo egit et adhuc agit, ut non dubitem nos habituros, quod optamus. Non voluit nunc respondere literis tuis, quod confidat se propediem reipsa votis tuis satisfacturum: modo parvam moram aequo feras animo, magnopere te rogatum volo.

Domino Doctori FISCHERO, Viro certe opt. et doctissimo, gratissimae fuerunt literae tuae, daturo modis omnibus operam, ut suam tibi fidem et diligentiam omni, quod a se praestare poterit, officio probet. Nec te spero unquam poenitebit tuae in ipsum benevolentiae.

De Bibliotheca Duditiana, quae mihi est notissima, velim mihi credas. Eam nunc velut inter coelum et terram pendere, postquam ab haeredibus DUDITIJ non possidetur, sed alteri cuidam pro certa pecuniae summa non tam vendita est quam oppignorata. Iacet nunc misera apud nos in domo quadam, et non aliter iacet (vidi enim aliquoties) quam solent apud nobiles iacere acervi frumentorum: neque in illam plenum ius habet Emtor neque etiam venditor. Res plane intricata est, et metuo, ne libri isti magnum aliquod et irreparabile damnum accipiant.

Dictum mihi est nuper ab amico quodam, instrumenta tua Mathematica non levi iactura fuisse per vim ventorum et tempestatum in arce istac tua affecta. Si ita est, admodum tibi condoleo. Dubito tamen, an sit, cum tu nullam eius rei mentionem facias.

Magnificus huius urbis et Ducatus Capitaneus, Dn. ABRAHAMUS IENGTIUS, olim summi nostri WITICHIJ, dum viveret, patronus, tui amantiss. et studiosissimus, magnopere te salutat. Cogitat paulo post ad thermas Boiemicas proficisci, et plane constituit in illo itinere te convenire, ut te videat coram, quem dudum est unice miratus. Dixit ei nuper Doctor IESSENIUS de quodam libro tuo recens edito, quem obtuleris Caesari. Eum ipse unice videre gestit, et iam semel et iterum an viderim ex me quaesivit. Epistolarum tuarum volumen, quod ex dono liberalitatis tuae habeo, apud me primus vidit, et per aliquot dies secum habuit.

Si quid ad me scribere aut mittere voles, scias rectissime ad me perventurum, quicquid Pragam per certos homines miseris ad Dn. IOANNEM MYLLNERUM, Sacrae Caesae Matis Consiliarium et Regni Boem. Secretarium supremum, Compatrem meum cariss. et omni fide observandum. Apud illum enim vivit IOANNES PALUDIUS, Principis mei Consiliarius Pragae habitans et negotia Cels. suae in aula illa curans. Is et diligenter et libenter curabit, quicquid ad me pertinens acceperit. Bene et feliciter vale, Vir praestantissime, et me, quem semel amare coepisti, perpetuo amare perge: sic te vicissim curet ametque Deus.

Vratisl. XIIIJ Iunij 1600.
T. Μ. P. observantiss. et amantiss.
IAC. MONAW.
text.english:
**To the magnificent, most noble, and most ample man, Lord Tycho Brahe, Prince of the Mathematicians of our age — and especially with the most sacred Imperial Majesty — his Lord and friend most highly to be respected. [To] Benátky of the Bohemians.**

Magnificent Lord Tycho, most excellent Man: I was filled with no common joy when your letter, written **16 May**, was delivered to me, from which I most gladly learned that mine, which I had written in **March**, came straight into your hands; for I was somewhat anxious about them, after they had been sent to him whom they had not found at Prague.

As concerns our **printer**, I could easily imagine this very thing which happened — namely, that you can have your works printed somewhere at a fairer price than with us, where not everything is so expedited and ready at hand. Yet you will take in good part my zeal, such as it is, to gratify your requests and desires; I wish from my heart that in some other matter I may prove to you my mind most devoted to you.

As concerns **Doctor Bucretius**: he greets you lovingly, diligently, and dutifully, and gives great thanks, most courteously, for the letters sent. I bid you hope well **both of the Wittich remains and of the papers of that other Astronomer who once lived among us**. In both cases he has dealt, and still deals, with the matter with such faith and diligence, and so accurately and assiduously, that I do not doubt we shall have what we wish. He did not wish now to answer your letters, because he trusts he will soon satisfy your wishes in deed; only bear a small delay with an even mind — which I greatly ask you to do.

To Lord **Doctor Fischer**, a man certainly most good and most learned, your letter was most welcome; he will give effort in every way to prove to you his faith and diligence by every service he can render. Nor, I hope, will you ever regret your benevolence toward him.

Concerning the **Library of Dudith**, which is very well known to me, I would have you believe me: it now hangs, as it were, **between heaven and earth** — since it is not possessed by Dudith's heirs, but has been, to a certain other party for a fixed sum of money, **not so much sold as pawned**. It now lies wretched among us in a certain house, and lies no otherwise (for I have seen it several times) than heaps of grain are wont to lie in the houses of the nobles: neither has the **buyer** full right in it, nor the **seller**. The matter is plainly entangled, and I **fear lest those books take some great and irreparable harm**.

It was lately told me by a certain friend that your **Mathematical instruments** had been damaged, with no slight loss, by the force of winds and storms in that castle of yours. If it is so, I greatly condole with you; yet I doubt whether it is, since you make no mention of the matter.

The Magnificent **Captain of this city and Duchy, Lord Abraham Jengtius** — formerly, while he lived, the patron of our great **Wittich**, most loving and devoted to you — greets you greatly. He thinks of setting out a little later to the **Bohemian baths**, and has fully resolved on that journey to meet you, that he may see in person you whom he has long uniquely admired. **Doctor Jessenius** lately told him of a certain book of yours recently published, which you had offered to the Emperor; he longs uniquely to see it, and has now once and again asked me whether I have seen it. The volume of your **Letters**, which I have from the gift of your liberality, he first saw at my house, and had with him for several days.

If you wish to write or send anything to me, know that whatever you send to Prague by sure men, to Lord **Johann Myllner**, Councillor of the Sacred Imperial Majesty and Supreme Secretary of the Kingdom of Bohemia — my dearest gossip, and to be trusted in all faith — will come most directly to me. For with him lives **Johann Paludius**, Councillor of my Prince, dwelling at Prague and managing his Highness's affairs at that court; he will both diligently and gladly take care of whatever pertaining to me he receives. Fare well and happily, most excellent Man, and continue to love perpetually me whom you once began to love; so may God in turn care for you and love you.

Wrocław, 14 June 1600.
Most respectful and most loving of Your Magnificence,
Jacob Monau.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender & occasion.** **Jacob Monau (Monavius)** of **Breslau (Wrocław)** — this is his **reply to Tycho's letter of 16 May 1600 (brahe-t_16000516001)**, answering it point by point (and confirming that Monau's own March letter, brahe-t_16000110001's antecedent, had reached Tycho after going astray "to him whom it had not found at Prague").
- **Significance — a major book-provenance letter (the fate of two libraries).**
 - **The Dudith Library (vivid and important).** Monau, "to whom it is very well known," reports that **Andreas Dudith's library** now "hangs between heaven and earth": **no longer the heirs', but pawned (not sold)** to a third party for a fixed sum, so that **neither buyer nor seller has full right**. It "lies wretched in a certain house … as heaps of grain lie in the houses of the nobles" (Monau has seen it several times), and he **fears "great and irreparable harm"** to the books — a poignant eyewitness account of the dispersal/decay of a famous humanist collection (the purchase-bid of brahe-t_16000516001).
 - **The Wittich remains.** Good hope, via **Doctor Bucretius**, both for the **Wittich remains** (*Wittichianae reliquiae* — the dispersed library of Paul Wittich, incl. the annotated Copernicus copies) and for the **papers of "that other Astronomer who once lived among us"** (the unnamed dead Breslau astronomer of brahe-t_16000110001 / brahe-t_16000516001); Bucretius "is dealing with both with such diligence … that I do not doubt we shall have what we wish."
 - **Abraham Jengtius — Wittich's former patron.** The **Captain (Landeshauptmann) of Breslau and the Duchy, Abraham Jengtius**, "formerly the patron of our great Wittich while he lived," sends warm greetings and plans to meet Tycho on a journey to the **Bohemian baths** (Karlsbad/Teplice); he longs to see the **book Tycho lately presented to the Emperor** (of which **Jessenius** had told him). A valuable provenance link (Wittich's patron) for the Wittich-library question.
- **The storm-damage rumour.** Monau passes on a report that Tycho's **instruments were storm-damaged at his castle** [Benátky], condoling — but doubts it, "since you make no mention of it." (Tycho's silence suggests the rumour was false or exaggerated.)
- **The relay channel.** For letters to Monau: send to Prague to **Johann Myllner** (imperial councillor and **Supreme Secretary of the Kingdom of Bohemia**, Monau's *compater*), with whom lives **Johann Paludius**, the Silesian Duke's councillor resident at Prague — who will forward to Breslau. A concrete glimpse of the Prague–Breslau correspondence infrastructure.
- **Persons named.** Jacob Monau (sender); **Daniel Bucretius**; **Tobias Fischer** (*Doctor Fischer*); **Andreas Dudith** (and his heirs); **Paul Wittich**; **Abraham Jengtius** (Breslau Captain, Wittich's patron); **Johannes Jessenius**; **Johann Myllner** (Bohemian Supreme Secretary); **Johann Paludius** (Silesian councillor at Prague); the printer (unnamed); **Rudolf II**.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Vratisl. XIIIJ Iunij 1600*; Silesia (Breslau) had adopted the **Gregorian (New Style)** calendar by 1600; marked [N.S.].
- Correction. Latin corrected: removed the interpolated clause 'quod ut facias' (Dreyer VIII p.325), which is absent from the printed text; this does not affect the published English, which already matched the Dreyer sense.

documents.abstract: Reports that the Magdeburg canons are ready to purchase Tycho's astronomical equipment and that two boatmen offer to ship it to Leitmeritz, pressing for a reply.
documents.incipit: GENEROSE et doctiss. D. TYCHO, vehementer expectant nostri Canonici tuæ Astronomicæ …

text.original:
DEM EDLEN EHRNVESTEN VND HOCHGELARTEN HERRN TYCHO BRAHEN AUFF KNUTHSTORFF, S. RÖMISCH KEYSERLICHEN MAYT.ASTROΝΟΜΟAUFF BENATHEN, MEYNEM ... GÜNSTIGEN HERRN.CITISSIME.

S.

GENEROSE et doctiss. D. TYCHO, vehementer expectant nostri Canonici tuæ Astronomicæ suppellectilis avectionem, et pecuniam promtam ad omnia offerunt. Accessit quoque me GRUTZMACERUS Dresdensis nauta, qui promittit se navibus suis Leutmeritium usque omnia recte advecturum. En alius quidam ex nostris, qui idem rogat, ut sibi committatur. Duabus enim navibus se omnia rite repositurum esse. Reliqua enim suppellex nuper Hamburgo quoque advecta est. Quid impediat, scripsi ante Pentecosten, et quia nihil impetro responsi, existimo non esse redditas meas. Quare rogavi hunc meum vicinum, ut has aut ipse redderet, aut conducto Pragæ nuncio, cui tu satisfaceres, de tua voluntate sciscitaretur. Est autem hæc mora, quod inventarium prioris vecturæ ANDREAS vester secum abstulit, ut sine insigni errore nos committere eam nautis prorsus nequeamus. Omnino ergo oportet ANDREAM ipsum redire ad nos, aut aliquem ex domesticis, cui nota sunt externo ab intuitu omnia, et qui ex navi reponat in littore, contra pluvias muniat, tibique postea deferenda curet. Quod peregrinus nec vult nec potest recte curare. Mittas ergo, quam primum potes, qui comes et inspector sit omnium. De me præstabo fidelissime omnia, quæ volueris et quæ potero.

B. V.
Magdæburgi 9 Iunij 1600.
Tuus
GEORGIUS ROLLENHAGEN.
text.english:
**To the noble, honourable, and highly-learned Master Tycho Brahe at Knudstrup, His Roman Imperial Majesty's Astronomer at Benátky, my … favourable lord. With all speed [CITISSIME].**

Greeting.

Generous and most learned Master Tycho, our Canons vehemently await the carrying-off of your astronomical equipment [*suppellex*], and offer ready money for everything. There also approached me Grützmacher, a Dresden boatman, who promises that he will convey everything rightly by his ships as far as Leitmeritz [Litoměřice]. And behold, another of our [townsmen], who asks the same — that it be entrusted to him, [saying] that with two ships he would duly stow everything. For the rest of the equipment has lately been conveyed from Hamburg too. What is the impediment, I wrote before Pentecost; and because I obtain no answer, I judge that my [letter] was not delivered. Wherefore I have asked this neighbour of mine either to deliver these [present lines] himself, or — a messenger being hired at Prague (whom you would pay) — to inquire about your will. But this is the [cause of] delay: that the inventory of the earlier carriage your Andreas took away with him, so that we cannot at all entrust it to the boatmen without notable error. Altogether, then, it is necessary that Andreas himself return to us, or someone of [your] household to whom everything is known by outward inspection, and who may restow [it] from ship onto the shore, protect [it] against rains, and afterward see to its conveyance to you. Which a stranger neither wishes nor is able rightly to attend to. Send, therefore, as soon as you can, someone to be the companion and overseer of everything. For my part, I will most faithfully perform everything you wish and that I can.

Fare well.
Magdeburg, 9 June 1600.
Yours,
Georg Rollenhagen.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Georg Rollenhagen** (1542–1609), rector of the Magdeburg cathedral school and a celebrated German poet (the *Froschmeuseler*); here acting as Tycho's logistics agent on the **Elbe transport route** for his instruments.
- **The instrument transport.** A vivid document of the **shipping of Tycho's astronomical equipment** (*suppellex Astronomica*) up the Elbe to Bohemia: the Magdeburg cathedral **canons** are eager for it to move on (and offer cash); the Dresden boatman **Grützmacher** (and a rival local) offer to carry it by ship as far as **Leitmeritz (Litoměřice)**; "the rest of the equipment has lately been conveyed from Hamburg too." The hold-up is that **Andreas**, Tycho's man, carried off the **inventory** (*inventarium*) of the first consignment, so no one can check the freight; Rollenhagen begs Tycho to send Andreas back, or another servant who knows the instruments by sight, to escort and protect them.
- ***CITISSIME*** ("with all speed") on the address marks urgent dispatch. *Canonici* = the Magdeburg cathedral canons. The German address-line's *ASTRONOMO* is printed with Greek letters (ΑΣΤΡΟΝΟΜΟ).
- **⚠ Date.** The dateline reads *Magdaeburgi 9 Iunij 1600* = **9 June 1600**; the edition (identifier …0619… / label "19. juni") gives **19 June**. The header follows the **as-written 9 June** and notes the catalogue's 19 June; the internal "I wrote before Pentecost" is consistent with an early-June date. Magdeburg (Lutheran) = **Old Style**.

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD IOSEPHUM SCALIGERUM.
ILLUSTRIS ET GENEROSE VIR DOMINE ET AMICE HONORANDISSIME.

ELAPSÆ sunt septimanæ, ni fallor, sex, ex quo in arce Cæsarea Bennaticha, ubi nunc sedes est habitationis meæ, Illustris Dominationis tuæ literas acceperim VI Eid. Martias Lugduni Batavorum scriptas, easque non saltem eruditionis eximiæ, quâ præpolles, sed et humanitatis et benevolentiæ erga me (pro quibus etiam officiosissime gratias habeo) refertissimas. Cum vero nuper a Scra Cæsa Mate, Domino nostro Clementissimo, postquam Pilsena, ubi per tres anni quadrantes ob pestem abfuit, in arcem consuetæ residentiæ huc nuper redijt, evocatus sum, siquidem ipsius Matas de quibusdam ad studia quæ tracto pertinentibus clementissime mecum loqui dignabatur (prout semel atque iterum affatim factum est) accidit, quod ante biduum Nobilis et eruditus hic Adolescens NICOLAUS SUCKERBACK de Myssen noviter ex Italia veniens me in aula inter alios ambulantem, Barone quodam indicante, agnosceret et compellaret, seque a Batavia oriundum, atque eo brevi cogitare indicaret, rogans, an quidpiam literarum ad amicos et isthic notos mittere vellem, cumque præ cæteris, an ad te meas dirigere possit, ab eo percontarer, id officij in se recepit. Existimavi autem eum tamdiu hîc mansurum, donec allatis tuis ultimis (de quibus dixi) literis e Bennaticha, ijs secundum singula earundem contenta, quatenus in hac urbe strepitus et interpellationes aulicæ ferunt, respondere possem; at is hodie me in hospitio quærens se circa meridiem hinc abiturum in ijs hominibus significavit, quare ne plane mearum vacuus ad vos rediret, has ieiunas et breviusculas, potius quam nullas ad te exarandas duxi. Quoniam vero literæ tuæ ad manus non sunt, nonnulla saltem, quæ ex ijs recordor, attingam.

Conceptiones tuas de æquinoctijs et motu octavæ Sphæræ aliter salvando, quas promittis, avide exspecto. Stellam Polarem ante plurima secula, quemadmodum reliqua omnia octavæ Sphæræ (uti vocant) affixa sidera in eodem cœli loco hærere, facile tibi concessero, modo declinationem et ascensionem rectam, tum quoque longitudinem et nonnihil etiam latitudinem, tam in hac quam in alijs alteratas fatearis. Quod autem id ipsum evenerit, non tam octavæ Sphæræ promotione quam æquinoctiorum anticipatione, prout magnus ille COPERNICUS pariter animadvertisse videtur, etiam tibi astipulor. Sed in hoc cardo negotij vertitur, quomodo anticipatio illa intelligenda et exsequenda sit. Per motum axis terreni, prout speculatus est COPERNICUS, reciprocum et liberatum annuæque restitutioni non plane coincidentem, id evenire frustranea, imo prorsus absurda est assumtio nec apparentijs vel hoc seculo, nedum cæteris omnibus satisfacit. Ego ipsum Solem hanc varietatem efficere statuo, dum aliam atque aliam diversis seculis designat Eclipticam, aliasque eiusdem cum Æquatore intersectiones retrorsum et quidem non admodum æqualiter inducit, prout suo loco latius Deo volente ostensurus sum. Nam et infimam Lunam non multum dissimili ratione suam orbitam singulis mensibus variare depræhendi, ita ut non saltem latitudo eius maxima ad tertiam gradus partem (quanta etiam omnino in Eclipticæ obliquitate hactenus comperta est differentia) mutetur, sed et nodi et intersectiones cum Ecliptica, licet antrorsum motu æquali, reciproce tamen et inæquali ratione id fieri satisque notabili discrimine, quod grad. 1¾ attingere queat, cognovi, prout lunaris curriculi restitutio propediem, favente Numine, in Progymnasmatis nostris publicanda plenius patefaciet. Si tibi aliqua ratio a nostra forte diversa innotuit, et ex historijs antiquissimis ratisque observationibus comperta est, quâ hæc commode explicari queant, vellem eam mecum communicari. Interim ut dicam id quod res est, assequi non possum, id quod tam in his literis, quam alibi innuisti: Polum nimirum mundi alium esse a Polo æquinoctialis et lineas meridianas moveri. Videtur id enim minus convenire, nisi forte tuam sententiam, quæ paulo obscurior est, necdum percipiam, quare hac de re uberius a te instrui cupio.

Pro MANILIO in integrum a te restituto mihique transmisso plurimas habeo gratias. Perlustravi eundem successivis horis, prout otium tulit, mihique tua industria et perspicacitas in hoc authore a mendis vindicando et expoliendo, quæ etiam in plurimis alijs satis explorata est, summopere placuit.

Plura scriberem, si literæ tuæ in promptu essent, ulteriorem procul dubio materiam suppeditaturæ, modo etiam id ferret huius loci irrequietudo, et is, qui hasce allaturus est, abitum adeo festinanter non acceleraret; quare hæc subito effusa Illustris Dominatio tua boni consulat, meque favore suo prosequi pergat, ac per internuncij oportunitatem suis cultissimis literis invisere non intermittat, quæso.

Vale.
Dabantur Pragæ Bohemorum die 23 Iulij stylo novo Anno Epochæ Christianæ Dionysiacæ et vulgatæ 1600.
Illustris Dominationis tuæ
studiosissimus
TYCHO BRAHE,
manu propria scripsi.


*[Postscript — restored from Dreyer, Opera Omnia VIII, p. 330; dropped by the working transcription. See Apparatus.]*
