text.original:
NOBILITATE GENERIS, DOCTRINA AC VIRTUTE PRAESTANTISSIMO VIRO, DOMINO TYCHONI BRAHE, DOMINO HÆREDITARIO IN KNUDSTORFF, ASTRONOMO EXCELLENTISSIMO, DOMINO ET AMICO SUO INPRIMIS HONORANDO. PRAGAe.

S. P.

NOBILISSIME et clarissime vir, Domine et amice inprimis colende. Binas abs te accepi literas hoc mense Septembri; priores die 8 mihi reddidit M. CHRISTIERNUS, qui ad tres septimanas Witebergae substiterat, posteriores tabellarius Praga a D. GODELMANNO huc ablegatus heri. Scis autem stylo nos Iuliano hîc uti. Utraeque negocium pecuniarium tuum mihi commendarunt, de quo et ad affinem meum Dn. Cancellarium D. BORDINGUM scripseras, quem Lubecae tum agentem ego monui, ut negocium istud suo loco promoveret. Venit is ante paucos dies Lubeca Gustrovium ab Illustriss. Principe UDALRICO vocatus, postquam Cels. eius in venatione tum circa Grabovium existenti nunciatum fuisset de obitu nepotis ex fratre Ducis SIGISMUNDI AUGUSTI, qui hydrope alijsque morbis diu conflictatus die 5 Septemb. Ivenaci pie decessit ex hac vita. Funus ei fiet die 10 Octob. Suerini, ubi parentis IOH. ALBERTI et fratris IOHANNIS aliorumque ex ea linea defunctorum corpora quiescunt. Eadem occasione Dn. Cancellarius Quaestorem Iuniorum Principum, qui et Ducis UDALRICI iam Quaestor est, in aula reperit, et effecit, ut hodie mihi per ministrum suum in meis aedibus 600 illos thaleros tibi debitos numeraverit, recepta apocha tua, quam interim apud me servaveram. Hanc ego pecuniam usque ad adventum D. GODELMANNI, quem huc brevi accessurum tibique in receptione pecuniae gratificaturum scribis, penes me retinebo. Ut autem in auream monetam commutem, haudquaquam fieri potest. Rarissime enim hîc vel minimum aureum cernimus, omni auro vel in Belgium vel in superiorem Germaniam, ubi maiori precio quam hîc censetur, hinc translato. Id tamen faciam, si potero, ut thaleros novos Belgicos, quorum multi summae huic intersunt, in alios Imperiales, uti vocant, commutem; hos enim gratiores istic esse arbitramur quam illos.

Porro quod ad continuationem Chronici D. CHYTRÆI p. m. qui postridie Iohannis nobis valedixit, attinet, neminem hoc quidem in loco eam ad rem magis idoneum esse iudico quam D. CHRISTOPHORUM STURTZIUM, qui historiarum lectioni in hac Academia magna cum laude praeest, ingenioque, memoria et facundia excellit. Quamprimum igitur Concilium Academiae convenerit, mentionem huius negocij et tuae commonefactionis inijciam, nec dubito, quin Domini Professores, quorum plerosque aetate, doctrina et prudentia graves esse non ignoras, id constituent, quod et Academiae nostrae et nomini magni illius CHYTRÆI honorificum et publice utile erit. Adveniente vero D. GODELMANNO, de eo, quod ad te privatim spectat, postremae Chronici parti inserendo, unâ cum D. CLINGIO, cum haeredibus D. CHYTRÆI libenter et diligenter agam, et si quae alia a me proficisci poterunt grata tibi officia, in illis promptum me semper reperies, donec vixero. Senesco enim iam, et post mensem, si Deus voluerit, annum 70 aetatis meae completurus sum. Facio tamen adhuc mediocriter vocationis meae in Ecclesia et Academia, per Dei gratiam, officia. M. CHRISTIERNUS paucis hîc diebus mansit, festinans in Daniam. Ego sane hunc virum nobiscum vivere et iuventutem nostram literariam in studijs Astronomicis, quae post obitum praestantissimi D. BRUCÆI segnius hîc tractata et culta sunt, erudire optarem. Tuas res honesto et incolumi adhuc statu esse, ac velle S. Caes. Mai. ut Pragae sibi adsis propius, gaudeo, et tibi tuisque deinceps etiam fausta feliciaque omnia precor.

Rumor isthuc delatus de dissidio inter Regem Daniae et nobilitatem suborto vanus est. Rex hoc tempore in Holsatia est cum coniuge, et genethliacis pompis ac convivio Gottorpij interfuturus dicitur, ubi soror eius IOHANNI ADOLPHO Holsatiae duci nupta filium peperit, quo et BUGISLAUS Pomeraniae dux legatum D. HENR. CAMERARIUM misit. Venationibus se Rex in Iutia oblectavit, magno cervorum numero caeso. Extruit passim munitiones Halmstadij et Overscherae in Sueciae finibus, quo cives ex vicinis oppidulis Rundeby et alijs migrare iussit, item Krempae in Holsatia. CAROLUS dux Sueciam clam nunc totam tenet pacifice, regiam vero coronam sibi a subditis oblatam nondum acceptare voluit, supplicio capitis 4 regni proceres captivos, ERICUM SPARRE Cancellarium, GUSTAVUM et STENONEM BANNER, et TURONEM BIELKEN, a concilio ordinum regni damnatos, affecit. Sunt et alij in Finlandia interfecti. Iam cum valido exercitu in Livonia est, omniaque Suecis hactenus subdita circa Revaliam cum hac ipsa urbe tenet, et Regi Poloniae bellum facturus existimatur, qui per Capitaneum suum GEORGIUM FARNSBECH exercitum circa Rigam conscripsit, qua de re certiora navibus nostris Riga redeuntibus cognoscemus. Cum Lubecensibus inducias pepigit, qui per legatos suos iam de pace cum eo agunt. Nuper duo Lubecensium Consules intra 24 horas obierunt, nec admodum bene inter Senatum et cives eius urbis convenit ob turbas Suecicas, quibus improvide Senatus inconsultis civibus se et urbem immiscuit, unde magna civibus in mari damna illata a CAROLO fuerunt.

In hisce regionibus, Dei beneficio, tranquillitas est, ac messem habuimus serenam et uberrimam. In Dania quoque segetes feliciter provenerunt, sed quia serior illic messis est, aër agricolis non adeo benignus fuit.

Postremo commendo tibi affinem meum ABRAHAMUM STOPIUM, qui istic aliquamdiu apud sororem et affinem vixit, eiusque negocium, quod haud dubie tibi exposuit, in quo si commodare ipsi apud Dn. Vicecancellarium vel alios proceres poteris, mihi quoque rem gratam feceris.

Bene et diu cum omnibus tuis vale.
Dabantur Rostochij 19 Septemb. stylo veteri Anno 1600.
Nobil. et Excel. T. studiosiss.
LUCAS BACMEISTERUS D.
text.english:
**To the man most excellent in nobility of birth, learning, and virtue, Lord Tycho Brahe, hereditary Lord of Knudstrup, most excellent Astronomer, his Lord and friend especially to be honoured. At Prague.**

Heartiest greeting.

Most noble and renowned man, Lord and friend especially to be revered. I have received two letters from you this month of September: the earlier, **M. Christiernus [Longomontanus]** — who had tarried about three weeks at Wittenberg — delivered me on the 8th; the latter, a courier sent hither from Prague by **Lord Gödelmann**, yesterday. You know that **we use the Julian style here**. Both commended to me your money-business, about which you had also written to my kinsman, the Lord Chancellor **Dr. Bording**, whom — then acting at Lübeck — I admonished to promote that business in its place. He came a few days ago from Lübeck to **Güstrow**, summoned by the most illustrious **Prince Ulrich**, after His Highness — then hunting near **Grabow** — had been told of **the death of his brother's son, Duke Sigismund August**, who, long afflicted with dropsy and other diseases, **piously departed this life at Ivenack on 5 September**. His funeral will be on **10 October at Schwerin**, where rest the bodies of his father **Johann Albert**, his brother **Johann**, and others deceased of that line. On the same occasion the Lord Chancellor found at court the **Treasurer of the Younger Princes** (who is now also Duke Ulrich's Treasurer), and brought it about that today, through his minister, **he paid me at my house those 600 thalers owed to you, my receiving your receipt** [*apocha*], which I had kept by me meanwhile. This money I will retain with me until the arrival of **Lord Gödelmann**, who, you write, will come hither shortly and assist you in receiving the money. **To exchange it into gold coin cannot be done at all**: very rarely here do we see even the smallest gold piece, all gold being carried hence either into the Low Countries or into upper Germany, where it is rated at a higher price than here. Yet I will do this, if I can: **exchange the new Belgian thalers** (many of which are in this sum) **into others, "Imperial" as they call them**; for we judge these more welcome there than those.

Further, as to the **continuation of the Chronicle of Dr. Chytraeus** (of pious memory, who **bade us farewell the day after [the feast of St.] John** [= 25 June]): I judge no one in this place fitter for the task than **Dr. Christoph Sturtz**, who presides over the lecture in history at this Academy with great praise, and excels in talent, memory, and eloquence. As soon, then, as the Council of the Academy meets, I will bring forward mention of this business and of your reminder; nor do I doubt that the Lord Professors — most of whom, as you know, are weighty in age, learning, and prudence — will resolve what will be both honourable to our Academy and to the name of that great Chytraeus, and publicly useful. And when Lord Gödelmann arrives, **about that which privately concerns you, to be inserted in the last part of the Chronicle**, I will gladly and diligently deal — together with **Dr. Clingius** — with Chytraeus's heirs; and if any other services welcome to you can proceed from me, you will always find me ready in them, as long as I live. **For I am now growing old, and after a month, God willing, I shall complete the 70th year of my age**; yet I still discharge moderately, by God's grace, the duties of my calling in the Church and the Academy. M. Christiernus stayed here a few days, hastening into Denmark. I should indeed wish this man to live among us, and to instruct our literary youth in the **Astronomical studies — which, since the death of the most excellent Dr. Brucaeus, have been more sluggishly handled and cultivated here**. That your affairs are still in an honourable and safe state, and that the Sacred Imperial Majesty wishes you to be nearer to him at Prague, I rejoice; and I pray all things auspicious and happy for you and yours henceforth too.

**The rumour carried thither, of a dissension arisen between the King of Denmark and his nobility, is empty.** The King is at this time in **Holstein** with his consort, and is said to be about to attend the birth-festivities and banquet at **Gottorp**, where his sister, married to **Johann Adolf, Duke of Holstein**, has borne a son — to which **Bogislaw, Duke of Pomerania**, sent as legate **Dr. Heinrich Camerarius**. The King has delighted himself with hunting in **Jutland**, a great number of stags being killed. He builds fortifications here and there — at **Halmstad** and **Överskär** on the Swedish borders (whither he has ordered the townsmen from the neighbouring little towns, Rundeby and others, to migrate), likewise at **Krempe** in Holstein. **Duke Charles** now secretly holds all **Sweden** peacefully, but has not yet been willing to accept the royal crown offered him by his subjects; he has **inflicted capital punishment on four captive nobles of the realm, condemned by the council of the estates: Erik Sparre the Chancellor, Gustav and Sten Banér, and Ture Bielke** [the Linköping Bloodbath]; and others have been killed in Finland. Now he is with a strong army in **Livonia**, and holds all that was hitherto subject to the Swedes around **Reval**, with that city itself, and is thought about to make war on the **King of Poland** — who, through his captain **Georg Farensbach**, has levied an army around **Riga**; whereof we shall learn more certainly from our ships returning from Riga. With the **Lübeckers** he has struck a truce; they now treat with him for peace through their legates. Lately two of the Lübeck consuls died within 24 hours; nor is it well agreed between the Senate and the citizens of that city, over the Swedish troubles, into which the Senate has imprudently entangled itself and the city without consulting the citizens — whence great damages at sea have been inflicted on the citizens by Charles.

In these regions, by God's benefit, there is tranquillity, and we have had a serene and most abundant harvest. In Denmark too the crops have come up happily, but since the harvest is later there, the weather has not been so kind to the farmers.

Lastly, I commend to you my kinsman **Abraham Stopius**, who lived there a while with his sister and kinsman, and his business (which he doubtless explained to you), in which, if you can accommodate him with the Lord Vice-Chancellor or other nobles, you will do me too a welcome thing.

Fare well, long, with all yours.
Given at Rostock, 19 September, Old Style, the year 1600.
Of Your Nobility and Excellency the most zealous,
**Lucas Bacmeister, Doctor.**

documents.apparatus:
- **Direction & correspondent.** **Incoming**, **Lucas Bacmeister → Tycho.** ⚠ **Identity correction (flagged).** This letter says the writer "will complete his **70th year** after a month" → **born c. 1530** → this is **Lucas Bacmeister the Elder (1530–1608)**, the Rostock theologian and church superintendent — **not** the Younger (1570–1638) named in the apparatus of brahe-t_16010415001. The financial-intermediary "Bacmeister" of the corpus is the **Elder**; the identification at brahe-t_16010415001 should be revised.
- **Significance — a dense Baltic news-letter, with the Linköping Bloodbath.**
 - **The Mecklenburg money.** The **600 thalers** of interest paid (via Chancellor **Bording** and the **Treasurer of the Younger Princes**, on the occasion of **Duke Sigismund August of Mecklenburg's** death and funeral arrangements at Schwerin); Bacmeister holds the sum for **Gödelmann's** arrival, and — unable to get gold (all exported) — will swap the **new Belgian thalers into Imperial thalers**. (Tycho's side: brahe-t_16010415001.)
 - **Chytraeus's *Chronicle*.** Confirms **David Chytraeus died 25 June 1600** ("the day after St. John's"; cf. brahe-t_16000808001). Bacmeister proposes **Christoph Sturtz** to continue Chytraeus's *Chronicle* and will handle, with **Dr. Clingius** and the heirs, the matter **"that privately concerns you, to be inserted in the last part"** — i.e. some notice of **Tycho** in the *Chronicle*.
 - **Rostock astronomy.** Wishes **Longomontanus** would stay to teach — astronomy at Rostock having languished **since Heinrich Brucaeus's death** (Tycho's old Rostock connection).
 - **The news bulletin.** *(a)* The **Danish king–nobility "dissension" rumour is false**; **Christian IV** is in Holstein, attending the birth at **Gottorp** (his sister **Augusta**, wife of **Johann Adolf of Holstein-Gottorp**, bore a son; **Bogislaw of Pomerania** sent **Dr. Heinrich Camerarius**); the King's Jutland hunting and his border fortifications (**Halmstad, Överskär, Krempe**). *(b)* **The Linköping Bloodbath (March 1600):** **Duke Charles** (future Charles IX) holds Sweden, has not yet taken the crown, and has **executed the four nobles Erik Sparre, Gustav Banér, Sten Banér, and Ture Bielke**; the **Polish–Swedish war in Livonia** (Charles around **Reval**; **Georg Farensbach** levying for Poland at **Riga**); the **truce with Lübeck** and the Senate-vs-citizens rift there.
- **Persons & places named.** Lucas Bacmeister (the **Elder**); **Longomontanus** (*M. Christiernus*); **Gödelmann**; Chancellor **Bording**; Duke **Ulrich III of Mecklenburg**; **Duke Sigismund August of Mecklenburg** (d. 1600) and his father **Johann Albert I** and brother **Johann**; the **Treasurer of the Younger Princes**; **Christoph Sturtz**; **David Chytraeus**; **Dr. Clingius**; **Heinrich Brucaeus**; **Christian IV**; **Augusta of Denmark** & **Johann Adolf of Holstein-Gottorp**; **Bogislaw [XIII] of Pomerania**; **Heinrich Camerarius**; **Duke Charles of Sweden**; **Erik Sparre, Gustav Banér, Sten Banér, Ture Bielke**; **Georg Farensbach**; **Abraham Stopius**; **Coraduz** (the Vice-Chancellor, unnamed). Places: Rostock, Prague, Wittenberg, Güstrow, Grabow, Ivenack, Schwerin, Holstein, Gottorp, Jutland, Halmstad, Överskär, Rundeby, Krempe, Sweden, Finland, Livonia, Reval, Riga, Lübeck, Denmark.
- **Calendar.** *19 Septemb. **stylo veteri** Anno 1600* → **19 September 1600 [Old Style]** (Bacmeister explicitly notes "we use the Julian style here"); header and label agree. *(Sigismund August's death-day is left blank in the source — "[—] September" — flagged.)*

- **Correction.** Corrected 'Regem Denmark' to 'Regem Daniae' in the Latin per Dreyer, TBOO VIII p.378, l.21 (no change to the English, already unambiguous).

documents.abstract: Chides Taubmann in verse for silence and owed poems, encloses verses by Melissus and a heroic poem from an Ingolstadt doctor received via Herwart von Hohenburg.
documents.incipit: TYCHO BRAHE AD TAUBMANNUM. Num, TAUBMANE, tibi vox rauca in faucibus haeret? Piscibus et …

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD TAUBMANNUM.
Num, TAUBMANE, tibi vox rauca in faucibus haeret?
Piscibus et stupidis mutior esne feris?
Forte Poëtarum quia mos est fingere quidvis,
Nos etiam vanis ludis imaginibus.
At praestare fidem vanos quoque Iura Poëtas,
Et rata pollicitis debita inesse iubent.
Solve igitur, quae iure mihi tu Carmina debes,
Falsaque (cum nequeas vera referre) refer.

EN habes hîc antesignani vestri tuique plasmatoris MELISSI (qui tamen raucos et mutos Poëtas creavit nunquam) Carmina nuper ad me missa, ubi nonnunquam dissimilis a seipso videtur. Adest etiam Doctoris cuiusdam Ingolstadiensis Heroicum, quod per Cancellarium Bavaricum, Dominum IOHANNEM GEORGIUM HERWARTUM ab HOHENBURG (cum quo mihi creberrima, ob studia, quibus impense afficitur, Mathematica, intercedit per literas familiaritas) hesterna vespera Monachio accepi: Tu lege, dispice, cognosce, et loquela recuperata, alio genere supple; ni mature parueris, Iambos in te vibrabo, et ex muto sordoque caecum, imo truncum te reddam, aut in saxum convertam, tanquam alter PERSEUS capite Gorgonio te petens. Sed prius Caducaei usum tibi adimam, et per MELISSUM tuum degradari faciam, alias enim nefas foret, sacros vates castigare et merita poena afficere.

Tuque vale, et tenerum cum matre valere columbum
Effice, sic vobis pullulet alma domus,
TYCHONISque memor, vates qui suspicit, esto,
Sique voles, carmen non breve mitte brevi.
Deproperabam Pragâ die 20 Septembr. stylo reformato Anno 1600.
text.english:
**Tycho Brahe to Taubmann.**

*Is your voice, Taubmann, stuck hoarse in your throat?*
*Are you more mute than fishes and dull beasts?*
*Perhaps, because the poets' way is to feign whatever they please,*
*you make sport of us, too, with empty images.*
*But the Laws bid that even vain poets keep faith,*
*and that due, ratified obligations inhere in promises.*
*Pay up, then, the Poems which you owe me by right,*
*and render falsehoods (since you cannot render truths).*

Behold, here you have the Poems — lately sent to me — of your party's standard-bearer and your own moulder, Melissus (who, however, never created hoarse and mute Poets), in which now and again he seems unlike himself. There is also at hand the Heroic [poem] of a certain Doctor of Ingolstadt, which I received yesterday evening from Munich, through the Bavarian Chancellor, Master Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg (with whom I have a most frequent familiarity by letters, on account of the Mathematical studies to which he is keenly devoted). You — read, examine, take note; and, your speech recovered, make good [your debt] with another piece. Unless you obey in good time, I will brandish Iambics against you, and from mute and deaf will render you blind — nay, maimed — or turn you into stone, like a second Perseus attacking you with the Gorgon's head. But first I will take from you the use of the Caduceus, and have you degraded through your own Melissus; for otherwise it would be impious to chastise sacred bards and visit them with deserved punishment.

*And fare you well; and make the tender dove fare well, with its mother;*
*so may a nurturing house teem [with young] for you;*
*and be mindful of Tycho, who looks up to the bards;*
*and, if you will, send before long a poem — not a short one.*
I hurried [this] off from Prague, on the 20th day of September, reformed style, in the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Friedrich Taubmann** (1565–1613), professor of poetry at **Wittenberg**, the celebrated humanist wit and Latin poet, protégé of Melissus. A **playful verse-and-prose letter** mock-scolding Taubmann for failing to send a promised poem, in the bantering register of the late-humanist *poetae*; the threats (Perseus, the Gorgon, the Caduceus, "Iambics") are jocular.
- **Persons.** *antesignanus vester … plasmator Melissus* = **Paul Schede Melissus** (1539–1602), the doyen ("standard-bearer" and "moulder") of the German neo-Latin poets, whose own *Carmina* on Tycho's affairs Tycho encloses (cf. brahe-t_16001116003). *Doctor Ingolstadiensis* = an unnamed Ingolstadt doctor whose *Heroicum* (heroic-verse poem) Herwart had just forwarded. *Cancellarius Bavaricus … Herwart ab Hohenburg* = **Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg** (the Munich correspondent of the whole 1600 series).
- **Mythological play.** *Iambos vibrabo* — "I'll brandish iambics" (the invective metre of Archilochus). *alter Perseus capite Gorgonio* — Tycho jokingly threatens to turn Taubmann to stone with the Gorgon's (Medusa's) head. *Caducei usum tibi adimam … per Melissum tuum degradari faciam* — "I'll strip you of the Caduceus [Mercury's herald-staff, the poet's emblem] and have you degraded through your Melissus" — i.e. drummed out of the poets' guild; *sacros vates* ("sacred bards") is the conventional dignity of poets.
- **Closing verse.** *tenerum cum matre columbum* — "the tender dove with its mother": an affectionate domestic figure (Taubmann's wife and child / household); *vobis pullulet alma domus* — a wish for a fruitful household. The whole sealed by the demand for "a poem — not a short one."
- **⚠ Calendar / dateline.** The printed dateline *Pragâ die Septembr. stylo reformato Anno 1600* gives **no day-number** ("on the … day of September"); the **day 20** is supplied from the edition (identifier …0920… / label "20. september n.s."). *stylo reformato* = "reformed style" = **New Style** (Prague, imperial). Header dates **20 September 1600 [N.S.]**, the day-number flagged as editorially supplied.

- **§1 Dreyer collation:** the day "20" is **not** merely editorial — Dreyer (*Opera Omnia* VIII, p. 365; running-head 10/20 Sept.) prints *die 20 Septembr.* Restored to the Source dateline; the "supplied from the edition" qualification is withdrawn.
- **Verification note.** Re-examined the 'sordo'/'surdo' text error flag; confirmed by direct inspection that the required Dreyer page (TBOO VIII, on or after p.364) is absent from the supplied extract, which ends at p.363. Left unchanged; the defect is rejected as unverifiable against the edition of record.

documents.abstract: Agrees that Melissus's recent poems lack their usual polish, defers to Tycho on publication of the Elegy, and reports efforts with Chytraeus's sons about Tycho's chronicle entry.
documents.incipit: ILLUSTRIS et magnifice Domine, patrone colende. Ut doleo priores meas tibi non redditas …

text.original:
ILLUSTRI ET MAGNIFICO VIRO, DOMINO TYCHONI BRAHE, ASTRONOMO FACILE NOSTRI TEMPORIS PRINCIPI, DOMINO ET PATRONO COLENDO.
PRAGAM IN BEHMEN.

ILLUSTRIS et magnifice Domine, patrone colende. Ut doleo priores meas tibi non redditas esse, ita laetor posteriores te accepisse: quibus quod prolixe et humanissime respondes, pergratum mihi est. De Elegia mea statues, utcunque libet, nihil me offendet, neque a me edetur, antequam tu volueris. De MELISSI carminibus plane tibi assentior. Alius quodammodo et quasi vulgaris videtur in istis carminibus: vel senectus hoc facit (ut ipse solet interdum queri) vel laboris fuga: certe isti odae omnis lima et intentio videtur deesse. Sed haec tibi in aurem dixerim, apud ipsum nolim proferri, qui me nuper etiam Elogio ornavit in carmine de obitu CHYTRÆI, quod mitto. Diligentissime egi cum CHYTRÆI filijs de Designatione ista tuae migrationis in Germaniam. Dixerunt se legisse et meminisse, quod patri reddita esset: sed quamvis accurate inquisita, reperta nondum est. Deinde etsi reperiatur, nobis tamen non liquet, quomodo ea possit in huius anni Chronicon regeri ad finem, ut vis, cum incurrat reipsa in praecedentem. Praeterea Chronicon illud iam editum est post mortem CHYTRÆI in id tempus, quousque ipse deduxit: nam ut quispiam Venerem imperfectam perficiat, huius anni extrema absolvat, fortasse nemo reperietur. Exemplum tibi mitto. Sed in tui gratiam facile recudi posset, nisi priora obstarent: et hoc quoque, quod iam haec Exemplaria in hominum manibus versentur. Nihil sane est, quod malim, quam tibi gratificari, sed tu ipse de his cogitabis et statues, et si quid in mentem venerit, nos tantum docebis. Locutus sum de hoc negocio etiam cum D. LUCA, qui suam sententiam sine dubio ipse perscribet.

De carmine ad Caesaream Maiestatem tali, quale innuis, quid fieri possit, dispiciam, quando otium nactus fuero. Modo versor in campo Eloquentiae et Intemperantiam ac sectatores eius vehementi oratione seu libro castigo. Erasmianum illud erit quiddam, ut spero. Sed haec ante dicens, in lente unguentum quaero.

Obijt nuper SIGISMUNDUS Megapolitaniae princeps, IOHANNIS ante defuncti (cuius duo filij supersunt) frater: corpus eius humabitur Suerini 10 Octobris stylo veteri. CAROLUS dux Sueciae cum magno exercitu et tota familia contulit se in Livoniae partes; quid moliturus et quo res evasura sit, videbimus. Transylvaniam periclitari audimus, et propter adventum Turcae et tyrannidem Walachi, de quibus ex illis locis nos incertiora audimus, vos, qui prope adestis, certa.

Irascor illi, qui effecit, ut suppressis literis meis VARADINUM nostrum nondum legeris. Habe vero iam etiam sero: quod tibi probatum iri omnino confido, magno equidem mihi labore constitit. Elegantius videbitur, si conferetur cum inepto quodam Silesij Carmine, qui idem argumentum susceperat ante, sed sine Minerva et Gratijs, adeoque nimis pueriliter. RHEDERUM audio id misisse ad Typographiam Lignicensem, ut recudatur.

M. CHRISTIANUS iam discessit in Daniam, cum ante mihi adfuisset. Tu ut diutissime valeas et in Germania nostra floreas, utque tibi diu etiam incolumis sit ille Caesar optimus et clementissimus: illud vero est, quod opto et voveo summopere.

Bene vale, vir magnifice.
Datae Rostochij 20 Septemb. Anno 1600.
T. Magnif.
reverenter colens
MARTINUS BRASCHIUS.
text.english:
**To the illustrious and magnificent man, Lord Tycho Brahe, easily the prince of the astronomers of our time, Lord and patron to be revered. [To] Prague in Bohemia.**

Illustrious and magnificent Lord, patron to be revered. As I grieve that my earlier letters were not delivered to you, so I rejoice that you received the later ones; and that you answer them at length and most courteously is most pleasing to me. Concerning my Elegy, you will decide however you please: nothing will offend me, nor will it be published by me before you wish it. Concerning **Melissus's poems** I plainly agree with you. He seems somehow different, and as it were commonplace, in those poems — either old age does this (as he himself is wont sometimes to complain) or the avoidance of labour; certainly that ode seems to lack all polish and concentration. But these things I would say in your ear; I should not wish them brought out to him, who lately even adorned me with a eulogy in his poem on the death of **Chytraeus**, which I send. I have dealt most diligently with Chytraeus's sons about that account of your migration into Germany. They said they had read it, and remembered that it had been delivered to their father; but, though carefully sought, it has not yet been found. And then, even if it be found, it is not clear to us how it could be inserted into this year's Chronicle at the end, as you wish, since it really falls into the preceding [year]. Besides, that Chronicle has already been published, after Chytraeus's death, up to the time to which he himself carried it down; for, that someone should complete an unfinished Venus, and finish off the last parts of this year — perhaps no one will be found. I send you a copy. But for your sake it could easily be reprinted, did not the earlier [matters] stand in the way — and this too, that these copies are already in men's hands. There is indeed nothing I would rather do than gratify you; but you yourself will think and decide about these things, and if anything come to mind, you have only to instruct us. I have spoken about this business also with Lord **Lucas** [Backmeister], who will doubtless write out his own opinion himself.

Concerning a poem to the Imperial Majesty, such as you hint at, I will consider what can be done, when I have got leisure. Just now I am engaged in the field of Eloquence, and chastise Intemperance and its followers with a vehement oration, or book; it will be something Erasmian, I hope. But, saying these things beforehand, I seek ointment among lentils [I lavish pains on a trifle].

Recently died **Sigismund, prince of Mecklenburg**, brother of the previously deceased **Johann** (whose two sons survive); his body will be buried at Schwerin on 10 October, Old Style. **Charles, Duke of Sweden**, with a great army and his whole household, has betaken himself into the parts of **Livonia**; what he intends, and how the matter will turn out, we shall see. We hear that **Transylvania** is in peril, both from the coming of the Turk and the tyranny of the Wallachian — about which we hear more uncertain [reports] from those places, [while] you, who are near, [hear] sure ones.

I am angry at the one who brought it about that — my letters being suppressed — you have not yet read our ***Varadinum***. But have it now, even if late; which I am wholly confident will win your approval, for it cost me indeed great labour. It will seem the more elegant if compared with a certain inept Poem by a Silesian, who had taken up the same subject before, but without Minerva and the Graces, and so too childishly. I hear that **Rhederus** has sent it to the Liegnitz printing-house, to be reprinted.

**Master Christen** [Longomontanus] has now departed into Denmark, having before been with me. That you may fare most long, and flourish in our Germany, and that that best and most clement Emperor may long be safe for you — that, indeed, is what I wish and vow most greatly.

Fare well, magnificent man.
Given at Rostock, 20 September, the year 1600.
Reverently revering Your Magnificence,
Martin Brasch.

documents.apparatus:
- **Significance — Brasch's reply to Tycho's literary-critique letter.** This is **Martin Brasch's direct answer to Tycho's letter of 29 March 1600 (brahe-t_16000329004)**, responding point by point. Brasch (1565–1601), the Rostock humanist and *Poeta laureatus*, opens by noting that his *earlier* letters miscarried but the *later* reached Tycho, who answered "at length and most courteously."
- **Point-by-point with letter 106.**
 1. **The Elegy.** Brasch accepts Tycho's verdict entirely: "you will decide however you please … nor will it be published by me before you wish" — yielding the suppress-pending-revision control Tycho had asked for.
 2. **Melissus's verses.** Brasch "plainly agrees" with Tycho's low estimate of **Paul Melissus's** recent poems — "commonplace … either old age or the avoidance of labour … that ode lacks all polish and concentration" — but begs discretion (*in aurem*, "in your ear"), since Melissus had just honoured *him* with a eulogy in a poem on **David Chytraeus's death** (enclosed).
 3. **The Chytraeus migration-narrative.** Brasch reports on the hunt for Tycho's *Designatio* of his **migration into Germany** (cf. brahe-t_16010415002, where Sturtz pursues the same): Chytraeus's **sons** recall it was delivered to their father but cannot find it; and even if found, it cannot be fitted into "this year's Chronicle" (it belongs to the previous year), which is **already published** to the point Chytraeus reached before dying — "for, that someone should complete an **unfinished Venus** [the topos of Apelles' Venus, left unfinished at his death and which none dared complete], perhaps no one will be found." He has consulted **Lucas Backmeister** (Superintendent of Rostock; cf. brahe-t_16001115002), who will write separately.
 4. **The imperial poem.** Brasch will consider the *carmen ad Caesaream Maiestatem* Tycho had hinted at, when free; he is now writing an "Erasmian" oration against Intemperance.
- **News (autumn 1600) — cross-links.**
 - **Death of Sigismund of Mecklenburg**, "brother of the previously deceased **Johann** (whose **two sons survive**)" — to be buried at **Schwerin, 10 October O.S.** This identifies the **"younger princes of Mecklenburg"** of Tycho's 10,000-thaler loan (brahe-t_16000331001, brahe-t_16001115002 etc.) as **Duke Johann's two surviving sons**.
 - **Charles of Sweden** (later Charles IX) gone into **Livonia** with an army — the Polish-Swedish war (cf. Henniochus, brahe-t_16010321001).
 - **Transylvania imperilled** by "the Turk and the tyranny of the Wallachian" [Michael the Brave] — the Long War (cf. Sturtz, brahe-t_16010415002); Brasch notes Tycho, being "near," has the surer reports.
- **Brasch's own work.** His poem ***Varadinum*** (on **Várad / Oradea**, the Transylvanian fortress), at last sent; he commends it against "a certain inept Silesian poem … without Minerva and the Graces" on the same subject, which *Rhederus* has sent to the **Liegnitz (Legnica) press** to be reprinted.
- **Persons named.** Martin Brasch (sender); **Paul Melissus**; **David Chytraeus** (and his sons); **Lucas Backmeister**; **Sigismund** and **Johann** of Mecklenburg; **Charles, Duke of Sweden**; the **Wallachian** (Michael the Brave); *Rhederus*; ***M. Christianus* = Christen Sørensen Longomontanus**, who "has now departed into Denmark" (cf. brahe-t_15981231001, where Tycho urged him to come — he had been with Brasch en route); **Rudolf II** ("that best and most clement Emperor").
- **Allusions / proverbs (kept and glossed).** *Venerem imperfectam perficiat* — the unfinished Venus of **Apelles** (none dared complete it); *in lente unguentum quaero* — "ointment among lentils," the classical figure for misplaced/lavished effort; *sine Minerva et Gratijs* — "without Minerva and the Graces," i.e. without skill or charm.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Rostochij 20 Septemb. Anno 1600*; Lutheran Rostock kept the **Julian (Old Style)** calendar — confirmed by Brasch's own *"10 Octobris stylo veteri"* for the burial. Header marked [O.S.].
- **Correction.** Latin address heading corrected from 'PRAGAMIN BEHMEN.' to 'PRAGAM IN BEHMEN.' per Dreyer, TBOO VIII p.379; no change to the English, which already read correctly.

documents.abstract: Sends two books Tycho requested: the Works of Apollonius of Perga and the astronomical tables of Blanchinus, Prugner, and Peurbach.
documents.incipit: MITTO, Vir Nobilissime atque Mathematicorum omnium facile princeps, his iunctos libros ex …

text.original:
NOBILISSIMO DOCTISSIMOQUE VIRO, DOMINO TYCHONI BRAHE, DOMINO A KNUDSTRUP ET URANIBURGO, MATHEMATICORUM OMNIUM FACILE PRINCIPI, DOMINO ET AMICO SUO SINGULARI OBSERVANTIA COLENDO.
PRAGÆ.
IN ABWESEN HERRN ALEXANDER PRENDTL FÜRSTL. BAYER. AGENTEN ABZUEGEBEN.

MITTO, Vir Nobilissime atque Mathematicorum omnium facile princeps, his iunctos libros ex ijs, quos desideras, APOLLONIJ Pergæi Opera No. 73 et Tabulas BLANCHINI, PRUGNERI et PURBACHIJ No. 34. Tibique fœlicissima quæque ex animo precor et opto.

Datæ Monachij die 23 Sept. A. 1600.
D. T. Nobilmæ
Addictissimus
IOAN. GEORG. HERWART AB HOHENBURGK.
text.english:
**To the most noble and most learned man, Master Tycho Brahe, Lord of Knudstrup and Uraniborg, easily the prince of all mathematicians, his lord and friend to be honoured with singular respect.**
**At Prague.**
**In the absence of Herr Alexander Prendtl, the Bavarian ducal agent, to be delivered.**

I send, most noble man and easily prince of all mathematicians, joined herewith, these books out of those that you desire: the *Works* of Apollonius of Perga, No. 73, and the *Tables* of Blanchinus, Prugner, and Peurbach, No. 34. And I pray and wish you from my heart every happiness.

Given at Munich, the 23rd day of September, in the year 1600.
Most devoted to Your most noble [self],
Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg.

documents.abstract: Thanks the Chapter for forwarding his stored goods from Magdeburg to Prague at their own expense, noting the Emperor received this service with favour.
documents.incipit: REUERENDISSIME et nobilissime domine decane. Do:ie honorandissime, advenerunt res meæ, …

text.original:
[TYCHO BRAHE AD DECANUM CAPITULI MAGDEBURGENSIS].

REUERENDISSIME et nobilissime domine decane. Do:ie honorandissime, advenerunt res meæ, quæ Magdeburgi repositæ erant, hisce præteritis diebus Leutmeritzium quousque Albis versus Bohemiam est nauigabilis. Quod autem in gratiam sac:æ cæs:æ maiestatis, domini nostri clementissimi, Dominatio Vestra vna cum cæteris reuerendissimi capituli Magdeburgensis collegis eas tam prompte et liberaliter proprijs sumtibus huc procurare non degrauati estis, id ipsius maiestas clementissimo animo acceptissimum habuit, prout ab ipsius maiestate, cui hoc vestrum obsequentissimum officium ante paucos dies, cum in horto prope arcem illi subiectissime adessem, commendabam, non saltem ipsemet cognoui sed et heri à magf:co d:no Baruitio, supremo secretario et ipsius ma:ti a consilijs intimo, percepi, qui etiam hac de re se ad vestri reuerendissimi capituli vicecancellarium Chilianum Stösserum scripsisse mihi insinuauit. Ego vero pro mea persona hanc vestram benignissimam voluntatem, quod meis desiderijs tam libere et libenter annueritis, et supellectilem, qua diu non sine incommodo destitutus sum, ad me direxeritis, gratias vestris impensis et habeo et debeo immortales; cumque ad compensandum imparem me agnoscam, id saltem polliceri possum me perpetuo grata mente hoc singulare reuerendissimarum Dn:m Vestrarum in me collatum beneficium recoliturum, et apud optimos quosque (quod et alias facere soleo) deprædicaturum, imo per oportunitatem id ipsum publice testaturum. Et si quid unquam fuerit in quo mea opella Vestris reuerendissimis Dom:bus, quod acceptum fuerit, vicissim præstare possit, re ipsa, quantum in me est, ostensurus sum, me huius singularis beneuolentiæ haud immemorem esse. Quod omnibus et singulis reuerendissimi capituli vestri membris officiosissime significari velim. Devs opt. max. Vestram reuerendissimam Dominationem vna cum honorandissimis cæteris capitularibus quam diutissime florentem et incolumem conseruet.

Dabantur Pragæ Bohemorum die 26. septembris stylo nouo anno 1600.
text.english:
**[Tycho Brahe to the Dean of the Chapter of Magdeburg.]**

Most reverend and most noble Lord Dean, most honoured Sir: my belongings, which had been stored at Magdeburg, arrived in these last few days at Leitmeritz, the point to which the Elbe is navigable toward Bohemia. That Your Lordship, together with the other colleagues of the most reverend chapter of Magdeburg, did not find it a burden to procure and forward them hither so promptly and liberally, at your own expense, for the favour of His Sacred Imperial Majesty, our most clement Lord — this His Majesty received with most gracious mind as most welcome; as I learned not only from His Majesty himself (to whom I commended this most obliging service of yours a few days ago, when I attended him most humbly in the garden near the castle), but also yesterday from the Magnificent Lord Barvitius, supreme secretary and privy councillor to His Majesty, who intimated to me that he had himself written about this matter to the vice-chancellor of your most reverend chapter, Kilian Stösser. For my own part, indeed, for this your most kindly disposition — that you assented so freely and willingly to my wishes, and directed to me the furnishings of which I have long, and not without inconvenience, been deprived — I both render and owe you undying thanks for your outlay; and since I acknowledge myself unequal to repaying it, this at least I can promise: that I shall ever, with grateful mind, cherish this singular benefit conferred upon me by Your most reverend Lordships, and shall proclaim it before all the best men (as I am wont to do on other occasions), nay shall, when occasion offers, publicly attest the very same. And if ever there be anything in which my poor service may in turn render Your most reverend Lordships something that shall be acceptable, I shall show by the deed itself, so far as in me lies, that I am by no means unmindful of this singular goodwill — which I would wish to be most dutifully signified to each and every member of your most reverend chapter. May God, best and greatest, preserve Your most reverend Lordship, together with the rest of the most honoured chapter-members, flourishing and unharmed for the longest time.

Given at Prague in Bohemia, the 26th day of September, New Style, in the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe**, now at **Prague** (he had moved from Benátky to the city in the late summer of 1600). The letter concerns the long-distance transport of his household goods — part of the effects shipped out of Denmark and across Germany after his 1597 departure from Hven.
- **Recipient.** The **Dean of the Cathedral Chapter of Magdeburg** (*decanus capituli Magdeburgensis*), addressed by office, not by name; the goods had been in storage (*repositae*) at Magdeburg, a natural staging-point on the river route, and the chapter forwarded them downstream at imperial request.
- **Persons named.**
 - *Magnificus Dominus Barvitius* = **Johann Anton Barvitius (Barwitz)** (d. 1620), Latin secretary and privy councillor (*a consilijs intimo*) to Rudolf II — one of Tycho's principal channels to the Emperor at Prague (he recurs across the late correspondence as *Coraduz/Barvitius*).
 - *Chilianus Stösserus* = **Kilian Stösser**, vice-chancellor of the Magdeburg chapter, Barvitius's correspondent in the matter.
 - *Sacra Caesarea Maiestas, dominus noster clementissimus* = **Emperor Rudolf II**.
- **Places.** *Leutmeritzium* = **Leitmeritz / Litoměřice** on the Elbe (*Albis*), here named as the upstream limit of navigation toward Bohemia. *Praga Bohemorum* = **Prague**.
- **Witness note.** The Basel manuscript is catalogued as a *Kladde* — a **draft / retained office copy**, not the dispatched original; hence the bracketed editorial heading *[Tycho Brahe ad decanum capituli Magdeburgensis]* supplies the address the fair copy would have borne.
- **Register & formulae.** A formal letter of thanks in high curial register: cascading superlatives (*reverendissime, honorandissime, clementissimo animo, immortales*), the humility topos (*ad compensandum imparem me agnoscam*), and the closing benediction *Deus optimus maximus … quam diutissime florentem et incolumem conservet*. *Dabantur* (epistolary "they were given," i.e. dispatched) rendered "Given."
- **Calendar.** Dateline *die 26. Septembris stylo novo* — explicitly **New Style (Gregorian)**, as expected of Tycho's Prague correspondence; reproduced, not converted.

documents.abstract: Acknowledges Duke Otto of Brunswick's requests, encloses a reply for him, and reports his instruments installed in an Italian-style house beside the Emperor's garden at Prague.
documents.incipit: MAGNIFICE et excellentissime Domine D. VITE WINSHEMI, amice inprimis honorande: Ex …

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD VITUM WINSHEMIUM.

MAGNIFICE et excellentissime Domine D. VITE WINSHEMI, amice inprimis honorande: Ex literis Excell. Væ ijsdemque adiunctis, quæ Illustrissimus Princeps OTTHO dux Brunsvicensis et Luneburgensis Clementissime a me requirat, intellexi; utque ipsius Celsitudo sciat, me ea in parte officiosissime illi pro meo modulo morem gesturum, dedi ad ipsius Celsitudinem literas meum responsum brevibus complectentes, quas ut ex me debita cum submissione ad ipsius Celsitudinem dirigere E. V. velit, peramanter rogo.

Meæ res adhuc in eodem sunt statu quo antea. Versor etiamnum Pragæ cum tota familia, huc a Sacra Cæs. Maiestate, paulo postquam Pilsena redierat, Clementissime evocatus. Instrumenta mea Astronomica, quotquot in arce Benachiæ habui, huc iussu ipsius Maiestatis allata sunt, atque in domo illa, quæ iuxta hortum Cæsaris prope arcem situm magnifice Italico more extructa est, et cupro superius tecta, quam E. V. proculdubio novit, disposita sunt, ut ipsius Maiestas ea promptius, cum lubuerit, perlustrare possit, quod et ante paucos dies, quamprimum ibi erecta erant, me præsente factum est, quæsivitque tunc ipsius Maiestas de cæteris, quæ cum Leutmeritzium advenisse percepit, etiam in eandem domum transferri atque aliquantisper ibi collocari, donec de loco oportuno, ubi rectius ad usum constitui atque perpetuo conservari possint, providerit, benignissime mandavit. Quid hac in re fiet, postmodum V. E. ex me cognoscet; procedunt hîc omnia (ut scit) ob rerum gerendarum copiam et molem lento gradu, quod patienter ferendum est. Interim in domo quadam ampla, non longe ab arce remota, satis commode cum meis habito, et consuetis studijs, quantum interpellationes et conversationes cum Illustribus Viris in tantæ aulæ præsentia ferunt, vaco.

Gaudeo rem esse compositam inter nostrum Serenissimum Regem et Anglam; Deus author Pacis avertat in posterum discordiarum semen et occasiones.

FREDERICUS ROSENKRANZIUS iam est in Ungaria in exercitu equitatus Cæsaris nostri, sed vereor, ne illi plus periculi immineat ex Asthmate et pulmonum vitijs, quibus graviter obnoxius est, præsertim si vinis istis fortioribus nimium indulserit, quam vel ab hoste propinquo, vel aliunde. Fuit hîc ante biduum quidam ex eius ministris, qui in Daniam properavit illi forte pecunias allaturus, cum quo OLIGERO nostro scribere voluissem, nisi tantopere festinasset, et eram alias uti nunc quoque admodum occupatus. Filia nihilominus mea natu maior ad illum quasdam exaravit, commonefacientes de equo quodam promisso, quem sponsione quadam, dum Wandesbeci essemus, amisit. Et quia nunc commoda datur occasio, equum illum cum patruelis sui ministro, qui eum proculdubio accedet, mittendi (is enim ibi resolutus in eo huc equitare poterit) voluit illa, me sic iubente, OLIGERO id insinuare. At minister ille iter accelerans hinc abierat, antequam literæ dictæ obsignatæ essent. Quare eas nunc Hamburgum ad SIMONEM de PETKUM mitto. Si Væ Exæ in promptu est commoditas eas ad OLIGERUM dirigendi, rogo id facere non degravetur. Sin minus, poterint GERHARDO RANZOVIO unâ cum alijs ipsi inscriptis transmitti, ita ut OLIGERUS eas recipiat, antequam FRIDERICI minister inde se huc et deinceps in Ungariam receperit. Sed sive id fiat, sive non, parum interest. Quare de tam levi re plura non addam, cum hæc ipsa per se nimia sint.

Turcam Canisium obsidere voluisse, sed ob aquarum copiam, cum udus et paludosus sit locus, inde discessisse ferunt. Quorsum, necdum satis constat; habet exercitum quadruplo maiorem nostro, sed ultra mensem ob instantem hyemem ibi perdurare nequit. Dicunt eum pacem expetere, an vero id serio, et æquis conditionibus, dubium est. Cæsar noster adhuc præsenti est animo, nec tam potentem hostem extimescit, utut Germaniæ Principum subsidijs maiori ex parte destitutus. Deus omnia vertat ad felicem exitum, et Christianismum protegat, cui æviterno numini te unâ cum tuis commendatum habeo.

Vale.
Dabantur Pragæ Bohemorum Die 26 Sept. Anno 1600.
text.english:
**TYCHO BRAHE TO VITUS WINSHEMIUS.**

Magnificent and most excellent Lord Doctor Vitus Winshemius, friend especially to be honoured: from Your Excellency's letter, and its enclosures, I have understood what the Most Illustrious Prince **Otto, Duke of Brunswick and Lüneburg**, most clemently requires of me; and that His Highness may know I will most dutifully comply with him in that part, according to my measure, I have given to His Highness a letter comprising my answer briefly — which I lovingly ask that Your Excellency would direct to His Highness from me, with due submission.

My affairs are still in the same state as before. I still dwell at Prague with my whole household, summoned hither most clemently by the Sacred Imperial Majesty, a little after he had returned from **Pilsen**. My astronomical instruments, as many as I had in the castle of **Benátky**, have been brought hither by His Majesty's order, and arranged **in that house which is magnificently built in the Italian manner beside the Emperor's garden, near the castle, and roofed above with copper — which Your Excellency doubtless knows** — so that His Majesty may the more readily survey them when he pleases; which, a few days ago, as soon as they were erected there, was done in my presence. His Majesty then asked about the rest, which when he learned had reached **Leitmeritz [Litoměřice]**, he most kindly ordered to be transferred also into the same house and placed there for a while, until he should provide a convenient place where they could be more rightly set up for use and perpetually preserved. What will be done in this matter, Your Excellency will afterward learn from me; here all things proceed (as you know) at a slow pace, on account of the abundance and mass of business, which must be patiently borne. Meanwhile I dwell, conveniently enough, with my household in a certain ample house not far from the castle, and am free for my accustomed studies — as far as the interruptions and conversations with Illustrious Men, in the presence of so great a court, allow.

I rejoice that the matter has been **settled between our Most Serene King and the Englishwoman** [Queen Elizabeth]; may God, the author of Peace, avert in future the seed and occasions of discords.

**Frederik Rosenkrantz** is now in **Hungary**, in the cavalry army of our Emperor; but I fear more danger threatens him **from the Asthma and lung-defects** to which he is gravely liable — especially if he indulges too much in those stronger wines — than either from the near enemy or from elsewhere. There was here, two days ago, one of his servants, who hastened into Denmark, perhaps to bring him money, with whom I would have wished to write to our **Holger** [Rosenkrantz], had he not hastened so; and I was otherwise (as now too) quite occupied. Nevertheless **my elder daughter** wrote some lines to him [Holger], reminding him of a certain **promised horse, which he lost by a wager, while we were at Wandsbek**; and because a convenient occasion is now given of sending that horse with his cousin's servant — who will doubtless come to him (for he, being at leisure there, will be able to ride hither on it) — she wished, at my bidding, to intimate this to Holger. But that servant, hastening his journey, had departed before the said letter was sealed. Wherefore I now send it to Hamburg, to **Simon von Petkum**. If Your Excellency has at hand a means of directing it to Holger, I ask you not to find it burdensome to do so; if not, it can be sent to **Gerhard Rantzau**, together with others addressed to him, so that Holger may receive it before Frederik's servant betakes himself thence hither, and then into Hungary. But whether it be done or not, it matters little; wherefore I will add no more about so trifling a matter, since these very [words] are in themselves too much.

They report that the **Turk** wished to besiege **Kanizsa**, but, on account of the abundance of waters (the place being wet and marshy), departed thence — whither, it is not yet sufficiently certain. He has an army **four times greater than ours**, but cannot endure there beyond a month, on account of the approaching winter. They say he seeks peace, but whether seriously, and on fair terms, is doubtful. Our Emperor is still of resolute mind, and does not greatly dread so powerful an enemy, although for the most part destitute of the German Princes' subsidies. May God turn all things to a happy outcome, and protect Christendom — to which everlasting Power I hold you, with yours, commended.

Farewell.
Given at Prague of the Bohemians, the 26th day of September, the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Vitus Winshemius** (the younger), Wittenberg professor of medicine and Tycho's go-between (cf. brahe-t_15980328001, the Bökel affair). The MS is in Basel.
- **Duke Otto's request.** Tycho answers (via Winshemius) a *requirit* from **Otto, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg**, enclosing a brief reply to be forwarded to the Duke "with due submission" — the matter itself not specified.
- **Significance — the instrument installation near Prague Castle (material history).** A precise account of where the instruments first went on reaching Prague: **the Benátky instruments were set up in "that house … magnificently built in the Italian manner beside the Emperor's [pleasure-]garden, near the castle, and roofed with copper,"** where **Rudolf II viewed them in Tycho's presence** "a few days ago"; the rest, arrived at **Leitmeritz (Litoměřice)** up the Elbe, the Emperor ordered brought to the same house "until a convenient place" be found (the move to the Curtius house would follow). Meanwhile Tycho lodges "in a certain ample house not far from the castle." Complements brahe-t_16001008001, brahe-t_16001009001 (the Benátky/Magdeburg → Leitmeritz → Prague transport).
- **The Anglo-Danish peace.** Tycho rejoices the dispute "**between our Most Serene King and the Englishwoman**" (Christian IV and **Elizabeth I**) is settled — the **Emden conference** outcome (cf. brahe-t_16000516001, where he had feared it might "breed war").
- **Frederik Rosenkrantz and the horse (family/personal detail).** **Frederik Rosenkrantz** — of the disgrace-and-rehabilitation thread — is now serving in the **imperial cavalry in Hungary**; Tycho fears his **asthma and weak lungs** (worsened by "stronger wines") more than the enemy. A charming domestic vignette: **Tycho's elder daughter** wrote to **Holger Rosenkrantz** about a **horse Holger had lost to her in a wager at Wandsbek**, now to be sent via a servant; the letter, missing the courier, is routed to **Simon von Petkum** at Hamburg, thence (via Winshemius or **Gerhard Rantzau**) to Holger.
- **The Turkish war.** The **Turk** abandoned the siege of **Kanizsa (Nagykanizsa)** because of flooding/marsh; his army "four times greater than ours" but unable to winter there; reportedly seeking peace (doubtfully). **Rudolf II** "of resolute mind," though "for the most part destitute of the German Princes' subsidies." (Cf. the Long-War news of brahe-t_16000916002, brahe-t_16010415002.)
- **Persons named.** Vitus Winshemius; **Otto, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg**; **Rudolf II**; **Christian IV** and **Elizabeth I**; **Frederik Rosenkrantz**; **Holger Rosenkrantz** (*Oligerus*); Tycho's **elder daughter** (unnamed — Magdalene or Elisabeth Brahe); **Simon von Petkum** (Hamburg factor); **Gerhard Rantzau**.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Pragae Bohemorum Die 26 Sept. Anno 1600*; **New Style** (imperial). Header agrees with the label.

translation.warrant: Collated against **Dreyer, *Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia*** (the edition of record), reading the printed page images. Collated in full against Dreyer TBOO VIII pp.366-369 (all 4 pages read as page images). The letter occupies pp.367-368; p.366 carries the tail of Herwart's letter to Tycho and the start of Tycho's letter to Otto of Brunswick, and p.369 carries the start of Tycho's letter to Georgius Rollenhagius, all correctly excluded. Full Latin text collated line by line: Otto Duke of Brunswick/Luneburg, the instrument transfer from Benatky to the Emperor's Italianate copper-roofed house, Leitmeritz, the Anglo-Danish settlement, Frederik Rosenkrantz's posting in Hungary and his asthma, the promised-horse/Wandsbek wager episode, Holger Rosenkrantz, Simon von Petkum, Gerhard Rantzau, the Turkish siege of Kanizsa and the 'four times greater' army figure, and the closing date (26 Sept. 1600) all match Dreyer exactly. No defects found.
