documents.incipit: EX itinere, quo peregre abieram, Vir Nobilissime atque Mathematicorum omnium facile …

text.original:
IOANNES GEORGIUS HERWARTUS HOHENBURG AD TYCHONEM BRAHE.

EX itinere, quo peregre abieram, Vir Nobilissime atque Mathematicorum omnium facile Princeps, iam tandem reversus, relegi literas tuas 28 die Augusti ad me datas, et ex adiunctis exemplis deprehendi, me semel atque iterum in calculo lapsum esse, quo nomine gratias tibi ago eô maiores. Sed inprimis summe miror, atque adeo satis mirari nequeo, calculum tuum novissimum Eclipseos Solaris diei 10 Iulij huius anni ἀκριβέστατον tam praecise observationi coelesti eidemque exactae congruere, ita ut nec sexagesimâ quidem particulâ unius gradus a se invicem discrepare videantur.

Ἦ μέγα θαῦμα τόδ’ ὀφθαλμοῖσιν ὁρῶμαι.
Respondet numeris tua contemplatio coeli
Unius arctataque ad sexagessma partis.
Θαῦμα ἴδεσται.
Respondent coelo numeri, quibus attrahis astra,
Unius arctatique ad Sexage partis.
Θαῦμ’ ἀκόεσται.

Summo itaque desiderio flagro, ut quanto citius pollicitationem hac in re tuam adimpleas, totus enim iam calculum hunc tuum Solis et Lunae novissimum, posteaquam eundem plane absolveris, exspecto et opto.

Libros, quos petijsti, habeo, sed iam deest tabellarius. FRANCISCUS VIETÆUS Ao 89 Londini edidit librum in folio Regali, cui titulus FRANCISCI VIETÆI opera Mathematica, in quibus tractatur Canon Mathematicus, seu ad Triangula, item Canonion Triangulorum laterum rationalium, unâ cum universalium inspectionum ad Canonem Mathematicum libro singulari etc. In eoque libro multa tractat de resolutionibus triangulorum, quare plane conijcio ADRIANUM ROMANUM de hoc ipso libro locutum esse. Quod si eum desideres, eurabo omnino, ut habeas. ALBATEGNIUS latius habetur, sed is ipse, qui multis in locis incorrectus est, Norimbergae Ao 37 unâ cum ALFRAGANO editus, et nec is quidem facile invenitur, attamen πολλαπλασίωσις pretij effecit, ut ego quoque exemplar eiusdem mendosae impressionis ex Bibliotheca quadam redemerim. Quod si nihilominus eundem petas, mittam illico. Mihi sane, praeter nomina propria, non videtur adeo mendosus, si unica cautio adhibeatur; solet enim numerum binarium et quinarium confundere. Quod si hoc unicum caveatur, in calculo vix error oboriatur.

Iungo his literis Catalogum nundinarum autumnalium, quem ipsum quoque iam demum e peregrinatione domum reversus sum nactus; quod si aliquos libros ex ijs desideres, transmittentur. Affinis meus PAULUS ZEHENTNER ab ZEHENTGRUEB quaedam meo nomine tibi referet, atque hisce vale quam foelicissime.

Datae Monachij die 8 Nov. A. 1600.
text.english:
**Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg to Tycho Brahe.**

Now at last returned from the journey on which I had gone abroad, most noble man and easily Prince of all Mathematicians, I have reread your letter sent to me on the 28th of August, and from the worked examples enclosed I have detected that I went astray, once and again, in calculation — for which I thank you all the more. But above all I greatly marvel, and indeed cannot marvel enough, that your latest calculation of the Solar Eclipse of the 10th of July this year — most exact [ἀκριβέστατον] — agrees so precisely with the exact celestial observation, that they do not seem to differ from each other even by a sixtieth part of one degree [i.e. one arc-minute].

*Truly, a great wonder is this I behold with my eyes!* [Greek]
Your contemplation of the heaven answers to the numbers,
drawn close [to within] a sixtieth of a single part.
*A wonder to behold.* [Greek]
The numbers by which you draw down the stars answer to the heaven,
[to within] a sixtieth of a single part.
*A wonder to hear.* [Greek]

I burn, therefore, with the highest longing that you fulfil your promise in this matter as soon as may be; for I now wholly await and desire this your latest calculation of the Sun and the Moon, once you have fully completed it.

The books you asked for, I have — but now a courier is lacking. François Viète published, in the year [15]89, at London, a book in royal folio, titled *The Mathematical Works of François Viète, in which are treated the Mathematical Canon, or [the road] to Triangles; likewise the Canonion of Triangles of rational sides, together with a separate book of universal inspections to the Mathematical Canon, etc.* And in that book he treats many things about the resolutions of triangles; wherefore I plainly conjecture that Adriaan van Roomen spoke of this very book. If you should want it, I will entirely see to it that you have it. Albategnius is more widely to be had, but that very [edition] — which is incorrect in many places — was printed at Nuremberg in the year [15]37 together with Alfraganus, and not even that is easily found; yet the multiplying [πολλαπλασίωσις] of the price has brought it about that I too redeemed a copy of that same faulty impression from a certain Library. But if you should ask for it nonetheless, I will send it at once. To me, in truth, apart from the proper names, it does not seem so faulty, provided one single caution be used; for it is wont to confuse the number two and five. If this one thing be guarded against, scarcely an error would arise in the calculation.

I join to this letter the Catalogue of the autumn fair, which I myself only just came by, now returned home from my travels; if you should want any books from them, they will be sent on. My kinsman Paul Zehentner von Zehentgrueb will report some matters to you in my name; and with these, fare most happily.

Given at Munich, the 8th of November, in the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Direction & sequel.** An **inbound** scientific letter **to** Tycho, the **sequel to brahe-t_16000504003** (Herwart, 4 May 1600). **Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg** (1553–1622), Chancellor of Bavaria, writing again from **Munich**, now reacting with astonishment to Tycho's solar tables.
- **The eclipse-calculation match (the scientific point; this chapter's convention).** Herwart marvels that Tycho's *calculus novissimus* of the **solar eclipse of 10 July 1600** agrees with observation to within "not even a sixtieth part of one degree" — i.e. **better than one arc-minute** (*sexagesima particula unius gradus* = 1/60°). Tycho had enclosed *adiuncta exempla* (worked examples) that exposed Herwart's own computational slips. Herwart presses for Tycho's promised *calculus Solis et Lunae novissimus* — the renewed **solar and lunar theory** (the *restitutio luminarium*,).
- **The Greek-Latin verse (this chapter's convention, — Greek transcribed and translated; corruption flagged).** Herwart frames his wonder in macaronic couplets alternating Greek tags with Latin elegiacs:
 - *Ἦ μέγα θαῦμα τόδ' ὀφθαλμοῖσιν ὁρῶμαι* — "Truly, a great wonder is this I behold with my eyes" (a Homeric-style hexameter; *cf.* the epic formula *θαῦμα ἰδέσθαι*, "a wonder to behold").
 - *Θαῦμα ἰδέσθαι* / *Θαῦμ' ἀκοῦσθαι* (so to be read; source prints *ἴδεσται* / *ἀκόεσται*) — "a wonder to behold" / "a wonder to hear."
 - The two Latin lines are transmitted **corruptly** in the working text: *"Unius arctataque ad sexagesim[a]e partis"* and the manifestly garbled doublet *"Unius ar & atique ad Sexage partis."* The sense is recoverable — *your reckoning of the heavens answers [the observations], drawn close to within one-sixtieth of a single degree* — and is so rendered; the corrupt forms are preserved verbatim in the source block by this chapter's convention, not silently emended.
- **The bibliographical postscript (instrument of the book-exchange).**
 - *Franciscus Vietaeus* = **François Viète (Vieta)** (1540–1603); Herwart describes his *Opera Mathematica* — the **Canon Mathematicus** (on triangles / trigonometric tables) — though his "London 1589, royal folio" details are garbled (Viète's *Canon mathematicus seu ad triangula* was Paris, 1579). He conjectures this is the book **Adriaan van Roomen (Adrianus Romanus)** had mentioned to Tycho.
 - *Albategnius* = **al-Battānī** and *Alfraganus* = **al-Farghānī**, in the faulty **Nuremberg 1537** edition (al-Battānī's *De motu stellarum*, ed. with al-Farghānī) — scarce and dear (*πολλαπλασίωσις pretij*, "the multiplying of the price"); Herwart notes its one systematic flaw, a tendency to **confuse the numerals 2 and 5**.
 - *Catalogus nundinarum autumnalium* = the **Frankfurt autumn book-fair catalogue**, enclosed.
 - *Paulus Zehentner ab Zehentgrueb* = **Paul Zehentner von Zehentgrueb**, Herwart's kinsman and a further messenger.
- **Greek vocabulary (transcribed + glossed,).** *ἀκριβέστατον* = "most exact"; *θαῦμα* = "wonder"; *πολλαπλασίωσις* = "multiplication."
- **Place.** *Monachium* = **Munich**.
- **Epistolary formulae.** *vale quam felicissime* → "fare most happily"; *Datae* (epistolary) → "Given."
- **Calendar.** Dateline *die 8 Nov. A. 1600* at Munich; **n.s.** (Catholic Bavaria, Gregorian). Reproduced. The eclipse is dated *10 July 1600* on the same New-Style reckoning.
- **Correction.** Corrected the Latin verse: "ar & atique" restored to Dreyer's single word "arctatique" (TBOO VIII p.386).

documents.incipit: CUM Illustrissimæ Celsitudinis Vestræ Legatus Magnificus, Dominus IOHANNES de …

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD MAURITIUM LANDTGRAVIUM HASSIÆ.

CUM Illustrissimæ Celsitudinis Vestræ Legatus Magnificus, Dominus IOHANNES de Bopenhaussen, qui magni Regis Persarum Legationem huc, Celnis Tuæ iussu, deduxit, mihi (siquidem interea dum hîc fuit, nonnulla ex mutuo aliquoties congressu atque colloquio nobis intercessit familiaritas) indicâsset, se reditum in Hassiam ad Celnem Vm maturare, mei officij esse duxi Illmam Cm Vm hisce meis literis demisse salutare, et quæcunque ex mea tenuitate proficisci poterint obsequia, omni debitâ reverentiâ offerre. Auxit hanc scribendi confidentiam, et idipsum ut non omitterem, persuasit, non saltem ea, qua Laudatissimæ memoriæ Vræ Celnis Dominus Parens, quoad vixit, me Clementissime prosecutus est benevolentia, sed et insuper Vræ ipsius Celnis benignissimus animus et perseverans erga me favor, ut vel inde liquet, quod Celdo Vra etiam post obitum Parentis suis Clementissimis et cultissimis literis dignata sit. Quin et ex prædicto Celnis Vræ Legato gratissimâ mente nec sine voluptate percepi, Cm Vm etiamnum subinde per occasionem nonnunquam mei mentionem facere, quod constantis erga me Clementiæ et benignitatis indicium, quâ possum submissione ac gratiarum devota actione, lubens agnosco, inque eo mihi non parum congratulor.

De migratione autem e Dania, Patria mea, ante quadriennium factâ, quoniam Cm Vm non saltem ex proprijs meis literis, interea ad eam officiosissime datis, sed et aliorum proculdubio relatione per suas circumstantias iam satis edoctum esse, nihil addubito, nolo ulterius ea de re quippiam commemorare. Existimo etiam Celni Vræ iam antea innotuisse, quomodo a Sacra Cæsa Mate, Domino nostro Clementissimo, huc in Bohemiam ante biennium Clementissime vocatus et in ipsius Cæsæ Matis Clientelam benignissime receptus, quodque Mecœnatem eorum, quæ diu multumque tracto, studiorum Astronomicorum in ipsius Mate invenerim liberalissimum. Quocirca advectis, ex ipsius etiam Cæsæ Matis Clementissimo mandato, per Albim fluvium omnibus meis, quibus in Dania ad tam sublimis scientiæ exercitium et redintegrationem usus sum, Organis, ea nuper, ipsius quoque Mate sic Clementissime decernente, in domo quadam ampla et magnifice hîc iuxta Arcis hortum extructa disposui, quæ numero sunt 28, tam formæ et fabricæ quam magnitudinis et utilitatis varietate discreta, quemadmodum supra memoratus Celnis Vræ Dominus Legatus, qui ea singula coram intuitus est, ad Cm Vm plenius referre poterit. Etsi vero in libro Epistolarum, qui Illmi et nunquam satis laudati Patris vestri literas de re Astronomica mihi Clementissime scriptas, unâ cum mea responsione, complectitur (quem Illmæ Celni Vræ a me submisse dedicatum eam accepisse opinor) suo loco nonnulla horum Instrumentorum reperiatur descriptio, et licet insuper icones quasdam, pleraque ex hisce Instrumentis repræsentantes, postea miserim, de quibus, quod eas Celdo Vra obtinuerit, Opus illud Palatinum, mihi vicissim dono Clementissime remissum, omne exemit dubium: Tamen cum Organa mea Astronomica postmodum plenius delineari atque excidi, unâ cum uberiore Fabricæ et Usus explicatione, atque in peculiari libro inprimi curârim, quem Imperatoriæ Mati humilime dedicatum, unâ cum duobus alijs pari formâ et magnitudine, quorum unus de mille affixarum stellarum accuratissime a nobis facta Restitutione, alter de ☉lis et ☾næ verificatis motibus agit, cum primum huc advenissem, subiectissime obtulerim, Vræ Illmæ Celni eum, qui de Mechanica Astronomiæ parte tractat, cum hoc ipso suo Nobilissimo et eximio Legato demisse dono mittendum duxi, quem et Celdo Vra benignâ fronte accipere non dedignetur, quâ possum reverentia oro. Si reliquos duos Celdo Vra unâ Clementissime expetierit, præsertim eum, qui affixarum Rectificationem scrupulose exequitur, ut collatio cum ijs stellis, quas Vra Celdo ibi pariter observatas habet, institui possit, eos quoque per temporis oportunitatem quam obsequentissimo animo impertiar. Quod et nunc præstitissem, si exempla conficiendi (sunt enim ambo manu scripti) commoditas superfuisset. Quin etiam cum alia ex meis Operibus lucem publicam viderint, ea cum Celne Vra omni debita submissione communicare, eiusque solertissimo et gravissimo submittere iudicio non supersedebo: Et quacunque alias in re pro mearum virium modulo quippiam, quod Celni Vræ gratum sit, præstare potuero, habebit ea in me servitorem fidelem, cui id, quicquid erit, libere demandet, qui etiam pro virili Vræ Celnis Clementissimis desiderijs omni animi submissione obtemperaturus sit. Sed ne diutius, quam par est, Cm Vm, cui me meaque studia commendata esse submisse cupio, hac interpellatione, gravioribus negocijs intentam, remorer, eam quam prosperrime florere et quam diutissime saluberrimeque valere unâ cum Illma Coniuge et inclytis liberis, a Deo Opt. ter Maximo devoto pectore precor.

Dabantur Pragæ Bohemorum Die 10 Novembris Anni 1600.
text.english:
**TYCHO BRAHE TO MORITZ, LANDGRAVE OF HESSE.**

Since Your most illustrious Highness's magnificent Envoy, Lord **Johann von Bopenhausen** — who conducted hither, by Your Highness's command, the Legation of the great King of the Persians — had indicated to me (for while he was here some familiarity arose between us from our repeated meeting and conversation) that he was hastening his return into Hesse to Your Highness, I judged it part of my duty humbly to greet Your most illustrious Highness by this my letter, and with all due reverence to offer whatever services can proceed from my slenderness. What increased this confidence to write, and persuaded me not to omit it, was not only the benevolence with which **Your Highness's Father, of most praised memory, while he lived, most clemently attended me**, but also Your own Highness's most kindly disposition and persevering favour toward me — as is clear even from this, that Your Highness, even after Your Father's death, deigned to honour me with most clement and cultivated letters. And indeed I learned, from the said Envoy of Your Highness, with most grateful mind and not without delight, that Your Highness still now and then, as occasion offers, makes mention of me — which token of constant clemency and kindness toward me I gladly acknowledge, with what submission and devoted giving of thanks I can, and in it I congratulate myself not a little.

But of my **migration from Denmark, my fatherland, made four years ago** — since I in no way doubt that Your Highness has already been sufficiently instructed in its circumstances, not only from my own letters, dutifully sent meanwhile, but doubtless also from the report of others — I will recount nothing further about that matter. I think too that it has already become known to Your Highness how, **by the Sacred Imperial Majesty, our most clement Lord, I was two years ago most clemently called hither into Bohemia and most kindly received into His Imperial Majesty's clientele**, and that I have found in His Majesty a **most liberal Maecenas of those Astronomical studies which I have long and much pursued**. Wherefore — all my **Instruments**, which in Denmark I used for the exercise and renewal of so sublime a science, having been **transported by the river Elbe**, by His Imperial Majesty's most clement mandate also — I have lately, His Majesty so most clemently decreeing, **set them up in a certain ample house, magnificently built here beside the Castle garden**; they are **28 in number, distinguished by variety as much of form and fabric as of magnitude and usefulness** — as Your Highness's above-mentioned Lord Envoy, who beheld each of them in person, will be able to report more fully to Your Highness. And although in the **Book of Epistles** — which comprises the letters on Astronomical matters most clemently written to me by Your never-sufficiently-praised illustrious Father, together with my reply (which I think Your most illustrious Highness received, humbly dedicated to You by me) — some description of these Instruments is found in its place; and although I afterward sent besides certain **engravings [*icones*] representing most of these Instruments** (and that Your Highness obtained them, **that Palatine Work [*Opus Palatinum*], most clemently sent back to me in turn as a gift, removed all doubt**): yet, since I have since had **my Astronomical Instruments more fully delineated and engraved, with a richer explanation of their Fabric and Use, and printed in a special book** — which, humbly dedicated to the Imperial Majesty, **together with two others of equal form and size (one of which treats of the *Restitution of the thousand fixed stars*, most accurately made by us, the other of the *verified motions of the Sun [☉] and Moon [☾]*)**, I most submissively offered as soon as I had come hither — I have judged that the one which treats of the **Mechanical part of Astronomy** should be humbly sent as a gift to Your most illustrious Highness, by this same most noble and excellent Envoy of Yours; which Your Highness may not disdain to accept with kindly countenance, I pray with what reverence I can. **If Your Highness should clemently desire the remaining two as well — especially the one that scrupulously carries out the Rectification of the fixed stars, that a collation may be set up with those stars which Your Highness has likewise observed there** — I will impart these too, in time's opportunity, with a most obedient mind. Which I would have done even now, had the convenience of making copies remained (for both are in manuscript). And indeed, when others of my Works shall have seen the public light, I will not forbear to communicate them to Your Highness with all due submission, and to submit them to Your most skilful and weighty judgement. And in whatever matter otherwise I shall be able, according to the measure of my powers, to do anything welcome to Your Highness, You shall have in me a faithful servant, to whom You may freely entrust whatever it be, and who will, to the utmost, obey Your Highness's most clement desires with all submission of mind. But lest I detain Your Highness — to whom I humbly wish myself and my studies commended — longer than is fitting with this interruption, [You being] intent on weightier affairs, I pray from a devoted heart to God the Best and Thrice-Greatest that You may flourish most prosperously and fare most long and healthily, together with Your illustrious Consort and renowned children.

Given at Prague of the Bohemians, the 10th day of November, the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Moritz "the Learned," Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel** (1572–1632) — son and successor of the astronomer-prince Wilhelm IV. The letter is formal court Latin, all in the deferential third-person *Celsitudo Vestra* ("Your Highness") register.
- **The late father.** *Illustrissimi et nunquam satis laudati Patris vestri* = **Wilhelm IV of Hesse-Kassel** (1532–1592), the observing prince of the Kassel observatory, Tycho's great correspondent — "of most praised memory."
- **The envoy & the Persian embassy.** **Johann von Bopenhausen**, the Hessian envoy who "conducted hither the Legation of the great King of the Persians" — i.e. the **Safavid embassy** (Husain Ali Beg / the Sherley mission) that reached Prague in 1600; he is the bearer of this letter and of the gift book back to Kassel, having seen Tycho's instruments in person.
- **Significance — the Prague instrument-installation and the three-volume imperial program.**
 - **The 28 instruments at Prague.** Tycho's instruments, **shipped from Denmark up the Elbe** by imperial mandate, are now **set up in "an ample house, magnificently built beside the Castle garden"** (the Curtius house; cf. brahe-t_16010415001, "the new Rudolphine Uraniborg") — **"28 in number, varied in form, fabric, magnitude and usefulness."** A precise, datable census of the working Prague apparatus.
 - **The three Opera offered to Rudolf II.** Tycho names the program he presented to the Emperor on arrival: (1) the book "**on the Mechanical part of Astronomy**" = the *Astronomiae Instauratae **Mechanica*** (the gift here sent); (2) "**the Restitution of the thousand fixed stars**" = the *Stellarum octavi orbis … restitutio* / the 1000-star catalogue; (3) "**the verified motions of the Sun and Moon**" = the *Progymnasmata*. Crucially, **(2) and (3) were still in manuscript** in November 1600 ("for both are in manuscript … no convenience of making copies remained").
- **A documented *Mechanica* gift-distribution event.** Tycho **sends Landgrave Moritz a gift copy of the *Mechanica*** via Bopenhausen (Prague → Kassel, Nov 1600), offering the star-catalogue volume too — explicitly **for collation against the Kassel star observations** ("those stars which Your Highness has likewise observed there"). Cross-ref the Mechanica production/distribution layer.
- **The earlier books referenced.**
 - The **"Book of Epistles"** = Tycho's *Epistolarum astronomicarum liber* (Uraniborg 1596), which printed **Wilhelm IV's astronomical letters with Tycho's replies**, dedicated to Moritz — with some instrument-descriptions already in it; Tycho had also sent **engravings (*icones*)** of the instruments.
 - The ***Opus Palatinum*** = the *Opus Palatinum de triangulis* of **Rheticus / Valentin Otho** (Neustadt an der Haardt, 1596), which **Moritz had sent Tycho as a return gift** — proof that Moritz received the engravings.
- **Persons & works named.** Moritz of Hesse-Kassel; **Wilhelm IV** (the late father); **Johann von Bopenhausen** (envoy); the **King of Persia** (the Safavid embassy); **Rudolf II**; the *Epistolae astronomicae* (1596); the *Opus Palatinum* (Rheticus/Otho); the *Mechanica*, the 1000-star *Restitutio*, the *Progymnasmata* (Sun/Moon motions). Places: **Prague** (the house by the castle garden), **Denmark**, the **Elbe**, **Kassel** (implied "there").
- **Calendar.** *Die 10 Novembris Anni 1600* at Prague (imperial reckoning) → **10 November 1600 [N.S.]**; header and label agree.

documents.incipit: [TYCHO BRAHE AD JACOBUM BORDINGUM]. Magnifice et excellentissime vir, amice inprimis …

text.original:
[TYCHO BRAHE AD JACOBUM BORDINGUM].
Magnifice et excellentissime vir, amice inprimis honorande.

ACCEPI tandem diu desideratum responsum Magnif: Tuæ ad petitionem meam bis vel ter reiteratam nimirum de 600 joachimicis, qui loco interesse a quæstore juniorum principum Megapolensium isthic mihi debentur, et simul caussas, cur expectatione mea tardius M: T: mihi de hoc ipso negotio rescripserit, ex ijs quas 19. septembris Gustrouio ad me dedit, intellexi. Quibus etiam acquiesco. Sexcentos vero illos joachimicos ad clarissimum virum d. d. Lucam Backmeisterum, affinem tuum et communem nostrum amicum, missos esse, lubenter ex ijsdem percepi. Scribit is ad me, se pecuniam illam secum reseruaturum, donec illustriss: Saxoniæ electoratus administratoris magnificus legatus d:ns d. Gödelmannus illuc aduenerit. Quod etiam mihi non est ingratum, siquidem jam antea ipsum ob penuriam occasionum aliarum tuto mittendi, vt ita faceret, admonuerim. At cum prædictus d:ns Gödellmannus, tardius quam sperassemus, hinc discedat, adeo vt vix ante initia anni Juliani vestri Rostochium sit perventurus, nimis diu pecunia ista careo, quod tamen, siquidem aliter fieri non potuit, ferendum. Quia vero postea circiter quadrans anni solummodo restabit ad completionem ejus temporis, quo reliqui 600 loco hujus anni interesse numerandi sunt, Mag: T: enixe et peramanter rogatam habeo, vt efficere velit, totam summam a quæstore juniorum principum exsolui, et prædicto d:no Gödellmanno, dum isthic est, committi, ita vt 1200 joachimici, qui mihi ad instantis anni calendas aprilis pro duobus transactis annis debentur, pariter cedant, neque enim id iniquum censeri poterit, licet pauculi menses restent ad terminum præfinitum, quo sic aliquatenus compensetur ea, quam modo passus sum, plus quam dimidij anni frustratio. Quod autem id per eundem fieri quam maxime desiderem, duæ me impellunt graues caussæ, quarum vnam ex ipso d:no Godelmanno aut saltem ab affine tuo cognosces. Altera est, quod tam certam et tutam rationem 600 illos alios circa initia aprilis instantis anni huc adferendi non invenire potero quam hæc ipsa est per sæpedictum d:nm d. Gödellmannum, amicum meum singularem, huc expeditis Rostochij suis rebus, quam citissime fieri poterit, reuertentem, qui etiam suam mihi hac in re operam beneuole addixit. Quin et hoc Magnificentiam Tuam celare non possum, si id ipsi prius forte non innotuit, me certis de caussis et deliberato consilio totam summam decem illorum millium joachimicorum, quam illustrissimis junioribus principibus mutuo dedi, ad præfinitum terminum juxta tenorem contractus nostri reposcere, quod et antea d:no quæstori indicari jussi. Et jam denuo ipsum de eodem per literas admonui, neque enim ex re mea est, vt pecunia illa in loco hinc adeo remoto, a quo interesse statuto tempore huc non sine periculo et difficultate peruenire possit, diutius hær[eat], cum etiam alias plus commodi et usufructus intermediante eadem pecunia hic nancisci queam, veluti ipse quoque d:ns d. Gödellmannus plenius meum hac de re propositum aperiet. Quibus igitur possum precibus M: T: rogatam habeo, vt votis meis in hisce per omnia adesse non degrauetur. Ego, quæcumque a me vicissim proficisci poterint officia, eidem quam paratissimo animo defero, atque M: Tuam cum conjuge et familia quam diutissime et optime valere a Deo ter optimo maximo opto.

Dabantur Pragæ Bohemorum die 15to nouembris a:o 1600.
text.english:
**[TYCHO BRAHE TO JACOB BORDING].**
Magnificent and most excellent man, friend especially to be honoured.

I have at last received Your Magnificence's long-desired reply to my petition, twice or thrice repeated — namely concerning the **600 joachimsthalers** which are owed me there, in lieu of interest, by the treasurer of the younger princes of Mecklenburg — and at the same time I have understood, from those [letters] you sent me from **Güstrow on 19 September**, the reasons why Your Magnificence wrote back to me on this business later than I expected. With which I also acquiesce. That those six hundred joachimsthalers were sent to the most renowned man Lord Doctor **Lucas Backmeister**, your kinsman and our common friend, I gladly gathered from the same. He writes to me that he will keep that money with him until the magnificent legate of the most illustrious **Administrator of the Saxon Electorate**, Lord Doctor **Gödelmann**, shall arrive there — which is not unwelcome to me, since I had already advised him to do so, for the scarcity of other ways of sending it safely. But since the said Lord Gödelmann departs hence later than we had hoped — so that he will scarcely reach **Rostock** before the beginning of your **Julian year** — I am too long without that money; which, however, since it could not be otherwise, must be borne. And since afterward only about a quarter-year will remain to the completion of the time at which the **other 600**, in lieu of this year's interest, are to be paid, I earnestly and lovingly ask Your Magnificence to bring it about that the **whole sum** be paid out by the treasurer of the younger princes, and entrusted to the said Lord Gödelmann while he is there, so that the **1,200 joachimsthalers** owed me by the Kalends of April of the coming year, for the two elapsed years, may come to me together — nor can this be judged unfair, though a few months remain to the appointed term, that thereby the frustration of more than half a year, which I have just suffered, may be somewhat compensated. That I most greatly desire this be done through the same [Gödelmann], two weighty reasons impel me: one you will learn from Lord Gödelmann himself, or at least from your kinsman; the other is that I shall find no way so sure and safe of bringing those other 600 hither, about the beginning of April of the coming year, as this very one — through the oft-mentioned Lord Gödelmann, my especial friend, returning hither as quickly as may be once his affairs at Rostock are dispatched, who has also kindly promised me his help in this matter. Moreover I cannot conceal from Your Magnificence, if it has not perhaps become known to you before, that I — for certain reasons and by deliberate counsel — **demand back the whole sum of those ten thousand joachimsthalers** which I lent to the most illustrious younger princes, at the appointed term according to the tenor of our contract, which I also previously ordered to be indicated to the treasurer; and now again I have admonished him of the same by letter. For it is not to my advantage that that money remain longer in a place so remote from here, whence the interest cannot reach hither at the set time without danger and difficulty, since I can otherwise obtain more advantage and usufruct with the same money here — as Lord Gödelmann too will more fully disclose my purpose. With what prayers I can, therefore, I ask Your Magnificence not to find it burdensome to assist my wishes in these things in every way. I, in turn, offer you with most ready mind whatever services can proceed from me, and wish from God thrice best and greatest that Your Magnificence may fare most long and well, with your wife and household.

Given at Prague of the Bohemians, the 15th day of November, the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient & companion letter.** **Jacob Bording** of **Lübeck** (cf. brahe-t_16000331001, brahe-t_16010412001). This is the **Latin companion** to Tycho's same-day German letter to the rent-master **Andreas Meier** (brahe-t_16001115002, Prague, 15 Nov 1600): the two coordinate the same collection.
- **Position in the Mecklenburg debt-thread.** Acknowledging Bording's reply (from **Güstrow, 19 Sept 1600**), Tycho confirms the **first 600-thaler interest tranche** was sent to **Lucas Backmeister** (Superintendent of Rostock, Bording's kinsman), who holds it until **Gödelmann** — *here styled "legate of the Administrator of the Saxon Electorate"* — reaches Rostock (scarcely "before the beginning of your **Julian year**," i.e. O.S. New Year). Tycho asks that the **whole 1,200 thalers** (two years' interest, due by **1 April 1601**) be paid out together to Gödelmann now, to compensate the half-year's delay; and re-announces that he is **calling in the entire 10,000-thaler principal** at the contract term, "since I can obtain more advantage with the money here" in Bohemia.
- **Persons named.** Jacob Bording; **Lucas Backmeister** (Bacmeister, Superintendent of Rostock); **Johann Georg Gödelmann** (now legate of the Saxon Administrator); the **treasurer of the younger Mecklenburg princes**; the younger princes (Duke Johann's sons, cf. brahe-t_16000920002).
- **Calendar note.** Tycho's phrase *initia anni Juliani vestri* — "the beginning of **your Julian year**" — neatly marks the O.S./N.S. divide: Bording's Lübeck and Rostock keep Julian, Tycho's Prague keeps Gregorian. Dateline *Pragae … die 15to Novembris a:o 1600*, **New Style**; header agrees with the label.
- **Abbreviations.** Chancery contractions (*M: T:* = *Magnificentia Tua*, *d:ns d.* = *dominus doctor*, *a:o*) silently expanded; the source block keeps them.

text.original:
[TYCHO BRAHE AD ANDREAM MEYERUM].

MEIN freundtlichen gruß mit wunschunge alles guten zuuor. Ehrenuester vndt vornemmer herr rentmeister, ich kan dem herrn freundtlicher meinung nicht bergen, wie ich auß des herrn doctoris Lucae Backmeisterj, superintendentis zue Rostochk, neulich an mich gethonen schreiben vernommenn, das er die 600 thaller, so ich im anfang aprilis dießes lauffenden 1600 jahrs solte bej euch loco interesse von wegen der bewusten summa haben gehabt, von meinetwegen empfangen haben, wiewohl solchs nicht zur rechter zeit vber verhoffen geschehen ist. Das ich darumb noch bißhero daßelbige geldt durch gütte gelegenheit nicht habe könnenn erlangen, sondern allereerst durch dem herrn doctorem Johannem Gödelmannum, der gen Rostoch von hinnen zue verreisen in willens ist, alleine laßen abfodern, vndt dieweil er kaum furn neuenjahrstagk dahin gelangen kan, vndt hernacher nur drey monat restiren zu den termin, auf welchen ich die andern 600 thaller fur dießes jahrs interesse haben soll, so ist an dem herrn mein gantz fleißiges bitten vndt begeren, er wolle obgedachten h. doctor Gödellman die andern 600 thaller auf lieferung meiner quitantze zustehen laßen, dan ich sunsten keine so gewiße gelegenheit weis, dieselbe abholen zu laßen. Vndt wen schon die zeit, da dieses interesse sol bezahlt werden, nicht gentzlich alßdan verfloßen ist, sundern 2 oder 3 monat restiren, so ist hiergegen zue erachten, das ich in dießes jahrs zinse lenger alß ein halb jahr, nicht ohne meine schaden, bin aufgehalten vndt verhindert worden, vndt nun nicht vnbillig ist, das mir ein solche leidliche compensation hierinne wiederumb geschehen. Vndt nachdeme ich vor lengst inn Dennemarck geschrieben zue ein edelman von meinem blutßuerwandten mit nahmen Eske Bilde, das er von meinetwegen solte auf nechstverschienen Michaelis die gantze hauptsumme, alß 10000 thaller, aufsagen vndt resigniren, auf das ich dieselbige auf zukumpfftige ostern oder anfange des aprilis köntte zue Lübeck oder Hamburgk, durch ainen darzue gedeputirten treuen man, wiederbekommen, so versihe ich mich, das er daßelbe verrichtet hat, vndt bitte darumbe den herrn rentmeister, das er woll die versehunge thuen vndt eingedenck sein, das ich auf dieselbige zeit die gantze hauptsum an guetten reichsthaller, so in Ober-Teutschlandt gangkbar sein, köntte wiederbekommen. So ferne es aber nicht geschehen ist, entweder durch genanten Eske Bilde oder andern von meinetwegen, so will ich hiemit, krafft dieses brieffes, dieselbe hauptsumme auf nechstkommenden Michaëlis des 1601 Jahrs geresignirt vndt aufgesagt haben, dan mir nicht zutreglich, das dieselbe lenger alda stehen bleibe, vndt weis alhier in kunigreich Behemen besser nutz vndt profit damit zueschaffen. Welchs ich den herrn zeitlich zuuerstehen zue geben nicht habe sollen vnterlaßen, vndt wirt der obgedachte herr doctor Gödellman alda weiter bescheidt, nachdeme vonnothten, mundtlich oder schrifftlich, wißen zuberichten. Bitte der herr wolle hierinne thuen wie es vor sich selbst billich, vndt ich mich zue ihme gentzlich verlaße. Hiemit dem allmechtigen Gott beuehlen.

Datum Prag denn 15 dag nouembris anno 1600.
Des herren allzeit freundtwilliger
Tycho Brahe
mitt eigen h:tt.

vndt quittirung, die ich hiemit vbersende, nitt allerdinge friedtlich, soll

text.english:
**[TYCHO BRAHE TO ANDREAS MEIER].**

My friendly greeting, with the wish of all good, beforehand. Honourable and distinguished Lord rent-master, I cannot, in friendly intent, conceal from you that I have learned, from the letter lately written to me by Lord Doctor Lucas Backmeister, Superintendent at Rostock, that he received on my behalf the 600 thalers which I was to have had from you at the beginning of April of this current year 1600, in lieu of interest on the known sum — although this happened, contrary to expectation, not at the right time. Hence I have hitherto not been able to obtain that money through a good opportunity, but have only now let it be fetched solely through Lord Doctor Johann Gödelmann, who intends to travel from here to Rostock; and since he can scarcely reach there before New Year's Day, and thereafter only three months remain to the term at which I am to have the other 600 thalers for this year's interest, my wholly diligent request and desire of you is that you would let the aforesaid Lord Doctor Gödelmann have the other 600 thalers upon delivery of my receipt; for otherwise I know no such sure opportunity to have it fetched. And even though the time when this interest is to be paid is not then wholly elapsed, but 2 or 3 months remain, yet against this it is to be considered that I have been held up and hindered in this year's interest for more than half a year, not without my loss, and it is now not unfair that such a tolerable compensation be made me in return.

And since I long ago wrote into Denmark to a nobleman of my blood-relations named Eske Bille, that he should on my behalf, at the last past Michaelmas, give notice on and resign the whole principal sum — namely 10,000 thalers — so that I might recover the same at the coming Easter, or the beginning of April, at Lübeck or Hamburg, through a trusty man deputed thereto: I assume that he has done so, and therefore ask you, Lord rent-master, that you would make the provision, and be mindful, that I might at that same time recover the whole principal sum in good Reichsthalers, such as are current in Upper Germany. But insofar as it has not been done — either through the said Eske Bille or another on my behalf — I will herewith, by force of this letter, have the same principal sum resigned and given notice on for the coming Michaelmas of the year 1601; for it is not advantageous to me that it remain standing there any longer, and I know how to make better use and profit with it here in the kingdom of Bohemia. Which I ought not to have omitted to give you to understand in good time; and the aforesaid Lord Doctor Gödelmann will know how to report further information there, as needed, orally or in writing. I ask that you would do herein as is in itself fair, and I rely on you entirely. Herewith [I] commend [you] to Almighty God.

Given at Prague, the 15th day of November, the year 1600.
Your ever friend-willing
Tycho Brahe,
with his own hand.

In case the Lord Receiver [Rentmeister] should perhaps not be entirely satisfied with this document and receipt, which I herewith send, then Lord Doctor Gödelmann shall, on my behalf, let another [document] follow to you, under his own hand and seal, concerning these six hundred thalers which will fall due on the coming first of April of the year 1601 — [a document] which shall be worth exactly as much as if it had been done by myself. In witness whereof I have signed once again. Done on the day and in the place as above.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Andreas Meier**, ducal Mecklenburg **rent-master** (*Rentmeister*) at **Wismar** (cf. brahe-t_16010527001, brahe-t_16010718001). The MS is an autograph **draft (*Kladde*)** in the Basel Autographensammlung.
- **Significance — the earliest letter in the Mecklenburg 10,000-thaler debt thread.** This **15 November 1600** letter opens (chronologically) the documented exchange that the 1601 letters continue (Tycho→Meier 27 May & 18 July 1601; Tycho→Duke Ulrich 4 June 1601; the ducal replies of 24 July & 9 August 1601). It already lays out the whole financial structure:
 - The loan carries **semi-annual interest of 600 thalers** (*loco interesse*): the April-1600 tranche, paid late, was collected for Tycho by **Lucas Backmeister**, Superintendent of Rostock; the next 600 (due ≈ February 1601) Tycho asks Meier to release to **Johann Georg Gödelmann** against a receipt, since Gödelmann is travelling to Rostock and is Tycho's only sure carrier.
 - Tycho presses for a small **"tolerable compensation,"** since he has been kept out of this year's interest "for more than half a year."
 - **The principal (10,000 thalers).** Tycho has instructed his kinsman **Eske Bille** to give formal notice (*aufsagen und resignieren*) on the whole principal at the **last Michaelmas (29 Sept 1600)**, so he can recover it "at the coming Easter or beginning of April" at **Lübeck or Hamburg**, in **good Reichsthalers current in Upper Germany**. Should that notice have failed, Tycho here, "by force of this letter," **resigns the principal for Michaelmas 1601** — "for I know how to make better use and profit with it here in the kingdom of Bohemia."
- **Persons named.** Andreas Meier; **Lucas Backmeister** (Bacmeister, 1530–1608, Superintendent of Rostock; cf. brahe-t_16000919001), who collected the April interest; **Johann Georg Gödelmann** (the Mecklenburg jurist-diplomat carrier; cf. brahe-t_16010412001); **Eske Bille**, Tycho's Danish kinsman-agent.
- **Register / formulae.** Chancery German in the courteous third person (*der Herr*, "the Lord [= you]"); subscription *mit eigen Hand* (= *manu propria*). The Latin business terms (*loco interesse*, *quittance*, *resignieren*, *Termin*) embedded in the German by this chapter's convention
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Prag den 15 dag Novembris anno 1600*; **New Style** (Prague/imperial). Header agrees with the label.
- **Language.** This segment is Early New High German, continuous with the letter's published body (also German).
- **What it is.** A recovered closing clause of a business letter Tycho sent from Prague (15 November 1600) to Andreas Meier, evidently a Rentmeister (receiver/treasurer) at or near Rostock — the surviving published tail already shows Tycho withdrawing capital from Rostock to redeploy it "here in the kingdom of Bohemia."
- **The 600 thalers.** Very likely the same capital sum documented by Dreyer: an interest-bearing loan of Tycho's on which 6% annual interest was paid to his old friend Professor Lucas Backmeister at Rostock [Dreyer, *Tycho Brahe* (1890), citing *Breve og Aktstykker*, p. 145] — the published tail of this very letter names "Doctor Lucæ Backmeisterj, superintendentis zue Rostochk" directly.
- **Doctor Gödelmann.** Johann Georg Gödelmann appears elsewhere in Tycho's correspondence as early as 12 November 1598 (a letter to Tycho from Prague) [*Tycho Brahes Breve*, transcribing TBOO]. A Rostock-trained jurist, he is shown here acting as Tycho's legal proxy, empowered to issue a substitute, equally binding receipt for the loan if the original is not accepted — a concrete instance of Tycho managing financial affairs in his former territories by power of attorney while resident in Bohemia.
- **Legal formula.** The closing Latin tag "Actum die et loco ut supra" ("Done on the day and in the place as above") is standard notarial shorthand, appended even within an otherwise German business letter — evidence of the document's semi-legal, quasi-notarial character.

documents.incipit: MINN gandske wenlig hilsen nu och altidt forsendt med Vor Herre. Kierre Eske Bilde, …

text.original:
[TYCHO BRAHE AD ESCHILLUM BILDE].

MINN gandske wenlig hilsen nu och altidt forsendt med Vor Herre. Kierre Eske Bilde, broder och sønderlige gode wen, nest min wenlig och store tacksigelße for allt bewist gode, huilcket att forskylde ieg stedze will findis aff formuen willig yhues maade ieg kan giørre nogit, som du kanst haffue ære och gott aff. Giffuendis dig derhos ganske wenligen tillkiende, att epthersom ieg tillforen haffuer skreffuit dig till, att du willde fly mig det bref jndløst, som ieg haffde stoendis vdi Lantheholstein, och ieg forseer mig till, att du det till forgangen ombslag giortt haffuer, och att pengene erre vdi tiide bleffne opsagt vdi Lanthemeckelburg, epthersom ieg ocsaa tillforn haffuer skreffuit dig till och sent dig skrifftlig beskeen om, saa haffuer ieg nu skreffuit die vnge herre[r] aff Meckellburg deris rentmester till, vedt nauffn Andreas Meyer, att handt willde lade mig bekomme hoffuidtstollen vdigen, som er 10000 thaller, till den første dag aprilis eller 14 dage derepther y det seniste vdj dette tillkommendis aar. Er derfor min gandske wenlig bøn till dig, at du wilde well giørre och forschaffe det saa, att handt kunde bekomme det breff vdigien, som mig er giffuit paa samme penge, inden den termin kommer, att pengene kunde bliffue leuerit och oppeborrit vdj Lubeck eller Hamburgk hoß en wiß man, och siden hidt forskreffuen, epthersom ieg, nest Gudz hielp, inden den tidt kommer, will skriffue dig wijdre beskening till hervdom, och saa ieg megit gierne, att du medlertiidt met første muellighedt wilde skriffue mig till, huis du hervdj haffuer vdrettidt. Dersom det icke er skedt (huilcket ieg dog icke will forhoffue), daa beder ieg dig ganske gierne, att du willde flii det saa, att det wist skier met første muelighedt, och wille det bliffue well langt, om mandt skulle tøffue dermedt till omslag kommer vdigien. Giør flux derfor dit beste, som ieg tig fulkommendis tilltroer, att alting kan gange for sig met første muelighedt.

Kierre Eske, kan ieg dig ocsaa wenligen icke forholde, att siden mit gotz met minne jnstrumenter ere alltsammen kommen hidt op formedelst Elben, saa wijt den er skiffrig, och epther rømisch. keys. mayt. naadigst befalling och forordnung bleffet ført hidt till Prag, hor ieg nu er, daa sauner ieg allehonde dervdjblant, som icke er metkommenn. Och kan icke wijde, om det er bleffuen tillbage vdj min gaar y Kiøbenhauffn eller och till Lybech, thi till Hamburg eller Magdeburg tror ieg icke lettelligen att nogit endnu skall findis deraff. Beder ieg dig derfor ganske gierne, att du wilde well giørre och lade grandgiffuellig forfare, hor det seder sammen dermedt, och hor det kan findis. Jeg sender dig herhoß en sedell, paa huilcken ieg haffuer ladit antegnit saa megit, som ieg kan saa snart komme yhu att werre bortte deraff, endog det kan well endaa werre mere endt ieg saa snart kan sauffne. Jeg forseer mig till dig, att du giørrer din beste flidt hervdj, och haffuer ieg ocsaa skreffuit min factor vdj Lubeck till dervdom. Kierre Eske och kierre broder, fortenck mig icke, att ieg saa bemøder dig met mine sager, kan ieg giørre nogit vdjgien, som dig kan werre tient met, daa skallt du alltidt finde mig ganske willig och redebon dertill, och achter ieg, nest Gudz hielp, ydremere at skriffue dig och mine andre wenner till, naar Peder Bradis karll kommer hidt igien, som er dragen indt for hannom y lanthe Vngern. Will derfor nu och alltidt haffue dig met allt huis du well wilt Gudt allmechtigste befallidt.

Datum Prag den 16 dag nouembris anno 1600.
text.english:
**[TYCHO BRAHE TO ESKE BILLE].**

My most friendly greeting, now and always, conveyed with [the blessing of] Our Lord. Dear Eske Bille, brother and especial good friend — next [after] my friendly and great thanks for all the kindness shown, which to repay I shall always be found willing according to my means, in whatever way I can do anything from which you may have honour and good. Giving you herewith quite amicably to know that, since I have previously written to you that you would redeem for me the **bond I had standing in the land of Holstein**, and I trust that you have done it by the past *Umschlag*, and that the money has been duly given notice on in the land of **Mecklenburg** (as I have also previously written and sent you written information about): I have now written to the rent-master of the young lords of Mecklenburg, by name **Andreas Meier**, that he would let me recover the **principal — which is 10,000 thalers — by the first day of April, or 14 days thereafter at the latest, in this coming year**. It is therefore my quite friendly request to you that you would be so good as to arrange it that he may recover the bond given to me on this money before the term comes, [and] that the money may be delivered and received at **Lübeck or Hamburg** with a sure man, and afterward transferred up hither — since I, with God's help, before that time comes, will write you further instruction hereon; and I should be very glad if you, meanwhile, at the first opportunity, would write to me what you have accomplished herein. If it has not been done (which, however, I will not expect), then I ask you quite gladly to arrange that it surely happens at the first opportunity; and it would become quite long [delayed] if one were to wait until the *Umschlag* comes round again. Do therefore quickly your best — as I fully trust you — that everything may proceed at the first opportunity.

Dear Eske, I cannot amicably withhold from you that, since my **goods, with my instruments**, have all come up here by the **Elbe** — as far as it is navigable — and by the Roman Imperial Majesty's gracious command and ordinance been brought hither to **Prague**, where I now am, I **miss all sorts of things among them, which have not come along**. And I cannot know whether it has been left behind in my house in **Copenhagen**, or at **Lübeck**; for at Hamburg or Magdeburg I do not easily believe anything of it should still be found. I ask you therefore quite gladly that you would be so good as to have it carefully investigated how matters stand with it, and where it may be found. I send you herewith **a note, on which I have had set down so much as I can so quickly recall to be missing** of it — although there may well be even more than I can so quickly miss. I trust you to do your best diligence herein; and I have also written to my **factor at Lübeck** about it. Dear Eske, and dear brother, do not think ill of me that I thus trouble you with my affairs; [if] I can do anything in return that may serve you, then you shall always find me quite willing and ready thereto. And I intend, with God's help, to write further to you and my other friends when **Peder Brahe's man** comes hither again, who has gone in on his behalf into the land of **Hungary**. I will therefore, now and always, commend you, with all that you wish well, to God Almighty.

Given at Prague, the 16th day of November, the year 1600.

documents.abstract: Discusses Swedish and Livonian affairs and leaves to Sturtz's judgement what the late Chytraeus wished inserted in the Historiola, with Gödelmann carrying the relevant documents.
documents.incipit: EX ijs quas paulo post æquinoctium Autumnale ad me dedisti literis, quo in statu res tuæ …

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD CHRISTOPHORUM STURCIUM.
NOBILIS ET CLARISSIME VIR, AMICE HONORANDE.

EX ijs quas paulo post æquinoctium Autumnale ad me dedisti literis, quo in statu res tuæ sint, et cur rarius ad me scripseris, intellexi. Ego vero tibi quietem illam et studiorum commoditatem congratulor, ac literarum intermissionem lubens excusatam habeo.

De rebus Suecicis et Livonicis similia ijs, quæ scribis, imo adhuc plura hîc cognovimus — quem das finem, pater alme, furorum?

Negotium illud de ijs, quæ Historiolæ huius anni Domini D. CHYTRÆI laudatæ memoriæ inseri ipse, dum in vivis esset, volebat, nec ego abnui, siquidem eius continuatio a te, uti etiam scribis, pertexenda erit, tuæ prudentiæ relinquo, quid in eo faciendum vel omittendum duxeris. Habet secum gener eius Dominus D. GÖDELMANNUS, qui hîc Legatum agit Saxonicum, amicus meus singularis, quæ hac de re inter Dominum D. CHYTRÆUM et me ventilata sunt, tibi monstranda, si forte priora isthic interierunt; is etiam plenius hac de re tecum loquetur, neque tamen in his quippiam vobis præscribo aut urgeo, sed relinquo liberum agere prout lubuerit. Perinde enim apud me erit, quacunque ratione id fiat, nec ægre feram, etiamsi plane omittatur.

In privilegio hîc obtinendo pro libris tuis in publicum edendis, lubens tibi meam navabo operam, sed scire prius oportet, quales illi sint libri, et quid contineant; si enim quippiam habent, quod religioni, quam Catholicam vocant, adversatur, aut eos, qui hanc non amplectuntur, commendet, vix quippiam impetrabimus.

Nova quæ hîc narrantur, a prædicto Domino GÖDELLMANNO percipies, qui etiam nonnulla ad continuationem historiæ huius anni facientia tecum facile communicabit. Plura non addo, sum enim ita alias occupatus, ut calamum hîc sistere oporteat.

Tu itaque cum omnibus tuis quam optime et felicissime vale.
Dabantur Pragæ Bohemorum 16to IXbris Anno 1600.
text.english:
**Tycho Brahe to Christoph Sturtz.**
Noble and most distinguished man, friend to be honoured.

From those letters which you sent me a little after the autumnal equinox, I understood in what state your affairs are, and why you have written to me more rarely. But I congratulate you on that rest and convenience for [your] studies, and gladly hold the interruption of letters excused.

About Swedish and Livonian affairs, we have learned here things similar to what you write — nay, still more: "*what end of the furies do you grant, kind father?*"

That business about the things which Master Dr. Chytraeus, of praised memory, himself wished — while he was alive — to be inserted into this year's *Historiola* (nor did I refuse), since its continuation will, as you also write, have to be woven by you, I leave to your prudence: what you judge ought, in it, to be done or omitted. His son-in-law, Master Dr. Gödelmann — who acts here as Saxon Legate, my singular friend — has with him the things which were ventilated about this matter between Master Dr. Chytraeus and me, to be shown to you, if perchance the earlier ones perished there; he will also speak with you more fully about this matter. Nor, however, do I prescribe or urge anything on you in these [matters], but leave [you] free to act as you please. For it will be all the same with me by whatever method it be done, nor will I take it ill even if it be entirely omitted.

In obtaining a privilege here for publishing your books, I will gladly do my service for you; but it is necessary first to know what kind of books they are, and what they contain. For if they have anything which is opposed to the religion which they call Catholic, or which commends those who do not embrace this [religion], we shall scarcely obtain anything.

The news which is told here, you will learn from the aforesaid Master Gödelmann, who will also easily share with you some things bearing on the continuation of this year's history. I add no more, for I am otherwise so occupied that I must here stop the pen.

You, therefore, with all yours, fare as well and as happily as possible.
Given at Prague of the Bohemians, the 16th of November, in the year 1600.

- **The Virgilian tag.** *quem das finem, pater alme, furorum?* — "what end of the furies [madnesses] do you grant, kind father?" — Tycho's witty adaptation of **Virgil, *Aeneid* I.241** (Venus to Jupiter: *quem das finem, rex magne, laborum?*), applied to the **Swedish/Livonian war** (the Charles-vs-Sigismund conflict; cf. brahe-t_16000329002, …16010310001). Rendered as the quotation it is.
- **The Chytraeus autobiography.** Tycho leaves it to Sturtz's judgement whether, and how, to insert into the continuation of **David Chytraeus's annual chronicle** the account of Tycho's life that Chytraeus had wanted (cf. brahe-t_16001116003); **Gödelmann** — here explicitly named as **Chytraeus's son-in-law** (*gener*) and "Saxon Legate" — holds the relevant material. Tycho is studiedly indifferent ("nor will I take it ill even if it be entirely omitted").
- **The book-privilege caveat.** Tycho will help obtain a **printing privilege** at Prague for Sturtz's books, but warns that, in Catholic imperial Prague, "if they have anything opposed to the religion they call Catholic, or commend those who do not embrace it, we shall scarcely obtain anything" — a candid note on Counter-Reformation censorship.
- **Calendar.** *Pragae Bohemorum 16to IXbris 1600* = **16 November 1600** (*IXbris* = November, the ninth month from March); Prague (imperial) = **New Style**. Header agrees with the label.

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD MARTINUM BRASCHIUM..

LITERIS tuis, eruditissime et amantissime Domine BRASCHI, etsi vix otium suppetat, ut nunc quæ vellem respondeam (sum enim plurimis alijs negotijs distractus) malui tamen potius hæc pauca quam nulla ad te dare, ne amicitiam nostram negligere viderer. De carminibus tam MELISSI quam tuis iam satis inter nos convenit, et par stat sententia.

Quæ Dominus D. DAVID CHYTRÆUS optimæ memoriæ, dum adhuc in vivis erat, de mea e Dania emigratione annuæ suæ historiolæ, me consentiente, inserere voluit, si ea istic interciderunt, Magnificum Saxonici Electoratus hîc Legatum agens, Dominus D. GÖDELLMANNUS, qui vos nunc accedit, in alio exemplo ea monstrare poterit, modo res sic postulet. Sed non multum interest, sive hæc fiant, sive non, quemadmodum hac de re ad Dominum D. LUCAM BACKMEISTERUM et Dominum D. STURTZIUM, historicum vestrum, plenius perscripsi. Carmen illud tuum, cuius antea meministi, iam accepi, quod mihi perplacet. Canisium, quod Hungariæ Camisium aliqui vocabant, siquidem eo detracto pateret hostibus in Stiriam et Austriam facilior aditus, ante paucas hebdomadas in Turcarum potestatem, quod dolendum est, pervenit, quo occupato mox Papam castrum obsederunt, quod ijs vix resistere poterit. Cœtera a Domino D. GÖDELLMANNO cognosces.

Iamque quam optime cum omnibus tuis vale.
Dabantur Pragæ Bohemorum 16 Novembris Anno 1600.
text.english:
**Tycho Brahe to Martin Brasch.**

To your letter, most learned and most loving Master Brasch — although leisure scarcely suffices for me to answer now as I would wish (for I am distracted by very many other affairs) — I preferred nonetheless to send you these few [words] rather than none, lest I should seem to neglect our friendship. About the poems, both Melissus's and yours, enough is now agreed between us, and [our] judgement stands equal [we are of one mind].

The things which Master Dr. David Chytraeus, of best memory, while he was yet among the living, wished — with my consent — to insert about my emigration from Denmark into his annual little history, if these have been lost there, Master Dr. Gödelmann — the Magnificent [man] acting here as Legate of the Saxon Electorate, who now comes to you — will be able to show in another copy, if the matter so require. But it does not much matter whether this be done or not, as I have written more fully about this matter to Master Dr. Lucas Backmeister and to Master Dr. Sturtz, your historian. That poem of yours, which you mentioned earlier, I have now received, and it pleases me greatly. Kanizsa — which some called the "Camisium of Hungary," seeing that, with it removed, an easier approach to Styria and Austria would lie open to the enemy — a few weeks ago came (which is to be lamented) into the power of the Turks; and this taken, they soon besieged the fortress of Pápa, which will scarcely be able to resist them. The rest you will learn from Master Dr. Gödelmann.

And now fare most well, with all your [people].
Given at Prague of the Bohemians, 16 November, in the year 1600.

documents.abstract: Requests more rigorous presentation of planetary hypotheses, specifying that Ptolemaic/Alphonsine and Copernican data each be used according to their own parameters.
documents.incipit: VENIT ad me Dresdâ hisce diebus M. AMBROSIUS RHODIUS, et nonnulla, quæ circa Hypotheses …

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD MELCHIOREM JŒSTELIUM..

VENIT ad me Dresdâ hisce diebus M. AMBROSIUS RHODIUS, et nonnulla, quæ circa Hypotheses tentasti, clarissime et præstantissime D. D. IŒSTELI, secum a te attulit. Utrumque mihi gratum fuit. Faciam, quantum ad illum attinet, prout mones. Hypotheses autem cuperem accuratius enodari, et magis perspicue explicari, ita ut nihil desit aut sit superfluum, atque ordine debito sese omnia insequantur. Neque quæstio est, ut loca Planetarum, per Hypothesin quamcunque inventa, cum meis observatis conferantur, quibus nulla ratio hactenus præsupposita consentiet, sed sufficit, ut ea, quæ secundum PTOLEMÆUM deducuntur, calculo respondeant Alphonsino, ita tamen ut Apogæa, Eccentricitates et dimensiones orbium adhibeantur, prout Alphonsina fert methodus, a PTOLEMÆO potissima ex parte derivata, nisi quod Apogæa hisce temporibus aliter applicantur. Quæ vero iuxta COPERNICUM fiunt, ea oportet ipsius pariter datis et assumptionibus, in ijs quæ modo dixi, inniti, et calculo Prutenico convenire, idque sive iuxta ipsius speculationem Solem ad centrum Universi quiescentem, in annuo orbe, eius loco revoluta Terra, statuemus, sive immutata hac, uti ego ostendi, Hypothesi, Terra ibidem immota permanente, et assumptis Eccentroepicyclis more Ptolemaico, cum circello circa centrum, loco æquantis, uti recte imitatus es. Sed hæc non est proprie inversio, sed potius permutatio quædam et cum Ptolemaicis hypothesium COPERNICI conciliatio. Nostra autem innovatio, quæ Epicyclos non minus quam ille negligit, Terra nihilominus immota permanente, etiam aliud adhuc particulare requirit, ut apparentijs satisfiat, quam a te iuxta COPERNICI proportiones factum est. Ostendunt siquidem apparentiæ, Planetarum circuitus proprios non medium, sed verum, adeoque ipsum corpus Solis, respicere, ita ut Martiæ stellæ, quæ præcipuam hîc parit differentiam, phænomena, etiam extra Acronychios situs, accurate et multipliciter considerata, nos ad ipsius Solis Apogæum iuxta initia ♋cri manuducant, ut de Eccentricitate nunc nihil dicam. Recte tamen a te factum est, quod nostram hypothesin Coperniceæ collatam, et assumptis ijsdem dedomenis, eundem præbere sideris locum, quem eius exigit numeratio, demonstrâsti. De his vero per oportunius ocium deliberatius cogita, et quæ vel hactenus perfectius elaborata habes, quam ea sunt, quæ misisti, vel inposterum elaborare dabitur, mecum communica.

Cœterum de Typographo LEMANNO sic habe. Precium quod annotavit pro Balla papyri 15 fl. nimium est, venditur enim hîc, ubi omnia longe cariora sunt quam Lipsiæ aut Witebergæ, una eiuscemodi Balla 8 Ioachimicis. Et cum Witebergæ essem, potui eam a cartopœis pro decem fl. si recte memini, obtinere. Verum quantum ad mercedem attinet, quam pro labore suo Typographico in imprimenda una Balla postulat, facile inter nos conveniret, si papyrum æquiore precio adhibuerit, ita ut decem fl. vel ad summum totidem Ioachimicis (quod tamen pluris est, quam hîc una Balla venit) comparetur. Qua de re ut cum ipso diligenter meo nomine agas, te peramanter rogatum habeo, utque promptius intelligat, hanc esse meam sententiam, idipsum Germanicis verbis contignatum illique tradendum, uti voluisti, adiungo. Exemplar autem, quod ea continebit, quæ de Luna in 6 illis quaternionibus excudenda erunt, quam primum ad mundum (in quo nunc laboratur) descriptum fuerit, mittam, modo prius de voluntate Typographi certior a te factus fuero, quod ut mature facias, etiam atque etiam peto. Vale et saluta amicos Witebergenses, quibus scribere nunc non vacat, sed fiet id, volente Deo, per oportunius otium, iterumque vale.

Dabantur Pragæ Bohemorum 18 Novembris Anno 1600.
text.english:
**TYCHO BRAHE TO MELCHIOR JÖSTEL.**

Master **Ambrosius Rhodius** came to me from Dresden these days, and brought with him from you, most renowned and excellent Lord Doctor Jöstel, some of what you have attempted concerning the **Hypotheses**. Both were welcome to me. As far as concerns him [Rhodius], I will do as you advise. But the Hypotheses I should wish to be more accurately unfolded and more perspicuously explained, so that nothing be lacking or superfluous, and everything follow in due order. Nor is the question that the places of the Planets, found by any Hypothesis whatever, be compared with my observations — with which no method hitherto presupposed will agree — but it suffices that what is deduced according to **Ptolemy** answer to the **Alphonsine** calculation, yet so that the **Apogees, Eccentricities, and dimensions of the orbs** be employed as the Alphonsine method bears (derived for the most part from Ptolemy, except that the Apogees are differently applied in these times). But what is done according to **Copernicus** must likewise rest on his own data and assumptions, in the things I have just mentioned, and agree with the **Prutenic** calculation — and that, whether we set the **Sun at rest at the centre of the Universe** according to his speculation, the Earth being revolved in its place in an annual orb; or whether, this Hypothesis being changed (as **I have shown**), the **Earth remaining there immobile**, and eccentric-epicycles being assumed in the Ptolemaic manner, with a **little circle about the centre in place of the equant** — as you have rightly imitated. But this is not properly an inversion, but rather a certain permutation, and a **reconciliation of the Copernican hypotheses with the Ptolemaic**. Our own innovation, however — which neglects the **Epicycles** no less than he does, the Earth nonetheless remaining immobile — requires yet one further particular thing, that the appearances be satisfied, beyond what has been done by you according to Copernicus's proportions. For the appearances show that the **planets' own circuits respect not the mean, but the true [Sun] — indeed the very body of the Sun** — so that the phenomena of the star **Mars** (which here produces the chief difference), even outside the **acronychal** [opposition] positions, accurately and manifoldly considered, lead us by the hand to the **Apogee of the Sun itself, near the beginning of Cancer ♋** — to say nothing now of the Eccentricity. Yet rightly was it done by you, that you demonstrated that **our hypothesis, compared with the Copernican** — the same data being assumed — **yields the same place of the star** which its computation requires. But about these things think more deliberately at a more convenient leisure, and share with me what you have hitherto elaborated more perfectly than what you sent, or what it shall hereafter be granted you to elaborate.

For the rest, concerning the printer **Lehmann**, take it thus. The price he noted for a **bale of paper — 15 florins — is too much**; for here, where everything is far dearer than at Leipzig or Wittenberg, one such bale sells for **8 joachimsthalers**; and when I was at Wittenberg I could get it from the paper-makers for **ten florins**, if I rightly recall. But as for the **fee** he demands for his typographic labour in printing one bale, we would easily agree, if he employed paper at a fairer price — say, procured for ten florins, or at most as many joachimsthalers (which is yet more than one bale sells for here). Wherefore I lovingly ask you to deal diligently with him in my name; and, that he may the more readily understand this to be my view, I add the same framed in German words, to be handed to him, as you wished. The **copy** containing what is to be printed concerning the **Moon in those 6 quaternions** I will send as soon as it has been fair-copied (on which work now proceeds) — provided I have first been informed by you of the printer's willingness, which I ask again and again that you do in good time. Farewell, and greet the Wittenberg friends, to whom there is now no leisure to write, but it shall be done, God willing, at a more convenient leisure; and again, farewell.

Given at Prague of the Bohemians, 18 November, the year 1600.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient & context.** **Melchior Jöstel**, Tycho's Wittenberg computational collaborator — this is the **follow-up to brahe-t_16000327001** (27 March 1600), where Tycho had set Jöstel the planetary-hypotheses task for the **second Book of the *Epistolae***. Jöstel's results were carried from Dresden by **Master Ambrosius Rhodius** (Ambrosius Rhode, 1577–1633, mathematician, later professor at Wittenberg).
- **Significance — a cornerstone statement of the Tychonic planetary theory.** One of the clearest concise expositions of Tycho's system and its computational reconciliation with its rivals:
 - **The reconciliation programme.** The hypotheses are *not* to be tested against Tycho's own observations ("with which no method hitherto presupposed will agree"), but made to **agree (a) with the Alphonsine calculation** on the Ptolemaic side — using the **apogees, eccentricities, and orb-dimensions** the Alphonsine method (itself "derived for the most part from Ptolemy") supplies — **and (b) with the Prutenic calculation** on the Copernican side.
 - **The Tychonic transformation.** Either set the **Sun at rest at the centre with the Earth in an annual orb** (Copernicus), *or* — "this Hypothesis being changed, **as I have shown**" — keep the **Earth immobile** and use **eccentric-epicycles in the Ptolemaic manner, with a little circle (*circellus*) about the centre in place of the equant**. Tycho insists this is **"not properly an inversion, but a permutation and a reconciliation of the Copernican hypotheses with the Ptolemaic."**
 - **The distinctive feature — orbits about the *true* Sun, proved from Mars.** "Our innovation … neglects the **Epicycles** no less than Copernicus … the Earth nonetheless remaining immobile," but **"requires one further particular thing"**: the appearances show **the planets' circuits respect not the *mean* but the *true* Sun — the very body of the Sun.** The decisive evidence is **Mars** (*"which produces the chief difference here"*): its phenomena, *even outside the acronychal (opposition) positions*, "lead us by the hand to the **Apogee of the Sun itself, near the beginning of Cancer**." (This — that planetary orbits are referred to the true Sun, and Mars as the critical case — is precisely the line later so consequential for Kepler.)
 - **Jöstel's correct result:** he had demonstrated that **the Tychonic and Copernican hypotheses, on the same data, yield the same planetary place** — confirming their geometric equivalence.
- **Technical terms (kept;).** *Hypotheses* (the planetary models); *Apogaeum* → **apogee**; *Eccentricitas* → **eccentricity**; *Eccentroepicyclus* → **eccentric-epicycle**; *aequans* → **equant**; *circellus* → **little circle**; *Acronychus situs* → **acronychal position** (opposition to the Sun); *medium / verum Solem* → **mean / true Sun**; *calculus Alphonsinus / Prutenicus* → the **Alphonsine** / **Prutenic** Tables; ♋ = **Cancer** (glyph kept in source). *dedomena* (Greek *δεδομένα*, "givens/data") rendered "data."
- **The printing business.** The printer ***Lehmann*** (*Lemannus*, a Leipzig/Wittenberg printer) quotes **15 florins per bale of paper** — too much (a bale sells for **8 joachimsthalers** at Prague, 10 fl. at Wittenberg); Tycho will agree the **printing fee** if paper is reckoned fairly, and encloses his terms "in German" for Jöstel to hand over. He will send the fair-copy of the **6 lunar quaternions** (the lunar-theory text; cf. brahe-t_15981231001, brahe-t_16000327001) once the printer's willingness is confirmed.
- **Persons named.** Melchior Jöstel; **Ambrosius Rhodius**; **Ptolemy**, **Copernicus** (and the Alphonsine/Prutenic tables); the printer **Lehmann**; the Wittenberg friends.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Pragae Bohemorum 18 Novembris Anno 1600*; **New Style** (Prague). The edition label gives only the place ("Prague"); date supplied from dateline/identifier.

documents.incipit: LITERAS tuas, Vir Nobilissime atque Mathematicorum omnium facile Princeps, quas quidem …

text.original:
IOANNES GEORGIUS HERWARTUS AB HOHENBURG AD TYCHONEM BRAHE.

LITERAS tuas, Vir Nobilissime atque Mathematicorum omnium facile Princeps, quas quidem die 14 huius mensis Pragæ ad me dedisti, ex Ingolstadio ad me transmissas, hac ipsa horâ probe accepi. D. CHRISTOPHORUS VARSEVICIUS, uti optassem, ad me non venit. M. IOAN. KEPLERUM male valere doleo, et æque contristor, conditione commodâ eum iam carere. Si apud Cæsaream Maiestatem, quod abominor, ei non sit permanendum, ipse quoque dispiciam, anne forte alibi res suas instituere queat.

Tabulas BLANCHINI, PRUGNERI et BEURBACHIJ, quas petis, curabo, si modo extent, ut habeas. IOANNIS ANGELI Astrolabium et Planum cum IACOBO ANGELO de Cometis ob defectum tabellariorum mitto hisce iunctum, teque quam fœlicissime florere ex animo opto.

Datæ Monachij die 27 Nov. A. 1600.
text.english:
**Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg to Tycho Brahe.**

Your letter, most noble man and easily prince of all mathematicians — which indeed you sent me at Prague on the 14th of this month, [and which was] transmitted to me from Ingolstadt — I have duly received this very hour. Master **Christoph Warszewicki** did not come to me, as I would have wished. I grieve that Master **Johann Kepler** is in poor health, and I am equally saddened that he now lacks a comfortable position. If he is not to remain with the Imperial Majesty — a thing which I abhor [to think] — I too will look about whether perhaps he may be able to set up his affairs elsewhere.

The *Tables* of **Blanchinus**, **Prugner**, and **Peurbach**, which you seek, I will see to it — if only they are to be had — that you have them. The *Astrolabium* and *Planum* of **Johann Angelus**, together with **Jacobus Angelus** *On Comets*, I send joined herewith, owing to a lack of couriers; and I wish from my heart that you flourish most happily.

Given at Munich, the 27th day of November, in the year 1600.

text.original:
IOANNES GEORGIUS HERWARTUS AB HOHENBURG AD TYCHONEM BRAHE.

PRÆVIA precatione fœlicis et auspicatissimi novi anni, Vir Nobilissime atque Mathematicorum omnium facile Princeps, mitto Alphonsinas Tabulas recognitas, Parisijs Ano 53 impressas, No. 43 signatas. Et simul unâ METHODIJ uti fertur Revelationem, quam describi curavi, cum liber, cui inserta fuerat, ob molem transferri nequeat. Neque iam occurrit aliud, quod ad te modo scribendum esse ducam. Summa enim illa tua ἀκρίβεια, quâ vel ad sexagesimam gradus partem novissimus tuus calculus Solis et Lunæ, cum exactissimâ tuâ cœlestium apparentium contemplatione, coincidit, eo me redegit angustiarum, ut quo me vertam, non habeam, et ob id ipsum Matheseos operationes tantisper omnino seponendas esse decreverim, donec calculum istum tuum novissimum abs te absolutum, quem liberali tuâ spontaneâ et benevolâ pollicitatione iam quodammodo meum fecisse videris, mihi impertiri dignatus fueris. Ea siquidem, quæ Arithmeticam concernunt, satis hac ætate elaborata esse videntur. Quæ vero Astronomica sunt, vel saltem cum ijs coniuncta, manifestis difficultatibus sunt implicita. Ut sive PTOLOMÆUM quis sequatur, sive ALPHONSUM, sive COPERNICUM, in multis offendat necesse est. Unice itaque restaurationem hanc tuam exopto, cui, tametsi forte nondum extremam manum adhibueris, tamen ea sine omni dubio aliorum calculos longe superabit. Atque hisce tibi fœlicissima quæque præsagio et ex animo precor.

Datæ Monachij 10 Decemb. A. 1600.
text.english:
**Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg to Tycho Brahe.**

With a prefatory prayer for a happy and most auspicious New Year, most noble man and easily Prince of all mathematicians, I send the **Alphonsine Tables**, revised, printed at Paris in the year [15]53, marked No. 43. And, at the same time, the *Revelation* (as it is called) of **Methodius**, which I had transcribed, since the book in which it had been inserted cannot be transferred [sent] on account of its bulk. Nor does anything else now occur which I judge ought, just now, to be written to you. For that supreme exactness [*ἀκρίβεια*] of yours, by which your newest calculation of the Sun and Moon coincides — even to the sixtieth part of a degree [i.e. one arc-minute] — with your most exact contemplation of the celestial appearances, has reduced me to such straits that I have nowhere to turn; and for that very reason I have resolved that the operations of Mathematics must be altogether set aside for a while, until you have deigned to share with me that newest calculation of yours, completed by you — which, by your liberal, spontaneous, and benevolent promise, you seem already in some manner to have made mine. For those things which concern Arithmetic seem, in this age, sufficiently elaborated; but the things which are Astronomical, or at least conjoined with them, are entangled in manifest difficulties — so that, whether one follow Ptolemy, or Alfonso, or Copernicus, one must necessarily stumble in many [points]. Uniquely, therefore, do I long for this restoration of yours, which — although perhaps you have not yet applied the final hand to it — will nonetheless, beyond all doubt, far surpass the calculations of others. And with these I presage for you, and pray from my heart, every happiness.

Given at Munich, 10 December, in the year 1600.

departures_from_tekstnet.basis: The text printed here descends from one harvest of tekstnet's page and was read against Dreyer's page images in July 2026; a second harvest of the same page is kept beside it. Where the two disagree in a word, both readings are listed: Dreyer's page decides, and unless the audit paragraph names the word, that check has not yet been made for it. documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Johann Georg Herwart von Hohenburg** (the Munich correspondent of the 1600 series), here in fulsome praise of Tycho's computational accuracy and impatient for his renewed tables.
- **Books sent.** *Alphonsinae Tabulae recognitae, Parisijs Ano 53 impressae, No. 43* = the **Alphonsine Tables** in the revised **Paris 1553** printing (item No. 43 on Tycho's desiderata list). *Methodij … Revelatio* = the apocalyptic *Revelations of [Pseudo-]Methodius* (the medieval *Apocalypse of Pseudo-Methodius*), transcribed for Tycho because the volume containing it was too bulky to send.
- **The praise of Tycho's accuracy.** *summa illa tua ἀκρίβεια* — "that supreme exactness [*akribeia*] of yours"; the claim that Tycho's "newest calculation of the Sun and Moon" agrees with observation *vel ad sexagesimam gradus partem* — "even to the sixtieth part of a degree," i.e. to one arc-**minute** (the *scrupulum primum*, 1/60°; corrected from an earlier "arc-second" gloss — the same correspondent uses the same phrase for the arc-minute in his 8 Nov letter, 16001108001). Herwart says this has driven him to **suspend his own mathematical work** until Tycho shares the finished tables — which Tycho's *restauratio* (his renewal of astronomy) will, he is sure, set above Ptolemy, Alfonso, and Copernicus alike. *extremam manum adhibere* = "to apply the final hand," i.e. to complete/polish.
- ***ἀκρίβεια*** (Greek) — "precision, exactness"; transcribed and rendered "exactness." *Alphonsum* = Alfonso X (the Alphonsine Tables' royal patron).
- **Calendar.** *Monachij 10 Decemb. 1600* = **10 December 1600**; Munich (Catholic Bavaria) = **New Style**. Header agrees with the label.
