documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Christophorus Henniochus** (Christoph Henioch), a **physician** (*Med.* = *Medicinae Doctor*) at **Rostock**, already in correspondence with Tycho (cf. Tycho→Henniochus, brahe-t_16000329003). A learned medical/alchemical contact of Tycho's Rostock circle.
- **Significance — a European news-letter (March 1601).** The body is a compact **survey of European affairs**, the kind of manuscript "avviso" exchanged among the learned. Its sweep:
 - **Sweden/Lübeck.** *Carolus … nunc protector Sueciae* = **Duke Charles** (later **Charles IX**), then **Protector/Regent of Sweden** (he took the crown only in 1604); his unsettled quarrel with the Hanseatic city of **Lübeck**.
 - **The Polish Diet at Warsaw & the Prussian fief.** The **Elector of Brandenburg** (Joachim Friedrich), backed by envoys of **Denmark**, of *"our prince"* (the **Duke of Mecklenburg** — Rostock's overlord; Henniochus writes "our"), and others, sought the **succession to the *Feudum Brutenicum*** (the **Ducal Prussian fief**, held of the Polish crown) — refused, conditional on aiding **Sigismund III Vasa**, *"King of Poland, now deprived of Sweden,"* to recover the Swedish throne *postliminio* (by right of return).
 - **The Polish-Swedish war in Livonia.** The Poles' declared enemies: **Charles of Sweden**, who had pushed so far into **Livonia** that "nothing remains to the Poles there but **Riga**"; the **Grand Duke of Muscovy**; and the **Voivode of Wallachia**.
 - **The Low Countries.** **Archduke Albert of Austria** (sovereign of the Spanish Netherlands) preparing to lead an army into **Holland**, resisted by the **Dutch States** — "the coming summer will not pass without great tragedies."
 - **The false Sebastian of Portugal.** **King Sebastian**, "lost in the African battle" (**Alcácer-Quibir, 1578**) and "now come back to life" — one of the **Sebastianist pretenders** — unacknowledged by Spain but favoured by his partisans, sheltering "with the King of France."
 - **Essex.** *Exseccius Comes Angliae* = **Robert Devereux, 2nd Earl of Essex**, rumoured successor to **Queen Elizabeth I**; sent to **Ireland** (1599), charged with mismanaging the campaign, "condemned in Parliament … in peril of his life."
 - **Denmark/Gotland.** **Christian IV** building fortresses in Denmark and Gotland.
 - **Hungary.** Henniochus expects *Tycho* (at the imperial court) to be his source for news of the **Ottoman–Habsburg "Long War."**
- **News-lag (worth noting).** By 21 March 1601 (O.S.) **Essex had already been executed** (25 February 1601); Henniochus reports him only as "a captive in peril of his life" — the news had not yet reached Rostock. A clean illustration of contemporary information-latency, preserved (not "corrected") by this chapter's convention
- **Persons named.** Christophorus Henniochus (sender); **Nicolaus Maul**, *"formerly your [Tycho's] servant,"* the prior courier; the unnamed **spagyrist** (*sphagirus* — an alchemical physician) carrying this letter, whom Tycho had wished to engage; Charles of Sweden; the Elector of Brandenburg; Sigismund III of Poland; Archduke Albert; King Sebastian (the pretender); the Earl of Essex; Queen Elizabeth I; Christian IV.
- **Address crux (flagged).** Tycho is styled *Dominus hereditarius in Knustorpff et **Heereswart***. *Knustorpff* = **Knudstrup** (his hereditary seat); ***Heereswart*** is uncertain — most likely the sender's garbling of a second estate-name (possibly **Herrevad**, where Tycho lived early, though he did not hold it hereditarily). Rendered as written and flagged; not resolved.
- **Lexical flags.** *muscitatus* (of Essex, "hitherto kept quiet/silent") is non-standard — apparently a coinage for "kept mute/inactive"; rendered by sense. The sentence *hoc bellum non solum ad Carolum pertinere videtur, nisi temeritatis … vitium attrahat* is slightly compressed; read as "this war concerns more than Charles alone — unless he is simply being rash," and flagged.
- **Greek/technical.** *grammatophorus* (Greek, "letter-carrier"); *sphagirus* (= *spagyrus*, a Paracelsian alchemical physician) — kept and glossed.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Rostochij 21 Martij anni 1601* — Rostock kept the **Julian calendar (O.S.)**. The edition label ("31 marts") disagrees with the dateline and the identifier (16010321001, the 21st); the **label is in error** and is rejected in favour of the source's own date, by this chapter's convention

- **§1 Dreyer collation.** News-postscript (Brunswick's renewed blockade + the failed imperial peace mediation), restored from Dreyer VIII, p. 408 (this is the Christophorus Henniochus→Tycho letter; the postscript follows Henniochus's signature).
No correction added. The single flagged defect (an alleged 'exercitum' interpolation) was checked against Dreyer, Opera Omnia VIII, p.407, which itself prints 'ALBERTUS dux Austriae exercitum ducet in Hollandiam' — identical to our published text. The audit's premise does not hold; the text stands as published.

translation.warrant:
Collated against **Dreyer, *Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia*** (the edition of record), reading the printed page images. Dreyer TBOO VIII pp.407-408 read as page images (within the 406-409 extract, flanked by the Camineaus and Rosenkrantz letters). The flagged postscript ('Dux Brunsuiccensis civitati denuo commeatum intercipit, nec ulla ratione placabilis dicitur, inter quos, missis et datis a Caesarea Maiestate commissarijs, nuper frustra de pace tractatum esse, notum est.') IS genuinely printed by Dreyer on p.408, immediately after the signature block and before the next letter's heading — the earlier restoration is verified word-for-word accurate, and its English rendering is correct. Names (Nicolaus Maul, Charles of Sweden, Essex, Sebastian of Portugal), the Warsaw Diet detail, and the closing date all match Dreyer. One unrelated single-word insertion ('exercitum', not in Dreyer) elsewhere in the letter caps the grade at C despite the letter being otherwise clean and the postscript restoration checking out.

**1 defect found:**
- **text error** (low). Dreyer's text has no 'exercitum' (army) here; the transcribed original and the English both add the word. The surrounding context ('apparatus... belli') already implies a military force, so the added word does not materially distort the sense. Dreyer prints: *ALBERTUS dux Austriae ducet in Hollandiam*.

**Repaired.** Verified the letter's single defect against Dreyer, Opera Omnia VIII, pp.406-409 (page images). Dreyer's own printed page directly contradicts the audit's claim: 'exercitum' is present in the edition of record, not an interpolation. Rejected with high confidence; no other issues were observed in the passage.

text.original:
GENEROSO MAGNIFICO ET NOBILISSIMO VIRO DOMINO TYCHONI BRAHE, EQUITI DANO, S. CÆS. MAIESTATIS CONSILIARIO PRÆCIPUO ET MATHEMATICO LONGE CELEBERRIMO, DOMINO AC PATRONO OBSERVANDO.
PRAGA.

S.

RECTE perlatas esse meas ad te literas, generose et nobilissime vir, index scida superiore Decembri me docuit. Volui, uti suggestum fuerat, rem denuo et statim prehendere; sed avocarunt morbus uxoris, negotia clientum, sexcenta alia. Nunc paullo expeditior, et amanter a vidua illa CUNONIS filia invitatus, libenter ei hoc operæ dare volui, ut, quod bono etiam publico futurum providerem, sollicitatoris partes susciperem, quo opus illud horologicum, multis, magnis ac diuturnis laboribus ac vigilijs elucubratum ac perfectum, lucem tandem sub tuo, aut cuiuscunque videatur nomine, aspicere possit. Superioribus addo hoc quoque, esse apud eandem viduam opus, secundum præcepta ista inchoatum, atque adeo semicompletum, quod morte præventus absolvere auctor non potuit. Qui librum emat paullo liberalius, facile unâ idipsum quoque impetret; cui summam manum peritus in arte et libro isto instructus sine negotio imponat. Sumptum credo facile libenterque ferat pietate, sapientia, virtute et meritis in rempub. maximus, Divus Cæsar RUDOLPHUS, mathematicis disciplinis ipse quoque et supra conditionem principum excultus, quem non ALPHONSUM alterum, sed et illo potiorem non immerito prædicamus. Neque dubium mihi est, quin monitu suggestuque tuo res procedat melius: quod ut facias, sive viduæ illius pauperculæ nomine, sive boni publici respectu, sive quod hanc operam haud difficulter te præstiturum virtus et humanitas mihi tua spondet, quam possum officiose submisseque rogo. Qua de re literas tuas, vel si ijs non vacat, saltem nutum tuum expecto. Si quid ad me velis, et occasio alia non sit, Bratislaviam ad clarissimum Dn. MONAVIUM mittere possis, qui, qua est humanitate et virtute, id porro haud gravate curet. Vale, vir generose et optime, meque et studia mea, quibus ipsis quoque MÆCENATE opus sit, apud Sacram Cæsaream Maiestatem, cui vitam ac felicitatem perpetuam precor, tibi commendata habe.

Vale iterum.
Francofurto cis Viadrum a. d. XII Martij Anno MDCI.
Generostis ac magnif. t. observantiss.
BALTHASAR CAMINAÆUS I. V. D. et professor publ.
text.english:
**To the generous, magnificent and most noble man, Lord Tycho Brahe, Danish knight, principal councillor of His Imperial Majesty and by far the most celebrated mathematician, his lord and patron to be revered. Prague.**

Greeting.

That my letters were duly delivered to you, generous and most noble man, a note informed me last December. I wished, as had been suggested, to take the matter up anew and at once; but the illness of my wife, the affairs of clients, and six hundred other things called me away. Now a little freer, and kindly invited by that widow, the daughter of Cuno, I have willingly wished to devote this effort to her: that — foreseeing it would be for the public good as well — I might take up the part of advocate, so that that horological work, elaborated and perfected by many, great and long-continued labours and vigils, might at last see the light under your name, or whosever's may seem [best]. To the above I add this too: that there is with the same widow [another] work, begun according to those precepts, and indeed half-completed, which the author, forestalled by death, could not finish. Whoever should buy the book a little more liberally would easily obtain that very thing along with it; on which an expert, skilled in the art and instructed in that book, might without trouble lay the finishing hand. The cost, I believe, would be easily and gladly borne by the Divine Emperor Rudolph — greatest in piety, wisdom, virtue, and services to the commonwealth, himself too cultivated in the mathematical disciplines beyond the condition of princes — whom we proclaim, not undeservedly, not a second Alphonso, but even greater than he. Nor do I doubt that by your advice and prompting the matter will go forward the better; and that you would do this — whether in the name of that poor little widow, or out of regard for the public good, or because your virtue and humanity assure me you will render this service without difficulty — I ask as dutifully and submissively as I can. On which matter I await your letter, or, if you have no time for that, at least your nod. If you should want anything from me, and there be no other occasion, you could send it to Breslau, to the most renowned Lord Monavius, who, being of the humanity and virtue he is, would see to it further without grudging. Farewell, generous and excellent man; and hold me and my studies — which themselves too have need of a Maecenas — commended to you with the Sacred Imperial Majesty, to whom I pray perpetual life and happiness.

Farewell again.
From Frankfurt-on-the-Oder, the 22nd of March, in the year 1601.
Most observant of Your Generosity and Magnificence,
Balthasar Caminaeus, Doctor of Both Laws and public professor.

documents.apparatus:
- **Direction & sender.** An **inbound** letter **to** Tycho at Prague. **Balthasar Caminaeus** (Caminäus), *Iuris utriusque doctor et professor publicus* — **doctor of both laws and public professor at Frankfurt an der Oder** (*Francofurtum cis Viadrum*, "Frankfurt on this side of the Oder," to distinguish it from Frankfurt-am-Main).
- **Purpose.** Caminaeus acts as **advocate (*sollicitator*)** for a widow seeking to get a deceased author's **horological work** (*opus horologicum* — a treatise on, or design for, time-measuring / astronomical clockwork) into print, plus a second, **half-finished** work in the same vein. He asks Tycho to lend his name and influence, and floats **Emperor Rudolf II** as the natural patron to bear the cost.
- **Persons named.**
 - *vidua illa Cunonis filia* = "that widow, **the daughter of Cuno**" — the heir pressing for publication; neither she nor her late husband (the *auctor* of the horological work) is further identified in the source.
 - *Divus Caesar Rudolphus* = **Emperor Rudolf II**, praised as himself learned in mathematics and likened to **Alfonso X of Castile** ("the Wise," patron of the *Alfonsine Tables*) — *non Alphonsum alterum, sed et illo potiorem*, "not a second Alfonso, but greater than he."
 - *clarissimus Dn. Monavius* = **Jacob Monau (Jacobus Monavius)** (1546–1603), the Breslau humanist and patron of letters, proposed as a relay for any reply.
 - *Maecenas* invoked generically as the type of the literary patron.
- **Place.** *Francofurtum cis Viadrum* = **Frankfurt an der Oder**; *Bratislavia* here = **Breslau / Wrocław** (the Neo-Latin name *Vratislavia*, spelled *Bratislavia*), Monau's city — **not** modern Bratislava.
- **Epistolary formulae & titles.** *S.* = *salutem*; *Vale … Vale iterum* → "Farewell … Farewell again"; subscription *Generosit[at]is ac magnif[icentiae] t[uae] observantiss[imus]* → "Most observant of Your Generosity and Magnificence"; *I. V. D.* = *Iuris Utriusque Doctor* ("Doctor of Both Laws," civil and canon).
- **Calendar & dating crux.** The working transcription's dateline reads *a. d. XII Martij Anno MDCI* — literally "the 12th of March 1601," which does not match the edition's placement. Read as Roman reckoning, the intended form is **a. d. XI Kal. Apriles** (*ante diem undecimum Kalendas Apriles*) = **22 March**, and Dreyer/the catalogue date the letter accordingly; the transcribed "*XII Martij*" is a corruption of that Roman dateline. Following Dreyer by this chapter's convention, the header gives **22 March 1601 (New Style)** — Frankfurt an der Oder being in Brandenburg, but the letter directed to Catholic-Imperial Prague and dated New Style in the edition. The source form is preserved in the block; the reading is explained here rather than silently emended.

documents.incipit: MINN gandske venlig hilsen nu och altiidt med Vor Herre. Kierre Holger Rossenkrantz, …

text.original:
ERLIG OCH WELBYRDIG MANDT HOLGER ROSENKRANTZ TIL ROSENHOLM, MIN KIERRE SWOGER, SLECHT OCH BØRDT, OCH SØNDERLIGE GODE WENN, GANDSKE WENLIGEN TILLSKREFFVITT.

MINN gandske venlig hilsen nu och altiidt med Vor Herre. Kierre Holger Rossenkrantz, slecht och byr, swoger och sønderlig gode ven, Gudt almechtigste verre nu och altijdt hoß eder och beuare eder lenge och well frae allt det, eder kan werre skadelligt enten till sæll eller liff, och nest megenn tacksigelse for allt bewijst gode, hvilcket ygien aff formuen att forskylde ieg altijdt will findiß willig och redebon.

Giffuendiß eder herhoß gandske wenligen tillkiende, att epthersom jeg nest Guds hielp achter engang emellumb paske och pinsdag nu nestkommendis her udj Prag paa dette Curtianiske huß, som jeg nu bor, att giørre min kierre datters erlig och welbyrdig iomfru Elisabet Brahes brøldup med en herremandt, født udj Westfalen, som tiener her y röm: key: may: gaardt, vedt nauffn Frantz Tegnagel till Campe, saa er derfor min gandske wenlig bøn till eder, att y wille well giørre och till forneffnte tijdt komme hidt, och giørre eder løstig och gladt med andre fornemme herrer och gott folck aff høibemelte key: may: raadt och anden y dette loufflig kongeriige Bohemen, som jeg forhaabiß daa till samme tijdt her hoss mig att forsamblis. Kierre Holger och kierre swoger, giører nu her udj, epthersom jeg mig till eder forlader, saa viit eder nogenlunde mueligt kan werre; eder och eders att tiene vdigien, will jeg altijdt findis willig. Och will jeg nu icke lenger opholde eder med denne min skriffuelse, menß nu och altijdt haffue eder Gudt almechtigste bode till sæll och liff befallidt.

Daterit vdj Prag paa dett Curtianske huß, som ehr yderst vedt bøen, som jeg nu bor, den 4. aprilis anno 1601. Stylo novo.
Tyghe Brahe
egenh.
text.english:
**Honourable and well-born man Holger Rosenkrantz to Rosenholm, my dear brother-in-law, kin and blood, and especial good friend, written to in all friendliness.**

My quite friendly greeting, now and always, with Our Lord. Dear Holger Rosenkrantz — kin and blood, brother-in-law and especial good friend — may God Almighty be now and always with you, and preserve you long and well from all that can be harmful to you, whether to soul or to life; and next, much thanksgiving for all the good [you have] shown, which to requite in turn, of [my] ability, I will always be found willing and ready.

Giving you herewith, in all friendliness, to know: that, since I intend — next, with God's help — at some time between Easter and Pentecost now coming, here at Prague, at this Curtius house where I now dwell, to make the wedding of the honourable and well-born maiden Elisabeth Brahe, my dear daughter, with a nobleman born in Westphalia who serves here in the Roman Imperial Majesty's court, by name Frans Tengnagel to Camp — so is, therefore, my quite friendly request to you, that you would do well, and come hither at the aforesaid time, and make yourself merry and glad with other distinguished lords and good folk of the high-mentioned Imperial Majesty's Council, and others in this lawful kingdom of Bohemia, who, I hope, will then at the same time be gathered here with me. Dear Holger, and dear brother-in-law, do now herein — as I rely upon you — so far as may be at all possible for you; to serve you and yours in return, I will always be found willing. And I will not now detain you longer with this my writing, but, now and always, have you commended to God Almighty, both to soul and to life.

Dated at Prague, at the Curtius house — which is at the outermost edge of the city — where I now dwell, the 4th of April, in the year 1601. New Style.
Tyge Brahe,
[his] own hand.

documents.apparatus:
- **The wedding invitation.** A document of high biographical value: Tycho invites **Holger Rosenkrantz** (his kinsman) to the **wedding of his daughter Elisabeth Brahe to Frans Tengnagel**, to be held **at Prague between Easter and Pentecost 1601**. The marriage of **Elisabeth (Elisabet) Brahe** to **Frans Gansneb Tengnagel van de Camp** (*Frantz Tegnagel till Campe*) — Tycho's long-serving noble assistant (the "living letter" of the 1600 letters), here "a nobleman born in **Westphalia** who serves at the Imperial court" — took place at Prague in **June 1601**, a few months before Tycho's death (October 1601).
- **The Curtius house — a notable identification.** *dette Curtianiske hus … som er yderst ved byen* = "**this Curtius house**, which is at the outermost edge of the city, where I now dwell." This is the Prague mansion of the late Imperial Vice-Chancellor **Jakob Kurz von Senftenau (Jacob Curtius**, d. 1594) — the very Curtius commended in brahe-t_15980626002 and mourned by Herwart in brahe-t_16000908001 — which Tycho occupied as his Prague residence and observatory after the move from Benátky.
- **Recipient.** **Holger Rosenkrantz** "the Learned," addressed as *svoger, slægt og byrd* ("brother-in-law, kin and blood") — the kinsman of the Cramer/Liddel and 1598 letters (brahe-t_15980331001, …0524001, …0914001); asked to come and to bring the festal company of imperial councillors.
- **Orthography.** Late Danish chancery: *erlig/welbyrdig*, *swoger* (brother-in-law/kinsman), *brøldup* (bryllup, wedding), *iomfru* (maiden), *herremandt* (nobleman), *till saell eller liff* = *til sjæl eller liv* ("to soul or to life"), *forsamblis* (forsamles, be gathered), *egenh.* = *egen hånd* ("own hand"). Reading-verified as **Danish**.
- **Calendar.** *Prag … den 4. aprilis anno 1601. Stylo novo* = **4 April 1601, New Style** (explicit; Prague, imperial). Header agrees with the label. The wedding itself is set "between Easter and Pentecost" (so c. April–May/June 1601).

documents.incipit: PRÆPROPERUS Patruelis tui hinc ad vos discessus, exoptatissime mi OLIGERE, fecit, ut …
documents.editorial_note: **Text recovered.** The postscript or enclosure, missing from the first transcription, has been restored from the text of record and translated. The Source and English columns below are now complete.

text.original:
NON SALTEM GENERIS NOBILITATE SED ETIAM INSIGNI DOCTRINA ILLUSTRI VIRO OLIGERO ROSENKRANTZIO, DOMINO DE ROSENHOLM, AMICO, CONSANGVINEO ET AFFINI SUO INTEGERRIMO.

PRÆPROPERUS Patruelis tui hinc ad vos discessus, exoptatissime mi OLIGERE, fecit, ut tibi, prout alias voluissem, tunc non scripserim; concredidi nihilominus illi nonnulla oretenus tibi secreto referenda, quod et præstitum esse, modo tecum fuit, nullus dubito. Cæterum nunc nactus commodiorem oportunitatem, has subsequi volui. Neque tamen eorum, quæ ille viva voce (uti mihi persuadeo) tibi exposuit, quidpiam hîc repetam. Intercessionem Cæsaream pro illo sæpe et diligenter, interea dum abfuit, ursi, nec quidem unquam mihi denegata est a Domino CORRADUCIO, Vicecancellario, sed cum tam multa simul inciderint, gravissime Rempublicam concernentia, semper excusavit se, quod non haberet oportunitatem eiuscemodi particularia proponendi, antequam principaliora et magni momenti negotia expedita essent, et sancte affirmavit, nulla sua negligentia, sed necessitate sic efflagitante, id retardari. Rogavit itaque, ut hanc dilationem patienter ferrem, se nihilominus omnia in meliori forma effectui daturum. Nunc vero ante biduum mihi referri fecit, impetratam iam esse intercessionem illam, atque in secreto consilio, ut scribatur, conclusum. Quare se confestim, ut concipiatur et ad mundum exaretur, effecturum; unde adhuc pauculos dies exspectare oportebit, antequam voti compotes reddemur. Quin et postea aliquot interlabi poterunt, priusquam Cæsarea Maitas sua manu subscripserit, adeo lente procedunt hîc omnia, præsertim hoc tempore, ob periculum a Turca imminens, propter occupatum Canisium et denuo ferme amissam Transylvaniam. In me tamen nulla erit mora, quin, ut negotium hoc mature absolvatur, operam dem; postea tibi exemplum mittam, originale autem mecum reservabo, donec FRIDERICUS redierit, sic enim fieri voluit, si res nimis diu protraherentur.

Habito nunc in ædibus a priore Procancellario Domino IACOBO CURTIO Laudatæ Mem. exstructis et a viduâ relictâ liberalitate Cæsareæ Maitis pro 10000 Ioachimicis in meos usus coëmtis, quæ tamen duplo pluris exædificatori constiterunt. Accepique hîc exoptatam commoditatem pro studijs, observationibus et domesticis rebus debite administrandis; amœnissimus hortus ædes undique circumdat, Muro circumseptus. Constitui vero, favente Numine, in his ipsis ædibus Nuptias filiæ ELIZABETÆ cum Nobili viro FRANCISCO TEGNAGLIO, quem nosti, celebrare aliquo oportuno tempore inter Pascha et Pentecosten; quo nomine ad præcipuos quosdam et maxime singulares in Dania et Holsatia amicos Literas Nuptiales dedi, non quod eos interfuturos sperem, sed saltem ut conscij sint. Aliquos tamen ex intimis propriâ Personâ adventuros, aut saltem quempiam suo loco missuros confido. Cumque te inter sinceriores et integerrimos præcipuo loco reputem, quibus possum verbis, te rogatum velim, ut assumpta coniuge tuâ charissimâ, meâ ex fratre Nepte, tuâ præsentiâ hanc solennitatem augere et condecorare non degraveris. Iter non admodum longinquum, viæ tunc erunt faciles, et sumptus non multum excedent domesticos. Licebit sic in via veteres tuos amicos Wittebergenses iucunde revisere, et hîc aulam Imperatoriam variaque visu digna cognoscere, quæ tibi voluptati et forte etiam aliquando commodo erunt. Adsunt insuper in propinquo binæ thermæ, quas si sanitatis caussa ingredi lubuerit, minimo impendio id unâ fieri poterit. Interea sobolem tenellulam facile et tuto alicui Heroinæ e consangvineis commendabis. Adveniet etiam (uti spero) Soror mea SOPHIA, et ubi adveneritis, tum demum diem certum nuptialem præfiniam, ut et hîc Illustres et præcipui viri, amici et noti invitentur. Rogavi FRIDERICUM, ut serio tecum hac de re ageret, daretque operam, quo persuaderet, licet ego de tua in me fide et constantiâ nihil addubitem. Quare pluribus id contendere nolo. Sed te avide et certo expecto, utque queas nobis salvus adesse. Vale, saluta coniugem et matrem tuam ex me officiosissime.

Datum Pragæ in novo Uraniburgo Cæsareo die 5. Aprilis Anno 1601, Stylo novo.
Tuus TYCHO BRAHE.

Filius meus TYCHO abijt cum Legatis Persicis per Italiam,
Galliam et Hispaniam transiturus, munitus
salvo conductu Imperatoris. Habes hîc
Effigies duorum præcipuorum ex Legatis, et Cæsaris responsum.
text.english:
**To the man illustrious not only by nobility of birth but also by distinguished learning, Holger Rosenkrantz, Lord of Rosenholm, his most upright friend, kinsman, and relative.**

The over-hasty departure hence to you of your cousin, my most longed-for Holger, made it that I did not then write to you as I should otherwise have wished; nevertheless I entrusted to him some things to be related to you secretly by word of mouth, which (as he was just now with you) I do not doubt was done. But now, having got a more convenient opportunity, I wished these [lines] to follow — yet I will not repeat here anything he set out to you, as I am persuaded, by living voice. **The imperial intercession for him I urged often and diligently while he was away**, nor was it ever denied me by Lord **Coraduz**, the Vice-Chancellor; but since so many things befell at once, most gravely concerning the Commonwealth, he always excused himself that he had no opportunity of proposing such particulars before the more principal and weighty matters were dispatched, and solemnly affirmed that it was delayed by no negligence of his, but by pressing necessity. He asked, therefore, that I bear the delay patiently, [saying] he would nonetheless bring everything to effect in a better form. But now, two days ago, he had it reported to me that **that intercession has now been obtained, and resolved in the privy council that it be put in writing**; wherefore he will at once have it drafted and fair-copied — whence it will be needful to wait yet a few days before we are made masters of our wish. Nay, and afterward several [days] may slip by before the Imperial Majesty has signed it with his own hand — so slowly do all things proceed here, especially at this time, on account of the danger threatening from the **Turk**, with **Kanizsa occupied and Transylvania again nearly lost**. Yet in me there will be no delay; I will see that this business is completed in good time; afterward I will send you a copy, but keep the original with me **until Frederik returns** — for so he wished it done, should the matter be drawn out too long.

I now dwell in the house built by the former Vice-Chancellor Lord **Jacob Curtius**, of praised memory, and **bought from his widow, by the Imperial Majesty's liberality, for 10,000 joachimsthalers for my use** — which, however, cost the builder double the price; and I have here a most desired convenience for duly conducting my studies, observations, and domestic affairs, a most pleasant **garden** surrounding the house on all sides, enclosed by a wall. And I have resolved, God favouring, **to celebrate in this very house the wedding of my daughter Elisabeth with the noble man Franz Tengnagel, whom you know, at some convenient time between Easter and Pentecost**; on which account I have sent **Wedding-Letters** to certain chief and most especial friends in Denmark and Holstein — not that I hope they will attend, but only that they may be aware; yet I trust some of my intimates will come in person, or at least send someone in their place. And since I reckon you in a chief place among the more sincere and upright, with what words I can I would ask that, **taking your dearest wife — my niece by my brother — you would not find it burdensome to augment and adorn this solemnity by your presence**. The journey is not very long, the roads will then be easy, and the costs will not much exceed those at home. You will thus be able, on the way, pleasantly to revisit your old **Wittenberg** friends, and here to see the imperial court and various things worth seeing, which will be a pleasure — and perhaps sometime an advantage — to you. There are, moreover, two **thermal baths** nearby, which, if you wish to take for your health, can be done at the same time at very little expense. Meanwhile you will easily and safely commend your tender little child to some noble lady of [your] kin. **My sister Sophie**, too, will come (as I hope); and when you have [all] come, then at last I will fix the certain wedding-day, that here too illustrious and chief men, friends and acquaintances, may be invited. I have asked **Frederik** to deal seriously with you on this, and take pains to persuade you — though I doubt nothing of your faith and constancy toward me. Wherefore I will not press it further. But I eagerly and surely await you, [praying] that you may be able to be safely with us. Farewell; greet your wife and your mother from me most dutifully.

Given at Prague, in the new imperial Uraniborg, the 5th day of April, the year 1601, New Style.
Your Tycho Brahe.

My son Tycho has departed with the Persian Legates, about to pass through Italy, France, and Spain, furnished with the Emperor's safe-conduct. Here you have the Portraits of two of the chief among the Legates, and the Emperor's reply.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Holger Rosenkrantz** "the Learned" of Rosenholm — Tycho's *consanguineus et affinis* (cf. brahe-t_15980628001, brahe-t_15981231002). The MS is a later Langebek *afskrift*.
- **Significance — the wedding invitation, and the imperial intercession for Frederik Rosenkrantz.** Two intertwined matters:
 1. **The imperial intercession for Frederik Rosenkrantz.** Frederik (Holger's *patruelis*/cousin — the disgraced-then-rehabilitated nobleman now in imperial service; cf. brahe-t_16000926002) had come and gone (carrying secret oral messages). Tycho had repeatedly pressed **Coraduz** for an **imperial letter of intercession** on Frederik's behalf (toward his rehabilitation in Denmark); it was always granted in principle but delayed by graver state business, and is **now obtained and ordered drafted** in the privy council — awaiting only Rudolf II's signature, slow "on account of the danger from the **Turk**, with Kanizsa occupied and Transylvania nearly lost." Tycho will keep the **original until Frederik returns**.
 2. **The wedding of Elisabeth Brahe and Franz Tengnagel (the central occasion).** Tycho announces he will **celebrate the wedding of his daughter Elisabeth with Franz Tengnagel** "in this very house [the Curtius house], between Easter and Pentecost [1601]," having sent **Wedding-Letters** to chief friends in **Denmark and Holstein**. He warmly **invites Holger and his wife** — *"my niece by my brother"* (Sophie Brahe, daughter of Tycho's brother **Axel Brahe** — not to be confused with Tycho's sister Sophie, named just below) — promising easy roads, the sights of the imperial court, and the nearby **thermal baths**; **his sister Sophie** is also expected, after whose arrival the firm wedding-day will be set. (Parallel to the same-period invitation to Duke Ulrich, brahe-t_16010415003.)
- **The Curtius house (cross-ref).** The "new imperial Uraniborg": **Jacob Curtius's house, bought from his widow by Rudolf II for 10,000 joachimsthalers** (though it had cost the builder double), with its walled garden — consonant with brahe-t_16010415002, brahe-t_16010412001, brahe-t_16010410001.
- **Persons named.** Holger Rosenkrantz and his wife **Sophie Brahe** (Tycho's niece, Axel Brahe's daughter) and mother; **Frederik Rosenkrantz** (Holger's cousin, the intercession's beneficiary); **Coraduz** (Vice-Chancellor); **Jacob Curtius** (and his widow); **Elisabeth Brahe** and **Franz Tengnagel** (the bridal couple); **Sophie Brahe** (Tycho's sister); **Rudolf II**.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *die 5. Aprilis Anno 1601, Stylo novo*; **New Style** (Prague). Header agrees with the label.
- **What this is.** A striking piece of enclosed news and physical enclosures — engraved or drawn portraits ("Effigies") of two leading members of a Persian embassy, plus a copy of Emperor Rudolf II's official reply to that embassy — sent along with this letter, which the published tail confirms is Tycho's invitation to Holger Rosenkrantz for the wedding of his daughter Elisabeth Brahe to Franz Tengnagel.
- **Tycho the Younger.** "My son Tycho" is Tycho Tygesen Brahe. Christianson's *On Tycho's Island* records that he travelled to Italy in 1601 to pursue university studies [Christianson, *On Tycho's Island* (Cambridge, 2000)] — but says nothing there about a Persian embassy. This recovered passage supplies a genuinely new specific detail absent from that standard secondary account: that he travelled in company with a Persian legation, under an imperial safe-conduct, continuing on through France and Spain as well as Italy.
- **This exact letter, cross-referenced.** Dreyer's biography independently identifies this 5 April 1601 letter to Holger Rosenkrantz as the Latin companion to a Danish-language wedding-invitation Tycho sent the same correspondent the previous day, both concerning the Tengnagel–Elisabeth Brahe marriage [Dreyer, *Tycho Brahe* (Edinburgh, 1890)]; Thoren's *Lord of Uraniborg* prints a translation of the companion Danish letter (his "Letter 7," 25 March/4 April 1601) describing Rosenkrantz there as Tycho's "kinsman by birth, brother-in-law" [Thoren, *The Lord of Uraniborg* (Cambridge, 1990)].
- **The Persian legation — not further identified in the works consulted.** No source searched named the specific embassy passing through Prague at this date; contextually this falls in the period of diplomatic contacts between Shah Abbas I of Persia and European courts (the historically well-known Husain Ali Beg mission reached several European capitals around 1600–1601), but this is inference from the general period, not an identification confirmed in the literature, and is flagged accordingly rather than asserted.

documents.abstract: Reports the Emperor's continued imperial favour and the recent purchase of a large house for 10,000 thalers for his use and astronomical study.
documents.incipit: DURCHLAUCHTIGSTER hochgeborner furst, gnedigster herr. Ewer Furstl: Gnaden sein meine …

text.original:
DEM DURCHLAUCHTIGSTEN HOCHGEBORNEN FURSTEN VND HERRN, HERRN VLDARICH, HERTZOGEN ZU MECHELLENBURGK, FURSTEN ZU WENDEN, GRAFFEN ZU SCHWERIN, DER LANDE ROSTOCH VND STARGARTTEN HERRN, MEINEM GNEDIGSTEN FURSTEN VNDT HERRN.

DURCHLAUCHTIGSTER hochgeborner furst, gnedigster herr. Ewer Furstl: Gnaden sein meine vnterthenigste, gantzwillige dienste iederzeit hochstes fleißes beuor. Vndt seitenmahl ich itzo ainen aigenen potten inn Dennemarck abgehen laße, hab E: Furstl: Gnaden ich mit dießem meinem geringen schreiben in vnterthenigkait zu ersuchen vnd deroselben vor die vielfaltige mir bezaigte gut vndt wohlthatten zu dancken nitt vmbgehen könnenn.

Waß dan meinem itzigen zustandt betrifft, werden E: Furstl: Gnaden denselben vnlangst auß mainem vorigen schreiben vmbstendiglichen vernomen habenn, darumb hie ferner zu wiederholen vnuonnötten. Dan ihre rom: key: may:, mein allergnedigster herr, nochmahlß (wie vor, ie lenger ie mer) mir mit allen keyßerlichen gnaden (Gott lob) gewogen, vndt haben erst neulich deß gewesen reichs vice-cancellarij Jacobj Curtij l. m. ansehenliche vndt statliche behausung, so ahn ainen hohen ortt eußerst an der königlichen hauptstadt Prag gelegen, vmb zehentausendt thaller zu meinem vnd deß studij astronomicj nutz mildtlichen kauffen laßen, wo alle meine jnstrumenta so ain zeitlang in jhr kay: maytt: lustgarten nahe beim schloß gestanden, itzo conuenientj modo disponirt, auch ain laboratorium pro spagyricis exercitijs angerichtet wirt.

Ferner kan E: Furstl: Gnaden ich vnterthenigst nit verhalten (wie dieselben auch noch gnedigst werden wißen zu entsinen), daß vor ainem halben jahr die summa von zehentausendt reichsthallern, so der jungen herschafft zu Mechlenburgk von mir gutwillig vorgestrecht, deroselben rentmeistern Andreß Meiern durch meinen vettern vndt volmechtigen derer örter Eske Bilden auffkundigen laßen, dan ich dießer örter landtgütter eingekaufft, zu welcher entrichtung ich darzue vervrsacht worden, worein dan E: Furstl: Gnaden damahlß (immaßen sölliches der pilligkeit gemeß) sich gantz gnedigst vndt willfharlich erzaigt, jch auch alhie die leutte darauff vertröstet habe. Anietzo aber werde ich von herrn doctore Gödellman, welchem ich die zehentausendt thaller hauptsumma sampt dem interesse meinentwegen einzuenehmen volnkomblich commission gegeben, glaubwürdig berichtet, daß obgedachter rentmeister nitt allein in der summen, sondern auch deß schon verschienen interesse erstattung weigerlich befunden werde vndt andere große außgaben furwende.

Dieweiln dan E: Furstl: Gnaden alß hochstgedachter jungen herschafft vormund darin gnedichst gewilfharet, sollichs auch ann ihme selbs pillich vndt ich andern leutten darauff zuegesagt, alß gelanget an E: Furstl: Gnaden mein vntherthenigste gantz fleißige pitt, sie wollen nit geschehen laßen, daß meine wort zue nichte gemacht vndt ich dadurch an meinem biß dato wohllhergebrachten nahmen vnd glimff abbruch erleiden, sondern mehrgedachte summa vndt interesse furderlichst, wofern sölliches vber hoffnung noch nitt geschehen, anhero vberkommen muege. Sölliches vmb E. Furstl. Gnaden (wozue dan dero gnedigsten thats ich mich vnterthenig getroste) eußerste mueglicheit gehorsambst zuverdienen, erkenne ich mich stetz schuldig vnd geflißen.

Thue hiemit E: Furstl: Gnaden sampt dero vielgeliebten gemahlen zu glucklicher langwehrender regierung vndt zue deren ferneren furstlichen gnaden mich vnterthenigst vndt getreulich entpfhelen.

Datum Prag, den 10 ap. anno 1601.
Ewer Furstlichen Gnaden vnterthenigster gantz williger
Tycho Brahe
Eigenhn.
text.english:
**To the most serene, high-born Prince and Lord, Lord Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg, Prince of the Wends, Count of Schwerin, Lord of the lands of Rostock and Stargard, my most gracious Prince and Lord.**

Most serene, high-born Prince, most gracious Lord. To Your Princely Grace [be] my most humble, wholly willing services at all times, with the utmost diligence, beforehand. And since I am now dispatching a courier of my own into Denmark, I could not pass by approaching Your Princely Grace in humility with this my poor letter, and thanking the same for the manifold kindness and benefits shown me.

As concerns my present state, Your Princely Grace will have learned it in detail, not long ago, from my previous letter, so it is needless to repeat it further here. For His Roman Imperial Majesty, my most gracious lord, is again — as before, the longer the more — favourably disposed toward me with all imperial graces (God be praised); and has but recently graciously had bought, **for 10,000 thalers**, for my use and that of astronomical study, the imposing and stately house of the late imperial Vice-Chancellor **Jacob Curtius** — situated at a high place, on the outermost [edge] of the royal capital city of **Prague** — where all my instruments, which for a while stood in His Imperial Majesty's pleasure-garden near the castle, are now being arranged in a convenient manner, and a **laboratory for spagyric exercises** is also being set up.

Further, I cannot most humbly conceal from Your Princely Grace (as the same will also still graciously recall) that **half a year ago I had the sum of 10,000 Reichsthalers** — which was willingly advanced by me to the young lordship of Mecklenburg — given notice on to their rent-master **Andreas Meier**, through my cousin and plenipotentiary in those parts, **Eske Bille**; for **I have bought landed estates in these parts**, for the payment of which I was thereby occasioned [to need it]. Wherein Your Princely Grace then (as is in accordance with fairness) showed yourself quite graciously and compliantly, and I have also reassured the people here on that [basis]. But now I am credibly informed by Lord Doctor **Gödelmann** — to whom I have given full commission to receive the 10,000-thaler principal together with the interest on my behalf — that the aforesaid rent-master is found refusing not only the sum, but also the repayment of the already-elapsed interest, and pleads other great expenditures.

Since, then, Your Princely Grace — as guardian of the aforesaid young lordship — graciously complied therein, and since it is in itself fair, and I have promised it to other people: there comes to Your Princely Grace my most humble, wholly diligent request, that you would not let it happen that my word be brought to naught, and that I thereby suffer damage to my hitherto well-established name and good repute; but that the oft-mentioned sum and interest may, with all speed — if (against hope) it has not yet happened — be conveyed hither. This, toward Your Princely Grace (to whose most gracious deed I humbly trust), I acknowledge myself ever bound and zealous to deserve, to the utmost of my ability, obediently.

I herewith most humbly and faithfully commend Your Princely Grace, together with your much-beloved consort, to a happy, long-lasting reign, and [commend] myself to your further princely graces.

Given at Prague, the 10th of April, the year 1601.
Your Princely Grace's most humble, wholly willing
Tycho Brahe,
[his] own hand.

- **Position in the debt-thread.** This **10 April 1601** appeal to the Duke **precedes** the more pressing one of **4 June 1601** (brahe-t_16010604001) and follows the agents'-level letters (Tycho→Meier 15 Nov 1600; Tycho→Bording; the Eske Bille letter). It conveys the same core: the **10,000-thaler principal** lent to the *junge Herrschaft* (Duke Johann's sons, of whom Ulrich is **guardian**) was called in half a year ago, via **Eske Bille**, but **rent-master Meier now refuses** both principal and elapsed interest, pleading other expenditures; Tycho asks Ulrich to compel payment lest his "word be brought to naught" and his "name and good repute" suffer.

(Note the coincidence of figures: the Curtius house cost 10,000 thalers, the same nominal sum as the Mecklenburg principal.)
- **Persons named.** Duke Ulrich III; **Jacob Curtius** (the late Vice-Chancellor); **Andreas Meier** (Mecklenburg rent-master); **Eske Bille** ("my cousin and plenipotentiary"); **Johann Georg Gödelmann** (Tycho's commissioned collector); the *junge Herrschaft* (Duke Johann's sons); **Rudolf II**; Ulrich's consort (Anna of Pomerania-Wolgast — not named in the text).

documents.abstract: Follows up on a request to have household goods moved from Lübeck to Hamburg and raises the matter of recovering money from the treasurer of the younger Mecklenburg princes.
documents.incipit: [TYCHO BRAHE AD JACOBUM BORDINGUM]. Magnifice et clarissime vir, d:ne et amice honorande.

text.original:
[TYCHO BRAHE AD JACOBUM BORDINGUM].
Magnifice et clarissime vir, d:ne et amice honorande.

SCRIPSI Mag:iæ T:æ non ita dudum nonnulla de statu mearum rerum et simul eam rogaui, ut ab ampliss:o senatu Lubecensi sua intercessione et authoritate impetrare non degrauaretur, quo ea, quæ etiamnum ex mea supellectile isthic residua sunt, eorum iussu et provisione Hamburgum per flu[u]iolum interlabentem, mature deportentur, idque in gratiam s:æ cæs:æ m:tis, d:ni nostri clementissimi, cuj hoc officium gratiose placiturum. Spero itaque M:am T:am id ipsum executioni aut iam mandasse aut breuj mandaturam, quare nihil ulterius hac de re nunc repetam, ne videar de M:æ T:æ erga me beneuolentia, diu multumque mihi satis perspecta, quidpiam hæsitare.

Verum aliud quid maioris momentj nunc addam. Repetij, vtj scit M: T:a, totam pecuniæ summam ab jllustrissimorum juniorum principum Megapolitanorum quæstore, quam illis mutuo dederam et quidem legitimo tempore, prout literæ contractus habent, repetij. Verum is nunc prætendens ærarij vacuitatem summam promissam ac interesse ad tempus calendarum aprilis præfinitarum numerare tergiuersatur, aliter quam ab jll:mo duce Vldarico, d:no meo clementiss., constitutum illique iniunctum est. Cumque hæc procrastinatio mihi sit intolerabilis, siquidem in vltimis huius regni comitiis mense februario proxime elapso celebratis quibusdam præcipuis viris decem illa millia joachimicorum addixerim, atque inde plus commodj sperem quam prius obtinui, oportet utique me promissis stare et fidem datam redimere, nec etiam mihi integrum est interesse illo diutius carere, satis graue fuit, quod alterius anni usum fructum nunc primum per dd. Gödelmannum receperim. Scripsi itaque ad jllustrissimum ducem Vldaricum hac de re submisse et diligenter, vt ipsius cel:do dignetur sua authoritate efficere, quo mihi eueniat, id quod æquitas postulat. Quocirca M:am T:am magnopere rogatam habeo, ut apud ipsius c:nem negotium hoc promouere velit. Si quid fuerit quod apud s:am cæs:am, m:tem, d:num nostrum clementiss:m, in hac aula ipsius cel:tudini gratum præstare potuero, offero omni debita reuerentia et obsequio meam opellam quam fidelissime, quam etiam eodem modo inclytæ ciuitati Lubecensi officiosissime defero, quod et vtrisque T:a M:a meo nomine annuntiare velit. Quin et si qua in re M:æ T:æ vsui vnquam esse potuero, utatur me tanquam amico integro et constante, eius desiderijs, quantum in ipso est, non defuturo.

Jamque valeat M:a Tua cum tota sua domo quam optime et diutissime.
Dabantur Pragæ ex ædibus quondam Curtianis, nunc nouo Vraniburgo Rudolphæo die 12 aprilis anno 1601 stylo nouo.
text.english:
**[TYCHO BRAHE TO JACOB BORDING].**
Magnificent and most renowned man, my lord and friend to be honoured.

I wrote to Your Magnificence not so long ago some things about the state of my affairs, and at the same time asked you not to find it burdensome to obtain, by your intercession and authority, from the most ample Senate of Lübeck, that those things which still remain there of my household goods may, by their order and provision, be conveyed in good time to Hamburg by the little river that flows between — and this for the sake of His Sacred Imperial Majesty, our most clement Lord, to whom this service will be graciously pleasing. I hope, therefore, that Your Magnificence has either already given this very thing to execution, or will shortly; wherefore I shall now repeat nothing further on the matter, lest I seem to harbour any doubt about Your Magnificence's benevolence toward me, long and amply well known to me.

But I will now add something of greater moment. I have called in, as Your Magnificence knows, the whole sum of money from the treasurer of the most illustrious younger Princes of Mecklenburg — the sum which I had given them on loan, and that at the lawful time, as the letters of contract provide; I have called it in. But he now, pleading the emptiness of the treasury, shuffles over paying out the promised sum and the interest at the appointed term of the Kalends of April [1 April], otherwise than was determined by the most illustrious Duke Ulrich, my most clement Lord, and enjoined upon him. And since this procrastination is intolerable to me — seeing that at the last Diet of this kingdom [Bohemia], held this past February, I have assigned those ten thousand joachimsthalers to certain leading men, and from that I hope for more advantage than I obtained before — I must by all means stand by my promises and redeem the faith I have pledged; nor is it open to me to be without that interest any longer. It was grievous enough that I have only now received, through Dr. Gödelmann, the usufruct [the interest] of the other year. I have therefore written to the most illustrious Duke Ulrich about this matter, humbly and earnestly, that His Highness may deign by his authority to bring it about that there come to me what fairness requires. Wherefore I earnestly entreat Your Magnificence to be willing to advance this business with His Highness. If there be anything I can perform, pleasing to His Highness, with His Sacred Imperial Majesty — our most clement Lord — in this Court, I offer my poor service most faithfully, with all due reverence and obedience; the same I likewise most dutifully tender to the renowned city of Lübeck — which Your Magnificence will be willing to announce to both in my name. Nay, if ever I can be of use to Your Magnificence in any matter, use me as a whole and constant friend, who will not fail your wishes, so far as in him lies.

And now may Your Magnificence fare as well and as long as possible, with all your house.
Given at Prague, from the house formerly Curtius's — now the new Rudolphine Uraniborg — the 12th day of April, in the year 1601, New Style.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Jacob Bording**, a leading man of **Lübeck** (jurist/magistrate of the Hanseatic city) able to act *"with the most ample Senate of Lübeck"* on Tycho's behalf — addressed throughout in the high civic register *Magnificentia Tua* ("Your Magnificence"). The witness is an autograph **letter draft** (*Brevudkast*) in the Basel Autographensammlung.
- **First business — the goods at Lübeck.** Tycho asks Bording to procure from the **Senate of Lübeck** an order to ship the remainder of his *supellex* (household goods/effects) still lying there onward to **Hamburg** *per fluviolum interlabentem* — "by the little river that runs between" (the Lübeck–Hamburg water route, the Stecknitz/Trave–Elbe connection) — framing the favour as pleasing to **His Imperial Majesty** (Rudolf II). This tracks the slow westward removal of Tycho's possessions from the Baltic toward his new imperial seat.
- **Second business — the Mecklenburg loan (the principal matter).** This letter belongs to the **10,000-thaler Mecklenburg-debt thread**: Tycho had lent **10,000 joachimsthalers** to the *younger princes of Mecklenburg* (*illustrissimi juniores principes Megapolitani*; *Megapolitanus* = Mecklenburg) and had called the principal + interest due at the lawful term — **the Kalends of April (1 April) 1601** — as fixed by **Duke Ulrich**. The dukes' *quaestor* (treasurer) now stalls, pleading an empty treasury. Tycho's urgency is concrete: at the **Bohemian Diet of February 1601** he had already *assigned* those 10,000 thalers to certain magnates (on better terms than before) and must keep his word. Cf. the parallel chain — Tycho→Andreas Meier, 27 May 1601 (brahe-t_16010527001) and 18 July (brahe-t_16010718001); Tycho→Duke Ulrich, 4 June 1601 (brahe-t_16010604001); and the ducal letters of 24 July (brahe-t_16010724001) and 9 August (brahe-t_16010809001).
- **Persons named.**
 - *Duke Vldaricus* = **Ulrich III, Duke of Mecklenburg-Güstrow** (1527–1603), Tycho's *dominus clementissimus* in the matter, who had ordered payment.
 - *dd. Gödelmannus* = **Johann Georg Gödelmann** (1559–1611), jurist and Mecklenburg councillor/diplomat (later in imperial service), through whom Tycho had at last received the previous year's interest. (*dd.* = *dominum doctorem*.)
 - *quaestor* of the younger princes — the ducal **treasurer**, unnamed here (the rent-master **Andreas Meier** of Wismar in the companion letters).
- **Place / self-styling.** *Pragae ex aedibus quondam Curtianis, nunc novo Uraniburgo Rudolphaeo* — Prague, from the **Curtius house** (the *aedes Curtianae*, Tycho's Prague residence) which he renames *"the new Rudolphine Uraniborg,"* transplanting the name of his lost Hven seat onto his imperial quarters.
- **Calendar.** Dateline explicitly *stylo novo* — **New Style (Gregorian)**, correct for Tycho's imperial-service dating. Reproduced, not converted.
- **Abbreviations.** The draft is heavily contracted in chancery style — *M:ae T:ae* (*Magnificentiae Tuae*), *s:ae caes:ae m:tis* (*sacrae caesareae maiestatis*), *jll:mo* (*illustrissimo*), *cel:do / cel:tudini* (*celsitudo / celsitudini*), *dd.* (*dominum doctorem*), *a:o* etc. — all silently expanded in translation; the source block keeps them as written.

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD MARTINUM BRASCHIUM.

NULLA tui oblivione nec mea negligentia accidit, eruditissime Domine BRASCHI, quod Mag. Dominus GÖDELLMANNUS, Legatum hîc agens Saxonicum, sine meo ad te responso Rostochium venerit. Iam enim illud inchoatum erat, sed is mea opinione citius abijt, ut vix eas, quæ magni momenti erant, et pecunias meas istic hærentes concernebant, complere licuerit, ideoque oretenus illi quædam dixi tibi insinuanda, quæ etiam literis ad Dominum D. BACKMEISTERUM, quas tum præ manibus habui, quatenus tempus tulit, subiunxi. Mitto autem nunc ea, quæ per quendam meorum de Astronomiæ historia e quodam libro descripta sunt. Plura invenies sub initium Astronomici Cæsarei APPIANI, tum quoque nomina quorundam Astronomorum, in priori parte tabularum primi mobilis REINHOLDI, quemadmodum etiam in Sphæra PEUCERI, quod tuæ industriæ relinquo, mihi enim non suppetit otium talia inquirendi. Carmen quomodo disponendum et concinnandum, tuæ discretioni et venæ Poëticæ liberum relinquo. Principium paulo aliter ordinandum censerem, nec volo, ut mei in primis carminibus fiat ulla mentio, sed omnia conveniente methodo per mundi ætates successive deducantur ad hunc Cæsarem RUDOLPHUM Secundum, postea, si tibi sic placuerit, poteris migrationem meam e Dania, quod ad hoc studium ab Augustissimo Imperatore huc clementissime vocatus sim, paucis attingere, sicque in Cæsaris laudem, hoc etiam nomine, discurrere, ita tamen ut optimum illum Regem FRIDERICUM Secundum, laudatissimæ memoriæ, qui hæc studia in suo regno, quoad vixit, liberaliter fovit, sub quo etiam Uraniburgum exædificatum est, non prætereas. Si quid aliud inciderit, de quo te monendum duxerim, in quadam charta adiungam, neque enim nunc tantum suppetit temporis, ut carmen tuum relegere atque omnes circumstantias dispicere valeam. Ubi integre tuas conceptiones ad colophonem deduxeris, mitte mihi exemplar, antequam imprimantur, et si liberum reliqueris, meam interponere sententiam, ingenue id faciam, daboque postea operam, quantum in me est, ut Cæsarea Mtas liberalem vicissim erga te clementer praebeat. Plura adderem, modo aliæ interpellationes aliaque negotia id paterentur. Tu itaque, mi optime BRASCHI, rectius quam nuper vale, et pleniores per meliorem oportunitatem a me expecta. Dabantur Pragæ ex ædibus olim Cæsaris, nunc novo Uraniburgo Cæsareo 14 Aprilis Anno 1601.

HISTORIA ILLUSTRIUM ASTRONOMORUM INDE A MUNDI EXORDIO AD NOSTRUM ÆVUM HEROICO CARMINE CONCINNATA.

NON placet in primo carmine radioque potentes, nam licet apud VIRGILIUM sit Descripsit radio, tamen hoc verbum radius non habet hîc emphasin in ipso carminis frontispicio, sed potius alicubi in medio. Videtur etiam principium nimis humile, quare sic mallem:

Artifices summos Divina scientia cœli
Quos celebres genuit, quæque incrementa Mathesis
Docta habuit, pedetentim Mundi ab origine prima
Ætatem in nostram, certis deducere fastis
Mens amet et clausos Heliconis inire recessus,
Arduum opus, atque alijs res intentata Poëtis,
Res preciosa licet et Musis digna canoris etc.

vel in eandem ferme sententiam per teipsum melius. Hæc saltem admonitionis causa assignare lubuit, prout nunc in buccam venerunt.

Postea inferre, cur hoc potius Argumentum arripueris, quam alias res ludicras huius inferioris scenæ mundanæ, quales sunt bella, victoriæ, triumphi, amores, Bucolica, et similia a prioribus Poëtis sæpe decantata, sed potius sublimia illa et præstantiora, quæ varijs fluctuationibus et vanitati non ita sunt obnoxia, quæque in tanto cœtera illa dignitate antecellunt, quantum arduus æther declivis terræ superat loca.

Huc addatur invocatio ad verum DEUM, totius cœli et universitatis creatorem, non Deastros licet fictitios, quos gentiles Poëtæ implorant, et tandem narratio exordium habeat ab ijs, quæ a MOISE primo capite Geneseos de cœli et siderum creatione referuntur. Deinde ex IOSEPHO antiquitatum Iudaicarum scriptore, quod ADAM docuerit suos filios et nepotes Astrorum scientiam, et duabus columnis excitatis in Siria ab ijsdem, et de NOAH, quem BEROSUS ait aliqua etiam ex parte Diluvium prævidisse ex Astrorum dispositione, et de ABRAHAMO, quod insignis Astronomus et Geometra fuerit, atque artes Ægyptios docuerit, quodque ex ijs, quæ circa Solem, Lunam et Sidera, terrasque et maria apparent, cognoverit unum saltem esse DEUM boni autorem in Natura, quod prædictus habet IOSEPHUS, et quod ABRAM appellatus sit, dum ex sola Astrorum scientia claruit et DEUM hinc aliquatenus agnovit, postquam vero divinitus est plenius edoctus et illuminatus, ABRAHAM, sic volente DEO, est dictus, ut PHILO Iudæus infert, quod etiam a MOISIS relatione non videtur alienum.

Deinceps poteris ordine recensere, quæ e profanis etiam scriptoribus colligi poterunt, quorum etiam aliquam indicationem suppeditabit liber Domini HENRICI RANZOVIJ de Regibus et Principibus, qui Astronomiam foverunt. Omnia autem ordine se sequantur, prout tempora ætatum mundi requirunt, sed decenti methodo, ut principaliora præcedant ea, quæ minus ad rem faciunt; et narretur etiam, quomodo Astronomia peregrinata sit ex Siria et Mesopotamia in Ægyptum, hinc ad Chaldæos, Arabes, Æthiopes, Indos, ex Ægypto etiam venisse in Græciam, hinc in Italiam et Hispaniam ac Mauritaniam, postea in Galliam et Germaniam, atque ibi præcipua lumina, quæ in hac arte apud Germanos viguerunt, commemorare, usque ad COPERNICUM et REINHOLDUM, et quod tandem in Daniam transfretârit, ubi regnante optimo Rege FRIDERICO Secundo quietem et portum aliquandiu invenit, exædificata arce Uraniburgo in Insula celebris illius Porthmo Danici Huenna, et fabricatis magnis et idoneis Instrumentis, qualia non alibi reperiuntur, ubi etiam per 21 annos strenue exercebatur, quamdiu idem Rex vixit, tum quoque in octennali interregno post ipsum. Verum cum sequentibus annis firmam sedem ibi habere nequierit, in Germaniam redijt, et in Holsatia feudoque Producis HENRICI RANZOVIJ aliquandiu quievit, et ibi laudare RANZOVIUM, tam ob hanc quam alias virtutes, et quod aliæ circumiacentes regiones, ut Gallia, Anglia et Batavia, interea eam ambiverint, sed vocata ab Augustissimo Imperatore RUDOLPHO II Austriaco, in Bohemiam ad ipsum concedere prætulerit, ubi ab eodem munifice non sine aliorum invidia sustentata est, et primum de arce Bennatika, ubi per annuum spacium mansit, postea de Praga, ubi est residentia Cæsaris et Regis Bohemici, hisque ædibus Curtianis in eos usus liberaliter a Cæsare coemptis. Hoc etiam loco quædam de earundem structore, Domino IACOBO CURTIO, priore Procancellario, inserenda, siquidem is Mathesi et Astronomicis studijs impense addictus fuerit, atque ea de causa hasce ædes in maxime ædito civitatis loco magnis impensis exstruxerit, quodque, dum adhuc in vivis esset, mihi etiamnum in Dania commoranti inhabitandas obtulerit, si huc Pragam venire vellem, quod, vivente tunc Rege FRIDERICO, non concedebatur, et nunc post fata eiusdem Domini CURTIJ non sine numine et Divino provisu ex liberalitate Cæsaris RUDOLPHI easdem ædes mihi cessisse, pro Astronomia hîc excolenda. Postmodum elogia domus Austriacæ subiungere, atque ad hunc RUDOLPHUM omnia deducere, atque in eius excurrere laudes easque ampliare, atque victorias et præclare gesta commemorare, inter quæ hoc quoque non postremum, quod Astronomiam foveat, qua in re non cedat ALPHONSO Regi, cuius fama per Tabulas et liberalitatem in eas construendas cœlo coæva durabit, cumque id numeri ipsi cœlo non per omnia correspondentes tribuere potuerint, quid tibi, Cæsar Austriace, ubi Tabulæ Rudolpheæ sub auspicijs tuis cœlestes motus exactissime æmulantes lucem viderint? etc.
text.english:
**TYCHO BRAHE TO MARTIN BRASCH.**

It is by no forgetfulness of you, nor negligence of mine, most learned Lord Brasch, that the magnificent **Lord Gödelmann**, acting here as Saxon Legate, came [back] to Rostock without my answer to you. For it was already begun; but he left sooner than I thought, so that I could scarcely complete those [letters] which were of great moment and concerned my monies stuck there; and so I told him by word of mouth certain things to convey to you, which I also subjoined — so far as time allowed — to the letter to **Lord Doctor Backmeister** that I then had in hand. But I now send **what one of my men copied out, from a certain book, about the history of Astronomy**. You will find more at the beginning of **Apian's *Astronomicum Caesareum***, and also the names of certain Astronomers in the former part of **Reinhold's tables of the primum mobile**, as likewise in **Peucer's *Sphaera*** — which I leave to your industry, for I have no leisure to inquire into such things. How the poem is to be arranged and composed, I leave free to your discretion and poetic vein.

The beginning I should think is to be ordered a little otherwise; and **I do not wish that any mention of me be made in the first verses, but that everything be deduced, by a fitting method, through the ages of the world successively, down to this Emperor Rudolf II**; afterward, if it so please you, you may **touch briefly on my migration from Denmark — that I was most clemently called hither for this study by the most august Emperor — and so discourse, on this account too, to the Emperor's praise; yet so that you do not pass over that excellent King Frederick II, of most praised memory, who liberally fostered these studies in his realm while he lived, under whom too Uraniborg was built**. If anything else occur of which I judge you should be advised, I will add it on a sheet; for I have not now so much time as to re-read your poem and consider all the circumstances. When you have brought your conceptions entire to the colophon, send me a copy before they are printed; and if you leave me free to interpose my opinion, I will do it frankly; and I will afterward take pains, so far as in me lies, that the Imperial Majesty in turn show himself clemently liberal toward you. I would add more, if other interruptions and other business allowed it. So fare better than of late, my excellent Brasch, and await fuller [letters] from me by a better opportunity. Given at Prague, from **the house once the Emperor's, now the new Imperial Uraniborg**, 14 April, the year 1601.

**HISTORY OF ILLUSTRIOUS ASTRONOMERS, FROM THE BEGINNING OF THE WORLD TO OUR AGE, COMPOSED IN HEROIC VERSE.**

I do not like, in the first verse, "*radioque potentes*"; for although in **Virgil** there is "*Descripsit radio*," yet this word *radius* has no emphasis here, at the very frontispiece of the poem, but rather somewhere in the middle. The beginning, too, seems too humble; wherefore I should prefer thus:

> *Let my mind love to bring forth, step by step — from the world's first origin into our age, by sure annals — the supreme craftsmen whom the divine science of heaven begot famous, and what increments learned Mathematics has had; and to enter the closed recesses of Helicon — an arduous work, a thing untried by other Poets, yet a precious thing, and worthy of the tuneful Muses,* etc.

— or to nearly the same sense, better, by yourself. These I was pleased to set down only by way of admonition, as they now came to the mouth.

Afterward, bring in **why you have seized this Argument rather than the other frivolous things of this lower worldly scene** — such as wars, victories, triumphs, loves, Bucolics, and the like, often sung by earlier Poets — but rather those sublime and more excellent things, not so subject to various fluctuations and to vanity, and which excel the rest in dignity as much as the high aether surpasses the low places of the sloping earth.

To this let there be added an **invocation to the true GOD, creator of all heaven and the universe** — not the fictitious godlings whom the gentile Poets implore — and at last let the narration take its beginning from what is reported by **Moses, in the first chapter of Genesis**, on the creation of heaven and the stars. Then from **Josephus**, writer of the Jewish Antiquities: that **Adam taught his sons and grandsons the science of the Stars**, and of the two columns raised in Syria by them; and of **Noah**, whom **Berosus** says foresaw the Flood partly from the disposition of the Stars; and of **Abraham**, that he was a notable Astronomer and Geometer, and taught the arts to the Egyptians, and from what appears about the Sun, Moon, Stars, lands, and seas knew that there is but one GOD, author of good in Nature (which the aforesaid Josephus has) — and that he was called **Abram** while he was famed from the science of the stars alone and thence somewhat knew God, but, after he was more fully taught and illuminated divinely, was called **Abraham** (God so willing), as **Philo the Jew** infers — which too does not seem alien from Moses's account.

Thereafter you may recount, in order, what can be gathered from the **profane writers** too — of which some indication will be supplied by the book of **Lord Henry Rantzau, *On the Kings and Princes who fostered Astronomy***. But let all follow in order, as the times of the world's ages require, yet by a decent method, so that the more principal things precede those that make less to the matter. And let it be narrated **how Astronomy travelled from Syria and Mesopotamia into Egypt, thence to the Chaldeans, Arabs, Ethiopians, Indians; from Egypt came also into Greece, thence into Italy and Spain and Mauritania, afterward into Gaul and Germany** — and there commemorate the chief lights who flourished in this art among the Germans, **up to Copernicus and Reinhold**; and that at last **it crossed over into Denmark, where, under the reign of the excellent King Frederick II, it found rest and a port for a while** — the castle **Uraniborg** built on the Island, in that famous Danish Sound, **Hven**, and great and suitable Instruments fabricated, such as are found nowhere else, where also [Tycho] was strenuously occupied **for 21 years, as long as that King lived, and also in the eight-year interregnum after him**. But since in the following years he could not have a firm seat there, **he returned into Germany, and rested a while in Holstein and the fief of the Pro-duke Henry Rantzau** — and there praise **Rantzau**, both for this and for his other virtues; and that other surrounding regions — **Gaul, England, and Holland** — meanwhile courted her [Astronomy], but, **called by the most august Emperor Rudolf II of Austria, she preferred to go to him into Bohemia**, where by him she was munificently sustained (not without others' envy): first at the castle **Benátky** (where she stayed for a year's space), then at **Prague**, the residence of the Emperor and King of Bohemia, in **the Curtius house, liberally bought for these uses by the Emperor**.

In this place, too, **something is to be inserted about the builder of that house, Lord Jacob Curtius [Kurz], the former Vice-Chancellor** — since he was deeply devoted to Mathematics and Astronomical studies, and for that cause built this house, at great cost, in the very highest place of the city; and that, **while he was yet alive, he offered it to me — still dwelling then in Denmark — to inhabit, if I would come hither to Prague**; which, King Frederick then living, was not permitted; and now, after the death of that same Lord Curtius, **not without [divine] will and providence, the same house was ceded to me by the liberality of the Emperor Rudolf, for cultivating Astronomy here**. Afterward subjoin the **elogia of the House of Austria**, and deduce all things to this **Rudolf**, and run out into his praises and amplify them, and commemorate his victories and glorious deeds — among which this too [is] not the least, **that he fosters Astronomy, in which matter he yields not to King Alfonso**, whose fame, through the Tables and his liberality in constructing them, will endure coeval with heaven; and since [those Alfonsine] numbers could not correspond to heaven in all things — **what [praise] for you, Austrian Caesar, when the *Rudolphine Tables*, under your auspices, most exactly emulating the celestial motions, shall have seen the light?** etc.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Martin Brasch / Martinus Braschius (1550–1601)**, the Rostock poet (cf. brahe-t_16000915001; the "Nicolaus" name-error in brahe-t_16000808001). Written from the **Curtius house, "the new Imperial Uraniborg"** (one day before brahe-t_16010415001 to Bacmeister, dated from the same place).
- **Significance — Tycho's outline for a verse *History of Astronomy*, and the naming of the *Rudolphine Tables*.** A remarkable document: Tycho **commissions and minutely plans an epic poem**, the ***History of Illustrious Astronomers from the Beginning of the World to Our Age***, to culminate in Rudolf II — and supplies:
 - **Sources for Brasch:** a copied extract on the history of astronomy, plus **Apian's *Astronomicum Caesareum*, Reinhold's tables of the *primum mobile*, Peucer's *Sphaera***, and **Heinrich Rantzau's *De regibus et principibus qui astronomiam foverunt***.
 - **Tycho's own hexameter verse** — seven lines he prefers to Brasch's "too humble" opening (rejecting "*radioque potentes*" with a point about Virgil's "*Descripsit radio*"). A **rare specimen of Tycho composing Latin poetry**.
 - **The structural plan:** a *recusatio* (why astronomy, not wars/loves/Bucolics); an **invocation to the true God** (not "fictitious godlings"); a **Biblical/patristic prologue** (Moses/Genesis; Josephus on Adam's star-science and the two Syrian columns; Noah/Berosus and the Flood; **Abraham the astronomer-geometer**, the Abram→Abraham etymology per Philo); then the **migration of astronomy** Syria→Egypt→Chaldeans/Arabs/Ethiopians/Indians→Greece→Italy/Spain/Mauritania→Gaul/Germany→**Copernicus & Reinhold**→**Denmark**.
 - **Tycho's autobiographical self-presentation** (in the third person, for the poem): **21 years at Uraniborg/Hven under Frederick II + the 8-year interregnum**; the return to **Holstein under Heinrich Rantzau**; the courting by **Gaul, England, Holland**; the **imperial call**; **Benátky (one year) → Prague / the Curtius house**.
 - **The Curtius-house backstory (new detail).** **Jacob Curtius (Kurz von Senftenau)**, the mathematically-devoted former Vice-Chancellor, **built the house and had offered it to Tycho years earlier** (declined while Frederick II lived); after Curtius's death it passed to Tycho by Rudolf's gift — "the new Imperial Uraniborg."
 - **The climax — the *Rudolphine Tables*.** Casting Rudolf as surpassing **Alfonso X** (whose Alfonsine Tables "could not correspond to heaven in all things"), Tycho gives Brasch the poem's intended peroration: **"what [praise] for you, Austrian Caesar, when the *Tabulae Rudolpheae*, under your auspices, most exactly emulating the celestial motions, shall have seen the light?"** — *the earliest naming of the Rudolphine Tables in this corpus*, by Tycho himself, months before his death (the work Kepler would complete and publish in 1627).
- **Cross-references.** A keystone for the **Rudolphine Tables** project, the **Curtius-house / "new Uraniborg"** identity (brahe-t_16010415001, brahe-t_16000103001), the **exile/autobiography** thread, and the **Alfonsine comparison** (brahe-t_16000915001).
- **Persons & works named.** Martin Brasch; **Gödelmann**; **Lucas Backmeister**; **Apian** (*Astronomicum Caesareum*), **Erasmus Reinhold**, **Caspar Peucer** (*Sphaera*); **Virgil**; **Moses, Josephus, Adam, Noah, Berosus, Abraham, Philo Judaeus**; **Heinrich Rantzau** (*De regibus … qui astronomiam foverunt*); **Copernicus**; **Jacob Curtius (Kurz)**; **Alfonso X**; **Rudolf II**, **Frederick II of Denmark**; **the *Rudolphine Tables***. Places: **Prague** (Curtius house), **Benátky**, **Hven/Uraniborg**, **Holstein**, Denmark, the whole *translatio* of astronomy (Syria→…→Germany→Denmark).
- **Calendar.** *14 Aprilis Anno 1601* at Prague (imperial reckoning) → **14 April 1601 [N.S.]**; header and label agree.
