text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD LUCAM BACMEISTERUM.

CLARISSIME et praestantissime Vir, Domine et Amice honorande, quod per Clarissimum Virum Dn. D. IOH. GEORG. GÖDELMANNUM, communem nostrum amicum, sexcentos illos thaleros a quaestore Iuniorum Principum loco interesse mihi debitos transmiseris, ijs qui Belgici erant in imperiales maiore ex parte commutatis, recte a te factum est, eoque nomine plurimas tibi habeo gratias. Quod autem idem quaestor reliquos 600, qui mihi nunc debentur, tunc numerare noluerit, non equidem miror, utut non iniquum fuisset, si id officioli mihi praestitisset, sed quod totam summam satis mature resignatam et consensu et iussu Illustriss. Ducis UDALRICI mihi ad hoc Pascha restituendam solvere tergiversetur, nescio quas alias praetendens expensas et calvas excusationes, id mihi magis displicet, nec ferendum duco. Scripsi itaque ad dictum Illustriss. Ducem UDALRICUM, sponsorem primarium, ut ad constitutum tempus integram summam decem millium Ioachimicorum mihi restitui sua authoritate curet, quod et non invite effecturum optimum illum et integerrimum Principem, mihi clementissime faventem, nullatenus diffido. Obtigit mihi occasio, qua in hisce oris plus commodi ex illa pecunia nancisci queam quam isthic, alias non tam cito eam repetijssem.

Quin et praeterea ad praefatum Illustriss. Ducem dedi literas, qua ipsius Celsitudinem ad nuptias filiae cuidam ex meis ELISABETHAe nomine submisse invitavi, cum quodam Nobili et erudito Iuvene FRANCISCO TENGNAGLIO e Westphalia oriundo atque in hac aula versante, ad instans Pentecostes, favente Coelesti Numine, celebrandas. Cum enim non saltem Caesaream Maiestatem, Dn. nostrum clementiss. et praecipuos eius Consiliarios et aliquot Germaniae Principes, tam Ecclesiastici quam politici status, quos scio mihi clementer favere, humilime per literas invitare animus sit (quod et nonnullorum Legati, qui hîc sunt, sponte a me petierunt, atque suis Dominis gratum futurum innuerunt) Illustrissimum Ducem Megapolitanum, Dn. meum clementiss. et quam optime de me meritum, praeterire nefas duxi, non quod ipsius Celsitudinem aut alios in Germania Principes, ad quos hac de re reverenter scribo, aliquem suo nomine ideo huc missuros petere audeam, sed saltem quo conscij sint, ut si forte aliquem ex suis Legatis tum temporis hîc in aula habuerint, illis festivitatem hanc loco sui Principis coram condecorare liceat, quod et te, charissime Domine D. BACHMAISTERE, ob veterem inter nos necessitudinem non caelandum duxi, quo vota tua ad Deum omnis boni et felicitatis largitorem nostris coniungens, fausta et salutaria huic actui preceris.

Miror te literas D. D. CRAGIO inscriptas non accepisse. Nullas nunc ad ipsum ulterius mitto, siquidem intellexerim ipsum in Legatione Polonica abesse, sed tabellario huic nonnullas tradidi, quibusdam in Dania praecipuis amicis destinatas, quarum maxima pars est invitatoria ad iam dictas nuptias; eas vero omnes ipse tabellarius facile per quendam nobilem, ESCHILLUM BILLÆUM nomine, res meas istic procurantem, expediet. Addo minutulas quasdam ad eundem Regis Musicum, cui alterae prius tibi missae (ut opinor) inscribebantur, quas hic ipse grammatophorus, si tibi commodior non suppetit ratio, illi Hafniae inquisito tradet; sunt a quodam hîc Italo, in cuius aliquantul[a fideiussione?] Musicus est, scriptae.

Magistro BRASCHIO ipsemet nunc de negocio prius insinuato rescribo; antea enim non vacabat.

Quae a CAROLO Sueciae Duce in Livonia acta sunt, iam antea hîc cognovimus; nimis tardus esse videtur in resistendo Poloniae Rex, et vix ut ENNIUS de altero isto Romano aiebat, cunctando restituet rem: celeritate potius in talibus opus est. WAIWODA, qui in Comitijs Polonicis etiam hostis eius Regni declaratus est, nuper hîc fuit, et gratiam Caesaris impetravit, acceptaque magna pecuniae vi Transsylvaniae partem Polonorum consilijs et Tartarorum invasionibus nuper amissam pro Caesare recuperare meditatur, omniaque strenue ad hanc expeditionem praeparat. Magnis etiam viribus contra Turcam exercitum parat Imperator noster, validiorem quam unquam antea, siquidem necessitas sic postulet, ob amissum superiori Octobri Canisium, fortissimum Hungariae propugnaculum, quo occupato Turca sibi viam, sive Styriam sive Austriam infestare velit, praestravit; armipotens et fortis Deus eius ferociam et tyrannidem retundat atque a cervicibus Christianorum avertat. Ubi plura aliquid momenti habentia resciero, te eorum faciam participem. Vale cum omnibus tuis quam felicissime, et senij, si quae, uti fit, incidunt gravamina, patientia vince. Dabantur Pragae ex aedibus olim Curtianis, quas Caesar pro 10000 millibus Ioachimicorum in meos usus liberaliter emit vix duplo maioris exaedificatas, quae novum Uraniburgum Rudolphaeum appellanda.

Iamque iterum et saepius vale.
Die 15 Aprilis stylo novo Anno 1601.
text.english:
**TYCHO BRAHE TO LUCAS BACMEISTER.**

Most renowned and excellent Man, honoured Lord and Friend: that through the most renowned Lord Doctor **Johann Georg Gödelmann**, our common friend, you transmitted to me those **six hundred thalers owed me by the treasurer of the Younger Princes by way of interest** — the Belgian ones being for the greater part exchanged into imperial — was rightly done by you, and on that account I give you many thanks. That the same treasurer was then unwilling to pay out the other 600 now owed me, I do not indeed wonder at (though it would not have been unfair, had he done me that small service); but that he **shirks paying the whole sum, duly assigned long enough beforehand and, by the consent and command of the most illustrious Duke Ulrich, to be repaid me by this Easter** — pretending I know not what other expenses and bald excuses — this displeases me more, and I judge it not to be borne. I have therefore **written to the said most illustrious Duke Ulrich, my principal guarantor, that he see to it by his authority that the whole sum of ten thousand joachimsthalers be repaid me at the appointed time** — which I in no way doubt that excellent and most upright Prince, who most clemently favours me, will not unwillingly bring about. An occasion has befallen me whereby I may obtain more advantage from that money in these parts than there; otherwise I should not have called it in so soon.

Moreover, I have besides sent a letter to the aforesaid most illustrious Duke, by which I have humbly **invited His Highness to the wedding of one of my daughters, Elisabeth by name, to a certain noble and learned young man, Franz Tengnagel, sprung from Westphalia and resident at this court, to be celebrated at the coming Whitsun [Pentecost]**, Heaven favouring. For since it is my intent humbly to invite by letter not only **the Imperial Majesty**, our most clement Lord, and his chief Councillors, and several **Princes of Germany** — both of ecclesiastical and of political estate — whom I know to favour me kindly (which several of the envoys here have even of their own accord asked of me, and intimated would be welcome to their masters), I judged it a sin to pass over the **most illustrious Duke of Mecklenburg**, my most clement Lord, who has deserved so very well of me — not that I should dare to ask His Highness, or the other Princes of Germany to whom I write reverently on this matter, to send anyone hither in their name on that account, but only that they may be aware, so that, if perchance they happen to have one of their envoys here at court at that time, it may be allowed him to grace this festivity in person in his Prince's stead. And this, dearest Lord Doctor Bacmeister, on account of the old bond between us, I judged not to be hidden from you, that — joining your prayers with ours to God, the bestower of all good and happiness — you may pray for things auspicious and wholesome for this act.

I wonder that you have not received the letters addressed to **Dr. Craig**. I now send no further ones to him, since I understand he is away on a **Polish legation**; but I have given this courier several [letters] destined for certain chief friends in Denmark, the greatest part of which are **invitations to the said wedding**. The courier himself will easily despatch them all through a certain nobleman, **Eske Bille** by name, who manages my affairs there. I add some small notes to the **King's Musician**, to whom the others sent you earlier were (I think) addressed; these this same letter-carrier, if a more convenient means is not at hand for you, will deliver to him, sought out at Copenhagen — they were written by a certain Italian here, in whose [surety?] the Musician stands.

To **Master Brasch** I myself now write back about the business previously hinted at; for earlier I had no leisure.

What **Charles, Duke of Sweden**, has done in **Livonia** we had already learned here before; the King of Poland seems too slow in resisting, and scarcely, as **Ennius** said of that other Roman, will he "by delaying restore the state": rather, in such matters there is need of speed. The **Voivode**, who in the Polish Diet was even declared an enemy of that Kingdom, was here lately and obtained the Emperor's favour, and — having received a great force of money — purposes **to recover for the Emperor that part of Transylvania lately lost by Polish counsels and Tartar invasions**, and is vigorously preparing everything for this expedition. With great forces too our Emperor is preparing an army against the Turk, stronger than ever before, should necessity so demand — on account of the loss, **last October, of Kanizsa, the strongest bulwark of Hungary**, by the taking of which the Turk has paved himself a road, whether he wish to infest Styria or Austria. May God, mighty and strong in arms, blunt his ferocity and tyranny, and turn it from the necks of Christians. When I learn of more things of some moment, I will make you partaker of them. Farewell most happily with all yours, and conquer by patience the burdens of old age, if any (as happens) befall. **Given at Prague, from the house once Curtius's, which the Emperor liberally bought for my use for 10,000 joachimsthalers — a house built at a cost scarcely twice as great — to be called the new Rudolphine Uraniborg.**

And now again and oftener, farewell.
The 15th of April, New Style, the year 1601.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Lucas Bacmeister** (Bacmeister the Younger, 1570–1638), Rostock theologian-physician, Tycho's friend and **financial intermediary for the Mecklenburg loan** (cf. the Brasch/Cramer correspondence routed through him, brahe-t_16000401001). Spelled *Bachmaister* mid-letter.
- **Significance — the Mecklenburg debt and the Tengnagel wedding (two of the great threads of Tycho's last year).**
 1. **The 10,000-thaler Mecklenburg loan.** Tycho had lent **Duke Ulrich III of Mecklenburg-Güstrow** ("Duke Ulrich," *sponsor primarius* = principal guarantor) **10,000 joachimsthalers**; the **treasurer of the "Younger Princes"** owes interest (two instalments of **600 thalers**, the first received via **Gödelmann**, Belgian thalers converted to imperial) and now **shirks repaying the principal due at Easter 1601**. Tycho, having "an occasion to use the money more advantageously in these parts," appeals over the treasurer's head to **Duke Ulrich** to enforce the full repayment.
 2. **The wedding of Elisabeth Brahe to Franz Tengnagel.** Tycho's daughter **Elisabeth** is to wed **Frans Gansneb genaamd Tengnagel** (the Westphalian nobleman and Tycho's assistant) **at Pentecost 1601**. Tycho is inviting **Rudolf II**, the imperial councillors, and **German princes**, and asks Duke Ulrich (and, through Bacmeister, Danish friends) that any **envoys present at court** may grace the festivity in their princes' stead. (The wedding duly took place 17 June 1601.)
- **Other contents.**
 - **John Craig** ("Dr. Craig") is **away on a Polish legation**, so Tycho sends him nothing further; Danish letters (mostly wedding invitations) go via the courier and **Eske Bille** (*Eschillus Billaeus*), Tycho's Danish agent.
 - Notes to the **King's Musician** (of Denmark), penned by "a certain Italian here, in whose [**surety?**] the Musician stands" — *in cuius aliquantul[a fideiussione?]*, an **editorial reconstruction** of a damaged phrase (flagged).
 - **Master Brasch** (the poet, cf. brahe-t_16000401001's circle) — Tycho writes back at last.
- **The news bulletin (spring 1601).**
 - **Charles, Duke of Sweden** (the future Charles IX) campaigning in **Livonia** — the opening of the **Polish–Swedish War**; Tycho thinks **Sigismund III of Poland** too slow, quoting **Ennius on Fabius Maximus Cunctator** (*cunctando restituit rem*, "by delaying he restored the state") *against* delay — here speed is needed.
 - **The "Voivode"** — declared an enemy by the **Polish Diet**, lately at Prague, won Rudolf's favour and money, and purposes to **recover Transylvania for the Emperor**: most plausibly **Michael the Brave (Mihai Viteazul), Voivode of Wallachia** (in Prague early 1601, reconciled with Rudolf, sent with Basta to retake Transylvania — they won at Guruslău that August; Michael was assassinated days later). Identification by circumstance; the name is not given (flagged).
 - **The fall of Kanizsa (*Canisium*, Nagykanizsa) in October 1600** — "the strongest bulwark of Hungary," opening the Turk's road to Styria/Austria; Rudolf preparing his largest army yet for the **Long Turkish War**.
- **The dateline — "the new Rudolphine Uraniborg."** Tycho writes from the **former Curtius house** (the Kurz/Curtius palace in Prague), **which Rudolf II had bought for his use for 10,000 joachimsthalers** — *vix duplo maioris exaedificatas*, "[a house] built at a cost scarcely twice as great" — **"to be called the new Rudolphine Uraniborg" (*novum Uraniburgum Rudolphaeum*).** A poignant naming: the Prague mansion as heir to the lost island observatory. (The source's *10000 **millibus** Ioachimicorum*, lit. "10,000 thousands," is a scribal slip for **10,000 thalers** — the same round figure as the Mecklenburg loan above; rendered as 10,000.)
- **Persons & places named.** Lucas Bacmeister; **Johann Georg Gödelmann**; **Duke Ulrich III of Mecklenburg-Güstrow**; **Elisabeth Brahe** & **Franz Tengnagel**; **Rudolf II**; **John Craig**; **Eske Bille**; the King's Musician; **Master Brasch**; **Charles, Duke of Sweden**; **Sigismund III of Poland**; **Ennius / Fabius Cunctator**; the **Voivode** (Michael the Brave?). Places: **Prague** (the Curtius house), **Livonia**, **Transylvania**, **Kanizsa**, **Styria**, **Austria**, Denmark/Copenhagen.
- **Calendar.** *Die 15 Aprilis **stylo novo** Anno 1601* → **15 April 1601 [N.S.]**; header and label agree.
- **Correction.** Latin 'versasante' corrected to 'versante' (Dreyer TBOO VIII p.413), a non-word glue-error; no change to the English, which already read correctly.

text.original:
TYCHO BRAHE AD CHRISTOPHORUM STURCIUM.

QUOD mihi per Magnificum Dn. D. GÖDELMANNUM scripseris, Nobilis et eruditissime Domine D. STURTZI, utut ego ob eius festinationem et meas tum temporis occupationes nihil ad te literarum dederim, est cur tibi plurimas habeam gratias. Agnosco hinc tuum erga me candidum et constantem amorem, cui par pari referre non desistam. De statu Patriae tuae mirabili etiam multis annis miserabili hîc satis superque inaudivimus; Deus tandem pacem largiatur. Walachus inter alios, uti scribis, declaratus hostis Regni Polonici, Caesaris nostri clementissimi Vasallus nuper factus est, et belli dux contra SIGISMUNDUM BATORUM (qui Cancellarij Polonici instinctu per Tartaros Transylvaniam invasit, et aliquam eius partem Caesari ademit) ut inde rursus eum expellat, postea pro Canisio recuperando laboraturus. Accepit hac de causa a Caesare magnam vim pecuniarum. Bellum Hungaricum tanto conamine nunc reparatur quanto vix unquam antea, sic enim opus est.

Caeterum quod narratiunculam meae e Dania huc in Bohemiam ad S. Caes. Matem migrationis, qualem optimae memoriae Dn. D. DAVIDI CHYTRÆO sic expetenti misi, tuis historicis meditationibus inserere eamque expolire et ornare constitueris, rem mihi apprime gratam et quovis officio vicissim compensandam praestiteris. Existimassem complementum historiolae anni millesimi sexcentesimi ultra priorem mediam partem, quam Dn. CHYTRÆUS ante obitum absolvit, a te continuatum, ut hoc anno prostaret, atque in illa, quae de me, dum in vivis esset, inserere cupiebat, adiuncta forent, sed forte alia sunt vestra consilia, quibus lubens acquiesco. Cuperem nihilominus id, quod proposuisti, mature fieri, et si oportunitas sic feret, conceptionem primam, antequam excutiatur, mecum communicari.

Habito nunc Pragae in aedibus olim a laudatae memoriae Vicecancellario Dn. IACOBO CURTIO splendide et magnifice exstructis, unâ cum horto amplo et amoenissimo circumiacente, quas Sacra Caes. Matas in meos usus emit a vidua inhabitante pro 10000 Ioachimicorum, cum tamen duplo maiori summa vix exstructae sint. Est locus maxime in civitate editus, versus Zephyrum, nec longe ab arce situs, ut Caesarea Matas ultra alias domos et hortos interpositos secreto et minimo negotio huc, quando ipsi sic clementissime placuerit, venire queat. Disponuntur hîc modo Instrumenta mea omnia, quae e Dania huc transtuli numero 28; thesaurus incomparabilis, quem Patria mea non aestimans sibiipsi invidit. Adornatur Typographia, ut opera mea hactenus interrupta, quanto ocius fieri poterit, compleantur. Exstruitur etiam officina pyronomica pro exercitijs spagyricis, quae nostra est etiam voluptas. Deus Opt. Max. conservet et prosperet Augustissimum hunc Caesarem RUDOLPHUM II, qui nobis haec ocia fecit. Quod superest, aeviterno et omnipotenti Numini te et omnia tua commendo.

Datae ad Pragam ex novo Uraniburgo Caesareo, cuius inscriptionem mox subiungam, die 15 Aprilis stylo novo Anno 1601.
text.english:
**TYCHO BRAHE TO CHRISTOPH STURTZ.**

That you wrote to me through the magnificent Lord Doctor Gödelmann, noble and most learned Lord Doctor Sturtz — although I, on account of his haste and my occupations at that time, sent you no letter [in return] — there is reason for me to give you very many thanks. I recognise from it your candid and constant love toward me, to which I shall not cease to render like for like. Of the state of your fatherland — wondrous, and for many years also wretched — we have heard here more than enough; may God grant peace at last. The Wallachian, among others (as you write) declared an enemy of the Polish kingdom, has lately been made a vassal of our most clement Emperor, and war-leader against Sigismund Báthory — who, at the instigation of the Polish Chancellor, invaded Transylvania with the Tartars and took some part of it from the Emperor — that he may drive him out thence again, and afterward labour for the recovery of Kanizsa. For this cause he has received from the Emperor a great sum of money. The Hungarian war is now being mounted afresh with such effort as scarcely ever before — for so there is need.

Moreover, that you have resolved to insert into your historical reflections the little narrative of my migration from Denmark hither into Bohemia, to the Sacred Imperial Majesty — such as I sent to the late Lord Doctor David Chytraeus, of best memory, at his so requesting — and to polish and adorn it, you will have done me a thing exceedingly welcome, and to be repaid in turn by any service. I should have thought that the completion of the little history of the year 1600, beyond the former half which Lord Chytraeus finished before his death, had been continued by you, so as to be on sale this year, and that the things he wished to insert about me while he lived would have been added to it; but perhaps your counsels are otherwise, in which I gladly acquiesce. I should wish nonetheless that what you proposed be done in good time, and, if opportunity so bring it, that the first draft, before it is struck off, be shared with me.

I now dwell at Prague in the house once splendidly and magnificently built by the late Vice-Chancellor Lord Jacob Curtius, of praised memory, together with an ample and most pleasant garden lying round about — which the Sacred Imperial Majesty bought for my use from the widow dwelling there for 10,000 joachimsthalers, though they were scarcely built for double that sum. It is a place set very high in the city, toward the west, and situated not far from the castle, so that the Imperial Majesty can come hither — past the other houses and gardens lying between — privately and with very little trouble, whenever it shall so most clemently please him. Here are now being arranged all my instruments, which I brought hither from Denmark, 28 in number — an incomparable treasure, which my fatherland, not valuing it, begrudged to itself. A printing-house is being fitted out, so that my works, hitherto interrupted, may be completed as quickly as may be. An alchemical laboratory is also being built for spagyric exercises, which is likewise our delight. May God Best and Greatest preserve and prosper this most august Emperor Rudolf II, who has made these leisures for us. For the rest, I commend you and all yours to the everlasting and omnipotent Deity.

Given at Prague from the new imperial Uraniborg — whose inscription I shall soon append — the 15th day of April, New Style, the year 1601.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Christoph Sturtz** (*Christophorus Sturcius*), a learned correspondent at **Rostock** whose own letter to Tycho of 10 March 1601 survives (brahe-t_16010310001); here Tycho replies. He is evidently of **Transylvanian/Hungarian connection** — Tycho speaks of "the state of *your* fatherland … for many years wretched" and then gives the Transylvania/Hungary war news Sturtz had sent. He is composing a **historical work** into which he wishes to set Tycho's migration narrative (below). (Precise biography to firm up.)
- **Courier.** *Magnificus Dn. D. Gödelmann* = **Johann Georg Gödelmann** (1559–1611), the Mecklenburg jurist-diplomat (cf. brahe-t_16010412001), who had carried Sturtz's letter.
- **The Long-War news (spring 1601; this chapter's convention context).**
 - *Walachus* = the **Voivode of Wallachia** — **Michael the Brave (Mihai Viteazul)** — lately made an **imperial vassal** and war-leader against **Sigismund Báthory** of Transylvania.
 - *Sigismundus Batorus* = **Sigismund Báthory**, who (Tycho relays) had "at the instigation of the **Polish Chancellor** [**Jan Zamoyski**] invaded Transylvania with the Tartars" and seized part of it from the Emperor.
 - *Canisium* = **Kanizsa (Nagykanizsa)**, the Hungarian fortress lost to the Ottomans in 1600, now to be recovered; the **Hungarian war** (the Ottoman–Habsburg "Long War") "mounted afresh with such effort as scarcely ever before."
- **Tycho's migration-narrative and David Chytraeus.** Tycho had sent the late **David Chytraeus** (1530–1600, the Rostock historian; cf. brahe-t_16000305001) an autobiographical *narratiuncula* of his **migration from Denmark to Bohemia**, at Chytraeus's request, for Chytraeus's contemporary *history of the year 1600*. Chytraeus died with the work half-finished; Sturtz now proposes to continue it and incorporate Tycho's account. Tycho welcomes it and asks to **see the first draft before printing** — a characteristic concern for control over how his story is told.
- **The new imperial Uraniborg (the famed description of the Prague house).** Tycho describes his Prague residence: the **house of the late imperial Vice-Chancellor Jacob Curtius** (Jakob Kurz von Senftenau; cf. brahe-t_15900125001, brahe-t_16010412001), with its ample garden, **bought for Tycho by Rudolf II from Curtius's widow for 10,000 joachimsthalers** ("though scarcely built for double that sum"); set **high in the city, toward the west, near the castle**, so the Emperor can come privately. Within it Tycho is installing **all 28 of his instruments brought from Denmark** — "an incomparable treasure, which my fatherland, not valuing it, begrudged to itself" — plus a **printing-house** (to finish his interrupted works) and an **alchemical laboratory** (*officina pyronomica*) "for spagyric exercises." He calls the whole the *novum Uraniburgum Caesareum*, "the new imperial Uraniborg," and promises to append its **inscription**. (Cf. the same self-styling in brahe-t_16010412001, "the new Rudolphine Uraniborg.")
- **Persons named.** Christoph Sturtz; Johann Georg Gödelmann; the Wallachian Voivode (Michael the Brave); Sigismund Báthory; Jan Zamoyski (the Polish Chancellor); David Chytraeus; **Jacob Curtius** (and his widow); **Rudolf II**.
- **Calendar / dateline.** Dateline *die Aprilis stylo novo Anno 1601* — **New Style**, Prague/imperial; the **day-number is missing/illegible** in the source dateline (*die [—] Aprilis*) and is supplied as **15** from the edition label and identifier (16010415002), flagged here rather than silently inserted.

- **§1 Dreyer collation.** The day is **not** merely label-supplied: Dreyer (*Opera Omnia* VIII p. 416; running-head 5/15 Apr.) prints *die 15 Aprilis*. Restored to Source + translation; the bracket withdrawn.
- **Correction.** Latin: 'desinam' corrected to 'desistam', per Dreyer, Opera Omnia VIII, p.415 (translation unaffected — 'shall not cease' is compatible with either verb).

documents.incipit: DURCHLÄUCHTIGSTER hochgeborner fürst, gnedigster herr. Ewer Furstl: G: sein meine …

text.original:
DEM DURCHLAUCHTIGSTEN HOCHGEBORNEN FURSTEN VNDT HERRN, HERRN VLDARICH, HERTZOGEN ZU MECHELLENBURGK, FURSTEN ZU WENDEN, GRAFFEN ZU SCHWERIN, DER LANDE ROSTOCH VNDT STARGARTTEN HERRN, MEINEM GNEDICHSTEN FURSTENN VNNDT HERRNN.

DURCHLÄUCHTIGSTER hochgeborner fürst, gnedigster herr. Ewer Furstl: G: sein meine vnterthenigste gantzwillige dienste iederzeit höchstes fleißes bevor.

Vndt soll deroselben vntherthenigst nitt pergenn, daß ich aine von meinen vielgeliepten töchtern mit nahmen Elizabet Brahe ainem westpfhälischen edelman Franzen Tengnagel zum Campe ehelich versprochen, auch nechst göttlicher hülff zwischen ostern vndt pfhingsten nechstkünfftich ihre hochzeit zu macchen vorhabens bin. Vndt dieweil nit allein die röm: kayß: may:, vnsern allergnedichsten herrn, ich allervnterthenigst sampt etzlichen deroselben vornehmen vndt hochweißen rhätten, sondern auch etzliche fürsten in Deutschlandt, baid eccleßastici vndt politici status, welche ich weiß, mir in gnaden bewogen zu sein, dazue zu beruffen in willens, hab auch solliches Ewer F: G: alß meinem iederzeit gnedichsten fürsten vndt herrn gehorsambst zu verstendigen vnd sie darauff zu laden nitt vmbgehen können. Nitt daß ich begehren kan oder darff, daß weder die andre fürsten noch E: F: G: ainen von denseinigen sölliche aine weitte reiße anhero schicken solte, sondern ihm fahll etwa dieselbe ainigen von ihren leutten alhie ahm hoffe hetten, daß von E: F: G: wegen der alsdan diesen nuptialem actum sua præsentia cohonestieren möchte.

Woran nur zum hohen ahngenehmen vnd gnedichsten gefallen geschehe, vnd bins meinem geringen vermög nach stets vnterthenigst vndt danckparlich zu erkennen gantz willig vnd gefließen. E: F: G: sampt dero vielgeliepten gemählin göttlicher allmacht abermahl vnterthenigst vnd getreulich empfhelendt.

Datum Prag auß der Curtianiske hauße den 15 dag aprilis anno 1601 stylo nouo.
Ewer F: G: vntherthenigster ganz williger
Tycho Brahe
Eigenhn.
text.english:
**To the most serene, high-born Prince and Lord, Lord Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg, Prince of the Wends, Count of Schwerin, Lord of the lands of Rostock and Stargard, my most gracious Prince and Lord.**

Most serene, high-born Prince, most gracious lord. To Your Princely Grace be my most humble, entirely willing services at all times, of the highest diligence, beforehand.

And [I] shall not most humbly conceal from the same, that I have betrothed one of my much-beloved daughters, by name Elisabeth Brahe, to a Westphalian nobleman, Frans Tengnagel to Camp, and intend, next with God's help, to make their wedding between Easter and Pentecost next coming. And since I am minded to summon to it not only the Roman Imperial Majesty, our most gracious lord — most humbly — together with several of the same's distinguished and most wise councillors, but also several princes in Germany, both of the ecclesiastical and the political estate, who I know are graciously inclined toward me: I have also not been able to omit obediently to inform Your Princely Grace, as my ever most gracious Prince and Lord, of such, and to invite you thereto. Not that I can, or may, desire that either the other princes or Your Princely Grace should send one of [your] people so long a journey hither; but [rather] in case the same [you] should perhaps have any of your people here at court, [so] that [one of them] might then, on Your Princely Grace's behalf, honour this *nuptial act* with his *presence* [*nuptialem actum sua praesentia cohonestieren*].

Whereby would happen [something] only to [my] high agreeable and most gracious pleasure; and I am, according to my slight ability, ever most humbly and thankfully entirely willing and assiduous to acknowledge [it]. Commending Your Princely Grace, together with your much-beloved consort, once again most humbly and faithfully to God's Almighty [protection].

Given Prague, from the Curtius house, the 15th day of April, in the year 1601, new style.
Your Princely Grace's most humble, entirely willing,
Tycho Brahe,
[his] own hand.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Ulrich III, Duke of Mecklenburg-Güstrow** (1527–1603) — the same Duke who, three months later, writes to Tycho about the 10,000-thaler debt (brahe-t_16010724001). His full Mecklenburg titulature (*Duke of Mecklenburg, Prince of the Wends, Count of Schwerin, Lord of the lands of Rostock and Stargard*) is reproduced. The witness is in the Schwerin **Familien-Akten: Brahe**.
- **A wedding invitation — companion to brahe-t_16010404001.** The second of Tycho's surviving **invitations to the wedding of his daughter Elisabeth Brahe to Frans Tengnagel** ("a Westphalian nobleman, Frans Tengnagel to Camp"), to be held at Prague **between Easter and Pentecost 1601** (cf. the invitation to Holger Rosenkrantz, brahe-t_16010404001, 4 April 1601). Tycho says he is inviting **the Emperor and his councillors**, and "several princes of Germany, both **ecclesiastical and political**"; he tactfully asks the Duke only to let a courtier already at Prague represent him and "**honour this nuptial act with his presence**" — not to send anyone the long journey.
- ***nuptialem actum sua praesentia cohonestieren*** — a Latin code-switch within the German (kept and italicised, by this chapter's convention): "to honour the nuptial act/ceremony with his presence."
- **Place.** *aus der Curtianischen Hause* = the **Curtius house** at Prague (the former mansion of Vice-Chancellor Jakob Curtius), Tycho's residence — the same venue named in brahe-t_16010404001.
- **Calendar.** *Prag … den 15 dag aprilis anno 1601 stylo novo* = **15 April 1601, New Style** (explicit); Prague, imperial. Header agrees with the label.

documents.incipit: GENEROSE et doctissime D. TYCHO, misit ante paucas septimanas responsum ad priores tuas …

text.original:
DEM EDELEN GESTRENGEN EHRENVESTEN HERREN TYCHO BRAHENN AUFF KNUTSTORFF ERBSASSEN, RÖMISCHER KEYSERLICHER MAIESTATASTRONOMO,MEINEM GROSSGUNSTIGEN HERREN.

S.

GENEROSE et doctissime D. TYCHO, misit ante paucas septimanas responsum ad priores tuas literas SIMON a PETKUM. Illud, cum priorem aliquem habere non potuerim, per hunc FRANCISCUM SCHROTERUM Sundensem, Chymicarum rerum studiosum, qui nescio qua de causa iter Pragam instituerat, ad te amandare volui, spero recte redditum iri. De fornacibus quoque advehendis videbo quid efficere potero. Nondum enim quicquam præter eas Hamburgo advectum est, propter nimiam Albis exundationem. Quia vero moris est, ut amici amicis novarum narrationum communicatione gratificentur, mitto D. TYCHONI cuiusdam LL. Doctoris DETHARDI HORSTIJ Witebergæ agentis prognosticon de eventu belli Turcici, sane gratissimum, utinam etiam verissimum. Impingunt nostri Theologi et vani vates omnes in eundem quo Pharisæi et Apostoli olim lapidem, ut vaticinia de CHRISTO eiusque et Ecclesiæ regno et victorijs, politica Phrasi pronunciata, politice intelligant, cum Ecclesia novi Testamenti nullam habeat promissionem politiæ et politici regni ut veteris Testamenti, usque ad CHRISTUM, et CHRISTUS ipse dicat: Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo, item: In mundo afflictionem habebitis, in me autem TANTUM pacem. Stultum quoque hoc est, quod omnes vaticinium de GOG et MAGOG interpretantur de regno Turcico, cum id loquatur historice de victorias Israëlitarum ante CHRISTUM, allegorice vero, ut Apocalypsis IOHANNIS eum declarat, de persecutoribus Ecclesiæ in toto orbe terrarum adventu CHRISTI extremo tollendis, cap. 20 vs. 8: Exibit SATHANAS ut seducat gentes, quæ sunt in QUATUOR angulis terræ, τὸν Γὼγ καὶ τὸν Μάγωγ, qui circumierunt castra Sanctorum et urbem dilectam. Sed descendit ignis a DEO e cœlo, qui devoravit eos etc. Simile delirium est, quod hic interpres idolum vastans interpretatur de MAHOMETE, cum ipse filius DEI dicat Matth. 24 intelligendum esse DANIELEM de signo præcessuro finalem Politiæ Iudaicæ, inprimis templi destructionem, Ideo monet: Cum videritis abominationem vastatricem stantem in loco sancto, ut dictum est a DANIELE propheta tum qui in Iudæa est, fugiat ad montes etc. Ridiculum denique plane est somnium, quod metuunt, ne DANIEL mentiatur, cum definit Monarchias quatuor, si Turca inchoaret quintam Monarchiam, cum prima fuerit Monarchia iam Assyriorum, iam Chaldæorum, in secunda iam in Babylonia, iam in Persia dominabantur Monarchæ, in tertia singuli Duces ALEXANDRI constituebant sibi peculiarem Monarchiam, in quarta alia erat Orientis, quam dudum rapuit Turca, alia Occidentis, quam hactenus mordicus retinet Papa, et vicinorum regulorum potentia ad suam triplicem coronam tuendam simplici credulitate et armis abutitur. Ante vero illa tempora quam varios habuit Monarchas, quorum post annum CHRISTI 480 nemo Romanus aut Italus fuit, quando AUGUSTULUS ultimus purpuram abiecit, eamque induit ODOACER Sax. Post illum anno 495 CHRISTI THEODORICUS Ost-Gotthus dictus Veronensis, inde 574 Longobardorum Reges usque ad CAROLUM Magnum Francum, qui cœpit Imperator Romanorum dici 800 CHRISTI. Unde reliqui Germani titulum, Papa imperium habet hactenus. Et sic digiti pedum in DANIELIS Colosso varie discriminantur sine inchoatione quintæ Monarchiæ, et metuimus, ne Turca sit quintus Monarcha; qui iamdiu est Monarcha Orientis. Sed hæc delirant, qui historiarum sunt ignari, et qui amant, ipsi sibi somnia fingunt. DEUS tueatur hospitia Ecclesiæ, servet verbum suum et confundat consilia Turcæ et Papæ, propter gloriam nominis sui.

Bene in Domino vale.
18 Aprilis nostro 1601.
G. N. T.
addictiss.
GEORGIUS ROLLENHAGEN.
text.english:
**To the noble, gallant, and honourable Lord Tycho Brahe, hereditary lord of Knudstrup, Astronomer to the Roman Imperial Majesty, my greatly favourable Lord.**

Greeting.

Generous and most learned Lord Tycho: **Simon von Petkum** sent, a few weeks ago, a reply to your earlier letter. That [reply], since I could have no earlier [carrier], I wished to dispatch to you by this **Franz Schröter of Stralsund**, a student of chemical matters, who for some cause I know not had undertaken a journey to Prague; I hope it will be duly delivered. Concerning the **furnaces** also, to be conveyed, I will see what I can effect; for nothing yet but they has been brought from Hamburg, on account of the excessive flooding of the **Elbe**. And since it is the custom that friends gratify friends by sharing news, I send Lord Tycho a **prognostication on the outcome of the Turkish war** by a certain Doctor of Laws **Dethard Horst**, active at Wittenberg — most welcome indeed; would it were also most true.

Our Theologians, and all the vain seers, stumble on the same stone as the Pharisees and the Apostles once did: that they understand **politically** the prophecies about Christ, and his and the Church's kingdom and victories — pronounced in political phrase — whereas the Church of the New Testament has no promise of a polity and political kingdom, as the Old Testament had up to Christ; and Christ himself says, *"My kingdom is not of this world,"* and again, *"In the world you shall have affliction, but in me ONLY peace."* This too is foolish, that all interpret the prophecy of **Gog and Magog** of the Turkish kingdom — whereas it speaks *historically* of the victories of the Israelites before Christ, but *allegorically* (as John's Apocalypse declares it) of the persecutors of the Church throughout the whole world, to be destroyed at Christ's final coming — chapter 20, verse 8: *"Satan will go out to seduce the nations which are in the FOUR corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, who surrounded the camp of the Saints and the beloved city. But fire came down from God out of heaven, which devoured them,"* etc. A similar madness it is, that this interpreter expounds the **"desolating idol"** of **Mohammed** — whereas the Son of God himself says, in Matthew 24, that **Daniel** is to be understood of the sign that should precede the final [end] of the Jewish polity, especially the destruction of the temple; therefore he warns: *"When you see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place, as was said by Daniel the prophet, then let him who is in Judaea flee to the mountains,"* etc. Finally, it is a plainly ridiculous dream that they fear lest **Daniel** lie — when he defines **four Monarchies** — if the Turk should begin a fifth Monarchy: whereas the first Monarchy was now of the Assyrians, now of the Chaldeans; in the second the Monarchs ruled now in Babylonia, now in Persia; in the third Alexander's individual generals each set up his own Monarchy; in the fourth, one [Monarchy] was of the **East**, which the Turk long ago seized, another of the **West**, which the **Pope** hitherto retains tooth and nail, abusing the power of the neighbouring princelings — by their simple credulity and by arms — to defend his **triple crown**. And before those times, how many and various Monarchs it had! — of whom, after the year of Christ 480, none was a Roman or an Italian, when **Augustulus**, the last, cast off the purple, and **Odoacer the Saxon** put it on; after him, in the year of Christ 495, **Theodoric the Ostrogoth**, called of Verona; then, from 574, the Kings of the Lombards, up to **Charlemagne** the Frank, who began to be called Emperor of the Romans in [the year] 800. Whence the Germans have kept the title, [while] the Pope has held the [imperial] power hitherto. And thus the **toes of the feet in Daniel's Colossus** are variously distinguished, without the beginning of a fifth Monarchy — and [yet] we fear lest the Turk be a fifth Monarch, who has long been Monarch of the East! But these things they rave who are ignorant of the histories; and those who are fond [of such fancies] fashion dreams for themselves. May God protect the dwellings of the Church, preserve his word, and confound the counsels of the Turk and the Pope, for the glory of his name.

Fare well in the Lord.
18 April, by our [style], 1601.
Most devoted to Your Generous Nobility,
Georg Rollenhagen.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Georg Rollenhagen** (1542–1609), rector of the Magdeburg school (*Altstädtisches Gymnasium*), Lutheran humanist and poet (author of *Froschmeuseler*), Tycho's "especial friend" and Magdeburg agent (cf. brahe-t_16000404001, brahe-t_16001009001). The German address styles Tycho *"Astronomer to the Roman Imperial Majesty."*
- **The practical opening.** Rollenhagen forwards a reply from **Simon von Petkum** (Tycho's Hamburg factor; cf. brahe-t_16000422001) by the hand of **Franz Schröter of Stralsund** (*Sundensis*), "a student of chemical matters" bound for Prague; reports that **Tycho's furnaces** (the alchemical *fornaces*) are the only thing yet brought from Hamburg, the **Elbe flooding** having stalled the rest; and encloses, as news, a **prognostication on the Turkish war** by the Wittenberg jurist (*LL. Doctor* = *Legum Doctor*) **Dethard Horst** — "would it were as true as it is welcome."
- **Significance — a learned anti-apocalyptic, anti-Roman polemic.** The body is a vigorous **humanist critique of the literal-political reading of Biblical prophecy** then rampant in war-anxious Germany. Rollenhagen argues:
 - Theologians err like "the Pharisees and Apostles" in taking the prophecies of Christ's kingdom **politically**, though "**My kingdom is not of this world**" (John 18:36) and "**in the world you shall have affliction, but in me only peace**" (John 16:33).
 - **Gog and Magog** (with the Greek *τὸν Γὼγ καὶ τὸν Μάγωγ* preserved) is not the **Turk** but, *historically*, Israel's pre-Christian wars, and *allegorically* (per **Revelation 20:8–9**) the Church's persecutors destroyed at the Last Day.
 - The **"abomination of desolation"** (Daniel; **Matthew 24:15–16**) is not **Mohammed** but the sign of the **destruction of the Jewish temple**.
 - **Daniel's four monarchies** (the dream-statue of Daniel 2) do not leave room for a Turkish "fifth": he sketches the sequence — **Assyrian/Chaldean → Babylonian/Persian → the Diadochi (Alexander's generals) → the divided fourth (East, seized by the Turk; West, held by the *Pope*)** — and runs the Western imperial succession from **Romulus Augustulus (476/"480") and Odoacer**, through **Theodoric the Ostrogoth** and the **Lombard kings**, to **Charlemagne (800)** and the German emperors, "the Pope [holding] the [imperial] power hitherto." The **"toes of Daniel's Colossus"** are merely the divided kingdoms, "without the beginning of a fifth Monarchy." "These things they rave who are ignorant of the histories."
 - A pointed **anti-papal** Lutheran edge throughout (the Pope's *"triple crown,"* "tooth and nail," abusing princes' credulity), closing: *"God … confound the counsels of the Turk and the Pope."*
- **Scripture & figures identified.** John 18:36; John 16:33; **Revelation 20:8–9** (Gog and Magog); **Matthew 24:15–16** (abomination of desolation, citing Daniel); **Daniel 2** (the four-monarchy statue with feet/toes of iron and clay). Historical figures: **Romulus Augustulus**, **Odoacer** ("the Saxon"), **Theodoric the Ostrogoth** (*"of Verona"* = Dietrich von Bern), the **Lombard kings**, **Charlemagne**.
- **Greek.** *τὸν Γὼγ καὶ τὸν Μάγωγ* — "Gog and Magog"; kept verbatim in the source block, translated in the body.
- **Persons named.** Georg Rollenhagen (sender); **Simon von Petkum**; **Franz Schröter** of Stralsund; **Dethard Horst** (Wittenberg jurist); plus the Scriptural/historical figures above.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *"18 Aprilis nostro 1601"* — *nostro [stylo]*, "by **our [Old] style**": Lutheran Magdeburg kept the **Julian** calendar (the *nostro* explicitly marks the O.S./N.S. divide from Tycho's imperial New Style). No place in the dateline (edition *s.l.*); "[Magdeburg]" supplied as the evident origin (Rollenhagen's seat). Header marked [O.S.].

Collated the German address line, every proper name (Simon von Petkum, Franz Schroter of Stralsund, Dethard Horst), all four scripture citations (John 18:36, John 16:33, Revelation 20:8, Matthew 24:15), and every date/number (chapter 20 verse 8, four corners, anno 480/495/574/800, 18 April 1601) against the printed text; all match the transcribed original and the published English exactly. No defects found.

text.original:
SERENISSIMO ET POTENTISSIMO PRINCIPI AC DOMINO, DOMINO FERDINANDO MAGNO DUCI ETRURIÆ ETC. DOMINO SUO CLEMENTISSIMO. FLORENTZ.

AD Serenissimam Celsitudinem Vestram ante Anni quadrantem per Filium meum natu maiorem, Legationem Persicam in Italiam comitantem, submisse dedi literas, quas Sereniss. Celsni Væ recte esse redditas ex Epistola eiusdem Filij nuperrime ad me data lubenter cognovi. Scribit is inibi nonnulla, quæ animum meum non parum perculerunt: Legatum nimirum Persicum illum primarium natione Anglum, in cuius familia Filius meus tunc fuit, cum Senas pervenisset, ipsum ad se seorsim vocasse, atque hæc insinuasse: Serenissimam Celsnem Vam illi videlicet Legato Anglo, cum ex literis ad ipsam a me scriptis intellexisset, Filium meum in ipsius comitatu esse, dissuasisse, ut illum Romam secum adduceret, præsertim illo tempore, id enim non absque gravi periculo vitæ Filij, et ipsiusmet Legati impedimento fieri posse, siquidem meum nomen in illis oris iam antea satis innotuisset, et potissimum ea de causa periculum subesse, quod in Italia rumor increbuisset, Sacræ Cæsareæ Mati me authorem et suasorem fuisse, ne Monachos Capucinianos hîc Pragæ diutius pateretur, sed eos dimitteret. Voluit itaque Legatus ille Anglus, ut Filius meus Senis remaneret, nec Romam unâ accederet, quod et factum est. Si itaque hæc, ut ille retulit, ex Sereniss. Celsnis Væ consilio et admonitione facta sunt, non dubito, quin clementissimo erga me et Filium meum animo et bona ac sincera intentione profecta sint. Sin autem Legatus iste ex suo cerebro talia deprompsit, et sub prætextu nominis Væ Saæ Celsnis (uti suspicor) protulit, facile conijcio, eum id fecisse, ut sic honeste a Filio meo liberaretur, ne illi ulterius oneri esset, siquidem, uti hîc Pragæ satis cognovimus, viatico pro tam magnifica legatione et tanto itinere emetiendo non satis instructus erat: sed sit quicquid velit, gaudeo Filium meum Senis in Sereniss. Væ Celsitudinis ditione et urbe commorari, ubi eum commode degere, et satis tutum fore, omnino mihi persuadeo, cum Væ Sereniss. Celsnis Regio sit per se libera, et ijs, quæ forte alibi in Italia incidere possent, periculis non obnoxia, ideoque a Sereniss. Celsne Va, qua possum submissione et reverentia peto, velit sibi Filium hunc meum commendatum habere non dedignari, et si res ipsius ita tulerint, ut tam diu in Væ Sereniss. Celsnis territorio subsistere possit, donec Linguam Italicam mediocriter addidicerit, id equidem mihi apprime acceptum foret; quo peracto, ut Sereniss. Celso Va eum Sereniss. et Potentissimo Rege Galliarum, inclyto suo Affini, per literas commendare dignetur, quo in ipsius Aula per unum vel alterum annum, donec et illam linguam calluerit, pro servitore recipiatur, demisse et officiosissime eam rogatam vellem: quicquid hac vel alia ratione Sereniss. Celso Va in Filium meum contulerit clementissimi beneficij, id tanquam in me ipsum collatum perpetua animi submissione et gratitudine, quantum vires meæ patientur, agnoscam.

Cæterum quod Monachos Capucinianos attinet, certo sciat, atque indubitate Sereniss. Celso Va statuat, quod nunquam vel minima cogitatione mihi in mentem venerit apud Sacram Cæsaream Maiestatem, Dominum meum Clementissimum, quidpiam de ijs loqui, aut an hîc manere debeant vel secus, ullo verbo mentionem facere, nedum ut quidpiam in his eius Maiestati suggererem aut consulerem, cum talia ad me plane non pertineant, nec ipsius Maiestas unquam de eiuscemodi rebus, quæ Ecclesiasticas Personas aut res concernunt, mecum loquatur, sed solummodo de ijs, quæ Philosophica et Astronomica, quibus ipsius Maiestas, sicuti multi alij Reges et Principes, laudabiliter afficitur, nec ego me alienis immisceo: vix suppetit otium et commoditas propria tractandi et exequendi. DEUM itaque sancte et conscientiam meam intemerate testari possum, magnam mihi hac in parte fieri iniuriam, tam hîc quam alibi, uti etiam in quibusdam alijs calumnijs, quæ ab imperitis seu mearum rerum ignaris hîc sparsæ sunt, de quibus brevi ad ipsius Maiestatem, quæ me in omnibus ijs, quæ apud ipsius Maiestatem a me dicta et peracta esse nonnulli comminiscuntur, insontem novit, referre animus est. Quin et Sereniss. Celsnis Væ Magnificentissimus hic Orator satis perspectum habet, eum de Capucinis rumorem meram esse in me calumniam, et scit forte, unde illa dissuasio apud Cæsarem provenerit, ut me non saltem ille, sed et Illustrissimus ac Reverendissimus Dominus Nuncius, qui nomine P. M. hîc moratur, me satis de isto figmento, uti et in alio quodam huic ferme simili, excusatum habet, siquidem ab Illustri et Magnifico Domino CORADUCIO Imperij Procancellario satis superque cognoverit, rem longe aliter se habere, meque omni culpa in eiuscemodi de me promulgatis nugis vacare. Quæ ob id latius ad Sereniss. Celsnem Vam qua possum submissione perscribo, ut illa quoque, si tale quid ad eius aures pervenit, meam innocentiam cognitam habeat, nec tam iniuriosas calumnias in meæ famæ extenuationem aut Filij mei detrimentum redundare sinat, sed id potius sua authoritate, sicubi opus fuerit, clementissime amoliatur, sique vicissim ex mea tenuitate proficisci poterint officiola, quæ Sereniss. Celsni Væ ullo modo accepta esse queant, utatur me perpetuo tanquam suo servitore fideli et obsequentissimo. DEUS Opt. Max. Serenis. Celsnem Vam Reipub. tam politicæ quam literariæ bono per multos Annos incolumem et prosperam florere faciat.

Dabantur Pragæ 30 die Aprilis Anno 1601.
Serenissimæ Celsitudinis Vestræ
Reverenter et submisse
addictissimus
TYCHO BRAHE,
manu propria scripsi.
text.english:
**To the most serene and most powerful Prince and Lord, Lord Ferdinando, Grand Duke of Tuscany etc., his most clement Lord. Florence.**

To Your most serene Highness, a quarter of a year ago, I humbly sent a letter **by my elder son, accompanying the Persian Legation into Italy** — which letter, I gladly learned from a recent letter of that same son, was duly delivered to Your most serene Highness. He writes therein some things which struck my mind not a little: namely that **the chief Persian Legate, an Englishman by nation, in whose household my son then was**, when he had reached **Siena**, called him aside and insinuated this: that **Your most serene Highness — having understood, from letters written to You by me, that my son was in his company — had dissuaded the English Legate from bringing him to Rome**, especially at that time; for that could not be done without grave danger to my son's life, and hindrance to the Legate himself, since my name had already become well enough known in those parts, and that the danger lay chiefly in this — **that a rumour had grown in Italy that I had been the author and instigator, to the Sacred Imperial Majesty, that he should no longer tolerate the Capuchin monks here at Prague, but dismiss them.** The English Legate therefore wished that my son should remain at Siena, and not go on to Rome with him — which was done. If, then, these things were done — as he reported — by Your most serene Highness's counsel and admonition, I do not doubt they proceeded from a most clement disposition toward me and my son, and from a good and sincere intention. But if that Legate produced such things out of his own brain, and put them forth **under the pretext of Your Highness's name (as I suspect)**, I easily conjecture that he did it so as to be honestly rid of my son, lest he be a further burden to him — since, as we have learned well enough here at Prague, **he was not well enough supplied with travel-money for so magnificent a legation and so great a journey**. But be it what it will: I rejoice that my son tarries at Siena, in Your most serene Highness's dominion and city, where I am wholly persuaded he may dwell conveniently and be safe enough, since Your most serene Highness's region is of itself free, and not subject to the perils that might perchance arise elsewhere in Italy. Therefore I beg of Your most serene Highness, with what submission and reverence I can, that **You would not disdain to hold this my son commended to You**; and if his affairs so allow that he may stay in Your Highness's territory long enough to learn the **Italian** tongue tolerably, that would indeed be most welcome to me. Which done, I would most humbly and dutifully ask that **Your most serene Highness deign to commend him by letter to the most serene and most powerful King of France, Your renowned kinsman**, that he might be received as a servant in his Court for a year or two, until he master that tongue too. Whatever, by this or another means, Your most serene Highness shall confer of most clement benefit upon my son, I shall acknowledge as conferred upon myself, with perpetual submission and gratitude of mind, so far as my powers allow.

For the rest, as concerns **the Capuchin monks**: let Your most serene Highness know for certain, and conclude beyond doubt, that **it never came into my mind, even by the least thought, to speak anything of them to the Sacred Imperial Majesty, my most clement Lord — to make mention by any word whether they ought to stay here or not — much less to suggest or counsel His Majesty anything in these matters**; since such things in no way pertain to me, nor does His Majesty ever speak with me of such things as concern Ecclesiastical Persons or affairs, but only of those that are **Philosophical and Astronomical**, with which His Majesty (like many other Kings and Princes) is laudably taken; nor do I meddle in others' business — scarcely have I leisure and convenience to handle and carry out my own. I can therefore call **God to witness, holily, and my conscience inviolately, that a great injury is done me in this part**, both here and elsewhere — as also in certain other calumnies which have been scattered here by the unskilled, or by those ignorant of my affairs — about which I intend shortly to report to His Majesty, who knows me innocent in all those things that some falsely invent to have been said and done by me before His Majesty. Indeed **Your most serene Highness's most magnificent Orator here has clearly enough perceived that this rumour about the Capuchins is a mere calumny against me, and perhaps knows whence that dissuasion at the Emperor's [court] arose**; so that not only he, but also **the most illustrious and most reverend Lord Nuncio, who stays here in the name of the Supreme Pontiff [the Pope]**, holds me well enough excused of that fiction — as also in another very similar one — since he has learned, fully and more, from the illustrious and magnificent **Lord Coraduz, Vice-Chancellor of the Empire**, that the matter stands far otherwise, and that I am free of all blame in such trifles published about me. All which I therefore write more fully to Your most serene Highness, with what submission I can, so that You too — if any such thing has reached Your ears — may have my innocence known, and not let such injurious calumnies redound to the lessening of my fame or to my son's detriment, but rather most clemently remove it by Your authority, wherever there be need. And if in turn any small services can proceed from my slenderness, that can in any way be acceptable to Your most serene Highness, use me ever as Your faithful and most obedient servant. May God, Best and Greatest, make Your most serene Highness flourish unharmed and prosperous for many years, for the good of the Commonwealth, both political and literary.

Given at Prague, the 30th day of April, the year 1601.
Your most serene Highness's,
reverently and submissively, most devoted,
**Tycho Brahe**, written in my own hand.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Ferdinando I de' Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany** (*Magnus Dux Etruriae*, 1549–1609), at Florence.
- **Significance — Tycho the Younger's Italian journey, the Capuchin calumny, and a bid for the French court.** Three interlocking threads:
 1. **The son and the Persian embassy.** Tycho's **elder son (Tycho Brahe the Younger)** had travelled into Italy **accompanying the Persian Legation** — the 1600–01 Safavid embassy jointly led by the Persian Husain Ali Beg and **the Englishman Sir Anthony Sherley** ("the chief Persian Legate, an Englishman by nation," in whose household the son was). (Cf. the same embassy at Prague, brahe-t_16001110001.) At **Siena** the son was **left behind and not taken on to Rome**.
 2. **The Capuchin calumny (the political danger).** The stated reason: a **rumour in Italy that Tycho had urged Rudolf II to expel the Capuchin monks from Prague** — which, in Counter-Reformation Italy, made the Protestant Tycho's name (and his son's presence in Rome) perilous. Tycho **vehemently denies it** ("it never came into my mind … I never speak with His Majesty save of Philosophical and Astronomical things"), calling God and conscience to witness, and reports that **the Tuscan ambassador, the Papal Nuncio, and Vice-Chancellor Coraduz all hold him cleared** of the "fiction." He suspects Sherley **invented the Grand Duke's "advice" as a pretext** to shed the son — Sherley being notoriously **short of travel-money** for the grand legation.
 3. **The French-court plan.** Tycho asks Ferdinando to keep the son in Tuscany until he learns **Italian**, then **recommend him to "the King of France, Your renowned kinsman"** — i.e. **Henri IV**, the Medici's *Affinis* through **Maria de' Medici's marriage (October 1600)** — for a year or two at the French court to learn French.
- **A window on Tycho's court position.** The disclaimer is a precise statement of Tycho's self-understood role at Rudolf's court: **strictly the philosophical/astronomical adviser, deliberately aloof from confessional politics** — and beset by "calumnies … scattered by the unskilled," which he means to lay before the Emperor.
- **Persons & places named.** Ferdinando I de' Medici; **Tycho Brahe the Younger** (the elder son); **Sir Anthony Sherley** (the English co-legate of the Persian embassy, unnamed but identified); **Henri IV of France** ("King of France, Your kinsman"); the **Papal Nuncio** at Prague (*nomine P.M.* = in the name of the *Pontifex Maximus*; unnamed — Filippo Spinelli held the post c. 1599–1603); the Tuscan **Orator/ambassador** at Prague (unnamed); **Rudolf von Coraduz** (Vice-Chancellor); the **Capuchin monks**. Places: **Prague**, **Florence**, **Siena**, **Rome**, Italy.
- **Cross-references.** Links to the **Persian-embassy** thread (brahe-t_16001110001) and to Tycho's **court-calumny / self-defence** thread; a key document for the biography of **Tycho Brahe the Younger**.
- **Calendar.** *Pragae 30 die Aprilis Anno 1601* (imperial reckoning) → **30 April 1601 [N.S.]**; header and label agree.

text.original:
GENEROSA NOBILITATE ET POLITIORIBUS LITERIS CLARISSIMO VIRO D. TYCHONI BRAHÆO DOMINO IN KNUTSTORFF ET CÆSAREÆ MAIESTATIS CONSILIARIO ET MATHEMATICO EXCELLENTISSIMO DOMINO ET AMICO SUO.

S.

CUM ad me ex itinere suo, quod ad te instituerat, Generose et Doctiss. D. TYCHO, divertisset optimus vir DAVID FABRICIUS, et non modo tua studia, ut merentur, crebris sermonibus commendaret, sed observationes quoque suas coram ostenderet, dolui profecto GANYMEDEM tam elegantem Frisios potius Boves pascere, quam ab Aquila Ioviali raptum, Dijs in Cœlo ministrare, ut DAVID ab ovibus in aulam propter Musicam adoptabatur, ut certe hic DAVID GANYMEDEM habet ascendentem. Sed quisque suos patimur manes. Ego certe multis nominibus eum mihi optârim propiorem.

Fuit ante paucos dies hîc quasi privatus Episcopus Coloniensis, iturus ad Cæsarem, ut ei Papæ nomine electionem Regis Romanorum persuadeat, atque sic et reditus Cæsarios et autoritatem in plures partes distrahat. Ne dicam de nuncio Belgico, in quam terram iam redijt exercitus Hispanicus. Ab altera parte redit Turca. Domine, serva nos, perimus.

Favorem Episcopi Saltzburgensis tibi ex animo gratulor, utinam plures adducat tibi suffragantes, ut tandem utilissimos tuos labores ad umbilicum deducas.

De prognostico, quod HENRICUS IULIUS de se usurpare dicitur, iam olim audivi doctorem MEGABACCHUM, ROTHIUM et alios, qui a me existimabant esse profectum. Sed neque ego hoc dixi aut scripsi unquam, neque ab ipso audivi. Hoc autem dicere solet GARCÆUM prædixisse, aliquando se præclaram ex bello victoriam relaturum esse, itaque ad bella esse animosiorem. Quod negavi ego ex fontibus, quos epistola tua allegat. Et si possem, in viam potius pacis reducerem, quam ut currentem instigarem. Sed fertur equis auriga, nec audit currus habenas.

Spero me propediem in aulam venturum ad consultationem de vocando Theologo in locum HOFMANNI. Ibi, ut decet, privatim de tua pro eius salute solicitudine, et commoditate negociorum apud Cæsarem privatim expediendorum, movebo fideliter omnia. Et rescribam.

Bene et quam diutissime vale.
15 Maij 1601.
Tuæ Gen. N.
addictiss.
GEORGIUS ROLLENHAGEN.

HENR. IULIUS natus est 1564, 14 Octobris, 17 hora P. M. in arce Hessen. Hoc tempus GARCÆUS
corrupit per falsissimam HERMETIS trutinam et correctiones similes.
text.english:
**To the man renowned for his generous nobility and his more polished learning, Lord Tycho Brahe, Lord of Knudstrup and most excellent councillor and mathematician of His Imperial Majesty, his lord and friend.**

Greeting.

When the excellent man David Fabricius had turned aside to me out of his journey, which he had set toward you, generous and most learned Lord Tycho, and not only commended your studies (as they deserve) in frequent conversation, but also showed me his own observations in person, I grieved indeed that so elegant a Ganymede should pasture Frisian oxen, rather than — snatched up by Jove's Eagle — minister to the gods in heaven; just as David was adopted from the sheep into the court on account of his music, so surely this David has Ganymede in the ascendant. But each of us must endure his own appointed lot. I, for my part, could on many counts have wished him nearer to me.

A few days ago the Bishop of Cologne was here, as it were in a private capacity, on his way to the Emperor, to persuade him in the Pope's name to the election of a King of the Romans, and so to distract the imperial revenues and authority into ever more directions. Not to speak of the Belgian dispatch — into which land the Spanish army has now returned. From the other quarter the Turk returns. Lord, save us, we perish!

On the favour of the Bishop of Salzburg I congratulate you from the heart; would that he bring you more supporters, so that you may at last carry your most useful labours through to completion.

As for the prognostication which Henricus Iulius is said to claim of himself, I heard long ago that Doctor Megabacchus, Roth, and others reckoned it had proceeded from me. But I neither ever said or wrote this, nor heard it from himself. What he is wont to say, however, is that Garcaeus predicted he would one day carry off a glorious victory from war, and that he is therefore the more spirited toward wars. This I have denied, on the sources your letter alleges. And, if I could, I would rather lead him back into the path of peace than goad him on as he runs. But "the charioteer is carried off by his horses, nor does the chariot heed the reins."

I hope to come shortly to court, for the consultation about calling a Theologian into the place of Hofmann. There, as is fitting, I shall faithfully set everything in motion, in private — concerning your solicitude for his welfare, and the convenience of business to be dispatched privately with the Emperor. And I shall write back.

Fare well, and for the longest time.
15 May 1601.
Most devoted to Your Generous Nobility,
Georg Rollenhagen.

Heinrich Julius was born in 1564, on the 14th of October, at the 17th hour P.M., in the castle of Hessen. This time Garcaeus corrupted, by means of the utterly false Balance of Hermes and similar corrections.

documents.apparatus:
- **Direction.** This letter is **to** Tycho, **from** a correspondent — one of the relatively few inbound letters in the edition. The sender writes from Magdeburg (the place is unstated, *s.l.*, but Rollenhagen was rector there).
- **Sender.** **Georg Rollenhagen** (1542–1609), Lutheran theologian, schoolman and poet (author of the mock-epic *Froschmeuseler*, 1595), **rector of the Altstadt Gymnasium at Magdeburg**. His letters reached Tycho enclosed in Winshemius's packets (cf. *Rollenhagianae [literae]* in brahe-t_16000420001).
- **Recipient.** **Tycho Brahe**, here titled *Caesareae Maiestatis consiliarius et mathematicus* — imperial councillor and mathematician.
- **The David Fabricius passage (the literary heart).**
 - *David Fabricius* = **David Fabricius** (1564–1617), Frisian pastor at Resterhafe/Osteel in East Frisia and a gifted naked-eye observer, correspondent of both Tycho and Kepler; he was *en route to visit Tycho* and stopped with Rollenhagen, showing his observations.
 - The conceit turns on a triple play: Fabricius as **Ganymede** (the beautiful youth snatched to heaven by *Jove's Eagle* to serve the gods) "pasturing Frisian oxen" — i.e. wasted as a rural pastor instead of raised to astronomy; and the biblical **David** "adopted from the sheep into the court on account of his music" (1 Samuel 16). *Hic David Ganymedem habet ascendentem* puns on the astrological **ascendant**: this David "has Ganymede [= Aquarius, the water-bearer] rising" — both a horoscopic figure and the wish that he rise to the heavens. The wordplay is preserved, not flattened.
 - *Sed quisque suos patimur manes* quotes **Virgil, *Aeneid* VI.743** ("but each of us suffers his own shade") — "each must endure his own appointed lot."
- **The political news.**
 - *Episcopus Coloniensis* = the **Elector-Archbishop of Cologne**, **Ernst of Bavaria**, travelling "as if private" to the Emperor to press, in the Pope's name, the **election of a King of the Romans** (the contested Habsburg succession question).
 - *nuncius Belgicus … exercitus Hispanicus* = news from the **Low Countries**, where the Spanish army of the Eighty Years' War had returned; *redit Turca* = the renewed **Ottoman** threat of the Long Turkish War. *Domine, serva nos, perimus* echoes **Matthew 8:25** (the disciples in the storm) — "Lord, save us, we perish."
 - *Episcopus Saltzburgensis* = the **Prince-Archbishop of Salzburg**, **Wolf Dietrich von Raitenau**, whose favour toward Tycho Rollenhagen congratulates; *ad umbilicum deducas* = "bring [your labours] to completion" (Horace's *ad umbilicum*, the roller-end of a book-scroll).
- **The Heinrich Julius / astrology dispute.**
 - *Henricus Iulius* = **Heinrich Julius, Duke of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel** (1564–1613), then a leading figure at the imperial court. A **prognostic (*prognosticum*)** of a future war-victory was being attributed to him; Rollenhagen denies being its source.
 - *Garcaeus* = **Johannes Garcaeus the Younger** (1530–1574), Lutheran theologian and astrological author, named as the supposed authority for the war-prophecy.
 - *Doctor Megabacchus, Rothius* = two further parties to the rumour, not securely identifiable (see Confidence).
 - *Sed fertur equis auriga, nec audit currus habenas* quotes **Virgil, *Georgics* I.514** ("the charioteer is swept along by his horses, and the car heeds not the reins") — the runaway-chariot image for Heinrich Julius's martial ardour.
- **The Hofmann succession.** *de vocando Theologo in locum Hofmanni* = the consultation over **calling a theologian to replace Hofmann** — i.e. **Daniel Hofmann** (the Helmstedt theologian deposed in the "Hofmann controversy," 1598–1601), in whose vacated place Rollenhagen expects to help, while privately advancing Tycho's interests with the Emperor.
- **Epistolary formulae.** *S.* = *salutem*; *Bene et quam diutissime vale* → "Fare well, and for the longest time"; subscription *Tuae Gen[erosae] N[obilitati] addictiss[imus]* → "Most devoted to Your Generous Nobility."
- **What this is.** A geniture (nativity) record appended after the letter's close — a piece of raw astrological data, not epistolary prose: birth date, time, and place for a named prince, together with a technical complaint about how a published source mishandled that time.
- **The subject.** Heinrich Julius, Duke of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel and Prince-Bishop of Halberstadt, a major figure at the imperial court and a patron with scientific interests. Dates, hour, and place are preserved here exactly as given in the source, per instruction, without correction; note for the record that standard modern reference works generally give his birth as 15 (not 14) October 1564, so the day here may reflect either an authentic variant tradition, an error already present in Rollenhagen's source, or a transcription slip — flagged as a crux rather than silently harmonised.
- **The sender and his own astrological standing.** Georg Rollenhagen (1542–1609), rector of the Magdeburg Gymnasium from 1575 and author of the celebrated didactic beast-epic *Froschmeuseler*, was also himself a practising astrological author — his 1583 lectures on calendar-practice and astrology were later absorbed into David Origanus's *Ephemerides* [Oestmann, *Rantzau und die Astrologie* (2004)]. This explains why Rollenhagen is competent to adjudicate a technical dispute over Garcaeus's geniture-correction method, not merely relaying it. Elsewhere in the correspondence Rollenhagen is known to have fed Tycho inside information from the imperial court via his brother-in-law Caspar Lehmann, and to have first alerted Tycho to Ursus's plagiarism [Christianson, *On Tycho's Island* (2000)].
- **Johannes Garcaeus and the "Trutina Hermetis."** Johannes Garcaeus (1530–1574), author of *Astrologiae methodus* (Basel, 1570), a widely used printed collection of nativities/genitures [Oestmann, *Rantzau und die Astrologie*, citing a Garcaeus volume from the Breitenburg library]. The "Trutina Hermetis" ("Balance/Scale of Hermes") is a standard astrological rectification technique, drawn from the pseudo-Ptolemaic *Centiloquium* ("Fructus," aphorism 51): the Moon's zodiacal position at the moment of conception should match the ascendant at birth (or its opposite sign), and the technique is used to correct or verify an uncertain birth time [Oestmann, *Rantzau und die Astrologie*, quoting the rule in German translation]. Rollenhagen's charge is that Garcaeus misapplied this rule ("falsissimam... trutinam") and thereby corrupted Heinrich Julius's recorded birth hour.
- **Why this matters.** This is a rare glimpse of Tycho's circle doing hands-on astrological source-criticism — checking a published prince's geniture against the technical rectification method that was supposed to validate it, and finding the published source wanting.

documents.abstract: Complains of an unreceived letter and presses Meier for overdue repayment of 10,000 thalers and interest, noting the sum has been pledged to others and kinsman Eske Bille has given assurances.
documents.incipit: MEINE freundtwillige dienste zuvorn. Ehrnuester, achtpar, lieber herr rentmaister, …

text.original:
DEM EHRNUESTEN VND ACHTPARN ANDRESS MEIERN, FÜRSTLICHEM MECKLENBURGISCHEN RENTMEISTERN, MEINEM BESONDERN GUTEN FREUNDT. WISSMAR.

MEINE freundtwillige dienste zuvorn. Ehrnuester, achtpar, lieber herr rentmaister, insonders gueter freundt. Ewer schreibent von Wißmar, den 18. maij dieses lauffenden jhars datiert, ist mir wohl behendiget, aber das vorige, wovon ihr meldet, so wegen der fürgewandten verhindernuß dero 10000 thaller hauptsummen vnd zinsen erlegung ahn mich ergangen sein soll, hab ich bis dato nitt gesehen, geschweig die darinnen angezogene vrsacchen für erheblich ahnnehmen können. Vnd seitenmahl obgedachte summa zu rechter zeit vnsers hieruber auffgerichteten contracts auffgekündiget, vnd ihr auch (wie dan ahn ihm selbs pillich) dieselbigen ahngenohmen, hab ich die anderen leutten zugesagt vnd versprocchen, dan mir ohnedas vnleidlich, die zinse nitt zu rechter vnd gepüerlicher zeit zue entpfhangen, wie dan auch dieselbige von Rostogk anhero zu bringen kain mittel noch rhat weiß. Zu deme auch hatt mein blutsverwanter Esche Bilde meinentwegen ain thail deßelbigen geldes anderen leutten versprocchen, vnd wollen noch können ewerer ex postfacto angereugter vrsacchen halben vnser wort nitt wiedernehmen. Gelanget derowegen ahn euch mein abermähliges, ernstliches pitten vnd begehren, das ihr nochmahls dazu thuen wollen, damit mir ohne ainigen weittern verzugk zum allerlengsten innerhalb nechstkünfftigen s. Joannis thagk, wie ihr offtgedachtem Esche Bilden zuegeschrieben, mehrgedachte hauptsumma sampt dem interesse richtich erlegt werde.

Hieran thuet ihr was der pilligkait vnd meiner aigentlichen resolution gemeß, jhm fal ihr nit wollet, das ich die bürgen in schaden zue bringen, vnd bej jhr: f: g: hertzogk Vldricchen, meinem gnedichsten fürsten vnd herren, micch derentwegen zue beklagen verursaccht vnd genotdrenget werde.

Söllichs hinwiederumb auff zu tragendem fall vmb euch vnd die ewerige zu verschülden, bin ich iederzeit willig vnd geflißen. Euch hiemit göttlicher almacht entpfhelendt.

Datum Prag den 27. maij a:o 1601.
E: dienst- vnd freundtwilliger
Tycho Brahe
egenhn.
text.english:
**To the honourable and worshipful Andreas Meier, princely Mecklenburg rent-master, my especial good friend. Wismar.**

My friend-willing services beforehand. Honourable, worshipful, dear Lord rent-master, especial good friend: your letter from Wismar, dated the 18th of May of this current year, has duly been handed to me; but the earlier one, of which you make mention — which is said to have come to me concerning the alleged hindrance to paying out those 10,000 thalers of principal sum and interest — I have to this day not seen, much less been able to accept the reasons cited therein as weighty. And seeing that the above-mentioned sum was called in at the proper time of our contract drawn up over it, and that you too (as is indeed only fair in itself) accepted the same, I have pledged and promised it to other people; for it is in any case intolerable to me not to receive the interest at the proper and due time, just as I also know neither means nor counsel for bringing the same hither from Rostock. To this is added that my blood-relative Eske Bille has, on my behalf, promised a part of that same money to other people, and we neither will nor can take back our word on account of the reasons you have alleged after the fact. There comes to you, therefore, my renewed and earnest request and demand, that you will once more see to it that, without any further delay, at the very latest within the coming St. John's Day — as you wrote to the oft-mentioned Eske Bille — the said principal sum together with the interest be duly paid out to me.

In this you do what accords with fairness and with my actual resolve, if you would not have me caused and constrained to bring the sureties into loss, and on that account to lodge a complaint with His Princely Grace Duke Ulrich, my most gracious Prince and Lord.

To deserve this in return at your hands, should occasion arise, on behalf of you and yours, I am at all times willing and assiduous. Herewith commending you to divine omnipotence.

Given at Prague, the 27th of May, in the year 1601.
Your service- and friend-willing
Tycho Brahe
[in his] own hand.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender & context.** **Tycho Brahe** at **Prague**, five months before his death. This is the **earlier** of the two surviving Tycho→Meier letters on the Mecklenburg loan: 27 May 1601 (this) → 18 July 1601 (brahe-t_16010718001). Read together with Duke Ulrich's own letter to Meier of 9 August 1601 (brahe-t_16010809001), the three documents track the increasingly pressed recovery of a **10,000-thaler loan** (principal + interest) that the ducal house of Mecklenburg owed Tycho.
- **Recipient.** **Andreas Meier**, ducal Mecklenburg **rent-master** at **Wismar** (see brahe-t_16010718001 apparatus). Tycho has received Meier's letter of 18 May but *not* an earlier one Meier claims to have sent pleading a "hindrance" to payment — and rejects the excuse in any case.
- **Persons named.**
 - *mein Blutsverwandter Esche Bilde* = **Eske Bille**, a Danish nobleman and **kinsman of Tycho** acting as his financial agent in the matter; he has already re-promised part of the money to third parties, so the word given cannot be retracted. (In the 9 August ducal letter, Eske Bille has come from Denmark and "lies at Rostock" to collect.)
 - *J. F. G. Herzog Ulrich* = **Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg(-Güstrow)**, the prince to whom Tycho threatens to complain if payment fails.
- **Places.** *Wismar*; *Rostock* (whence Tycho sees no way to have the interest conveyed); *Prague*.
- **The deadline.** *nechstkünftiger S. Joannis Tag* = the **coming St. John's Day (24 June 1601)** — the term Meier had himself named to Eske Bille; the alternative Tycho holds over him is proceeding against the *Bürgen* (sureties).
- **Formulae & abbreviations.** Burgher register (*ehrnvest und achtbar*). Subscription *E: dienst- vnd freundtwilliger* = *Euer [Ehren] dienst- und freundwilliger*; *egenhn.* = *eigenhändig* ("in his own hand," autograph attestation — the German counterpart of *manu propria*).
- **Calendar.** Dateline *den 27. Maij a:o 1601 stylo novo* — explicitly **New Style**; the internal *S. Joannis Tag* is read consistently with the document's stated usage. Reproduced, not converted.
- **Correction.** Removed 'stylo nouo' from the closing dateline, and the corresponding 'New Style' from the translation; Dreyer's print (TBOO XIV p.222) has no such phrase in the letter's own closing line.
