documents.abstract: Müller acknowledges completing one year of imperial-commanded service with Tycho at Prague and records his petition to the Emperor for an honorarium covering expenses and trouble.
documents.incipit: JCH Iohannes Muller, churfurstlicher Brandenburgischer mathematicus, bekenne mitt dieser …

text.original:
JCH Iohannes Muller, churfurstlicher Brandenburgischer mathematicus, bekenne mitt dieser meiner eigenen handt, das vff der römischen keyß: m:statt, vnsers allergnedigsten herrn, allergnedigst begehren vnndt schreiben an den churfursten zu Brandenburgk, meinen gnedigsten herrn, jch vff ein jahrlang hieher nach Prag abgefoedert worden, das ich jhr maiestet zu allergnedigsten gefallen bei den edlen vnndt wohlgebornen herrn Tycho Brahen vff Knudtstrup vnndt Vraniburgk mich aufhaltten vnndt allda, was er in nahmen j: m: mier befehlen werde, gehorsamlich vorrichten soltte, welchem ich denn in allervnterthenigsten gehorsam nachkommen. Als aber nun die zeitt verfloßen, vnd jch vber dieselb (weil ich nicht lenger verlaub gehabt) mich nicht hab seumen dorffen, so habe an die hochermeltte römische k: maiestett ich vnterthenigst suppliciret, das dieselben mich mitt einer vorehrung fur meine aufgewandte vnkosten vnndt gehabte mühe allergnedigst bedencken woltten, vnndt wiewohl i: m: am ersten hierin jhe kein bedencken gemacht, sondern dem Francken befohlen, meine supplication dem Heiden zu lieffern, das er j: m: daran erinnern soltte, so woltte j: m: allergnedigst geruhen mier eine vorehrung zustellen zulaßen, so ist doch solchs baldt hernacher, vieleicht durch anderer angeben, mir wieder abgeschlagen worden. Auf das ich aber nicht ledig zu hauß ziehen möchte, vnndt es bei meiner gnedigsten herrschafft vnndt andern nicht das ansehen hette, als wan ich vmbsonst ausgewehsen wehr, so hatt der herr Tycho neben der kost vnndt herbergk, weil er mich vnndt mein weib die gantze zeitt vber vnterhaltten, mier 200 f: am gelde zugestellet, die ich dan auch zu meinen handen wohl empfangen, vnndt thue auch krafft dieses brieffs ermeltten herrn Tychonem vollstendig quittiren. Deßen zu mehrer vhrkundt habe ich diesen brieff mitt eigner handt geschrieben vnndt mitt meinem gewöhnlichen petzschafft besiegeltt.

Geschehen zu Prag den 29. maij a:o 1601.
Johannes Muller
manu pp:.
text.english:
I, Johannes Müller, Electoral Brandenburg mathematician, acknowledge with this my own hand, that — upon the Roman Imperial Majesty's, our most gracious lord's, most gracious desire and letter to the Elector of Brandenburg, my most gracious lord — I was summoned hither to Prague for [the space of] a year, [so] that I should, to His Majesty's most gracious pleasure, stay with the noble and well-born lord Tycho Brahe of Knudstrup and Uraniborg, and there obediently perform what he should command me in His Majesty's name; which I then complied with, in most submissive obedience. But now, the time having elapsed, and [I] not being permitted to delay beyond it (since I had no longer leave), I most humbly petitioned the highly-mentioned Roman Imperial Majesty that the same would most graciously bethink me of an honorarium for my expended costs and the trouble I had had; and although His Majesty at first made no objection at all herein, but commanded "the Franck" to deliver my supplication to "the Heyden," that he should remind His Majesty thereof, [and] that His Majesty would most graciously deign to have an honorarium delivered to me — yet such was, soon afterward (perhaps by others' instigation), again refused me. But so that I might not travel home empty[-handed], and that it should not have the appearance, with my most gracious lordship [the Elector] and with others, as though I had been [away] for nothing, the lord Tycho — besides board and lodging, since he maintained me and my wife the whole time over — delivered to me 200 florins in money, which I have then also well received into my hands; and I do also, by force of this letter, fully quit the said lord Tycho. In further witness whereof I have written this letter with my own hand, and sealed [it] with my usual seal.

Done at Prague, the 29th of May, in the year 1601.
Johannes Müller,
with his own hand.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender — the "Brandenburg mathematician Müller."** This resolves the thread of brahe-t_16000322003: **Johannes Müller, Electoral Brandenburg mathematician**, summoned (at the Emperor's request to the Elector of Brandenburg) to **Prague for a year** to serve Tycho "in the Emperor's name." His **quittance** (receipt-and-release) on departure, 29 May 1601.
- **Content.** Müller's year up, he petitioned **Rudolf II** for an *honorarium* (*Verehrung*) for his costs and trouble; though the Emperor initially ordered it (commanding "**the Franck**" to pass the supplication to "**the Heyden**" to remind him), the grant was "soon afterward, perhaps by others' instigation, again refused." So that he should not go home empty-handed and seem to have served "for nothing," **Tycho himself paid him 200 florins** (besides a year's board and lodging for Müller and his wife). Müller fully quits Tycho. A candid window onto the Rudolfine court's failure to fund even its own commissions — leaving Tycho to pay out of pocket.
- ***"dem Francken … dem Heiden"*** — **flagged**: two court officials named only by surname, *Franck* and *Hayd/Heyden*, through whom the supplication was to pass; not securely re-identified. Rendered "the Franck" / "the Heyden."
- ***200 f.*** = 200 florins (Gulden). *manu pp.* = *manu propria*.
- **Calendar.** *Prag den 29. maij a:o 1601* = **29 May 1601**; Prague (imperial) = **New Style**. Header agrees with the label.

documents.abstract: Presses again for repayment of 10,000 thalers and interest from the young Mecklenburg dukes, noting Duke Ulrich's prior order to rent-master Meier at Easter has gone unfulfilled.
documents.incipit: DURCHLÄUCHTIGSTER hochgeborner fürst, gnedichster herr. E: Fürstl: Gnaden sein meine …

text.original:
DEM DURCHLAUCHTIGSTEN HOCHGEBORNEN FURSTEN VND HERRN, HERRN VLDARICH, HERTZOGEN ZU MECHELLENBURGK, FURSTEN ZU WENDEN, GRAFFEN ZU SCHWERIN, DER LANDE ROSTOCH VNDT STARGARDEN HERRN, MEINEM GNEDIGSTEN FURSTEN VNDDT HERRN.

DURCHLÄUCHTIGSTER hochgeborner fürst, gnedichster herr. E: Fürstl: Gnaden sein meine vnterthenigste gantzwillige dienste iederzeit höchstes fleißes bevor. Vndt mag deroselben abermahl auß hochdrengenden vndt erheblichen vrsachen vnterthenigst nit pergen, wie dan auch E: F: Gnaden zweiffelsohn sich nochmahls gnedigst werden wißen zu entsinnen, daß die summa von 10000 thaller hauptstuel sampt dem interesse, so der jungen herschafft zue Mechelburgk von mir gehorsambst vndt guttwillig vorstreckt, ich wegen meiner sonderbaren notturfft vndt ahnligens zu rechter zeit vnsers hierumb auffgerichteten contracts auffgekundiget. Worein dan Ewer F: G: (in maßen es der pilligkait gemeß) so paldt solchs deroselben gehorsambst vorgetragen, gahr kein bedencken gehabt, sondern dero rentmeistern Andreas Meiern ahn stundt die gnedigste ahnordenung gethan, obgemelte summam vndt interesse gegen vergangenen ostern ohne ainigen verzuegk inhabe[r]n meines brieffes richtig wiederumb zueerstatten. Worauff auch (seitemahl sollichs geldt von Rostoch gehn Prag zue bekommen mir bißanhero fast beschwerlich gefallen) ich eß zue meinem vndt den meinigen besten vndt frommen andern leutten alhie, zum theil auch mein blutsverwandter Esche Bilde anderßwo meinentwegen zuegesagt vndt versprochen.

Nun aber wirdt mir von gedachtem E: F: G: rentmeistern wieder meinen verhoffen zuegeschrieben, daß anderer außgeben halben sollichs geldt noch nicht erleget vndt bezahlt werden könne, welchs zwar mir, weiln E: F: G: gnedigster zuesag zufolge ich gegen vergangenen ostern mich mit andern deßwegen eingelaßen, schmertzlich vndt frembd vorkhumpt.

Gelanget derowegen ahn E: F: G: mein vnterthenigste gantz fleißige pitt, E: F: G: wollen nit gescheen laßen, daß mihr ahn meinem biß dato wohlhergebrachten nahmen etwaß abgehen, vndt ich wieder mein wort handeln muße, sondern der gnedigsten befehlich thuen, daß mir zum allerlengster innerhalb nechstkunfftigen s: Johannis tagk mehrgedachtes geldt ohne fernere verzugerung gefollget werden muege.

Hirahn erzaigen E: F: G: mir ein große gnadt, vndt ich binß meiner geringfügigen personen nach iederzeit in vnterthenigster danckparkeit zue erkennen gantzwillig vndt geflißen. Dieselben hiemit sampt dero vielgeliepter gemahlin zu langwahrender gluchklicher regierung göttlicher almacht gehorsambst vndt getreulich entpfhelendt.

Datum Prag den 4 junij a:o 1601.
Ewer Furst: Gnaden vnterthenigster gantzwilliger
Tycho Brahe
manu pprj:
text.english:
**To the most serene, high-born Prince and Lord, Lord Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg, Prince of the Wends, Count of Schwerin, Lord of the lands of Rostock and Stargard, my most gracious Prince and Lord.**

Most serene, high-born Prince, most gracious Lord. To Your Princely Grace [be] my most humble, wholly willing services at all times, with the utmost diligence, beforehand. And I cannot, out of highly pressing and weighty causes, once again most humbly conceal from the same — as also Your Princely Grace will doubtless once more graciously be able to recall — that the sum of 10,000 thalers of principal, together with the interest, which was obediently and willingly advanced by me to the young lordship of Mecklenburg, I called in, on account of my special need and concern, at the proper time of our contract drawn up over this matter. Wherein Your Princely Grace (as accords with fairness), as soon as it was obediently laid before the same, had no hesitation at all, but at once gave to your rent-master Andreas Meier the most gracious order to repay duly the aforesaid sum and interest by the past Easter, without any delay, to the holder of my bond. Whereupon, too (since to bring such money from Rostock to Prague has hitherto fallen out quite burdensome for me), I have pledged and promised it — for my own and my people's best and benefit — to other people here, and in part also my blood-relative Eske Bille has, on my behalf, pledged and promised [it] elsewhere.

But now I am written to by Your Princely Grace's said rent-master, contrary to my expectation, that on account of other expenditures such money cannot yet be laid out and paid — which indeed comes to me as painful and strange, since, in accordance with Your Princely Grace's most gracious promise, I had by the past Easter committed myself to others on that account.

There comes therefore to Your Princely Grace my most humble, wholly diligent request, that Your Princely Grace will not let it happen that anything be lost to my hitherto well-established name [credit], and that I must act against my word, but [will] give the most gracious command that, at the very latest within the coming St. John's Day, the oft-mentioned money may be paid over to me without further delay.

In this Your Princely Grace shows me a great favour, and I am, according to my humble person, at all times wholly willing and zealous to acknowledge it in most humble gratitude. Herewith commending the same, together with your much-beloved consort, to the protection of Almighty God for a long-lasting and happy reign, obediently and faithfully.

Given at Prague, the 4th of June, in the year 1601.
Your Princely Grace's most humble, wholly willing
Tycho Brahe,
with his own hand.

documents.apparatus:
- **Recipient.** **Ulrich III, Duke of Mecklenburg-Güstrow** (1527–1603), with his full titulature reproduced (*Duke of Mecklenburg, Prince of the Wends, Count of Schwerin, Lord of the lands of Rostock and Stargard*) — exactly as in Tycho's invitation letter to the same Duke of 15 April 1601 (brahe-t_16010415003). The MS is the **original dispatched letter** (*Originalbrev*), filed at Schwerin under the apt rubric *Debita passiva principum* — "the passive debts [debts owed] of the princes."
- **Position in the debt thread.** This is Tycho's **direct personal appeal to the Duke** in the 10,000-thaler affair, written from Prague just under five months before his death. It sits between the appeal-to-the-go-betweens (Tycho→Bording, 12 April, brahe-t_16010412001; Tycho→rent-master Meier, 27 May, brahe-t_16010527001) and the later pressing of Meier (18 July, brahe-t_16010718001) and the ducal replies (24 July, brahe-t_16010724001; Ulrich→Meier, 9 August, brahe-t_16010809001).
- **The transaction.** Tycho had **advanced 10,000 thalers of principal** (*Hauptstuhl*) plus interest to the *junge Herrschaft zu Mecklenburg* — the **young lordship/junior dukes of Mecklenburg** — and had lawfully called it in at the contract term. Duke Ulrich had ordered his **rent-master Andreas Meier** (at Wismar) to repay it *by the past Easter* to the bearer of Tycho's bond. Relying on that promise, Tycho had **re-pledged the money onward** to creditors at Prague, and his kinsman **Eske Bille** (*Esche Bilde*) had likewise re-promised part of it elsewhere — so the rent-master's now pleading "other expenditures" threatens Tycho's word and credit (*mein wohlhergebrachter Name*).
- **The deadline.** *innerhalb nechstkünfftigen S. Johannis Tag* — within the coming **St. John's Day, 24 June 1601** — the same term named in the 27 May letter to Meier. The remittance difficulty *von Rostock gen Prag* (getting Baltic money to Bohemia) is the recurring practical snag of the whole affair.
- **Persons named.** Duke Ulrich III of Mecklenburg; the *junge Herrschaft* (junior dukes of Mecklenburg); **Andreas Meier**, ducal rent-master at Wismar; **Eske Bille**, Tycho's Danish kinsman and financial agent. The Duke's *vielgeliebte Gemahlin* ("much-beloved consort") is **Anna of Pomerania-Wolgast**, Ulrich's second wife (m. 1588) — named cautiously, not asserted from the text.
- **Register & orthography.** Deferential chancery Early New High German in the subject's first person to a prince: *E: F: G:* (*Euer Fürstliche Gnaden*, "Your Princely Grace") throughout; period spellings (*vndt, pitt, pilligkait, gnedigst, vorstreckt, zueerstatten*). Subscription *manu propria* (*manu pprj:*) marks the autograph. One slip in the witness rubric — *E: E: G:* for *E: F: G:* — is the clerk's, not significant.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *den 4 Junij a:o 1601* at Prague; **New Style**, per Tycho's imperial-service usage. Reproduced, not converted.
- **Correction.** Latin: 'E: E: G:' corrected to 'E: F: G:' per Dreyer, Opera Omnia XIV, p. 224.

documents.abstract: Inquires whether David Fabricius arrived safely after departing with fears about the dangers of the journey, and commends himself as a friend.
documents.incipit: QUANQUAM apud D. DAVIDEM FABRICIUM ad nobiliss. Magam T. scripserim de rebus omnibus, …

text.original:
NOBILISSIMO STRENUO ET MAGNIFICO VIRO TYCHONI BRAHEN DANO, SACRAe CÆS. MATHEMATICO, IMO ET FAUTORI SUO MULTIS NOMINIBUS COLENDISSIMO.
PRAGA.
Εὖ ζῆν καὶ εὖ πράττειν.

QUANQUAM apud D. DAVIDEM FABRICIUM ad nobiliss. Magam T. scripserim de rebus omnibus, Nobiliss. atque Magce vir, Domine multis nominibus colende, quas quidem literas meas unâ cum earundem latore, FABRICIO nostro, te accepisse et vidisse non dubito, facere tamen non potui, quin nobiliss. Magam T. hac schedula inviserem, sciscitaturus saltem, num dictus FABRICIUS noster salvus atque incolumis ad vos pervenerit. Multa enim metuebat atque, ut mihi videbatur, sibi persuadebat, quare non sine periculo hoc iter perficere posset. Veruntamen omnia in DEI praepotentis manu posita esse firmiter credo, sic ut eundem FABRICIUM, nisi DEO aliter visum fuerit, incolumem omnino ac salvum huc reversurum plane persuasum habeam. Porro nobiliss. Magam T. rogatam velim, uti me sibi commendatum et persuasum plane habeat, me ex eorum esse numero, qui nobiliss. Magam T. modis omnibus salvam optet atque incolumem, eiusque honoribus faveat quam maxume.

Caeterum quid Sacrae Caes. Matis Legatus et Consiliarius praecipuus D. HANNIWALT hîc rerum agat, quamque honorifice, ne dicam magnifice, ab Illri et generoso principe meo ENNONE, Orient. Frisiae Comite, exceptus sit, et quae porro Sacrae Caes. Mati ab Illri Cels. eius exspectanda sint officia atque servitia, meum non est perscribere, cum tempus ipsum atque exitus reipsa comprobatura sint, quali affectu Illris Dominus noster erga Sacratiss. Caes. Matem sit praeditus, quam ut DEUS opt. max. unâ cum nobiliss. Maga T. diutissime servet, ex animo precor. Ac si forsan occasio fuerit, ut Sacrae Caes. Mati mea quamvis humilia servitia commendare possis, quaeso studiorum, si non eorundem, attamen communium memor esto.

Haec scripsi αὐτοσχεδίως et quasi per satyram, propterea quod propter praesentiam praefati Caes. Matis Legati, qui pridie huc appulit, plusculis eram occupatus negocijs. Quare et festinationi et lituris ignosces, tum FABRICIO nostro hasce inclusas literas cum salute uberrima tradere haud dedigneris. Utinam vero sit aliquid, in quo nobiliss. Magae T. vicissim gratificari possim, neque enim labori, vigilijs, studijs, sumptui parcerem.

Vale vir nobiliss. atque Magce.
Scripta ex arce Auricana Frisiae Orientalis pridie Eidus Iunij stilo veteri Anno postremi temporis Ch. 1601.
Nobiliss. Magae T.
addictiss.
EBERARTUS SCHELE,
Orient. Frisiae Secret.


*[Postscript — restored from Dreyer, Opera Omnia VIII, p. 422; dropped by the working transcription. See Apparatus.]*
Quae hoc ipso die de occupatione propugnaculi ante Bergam ex Haga Comitis allata sunt nova, cum et incerta adhuc sint nec vobis ignota diu eße poßint, lubens praetereo.
text.english:
**To the most noble, valiant and magnificent man Tycho Brahe the Dane, mathematician of the Sacred Imperial [Majesty], nay also his patron most-to-be-revered on many accounts. Prague.**
*To live well and to fare well.* [Greek]

Although I wrote to your most noble Magnificence about all matters by way of Master David Fabricius — which letter of mine, together with its bearer, our Fabricius, I do not doubt you have received and read — yet I could not but call upon your most noble Magnificence with this note, [meaning] at least to inquire whether the said our Fabricius has reached you safe and unharmed. For he feared many things, and, as it seemed to me, persuaded himself that he could not complete this journey without danger. Nevertheless I firmly believe all things are placed in the hand of God almighty, so that I hold it plainly persuaded that the same Fabricius — unless it shall have seemed otherwise to God — will return here wholly unharmed and safe. Further, I would have your most noble Magnificence asked, to hold me commended, and be plainly persuaded that I am of the number of those who wish your most noble Magnificence safe and unharmed in every way, and who favour your honours as much as may be.

For the rest, what the Sacred Imperial Majesty's Legate and chief Councillor, Master Hannewald, transacts here, and how honourably — not to say magnificently — he has been received by my illustrious and generous prince Enno, Count of East Frisia, and what services and duties are further to be expected by the Sacred Imperial Majesty from His Illustrious Highness, it is not mine to write out; for time itself and the outcome will prove in fact with what affection our Illustrious Lord is disposed toward the most Sacred Imperial Majesty — whom, together with your most noble Magnificence, may God, best and greatest, preserve for the longest time, I pray from my heart. And if perhaps there be occasion that you can commend my services, however humble, to the Sacred Imperial Majesty, I pray you, be mindful of our studies — if not the same, yet shared.

These [lines] I have written offhand and as it were in a medley, because, on account of the presence of the aforesaid Imperial Legate (who landed here yesterday), I was occupied with rather many affairs. Wherefore you will pardon both the haste and the blottings; and you will not disdain to deliver to our Fabricius these enclosed letters, with most abundant greeting. Would, in truth, that there were anything in which I might in turn oblige your most noble Magnificence — for I would spare neither labour, nor vigils, nor studies, nor expense.

Farewell, most noble and magnificent man.
Written from the castle of Aurich in East Frisia, the day before the Ides of June, Old Style, in the year of the last age of Christ 1601.
Most devoted to your most noble Magnificence,
Eberhard Schele,
Secretary of East Frisia.


*[Postscript:]* The news that have been brought this very day from The Hague concerning the seizure of the fort before Bergen — since they are still uncertain, and cannot long be unknown to you — I gladly pass over.

documents.apparatus:
- **Direction & sender.** An **inbound** letter **to** Tycho at Prague. **Eberhard Schele**, *Secretarius* of **East Frisia** (Ostfriesland), writing from the comital seat at **Aurich**.
- **The David Fabricius thread (connective tissue).** The note's chief purpose is anxious solicitude over **David Fabricius** (1564–1617), the Frisian pastor-astronomer, who was **travelling to visit Tycho** carrying Schele's fuller letter — and who, Schele reports, dreaded the journey as dangerous. This is the **arrival half** of the episode whose departure half Georg Rollenhagen describes (brahe-t_16010515001, 15 May 1601: Fabricius "had turned aside to me out of his journey, which he had set toward you"). Schele asks Tycho both to confirm Fabricius's safe arrival and to hand Fabricius the *enclosed letters*.
- **Persons named.**
 - *D. David Fabricius* = **David Fabricius**, the courier and the object of Schele's concern.
 - *D. Hanniwalt* = **Andreas Hannewald (Hanniwald)**, secretary/councillor of Rudolf II, here as **imperial legate** to East Frisia, "landed yesterday" — his visit is the diplomatic backdrop and the reason for Schele's haste.
 - *Illustris princeps meus Enno, Orientalis Frisiae Comes* = **Enno III, Count of East Frisia** (1563–1625), Schele's sovereign, host to the imperial legate.
 - *Sacra Caesarea Maiestas* = **Emperor Rudolf II**, to whom Schele hopes Tycho may commend his "humble services."
- **Greek (transcribed + glossed, this chapter's convention).** The address bears the salutation-motto *Εὖ ζῆν καὶ εὖ πράττειν* — "**to live well and to fare well**" (the classical good-wish). In the body, *αὐτοσχεδίως* = "offhand, extempore"; the Latin idiom *per satyram* (= *per saturam*) = "in a medley / pell-mell."
- **Place.** *arx Auricana Frisiae Orientalis* = the castle of **Aurich**, East Frisia.
- **Epistolary formulae.** *Vale* → "Farewell"; subscription *Nobiliss. Magae T. addictiss.* = "Most devoted to your most noble Magnificence."
- **Calendar (this chapter's convention — explicit Old Style).** Dateline *pridie Eidus [Idus] Iunij **stilo veteri*** = "the day before the Ides of June, **Old Style**" = **12 June** (the Ides of June = the 13th). East Frisia, a Reformed/Lutheran territory, kept the **Julian** calendar; Schele marks it expressly *stilo veteri* — to be contrasted with the New-Style Prague dating of Tycho's imperial correspondence. The flourish *Anno postremi temporis Ch[risti] 1601* ("in the year of the last age of Christ 1601") is an eschatological commonplace, reproduced. Not converted.

- **§1 Dreyer collation.** News-postscript (Hague reports of the seizure of a fort before Bergen-op-Zoom), restored from Dreyer VIII p.422 (after "Eberartus SCHELE, Orient. Frisiae Secret."; dropped by the working transcription).
- **Correction.** Restored the word-space in the closing dateline: Dreyer prints "Auricana Frisiae" as two words (TBOO VIII p.422), not the glued "AuricanaFrisiae" of the prior transcription.

documents.abstract: Confirms the 10,000 thalers owed to Tycho fell due at Easter, explains the rent-master's failure to secure promised funds at the last hour, and assures Eske Bille repayment will be arranged.
documents.incipit: Vlrich etc.

text.original:
AN ESSKE BILDEN ZU KOPENHAGEN

Vlrich etc.

VNSERN gunstigen grues zuuor. Ehrnuester lieber besonder. Wir seind von dem erbarn Vnser cammerer vnd lieben getrewen Jochim von Stralendorff berichtet worden, was jhr wegen der 10000 thaler, damit Vnsere vnmundjge vettern vnd pflegesohne, die junge hertzogen zu Meckelnburgk, dem auch ernuesten Vnsern lieben besondern Tycho Brahen verhafft, vnd welche so auf negst verschienen ostern betagt gewesen, an jhn gelanget. Nun wißen Wir Vns dieser schuldtfurderung vnd das auf negst verschienen ostern das geldt hette erlegt werden sollen, woll zuerjnnern, haben auch von deßwegen bereits vorlengst hochermelter Vnserer pflegesohne rentmeister Andreas Meyern verwarnet, darzu verdacht zusein, das er auf rechte gesetzte zeit zur zahlung gelangen konte, jnmaßen Vns dan auch ferner nicht vnbewust ist, das er zu dero notturfft geldt besprochen, so jhm auch gegen die negstverschienen ostern gewisse zugesaget, aber auf die letzte stunde jhm allererst wieder ein bloßen geschlagen worden, dahero es sich dan verursachet, das er seines teils auf bestimbte zeit zu der versprochenen zahlung nicht gelangen können. Jedoch ist er noch in fleißiger bemuhung, das er mit dem ehisten geldt zuwege bringen muge, vnd verhoffen Wir numehr auch teglich von jhm diese gute erklerung, das er werde rath geschaffet haben. Vnd weill die sachen itzterzeltermaßen geschaffen, alß gesinnen Wir demnach an euch hiemit gantz gnediglich, jhr wollet euch wegen gedachtes Tycho Brahen noch eine kleine vnd geringe zeit gedulden, so seindt Wir des gnedigen erbietens, die versehung zuthun, das alßdan mit dem schleunigsten die wirckliche bezahlung erfolgen soll, dan Wir auf itzo mehrgedachten rentmeister derentwegen von newen wiederumb erjnnerung vnd auch starcken beuehll gethan. Habens euch immittelst zu gnediger erklerung nicht verhalten wollen, vnd Wir seind euch mit gnaden vnd allen gutten woll gewogen.

Datum Dobbran den 17. junij a:o 1601.
text.english:
**To Eske Bille at Copenhagen.**

Ulrich, etc.

Our favourable greeting beforehand. Honourable, dear, and especial [friend]. We have been informed by the honourable Our chamberlain and dear faithful [servant] Joachim von Stralendorff of what you have conveyed to him regarding the 10,000 thaler, with which Our minor cousins and foster-sons, the young Dukes of Mecklenburg, are indebted to the likewise-honourable Our dear and especial [friend] Tycho Brahe, and which fell due at the recently-past Easter. Now, We well remember this debt-claim, and that the money should have been paid at the recently-past Easter; and We have therefore already long since warned the rent-master of Our highly-mentioned foster-sons, Andreas Meyer, to be intent thereon, that he might come to the payment at the rightly-set time — just as it is also not further unknown to Us that he bespoke money for that need, which was also certainly promised him toward the recently-past Easter, but at the last hour was once again struck a blank; whence it then came about that he, for his part, could not come to the promised payment at the appointed time. However, he is still in diligent effort to bring the money about with the soonest; and We now also daily expect from him this good declaration, that he will have arranged the means. And since the matters stand in the manner just told, We accordingly desire of you herewith quite graciously that you would, on account of the said Tycho Brahe, have patience yet a little and short time; [and] so We are of the gracious offer to make the provision, that then, with the speediest, the actual payment shall follow — for We have now again, on that account, given the oft-mentioned rent-master fresh reminder and also strong command. We did not wish to withhold [this] from you meanwhile, for [your] gracious information; and We are graciously, and with all good, well inclined toward you.

Given Doberan, the 17th of June, in the year 1601.

documents.incipit: MEINEN freundtlichen grueß sampt wünschung alles gueten iederzeit bevor. Ehrnuester …

text.original:
DEM EHRNUESTEN VND ACHTPARN HERRN ANDRESS MAIERN, FÜRSTLICHEM MECKLE[N]BURGISCHEN RENTMEISTERN, MEINEM GUETEN FREUNDTE. WISSMAR.

MEINEN freundtlichen grueß sampt wünschung alles gueten iederzeit bevor. Ehrnuester achtpar, insonders gönstiger lieber her rentmeister. Was sider der auffkündigung dero 10000 thaller hauptsummae sampt dem interesse, damit jj: ff: gg: die junge herschafft zue Mecklenburgk mir verhafftet, vorgelauffen vnd was vngelegenheit mir auß verzugerung der zahlung (welcher termin (meiner auffkündigung nach) verfloßen gewesen den 1. aprilis dieses lauffenden jhars) entstanden, werdet ihr euch auß meinen hiebevor ahn euch ergangenen schreiben nochmahls zur genüege wißen zue entsinn[en]. Dieweiln dan ihr abermahl gegen gleichßfals verlauffenen s. Joannis thagk obangereugte summa vnd interesse richtich zu erlegen erpotten, hab ichs dabej, wiewohl ich dadurch in keinen geringen schaden gerhaten, j: f: g: hertzog Vldrichen etc., meinem gnedichsten herren, zue vnterthenigsten gefallen (wiewohl die bürgern laut vnseres contracts einzuemahnen ich guete vnd pilliche vrsacch gehabt) biß dato beruhen laßen. Vnd nehme mir in kainen zweiffel, ihr werdet nuhnmehr (seitenmahl lenger mitt dem gelde zue warten ich durchauß nitt kan oder bedacht bin) auff die mittel vnd wege gedacht, auch dazu gethon haben, das mehrgenante hauptsumma vnd interesse nuhnmaehr richtich verhanden vnd strax par außgezehlt werden solle vnd könne. Jnmittelst sehe ich gerne, das es bej ainem gewißen man zu Hamburgk oder Lübeck, bis es abgeholet wirt, auffgehoben oder verwahrt würde. Wie dan alßpaldt aine gewiße pottschafft ich derer orter zu senden daßselbige geldt abzuholen bedacht bin. Vnd hab mit zaigern dieses euch söllichs zuvor zu verstendigen, damit er alßpaldt damit gefürdert vnd nitt auffgehalten werde (worauß dan vns baiderseits, so wohl auch den bürgen, allerhande vngelegenheit entstehen würde), vor guet angesehen. Vns hiemit götlicher almacht entpfhelendt.

Prag den 18 julij st:novo a:o 1601.
EE: dienst- vnd freundtwilliger
Tycho Brahe
man: ppj:


*[Postscript — restored from Dreyer, Opera Omnia XIV, p. 226; dropped by the working transcription. See Apparatus.]*
Gelanget hieneben an den herren rentmeistern mein freundtliches pitten vnd söcchen, er wolle kainem, der nitt entweder von mir handtschrifft vnd sigell, von heut dato abzurechnen, oder auch von meinem vettern Esche Bilden, zaigen kan, dan auß etzlichen handlen söllichs vonnötten, jnsonderheit wolle er ainem holsteinischen jubilierer mit nahmen Bernhardt Fersten oder seinen dienern, welchen ich zwar vorhin Vollmacht, iedoch in anderer mainung, gegeben, itzo gar nichts folgen laßen. Datum ut [supra].
text.english:
**To the honourable and worshipful Lord Andreas Meier, princely Mecklenburg rent-master, my good friend. Wismar.**

My friendly greeting, together with the wish of all good, at all times beforehand. Honourable, worshipful, especially favourable, dear Lord rent-master: what has passed since the calling-in of those 10,000 thalers of principal sum, together with the interest, by which Their Princely Graces, the young rulership of Mecklenburg, stand bound to me, and what inconvenience has arisen for me from the delay of payment (the term for which, according to my notice of recall, fell due the 1st of April of this current year) — of this you will know well enough to remind yourself once more from my earlier letters sent to you. Since, then, you have once again offered to pay the above-mentioned sum and interest duly against St. John's Day (which has likewise now passed), I have — although I have thereby come to no small loss — let it rest until now, to the most humble pleasure of His Princely Grace Duke Ulrich etc., my most gracious Lord (although, according to our contract, I had good and fair cause to dun the sureties). And I have no doubt that you will by now (seeing that I altogether cannot, nor am minded to, wait any longer for the money) have thought upon the ways and means, and have so acted, that the aforesaid principal sum and interest shall and may now be duly to hand and at once paid out in cash. In the meantime I should be glad if it were deposited or kept safe with some reliable man at Hamburg or Lübeck until it is fetched; for I intend forthwith to send a trusty messenger to those parts to collect that same money. And I have thought it good to apprise you of this beforehand by the bearer of this [letter], so that he may at once be furthered with it and not held up (whence all manner of inconvenience would arise for us both, and for the sureties as well). Herewith commending us to divine omnipotence.

Prague, the 18th of July, New Style, in the year 1601.
Your Honour's service- and friend-willing
Tycho Brahe
[written] with his own hand.


*[Postscript:]* Herewith reaches the Lord rent-master my friendly request and entreaty, that he let nothing be paid out to anyone who cannot show either a bond and seal from me — to be reckoned from today's date — or [one] from my cousin Eske Bille, for, from certain dealings, this is necessary; in particular, that he let nothing at all now be paid out to a Holstein jeweller named Bernhard Ferst, or to his servants, to whom I had indeed earlier given a mandate, but with another intent. Dated as above.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender.** **Tycho Brahe** at **Prague**, less than four months before his death (24 October 1601). The letter is one of several late documents on his outstanding loans and finances.
- **Recipient.** *Andreas Meier (Andress Maiern), fürstlich-mecklenburgischer Rentmeister, Wismar* = **Andreas Meier**, the ducal Mecklenburg **rent-master (treasurer / financial officer)** at Wismar — the official charged with discharging the ducal debt.
- **The transaction.** A **10,000-thaler loan** (the *Hauptsumme*, principal) plus *Interesse* (interest) which the young Mecklenburg ruling house owed Tycho. Tycho had given formal *Aufkündigung* (notice of recall) with the principal falling due **1 April 1601**; when that lapsed, repayment was re-promised for **St. John's Day (24 June)**, which had also now passed. Tycho, though entitled by contract to proceed against the *Bürgen* (citizen-sureties), had forborne out of deference to Duke Ulrich. He now presses for immediate cash payment, to be lodged meanwhile with a trustworthy agent at **Hamburg or Lübeck** pending collection by his messenger.
- **Persons named.**
 - *J. F. G. Herzog Ulrich* = **Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg(-Güstrow)** (1527–1603), Tycho's "most gracious Lord" in the matter.
 - *die junge Herrschaft zu Mecklenburg* = **the young rulers of Mecklenburg** (the junior line for whom the debt stood) — *Their Princely Graces* (*Jhr Fürstlich Gnaden*).
- **Place.** *Wismar* — the Hanseatic port and Mecklenburg residence-town where the rent-master sat; *Hamburg / Lübeck* named as safe deposit-points for the funds.
- **Formulae & abbreviations.** Burgher-courteous register (*ehrnvest und achtbar*, "honourable and worshipful"). The subscription *EE: dienst- vnd freundtwilliger* = *Euer Ehren dienst- und freundwilliger* ("Your Honour's service- and friend-willing"); *man: ppj:* = *manu propria* ("with his own hand," autograph attestation). *J. F. G.* = *Jhr Fürstlich(e) Gnad(en)*; *J. J. F. F. G. G.* = the plural ("Their Princely Graces").
- **Calendar.** Dateline *den 18 Julij st:novo* — explicitly **New Style**, as in all Tycho's Prague letters. The internal deadlines (*1. Aprilis*; *S. Joannis Tag* = 24 June) are likewise to be read consistently with the document's stated New-Style usage; reproduced, not converted.

- **§1 Dreyer collation.** Closing postscript revoking the Holstein jeweller Bernhard Ferst's mandate, restored from Dreyer XIV p.226 (dropped by the working transcription).
- **Correction.** Latin: 'mist nahmen' corrected to 'mit nahmen' in the postscript, per Dreyer, Opera Omnia XIV, p. 227 ('mit nahmen Bernhardt Ferften').

documents.abstract: Renews the demand for repayment of 10,000 thalers and interest from Mecklenburg, recounting the contract terms and the loss caused by failure to pay at the agreed Easter deadline.
documents.incipit: DURCHLAÜCHTIGSTER hochgeborner fürst, gnedichster herr. Ewer Fürst: Gnaden sein meine …

text.original:
DEM DURCHLEUCHTIGSTEN HOCHGEBORNEN FURSTEN VNDT HERRN, HERRN VLDRICHEN, HERTZOGEN ZU MECKLENBURGK, GRAFFEN ZU SCHWERIN, DER LANDE ROSTOCH VNDT STARGART HERRN, MEINEM GNEDICHSTENN HERRN.

DURCHLAÜCHTIGSTER hochgeborner fürst, gnedichster herr. Ewer Fürst: Gnaden sein meine vnterthenigste gantzwillige dienste iederzeit höchstes fleißes bevor. Vndt soll deroselben abermahl vnterthenigster gueter wohlmainung nit pergen, welchergestallt ich zwar vngezweiffelte hofnung gefast gehabt, es wurde von Ewer Fürst: Gnaden rentmeistern Andres Meyern vnserem wegen dero 10000 thalern auffgerichteten contracts vnd auffkundigungesbrieff (inmaßen sie zue rechter zeit beschehen) zufolge mihr sölliche summa sampt dem interesse gegen vergangenen ostern ohne ainige fernere verzugerung dageraicht vndt gefolget sein. Weiln aber damalß wegen anderer von obgemeldten h: rentmeistern angereugter hohen vndt notwendigen außgaben sölliches nitt geschehen können (wiewohl zuvor die auffkundigung ohne ainigen bedencken ahngenohmen vndt ich meine sacchen alhie darnach gerichtet, auch andere leutte darauff vertrostet, vnd dardurch in keinen geringen schaden gerahten), so hab dennoch E: F: G: zue vnterthenigsten diensten vnd meinem schaden vngeacht ich biß das gegen vergangen s: Johan: der hauptstuel sampt dem interesse richtig erlegt vndt mir zuegestelldt würde (wie dan mehrgedachter h: rentmeister mir abermahl schriftlich versprocchen) mich gedulde[t]. Weiln dan dießer ander termin abermahl lengst verfloßen, alß nehme ich in kainen zweiffell, E: F: G: werden eß durch den rentmeistern schon dahin gedirigirt vnd gebracht haben, daß söllich geldt schon richtig verhanden, damit ich die burgen einzuemahnen nitt genotdrenget werde. Vndt bin derowegen eine gewiße pottschafft alßpaldt derer örtter daßelbige anhero zuholen abzuefertigen ihn willens.

Gelanget derowegen ahn Ewer F: G: mein vnterthenigste gantzfleißige pitt, sie geruhen den gnedichsten befehlich vnd anordnung zue thuen, damit derselbige, sopaldt ehr anlangen wirdt, nit damit auffgehalten, sondern ehist sich sampt dem gelde wiederumb anhero zue verfüegen gefurdert werden muege.

Diß vnd andere gut vnd wohlthatten vmb E: F: G: gehorsambst zue verdienen, will ich mir stetz zum höchsten angelegen sein laßen. Ewer F: G: sampt dero vielgeliepten gemahlin hiemit göttlicher allmacht vnd zue dero fernern gnaden mich vnterthenigst vndt getreulich entpfhelendt.

Datum Prag den 18. julij anno 1601.
Ewer Fürstlichen Ghnaden vnterthenigster gantz williger
Tycho Brahe
man: pprj:
text.english:
**To the most illustrious, high-born Prince and Lord, Lord Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg, Count of Schwerin, Lord of the lands of Rostock and Stargard, my most gracious Lord.**

Most illustrious, high-born Prince, most gracious Lord. To Your Princely Grace, my most humble, wholly willing services with the highest diligence, at all times beforehand. And I should not again conceal from the same, in most humble good intention, in what manner I had indeed conceived an undoubted hope that, by Your Princely Grace's rent-master Andreas Meier — pursuant to the contract drawn up over the 10,000 thalers and to the notice-of-recall (inasmuch as these took place at the proper time) — that sum, together with the interest, would be handed over and paid to me against the past Easter, without any further delay. But since at that time, on account of other high and necessary expenditures cited by the aforesaid lord rent-master, this could not be done (although the recall had previously been accepted without any hesitation, and I had ordered my affairs here accordingly, and reassured other people upon it, and thereby came to no small loss), I nonetheless — for Your Princely Grace's most humble service, and notwithstanding my loss — held my patience, until against the past St. John's [Day] the principal together with the interest should be duly paid and delivered to me (as the oft-mentioned lord rent-master again promised me in writing). Since, then, this second term too has long since passed, I have no doubt that Your Princely Grace will already have so directed and brought it about, through the rent-master, that such money is now duly to hand — so that I be not constrained to dun the sureties. And I am therefore minded to dispatch a trusty messenger at once to those parts to fetch the same hither.

There comes therefore to Your Princely Grace my most humble, wholly diligent petition, that you would deign to give the most gracious command and order, that the same [messenger], as soon as he arrives, be not held up with it, but be furthered to betake himself back hither with the money as soon as possible.

This, and other good deeds and benefactions, to deserve most obediently of Your Princely Grace, I will ever let be of the highest concern to me. Your Princely Grace, together with your much-beloved consort, I herewith most humbly and faithfully commend to divine omnipotence and to your further graces.

Given at Prague, the 18th of July, in the year 1601.
Your Princely Grace's most humble, wholly willing
Tycho Brahe
with his own hand.

documents.abstract: Explains that the 10,000 thalers have been lying ready in Güstrow since before Midsummer, and that Tycho need only send to demand them against return of the issued bond.
documents.incipit: Vlrich etc.

text.original:
AN TYCHO BRAHEN ZU PRAAG.

Vlrich etc.

VNSERN gonstigen grueß zuuor. Ehrnuester lieber besonder, Wir haben ewer schreiben empfangen vnd was jhr wegen richtiger erlegung der 10000 thaler, damit euch Vnsere vnmundige vettern vnd pflegesohne, die junge hertzogen zu Meckelnburgk etc., verhafft, an Vns gelanget, daraus vernommen. Nun ist nicht ohnedas gegen negst verschienen ostern diejennigen bej denen hochermelter Vnser pflegesohne rentmeister Andr: M[eyer] ewerntsowol auch anderer mehr leute halber geldt besprochen, welche jhm auch darauff gewisse vertrostung gethan, einen bloßen geschlagen. Wir haben aber dagegen in andere wege die versehung gethan, das man baldt hernacher die summa, so jhr haben sollet, zu wege gebracht, welche summa auch bereits vor negst vergangen Johannis baptistae alhie zur stedte gelegen, wie dan auch solch geldt hirselbst noch liegt, vnd hette man es, wan nur dasieder darumb anfurderung geschehen where, gegen wiedereinandtwortung der außgegebenen verschreibung wol mechtig werden konnen. Vnd mugen Wir euch hieneben nicht bergen, das Eßke Bilde vor Johannis einen seiner diener zu Vns gen Dobbran geschicket, vnd sich alda erkundigen laßen, ob das geldt verhanden where, deme Wir wieder anzeigen laßen, weil Wir alle stunde des rentmeisters ankunfft mit dem gelde vermütendt wheren, das er auff Johannis bej Vns wiederumb ansuchens vnd alßdan des geldes gewertig sein solle, es hat sich aber derselbe so weinig auf Johannis alse auch seidt der zeit bej Vns nicht angegeben; where es aber geschehen vnd er hette die außgegebene Verschreibung mit sich gebracht, solte auch gestracks die außzehlung darauff erfolget sein, vnd konnet jhr dahero ewers geldes auch nochmaln wol mechtig werden. Welchs Wir euch hinwieder zu gnediger erklerung nicht wollen verhalten, vnd Wir seind euch mit gnaden geneigt.

Datum Güstrow den 24. julij a:o 1601.
text.english:
**To Tycho Brahe at Prague.**

Ulrich, etc.

Our favourable greeting beforehand. Honourable, dear, and especial [friend]: We have received your letter, and have understood from it what you have conveyed to Us regarding the proper payment of the 10,000 thaler with which Our minor cousins and foster-sons, the young Dukes of Mecklenburg etc., are indebted to you. Now, it is not otherwise [than this]: toward the recently-past Easter, those with whom the highly-mentioned rent-master of Our foster-sons, Andreas M[eyer], had bespoken money — on your account, as also for the sake of several other people — and who had given him a certain assurance thereupon, came up empty [struck a blank]. But We, on the other hand, made provision by other means, so that soon afterward the sum which you are to have was brought about — which sum also already lay here in the town [ready] before the recently-past [feast of] John the Baptist [24 June], as indeed such money still lies here; and, had only the demand for it been made here, it could well have been obtained against the return of the issued bond. And We cannot conceal from you herewith that Eske Bille, before [the feast of] John, sent one of his servants to Us at Doberan, and had inquiry made there whether the money was on hand; to whom We had it indicated [in reply] that — since We were every hour expecting the rent-master's arrival with the money — he should, at [the feast of] John, apply to Us again, and then be in waiting for the money; but the same [rent-master] presented himself to Us as little at John['s feast] as he has since that time. But had it happened, and had he brought the issued bond with him, the payment thereon should straightway have followed; and you can therefore still well obtain your money. Which We did not wish to withhold from you, in turn, for [your] gracious information; and We are graciously inclined toward you.

Given Güstrow, the 24th of July, in the year 1601.

text.original:
DEM ERBARN WOLGEACHTEN VNDT FURNHEMEN ANDRESS MEYER, DIE JUNGE HERTZOGEN ZU MEKELBURG, J: F: G: RENTEMEISTER, MEINEM INSONDERS GUNSTIGEN GUEDTEN FREUNDE F[REUNDLICH] G[ESCHRIEBEN].

MEINEN freundtlichen gruß zuuorn. Freundtlicher lieber rentemester. Kan ich euch freundtlich nicht vorhaldten, daß mihr heudt dato ein schreiben ist behendiget worden, so mihr Berendt Ferste, burger zum Kil, zugesendet hadtt, vndt dieweiln dar kein namen eingeschrieben war, hadt mich doch der briefzeuger berichtet, daß daßelbige brieff von euch keme, vnndt waß dießelbige anlanget, daß ich soldte habenn zu Dobbran, in deß f: g: vorgemack, anlangen laßenn vmme 2000 thaler vnnd derselbige, so dermasßen meinendtwegen hadt angelanget, kein quitung nicht gebragt, so weiß ich nicht von sölche quitung odder 2000 thaler zusagen, habe auch darumme nicht anlangen lasßen, söndern ihr wisßet euch wol zuerinneren, daß ich vor lengst die 10000 thaler, worauff ich ein furstliche obligation habe, habe auffkundigen lasßenn vnndt auff die bestimbte zeidt, alß nemlich auff ostern, mein diener midt des f: obligation hinaußgesenndt daß geldt zu entfhangen, vnndt weiln erß nicht bekhommen hadtt, vndt ihr mich zugeschriebenn, daß eß auff Johannj soldte erlegtt werden, alß habe ich zum vberfluß widderumme mein diener abgefertigtt midt deß f: obligation, vnnd hadt er itzliche thage fur vndt nach Johannj zu Rostock in Joachim Lorman sein hauß gewardtet, vndt weiln daß geldt in d: Lucas Beckmester sein huß zuerlegen auffgekundigt war, hadt erß dem h: doctor wisßen laßen, wohr er zu finden war, ob dar wen kheme, der solche summa außzelen woldte, seindt doch keine nicht gekommen, hadt sich derhalben widderumme nach heim begeben, vnnd weiln ihr schrieben, daß die summa fur Johannj al beisamen ist gewesen, vndt nuhr die entfhenger wardten, so wil ich noch zum dritten mall selbst pershonlich hinaußkommen, vnndt ihr werdet mihr nicht vordenckenn, wo ferne die summa neben all jnterres vnd skaden nicht erlegt wirdt, daß ich dan andre mittel gebrauchen werde. Habe auch diß zum f[reun]dtlich andtwordt nicht vorhaldten khonn[en]. Vnndt thue vnß beiderzeidtz in den schudtz deß Almegtigen empfhelen.

Datum Kopennhagen den 24. julij anno 1601.
Eske Bille
text.english:
**To the honourable, well-respected and distinguished Andreas Meier, rent-master to the young Dukes of Mecklenburg, Their Princely Graces, my especially favourable good friend. Written in friendship.**

My friendly greeting beforehand. Friendly, dear rent-master: I cannot, in friendship, withhold from you that today a letter has been handed to me, which Berend Ferste, citizen of Kiel, has sent me; and since no name was written within it, the bearer nonetheless informed me that the same letter came from you. As to what it concerns — that I am supposed to have had application made at Doberan, in the antechamber of His Princely Grace, for 2,000 thalers, and that the man who thus applied on my behalf brought no receipt — I know nothing to say of any such receipt or of 2,000 thalers, nor have I had any application made for it. Rather, you will well remember that I long ago had the 10,000 thalers, on which I hold a princely bond, called in, and at the appointed time — namely at Easter — sent out my servant with the Prince's bond to receive the money; and since he did not get it, and you wrote to me that it should be paid at St. John's [Day], I again, for good measure, dispatched my servant with the Prince's bond, and he waited several days, before and after St. John's, at Rostock in Joachim Lorman's house. And since the money had been appointed to be paid out at Dr. Lucas Beckmeister's house, he let the Lord Doctor know where he was to be found, [to see] whether anyone would come there who would pay out the sum; but none came. He therefore betook himself home again. And since you wrote that the sum was all together before St. John's, and that only the receivers were awaited, I will yet a third time come out in person myself; and you will not think ill of me if — should the sum, together with all interest and damages, not be paid — I then resort to other means. This too I could not withhold, by way of a friendly answer. And I commend us both to the protection of the Almighty.

Given at Copenhagen, the 24th of July, in the year 1601.
Eske Bille

documents.apparatus:
- **Direction & sender.** **Eske Bille**, the Danish nobleman and Tycho Brahe's kinsman-agent, writing **in his own person** from **Copenhagen** to the ducal rent-master — the most circumstantial document of the Mecklenburg-debt thread, recounting from the creditor's side what Tycho's letters (brahe-t_16010527001, brahe-t_16010718001) and Duke Ulrich's (brahe-t_16010809001) describe from theirs.
- **Recipient.** **Andreas Meier**, **rent-master to the young Dukes of Mecklenburg** (*J. F. G.* = *Ihrer Fürstlichen Gnaden*, "Their Princely Graces"), at Wismar.
- **The narrative (fills the gaps in the thread).**
 - A garbled report had reached Eske Bille via **Berend Ferste, a citizen of Kiel**, in an *unsigned* letter — that Bille was to collect **2,000 thalers** at **Doberan** (the Mecklenburg ducal seat at Bad Doberan), in the prince's antechamber, but without a receipt. Bille disavows all knowledge of this.
 - He restates the real claim: the **10,000-thaler princely bond** (*fürstliche Obligation*) was called in long ago; his servant was sent with the bond to collect at **Easter**, then again "for good measure" around **St. John's Day (24 June)**, waiting at **Rostock** in **Joachim Lorman's house**.
 - Payment had been appointed at the house of **Dr. Lukas Beckmeister** at Rostock; the servant notified him but no payer appeared, and he went home empty-handed.
 - Bille now threatens to come **a third time in person**, and failing full payment of principal + interest + damages, to "resort to other means."
- **Persons named.** *Eske Bille* (sender); *Berend Ferste, Bürger zu Kiel* (the source of the false 2,000-thaler report); *Joachim Lorman* (Rostock householder where the servant lodged); *Dr. Lukas Beckmeister* (the Rostock doctor at whose house payment was to be made); *die jungen Herzöge zu Mecklenburg* (the under-age debtors).
- **Places.** *Kopenhagen* (place of issue); *Kiel*; *Doberan* (Bad Doberan); *Rostock*.
- **Language note.** The hand is **Danish-influenced chancery German**: Danish/Low-German orthography and forms surface throughout — *skaden* for *Schaden* ("damages"), *huß/hauß* for *Haus*, *wohr* for *wo*, *midt* for *mit*, *zuuorn*, *behendiget*, *vorhaldten*, *itzliche*, *pershonlich*. Rendered straight; the spelling is the writer's Dano-German chancery register, not error.
- **Formulae.** Burgher-courteous opening *meinen freundlichen Gruß zuvor* → "my friendly greeting beforehand"; address tag *F. G.* = *freundlich geschrieben* ("written in friendship"); *Datum* → "Given."
- **Calendar.** Dateline *den 24. Julij anno 1601* at Copenhagen; **Denmark kept the Julian (Old Style)** calendar until 1700, so this is Old Style — to be contrasted with the New-Style Prague datelines of Tycho's own letters in the same affair (the *St. Johannis* and *Ostern* terms are likewise Old Style here). Reproduced, not converted.

documents.incipit: MEINEN freundtlichen vndt gantz willigen diennst neben wunschungh alles guedtes beuorn, …

text.original:
DEM EDLEN VNNDT ERNUESTEN IOACHIM STRALENDORPFF, MECHLENBURGISCHE FURSTLICHE GNADEN VLRICI CAMMERJONKER, MEINEM FREUNDTLICHEN LIEBEN BRUDER ZU HANDEN, F[REUNDTLICH] G[ESCHRIEBEN].

MEINEN freundtlichen vndt gantz willigen diennst neben wunschungh alles guedtes beuorn, freundtlicher lieber Joachim Stralendorpf, bruder vnd insonders guedter freundt. Freundtlicher meinungh kan ich dihr nicht vorhaldten, daß mihr mein blutuorwandter vnd guedter freundt Tycho Brahen sein schreiben vor 9 oder 10 thage ist behandigtt worden, wor auß ich woll vornhommen, daß er nicht zwifelt (schreibt er) mihr die zehen thausendt thaler (dar ich dihr lestmals in mein schreiben vmme vormeldet habe) ja auff vorlauffenen Johanni seindt erlegtt worden. Vnndt weinig thagen zuuorn ist mihr Andreas Meyer sein schreiben auch behandigt worden, wohrinne ehr mich erinnertt, das einer meinendtwegen soldt zu Dobbran in meines g: f: vnd hernn, hertzog Vlrich, hertzog zu Mechelborig etc., f: f: g: vorgemach vmme zwe thausend thaler angehaldten haben vnd keine beweiß gehabtt, wohrauff ich ihme widderumme zugeschrieben habe, daß ich von keine 2000 thaler wuste, whe ich auch nicht weiß, sondern ehr wiste sich wol zuerinneren von wegen die 10000 thaler, so ich hochgedachte mein g: f: vnd hern auff vorgängen Michelj habe aufkundigen lasßen, worauff ich auch Meyer sein skrifftlich andtwordtt habe, daß solche summa midt sampt die zinse auff vorgangen ostern (whe billich) soldte gewis erlegt werden, vndt alß daß nicht geschehen ist, hadt ehr mich dan widderumme zugeschrieben, daß daß geldt gewisße auff Johannj soldte erlegt werden. Vndt weiln ich nuhn auf de rechte bestimbte zeidtt, alß nemlich auff ostern, habe mein diener hin ghenn Rostock geschicket midt deß furstlichen obligation vorgeschrieben summa zu empfhangen vnndtt nu widderumme auff vorgangen Johanni deßglichen midt hochgedachtes m: g: h: ihre f: g: obligation, vndt had mein diene[r] hir zu Rostock in Joachim Loherman sein hausß gelegen itzliche thage vor, auff vndt nach Johannj vnd sich in doctor Lucas Bachmester sein hauß angeben, weiln daß geldt dahr zuerlegen auffkekundigtt wahr, seindt doch keiner nicht da gewesen, der solche summa außzelen woldte. Vnnd gleichwol schreibt der rentemester inn bemeldte sein leste schreiben, daß die gantze summa vor Johannj ist beisamen gewesen vndt begierdt (weiln dahr keiner nicht meinentwegen auff Johannj ist gewesen, derß entfhangen woldte, schreibt er), daß ich doch wil her auß schicken vndt die 2000 thaler entfhangen lasßen, damidt Tyche daß vbrige [kon]te hinaußgeschicket werden, auff welchen sein skreiben ich mich nicht gnugsam vorwundren mach. Vnd habe ihme drauff schrifftlich geandtwortett, daß weiln ich nun zwey vnterschiedtliche mall, alß nemlich auff ostern vnnd Johannj, mein gewisße potschafft mitt hochgedachtes meines gnedigen fursten vnnd hern, j: f: g: obligation hir zu Rostock gehabtt, so wil ich nun zum vberfluß selbst zum dritten mal midt dem ersten kommen.

So bin ich nuhn, lieber bruder, hir zu Rostock heudt dato angekhommen, vnd auff den abent ist einer (deß namen oder pershon mihr vnbekandtt) bey mihr gewesen vndt auf Meyer sein wegen angegeben, das er habe 5000 thaler vormacht auff Prag, vndt dabey berichtet, daß ich mihr erkleren woldte, ob ich daß vbrige hir entfhangen woldte oder ghen Wißmer darnach zihen, worauff ich ihnen vor andtwordt gegeben habe, daß ich nu hergekommen ware die gantze summa midt sampt allen nachstendigen zinsen, auffgelauffenen skaeden vndt vnkost [zu empfangen], oder woferner solches nicht geschege, worde ich hochvorursachet andre mittel zu gebrauchen, welches Gott weiß ich vor mein pershon so wol alß mein bruede[r] Tycho vngerne thadten. Bitte dich derhalben freundtlich, lieber bruder, du woldtest doch meinem genedigen fursten vnndt hern anmelden, daß ich hir wardte, vndt daß sein f: g: sich gnedigst woldte erkleren, ob ich die summa mochte nuhn bekommen, weiln seiner f: g: schreiben sub dato Dobbran 17. junij anlanget, das ich ein kleine weile erwardten woldte, vorhoffe s: f: g: wirdt mihr ein gnedigen andtwordtt hir auf geben. Jch bitte dihr ghar freundtlich, du woldtest mihr vnuordecht haben, daß ich dihr so offte midt meinen sachen bemuhe; wohr ich dihr mein dage widderumme dienen kan, findest du mihr alletzeidt willich vndt erpottigh, vnd thue vnß beiderseidtz in den schudtz deß Almechtigen emptfhelen.

Datum Rostock den 8. augustj anno 1601.
Eske Bilde
text.english:
**To the noble and honourable Joachim Stralendorff, chamber-junker of His Princely Grace of Mecklenburg, Ulrich, to the hands of my friendly dear brother, amicably written.**

My friendly and wholly willing service, with the wish of all good, beforehand, friendly dear Joachim Stralendorff, brother and especial good friend. In friendly intent I cannot conceal from you that my blood-relation and good friend **Tycho Brahe**'s letter was handed to me 9 or 10 days ago, from which I well perceived that he does not doubt (he writes) that **the ten thousand thalers** (about which I last wrote to you) were indeed paid out to me on the past **St. John's Day**. And a few days before, **Andreas Meier**'s letter was also handed to me, wherein he reminds me that someone, on my behalf, was [said] to have demanded **two thousand thalers** in the antechamber of my gracious prince and lord, **Duke Ulrich** of Mecklenburg, at **Doberan**, and had no proof; whereupon I wrote back to him that I knew of no 2,000 thalers (as indeed I do not), but he should well recall, concerning the **10,000 thalers** which I had given notice on to my aforesaid gracious lord at the past Michaelmas — on which I also have Meier's written answer, that such sum, together with the interest, should certainly be paid at the past Easter (as was fair); and when that did not happen, he wrote to me again that the money should certainly be paid on St. John's Day. And since I have now, at the right appointed time — namely at Easter — sent my servant to Rostock with the princely bond to receive the aforesaid sum, and now again on the past St. John's Day likewise with my gracious lord's bond — and my servant lay here at Rostock in **Joachim Loherman's house** several days before, on, and after St. John's Day, and presented himself at **Doctor Lucas Backmeister's house** (since the money was given notice to be paid there) — yet **no one was there who would pay out such sum**. And yet the rent-master writes, in his last letter, that the whole sum was together before St. John's Day, and desires (since no one was there on my behalf to receive it) that I would send out here and have the **2,000 thalers** received, so the rest could be sent on to Tycho — at which letter of his I cannot wonder enough. And I wrote back that, since I have now twice — at Easter and St. John's Day — had my sure messenger with my gracious lord's bond here at Rostock, **I will now, for good measure, come myself, a third time**, at the first [opportunity].

So I have now, dear brother, arrived here at Rostock this very day; and in the evening someone (whose name and person are unknown to me) was with me and stated, on Meier's behalf, that **he had transferred 5,000 thalers to Prague [by bill]**, and asked therewith that I declare whether I would receive the rest here, or travel to **Wismar** for it; whereupon I answered that I had now come here [to receive] **the whole sum, together with all outstanding interest, accrued damages, and costs — or, failing that, I would be highly compelled to use other means**, which (God knows) I, for my person, as well as **my brother Tycho**, would unwillingly do. I therefore ask you amicably, dear brother, that you would announce to my gracious prince and lord that I am waiting here, and that His Princely Grace would graciously declare whether I might now receive the sum — since His Princely Grace's letter, dated **Doberan 17 June**, asks that I wait a little while; I hope His Princely Grace will give me a gracious answer hereupon. I ask you quite amicably to hold me unblamed, that I trouble you so often with my affairs; wherever I can serve you in return in my days, you find me always willing and ready; and I commend us both to the protection of the Almighty.

Given at Rostock, the 8th of August, the year 1601.
Eske Bille.

documents.apparatus:
- **Sender & recipient.** **Eske Bille**, Tycho's Danish kinsman and **plenipotentiary** in the Mecklenburg-debt affair (cf. brahe-t_16010604001, brahe-t_16001116001), writing to **Joachim Stralendorff**, **chamber-junker (*Kammerjunker*) of Duke Ulrich III of Mecklenburg** — the duke's man through whom Eske seeks an answer. The MS is the **original letter**, filed at Schwerin under *Debita passiva principum*.
- **Significance — the climax (and impasse) of the Mecklenburg 10,000-thaler debt, August 1601.** This first-hand account from the creditor's agent, **two months before Tycho's death**, shows the collection in deadlock:
 - **The muddle.** Rent-master **Andreas Meier** keeps writing of a **2,000-thaler** claim "demanded in the antechamber at **Doberan** without proof"; Eske replies he knows nothing of any 2,000 — only the **10,000-thaler principal** he gave notice on at **Michaelmas [1600]**, due (per Meier's own letters) first at **Easter**, then **St. John's Day [24 June 1601]**.
 - **The failed collections.** Eske's servant came to Rostock with the **ducal bond** at both terms, lodging at **Joachim Lohmann's** and presenting himself at **Backmeister's house** (the appointed pay-place) — but **no one paid**. Meier nonetheless claims the sum "was ready," and asks Eske to take **2,000** so "the rest could be sent to Tycho at Prague."
 - **Eske's third trip & ultimatum.** Disbelieving, Eske has now come **himself, a third time**; an unnamed man (for Meier) reports **5,000 thalers transferred to Prague by bill** and offers the rest at Rostock or **Wismar**. Eske demands **the whole sum with all interest, damages, and costs — or "other means"** (legal action), "which I and my brother Tycho would unwillingly do." He asks Stralendorff to get **Duke Ulrich's** answer (the duke's letter of **17 June, Doberan**, had asked him to "wait a little while").
- **Persons named.** Eske Bille; **Joachim Stralendorff** (ducal chamber-junker); **Tycho Brahe** ("my blood-relation … my brother"); **Andreas Meier** (rent-master); **Duke Ulrich III**; **Joachim Lohmann** (the Rostock host); **Lucas Backmeister** (Superintendent of Rostock, the pay-place). Places: **Doberan**, **Wismar**, **Rostock**, **Prague**.
- **Calendar.** Dateline *Rostock den 8. Augustj anno 1601*; Lutheran Rostock kept the **Julian (Old Style)** calendar; the *Doberan 17. Junij* ducal letter likewise O.S. Header marked [O.S.].
- Correction. English corrected the house-owner's surname from 'Lohmann' to 'Loherman', matching both the transcribed original and Dreyer (XIV p.230); the companion letter no.225 (XIV p.229) spells the same man 'Lorman'.

text.original:
DEM EHRSAMEN VNSERM LIEBEN GETREWEN ANDREÆ MEYERN, RENTMEISTERN, ZUR WISSMAR.

VON Gottes gnadenn Vlrich, hertzogk zu Mekelnburgk etc. Ehrsamer lieber getrewer. Was Eßke Bilde der 10000 tahler halbenn, damit Vnsere vnmündige vettern vnd pflegesohne, die jungen hertzogen zu Mekelnburgk etc., Tycho Brahen verhafft, an Vnseren cammerer Jochim von Stralendorffen abermals gelangen thuet, das hast du aus beyuerwartem seinem originalschreiben nach mehrer lenge zuersehenn.

Nun seind Wir der meynung, es werden die zehen tausend thaler sampt den zinsen, so gemelter Tycho Brahe haben soll, noch beysamen seinn, das sie auff begeren gegenn wiedereinandwortung der außgegebenen verschreibung alßbald außgezehlett werden konnen, wie Wir dan solches newlicher zeit, jnmaßen du aus inligender copey zuuernehmen, von Vns geschriebenn. Weil aber Eßke Bylde vnter andern in seinem schreiben gedenket, das sich gestern abend einer bey jhm zu Rostogk angegeben, so jhm von deinentwegen angemeldet hette, das du obgedachtenn Tycho Brahenn 5000 thaler hinauff nach Prage vbermachet, vnd Wir nicht wißenn können, was es hirumb vor eine gelegenheit hat, alß begeren Wir demnach an dich hiemit gnediglich, das du Vns vngeseumet bey zeigern hieuon eigentlichen vnd gewißen bericht zuschreibest, dan weill Eßke Bilde selbst vmb des geldes willen aus Dennemarken gekommen ist vnd zu Rostogk liegt, konnen die sachen gar keinen verzugk leiden. Vnnd haltenn Wirs auch dafür, weil du Vns das geringste dauon nicht angezeigett, das du das gelt hinauff nach Praag soltest vermachet haben, welches dan auch Vnsers bedünckens vor wiedererlangung der außgegebenen verschreibung nicht fuglich hat geschehen können, es werde die gantze summa noch bey einander seinn, damit es volnkomlich, sintemal es Eßke Bilde auch volnkomlich haben will, außgezehlet werden könne vnd müge. Vnd wirst du zeigern mit der begertenn andwort desto zeitiger wiederumb an Vns abfertigen, damit Wir dieselbe noch vor vnserm auffzuge von hinnen (so ob Gott wil am zukünfftigen dingestage morgen geschehen wirdt) gewiße mügen vberkommen. An dem erstatest du Vnsere gnedige zuuerleßige meynungk.

Datum Güstrow den 9. augustj an:o 1601.

Auch ehrsamer lieber getrewer, weil Eßke Bilde itzo zur stedte ist, vnd auf Vnserer vnmundigen vettern vnd pflegesohne vnkosten auf das geldt wartet, vnd Wir Vns erjnnern, das das geldt alhie jn Vnsere renterey verhanden ist, so begheren vnd beuehlen Wir dir demnach hiemit gnediglich, das du dich angelicus briefs erhebest vnd alhie noch vor Vnserm aufzuge bej Vns anlangest, damit Wir nicht allein von dir selbst rechten bericht erfharen, sondern auch die sachen desto ehe jhre richtige maße erlangen, vnd besorgender schade vnd vngelegenheit verhuetet pleiben muge.
text.english:
**To the honourable, our dear and faithful Andreas Meier, rent-master, at Wismar.**

By the grace of God, Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg etc. Honourable, dear, faithful one: what Eske Bille, concerning the 10,000 thalers with which our under-age cousins and foster-sons, the young Dukes of Mecklenburg etc., stand bound to Tycho Brahe, once again addresses to our chamberlain Joachim von Stralendorf — that you may see at fuller length from his original letter, enclosed herewith.

Now, we are of the opinion that the ten thousand thalers, together with the interest which the said Tycho Brahe is to have, are still on hand together, so that, upon demand, against the surrender of the bond that was issued, they may at once be paid out — as indeed we wrote to you about this recently (as you may gather from the enclosed copy). But since Eske Bille, among other things in his letter, mentions that yesterday evening someone presented himself to him at Rostock, who had reported to him on your behalf that you had remitted 5,000 thalers up to Prague to the aforesaid Tycho Brahe — and we cannot know what the circumstance of this may be — we therefore graciously desire of you herewith that you write us, without delay, by the bearer, an actual and certain report of this; for since Eske Bille has himself come from Denmark for the sake of the money, and lies at Rostock, the matter can suffer no delay whatever. And we also hold it [to be so] — since you have indicated to us not the least of it, that you should have remitted the money up to Prague, which moreover, in our judgement, could not properly have been done before the recovery of the issued bond — that the whole sum is still together, so that it may and can be paid out in full (since Eske Bille, too, wants it in full). And you will dispatch the bearer back to us with the desired answer all the more promptly, so that we may certainly receive it before our departure from here (which, God willing, will take place next Tuesday, tomorrow). In this you fulfil our gracious and trusty intent.

Given at Güstrow, the 9th of August, in the year 1601.


*[Postscript:]* [On a slip:] Post Scripta. Also, honourable, dear, faithful one: since Eske Bille is now on the spot, and waits for the money at the cost of our under-age cousins and foster-sons, and We recall that the money is here on hand in our treasury, We therefore desire and command you herewith, graciously, that upon [receipt of] the present letter you set out and present yourself to Us here before our departure, so that We may not only learn the true report from you yourself, but also that the matter the sooner attain its right measure, and the apprehended damage and inconvenience remain forestalled.

documents.apparatus:
- **Direction & sender.** A **ducal letter**, from **Ulrich, Duke of Mecklenburg(-Güstrow)** (1527–1603), to his own treasury official — the third surviving document of the Tycho/Mecklenburg debt thread, written from the ducal residence at **Güstrow**. (The edition labels the sender *Ulrich 3.*) It is included in the Tychonic correspondence because it concerns, and quotes, the recovery of Tycho's loan.
- **Recipient.** **Andreas Meier**, ducal Mecklenburg **rent-master at Wismar** — the same officer pressed in Tycho's own letters of 27 May and 18 July 1601 (brahe-t_16010527001, brahe-t_16010718001). The Duke, his master, now demands an accounting.
- **The transaction.** The **10,000-thaler loan** owed Tycho by the **young (under-age) Dukes of Mecklenburg**, the Duke's *vmündige Vettern und Pflegesöhne* ("under-age cousins and foster-sons") for whom Ulrich stood guardian. The Duke believes the full sum is in hand, to be paid against the surrender of the **bond (*Verschreibung*)** — but Eske Bille has reported a rumour that Meier already **remitted 5,000 thalers to Prague**, and the Duke demands urgent clarification: a partial remittance before the bond's recovery would be irregular.
- **Persons named.**
 - *Eßke Bilde* = **Eske Bille**, the Danish nobleman and Tycho's kinsman-agent, who has "come from Denmark for the sake of the money" and waits at **Rostock** (cf. brahe-t_16010527001).
 - *unser Kämmerer Joachim von Stralendorf* = **Joachim von Stralendorf**, the Duke's **chamberlain**, to whom Eske Bille's latest letter was addressed.
 - *Tycho Brahe*, the creditor; the *junge Herzöge zu Mecklenburg*, the under-age debtors.
- **Places.** *Güstrow* (ducal residence, place of issue); *Wismar* (Meier's seat); *Rostock* (where Eske Bille waits); *Prag* = **Prague** (where Tycho is, and whither the disputed 5,000 thalers were allegedly sent).
- **Register & formulae.** The princely **first-person plural** (*Von Gottes Gnaden … Wir … Unsere*) and the subject-address *unser lieber getreuer* ("our dear and faithful one") mark the sovereign-to-servant register, distinct from the burgher-courteous tone of Tycho's own letters to Meier. *Datum* → "Given." The internal deadline *am zukünftigen Dienstag, morgen* = "next Tuesday, tomorrow" (the Duke's imminent departure from Güstrow).
- **Calendar.** Dateline *den 9. Augusti a:o 1601*; the edition gives no style marker. As a **Lutheran north-German chancery** document, Mecklenburg in 1601 was still on the **Julian (Old Style)** calendar (Protestant Germany kept it until 1700) — to be contrasted with the explicit *stylo novo* of Tycho's Prague letters in the same thread. The date is reproduced as written; no conversion is performed.

- **§1 Dreyer collation.** "[In schedula:] Post Scripta" enclosed slip (Duke Ulrich commands Meier to come at once, the money being in the ducal treasury, Eske Bille waiting), restored from Dreyer XIV pp.231–232 (dropped by the working transcription).
